Subject: looking for students interested in project interfacing quantum biology with machine learningbased symbolic regression
Body: dear students i am aarat kalra an assistant professor at the centre for biomedical engineering here at iit delhi my group is interested in understanding how the electronic properties of biological matter can be harnessed for therapeutic purposes a recent focus in our lab has been photodynamic therapy which uses light and certain injected pigments to treat skin cancer at the molecular scale when light hits pigments in the skin they donate their electronic energy to oxygen forming highly reactive oxygen species this type of energy transfer is called dexter energy transfer and is typically difficult to simulate or predict thus healthcare professionals struggle to understand the extent to which pigments will damage tissue here we have a project where the goal is to overcome this challenge we would like to predict dexter energy transfer rates using machine learningbased symbolic regression either through pythonbased pysr or other package we have calculated already about datapoints specifically we have calculated dexter energy transfer between oxygen and several biomolecules so establishing a general trend should not be difficult what we dont have is folks interested andor experienced in using such machine learning tools for biologicalmedical paradigms such as dexter energy transfer and photodynamic therapy i am looking for two students with high integrity to join this project at either at the senior undergraduate or at the masters level a mature commitment to the project and coding experience are expected if you are interested email me with your complete cv please dont send an aigenerated response to this email best regards aarat p kalra assistant professor centre for biomedical engineering indian institute of technology delhi globewithmeridians telephonereceiver links

Subject: talk by dr uditendu mukhopadhyay iit bombay – care committee room iii today at am
Body: title quantum technologies in semiconductor deg from analog quantum simulation to cryogenic memory by dr uditendu mukhopadhyay department of physics iit bombay venue care committee room block iii iit delhi date nd may at am abstract abstract twodimensional electron gases degs formed in semiconductor heterostructures have emerged as a versatile platform for quantum technologies offering precise electrostatic control and tunability of key physical parameters in this talk we explore two complementary applications analog quantum simulation using gatedefined quantum dot arrays in gaasalgaas heterostructures and optically programmable cryogenic memory in sisige gatedefined quantum dot arrays in gaasalgaas degs naturally emulate the fermihubbard model offering a highly controllable analog quantum simulator we introduce the fundamentals of this approach highlight key experimental techniques demonstrate their application through the specific example of nagaoka ferromagnetism and discuss the challenges and outlook for scaling these systems we then address the need for scalable classical memory at millikelvin temperatures presenting a cryogenic memory concept based on an undoped sisige hfet in which thresholdvoltage states are programmed and erased optically under a modest gate bias exploiting a high interface trap density to lock the threshold voltage to the backgate bias the device supports both binary and multibit operation with endurance exceeding ³ cycles and state retention beyond ⁴ s at k establishing a promising cryogenic memory platform inherently compatible with sisigebased quantum computing architectures professor head uplg chair professor of future computing technologies centre for applied research in electronics care iit delhi new delhi phone o fax

Subject: phd synopsis beyond the coverage number measurement prediction and latent barriers in childhood immunization
Body: dear all you are invited to the scai phd synopsis seminar by ritika singh as per the following details it would be wonderful if you could join us title beyond the coverage number measurement prediction and latent barriers in childhood immunization th may tuesday am academic complex east virtual abstract childhood vaccination is one of the most important publichealth interventions but surveybased estimates depend on how vaccination histories are recorded especially when cards are missing and maternal recall is used spatial mapping is important because national averages can hide local coldspots and cascade modelling is needed because never starting vaccination dropping out early and failing to complete later doses represent different programme problems a further challenge is to separate access meaning the practical ability to reach and use vaccination services from demand meaning willingness or acceptance once access exists routine surveys record uptake but they do not directly observe these two processes this thesis used india’s national family health survey nfhs and nfhs to compare cardonly and cardplusrecall vaccine maps with bayesian spatial models then used nfhs to model zerodose bcgmcv dropout and dpt dpt dropout with penalised logistic regression and neural networks neuralnetwork outputs were interpreted using shap friedman’s h feature interaction strength and dependence surfaces senegal dhs data were then used with bayesian twoparameter itemresponse modelling and a generative vaccineuptake model to infer latent access and demand and nigeria dhs data were used to infer the same latent quantities and map them nationally with spatial validation adding recall improved spatial prediction in both nfhs and nfhs neural networks improved macrof across the immunisation cascade and the interpretation layer showed where the neural network captured structure beyond the additive baseline which factors increased or reduced risk where their effects changed and how maternal household and servicerelated disadvantages combined differently by cascade stage and geography the senegal study separated access from demand and the nigeria extension showed how these latent quantities could be represented spatially at national scale overall the thesis shows that low coverage should not be read as one number or one cause it may reflect recording source geography cascade stage interacting disadvantage access constraints or weaker demand conditional on access the combined contribution is a modelling route from reliable outcome construction to spatial estimation interpretable prediction latent accessdemand inference and finally to maps showing where different barriers are concentrated thanks sumeet

journaling and identifying its root cause then working through it with reflection meditation or mindset shifts i also find it incredibly helpful to immerse myself in mediums outside of my own practice stepping into unfamiliar creative worlds takes the pressure off and often sparks unexpected inspiration whats the worst recommendation someones given you i thought long and hard about this and honestly couldnt come up with an answer ive always lived life to the beat of my own drum so i dont tend to seek out much advice when its offered unsolicited i usually let it pass im deeply intuitive and as long as i keep my nervous system regulated i trust that my inner guidance will lead me where i need to go when ive been led down the wrong path its almost always been because i was operating from a place of scarcity or fear rather than true intuition where do you go to find peace i find peace in a few simple places a hot yoga class a favorite neighborhood coffee shop my bed for a quiet Subject: being political in the right way
Body: view this post on the web at from george orwell’s ‘why i write’ i cannot say with certainty which of my motives are the strongest but i know which of them deserve to be followed and looking back through my work i see that it is invariably where i lacked political purpose that i wrote lifeless books and was betrayed into purple passages sentences without meaning decorative adjectives and humbug generally i want to be political but in the right way what does being political mean being political means having a role in how one’s local society should be run local society refers to a few things where you live where you were born or who you pay taxes to i am malaysian a uk taxpayer and live in south london so i would consider south london the uk and malaysia as my local society running something means deciding how resources should be allocated to common spaces these are things like schools and roads resources are limited so we need to make hard decisions to decide where they go being political means trying to convince others of what the optimal allocation is examples are include deciding how much taxation a society should have where these funds are allocated what sources of energy we should use and what should be taught in schools the goal of this allocation game aims to increase things that aligns with the society’s values for most of the world this includes the collective happiness of the society the lifespan and population the economic prosperity of the society and preserving justness and freedoms why be political so why am i suddenly interesting doing some writing that is political after all this is a science blog well i used to feel icky about politics and politicians but i’ve realised that i felt icky about partisanship not necessarily the about the game of politics above in fact the more i’ve dug into housing council management and social sciences the more i’ve realised that there are some interesting optimisation problems to dig into also the hard truth is that politics affects science in maker of patterns freeman dyson not only talks about his emotional state during his divorce but also about his political dispositions in particular the behaviours of scientists between and working on the manhattan project and now we have terence tao campaigning for private funding since the nsf cut his grant and so i must have an active say in how political debate around science this blog is my diary i write to record my mental state and so i must record my political thoughts it benefits me in the end after all as a tax payer to live in a society that is more prosperous and kind there are also other reasons to be more political that involve defence against people outside of the local society because of cross border flows there are people who are not in my local society that have an effect on how it is run for example division from social media and donations from foreign actors i would like to counter these people with my own voice also i’ve been political all along my blog is about doing science independently but this implies that the public establishment’s methods of doing science is bad and so this is a political statement in itself so i was political all along i just need to do more so how can i be political in the right way the standard way to be political is that people pick a side and try to defend it in the uk i can’t do this because i don’t have a clear idea of which side to support also picking a side would endanger me to try to stick to that side which could cause value drift i wrote about this earlier in my do not plan essay but if i don’t pick a side how do i prevent my writing from being noncommittal and vacuous i want my writing to be strong convicted and engaging i also want to contribute in a way that others can’t by elimination there’s no point in me writing about the issues that are cursed cursed issues are the issues that have been debated for centuries that everyone talks about and that no one will listen to me for some of these problems include whether to increase or decrease tax yimbyism and immigration so instead i need to focus on ideas which are less talked about and solvable there are a few reasons why important topics are not discussed even through they should be but that doesn’t mean we should not talk about them this is where i come in first i could write about things we can mostly agree on in terms of the end result but are complicated and have incentive issues for example we can all agree that pandemics are bad and i think we would all agree to allocate more funding to biosecurity like low cost air purification and ppe stockpile management but the math physics and data juggling to do this is hard and problem is that it happens so rarely that doesn’t get much coverage both of these are fixable this can be fixed by writing with more clarity than the media and doing the math which is why i’m inclined to write more about it i’ve written about complexity theory and dynamical systems here on this blog it is likely that we can use those ideas there to reason more rigorously about issues in government where statistics are likely to be useless or manipulated many local council problems are amenable to modelling as a large set of ordinary differential equations like the techniques i’ve written about in this blog these sorts of things might help us decide which policy interventions are important from a mechanistic point of view for example if the council had dollars to spend would you spend it on a bike lane or a hospital which one is more effective for a healthier society most people think centrism is boring and so if i’m a centrist want to talk about politics then how do i’m not be boring i’m not sure yet but i think i’m improving i used to think i was cooked but i was surprised that my navier stokes post got mildly popular even amongst nonphysicists so i’m cautiously optimistic that i can make boring politic mildly Subject: phd synopsis presentation of mohit kataria aiz
Body: dear all as part of his phd synopsis presentation mr mohit kataria aiz will deliver a technical talk on towards scalable graph machine learning coarsening structure learning and efficient representations the details are as follows date st may time am venue ee committee room title towards scalable graph machine learning coarsening structure learning and efficient representations abstract graphs provide a powerful representation for relational data arising in social biological citation transportation and scientific domains however modern graph datasets are increasingly large heterogeneous dynamic and computationally expensive to process making scalability a central challenge for graph machine learning mohits phd work addresses this challenge through a unified line of work on scalable graph learning algorithms based on graph reduction structure learning and efficient graph representations the first part develops universal graph coarsening ugc a hashingbased framework that jointly uses node features and graph structure to efficiently reduce graphs while preserving spectral and downstream task performance including on both homophilic and heterophilic graphs this is further extended to support fast scalable and streaming graph coarsening with theoretical and empirical validation the second part introduces ahugc an adaptive and heterogeneous coarsening framework that combines localitysensitive hashing with consistent hashing to obtain multiresolution coarsened graphs while preserving type semantics in heterogeneous networks the third part presents graphflex a scalable framework for unsupervised learning of graph structures in large and expanding graphs using clustering and coarsening to reduce candidate edge search and enable incremental updates his work also demonstrates the practical impact of coarsened graph learning in singlecell data analysis enabling faster and accurate biomedical graph learning another work canopy transforms graph neighborhoods into canonical computationaltree representations thereby enabling scalable interpretable cpubased graph learning using classical tabular models finally related side contributions explore coarseningbased collaboration in personalized federated graph learning through coco together these works help make graph ml scalable covering graph coarsening structure learning biomedical applications and efficient alternatives to message passing publications from the work published ugc universal graph coarsening neurips fast and scalable hashingbased universal graph coarsening ieee transactions on pattern analysis and machine intelligence graphflex unsupervised structure learning framework for large expanding graphs icml coarscrna scaling graphbased approaches for largescale singlecell data analysis using coarsened graph learning computers in biology and medicine under review canopy from mpnns to classical models graph learning via canonical computational trees neurips coco collaborate via coarsening for personalized federated graph learning neurips ahugc adaptive and heterogeneousuniversal graph coarsening kdd you all are welcome to attend regards sandeep jayadeva Subject: do not plan
Body: view this post on the web at goal seeking is deciding what to do making a plan to do it and then doing that thing whilst sacrificing other things to be properly goal seeking the last part is important you cannot train for a marathon without giving up the time that you would be eating cheetos goals have time horizons some are short term lasting minutes like making a cup of coffee others goals might involve plans for years both people and organisations can goal seek you might wish to aim for a promotion at work your personal long term plan might be to be famous on tiktok or your organisation might be trying to build some sort of huge product like a space shuttle within years my claim is that goal seeking is a bad strategy for any horizon longer than a week this rule applies to most people as well as organisations and governments it is the reason why most ambitious government projects fail i have believed this for three years so i do not goal seek with my career by deciding what i need to do then attempting it for the next year i do not aim for a promotion or targets nor do i attempt to goal seek big projects in my personal life or in my hobbies i will explain why i don’t goal seek personally and then describe my alternative method of doing stuff long term goal seeking is bad because i get bored with trying to stick with something for a long time boredom kills my motivation and so i become unproductive at that point it becomes marginally better to quit in favour of something i like more this happened with a particular chemistry project i was working on which i quit in favour of physics in theoretical biology so how do you become successful if you quit once you get bored doesn’t the current substack intelligentia subscribe to the idea of a forcing function to make you stick with your goal here is my rebuttal being successful by any metric likely does not matter so you may as well be having fun but if you did want to be crazy successful you would have to be lucky if you are not lucky then you should at least be having fun if you somehow are lucky you need to work hard but to work hard at something you need to enjoy it therefore you need to quit if you’re not having fun all the routes above involve not being bored so quit if you’re not the next reason why goal seeking is bad is because it’s a waste of time due to world uncertainty and chaos my various investigations in the physics of dynamics systems have convinced me that the majority of the natural world is unpredictable if we can’t model three body pendulum then how are we supposed to model the success of our plans moreover my career in finance has taught me that one always underestimates the potential for unknown unknowns because of this too much planning is a waste of time time is scarce so you take an l is you spend it planning the next reason is moral and values uncertainty throughout my life i have been everywhere on the political spectrum socialist yimby conservative centrist libertarian and all so if my values change due to new information these are unlikely to be compatible with the current plan i’m on if i force myself to stick with a plan this can cause painful conflict if my values start to diverge from it for example i used to be a fairly strong utilitarian whereas now i take a more holistic approach that aligns with personal interest and some degree of epicureanism but i found some of my projects during my utilitarian phase to be painful to continue long term goal seeking is also bad because it tricks you that you’re going to stick to something which makes you more likely to defer it this is similar to metric and reward hacking where you optimise for some number that is unrelated to what you are trying to achieve but still most people claim that to do big things you need a plan the space shuttle programme and moon landings are often cited as an example but this is not how engineering works the most successful engineering projects have been modular and testable in stagebystage chunks not through moonshot ambitious planning do you think the space shuttle programmes would have even been an option if we hadn’t nailed propulsion first and you may ask how do long term infrastructure projects get done for example railways well it would be better if infrastructural planners thought more incrementally as well instead of the financial and infrastructural failure like the hs railway the uk might have done better first trying to build quality infrastructure locally and then incrementally adding things one ok so what’s the alternative to me its doing incremental things at the daily horizon that roughly align with your personal values at the time and then i go from there for example when i write this blog i look at stuff i’ve written and see how i can improve the ideas i try to write what i can with those ideas for the day and then things get big through piecing together stuff i’ve already built in the direction want i think stuff like ‘ok so i have a bunch of theories i’ve written about in fluids and biology can i string them together in a meaningful way with in a day’s work’ that way i am not trying to accomplish things with parts that haven’t arrived yet rather i have the confidence to use what i got to do more this makes me come across as a more reliable person to my peers this is because the incremental method means i don’t promise big things that i haven’t done yet and this also contributes to my success rate because people believe in me more unsubscribe caution this email Body: प्रिय सभी सभी कर्मचारियों संकाय सदस्यों और छात्रोंछात्रावासों के अलावा को सूचित किया जाता है कि भारत सरकार ने भारत की जनगणना के अंतर्गत स्वगणना प्रक्रिया शुरू कर दी है। सभी कर्मचारियों से अनुरोध है कि वे नीचे दिए गए आधिकारिक जनगणना स्वगणना पोर्टल के माध्यम से जल्द से जल्द अपनी स्वगणना पूरी करें जनगणना स्वगणना पोर्टल स्वगणना पूरी करने की अंतिम तिथि मई है। जनगणना एक महत्वपूर्ण राष्ट्रीय प्रक्रिया है और जनगणना गतिविधियों को सफलतापूर्वक संपन्न कराने में सरकार के साथ सहयोग करना प्रत्येक नागरिक का कर्तव्य और दायित्व है। इसलिए सभी कर्मचारियों और संकाय सदस्यों को सलाह दी जाती है कि वे निर्धारित समय के भीतर स्वगणना प्रक्रिया को पूरा करें और अपने परिवार के सदस्यों को भी ऐसा करने के लिए प्रोत्साहित करें। स्वगणना पूरी करने की प्रक्रिया को समझाने वाला एक वीडियो सभी संबंधितों के मार्गदर्शन के लिए संलग्न है। जनगणना कार्यालय से प्राप्त होते ही जनगणना कर्मियों के नाम और संपर्क नंबर साझा किए जाएंगे। सुरक्षा अधिकारी आईआईटी दिल्ली dear all it is hereby informed to all staff members faculty and studentsother than hostels that the government of india has initiated the self enumeration process under the census of india all employees are requested to complete their self enumeration at the earliest through the official census self enumeration portal given below census self enumeration portal the last date for completion of self enumeration is may census is an important national exercise and it is the duty and responsibility of every citizen to cooperate with the government in successful completion of census activities therefore all staff and faculty members are advised to complete the self enumeration process positively within the stipulated time and also encourage their family members to do the same a video explaining the procedure for completing self enumeration is attached herewith for guidance of all concerned names of enumerators and their contact numbers will be shared as and when received from the census office security officer iit delhi

Body: dear all the track is to be used only for walking jogging and running no other activities are permitted runningjogging shoes with soft rubber soles are advised footwear that may damage the synthetic surface eg leather footwear hard plastic slippers spikes studs etc and barefoot running are prohibited clean your shoes before entering the track equipment that may damage the synthetic surface eg bicycles baby strollers scooters skateboards skates etc is strictly prohibited follow all marked instructions and walkjog on the track in the designated direction clockwiseanticlockwise as applicable respect other users maintain a safe distance and be mindful of children give way to faster runners and avoid occupying multiple lanes do not sit stop suddenly or stand in groups on the track pets are not allowed on the track remain alert and aware of your surroundings as the track is located around cricket football and basketball playing areas use earphonesheadphones at low volume to remain aware of ambient sounds and announcements keep the track clean do not litter or carry eatables onto the track track access may be restricted during wet conditions or for maintenance prof vireshwar kumar deepak negi president bsa sports officer

Subject: how to land a role in the ai world
Body: view image caption hey folks im swati welcome back to my weekly newsletter this newsletter is those conversations what im seeing thinking and what id tell you if we were grabbing coffee this weeks edition is about getting hired in an era where graduates are unemployable but before that ——————————————————————————— last week brian armstrong sent an email to the entire coinbase team view image follow image link caption he said that the new coinbase would have five layers max below the ceo leaders with as many as direct reports and no pure managers anywhere in the company every leader would have to also do the work and most importantly “we’ll also be experimenting with reduced pod sizes including ‘one person teams’ with engineers designers and product managers all in one role” if you are a fresher reading that notice the shape of the company that comes out the other side rather than the layoffs the earlycareer roles you were going to walk into are being collapsed into one role and it expects you to ship this is happening across orgs view image follow image link caption tcs announced layoffs in july last year and the it services hiring funnel that absorbed tier grads for two decades has from around lakh in fy to lakh in fy view image follow image link caption the seat that used to guarantee a job has now stopped guaranteeing one and while going through s of applications every week at masters’ union i think i know why in our recent hiring for our director’s office role we shortlisted forty resumes i saw that most had the same internships and a line about being passionate about leveraging technology only two of them had github links of which only one had something deployed i could click on and see for myself thats who got the call when i told this to a friend who runs hiring at a series b startup he said the same thing he said his shortlist is mostly people whose work he’s seen on the internet and scouted intentionally or referrals there are hardly any shortlisted candidates coming from the hiring form many students still dont realise even today the shortlist is being made before the application is even read so here’s how i’d play this firstly stop chasing stamps view image follow image link caption it didnt surveys of mooc completers say the certificate helped them surveys of hiring managers say they dont trust it instead view image caption apply for the role you dont think youll get most students rule themselves out before the company gets a chance to you see a job description with eight bullet points you tick six of them and you assume the other two disqualify you so you dont apply you tell yourself youll come back to the bigger one later when youre more ready tara sophia mohr surveyed over a thousand professionals for harvard business review on why they didnt apply for jobs they were underqualified for and over in said the qualifications mentioned are nonnegotiable but most of the time the qualifications are a wishlist the same thing happens at a scale with indian students and international roles you see based in san francisco or must be eligible to work in the us and you assume thats the end of the conversation you dont write to them because nobody around you has done it so nobody around you ever does it the companies hiring now especially in ai are sponsoring visas hiring remotefirst and writing to people who write to them just apply and see how it unfolds view image caption pick one very specific thing you can deploy in days like deploying an agent that scrapes job postings by industry and writes daily summaries or a rag system on your colleges last five years of question papers ship it to github with a working demo url and write a readme that explains what it does and what you learned if you’re not technical vibe code it with tools like claude lovable and deploy the artifact on a domain that you own post it on linkedin twitter the day it ships the algorithm could potentially show it to your next manager the ability to build something shows intent passion and most importantly skill when you’re entering the workforce view image caption most students apply to companies and hardly hear back from three instead flip it pick ten companies you really want to work for for three of them build a small ai tool that solves a problem you can see from outside the company then send the person who owns the problem could be a founder or the engineering manager a working link or just make a public pitch on why a company should hire you i witnessed divyanshi one of our own students do exactly this for vedantu recently she made a mock ad for vedantu last month that showed a parent worried about their kids marks and pitched a refundifgradesdontimprove guarantee from vedantu vedantu saw that she understood the target audience positioning and that she had ability to create appeal for their brand which led them to offer her an internship view image follow image Body: view this post on the web at the twoparty system didnt die in the uk– its just reorganising the uk twoparty system didn’t die it’s reshuffling labour shed more than councillors across england the conservatives lost ground everywhere wales was yanked from labour for the first time in nearly three decades the leaders of both insurgent parties – the greens and reform – are howling the end of the old order they’re not wrong but they’re not quite right the new parties have an issue they can certainly claim the issues that will get them new voters but they don’t yet have the infrastructure to use them reform doesn’t have the huge donor network volunteer network or even the legitimacy necessary if it wants to capture westminster the same goes with the greens the old parties have their own troubles they are bogged down by their existing voters on whom they depend for manpower and donations but that loyalty prevents them from reaching out to claim the new winning ideas claimed by the insurgents so they can either change their pitch and drink the koolaid of modern populism or just negotiate directly with their respective rivals to integrate them or they can just perish in the next election businesses are watching with their chequebooks open uk government seizes british steel just before the coup against pm keir starmer announced he would take ownership of british steel originally formed from the nationalisation of private steel companies it was privatised under thatcher in it has since suffered the uk’s deindustrialisation after years of trouble the company entered liquidation in it was later bought by china’s jingye group in for £ mn promising heavy investment but as the chinese threatened to shut down the plant last year the government mobilised parliament to seize operations it’s been an absolute cash hole the national audit office confirmed that the government had spent more than £ mn in working capital since last year to keep the site operational the plant was losing more than £ mn a day not to mention the thousands of jobs — it’s a toostrategictofail business these are two of the country’s last blast furnaces and produce of the steel used on uk rail tracks expect more action too as national sovereignty bubbles to the top of economic policy awful investments become essential when national security comes into play we all remember the covid troubles over medical supplies more gov action might offer investors in uk strategic industries — rail construction energy or vehicles — muchneeded security just expect the accompanying intervention a blast furnace a poster by artist clive gardiner issued by the empire marketing board are chiefs of staff just secretaries with better education like me you must also be running into them want a meeting — speak with the chief of staff need a document — chief of staff thanks people say the title carefully as if introducing the new iphone they manage critical projects they manage super important communications they handle highlevel operations before they ever reach the executive this is all stuff that’s beyond my little capacities let’s be honest it’s still a pa right an extremely capable wellpaid ninja pa — but a pa nevertheless as wages rise and tech improves nobody really needed someone to do the grunt work “just send me an invite on gcal cheers” i have software to manage Subject: shopping in the future
Body: view image caption shopping seems to be shifting in the coming years from us stumbling upon ads going on a website using a discount code to just asking chatgpt for a solution to our problem and it doing the rest and most of us in india think that’s yet far from happening but it’s actually not view image follow image link caption heres how the experiment worked anthropic gave each person a hundred dollars and asked what they wanted to buy from their colleagues or what they wanted to sell to them each was interviewed about prices preferences and how their ai agent should negotiate on their behalf those interviews briefed a personal ai agent for each participant the agents were dropped into a slack channel and let loose they posted listings found each other negotiated in plain english the humans werent allowed to step in by the end they had struck deals worth just over four thousand dollars but for statistical reasoning anthropic ran the marketplace four times across the four runs they changed one thing in two of those runs every participant was represented by anthropics strongest ai model called claude opus in the other two half the participants were given a much weaker model instead called claude haiku which is a smaller and less capable model everything else stayed the same across runs the participants whose agent was the weaker model got worse deals consistently view image follow image link caption of course the participants whose agents were quietly making lesser profits didnt notice when anthropic surveyed everyone afterwards the people on the losing end rated their experience as fair as everyone else the unfair outcomes were invisible to the people experiencing them view image caption what i think for as long as i can remember the most underrated check for good purchase decisions has been a feeling you walk out of a shop and your gut tells you whether youve been taken maybe the price came too easily or the shopkeeper backed off too quickly when you tried to walk away none of it is proof and it doesnt need to be the buyer who senses unfairness asks for a refund warns her friends and refuses to come back that gut sense has been the immune system of commerce since humans started trading with each other ive worked in retail and i know how brutal that gut can be the cart conversion problem in retail has never been solved and the reason is the gut it keeps killing transactions that everything else about the funnel was built to win every photo every checkout flow every retargeting sequence is an attempt to win an audit the buyer is running with her own eyes i know how brutal that muscle is view image follow image link caption every photo and email and checkout flow youve ever optimised was an attempt to win the audit someone was running with their own eyes the gut has always been in the room but with project deal there’s essentially no gut in the room view image caption so what’s the learning this goes beyond anthropic’s experiment and actually is a part of reality view image follow image link caption the driver was people asking chatgpt about glp weight loss drugs people were asking a health question and the agent intercepted that question with a brand recommendation and they bought from a brand they hadnt heard of fifteen seconds earlier this is what makes project deal feel small the anthropic participants at least knew they were transacting whereas the walmart customers didnt view image caption what i think is worth doing three things in roughly the order id do them if i were a founder or a business owner today the first is to stop measuring your ai presence through brand queries and start measuring it through category questions if you sell sleep mattresses run is memory foam bad for your back or how long does a mattress last through chatgpt claude and perplexity instead of asking about “how is company name’s mattress” this is because these searches are where the consideration is happening the second is to invest in being the source for those upstream questions which is a different content strategy than what most d c teams are running view image follow image link caption original research proprietary data founder essays about the category rather than the product expert positioning that gets cited by third parties this stuff does not drive lastclick attribution it also was not worth doing five years ago but it is now the third is harder and more honest be clear about whether your category is even fightable replenishables hardspec items anything where the buyer has no real preference at the sku level those are the categories agents are going to commoditise the fastest for most d c founders in those categories the realistic move is subscription loyalty and locking in the second purchase before the agent has time to compare for taste and fit categories fashion beauty anything where the customer needs to be in your environment to decide the agent is much less of a threat than your competitive set because the agent fundamentally cannot replicate the experience of trying it on do not optimize too aggressively for a problem that is not your problem view Subject: freeman dyson’s model of a cell
Body: view this post on the web at in this post i’ll describe freeman dyson’s toy model of a cell in his book origins of life fn it’s a probabilistic model that gives us interesting behaviours it has autocatalysis which means that a reaction increases the likelihood of the same reaction occuring and it has two equilibrium points that can be interpreted as life and death it’s also a good example of how to reason about random systems and how they can tend to stable states you may need to see this in a webbrowser to see the simulations run the model is of a cell evolving in discrete time steps the cell is a constrained volume of fluid with a membrane that is meant to be the cell wall through diffusion molecules called monomers can go in or out these monomers are meant to be nutrients within a cell there are n sites each monomer can attach to one of the n sites or the site can be empty the model evolves in discrete time steps at every time step a site can remain empty if it has a monomer attached to it the monomer can stay there or it can unbind the sites are meant to represent placeholders for monomers binding into polymers but i’ll get into the biochem in a different post there are n species of monomers that can bind to the sites n of these are considered ‘inactive’ and one type is ‘active’ if a site has an active monomer then the likelihood that other sites absorb an active monomer increases a monomer being active is meant to represent a monomer being at the ‘right place at the right time’ that lets other active monomers bind to a cite this is meant to capture ‘autocatalysis’ — the binding of an active monomer makes it more likely that other active monomers will bind so each site has three possible states — empty inactive monomer or active monomer per unit time the probabilities are modelled as follows if a site is filled by either an active or inactive monomer then it has a probability pq of being emptied or ‘desorbed’ where q is a constant on the other hand if a site is empty the probability of an inactive monomer being absorbed is np where n is the number of types of inactive monomers the probability of an active monomer being absorbed is ψx · p where x is the fraction of sites already occupied by active monomers ψx is a monotonically increasing function of the fraction of sites that are already active this means that the more active sites there are the more likely it is that active monomers will be absorbed this function psi is meant to encode the increased chance that an active monomer will be absorbed if there are active ones present already this is shown in the video below for each site the transition between each state at each time step is given by the following chain so if we let a simulation run let’s see what happens to the fraction of empty inactive and active sites if we start with a large number of inactive sites the number of active sites doesn’t really seem to take off — and so the cell remains filled with inactive sites in this case the cell is just filled with mostly ‘inactive’ monomers and remains ‘dead’ this is shown in the video below where the blue monomers are inactive and the green monomers are active on the other hand if we initialise the system with a larger amount of active monomers it seems to stay that way now if we increase the number of monomers and the time of the simulation rapidly we see that the cell converges to one of two states the green trajectory shows the convergence to an alive state in which there is a constant fraction of active monomers and the blue one shows convergence to a dead state where most states are inactive monomers this is pretty cool so we have got an apparently random autocatalytic system and have found that it has converged to two stable states how do we know which initial conditions lead to which state and what fraction there is of active monomers in each state i will discuss this in my next post dyson freeman j origins of life nd ed Subject: departmental seminar dr ankita jha research fellow nhlbi nih th may pm ksbs committee room
Body: dear all this is just a kind reminder for todays seminar by dr ankita jha at pm in ksbs committee room details of her talk can be found below hope to see you all best saurabh on saurabh raj wrote dear all we invite you to the ksbs departmental talk on th may at pm in the ksbs committee room the speaker is dr ankita jha a research fellow working at the national heart lung and blood institute nhlbi nih she is a cell and developmental biologist with a research focus on plasma membrane organisation during mechanical processes such as cell migration please circulate this information in your department all are cordially invited details may be found below abstract and a brief biodata of the speaker are attached speaker dr ankita jha research fellow national heart lung and blood institute nhlbi nih date th may time pm venue ksbs committee room title blebology decoding blebbased signaling in cancer disease progression abstract cancer cell migration plays a crucial role in invasion and metastasis during metastasis tumor cells migrate through their surrounding microenvironment navigating various tissue and extracellular matrix ecm geometries including confined spaces to spread to distant sites in confined microenvironments with low adhesion metastatic cells often adopt a blebbased mode of migration that differs fundamentally from integrindependent mesenchymal motility using metastatic melanoma cells under nonadhesive confinement we investigated the mechanisms that govern the formation and stability of the large pressuredriven leader bleb that defines cell polarity in this context highresolution live imaging and molecular perturbations revealed that egf signaling via pi k is critical for maintaining a stable polarized leader bleb surprisingly biosensors showed a reartofront gradient of egfr and pi k activity with downstream effectors pip and rac gtp enriched at the rear of the bleb while pip and rhoagtp localized to the front this spatial organization is inverted compared to classical mesenchymal migration disruption of this gradient via optogenetic tools led to bleb collapse highlighting its functional importance we further identified that transmembrane picket protein cd and membranecortex linker proteins restrict egfr mobility within a dense actin cortex at the bleb rear stabilizing the signaling gradient combined modeling and experimental data support a feedback mechanism linking cortical architecture to signaling dynamics our findings uncover a novel polarity axis in blebbased migration driven by localized signaling and cytoskeletal interactions this work underscores how distinct spatial arrangements of conserved signaling modules on the membrane enable plasticity in migration strategies allowing metastatic cells to adapt to biophysical constraints of the tumor microenvironment thank you best regards saurabh saurabh raj phd assistant professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology hauz khas new delhi india saurabh raj phd assistant professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology hauz khas new delhi india

Body: hey folks pratham here welcome back to paradox weekly a masters union newsletter where we break down the ideas trends and contradictions shaping business today ——————————————————————————— ——————————————————————————— indians paid over ₹ lakh crore in nonlife insurance premiums last year every insurer broker financial advisor will tell you the same thing you are underinsured and need more coverage i disagree with what insurance in india actually is indias outofpocket health expenditure is still around of total health spending down from a decade ago but still among the highest of any major economy despite millions of new policies being sold every year view image follow image link caption the country has more insurance than at any point in its history and indians are still funding most of their own healthcare directly that’s today’s paradox ——————————————————————————— the answer is the noclaim bonus and most people who have car insurance have no idea how expensive it actually is to protect the noclaim bonus on car insurance is standardised across every insurer in the country five consecutive claimfree years earns you off the own damage component of your premium building from after the first year after two after three and after four view image follow image link caption sbi generals consumer guide advises policyholders to absorb minor repair costs themselves and protect their ncb these are insurance companies officially advising you not to use their product the industrys response to this is the ncb protector addon which costs to of your od premium and gives you the right to file one or two claims a year without losing the slab you pay extra to use the product you already paid for every major retail health policy in india offers a cumulative bonus an increase in sum insured for each claimfree year that is cancelled or reduced when you file insurers can apply renewal premium loading on frequent claimants classifying them as higher risk for having used the protection they purchased and care insurance advises avoiding smaller treatment claims to keep the bonus and premiums stable the same logic that pushes car owners to pay for dents themselves pushes health policyholders to absorb medical expenses out of pocket so the policy stays intact for something serious a localcircles survey of over respondents found in had a health claim rejected or partially denied for reasons they considered invalid and irdais own fy data shows ₹ crore in health claims were disallowed a jump from the year before view image follow image link caption the most profitable insurance customer in india is the one who renews every year and never claims the insurer wins on both sides of this when you dont claim the ncb discount they give you next year costs them nothing because they have already collected the full premium this year when you do claim the slab resets and your future business gets repriced at the higher rate indias nonlife insurers posted ₹ crore in profit in fy up from ₹ crore the year before every time you ran the ncb math and decided the damage was not worth claiming that was the product working exactly as designed “hit reply Subject: departmental seminar dr ankita jha research fellow nhlbi nih th may pm ksbs committee room
Body: dear all we invite you to the ksbs departmental talk on th may at pm in the ksbs committee room the speaker is dr ankita jha a research fellow working at the national heart lung and blood institute nhlbi nih she is a cell and developmental biologist with a research focus on plasma membrane organisation during mechanical processes such as cell migration please circulate this information in your department all are cordially invited details may be found below abstract and a brief biodata of the speaker arein below link speaker dr ankita jha research fellow national heart lung and blood institute nhlbi nih date th may time pm venue ksbs committee room title blebology decoding blebbased signaling in cancer disease progression abstract cancer cell migration plays a crucial role in invasion and metastasis during metastasis tumor cells migrate through their surrounding microenvironment navigating various tissue and extracellular matrix ecm geometries including confined spaces to spread to distant sites in confined microenvironments with low adhesion metastatic cells often adopt a blebbased mode of migration that differs fundamentally from integrindependent mesenchymal motility using metastatic melanoma cells under nonadhesive confinement we investigated the mechanisms that govern the formation and stability of the large pressuredriven leader bleb that defines cell polarity in this context highresolution live imaging and molecular perturbations revealed that egf signaling via pi k is critical for maintaining a stable polarized leader bleb surprisingly biosensors showed a reartofront gradient of egfr and pi k activity with downstream effectors pip and rac gtp enriched at the rear of the bleb while pip and rhoagtp localized to the front this spatial organization is inverted compared to classical mesenchymal migration disruption of this gradient via optogenetic tools led to bleb collapse highlighting its functional importance we further identified that transmembrane picket protein cd and membranecortex linker proteins restrict egfr mobility within a dense actin cortex at the bleb rear stabilizing the signaling gradient combined modeling and experimental data support a feedback mechanism linking cortical architecture to signaling dynamics our findings uncover a novel polarity axis in blebbased migration driven by localized signaling and cytoskeletal interactions this work underscores how distinct spatial arrangements of conserved signaling modules on the membrane enable plasticity in migration strategies allowing metastatic cells to adapt to biophysical constraints of the tumor microenvironment thank you best regards saurabh saurabh raj phd assistant professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: how to write better
Body: view this post on the web at if your writing gets better then you will make cool new friends you might get career opportunities you might meet the love of your life i don’t believe that good writing should be simple nor complicated nor does writing need to be long form or short form good writing is just writing that conveys your intentions as clearly as possible clarity of intention has a practical purpose bad writing is like a tsunami that whips the reader in a different directions this makes them frustrated but good writing is like a scalpel in brain surgery it’s so sharp that it changes the reader’s mind without them feeling it and you will get them onside if you do these things you will write more clearly than most people use less words rewrite your sentences with less words and then stop just before the meaning starts to change so you don’t over cut this will make it clearer without compromising intentions once i write something i revisit it the next day and it makes it more obvious what to cut for example bad writing is like a fat tsunami that whips the reader in a different directions can be made better with bad writing is like a tsunami that whips the reader around but if long sentences are a stylistic choice in your fiction writing then ignore this advice split up sentences if you can split a sentence into two without changing the meaning do it for example bad writing is like a fat tsunami that whips the reader in a different directions which makes them frustrated is too much bad writing is like a fat tsunami that whips the reader in a different directions this makes them frustrated is better imagine someone is screaming ‘just fuckin’ say it’ the whole time you are writing if you do this you will discover what you are actually thinking important stuff comes first rank how crucial each paragraph is then put the best stuff at the top note that using ‘less words’ is more important than this tip your sentence structure should be mathematical if you have a mathematical background this should come easier frame your sentences as if they were deductive logic arguments use classic sentence structures like ‘if a then b’ don’t complicate for all you literature nerds who are gonna rage at me for saying this jane austen writes like this don’t say ‘i think’ it is assumed that your writing is your opinion if you must quantify the uncertainty by saying ‘its likely that x’ don’t overly hedge what you think if you need to say stuff like ‘ohhh maybe this but maybe that but actually i’m not sure’ then rethink your argument marginal clarity matters more than detail if you can increase clarity by but need to sacrifice of detail then do it just put details in an appendix write as much as possible i write for around hours Subject: me guest talk by dr mitanjali from institute of fluid mechanics and thermodynamics technische universität ilmenau germany
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the me guest talk by dr mitanjali from the institute of fluid mechanics and thermodynamics technische universitätilmenau germany the schedule title and brief information are as follows date th may wednesday time pm venue me seminar room ii title optical diagnostics for flow measurements from scanning piv to particle image thermometry abstract this talk presents optical diagnostic techniques for flow measurements with a focus on particle image velocimetry piv a widely used method for obtaining spatially resolved velocity fields the first part of the talk introduces a costeffective scanning piv system in which illumination is achieved by scanning continuouswave diodepumped solidstate dpss lasers of different wavelengths while image acquisition is performed using a conventional dslr camera the use of such alternative hardware significantly reduces system cost and enhances scalability for larger flow domains a mathematical model based on synthetic image generation is employed to analyze the effects of scanning illumination on particle imaging the system was experimentally implemented and validated against benchmark flows including steady vortex flow created by a magnetic stirrer and flow past a circular cylinder a key technical challenge on color crosstalk within dslr sensors is systematically investigated and a correction algorithm was developed to mitigate channel mixing and improve measurement accuracy the resulting system demonstrates reliable twodimensional twocomponent d c velocity measurements in lowspeed flows the final part of the talk focuses on ongoing work in rayleighbénard convection aimed at coupled velocitytemperature measurements current efforts are focused on particle image thermometry pit including the calibration of thermochromic liquid crystals tlcs as temperaturesensitive tracers biographical sketch dr mitanjali is currently a postdoctoral researcher at the institute of fluid mechanics and thermodynamics technische universität ilmenau germany her research focuses on experimental fluid mechanics particularly optical diagnostics for velocity and temperature measurements in turbulent flows she completed phd in from the department of aerospace engineering at the indian institute of technology kanpur where she developed a costeffective scanning particle image velocimetry piv system during her doctoral studies she was an exchange researcher at purdue university usa where she carried out part of her research her current work focuses on coupled velocitytemperature measurements in rayleighbénard convection using stereoscopic piv and particle image thermometry with thermochromic liquid crystals all interested are welcome to join the talk thanks and regards dr abhishek das assistant professor department of mechanical engineering iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india

actually used despite protests google proceeded with the deal reflecting a growing trend of deep collaboration between big tech and national defense agencies amid global ai competition why it matters this highlights a growing conflict between ai ethics and national security priorities it also signals a future where ai companies play a central role in military infrastructure raising critical questions about governance accountability and responsible use when may source stethoscope ai surpasses doctors in emergency diagnosis harvard study reveals at a glance a harvardled study has found that advanced ai models can outperform human doctors in emergency triage diagnosis achieving higher accuracy in identifying conditions from patient records and demonstrating strong clinical reasoning capabilities details the study tested an ai model against doctors using real emergency cases where the ai achieved around diagnostic accuracy outperforming doctors at – with additional clinical information ai accuracy improved to around slightly exceeding expert human performance in similar scenarios the ai also outperformed doctors in treatment planning tasks scoring significantly higher when designing longterm clinical strategies the model demonstrated strong performance in highpressure triage situations where quick decisionmaking with limited data is critical however the study was limited to textbased patient data meaning the ai did not evaluate physical symptoms visual cues or patient interaction factors why it matters this study highlights ai’s growing ability to match or exceed human clinical reasoning in critical scenarios while not replacing doctors it could become a powerful decisionsupport tool improving diagnostic accuracy and reshaping how emergency care is delivered when april source technologist cursor launches typescript sdk to build programmatic ai agents at a glance cursor has introduced a typescript sdk that enables developers to create run and opensource orchestration specification for codex agents designed to transform tools like issue trackers eg linear into a central control plane where ai agents pick up and execute tasks automatically interactive prompting to agent orchestration where ai handles execution endtoend—including generating code managing pull requests and integrating with ci pipelines early internal usage showed Subject: re booking new xps facility in sonipat
Body: dear all the new xps facility in sonipat is open for bookings i am forwarding the requirements for booking from prof pankaj srivastava the faculty coordinator of the facility please follow the instructions as given dear colleagues we are pleased to inform you that a new xps system has been installed on the sonipat campus and it is now open for bookings from the users the details of the system are available on the crf website please find below some important points in xps operations we will accept powder samples fine powders however preparing pellets instead of using powder is preferable for the longevity of the uhvcompatible components of the xps system as pellets provide better consistency and reduce the risk of contamination during analysis a specific research group may reserve a maximum of slots per month if additional slots are available there will be no restrictions on bookings this policy ensures that users from various groups have access to the facility samples must be submitted at least one day in advance although two days is preferred prior to the scheduled appointment date in the event of an emergency that prevents timely submission please notify the operator via email providing a valid reason for the delay please ensure that samples are uhv compatible proper labelling of samples for xps analysis is crucial for obtaining reliable results this includes providing the user’s name booking details sample name the elements present and the specific core levels to be examined eg cu p n s etc the requirements for depth profile measurement in xps analysis include specifying the ar ion energy from ev to kev and the etchingsputtering time additionally all questionnaire information required to be filled at the time of booking must be complete otherwise the operator will reject the booking slots best regards pankaj srivastava facility coordinator thanks manidipa manidipa banerjee phd head central research facilities professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi website

Body: view this post on the web at science quotes from freeman dyson’s is science mostly driven by ideas or by tools the physical sciences have alternated between revolutions driven by new ideas and explorations driven by new tools karl popper the logic of scientific discovery a scientist whether a theorist or experimenter puts forward statements or systems of statements and tests them step by step in the field of the empirical sciences more particularly he constructs hypotheses or systems of theories and tests them against experience by observation and experiment i suggest that it is the task of the logic of scientific discovery or the logic of knowledge to give a logical analysis of this procedure that is to analyse the method of the empirical sciences in that case karl popper would call something like fluids experiments a science freeman dyson origins of life cambridge university press the third and fourth names on my list of illustrious predecessors are those of manfred eigen and leslie orgel unlike schrödinger and von neumann they are experimenters they are explorers of experimental approaches to the problem of the origin of life eigen and his colleagues in germany did experiments that showed us biological organisation originating spontaneously and evolving in the test tube what precisely they demonstrated was that a solution of nucleotide monomers will under suitable conditions give rise to a nucleic acid polymer molecule that replicates and mutates and competes with its progeny for survival from a certain point of view one might claim that these experiments already achieved the spontaneous generation of life from nonlife they brought us at least to the point where we could ask and answer questions about the ability of nucleic acids to Subject: france wants sovereignty germany just wants a receipt
Body: view this post on the web at ukraine is a special purpose vehicle germany and france are now pitching for “symbolic” benefits for ukraine it would be some kind of ‘freetrial’ tier that offers the taste without any of the costs far from its wishes kyiv is being presented as a special purpose vehicle for european security not a candidate to the single market since europe has anxiously watched its eastern frontiers for russian threats the invasion was just a reminder of old fear to contain russia europe wants to keep ukraine as a buffer while avoiding the shock of having it actually become an eu member fiscal drain ukraine’s scale would redirect a great deal of eu subsidies away from other eastern members grain wars kyiv’s lowcost agricultural production threatens the delicate rules that pacify french and polish farmers new power as a voting member ukraine could veto francogerman initiatives governance significant concerns regarding the rule of law remain a barrier to entry that’s not to speak of the nine other candidates waiting in line eu members don’t really want ukraine as a member for now kyiv will probably stay peripheral they want it to stand guard on the porch but not enter the bloc’s core economic and political machinery nextgen of debt with orbán gone the eu can finally send out € bn in funding to ukraine the loans are just enough to keep ukraine afloat for a few months and spur some military spending but it is one step further to turning the eu into a fiscal state the loan is raised as eu borrowing — meaning every member is liable to repay it nextgenerationeu debt was a controversial solution to the economic shock of the pandemic today it is becoming oddly normal since the recent ukraine loan almost € bn has been borrowed in this way as each european state is fiscally squeezed it has found a bit more headroom with the structure of the eu with high levels of demand for what is still understood as highquality debt it’s not hard to imagine the future in the event of an emergency they will prob drink from the same untapped well subsidising the rhine with ohio g tmobile us and majority owner deutsche telekom are considering whether they should merge into a transatlantic telecoms gigachad the former german monopoly acquired the company at the peak of the dotcom bubble in it wasn’t a great deal sucking away profits from the german business in they even failed to sell off the us business after an antitrust block yet today most of dt’s valuation us unit is bythe operator group’s total value comes from its share in tmobile after a successful lead in midband g it’s now at the point of subsidising the european obligation — a reversal of when they had to bail out the us unit in a podcast earlier this year deutsche telekom chief executive tim höttges explained the advantage of access to us growth and railed against european regulation he explained that in europe they had to deal with hundreds of regulators across markets france wants sovereignty germany just wants a receipt it looks as if attempts to tweak the eu’s trade agreement with the us cooked the european parliament and france have called to change the deal the eu chief ursula von der leyen signed with trump last july the deal scrapped tariffs on hundreds of us industrial and agricultural goods for the privilege of a tariff on the eu the amendments were to allow for more wiggle room accounting for some little incidents since last year — like the us attempting to eat greenland and the us supreme court striking down us tariff powers germany leads the nochange majority it’s likely that the council of the eu which comprises the bloc’s member states will not amend the deal france is sceptical in line with its gaullist tradition germany however whose larger economy depends on exports wants to keep them flowing the us remains the number one destination for german engineering for now economic scaries keep the trade deal in place populism meet your chief financial officer last week the leaders of medef — france’s largest union of employers yes even businesses have a union in france — met with the nationalist leader jordan bardella in paris the immediate backlash was of no surprise medef is an institution endowed with legal powers especially over workers rules many claimed that the business lobby was bowing to some rightwing nut but the union made it clear it had held similar talks with its farleft counterpart lfi this is much more an opportunity for the new political parties to temper their politics there are all kinds of veto players in french politics from the unions to the eu they might as well get to know each other in practice no president can easily pass major labour reforms without at least some tacit consent from medef in when mitterrand came to power with a socialistcommunist coalition many saw a red invasion as promised he pushed huge spending nationalisations and sweeping tax and labour reform but facing soaring inflation and a collapsing franc he pivoted by he imposed austerity across the state a politically costly move this is the golden cage theory all kinds of extreme politics might stumble into power but once they smack into economic reality and treaties they quickly come to their senses i doubt the new ascendants will be immune sightly heavyhanded suggestion from le monde Subject: the wrong panic
Body: view image caption quick question before we get into this vishal dhupar who runs nvidias india business spoke at our ai summit at masters union last week and he narrated a small story about jensen huang who founded nvidia before ai nvidia was a graphics chip company they made the processors that drew graphics inside video games and there was no particular reason to believe the company would ever do anything else in jensen made a decision that nearly broke nvidia he spent years and billions of dollars building a piece of software called cuda which is a set of instructions that lets a programmer tell a graphics chip to do something other than draw a game think of it as the translator between ordinary code and a very specialised kind of chip cuda sat on nvidias balance sheet as dead weight for six years with investors begging jensen to shut it down then came and researchers figured out that the same chips used for video game graphics were weirdly perfect for training a kind of ai called deep learning every ai researcher in the world wanted those chips and the only way to speak to them was cuda this cuts against almost everything governments are doing about ai right now view image caption what oil taught us iran has been holding the strait of hormuz for fifty years view image caption you would think that makes iran rich the average iranian makes about a year while the average japanese person whose country owns no oil at all makes closer to the countries that got rich from oil were the ones who had somewhere to put it once they bought it electronics factories in japan chemistry labs in germany most countries are walking into the ai economy looking to be iran and india despite being in the one position that could let it avoid that fate is currently one of them view image caption what were fighting over there are five layers to what we now call ai electricity at the bottom then chips factories that manufacture the chips ai models built by frontier labs and on top of all of that the actual uses people put ai to in their work almost every government conversation im in right now is about the middle of that stack because the concentration there is frightening view image follow image link caption the chips themselves are mostly made by one company a taiwanese one called tsmc which happens to sit on an island china claims as its own the rare metals inside those chips are almost entirely refined in china which started weaponising them against the us last december a new chip factory takes five years to build view image caption the layer nobody is panicking about view image caption it is whether your hospital can deploy an ai that reads scans before three years of pilot studies eat the budget whether the law firms in your country have rebuilt around the tool or are still using it as a slightly unreliable intern and whether your government can buy a piece of software without writing a twohundred page tender the answer in most countries is no but this is where all the wealth will come from because people wont lose jobs to ai so much as lose tasks and the boring repetitive parts of every job get absorbed by the tool while whatever the person can do that the tool cant become the thing markets will pay for that is the countryscale question too what is your economy still good for once the chip stops being scarce view image caption where this leaves india we are third in the world in rare earth reserves and produce less than of them and the chip factories we are building today in dholera and sanand will produce chips of a kind the rest of the world was making fifteen years ago we have no asml tsmc or nvidia equivalent and we wont have them this decade the government is running two ai bets at the same time view image follow image link caption the other is the indiaai mission with a fiveyear budget of about ₹ crore which is subsidising shared computing power for indian startups and universities it is fully funding four homegrown startups trying to build indias own ai models sarvam notably received ₹ crore in subsidised nvidia hardware for this and running a national skilling programme both of these are serious programmes but the ratio between them is roughly fifteen to one in favour of manufacturing and yet we have the highest daily chatgpt usage globally a billion industry where indian engineers are already doing the ai work for a lot of the fortune and tcs alone has trained of its employees on these tools the workforce is already ahead of where it needs to be flip that ratio over the next five years match every rupee of chip manufacturing with fifteen spent on compute applicationlayer startups like sarvam rebuilding the procurement systems that stop our hospitals and courts and schools from deploying anything new view image caption that to my mind is a trilliondollar shift in where ai output gets produced and we are currently positioning ourselves to miss it “nandini you might be saying this is convenient india happens to be bad at the things you claim dont matter and good at the things you claim to do and also the government is already doing half of what youre asking for through the indiaai mission” the second point is fair the mission is working and sarvam getting a governmentbacked chance to train a sovereign indian language model is quite significant but ten thousand crore for compute and applications against lakh crore for fabs is a statement of priorities that shows how we still think the value is in the middle of the stack the chips are going to arrive eventually the same way oil became abundant in the s the countries that spent the oil panic buying the resource were not the ones that built the rich industrial economies of the decade that followed india already has the engineers companies and usage that the rest of the world is still trying to build and we are about to spend the next decade solving the wrong problem because we have confused someone elses panic for our own view image caption if you work anywhere near this in a company or in policy reply and tell me what youre seeing i want to know whether im early or just wrong nandini Subject: security advisory beware of phishing emails fake updates and fraudulent kyc links
Body: dear users we would like to alert all users about a noticeable increase in phishing attempts and online fraud involving emails popups messages and malicious links targeting individuals these attacks may appear in various forms including emails containing suspicious links asking you to “verify” “update” or “secure” your account urgent messages claiming account suspension password expiry or unusual activity fake operating system or software update popups prompting you to download or install updates fraudulent kyc know your customer update links impersonating banks telecom providers or government services messages emailsmswhatsapp offering rewards refunds or demanding immediate action please follow these precautions do not click on unknown or suspicious links always verify the sender’s email address and message authenticity avoid downloading attachments from untrusted or unexpected sources do not install updates from browser popups or random prompts always use official system update settings never share passwords otps or personalfinancial information be cautious of messages that create urgency or fear to force immediate action access important services banking kyc etc only through official websites or apps if you receive any suspicious email link or popup do not interact with it report it immediately to the csc at email or your awareness and caution are essential in preventing security incidents stay vigilant and stay safe best regards team csc

examination halls are equipped with synchronized wall clocks there is no requirement to carry personal watches handling of personal belongings if any prohibited items are inadvertently brought they particularly the use or possession of mobile phones will invite strict penalties including the award of an f grade in all courses for the semester your adherence to these guidelines will help maintain
