Subject: a thermodynamics for biology
Body: view this post on the web at thermodynamics relates variables that are observable on a large scale macro to variables of objects that are very small micro the most celebrated result is the maxwellboltzmann distribution given the temperature of an ideal gas this result gives the probability distribution of the speeds of the particles in the gas it’s not obvious to link these two together the temperature is the macro variable and the speeds of the particles are near impossible to observe in isolation why is this important well it’s not easy to observe the speeds of particles in isolation but having a model for the speed distribution of particles then gives us the ability to compute other interesting things like heat capacity diffusion constants and more and these are observable there is one legendary result that uses the distribution to relate the viscosity heat conductivity and heat capacity all in one elementary kinetic theory gives two macroscopic variables viscosity and heat conductivity in terms of microscopic quantities — the number density n the mean speed ⟨v⟩ and the mean free path λ where η is the viscosity κ is the heat conductivity m is the mass per particle and cv is the heat capacity per particle when you take the ratio — all the messy microscopic quantities n ⟨v⟩ λ drop out and you are left with where cv cv m is the specific heat capacity per unit mass so if you measure any two of η κ cv the third is determined — a nontrivial macroscopic prediction that falls out of the microlevel distribution what would an analogous result in biology be last time i used david jordan’s bioreactor to observe the state variables of algae the macro variables here are temperature co concentration o concentration and so on it would be cool to link these variables to genetics which are the micro variables of biology in other words what information does a macro state variable give us about the probability distribution of genetic states in the algae and if we know that distribution can we relate it to any other macro variables that we can observe like behaviour thanks to david jordan for extensive discussions references roberto livi and paolo politi nonequilibrium statistical physics a modern perspective cambridge university press chapter doi chapter gives a clean derivation of the kinetictheory transport coefficients above unsubscribe caution Subject: endsemester exams instruction for students
Body: dear students the endsemester exams start on april th and are till may th including buffer days please note the following important instructions do not bring mobile phones or any other electronic gadgets eg smart watches ipads iwatch etc to the exam venue examples of actions taken in disciplinary committees for students carrying such devices f grades in all courses of the semester suspension for one or more semesters modifications of graduation requirements removal of present past and future pors etc your exam schedule seat number room number all are available at examiitdacin upon kerberos login in case the exam is not scheduled please contact your teacher the seat number will be available only a few hoursminutes before the exam till then the portal will indicate that the seat is allotted or not seat allotments will be done soon please reach your desk before time please carry your id card to the exam hall please sit only at the designated seat if you are found at a different place there will be penalties attached we are very very serious about your exam seat please be ethical in your conduct please remember that you signed an honour code we will be holding your conduct against your honour at the end of the day it is just an exam please try to perform as best you can do not fret if the exam does not go well in life in the long run a singular exam hardly matters students who are eligible and want to avail compensatory time please do not sit at your designated seat but report at lh for students requiring a scribe reach lh no compensatory time will be allowed if you sit at your designated seat students who are eligible but do not want to avail compensatory time nothing to be done please sit at your designated seat if you have had a handfracture for example or have a temporary disability we can help please let us know email or call the oae office iitd will appoint a scribe typically lab staff from your department who will help you with your exam the exam will be held at lh about the igrade if you are seriously ill and miss the exam please follow the steps i inform your teacher before the exam latest by the end of the exam ii apply through studentgeneralrequest under title remajori grade on your eacad portalpl do not raise request in any other title remember if you are availing of an iitd hostel room a medical certificate from iitdhospital is required to certify your inability to come to the exam please initiate the application first then visit the hospital to obtain your medical certificate note that you can raise the igrade request even when you dont have the medical certificate you must attach the medical certificate later when you are asked for it from academic section iii the last date to initiate your igrade application is the last day of exam iv your instructor will need to approve your request based on information you gave himher this will be followed by a final approval from the academic section v remajor for finally approved cases will be conducted in the first week of next semester a few quick notes as to some situations when your igrade request will be denied according to the teacher you do not have enough attendance through the semester to be present at the endsemester exam as per course policy you were actually found present at the exam fever after seeing the exam paper you did not a prior inform your teacher about your absence you had an exam from am but you informed your teacher at am you did not initiate the sgr online before the last day of exam you could not apply online because your fees is pending in such exceptional cases you need to apply on paper please visit ugs by th may you initiated your application online but did not produce a medical certificate even after repeated reminders you did not go to the iitd sick bay or the iitd doctor does not think your illness is serious enough exceptions are always made when you produce a hospital discharge summary to indicate that your condition was serious enough for a hospital admission your medical certificate says that you need to rest for days but you wrote a few exams in that period we check your actual reason for absence was a family emergency but you lied and tried to obtain a medical certificate your medical certificate was electronically doctored disco will be initiated we authenticate every medical certificate please remember the igrade is only for serious medical emergencies this is not a backup option for students who are unprepared frivolous igrade requests trivialize the requirements of those who are actually ill in the past the dean sa office has repeatedly tested the water quality of the hostels to assess if there was any real reason for the stomachupset epidemic during the exam connectors in claude enabling integration with everyday apps like uber spotify and instacart—bringing ai beyond work tools into daily life activities details claude now supports connectors for everyday apps like uber spotify instacart alltrails tripadvisor and turbotax expanding beyond work tools into daily activities such as travel food and entertainment the platform now includes connectors overall allowing users to combine multiple apps in a single conversation—eg planning trips booking services or managing tasks without switching platforms claude can dynamically suggest relevant apps based on user intent—for example recommending hiking routes via alltrails or booking rides via uber directly within the conversation the system is designed with privacy and control in mind ensuring that connected app data is not used for model training and that users must approve actions like purchases or bookings connectors are available across all claude plans with easy setup through a directory interface making integration accessible even for nontechnical users why it matters this moves ai from productivity tools to a unified interface for everyday life where one assistant can manage multiple apps seamlessly it signals a future where ai becomes a central operating layer for daily activities not just workrelated tasks when april source brain anthropic adds builtin memory to claude managed agents at a glance anthropic has introduced builtin memory for claude managed agents enabling ai systems to retain knowledge across sessions and improve performance over time without relying solely on context windows details the new feature introduces persistent crosssession memory allowing agents to store and recall information beyond a single interaction enabling continuity in longrunning workflows memory is implemented as a filebased system memories directory where agents can create read update and delete stored knowledge effectively building experience over time agents can automatically reference stored memory before executing tasks helping them pick up where they left off and avoid repeating mistakes in similar workflows developers can manage memory via apis including reviewing editing or seeding memory stores enabling better control debugging and governance of agent behavior this memory system supports longhorizon tasks where agents summarize context and persist key information overcoming limitations of traditional context windows why it matters memory turns ai agents from stateless tools into learning systems that improve with experience this is a critical step toward truly autonomous agents capable of handling complex longterm workflows with continuity and efficiency when april source laptop alibaba unveils qwen b delivering flagship coding in a compact model at a glance alibaba has released qwen b a dense opensource ai model that delivers toptier coding performance while remaining efficient enough for practical deployment on standard hardware details qwen b is a bparameter dense model meaning it avoids moe complexity and is easier to deploy while still achieving high performance across coding and reasoning tasks despite its relatively smaller size it delivers flagshiplevel coding performance outperforming much larger models like qwen ba b across benchmarks such as swebench and terminalbench the model shows strong agentic coding capabilities enabling it to handle realworld development workflows such as debugging repositorylevel reasoning and multistep problem solving it also supports multimodal reasoning and flexible “thinking modes” allowing developers to switch between faster responses and deeper reasoning depending on the task released with open weights and broad accessibility developers can use it via apis download it locally or deploy it on consumergrade gpus making advanced coding ai more widely usable why it matters qwen b proves that smaller efficient models can rival massive systems shifting focus from scale to optimization it accelerates the trend toward accessible highperformance open ai empowering developers without requiring massive infrastructure when april source robot openai introduces gpt with enhanced reasoning and multimodal capabilities at a glance openai has launched gpt a major upgrade focused on improved reasoning multimodal understanding and more reliable performance across complex realworld tasks details gpt delivers significant improvements in reasoning and problemsolving enabling better handling of complex multistep tasks across domains like coding research and analysis the model expands its multimodal capabilities allowing seamless understanding and generation across text images audio and potentially video making it more versatile for realworld applications it introduces stronger selfcorrection and reliability mechanisms reducing hallucinations and improving accuracy in highstakes tasks through better internal validation gpt is optimized for agentbased workflows supporting longrunning tasks tool usage and autonomous execution within applications and enterprise systems the release includes performance and efficiency improvements balancing higher capability with better cost and latency for scalable deployment gpt‑ is rolling out to plus pro business and enterprise users in chatgpt and codex why it matters gpt represents a step toward more reliable and autonomous ai systems capable of handling realworld complexity it reinforces the trend of ai evolving from assistants to intelligent agents that can reason act and deliver outcomes independently when april source puzzlepiece openai introduces workspace agents in chatgpt at a glance openai has launched workspace agents in chatgpt enabling teams to automate complex multistep workflows using persistent ai agents that can operate across tools and continue working autonomously details workspace agents are designed as an evolution of custom gpts moving beyond simple promptresponse interactions to systems that can autonomously handle complex multistep tasks across team workflows these agents operate inside a dedicated workspace with access to files tools code and persistent memory allowing them to maintain context and execute tasks more effectively over time built on codex and cloudbased infrastructure agents can run continuously in the background—even when users are offline—executing tasks and returning results once completed they are designed for team collaboration enabling workflows like pulling data from multiple systems coordinating across tools eg slack and requesting approvals before completing actions openai plans to allow conversion of existing gpts into workspace agents making it easier for users to transition from simple assistants to fully autonomous workflow systems why it matters workspace agents signal a shift from ai tools to ai teammates that can independently execute work across systems this could redefine productivity where teams delegate tasks to persistent ai agents instead of interacting with chatbased assistants when april source stethoscope openai enhances chatgpt for clinicians with specialized medical capabilities at a glance openai has introduced “chatgpt for clinicians” a specialized version designed to support medical professionals with tasks like documentation research and clinical decision support details openai launched a clinicianfocused version of chatgpt tailored to assist with realworld healthcare tasks such as documentation medical research diagnosis support and patient education materials the system is designed to reduce administrative burden helping clinicians draft notes summarize literature and generate reports—freeing up more time for direct patient care it introduces evidencebased reasoning workflows where the model can review medical literature and compile structured insights even supporting continuing medical education activities in benchmarks like healthbench professional chatgpt for clinicians outperformed base models and even physicianwritten responses highlighting strong performance in clinical reasoning tasks the tool is initially available free for verified healthcare professionals physicians nurse practitioners pharmacists etc signaling openai’s push to expand adoption in clinical environments why it matters this marks a major step toward aiassisted healthcare where clinicians use ai to enhance—not replace—medical decisionmaking it also reflects growing demand for specialized domainspecific ai systems especially in highstakes fields like medicine when april source microscope google introduces deep research max for nextgen autonomous research agents at a glance google has launched deep research max an advanced geminipowered ai agent capable of autonomously conducting deep multistep research and generating comprehensive highquality reports details deep research max is built on gemini pro and represents google’s most advanced research agent designed to plan execute and synthesize complex research tasks across web and private data sources the system operates as a fully autonomous research pipeline iteratively searching reading identifying knowledge gaps and refining queries to produce detailed cited reports rather than simple answers it can perform hundreds of searches up to in a single task and analyze multiple data sources—including enterprise data—before delivering structured insights and conclusions deep research max introduces native visualizations charts and mcp model context protocol support enabling richer outputs and integration with external tools and workflows compared to standard deep research the “max” version prioritizes depth and thoroughness over speed using extended compute cycles to generate more comprehensive and highquality analyses why it matters deep research max signals a shift from searchbased workflows to autonomous research systems that think explore and deliver complete insights it could transform industries like finance biotech and consulting where hours of manual research may be replaced by aidriven analysis pipelines when april source barchart claude can data visualization without manual setup details claude can now generate live dashboards from simple prompts transforming raw data or instructions into interactive visualizations like charts tables and metrics in real time these dashboards are dynamic and updateable meaning users can refine queries adjust data sources or modify visuals without rebuilding everything from scratch the feature is integrated into claude’s artifact and cowork workflows allowing dashboards to exist as live components within broader projects and tasks users can connect data inputs and iterate conversationally introduces “thinking” capabilities where the model reasons about prompts before generating images improving composition accuracy and alignment with complex instructions the system now supports native k resolution outputs delivering sharper visuals with better textures lighting and fine details suitable for professional use cases it integrates web search context allowing the model to incorporate uptodate or referencebased information into generated images when relevant the model significantly improves text rendering and structured layouts making it more reliable for use cases like posters ui mockups and infographics it is designed for iterative workflows enabling users to refine images conversationally while maintaining consistency across edits and variations why it matters chatgpt images moves image generation toward more intelligent and contextaware creation not just visual synthesis it signals a shift where ai combines reasoning generation making outputs more reliable and usable in realworld design workflows when april source rocket kimi k pushes opensource ai forward with advanced coding capabilities at a glance moonshot ai has introduced kimi k a powerful opensource model focused on longhorizon coding and autonomous agent workflows competing with top proprietary models in performance details kimi k is designed for longhorizon coding tasks meaning it can work autonomously perform thousands of tool calls iterate on solutions and improve performance over time without constant human input it shows major improvements in coding accuracy stability and instructionfollowing with benchmarks indicating gains in code quality longcontext reasoning and tool invocation success rates above k supports multimodal inputs text image video and can generate full applications—from frontend interfaces to backend logic—making it useful for realworld development workflows the model is opensource and optimized for costefficient largescale deployment positioning it as a strong alternative to closed models while maintaining competitive performance on coding benchmarks why it matters kimi k shows that opensource ai can now rival top proprietary systems in coding and autonomous execution it accelerates the shift toward agentdriven software development where ai systems can independently build optimize and maintain complex applications when april source brain Subject: it’s ok to be scared
Body: view this post on the web at everyone in the world seems to tell you to assume more risk both from career and personal standpoints here is some shit i keep hearing just everywhere leave your country and move away leave your current partner to find a better partner quit your job and do x startup mission whatever quit your job and travel the world in a dangerous place leave your main research program and try a risky one quit college i think this advice is mostly useless and stupid you should not default to want to take more risk in life for no reason the first reason is the obvious one this is because decisions with risk can go badly sometimes catastrophically things can go wrong by chance like doing a base jump or if you are uncomfortable taking risks then in high stakes situations you won’t be relaxed enough to make good decisions so if this is the case why do people love advertising taking risk so much why do people espouse it as strong advice this is because most people who tell you to take risk are either people who have irrationally more downside than upside taken risk then got lucky and so then start spreading the risk taking world view or they are people who can afford to take risk ie they have rich families a stable immigration situation live in a developed country or live in sf a lot of people are not in the latter camp that’s fine just a fact of life if you are outside your home country then your visa is likely dependent on a job with a required minimum salary or most people have kids and a family they need to support i myself only started to take more risks when i could afford to i built some savings until my immigration situation got more stable if i left my job prematurely and things didn’t work out i’d have to go back to malaysia which would be a fail so it was reasonable to wait on a safety net before taking risks like spending more time blogging and moving to riskier jobs and as you may notice my following has got a Subject: the oyo franchisee paradox
Body: ——————————————————————————— hey folks pratham here welcome back to paradox weekly a masters union newsletter where we break down the ideas trends and contradictions shaping business today theres a hotel in jaipur the owner built the property from scratch when he bought the land hired the staff pays for the electricity bill maintenance and salaries every rupee of capital risk is his view image follow image link caption the money improved and he was understandably happy he also has no idea what his guests are paying as oyo sets the price keeps the booking data and owns the customer relationship when the guest checks out the reconciliation sheet arrives weeks later showing what oyo decided the room was worth that night the hotel owner owns the hotel oyo owns the hotel business todays paradox you can own the building hire the staff absorb all the risk and still not be the hotelier oyo was the hotelier the hotel owners were the real estate ——————————————————————————— the pitch before oyo a room hotel in a tier city ran on word of mouth touts and walkin guests who had no other way to find you occupancy averaged and on a slow week half the rooms sit empty view image follow image link caption what hotel owners didnt see is that in a hotel the price is the only thing that determines whether owning the building is profitable the moment they handed over pricing they handed over the business the building was theirs but everything that makes a building a business now belonged to oyo ——————————————————————————— what the algorithm did oyo runs dynamic pricing across its entire portfolio every airline and hotel chain does this the difference is ownership when marriott cuts a rate they keep what the guest paid but when oyo cut the rate on a hotel it didnt own the hotel owner had no visibility into what the guest paid until the reconciliation sheet arrived sometimes weeks later view image follow image link caption when demand fell prices dropped sometimes well below the floor price the owner had agreed at contract signing vikrant singh owned a room property in bengaluru in late he was making close to in monthly profit by january he was at a monthly loss his rooms were filling but the economics had inverted view image follow image link caption then came the walkin penalty if more than of bookings came from guests who arrived directly rather than through oyo the platform deducted of total turnover a guest who walks in without oyo doesnt generate them data doesnt feed the review system and doesnt justify their take rate every direct booking was a transaction oyo couldnt control so they charged a penalty to stop it the platform that promised to fill empty rooms was fining owners for filling rooms themselves ——————————————————————————— the contract the oyo story usually gets framed as a platform exploiting small hotel owners i personally think that framing misses the point to guarantee ₹ lakh per month to hotels regardless of actual bookings oyo had to claw that money back from somewhere the algorithm undercutting ₹ floors at ₹ the hidden audit charges and the walkin penalty were just ways oyo was trying to fund a guarantee that couldnt be kept at scale hotel owners fighting to preserve the minimum guarantee were fighting to preserve the exact incentive structure that caused the behavior they were fighting against oyo lost ₹ crore in fy on ₹ crore in revenue and the guarantee was why by april hotels across cities had terminated agreements ——————————————————————————— view image follow image link caption ——————————————————————————— the turnaround when covid hit in march oyo invoked force majeure and suspended all guaranteed payments the workforce dropped from to roughly and partner properties contracted from to about by q view image follow image link caption they simply stopped pretending to be a partner and became a brand and distribution layer earning commission on someone elses real estate with no downside from empty rooms thats exactly the pure franchise model hotel owners had been demanding for years ie without any hidden charges or games and yet hotel owners lost the guaranteed income they had traded their pricing control to get the model that stopped destroying hotel owners also produced the lowest number of oyo hotel partners since the company launched oyo thrived but the network it had built did not ——————————————————————————— my read the hotel owners knew the offer was unusual a guaranteed ₹ lakh per month regardless of occupancy to someone who had spent years praying for walkins is the kind of offer you accept before asking how it works the protests came in in when the guarantee stopped paying out by then two years of good occupancy had made the original trade feel normal nobody was filing complaints about oyos pricing control when occupancy was im not saying oyo was clean floor price violations walkin penalty and opaque reconciliation are all legitimate grievances but the ownership illusion was written into the contract that hotel owners signed “which would you choose stability or control“ — i read every email until next week Subject: fluid dynamics for toddlers
Body: view this post on the web at the navierstokes equations are meant to model fluids i think they are cool i met one of my best buds on a beach bringing this up as a conversation topic but he’s now a lawyer anyways they look complicated and scary like seriously the hell is this in the above ρ is the density p is the pressure v is the velocity field μ is the viscosity coefficient and f is any external body force per unit volume — gravity for instance p is the pressure gradient how pressure changes from point to point and ∇² is the second derivative in space the second equation ∇ · v is the incompressibility condition which just says the fluid isn’t being squeezed or stretched anywhere — whatever flows into a region flows out confused yep it’s hard to work with but here’s a more intuitive way to think about it i will show you how you can derive and think about this formula in a more natural way for now i will ignore the incompressibility assumption and the stress tensor and focus on the main meat here goes it all goes back to newton from your high school days you learnt in newtonian mechanics acceleration is equal to the force divided by the mass and acceleration is the derivative of velocity so newton’s laws can be rewritten as so what’s the fluids version of this equation well a fluid isn’t a point mass like in newtonian mechanics it’s a field where every point in space has a value associated at different points in the fluid we have a vector for the direction of the flow a number for the pressure a number for the density and so on so the ‘velocity’ of a fluid is a velocity field where every point in the fluid has a given velocity associated with the flow the velocity at this point is the velocity that a particle would travel if you placed it there this is what the velocity field of a river looks like so how do we think about a ‘derivative‘ of a field if you wanted to measure the derivative of a quantity in a field the most natural approach is to pretend you put some measuring equipment in the flow let it travel and then observe the change in the measuring equipment imagine putting a thermometer in a river and then reading the change in temperature as it flows the change in quantity over time as something moves is called the material derivative it measures the change in some quantity f which is a function of a point in space and time taking into account that the point at which we are measuring changes as well the change over a small time δt is since the point itself is moving with the flow its displacement over δt is δx v δt where v dxdt is the velocity at that point taylor expanding f around xt t don’t worry if the upside down triangles confuse you these are just the derivatives but in three dimensions subtracting fx t dividing by δt and taking δt → the material derivative is the first term is how f changes at a fixed point in space the remaining three are how f changes because the probe is being carried along by the flow — one for each spatial direction weighted by the corresponding component of the velocity so the ‘acceleration’ in fluids space is just the material derivative of the velocity field now what about the other side of the equation well newton said that but we are dealing with a fluid so mass doesn’t make sense instead we should be using the density ρ mass per unit volume and so we have the equation but what is the force on a fluid well it can be whatever the physical situation calls for gravity friction whatever you need but for fluids one force that always appears is the pressure gradient differences in pressure cause particles to move — fluid gets pushed from high pressure to low pressure so the force per unit volume is −∇p putting that in and then we also have friction in fluids friction is known as viscosity this is a bit more technical but david tong has an excellent explanation here about why viscosity takes the form where μ is the viscosity coefficient and ∇² ∂²∂x² ∂²∂y² ∂²∂z² is the laplacian and so we finally have the navierstokes equations or multiplying through by ρ to match the form at the top bingo bango we’re done unsubscribe caution this email originated Subject: suspected spam how do you define success
Body: view image caption hey folks im swati welcome back to my weekly newsletter this newsletter is those conversations what im seeing thinking and what id tell you if we were grabbing coffee this weeks edition is about success but before that ——————————————————————————— a couple of weeks ago i received the inspiring women leader award for excellence in education innovation at the et women conclave and karisma kapoor handed it to me on stage in front of a packed room view image caption when it was over my phone filled up with messages from people i hadnt heard from in years a former manager seniors who had never reached out before and peers sending congratulatory notes youre killing it swati so well deserved i read every one of them and knowing how busy they are it means a lot when they take out two minutes to write that message later when i put my phone down and checked in with myself honestly i realised i wasnt happy in proportion to what the room seemed to think was happening and i’m sure you can relate view image follow image link caption that gap between what the world measures and what moves you is telling you which metric you are running on the metrics i see people build their careers around fall into four categories and all are correct in their own ways view image caption i know business people in india who run businesses worth crores and take home crores a year and despite that nobody outside their industry seem to know them view image caption this is the metric actors and cricketers are built around and increasingly founders too of all four this is the only one that requires an audience to sustain it view image caption their satisfaction comes from leverage over outcomes and more low key they are better it is for their role view image caption this is the metric that correlates least with the other three which is why people working toward it often look like theyre losing on every visible scoreboard i optimize for this hence the fame doesn’t really excite me as it would for someone who is optimising for it ——————————————————————————— niemiec ryan and deci followed postcollege adults and found that people who attained extrinsic goals wealth recognition image showed higher rates of shame anxiety and physical symptoms than those who hadnt these were people who actually got what they were chasing simply put most people end up Subject: making rayleighbénard convection cells
Body: view this post on the web at so today i made rayleigh benard cells this is a cheap demonstration of organising behaviour in a fluid i read about this experiment when reading about lorenz’s history in chaos by gleick lorenz initially derived his chaotic strange attractor when looking at simplified versions of fluid convection i’ll write another post on the theory later for now i’ll write about how to do it and show my results i got silicone gel mica powder a hot plate and a borosilicate petri dish i used cst high temp silicone fluid like this then i just got the regular mica powder from amazon i then put the oil in a borosilicate petri dish a pinch of the mica powder and then mixed it pretty thoroughly to get it even then i heated it the mix using my cheaper hot plate that i got from alibaba at first some discrete cells started to form both and the middle and the sides you can see the boundaries start to form and then after a while the cells start to get really organised even after i cooled it down whilst the experiment is simple i think there are endless interesting questions is it easy to predict or model the size of the cells when it settles do the number of cells depend on how quickly the temperature was increased what temperature do the cells break down and turbulence arises are the number of cells dependent on the steepness of the temperature gradient i also wanted to figure out a better way to automate the process here i was thinking of attaching a camera on bird’s eye view and then doing some image segmentation over a long time periods to see the evolution i also wanted a way to program my hotplate to control the temperature gradients unsubscribe caution this email originated from outside of iit delhi do not click links or open attachments unless you recognize the sender and know the content is safe

Subject: reject to win
Body: view image caption quick question before we get into this the exhaustion most professionals feel right now has nothing to do with ai skills or tools the more i think about it the more i think its the sensation of losing a way of thinking they didnt know they were using and calling the loss by the wrong name for about twenty years professional work was judged mainly on execution you usually needed to produce the work yourself to express any point of view which meant years of learning software writing memos building decks or typing code you couldn’t express taste about anything unless you made it yourself as a result people mostly compared work with others who had similar production skills and that shaped how the field looked then ai happened and the filter dropped now no one needs the decade of training because the decade was training in execution and execution itself is now a series of prompts and the right tool which means your work was never as scarce as the market made it look and the execution moat is no ones view image caption what clients pay for now view image caption a tool can now produce forty versions of a thing in a minute the work is looking at the output and saying in thirty seconds none of these do it again make the colour colder and the type heavier the rejection is the work view image caption most people cant do this at speed they can appreciate good work when they see it and feel when something is off but both of those are softer versions of the real thing view image caption i dont think this skill has a clean name yet its taste plus speed plus articulation plus the psychological willingness to be certain most professional work so far rewarded the opposite patient iterative letssitwithit method that made it expensive when making becomes inexpensive patience stops being thoughtful and starts being paralysis view image caption how most of us think we arrived with a rough instinct sketched reacted to what came out and somewhere in the middle of the making we discovered what we thought the making was the thinking this worked for a century because making was slow enough to think during working on a logo on a typical twoweek timeline meant it was two weeks of the designer figuring out through the making what the logo should be the client was paying for the designer to use the production process as a thinking process ai compressed the thinkingthroughmaking process to zero the tool produces forty options before youve thought through one which means iterating is basically thrashing and not thinking view image caption view image caption the real problem is that their way of thinking requires slow execution and execution is no longer slow the bottleneck is whether you show up already knowing what you think view image caption where the view gets built the people who show up to tools with a stable formed view built it in the unpaid hours reading things nobody asked them to read forming opinions about work in their field that nobody commissioned or staying up too late on a tuesday because they couldnt stop thinking about a problem that wasnt theirs nobody pays you for any of this you do it because something in you wont let the question go thats the split you are either the person who has been doing this for years and your reference library is about to compound in a way nobody tracked on a résumé or you are the person whose relationship with your field was contained inside the working day and the working day has just been automated out from under you you cant manufacture a reference library by deciding tomorrow to build one view image caption your professional identity was loadbearing on paid hours and the paid hours have stopped generating the thing that mattered either you have been or you havent view image caption reply and tell me which one and what youre going to do about it nandini ps hopefully this gives you a real sense of leverage increasing output per person and reducing headcount ——— Subject: an agentic home bioreactor
Body: view this post on the web at this would not be possible without the help of david jordan for whom i am grateful to work with drop david an email at david at livingphysics dot org for enquiries purchasing a bioreactor i tested david jordan’s tabletop bioreactor in my last post i have a day job so need to be able to run experiments whilst i’m out of the house i also realised how painful it is to change parameters in reruns of experiments so i wanted to reduce friction in the whole process and make it much easier to interact with the bioreactor after all the less friction there is the more likely i’ll do stuff so we thought it would be useful to automate the bioreactor so that it can run experiments on its own in an agentic fashion and it would be cool if we could tell it what to do in plain english so instead of writing an experiment with ad hoc code that looks like this… import time import requests bioreactor def settemperaturecelsius float requestspostfbioreactorheater jsontargetc celsius def readod return requestsgetfbioreactorodjsonod def setstirrerrpm int requestspostfbioreactorstirrer jsonrpm rpm def pumpmediaml float requestspostfbioreactorpumpin jsonvolumeml ml def drainml float requestspostfbioreactorpumpout jsonvolumeml ml algae growth experiment hold at c stir at rpm sample od every minutes dilute once od crosses settemperature setstirrer log start timetime while timetime start od readod logappendtimetime start od if od drain pumpmedia timesleep which is hard and annoying wouldn’t it be cool if you could just ask it something like this ‘please loop at different temperatures and measure the photosynthesis rate in increments of making sure that each temperature has enough time to test what you need to test for each loop flicker the light on for seconds on and off’ and so i tried to build a rough version and got it working have a look at the first version which is me telling to change the colours of the led light in the bioreactor that the organisms are exposed to here’s the architecture the bioreactor is controlled by a raspberry pi i enabled ssh on it so that i could access the pi remotely from my laptop on my local network i then installed claude code on the pi david jordan then built an api that could control each of the hardware elements which consist of temperature and gas sensors a lighting element a heating element and an optical sensor to get it agentic i built a model context protocol server on the raspberry pi the model context protocol lets claude ping the api provided that the server is running and to communicate with the bioreactor the easiest way was to run claude code in headless mode at that point claude then converts my plain english commands to api commands that control the bioreactor moving forward the next step is to create a memory file and data log so that the agent can continually refer to the logs of data as it makes decisions that are in line with the human’s commands but this should be easy i’m excited about this for multiple reasons it allows people do do experiments much more easily myself included it also lets people who are less physically able do science do experiments and since i care about biosecurity it fits as a great minimal model in discovering where we should protect ourselves unsubscribe caution this email originated from outside of iit delhi do not click links or open Subject: indian pharma paradox
Body: hey folks pratham here welcome back to paradox weekly a masters union newsletter where we break down the ideas trends and contradictions shaping business today ——————————————————————————— ——————————————————————————— in yusuf hamied made an offer that changed the trajectory of the global aids epidemic ciplas managing director now chairman offered africa the aids tripledrug cocktail for per patient per year at a time when western pharma was charging million africans had hiv and fewer than of them could afford treatment thirtynine multinational companies dropped their lawsuit against south africa the number of africans on treatment went from to million in a decade view image follow image link caption but i disagree with the version of this story we tell ourselves if you see the chronology of events six years later the aids healthcare foundation ran fullpage newspaper ads in india with the headlines cipla tell the truth” and “profit at what cost aids drugs for all” the finding was that cipla was charging indian hiv patients twice more than african patients for the identical pill the company that saved africa from aids had not extended the same courtesy to its own country ——————————————————————————— india supplies of all generic prescriptions filled in the united states of the worlds vaccines come from here view image follow image link caption and yet million indians fall below the poverty line every year because they cannot pay for healthcare million of them specifically from spending on medicines the country that makes the worlds cheapest drugs sends million of its own people into poverty every year paying for them that’s todays paradox let me explain how when you walk into a chemist of whats on the shelf is technically a generic because the patent expired and the molecule is cheap to produce but of those are branded generics the same compound sold under a company trade name priced separately from every other company selling the exact same thing view image caption a study tested drug samples across branded and generic versions and found passed all pharmacopoeia quality tests clinically identical fourteen times the price for the same pill cancer drugs are worse the branded version of doxorubicin mg is times the generic price ——————————————————————————— your doctor prescribed the expensive one because india has medical representatives visiting clinics daily with of all pharma promotional spend going to field force activities the dolo case made the scale visible micro labs allegedly spent ₹ crore gifting doctors including televisions international trips and cash just to prescribe a paracetamol tablet view image follow image link caption the government does have an answer jan aushadhi stores sell unbranded generics at registered ⟨ below market prices but there are over of them against private pharmacies less than of outlets the national medical commission tried mandatory generic prescribing in a policy where doctors write the molecule not the brand and withdrew it within three weeks under industry pressure and i honestly think the way we talk about indias healthcare problem is completely wrong the default argument is that indians cant afford medicine because india is a poor country with an underfunded healthcare system but india already manufactures the cheap version it exists qualitytested and is sitting in a government store near you view image follow image link caption the same companies that humiliated western pharma on behalf of africa built a ₹ crore gifting machine to make sure indian patients never reached the cheap shelf the companies that saved africa from aids are the same ones paying your doctor to prescribe the expensive version simply put this is not a problem of poverty but it is one of incentives a system hasn’t been built that lets cheap drugs reach the patient because too many people between the factory and the prescription make money off the expensive version staying expensive “hit reply do you know where your nearest jan aushadhi store is have you ever actually bought medicine there“ — i read every email until next week pratham ——— you are reading a plain text Subject: ieor seminar series talk by shri gvl satya kumar md centre for railway information systems cris on april
Body: dear all due to some unavoidable circumstances at the speakers end this talk has been postponed we regret the inconvenience caused and will come back with the new date and time best regards prashant dear all we welcome you to an interesting session as a part of the industrial engineering and operations research ieor seminar series our next speaker is shri gvl satya kumar managing director of the centre for railway information systems cris please find the details about the talk and the speaker below date and time friday april from am pm venue me seminar room block iit delhi title ai and operations research for intelligent decision systems in indian railways abstract indian railways ir one of the world’s largest transportation networks manages highly complex passenger and freight operations across a vast infrastructure system the scale and diversity of operations create significant opportunities for applying operations research or artificial intelligence ai and machine learning ml to improve efficiency reliability and service quality the centre for railway information systems cris the it arm of indian railways develops and manages enterpriselevel digital platforms supporting core functions such as ticketing freight operations crew management infrastructure maintenance finance hr and procurement building on these digital foundations cris is enabling datadriven decisionmaking systems through optimisation predictive analytics simulation and aiml this talk will briefly introduce the scale and operational context of indian railways followed by a discussion of the role of cris in developing technology platforms it will then highlight the potential of or and aiml to address complex railway problems such as timetable optimisation optimal asset utilisation conditionbased maintenance and customer service automation selected use cases already implemented include eta prediction loco and crew optimisation waitlist prediction nlpbased complaint processing and search and aienabled cleanliness monitoring ongoing work includes digital twinbased simulation precision timetabling route optimisation and asset failure prediction with iit delhi amongst others future opportunities include aiassisted traffic control intelligent capacity utilisation workforce analytics and financial planning models the talk illustrates how or and ai methods can support largescale public systems in achieving improved operational efficiency better resource utilisation and enhanced passenger experience biography shri gvl satya kumar is the managing director of the centre for railway information systems cris the it arm of indian railways responsible for the development and management of enterprise information systems supporting passenger services freight operations infrastructure management and organisational processes he is an officer of the indian railway traffic service irts with extensive experience in railway operations transportation planning evidencebased decision making and digital transformation he holds a bachelor’s degree in electronics engineering from the iit madras and an mba from the university of melbourne over his career in indian railways he has held diverse leadership roles across operations commercial management and strategic planning contributing to initiatives to improve capacity utilisation operational efficiency and service delivery in a large and complex transportation network including railways and ports at cris he is guiding the adoption of emerging technologies including operations research artificial intelligence machine learning and advanced analytics to enable datadriven decisionmaking across core railway functions his work focuses on leveraging digital platforms and optimisation techniques to enhance operational performance improve customer experience and support evidencebased policy and planning in indian railways thanks and best regards prashant palkar assistant professor ieor department of mechanical engineering iit delhi

Subject: ieor seminar series talk by shri gvl satya kumar md centre for railway information systems cris on april
Body: dear all we welcome you to an interesting session as a part of the industrial engineering and operations research ieor seminar series our next speaker is shri gvl satya kumar managing director of the centre for railway information systems cris please find the details about the talk and the speaker below date and time friday april from am pm venue me seminar room block iit delhi title ai and operations research for intelligent decision systems in indian railways abstract indian railways ir one of the world’s largest transportation networks manages highly complex passenger and freight operations across a vast infrastructure system the scale and diversity of operations create significant opportunities for applying operations research or artificial intelligence ai and machine learning ml to improve efficiency reliability and service quality the centre for railway information systems cris the it arm of indian railways develops and manages enterpriselevel digital platforms supporting core functions such as ticketing freight operations crew management infrastructure maintenance finance hr and procurement building on these digital foundations cris is enabling datadriven decisionmaking systems through optimisation predictive analytics simulation and aiml this talk will briefly introduce the scale and operational context of indian railways followed by a discussion of the role of cris in developing technology platforms it will then highlight the potential of or and aiml to address complex railway problems such as timetable optimisation optimal asset utilisation conditionbased maintenance and customer service automation selected use cases already implemented include eta prediction loco and crew optimisation waitlist prediction nlpbased complaint processing and search and aienabled cleanliness monitoring ongoing work includes digital twinbased simulation precision timetabling route optimisation and asset failure prediction with iit delhi amongst others future opportunities include aiassisted traffic control intelligent capacity utilisation workforce analytics and financial planning models the talk illustrates how or and ai methods can support largescale public systems in achieving improved operational efficiency better resource utilisation and enhanced passenger experience biography shri gvl satya kumar is the managing director of the centre for railway information systems cris the it arm of indian railways responsible for the development and management of enterprise information systems supporting passenger services freight operations infrastructure management and organisational processes he is an officer of the indian railway traffic service irts with extensive experience in railway operations transportation planning evidencebased decision making and digital transformation he holds a bachelor’s degree in electronics engineering from the iit madras and an mba from the university of melbourne over his career in indian railways he has held diverse leadership roles across operations commercial management and strategic planning contributing to initiatives to improve capacity utilisation operational efficiency and service delivery in a large and complex transportation network including railways and ports at cris he is guiding the adoption of emerging technologies including operations research artificial intelligence machine learning and advanced analytics to enable datadriven decisionmaking across core railway functions his work focuses on leveraging digital platforms and optimisation techniques to enhance operational performance improve customer experience and support evidencebased policy and planning in indian railways thanks and best regards prashant palkar assistant professor ieor department of mechanical engineering iit delhi

Subject: me guest talk by dr pranav agrawal university of california los angeles ucla
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the me guest talk by dr pranav agrawal university of california los angeles ucla the schedule title and brief information are as follows date nd april time pm venue me seminar room ii title modeling complex structural systems from cableharnessed structures to water distribution networks abstract modern engineering challenges require highfidelity modeling and sensing frameworks to understand and manage the behavior of complex structural systems this research presentation explores two distinct yet fundamentally related research domains the dynamics of continuum structures with cable harnesses and the application of acoustic sensing for leak localization in urban water distribution networks the first part of the presentation addresses a critical gap in structural dynamics how nonstructural components specifically cable harnesses influence the dynamics of host structures such as beams and plates while often treated as lumped mass elements these cables significantly alter modal characteristics of the host system this presentation presents the analytical and experimental frameworks developed during my doctoral research to quantify these effects and provide an understanding of cableharnessed systems transitioning from structural characterization to infrastructure resilience the second part of the presentation focuses on my recent work on urban water distribution networks here we address the global crisis of nonrevenue water losses by developing advanced acoustic sensing and probabilisticbased frameworks i will discuss the methodologies used to localize and pinpoint leaks within complex underground environments transforming failing infrastructure into resilient datadriven systems by bridging the gap between fundamental structural modeling and applied infrastructure monitoring this work underscores the role of mechanical insights in building the next generation of resilient systems bio pranav agrawal is a postdoctoral scholar at the sensing and robotics for infrastructure sri lab at the university of california los angeles ucla he currently leads multiple research initiatives focused on the detection and localization of leaks in underground water distribution networks using advanced acoustic sensing and signal processing dr agrawal earned his phd in mechanical and mechatronics engineering from the university of waterloo in specializing in the vibrations of continuous systems for space applications following a btechmtech dual degree from iit kanpur in his research is featured in articles in prestigious journals including publications from asme asce and springer and has earned recognition from the acoustical society of america and the ucla chancellors office he is also deeply passionate about pedagogy having completed multiple teaching and learning certificate programs and successfully developed and delivered undergraduate and graduate courses at the university level his professional background includes an industrial tenure as an rd technical manager in the noise vibration and harshness nvh division at tata motors limited pune all interested are welcome to join the talk thanks and regards dr abhishek das assistant professor department of mechanical engineering iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india email phone

Subject: re seminar announcement nithya bashyam intel apr bharti
Body: reminder seminar today at on preeti ranjan panda wrote seminar announcement title challenges in scaling memory bandwidth in modern socs speaker nithya bashyam intel datetime thursday april am venue bharti abstract memory bandwidth scaling has emerged as a critical bottleneck as compute capabilities continue to grow faster than dram performance this talk examines why higher memory frequencies do not directly translate to higher delivered bandwidth focusing on bandwidth efficiency rather than peak bandwidth it discusses key constraints arising from dram organization timing parameters power reliability and security and highlights the roles of memory controllers soc architecture and workload behavior the talk provides a framework to understand the architectural trade‑offs involved in sustaining memory bandwidth scaling in modern socs biography a principal engineer in client soc performance architecture at intel nithya bashyam holds an mtech in electronics design from cedt iisc he joined intel in initially working on front‑end design for two years before moving in to the cpu soc architecture team he contributed to the industry’s first cpu with integrated graphics and memory controller on sandy bridge released in followed by work on a few generations of server cpus since skylake he has focused on client cpus working across the core‑to‑memory path including cache ring memory controllers and aspects of the io subsystem he has led memory subsystem performance for several generations of client socs and led soc performance for lunar lake and panther lake

Body: today is my last day at github i’ve been here for years i got promoted to senior engineer built the first version of our ai support system and helped other engineers across the org figure out how to ship mature llm solutions github gave me credibility in this industry and i genuinely valued every part of it but over the past year i started noticing something i couldn’t ignore companies are replacing entire parts of the software development lifecycle with ai agents and not just code generation review testing deployment decisions even architectural choices are being handed to agents with less and less human oversight i wanted to do something direct about it so i accepted a role at an ai safety research lab in london where i’ll be building monitoring systems that catch the failures these agents introduce before they reach production i start next week the role is inperson more demanding than anything i’ve done before and honestly i’m a bit nervous but i also know this is the right move i’ll tell you more about it when i get started for now i just wanted to share this moment with you because you’ve been following this journey zen ps one thing worth knowing at the end of this month my ai native engineer program goes from to forever if you are a member now you keep the old price forever starting a role like this means i have less time to coach and the pricing needs to reflect the proven value i deliver if you’ve been thinking about joining now is a good time to lock in forever ​become a confident highpaid ai engineer ​ ​ ​unsubscribe ​ caution this email originated from outside of iit delhi do not click links or open attachments unless you recognize the sender and know the content is safe

Subject: suspected spam who to take advice from
Body: view image caption hey folks im swati welcome back to my weekly newsletter this newsletter is those conversations what im seeing thinking and what id tell you if we were grabbing coffee this weeks edition is about taking advice but before that ——————————————————————————— while exploring options after graduating from iit delhi i had a chance to get into iim bangalore my family and several seniors id spoken to were saying the same thing go but one senior i respected a lot told me not to and i listened to her looking back i realized that the seniors pushing iimb were all iim alumni the one who had gone to harvard for her mba didnt push it and the one who went straight to mckinsey didnt push it either i had all the voices i needed when i was tilting towards iim i realised that i was weighing heavily one persons authority eg a professor or my parents without examining whether their reasoning for that specific decision applied to my situation and i see this often view image caption a few years ago my father sat me down and explained how hed built his career he came from a place of good intention based on his experience he told me to stay loyal to one organization build steadily within a structure and let tenure do the talking the career landscape he navigated in stable long tenures hierarchical progression loyalty repaid with security has shifted considerably since then the bureau of labor statistics put median job tenure at years in the lowest in two decades view image follow image link caption my father’s advice was built on a world he knew well one that had already shifted by the time i was making those decisions people advising you arent being careless their brain finds a match from their own experience and stops searching thats how expertise works but the problem is when the match no longer fits the world youre in view image follow image link caption most people treat advice the way i treated inputs about iimb decision they find one source they trust weigh it disproportionately and stop there when i ask students who they spoke to its always the people who have made that choice without knowing what the other side is they got one perspective five times and mistook the repetition for consensus view image follow image link caption and when advice does come from varied sources people tend to discard whatever cuts against what they already lean toward the input that confirms the existing instinct feels like validation and the one that contradicts it feels like the person doesnt understand the situation the research shows why averaging works better than choosing but most people never get there they pick one voice commit to it and move on and the voice they tend to give the most weight to is usually the most confident one which turns out to be the one least likely to have considered alternatives so the advice you receive from your most trusted senior is often the advice least likely to account for possibilities they havent considered view image follow image link caption theres also a cost to the decision you didnt really own when a choice you deferred to someone else turns out badly the regret is heavier because the regret belongs to a decision that was never fully yours a few things id do differently view image caption a senior who navigated your industry ten years ago has a different vantage point from someone who made a similar move last year someone who stayed in india sees things differently from someone who relocated and a corporate lifer weighs tradeoffs differently from someone who built something from scratch the goal is to hold your own judgment against enough different frames that you can see where it holds and where it doesnt view image caption most career advice is survivorship testimony the person giving it followed a particular path it worked for them and theyre reporting what worked which may or may not apply to your context right now before you act on advice ask when was this formed what was the market like when this person made their choices does the underlying logic hold in or does it depend on conditions that no longer exist advice built on the old model can sound completely sensible and still be wrong for today view image caption when you disagree with someone you respect theres a pull toward finding permission you want to locate someone who agrees so the responsibility feels distributed the problem is that a decision made to satisfy other peoples approval rather than your own judgment leaves you without the psychological ownership that makes you commit to it and work through the hard parts if youve gathered the input evaluated what each perspective is assuming and still landed somewhere different from what the people around you recommended that decision is yours to make and yours to live with a good relationship survives a career disagreement just remember your career is yours to build and the advice you receive is one of many inputs Subject: how to get cheaper lab equipment
Body: view this post on the web at one problem for independent scientists is cost lab equipment is expensive but you can get much cheaper lab equipment by buying direct from china you can also buy second hand or through secondary auctions but i’ve found this harder i’ve been ordering a lot of lab equipment from alibaba or aliexpress when i first scanned through these websites the prices were so low that i thought that most of the stuff wouldn’t work or be of low quality but for my lab equipment at least i’ve been wrong most of the stuff i’ve got so far works fine to do this i try to find things that have legit looking reviews and are not obvious scams to tell what is an obvious scam i ask claude if the price is reasonable given the cost of components and i usually get an idea of what’s completely fake this has now become the default way i buy equipment i’ve been so impressed that i now suspect that european companies buy from alibaba stick a tag on and jack up the price for example i wanted to buy a magnetic stirrer and hot plate for my chemistry experiments but the main scientific providers price this at around bucks but on aliexpress i looked around and found the same thing for bucks and free shipping the reviews looked decent and it’s literally a fifth of the cost a fifth it arrived in a couple of days and works fine shipping was just as fast as anything on amazon take a look on alibaba i can also request for custom parts and they arrive fine as well here i’m bartering for a custom far uvc bandpass filter which they quoted bucks this would usually be bucks if i ordered it from an optics company in the uk the customer service is better and the reps usually speak perfect english it came fine wild surely this is a no brainer i am not sponsored by endorsing or nonendorsing anyone in this post unsubscribe caution this email originated from outside of iit delhi do not click links or open attachments unless you recognize the sender and know the content is safe

Subject: seminar announcement nithya bashyam intel apr bharti
Body: seminar announcement title challenges in scaling memory bandwidth in modern socs speaker nithya bashyam intel datetime thursday april am venue bharti abstract memory bandwidth scaling has emerged as a critical bottleneck as compute capabilities continue to grow faster than dram performance this talk examines why higher memory frequencies do not directly translate to higher delivered bandwidth focusing on bandwidth efficiency rather than peak bandwidth it discusses key constraints arising from dram organization timing parameters power reliability and security and highlights the roles of memory controllers soc architecture and workload behavior the talk provides a framework to understand the architectural trade‑offs involved in sustaining memory bandwidth scaling in modern socs biography a principal engineer in client soc performance architecture at intel nithya bashyam holds an mtech in electronics design from cedt iisc he joined intel in initially working on front‑end design for two years before moving in to the cpu soc architecture team he contributed to the industry’s first cpu with integrated graphics and memory controller on sandy bridge released in followed by work on a few generations of server cpus since skylake he has focused on client cpus working across the core‑to‑memory path including cache ring memory controllers and aspects of the io subsystem he has led memory subsystem performance for several generations of client socs and led soc performance for lunar lake and panther lake

Body: dear all dr kapil vaswani will be delivering a talk tomorrow at pm in bharti on the state of confidential computing hope to see you all there best svs title state of confidential computing abstract over the last decade confidential computing has emerged as an advanced security and privacy primitive that can fundamentally change the nature of trust that we place in digital services in this talk we will take a journey through the evolution of confidential computing and understand its current state and open problems that will need to be solved towards the end i will introduce sparc a new research center working at the intersection of ai and security and our view of the opportunities that confidential computing creates for building the next generation of ai systems bio kapil vaswani is the founder of sparc he is a security researcher with years of experience in research spanning computer architecture programming languages systems hardware security and ai security at microsoft research he led research on problems in confidential computing privacypreserving ai database security supply chain security and formally verified hardware his research has been published in many top tier conferences such as popl pldi asplos micro osdi oakland and usenix security his work directly led to several products at microsoft including sql server always encrypted azure confidential gpu vms azure ai confidential inferencing azure confidential clean rooms and ad selection api in his capacity as a volunteer with ispirt he has led the development of the depa inferencing and training framework ​kapil vaswani has a masters and phd from the indian institute of science bangalore

Subject: back to inperson
Body: view image caption quick question before we get into this two months ago bier predicted that imessage phone calls and gmail would become functionally unusable within days view image follow image link caption bier runs product at x he was looking at what ive been watching in my work with founders opensource tools that clone a voice from three seconds of audio deployed at scale for almost no cost were about days into his timeline now ive been getting calls from founders trying to figure out what this actually changes about how communication works beyond the deepfake scam angle everyones already covering honestly growing up i hated when people would call the landline and quiz you asking “pehchana” i keep thinking about something that seems kinda related how do we verify that anyone is who they say they are view image caption what we built without noticing for twenty years your phone number was your identity when mom called you saw mom on the screen and that was enough when your cfo emailed from their work address you trusted it was them or when a colleague appeared on video looking and sounding like your colleague you assumed they were your colleague we never had to think of these as verification systems because nothing could convincingly fake them view image follow image link caption what’s worth noticing here is that the employee wasnt careless he was on a video call with people who looked and sounded exactly like his colleagues confirming instructions in real time he basically did what any of us would have done view image caption what im seeing ive been watching this play out across a few different industries at once view image follow image link caption at one recruiting firm in dallas inperson interview requests jumped from to in a single year some companies adding inperson steps are seeing sharper dropoff in the process a pattern that fits broader hiring data showing candidates often ghost employers during interviews the global events industry hit trillion last year growing nearly of executives increased their meeting budgets online made physical presence feel premium now its becoming the only verification that holds view image caption the avatar paradox the same technology eroding trust in video is creating a new category of productivity tools klarnas ceo sent an ai double to deliver his quarterly update our pgp acceptance emails had personalised video messages for each student using the same technology heygen lets you send a clone to multiple zoom calls where it can think talk and answer from your knowledge base synthesia says users created ai avatars of themselves last year view image follow image link caption i dont know exactly where this settles but the direction seems clear enough oneway communication goes to the avatar you show up for the moments that require thinking together in real time or where presence itself is the point view image caption what this means for education i watch this constantly the association of chartered certified accountants announced it will scrap remote exams entirely view image follow image link caption airelated misconduct now represents over of all academic cheating cases remote verification broke and going back in person is the most direct response to that and the same thing is happening in hiring gartner predicts that by one in four job candidate profiles will be fake already of it leaders say their company has hired a fraudulent candidate education and hiring are just the places where it showed up first both run entirely on being able to verify that a person can do what they claim they can do view image caption the devils advocate maybe none of this matters as much as i think email didnt die from phishing and phone calls didnt die from robocalls every communication technology has faced an abuse crisis and eventually reached some version of equilibrium a single researcher built a synthetic interview identity in minutes with consumer hardware even as deepfake‑detection and identity‑verification startups are raising hundreds of millions maybe we end up somewhere familiar with more friction and more verification steps but the same underlying channels view image caption code words agreed with the family in advance or video calls that require a quick authentication step before anything sensitive gets discussed it is more friction but a manageable version of it view image caption where the new stack is being built in january the nsa published a report recommending that government agencies adopt something called content credentials the standard was built by a coalition that includes google openai adobe and microsoft among others the way it works is simple every digital file carries a cryptographically signed record of who made it when and what tools were used and it is being fasttracked as an iso standard this year meanwhile the identity verification market has crossed billion view image follow image link caption the underlying bet across all of it is that proving who you are is about to become as fundamental as having an internet connection both tracks are trying to close the same gap and neither has done it yet view image caption what im telling founders content provenance and identity verification look like two separate markets but they are trying to answer the same question and whoever builds the infrastructure that answers both simultaneously is building what the arup employee needed vouched launched something called know your agent this year which is designed to verify ai agents the same way you would verify a human because the next version of this problem is not just fake people on video calls but ai agents acting on your behalf inside systems that still trust them by default that is a harder problem than the one everyone is already working on the infrastructure is still being assembled with content provenance and human identity verification developing as separate stacks and the layer that connects them at the moment of a transaction or a conversation has not been built yet view image caption reply and tell me if youre building around this or what youre seeing that im not
