Subject: onecredit course asv floated at cas
Body: dear students prof atul jain visiting professor at cas and distinguished alumnus awardee has floated a onecredit course asv special topics in climate carbon cycle as it relates to climate the course description is given below the course will run at pm on th th th th th st nd rd and th april venue cas seminar room vi if you are interested in taking the class auditing or sitting through phd students who completed the coursework can also join respond to this email or report at pm on monday course brief description carbon is in most things around us people plants trees soil oceans and even the air we breathe there is only a certain amount of carbon in on and around earth the total amount of carbon remains constant it changes from one form to another this is called the carbon cycle in the context of climate change the carbon cycle is critically important because it regulates the amount of carbon dioxide the most important greenhouse gas in this short course we will examine how the carbon cycle functions explore natural and human influences on the global carbon cycle and consider actions to mitigate climate change course outline lecture to understand how the climate system changes we first examine its workings and how it depends on factors influenced by natural and human forcings lecture it examines various ways in which earths climate can be changed first we examine how earths climate has undergone considerable changes throughout the geological past we discuss the evidence of climate change during the geological past prior to the period of instrumental measurements we will then examine co concentrations temperature and other instrumental records to assess how humans have influenced earths climate over the past years lectures and we will begin with the importance of the carbon cycle and its role in predicting historical and future climate change and its impacts we will also examine how rapidly carbon dioxide is increasing in the atmosphere and which human sources are contributing to this increase you will also learn about the major reservoirs of the carbon cycle lectures and you will learn about the ocean carbon cycle particularly the processes that transfer carbon between the atmosphere the ocean mixed layer and the deep ocean we will also examine how rock weathering removes co from the atmosphere and the ocean system lecture we will examine the functioning of the terrestrial carbon cycle we will begin with the processes that transfer carbon between the atmosphere vegetation and soil we will then examine how gross primary production net primary production and ecosystem production are related and how they constrain primary production locally and globally lectures we will examine the global carbon budget we will begin by quantifying the amount of co released into the atmosphere from fossil fuel combustion and deforestation next we will look at where all the carbon dioxide emissions are going we will discuss current methods for estimating the global carbon budget finally we will examine productionbased and consumptionbased approaches to carbon control in forestry and agriculture prof sagnik dey head centre for atmospheric sciences vipula and mahesh chaturvedi chair professor in policy studies indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india fellow american geophysical union adjunct professor Subject: me guest talk by dr debjit kundu lead engineer at ge aerospace
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the me guest talk by dr debjit kundu lead engineer at ge aerospace the schedule title and brief information are as follows date nd april time pm venue me seminar room ii title aerosols in asymmetric airways in health and in disease abstract deposition of inhaled particles within the lungs is a critical factor mediating the spread of airborne infections and the efficacy of pulmonary drug delivery particle trajectories in the human respiratory tract are strongly influenced by the unique anatomical features of each individual contributing to considerable intersubject variability in infection susceptibility and therapeutic outcomes this variability alongside differences in host immune responses explains why individuals exposed to similar viral loads can exhibit divergent clinical manifestations from asymptomatic to severe pneumonia and why inhaled treatments show varied efficacy across patients in this work we develop and employ physicsbased reducedorder models of the human airways to investigate the flow physics governing these structurefunction relationships our results elucidate key mechanisms controlling particle transport and deposition patterns that drive differential drug delivery efficiency and infection risk among individuals additionally we analyze how obstructive airway diseases modulate local airflow dynamics modifying particle deposition and potentially altering infection progression and treatment effectiveness this work provides new insights into the complex interactions between respiratory fluid mechanics anatomy and disease with implications in personalized inhalation therapy design and infection control brief bio dr debjit kundu is a lead engineer at ge aerospace where he works on thermal management and transport processes in advanced engineering systems he received his phd in applied mechanics and biomedical engineering from iit madras as a prime ministers research fellow pmrf and holds a bachelors degree in mechanical engineering from jadavpur university where he worked on numerical simulations of combustion and heat transfer his research lies at the intersection of fluid mechanics transport phenomena and computational modeling with a particular focus on transport in complex branched systems during his doctoral work he developed physicsbased reducedorder models of the human respiratory system to investigate how airway branching asymmetry influences aerosol transport pulmonary drug delivery and airborne viral infection dynamics his current interests include extending these fundamental concepts to broader transport problems across both biological and engineered networked systems all interested are welcome to join the talk thanks and regards dr abhishek das assistant professor department of mechanical engineering iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: so my friend made me a bioreactor
Body: view this post on the web at drop david an email at david at livingphysics dot org for enquiries my friend david jordan built me a modular bioreactor it ended up being really easy to use and it works on my desk top at home here are my notes on testing it a bioreactor is something that monitors and controls biological media this allows us to do experiments in a controlled environment bioreactors traditionally are a complicated and expensive piece of equipment but the awesome thing that david did was to make one that’s super easy to use that fits on my table here it is with my finger for scale… david’s bioreactor has a compartment to put a vial of biological media inside it then there’s a gas sensor that screws on top to complete the seal once the vial is inside the compartment there are sensors to measure things and also pieces that control the environment like light and heat the sensors and the environment components are all connected to a raspberry pi which can be automated or operated remotely this particular bioreactor has a few sensors a co concentration sensor an o concentration sensor a temperature sensor an optical density sensor to see how cloudy the water is to track population growth then there are components that change the environment of the vial there is a heating element to control the temperature there is an led to expose the vial inside to light the sensors heating element and led are connected to a raspberry pi computer on the pi theres a python script that records the reading of each element david wrote a script but it’s fully customisable and you can ssh into it too like a regular server robot lab geeks take note for the first experiment i put some algae in some growth media to prevent contamination i used my cheaper laminar flow hood which pumps out hepa filtered air over the workspace here’s a picture of me getting the algae out then i put the algae in growth media and then screwed the gas sensor on top sliding the vial into the compartment then i turned the bioreactor on by hooking up the raspberry pi to a monitor keyboard and mouse overall super easy to set up you can see the measurements on the monitor the first thing to try was turn the light on and off in hour cycles this was done with a python script which also was used to regulate the temperature so i started the bioreactor turned on the sensors turned on the light cycle and the heating element kept the system at constant temperature and what did i observe the algae did photosynthesis and respiration the graph shows the oxygen and co concentration during the periods where the light was off and on the dark region shows when it’s off when it’s dark in the beginning you can see the co rising and the oxygen concentration falling and then it’s light it flips pretty cool the co eventually goes to zero but you can see the oxygen concentrations fluctuate the optical density plot is a proxy for the density of the species which is also recorded and you can see also that the bioreactor kept the temperature constant pretty well above all this bioreactor was super easy to set up and easy to use it makes me feel excited about the possibilities of being able to do science more easily i’m also more optimistic about the role of table top safe experiments for independent scientists david and i have spoke about the modularity of this design i think a bioreactor has a cool interpretation in that you’re viewing life forms not as themselves but through the macro variables of the environment that they are in i’ve written a lot about state variables and phase space both in thermodynamics and biology and think there are a whole host of interesting things to explore along these lines with a bioreactor on your table top Subject: evaluating job offer
Body: view image caption hey folks im swati welcome back to my weekly newsletter this newsletter is those conversations what im seeing thinking and what id tell you if we were grabbing coffee this weeks edition is about how to pick a job but before that ——————————————————————————— its placement season at mu last week a student came to me she had two offers one from a large corporate paying ₹ lpa and the other from an earlystage startup offering ₹ lpa she took the corporate when i asked her why she said my next employer will look at my current ctc this number will help me negotiate that logic makes complete sense but it also doesn’t most people in placement season are optimising for a number and for six weeks a year ctc becomes a proxy for how well you did but your job is to maximise your career trajectory and that’s not restricted to your ctc view image follow image link caption your first job routes you where you end up in five years depends far more on the skills you built the problems you owned and how fast you were stretched than on the number you accepted in month one at whitehat jr i watched people join as sales executives and become sales vps in two years that trajectory doesnt happen at a large corporate in two years there you spend the first two years learning the process navigating hierarchy and proving yourself on a small piece of a large machine at an earlystage startup you might own the entire machine the ₹ lpa gap reduces quickly when someone in a startup is promoted into a role that would have taken five years to reach at a corporate it inverts when that startup doesnt compound whether it grows you faster is the only question that remains view image follow image link caption unfortunately nobody during the placement season asks about their manager your manager decides what you work on how much you own and whether youre stretched or managed two people can join the same company and leave with completely different skills depending on who they reported to view image follow image link caption the increment rate matters more than the starting number over any fiveyear window and it is almost entirely determined by the quality of what youre building and learning so heres what id actually do view image caption find the hiring manager on linkedin and look at where the people theyve managed have gone if the last three people who reported to them moved up or to better companies thats the trail a good manager leaves one question in the interview gets you this directly what happened to the last person in this role view image caption search linkedin for people who held this exact role at this company two to three years ago and look at their current positions if theyre in senior roles at strong companies youre looking at a strong learning environment and if theyre cycling through flat moves youre looking at a place that extracts without developing glassdoor reviews and industryspecific communities on reddit tell you more about the culture than you can gauge from an interview view image caption finance pe investment banking has a steep early curve if you move well roletorole jumps of are normal fmcg is steadier but the path to leadership is longer and tech varies entirely by company stage healthcare is growing fast in india but compensation is regulated differently so comparing a ₹ lpa offer in fmcg with a ₹ lpa offer at a series a fintech is comparing two completely different trajectories also do keep in mind how esops could multiply depending on the growth trajectory of early to mid stage companies view image caption hit reply whats a question you wish youd asked before accepting a job i read every email swati ——————————————————————————— ps if you know someone who’s deciding between job offers send Body: a polite reminder for todays maths department colloquium speaker mr hemang mandalia an experienced industry engineer senior vice president quant equities portfolio manager alphagrep mumbai title equities pm date from seminar to allfaculty allstudents dear colleagues and students there is a minor modification to the previous announcement “department seminar” has been replaced with “department colloquium” all other details remain unchanged for completeness the details are provided below speaker mr hemang mandalia an experienced industry engineer senior vice president quant equities portfolio manager alphagrep mumbai date day april wednesday time pm venue lhc title machine learning for pattern discovery in equities abstract this talk provides a practical overview of how machine learning techniques can be applied to discover patterns and predictive signals in equity markets after introducing core ml paradigms—supervised unsupervised and reinforcement learning—we walk through the endtoend datascience pipeline used in quantitative trading data preparation feature engineering model selection and robust evaluation special emphasis is placed on challenges unique to financial data including noise nonstationarity and overfitting along with methods such as regularization crossvalidation and ensemble approaches to address them the session concludes with realworld use cases—returns prediction regime modeling peer discovery anomaly detection—and research directions involving deep learning graph networks and reinforcement learning for strategy design speakers bio mr hemang mandalia has over years of experience in the quantitative finance industry at alphagrep he has worked on medium and lowfrequency quantitative strategies for global equities leveraging machine learning and datadriven pipelines for strategy discovery and risk management he has also built and mentored highperforming collaborative quant teams prior to his current role and position in alphagrep he was quantitative research director at millennium and prior to that at qube research technologies qrt where he worked for almost years including groups time at credit suisse cs his initial years work experience at cs was on tech developing algotrading and backtesting systems you all are encouraged to attend and actively participate in the interactive discussion with best regards mathematics Subject: re seminar on machine llearning for pattern discovery in equities on pm
Body: on aparna mehra wrote dear all a seminar by mr hemang mandalia experienced engineer senior vice president quant equities portfolio manager alphagrep mumbai date day april wednesday time pm venue lhc title machine llearning for pattern discovery in equities abstract this talk provides a practical overview of how machine learning techniques can be applied to discover patterns and predictive signals in equity markets after introducing core ml paradigms—supervised unsupervised and reinforcement learning—we walk through the endtoend datascience pipeline used in quantitative trading data preparation feature engineering model selection and robust evaluation special emphasis is placed on challenges unique to financial data including noise nonstationarity and overfitting along with methods such as regularization crossvalidation and ensemble approaches to address them the session concludes with realworld use cases—returns prediction regime modeling peer discovery anomaly detection—and research directions involving deep learning graph networks and reinforcement learning for strategy design mr hemang mandalia has over years of experience in the quantitative finance industry at alphagrep he has worked on medium and lowfrequency quantitative strategies for global equities leveraging machine learning and datadriven pipelines for strategy discovery and risk management he has also built and mentored highperforming collaborative quant teams prior to his current role and position in alphagrep he was quantitative research director at millennium and prior to that at qube research technologies qrt where he worked for almost years including groups time at credit suisse cs his initial years work experience at cs was on tech developing algotrading and backtesting systems you all are encouraged to attend and actively participate in the interactive discussion thank you best wishes aparna

Body: dear students and colleagues we are delighted to invite you to an institute lecture by prof atul k jain department of climate meteorology and atmospheric sciences university of illinois urbanachampaign urbana on th april at pm in lh at iit delhi please be seated by pm title of the talk water energy and carbon footprint from bioethanol production we look forward to your enthusiastic participation regards shilpi shilpi sharma sheher associate dean academics outreach new initiatives batch of chair professor department of biochemical engineering and biotechnology indian institute of technology delhi new delhi india abstract of the talk bioethanol crops have the potential to meet future energy demands and mitigate climate change by partially replacing fossil fuels however the largescale cultivation of these crops may also impact climate change through changes in terrestrial water and energy balances carbon and other nutrient dynamics and their interactions this represents a pivotal challenge within the foodenergywater system fews nexus our study estimates potential bioethanol yield across the us based on crop field studies and conversion technology analyses for three crops corn miscanthus and two switchgrass cultivars caveinrock and alamo this presentation will provide a detailed analysis of the implications of expanding bioethanol crops for water and energy resources as well as ghg emissions additionally the presentation will examine how the increasing severity of extreme climate events including droughts and heat waves is shaping these critical factors while the results are presented for the united states the analytical framework linking bioenergy production with land water and climate interactions can be applied to other regions including emerging bioenergy systems in india and other parts of the global south

Subject: how to think about dynamic systems
Body: view this post on the web at i’ve been thinking about how to reason about state in biological and physical systems in classical mechanics one way to describe dynamical systems is through the variables we can measure at a point in time for example the measurable variables for a single particle are its position and velocity if it’s moving in one dimension the position is a single number and the velocity is a single number for a total of two variables phase space is the space of where these state variables can live take a pendulum i can describe the system through the angle it makes with the vertical axis and the velocity of this angle if we plot the values against each other and then let time pass we can trace out the phase space of a pendulum and see some interesting shapes evolve in the case of a pendulum with no friction we get a closed loop the x axis is the angle and the y axis is the angular velocity the animation below shows how phase space is traced out as the system evolves it’s not all the time that we get closed loops though if we add air resistance we get a spiral since the pendulum converges to a stationary point there are already interesting questions about viewing mechanical systems through this lens a lot of these are geometric for example is the phase space ‘bounded’ in its geometry does the phase space lie on some interesting surface or subset and if so what’s the dimension of the subset what do the ‘orbits’ of points look like in phase space and is there a way i can tell if orbits overlap trajectories in phase space have their own nomenclature attracting points in phase space are points that the system converges to if the initial conditions start in some ‘basin of attraction’ chaotic systems often have a never ending trajectory that is bounded but never overlaps on itself these are called strange attractors the van der pol oscillator is a system where no matter where you start in phase space the point converges to a fixed cycle geometry then we have the questions of dynamics if i start on a point in phase space what path is subsequently traced out in high school we use newton’s laws to calculate the equations of motion to do this we use newton’s laws to figure out what the acceleration will be once you solve for the forces but there is another way to do this called the hamiltonian method this method tells you where a point in phase space will go to as time evolves to do this we first need to calculate the hamiltonian of a physical system which is the sum of its kinetic and potential energy as a function of its phase space variables if we label momentum as p and position as q the hamiltonian is given by where tp is the kinetic energy and vq is the potential energy with this hamiltonian we can calculate how each state variable will evolve according to hamilton’s equations the equations relate the time derivative of each state variable as a function of the hamiltonian and crucially gives us an avenue to see how the state of a system evolves as an example lets look at the motion of a spring a spring’s hamiltonian is where m is the mass k is the spring constant q is the displacement and p is the momentum in this formulation we treat position and momentum as its own variables and then see what pops out hamilton’s equations for the spring give us the following equations now if we treat both variables as a function of time and then solve it we get that the solution is where omega sqrtkm is the natural frequency of the spring and q and p are the initial displacement and momentum now if we choose a point in phase space we can let the equations play out and see what lines we trace in the case of a spring it traces out an ellipse this is equivalent to just solving newton’s equations the there are also interesting modern treatments that use phase space to predict the dynamics of a system one such way is the delayed embedding method which is a way to ‘learn’ the phase space trajectory by taking many observations you could also think about phase space in terms of any state you want for example in biological systems these could be temperature co concentration and oxygen concentration Subject: suspected spam ai replacing marketers
Body: view image caption there is a version of aiassisted marketing that works you scope a task tightly give it a clear input evaluate the output against something measurable and keep a human in the loop on anything where a wrong answer compounds several tools have built real businesses doing exactly this but okara is trying to do something different on march they launched what they called the worlds first ai cmo enter your website url and six agents handle your seo content reddit twitter and geo for a month their claim is that it replaced cxos paid top tier salary and came with a lot of experience view image follow image link caption view image caption what came back the seo panel showed twelve checks title tag confirmed h present meta description within character limits mostly things google search console gives you for free view image caption then the tweets the first called a prospective student a psychopath for coldemailing alumni and searching for syllabi online which is crazy the second was a promotional post for okara written in masters unions voice asking our own audience to be impressed that we had hired an ai cmo the agent was running okaras marketing through our account view image caption it had no mechanism to know that masters union needs to earn trust from students making a significant financial and professional decision that kind of context accumulates through months of being inside an organisation understanding what the brand has promised and knowing who is in the room when decisions get made the agent optimised for engagement because engagement was the signal it could read trust was not legible to it a human marketer who had spent a week with the brand would have known the register was wrong before writing a single word view image caption the pattern jasper ai hit million in revenue in and raised million at a billion valuation then chatgpt launched by revenue had fallen by more than half and both cofounders had stepped down the tools that collapsed were the ones that promised to remove human judgment from the loop persado optimises language for large enterprise clients and claims its outputs beat human copy of the time it did not claim to replace a cmo it required trained marketers to set the direction and interpret the results the difference here is the scope of the task crawling a site finding technical errors and flagging pages with thin content all have a clear input a measurable output and a fast feedback loop the agent does not need to understand your brand to tell you that a page has a error the human decides what to do with that information the moment you try to hand over the judgment about what the information means and what the brand should do with it you are removing the part of the work that protects the brand view image follow image link caption even if the outputs had been better he would still have spent considerable time editing them into something usable at that point you might as well start from scratch view image caption the audience has already noticed view image follow image link caption cocacolas aigenerated holiday ad was called soulless toys r us debuted the first brand film made with openais sora at cannes lions and positive sentiment fell from to last week on twitter someone posted a screenshot of an email from the founder of composio explaining it had been sent by his ai agent view image caption the replies were not kind what the founder read as efficient the audience read as the founder not thinking they were worth his time this is the cost of skipping judgment empathy and connection which leads to brand distrust almost infidelity for loyal customers reddit moderators can usually tell when a post is promotional and aigenerated and hacker news has rejected marketing copy for years the audiences most attuned to ai content are also the ones most likely to become your first users view image caption ai slop was named word of the year in once a phrase like that catches on it sticks view image caption wrong tool wrong moment view image caption i understand the positioning but i have a problem with who they are targeting a solo founder at the prepmf stage is still finding their first hundred users and still testing whether the product solves a real problem that person does not need a cmo ai or otherwise seo takes four to six weeks to index and that assumes you already know what you are optimising for and geo assumes people are searching for your category a reddit strategy assumes there are communities where your potential users are having honest conversations about your problem all of this is downstream of knowing who your customer is and why they would buy from you that work gets done through conversations an agent cannot substitute for those conversations at the early stage it can only perform activity that looks like marketing while the actual work of understanding your customer goes undone the judgment you are trying to skip at the start is the judgment you will need for every decision that follows view image caption the launch okaras own best marketing was a single provocative tweet written by a human that received over million impressions view image follow image link caption view image caption the product that promises to handle your twitter presence launched itself with exactly the kind of content its agents could not produce that tells you everything reply and tell me what you have tried and what came back nandini view image caption ps the junior displacement numbers employment for people aged to in aiexposed roles down to since late are a separate conversation but they are downstream of the same dynamic ——— you are reading a plain text version of this post for the best experience copy and paste this link Subject: reminderme guest talk by dr sai tej paruchuri research scientist lehigh university usa
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the me guest talk by dr sai tej paruchuri research scientist lehigh university usa as per the schedule below date th april time pm venue me seminar room ii title kernelbased adaptive estimation and control from piezoelectric oscillators to fusion plasmas abstract adaptive techniques are a class of estimation and control methods that learn and adjust their behavior in real time based on incoming data they are designed to handle system uncertainties and maintain reliable performance under unknown or changing operating conditions classical adaptive methods typically rely on finitedimensional parameterizations of the uncertainties in the model however in complex dynamical systems a finite set of parameters may not be sufficient to capture the unknown dynamics this talk presents how embedding model uncertainties in reproducing kernel hilbert spaces rkhs provides a framework for nonparametric adaptive estimation and control of complex dynamical systems the first part of the talk focuses on kernelbased adaptive estimation of nonlinearities in piezoelectric oscillators and other representative dynamical systems it also illustrates how the kernelembedding framework leads to simple conditions for assessing whether the available data are sufficiently rich for accurate estimation offering practical guidelines for experimental implementation the second part extends the rkhs framework to adaptive control of magnetically confined nuclear fusion plasmas it also highlights experimental results that demonstrate classical adaptive control concepts in a simplified fusiondevice setting providing an important step towards the future implementation of nonlinear kernelbased controllers short bio sai tej paruchuri is a research scientist in the plasma control laboratory within the department of mechanical engineering and mechanics at lehigh university his current research focuses on modelbased and learningbased control of magnetically confined plasmas and nuclear fusion systems in collaboration with international fusion research facilities such as diiid kstar and tcv his broader research goal is to integrate approximation and learning theory into control theory to develop intelligent algorithms for controlling complex dynamical systems he received his phd in mechanical engineering and ms in mathematics from virginia tech where his work spanned adaptive estimation of nonlinearities in piezoelectric oscillators and control of systems governed by delay differential equations all interested are welcome to join the talk thanks and regards dr abhishek das assistant professor department of mechanical engineering iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Body: we are pleased to invite you and your colleagues to an upcoming interdisciplinary conference “unriddling inference from pramāṇa theory to modern logic and ai” date am pm ist april venue lh iit delhi mode offline about the event while modern artificial intelligence has reached unprecedented heights in predictive power it often remains epistemically agnostic failing to provide explicit accounts of justification source reliability or the conditions of valid inference classical indian pramāṇa theory offers a sophisticated alternative framework for valid cognition unlike purely formal systems the indian logical tradition treats inference as an epistemically grounded act of knowing this conference seeks to move beyond a historical appreciation of iks positioning it as a living framework that can contribute foundational insights to ai formal logicand reasoning this initiative offers a rare opportunity for faculty staff and students to engage with iks in a modern operative context for further details and registration please visit the conference website or refer to conference webpage for further queries please feel free to contact dr jyotiranjan beuria at or email at prof suresh bhalla and prof sahil garg civil engineering department

Body: seminar announcement title aidriven design and optimization of heterogeneous chiplet architectures for server scale ai workloads speaker dr harsh sharma amd datetime tuesday april am venue sit a abstract the rapid rise of foundation models has significantly increased the computational demands of modern ai systems exposing the limitations of monolithic systemonchip designs heterogeneous chipletbased architectures have emerged as a scalable alternative enabling modularity improved yield and higher performance this talk presents a unified approach to designing such systems through communicationaware chiplet organization topology optimization using spacefilling curves and integration of compute and memorycentric units by cooptimizing architecture interconnects devices and packaging these frameworks enable improved performance energy efficiency and reliability while highlighting key challenges in building nextgeneration ai infrastructure biography dr harsh sharma is a member of technical staff at amd working on designforyield innovations and architecture–package cooptimization for enabling next generation of heterogeneous chiplet architectures he received his phd in computer engineering from washington state university under the guidance of professor partha pande his research focuses on aidriven design and optimization of heterogeneous chipletbased systems for largescale ai workloads spanning computer architecture interconnect design and systemlevel modeling his work has been recognized with the edaa outstanding dissertation award outstanding graduate researcher award and multiple best paper awards at leading conferences he has authored several journal and conference publications in the area of chiplet architectures and ai systems

Body: department of humanities and social sciences ma culture society and thought public lecture speaker prof gopal guru topic possible universal date april tuesday pm venue seminar hall all are invited bio professor gopal guru retired from the centre for political studies at jawaharlal nehru university new delhi was the editor of economic and political weekly his scholarly engagement with caste as an analytical category has profoundly transformed social science writing and theorising recognised as one of the foremost thinkers and theorists of indian political processes professor guru has authored several influential books and specialises in political theory and philosophy his research spans key areas of indian political processes and the politics of multiculturalism caste and dalit politics have remained central to his academic pursuits throughout his distinguished career one of his earlier edited volumes humiliation claims and context redefined the concept of experience and made a significant contribution to the discipline this theme was further developed in the cracked mirror an indian debate on experience and theory a set of essays coauthored with sundar sarukkai in which the two scholars engage in a debate on the role of dalit experience as a critical category for developing new theoretical frameworks within indian social sciences

Subject: the triumph of the embryo
Body: view this post on the web at i am interested in how structure arises from disorder this is why embryology is particularly fascinating to me because it’s about how biological structure emerges from a fertilised egg the triumph of the embryo by lewis wolpert is a book about the developmental biology of embryos it is written clearly for nonspecialists like me and has beautiful illustrations by deborah skinner i’m not an expert on this topic but i wanted to write some parts of the book that have stuck out none of this is my original work of course i learned that the most important event for an embryo is gastrulation wolpert himself famously said that “it is not birth marriage or death but gastrulation which is truly the most important time in your life” p a newly fertilised egg soon becomes a blastula which is a spherical ball of cells gastrulation is when this ball of cells develops a form which begins with the formation of the gut to do this cells move inward and take a different type moulding the blastula to look like this as a mathematician this to me is a case of biological symmetry breaking initially the blastula has a spherical symmetry but then this breaks and the embryo becomes cylindrically symmetric approaching the topology of a torus an exercise to the reader what hamiltonian if any exhibits symmetry breaking from a sphere to c on the empirical side of things i learned that the history of embryology started during the time of the greeks aristotle was amongst the first to investigate the development of embryos by cracking open fertilised chicken embryos and there was a debate until the th century about whether embryos came preformed or developed throughout time epigenesis ch one useful thing i learned is about the ease of using sea urchin embryos as a model study wolpert says that these are popular amongst developmental biologists because they’re easily available ch the embryos are transparent so you can easily see the development through a microscope i’ve been thinking a lot about how i could do this safely at home too more on that in a future post references wolpert l the triumph of the embryo illustrated by d skinner oxford Subject: ai agents to organise my secret societys dinners
Body: view this post on the web at if you are in london and work on independent science please dm me if you would like to join our meetups discord i’m trying to run the london independent science society ’s meetups with less work the less work i have the more meetups i can run but reducing work does not mean spending less time on it nor caring about it less i love thinking about how to curate a dinner designing an agenda and meeting people and i want to spend more time on that stuff so to me less work means reducing the friction involved with bullshit admin this friction is like a cognitive hump that stops me from doing something easy for no reason the usual way i’ve setup events is by first polling people’s availability on discord and whatsapp and then setting up an event page in a tool called luma that’s then shared around this already involves three websites i need to click through cognitive friction and one bullshit admin task is making these event pages in luma it’s fiddly and involves me clicking buttons to setup an event with its date and time i already spend time on whatsapp a lot so polling availability is not a problem for me so i wanted to make the luma part smoother i realised luma had an api so i set up a lightweight hetzner server got the luma api got claude code to learn and test the luma api by pointing it to the docs created an model context protocol on my hetzner server so that my claude could interact with the luma api via its ‘customisation’ function this model context protocol is basically a set of api endpoints that are invoked by claude which in this case take the suggested time and place of my commands and shove it into the luma api call added oauth to secure the end point to the server done so now when i’m on claude on my phone on the bus or whatever when i have a free moment all i have to do is ask my claude app to make the event page for me i can preload in the notes of the mcp my preferred time of day for coffee as well as the geolocations of the cafes i always pick i can’t do automated bookings yet but i can do this and it works… i can also tell it to update the description reschedule it customise the image and all that jazz this is enough friction reduction for me to make scheduling a lot easier i’m thinking of making a website for the society too and i can easily add to the mcp protocol list to add the events to the website easy unsubscribe caution this email originated from outside of iit delhi do not click links or open attachments unless you recognize the sender and know the content is safe

Subject: april pm rd prof rrgaur memorial oration
Body: to all facultystaffstudents national resource centre for value education in engineering nrcvee iit delhi is delighted to invite you to the third rrg memorial oration on science technology and human values the details of the lecture are provided below speaker shri ts ananthu title signs of a new science that replaces particles of matter with pure love as the foundation of reality datetimevenue th april pm senate room link to the poster abstract the talk would begin with a few words on the speakers association with prof rr gaur through the study circle at iitd that was formed under the aegis of the physicist and educationist prof dskothari which ultimately led to the course on science and humanism and the formation of nrcvee the focus will be on the recent work of federico faggin a recognized expert in the field of quantum mechanics it and ai his new thesis portrays consciousness whose essence is pure love as the principal element responsible for what appears to us as matter the speaker will then revisit the oftenoverlooked reflections of scientists such as planck schrödinger and einstein highlighting the role of inner inquiry holistic perception and mystic insight in major scientific breakthroughs the talk emphasizes the notion of underlying oneness – expressed across traditions as advaita wholeness infinity etc – and examines ideas such as zero infinity energy and fractals as scientific metaphors for this unity finally the talk will focus on how einsteins definition of a human being can be used to carry out deep research into this subject leading to a fresh perspective on understanding progress and evolution with the aim of becoming better and happier human beings about the speaker shri ts ananthu is a btech in electrical engineering from the batch of iit madras he got his ms from stanford university in management science and engineering in he worked in the area of systems engineering at xerox esso and ibm between and first in the united states and subsequently in india since he has been a fulltime social worker seva with intense research work in the confluence of science with spirituality please be seated in the venue minutes before pm the duration of the talk will be about one hour followed by discussion for about mins head nrcvee

Subject: my two cents on crowdfunding
Body: ——————————————————————————— hey folks pratham here welcome back to paradox weekly a masters union newsletter where we break down the ideas trends and contradictions shaping business today our head of partnerships preordered a limitless pendant last year view image follow image link caption in december meta acquired the company and stopped selling the pendant the same day eu and uk users had their service discontinued within two weeks our head of partnerships like many others found out through a tweet first that is the crowdfunding paradox equitylevel risk for customerlevel return ——————————————————————————— pebble had the same ending just twelve years earlier in april eric migicovsky launched pebble on kickstarter after failing to raise venture funding for his smartwatch he had been working on the idea since his time as a student in the netherlands where he built an earlier prototype investors saw hardware as too risky and the market as unproven view image follow image link caption they got the watch they had paid for but my friend saw the other outcome last december she had been on the limitless waitlist for months and the bought her the feeling of having believed in what the product could become before it was obvious when meta made the call that feeling was what she lost about of successfully funded kickstarter projects never deliver anything around ship late if you back a campaign you have no consumer protection or investor rights the earliest supporters carry risk that would normally sit with founders and earlystage investors compensated with whatever a regular customer gets and i have a problem with the standard framing here which is that backers are getting played of people who backed a project that completely failed say they would fund a different creators next campaign despite losing money that is a deliberate preference and it tells you what people are actually paying for by pebble had sold a million watches taken some institutional vc money and turned down a million acquisition offer before being acquired by fitbit view image follow image link caption the people who backed pebble in spent the next decade telling anyone who would listen that they helped build the worlds first smartwatch but backers also fund the campaign because they genuinely believe a product will change something in their own life and they want access before the rest of the world does that combination of conviction and early access is what no ad or launch event can create and it does not pay out in cash but people are clearly willing to pay for it anyway what a crowdfunding backer is buying has almost nothing to do with the product ——————————————————————————— this is also why the most sophisticated companies use it for a completely different reason with a billion valuation and of the indian smartphone market xiaomi didnt need the money when they launched mi crowdfunding in india in view image caption raghu reddy their head of online sales explained “in china the company gets the prototype ready and puts on the xiaomi crowdfunding platform to gauge customer interest in those products if it hits a certain threshold we try to then take it from a prototype into a fullscale manufacturing it serves as a good way to test market the product before launching it” if it does not hit the threshold the product doesn’t launch this prevents a wasted manufacturing run and public failure view image caption they had the capital and cofounder tony wright was direct about why they ran the campaign anyway the biggest existential question for the company was is the thing were building as groundbreaking as we think it is most successful campaign creators say demand validation is their primary reason for running a campaign a thousand people paying upfront for something that does not exist is a more honest market signal than any survey focus group or investor pitch ——————————————————————————— what i think crowdfunding was supposed to give founders direct access to capital when institutions would not in practice the most valuable thing the crowd gives you is certainty and that is worth more than the money for pebble the more instructive moment came in eric chose kickstarter again because what he needed was proof the people who mattered still believed i see this pattern regularly among founders i work with at masters union someone builds a product pitches investors who want traction first then debates whether to go direct to customers the answer crowdfunding gives them is the knowledge that a specific kind of person cares enough to pay before it is real view image caption when the product ships the category is proven and the company gets acquired they do not get an exit in terms of a dollar amount they get the right to say they knew before anyone else did and for a certain kind of person that is enough “hit reply have you ever backed something before it was real as a founder or a customer i want to know what made you pull the trigger“ — i read every email until next week pratham ——— you are reading a plain text version of this post for the best experience copy and paste this link in your browser to view the Subject: from reversibility to irreversibility
Body: view this post on the web at one of the major paradigm shifts in physics was the transition from classical mechanics to the study of heat in the eighteenth century i wanted to learn about the history because of my search for potential paradigm shifts in other fields indeed the first chapter of erwin schrödinger’s book what is life forecasts the impact that thermodynamics could have in biology in classical mechanics if you knew the state of the world with no friction you could in theory reverse time and find out its initial state this is because newton’s second law is a differential equation that fully specifies a path of a system if you know the necessary initial conditions but if you heated one side of a metal rod stopped heating it and then waited the heat would spread out uniformly across it and so there would be no way to figure out which side you initially heated therefore processes in heat couldn’t be reversed it was rudolph clausius who formalised the first ‘non reversible quantity’ called entropy that could never decrease he was building on the work of carnot’s reflections on the motive power of fire carnot concluded that the most ideal steam engine the carnot cycle could never create motion from nothing references erwin schrödinger what is life cambridge university press sadi carnot reflections on the motive power of fire bachelier unsubscribe caution this email originated from outside of iit delhi do not click links or open attachments unless you recognize the sender and know the content is safe

Subject: maths department colloquium machine learning for pattern discovery in equities pm
Body: dear colleagues and students there is a minor modification to the previous announcement “department seminar” has been replaced with “department colloquium” all other details remain unchanged for completeness the details are provided below speaker mr hemang mandalia an experienced industry engineer senior vice president quant equities portfolio manager alphagrep mumbai date day april wednesday time pm venue lhc title machine learning for pattern discovery in equities abstract this talk provides a practical overview of how machine learning techniques can be applied to discover patterns and predictive signals in equity markets after introducing core ml paradigms—supervised unsupervised and reinforcement learning—we walk through the endtoend datascience pipeline used in quantitative trading data preparation feature engineering model selection and robust evaluation special emphasis is placed on challenges unique to financial data including noise nonstationarity and overfitting along with methods such as regularization crossvalidation and ensemble approaches to address them the session concludes with realworld use cases—returns prediction regime modeling peer discovery Subject: how to benefit from the claude code leak
Body: hey friend by now you’ve likely seen the claude code source leak everywhere lines of typescript are sitting in public repos including a buildable research fork i went through parts of it and the system prompt alone changed how i think about agent design the prompt is a massive document dynamically assembled at runtime from modular builder functions it covers behavioral rules safety constraints and edge cases even though its just clientside code there are a lot of useful nuggets to build your own agents that level of detail is why claude code feels reliable and most hobby agents don’t the multiagent orchestration is worth studying too the coordination logic lives entirely in prompts not in code one line literally says “do not rubberstamp weak work” another tells agents to “understand findings before directing followup work” you can take these exact prompt patterns and use them in your own multiagent systems today then there’s the cost engineering they built a frustration detector using a regex that catches when you type “wtf” or “this sucks” the agent uses it to adjust its tone they picked a regex over an llm call because inference costs money and a pattern match is faster production ai engineering is full of tradeoffs like that tutorials skip them because tutorials don’t have real traffic or real bills the code is public right now if you’re Subject: how not to resign
Body: view image caption hey folks im swati welcome back to my weekly newsletter this newsletter is those conversations what im seeing thinking and what id tell you if we were grabbing coffee this weeks edition is about how to resign from a job but before that ——————————————————————————— in february this year deepinder goyal wrote to every former zomato employee whether they had left on their own or been asked to leave and told them the door was not closed he invited them back listed what was hiring and asked them to reach out directly he received emails in a week then posted again to say over people at eternal were already in their second or third stint there view image follow image link caption this reminded me about a friend who used to work at flipkart she left about eighteen months ago after a stretch where she felt her growth had stalled and a conversation with her manager had not gone the way she expected she sent her resignation and served her notice period but she stopped coming to team meetings she left before the working day ended when her replacement was being onboarded she was not available to answer questions and chose not to complete the handover about months ago she applied for a more senior role at flipkart through someone she knew here she didn’t make it through their hiring rounds she reached out to a colleague to ask what had happened here’s what she heard her former manager had been asked informally before anything moved forward and despite two years of good work those last four weeks of her employment made it difficult to trust her and you can probably relate to the logic she was running if not the situation she felt the performance conversation had been unfair and that she had given the company everything and been let down so she decided around week two of her notice period that she did not owe them her best effort anymore that logic felt justified and it cost her the one thing she hadnt thought to protect her standing with the people whod watched her leave most people who resign feel entitled to it view image follow image link caption most people who resign have never actually had the conversation about what it would take to stay it could be a different manager or different scope of work that conversation requires the ability to have a difficult conversation with someone who has power over you which is harder than writing an email at midnight so most people skip it view image follow image link caption your manager is not averaging two years of your work when someone asks about you they are remembering your best moment and your last few weeks which is why the notice period carries a lot of weight when they remember you view image follow image link caption a few things i would do differently view image caption if youre about to resign over a difficult manager or a role that stopped making sense check whether youve actually said that to someone who could change it and not vented to a colleague but said it directly to your manager or theirs view image caption most people walk into the resignation conversation focused entirely on what they have decided the moment you resign your manager has a gap to fill and a story to tell upward if you walk in and acknowledge that and tell them you want to help make it as clean as possible that framing changes what they say about you for years sending an email before having that conversation does the opposite view image caption ​​the handover document is the last visible piece of work you do at a company and the one people still talk about after you are gone write down every live project every pending decision every contact your replacement will need do it early enough that your manager can ask questions before you leave ——————————————————————————— in india the relieving letter your next employer will ask for is issued at your current companys discretion the professional circles connecting your previous manager to your next one are much closer than most people account for when they are deciding how seriously to take those final weeks ——————————————————————————— question have you ever resigned from something that a conversation might have fixed i read every email swati ——————————————————————————— ps if you manage a team and someone is about to resign without telling you they probably had a version of this conversation in their head and Subject: spp seminar series political economy of aggregated digital private data april pm spp seminar room prof shishir jha iitb
Body: dear students and faculty colleagues we are delighted to be hosting shishir jha professor at ashank desai centre for policy studies iit bombay this week the details of the talk are given below time pm april spp seminar room room academic complex west speaker shishir k jha has over twentyfive years of teaching experience at different institutions including iit bombay iim bangalore iim kozhikode and ithaca college new york he is actively engaged in analyzing and theorizing various aspects of the data economy particularly the structural dimensions of digitization on information flows his interest ranges from political economy of data storage data monetization competitiveness of digital markets venture capitalism and digital economy digital identity and governance among others he was the national lead for the launch of the creative commons india chapter in title challenges in the public good provisioning of private platform digital data abstract i intend to closely examine the political economy of the growth of aggregated digital private data by initially tracing how the rise of information goods and powerful data extraction methods have become the dominant organizing logic of production in the st century historically speaking the digital economy represents a new and rather unprecedented stage of development that is centred on information goods and data from googles pioneering role in transforming personal data crumbs into predictive advertising the platformisation and extraction of personal data at large scale from onwards where platforms began the process of scaling into monopoly positions and creating multisided infrastructures and the current hegemonic model from onwards characterized by massive cloud services and the rise of data centers with their unceasing collection and datas use in profiling prediction and optimization venture capital funding global acquisitions and infrastructure investment underpinned this transformation the central question is whether private aggregated digital data padd which is generated from billions of individuals and stored with significant public resources like land and other subsidies can be potentially harnessed as digital public goods dpgs to generate public value a few examples that illustrate this potential a norways nicfi program which funds open access to tropical forest imagery for global monitoring b grabs ride hailing app provision of anonymized mobility data to southeast asian governments for traffic and transit planning and c indias bharat bill payment system whose aggregated data informs subsidy and consumption policies relying on private platforms to provision for public goods raises certain risks such as lockin to proprietary ecosystems business model misalignments the pushback in privileging profit over public interest and accountability deficits in data governance mitigation strategies include strong regulatory frameworks like indias dpdp act modular open infrastructures eg upi and the establishment of data trusts in mobility health fintech and climate sectors reciprocity between public and private actors combined with transparency and accountability mechanisms is essential to ensure that the implacable growth of private digital products yields genuine public digital value i will seek to produce a political economy and public policy account of such a transformation from aggregated digital private data into a digital public good what are some of the public policy challenges and concerns in such a suggested transition do join us on thursday Subject: how i fixed my headaches
Body: view this post on the web at some things are pleasurable and make you a more effective person reducing pain is one of those things one such pain was mild headaches i used to get throughout the day these were so common that i didn’t realise them until i started finding ways to alleviate them here are some things i’ve tried in the mornings i would have a dull ache in my temples but a few years ago i went to a dentist who pointed out that i was grinding my teeth i had trouble chewing so it checked out to fix this i got a thick acrylic mouthguard fitted which cost around three hundred pounds and just like that this weird type of dull ache that i would get in the mornings reduced significantly but headaches in the mornings would still come periodically i realised that this was me feeling shitty from lack of sleep the biggest fix was an eye mask that amelia bought me at boots i also bought m foam earplugs i shifted my sleep schedule to go to sleep before pm so that i could wake up without an alarm i stopped drinking coffee after pm as well soon enough my ‘sleepiness headaches’ were less frequent the third reason for headaches seemed to be dehydration my fix is to now carry a big water bottle around to inhale as much water as i can the psychological ‘game’ i try to play is making my pee clear every time the fourth reason for my headaches is motion sickness on the bus so i try to cycle or walk everywhere i can i also realised that my headaches would reduce if i spent less time on screens so during the evenings i try to avoid screens the main way is through an internet block on all types of social media or unintentional sources of information i do this through modifying my etchosts on mac this forces me to read books and write with a pen during the evenings i also put my phone in a drawer so i’m not looking at it for emergencies i’m thinking of getting a second nokia phone that people can call me on the reduction in headaches has conditioned me in a pavlovian way to continue these behaviours i don’t need to remind myself to read at night or drink water rather i do those things to manage unwanted pain it could all be placebo too but i don’t mind since all Subject: leetcode is useless and critical to get a job
Body: i went through five interview rounds for a senior engineer role recently the job posting explicitly said “no leetcodestyle interviews” and indeed nobody asked me to reverse a linked list or sort an array the takehome assessment required building a product where users could edit any message in a conversation they could fork it from any point multiple people could branch from the same message i stared at the spec for a few minutes then i realized what i was looking at each message is a node editing creates a new child walking from any leaf back to the root reconstructs that branch’s full conversation finding where two branches split apart is a common ancestor problem i built the whole thing as a tree the traversal logic took me maybe twenty minutes to write that code made the rest of the app fall into place if i hadn’t studied tree structures i would have tried to manage everything in flat arrays the branching logic would have been a mess i would have spent an hour fighting edge cases that twenty minutes of clean tree code is probably why i passed nobody asked me to solve a tree problem explicitly but my experience made me recognize it was the right solution i recognized it because i’d studied the fundamentals this is what i keep telling people about data structures you don’t need to grind leetcode problems most of those puzzles will never show up in your career but understanding trees graphs hash maps and when to use each one that does show up even with agentic coding you see it in database schemas api responses and state management the companies dropping Subject: re phd synopsis presentation on spatial provenance in vehicular networks
Body: quick update venue moved to bharti school thanks harshan original message subject phd synopsis presentation on spatial provenance in vehicular networks date from harshan jagadeesh to dear all as part of his phd synopsis presentation mr manish bansal will deliver a technical talk on lowlatency spatial provenance recovery in vehicular networks the details are as follows date th march time pm venue ee committee room title lowlatency spatialprovenance recovery with relaxedprivacy in multihop vehicular networks abstract multihop vehicletoeverything v x networks require road side units rsus to localize all vehicles forwarding the packet in a multihop communication path to deliver locationbased services and detect security threats although vehicles utilize the global positioning system gps for navigation they may refrain from sharing their precise gps coordinates due to privacy concerns to address this tradeoff a relaxedprivacy model is proposed wherein the rsu partitions its coverage area into uniform segments and vehicles share only their segment identities three spatialprovenance recovery strategies are proposed location node embedding lne bisegment embedding bse and trisegment embedding tse all employing correlated linear bloom filters in lne every forwarding vehicle independently embeds its own segment identity offering the strongest intervehicle privacy in bse every alternate vehicle embeds two segment identities reducing embedding operations along the path in tse every third vehicle embeds three segment identities offering the lowest endtoend delay for each strategy analytical expressions for false positive events are derived to optimize bloom filter parameters and a rigorous privacy analysis is presented the proposed protocols are validated on a zigbee and lora testbed and timing analysis using g parameters demonstrates significant latency gains and resilience against security threats such as lowpower jammers you are welcome to attend regards harshan

Body: dear all we are pleased to invite you to the gyan ganga distinguished lecture series on river sustainability organized by the nmcgiitddutch collaboratory for intelligent river systems and clean yamuna center of excellence on water indrivers we will be joined in person by shri safi ehsan rizvi ips retd exadvisor mitigation national disaster management authority ndma he will share his experiences in translating the scientific knowledge into policy frameworks for disaster mitigation event details talk adaptation bridging science and policy date april time pm pm venue senate room iit delhi event poster ms teams link about the lecture the talk examines how scientific knowledge is translated into policy frameworks and implemented in practice across diverse hazard scenarios advances in geospatial technologies have significantly improved the ability to map monitor and analyze risk supporting decisionmaking through spatial analysis scenario modeling and realtime information enabling more precise planning and resource allocation across scales urban flooding is considered as a critical domain where multiple components interact in complex ways understanding these interactions requires integrated approaches that combine geospatial data with urban planning frameworks to assess vulnerabilities identify risks and inform mitigation strategies the emphasis is on how such knowledge is operationalized within institutions to support effective and relevant interventions through a set of casestudies spanning multiple hazards and timelines including earthquakes glofs and subsidence the talk outlines the role of riskinformed planning institutional mechanisms and crossdomain coordination in translating science into disaster mitigation policies about the speaker shri safi ahsan rizvi is a former ips officer batch with over three decades of distinguished service in governance national security and disaster management he recently retired as advisor at the national disaster management authority ndma government of india where he played a central role in shaping national policies on disaster risk reduction preparedness and postdisaster reconstruction he also briefly held additional charge of the national institute of disaster management a significant part of his career was spent in the uttar pradesh police where he held key leadership roles including superintendent of police and deputy inspector general handling complex law and order responsibilities across diverse regions he later served as special director in the ministry of home affairs government of india working on national security geostrategy counterterror financing and policy innovation with a strong background in governance and public policy shri rizvi has played a pivotal role in implementing strategies and policies that focus on mitigating the impacts of natural disasters and improving response mechanisms his work spanned multiple hazards and geographies with a strong focus on riskinformed planning institutional strengthening and integration of risk finance into disaster management frameworks his contributions have been recognized in both national and international platforms making him a respected figure in the field of disaster risk management warm regards manabendra saharia and b r chahar faculty dept of civil and env engg pi centre of excellence on water Subject: consumer branding
Body: ——————————————————————————— hey folks pratham here welcome back to paradox weekly a masters union newsletter where we break down the ideas trends and contradictions shaping business today a company youve probably never heard of makes one in two smartphones sold in india its brands have been number one in the indian premium segment the budget segment and the midrange simultaneously the company is called bbk electronics the brands are oppo vivo oneplus realme and iqoo most people reading this have owned at least one of them but don’t know they’re all owned by the same company and that’s today’s paradox invisibility of ownership helps penetrate the market further ——————————————————————————— the flagship killer nobody planned to keep in november pete lau resigned from oppo after a decade including a stint as vp a month later he and carl pei a yearold who had been managing oppos international markets founded oneplus with six employees and one institutional backer oppo itself the context oppo and vivo had built massive offline retail empires across china and india through celebrity endorsements and deep distributor margins but they had zero premium credibility in western markets and minimal traction in indias ₹ segment oneplus was engineered to be everything its parent couldnt be onlineonly communitydriven nearstock android global presence based on price and product rather than influencers view image follow image link caption oneplus launched exclusively on amazon india in december with an invite system get invited share invites with friends that are timebound and by it had of indias premium smartphone market ahead of samsung and apple by it was the undisputed number one premium brand in india for the full year the first chinese brand to achieve that the strategy worked because onepluss software was genuinely cleaner than any chinese competitor its community forums shaped product decisions and the never settle positioning worked because the company was kept separate from its parent ——————————————————————————— view image follow image link caption ——————————————————————————— the ripple that proved the plan oneplus cracking indias premium segment proved two things the rest of the bbk family needed indian consumers would pay premium prices for a chinese brand and directtoconsumer ecommerce worked at scale on may shortly after oneplus demonstrated premium viability realme was born founded by a former oppo vp indiafirst onlinefirst priced to take xiaomis budget market directly its cmo openly acknowledged the structural advantage they shared a supply chain with oppo view image follow image link caption iqoo followed in for gaming vivo and oppo doubled down on offline and the market encirclement was complete by one companys portfolio controlled roughly half of every smartphone sold in india through five brands that publicly appeared to compete with each other the consumers chose freely but none of the options were actually independent ——————————————————————————— then the parent swallowed what it built carl pei left oneplus on october his st birthday he said he wanted to build without a parent company deciding what to do he founded nothing in london and by which has been among the fastestgrowing smartphone brands in india with pei gone the absorption began in earnest in january oneplus merged its rd team with oppos in june pete lau posted on the oneplus forums announcing deeper integration a leaked internal memo confirmed what many suspected with the integration oneplus becomes a brand within oppo oxygenos the clean nearstock android software that was the reason oneplus users stayed loyal was merged with oppos coloros by android central declared oxygenos was functionally aligned to coloros the alert slider disappeared preinstalled bloatware appeared and custom rom installation was restricted prices went from being of flagships to of them the market responded accordingly view image follow image link caption around indian retail stores reportedly stopped stocking it tldr what the enthusiasts loved about the brand was taken away by bbk the brand’s enthusiasts started looking elsewhere ——————————————————————————— heres my two cents this pattern has a name in management literature the icarus paradox where a companys strengths become its weaknesses but the oneplus case has a sharper edge the subbrands success is what triggers the parent and the parent is what destroys it bbk created a company called oneplus to solve a problem no premium credibility abroad oneplus solved it by being everything bbk was not that solution succeeded so completely that bbk absorbed it back and recreated the original problem i see versions of this constantly in indian business titan runs tanishq for premium jewelry fastrack for youth and sonata for economy same parent three completely different consumer perceptions all deliberate hul owns surf excel rin and wheel three detergent brands at three price points competing on the same shelf tata bought jaguar land rover for £ billion in most range rover owners globally have no idea their car is made by a tata company the invisibility of the parent is what makes the premium positioning of the child credible view image caption vw lets porsche tune a cayenne to feel nothing like the identicallyplatformed audi q lvmh gives each maison its own creative director and wont let synergies bleed through into the customer experience they understand that the cost of independence is the price of the strategy the moment you stop paying it youve already begun destroying what you built that’s the bbk and oneplus story think about it was oneplus really a startup or was it disguised into one to create a community that’s the beauty of brand building i read every email until next week pratham ——— you are reading a plain text version of this post for the best experience copy and paste this link in your browser to view the post online Subject: remote work wont make you senior
Body: hey friend i’m not an extremist on the remote vs office debate i’ve done both for years and in fact i did grow to senior at github in a remote role yet i continue to believe most wont make it to senior quickly remotely if you’re a junior engineer working fully remote your growth is probably slower than you think when i was coming up at microsoft the biggest leaps came from proximity to senior engineers none of it was planned i’d overhear a senior debug a production incident i’d catch a design review conversation between two staff engineers i picked up on how someone frames a problem in a doc i didn’t even realize i was learning until months later you can’t search for this on slack because you don’t know the question exists yet remote is great for solved problems building a standard api setting up infrastructure writing tests you know what to do you just need focus time remote wins for that but the jump from “competent” to “experienced” still comes from being around people who’ve been through it ai can help you learn faster i genuinely believe that it can get you to the average faster than ever before but ai won’t give you the intuition of a battletested engineer the kind who survived am outages navigated politics during a rewrite and knows which shortcuts always backfire you learn that from sitting next to people with scars now for a lot of people average might be exactly what they want if you prefer remote for the lifestyle family time hobbies cost of living that’s a perfectly valid choice just be honest with yourself about what you’re trading don’t tell yourself you’re growing at the same rate if you’re not the engineers who grow fastest know what they’re optimizing for and what they’re giving up make the choice intentionally talk soon zen ps inside the
