Subject: building boards that last a lifetime
Body: view image caption hey folks im swati welcome back to my weekly newsletter this newsletter is those conversations what im seeing thinking and what id tell you if we were grabbing coffee this weeks edition is about building a personal board of advisors for your career but before that ——————————————————————————— a student came up after a session last month and said she was trying to figure out her next move after graduation i asked if she had anyone she spoke to regularly about this she said shed done a couple of topmate sessions and found them helpful and was planning to book another one when the next decision came up ive heard this a lot lately a minute paid call with a stranger is not a mentorship the person on the other end doesnt know your history what you tried last month or what youre worried about they give you the best answer they can in the time they have then move to the next call ie a consultation it leaves you feeling like you did something even though nothing was actually built most people have a few names theyd call mentors it could be a senior you met at an event who gave you their card a manager who was kind to you at your first job or even a college senior you still message when something goes wrong none of them are tracking your career right now and you havent set it up for them to be able to do so view image caption a companys board comes together as founders identify what they need recruit for specific roles and set a cadence for how the board stays useful over time view image follow image link caption one mentor cannot cover everything you need deep industry knowledge the willingness to say hard things and connections that open actual doors rarely live in the same person the other thing i hear often is why would a senior person invest time in someone early in their career especially in today’s times where everyone is busy and access feels hard view image follow image link caption senior people mentor younger folks to grow and to stay close to what’s happening in their field thats reason enough to reach out view image follow image link caption what id do view image follow image link caption before you start looking for names get clear on what you actually need maybe it’s guidance from someone in the field you want to move into honest feedback you won’t always like access to the right introductions or just a perspective from a few years ahead once you’re clear on that the names start to feel obvious and the gaps become harder to ignore view image caption start with people who already have some reason to care like professors seniors or past managers rather than strangers if you’re going to an event collecting cards becomes useless as by the end most have dozens if not more they will struggle to remember your face research and understand who’d be at these events pick one or two people in advance research about them nudge them for time before the event meet with them and build a relationship view image caption ​​however you find them dont lead with an ask connections like your college alumni former colleagues and people from companies youve been part of are easier to open because you already share something a lot of people will be willing to talk simply because of that common ground one of our students wanted to connect with the head of revenue at a sequoiafunded startup after just three months of using the product and thinking about it he didn’t have a mutual connection but he still put together a short deck with specific observations on where it was losing users and what could be improved in terms of retention then sent it with a note saying hed been following the company and wanted to share his thoughts the poc replied they got on a call and it turned into a mentorship that later became a job senior people get dozens of can i pick your brain messages every week most go unanswered because theres nothing in it for them what works is showing youve done the thinking like a sharp observation about their work or a question only they can answer understand what they do and see if you can find a gap and validate it before sending it to them if you’ve done something that they can use that’s a foot in the door for you view image caption the relationships that die are the ones where people disappear and only come back when they need something a simple way to avoid that is to send a short note every quarter share what you’ve been working on what you’ve learned and one thing you’re trying to figure out keep it to two paragraphs and one question so they stay updated without needing a call view image caption hit reply who is one person who should be on your board and what would you want them for i read every email swati ——————————————————————————— ps if you lead a team someone on Subject: social media lied to you about ai hiring
Body: i scrolled through linkedin last week and counted fourteen posts about people building apps with ai coding agents in a single afternoon i saw finished product screenshots in every other post one guy claimed he shipped an entire saas over a weekend i see this content every day i make content about ai coding myself not one of those posts mentioned what happens when a company bans ai from the interview i just went through that exact process five rounds for a senior engineer role the company builds ai products they understand these tools better than most of the people posting about them they still banned ai from every coding round these companies aren’t against ai they use ai tools internally every day they ban them from interviews because they need to see what’s underneath they’ve watched too many candidates freeze the moment autocomplete disappears i nearly froze too i had to spend a full week relearning how to code without ai before i was ready for the assessment i passed i got the offer the people who don’t pass they never talk about it nobody writes a linkedin post saying “i failed because i couldn’t code without ai” they quietly apply somewhere else so from the outside the only thing that seems to matter is speed and output the filter is real you just can’t see it from your feed my own team ran into the same thing at a hackathon recently we let an ai coding agent run for two days and ended up with lines of code nobody on the team could review what it actually built the teams that won wrote a fraction of that and built a real solution to an actual problem instead of bragging the same pattern is now showing up in hiring senior roles at companies that actually build ai are testing for the skills underneath the tools every round in my interview tested understanding architecture decisions product thinking technical depth not a single round measured how fast i could generate code i still use ai coding tools every day i teach people how to use them Subject: phd synopsis presentation on spatial provenance in vehicular networks
Body: dear all as part of his phd synopsis presentation mr manish bansal will deliver a technical talk on lowlatency spatial provenance recovery in vehicular networks the details are as follows date th march time pm venue ee committee room title lowlatency spatialprovenance recovery with relaxedprivacy in multihop vehicular networks abstract multihop vehicletoeverything v x networks require road side units rsus to localize all vehicles forwarding the packet in a multihop communication path to deliver locationbased services and detect security threats although vehicles utilize the global positioning system gps for navigation they may refrain from sharing their precise gps coordinates due to privacy concerns to address this tradeoff a relaxedprivacy model is proposed wherein the rsu partitions its coverage area into uniform segments and vehicles share only their segment identities three spatialprovenance recovery strategies are proposed location node embedding lne bisegment embedding bse and trisegment embedding tse all employing correlated linear bloom filters in lne every forwarding vehicle independently embeds its own segment identity offering the strongest intervehicle privacy in bse every alternate vehicle embeds two segment identities reducing embedding operations along the path in tse every third vehicle embeds three segment identities offering the lowest endtoend delay for each strategy analytical expressions for false positive events are derived to optimize bloom filter parameters and a rigorous privacy analysis is presented the proposed protocols are validated on a zigbee and lora testbed and timing analysis using g parameters demonstrates significant latency gains and resilience against security threats such as lowpower jammers you are welcome to attend regards harshan

Subject: europe condemns the iran war in the strongest possible terms again
Body: view this post on the web at in any international crisis you are resigned to accepting europe’s powerlessness we are month into the war it started with the tactical execution of iran’s regime leadership now a global energy crisis it was the unilateral act of the us and israel allies were neither consulted nor warned the uk distanced itself germany was sympathetic italy and france declared the war to be in breach of international law spain’s prime minister denounced the us meanwhile the eu as usual couldnt quite agree i have become weary of nations waving international law i’m all for it but i look at the leaders defending it and my confidence shrinks they clearly have more to gain in defending it because it is not them who foot the bill we are back to the highnoise lowaction equilibrium of european diplomacy if you can no longer exercise hard power with armies and factories you must find lowcost substitution to preserve your influence abroad you borrow your inheritance of relations and institutions declarations and coalitions are drafted for headlines events are affected the voters are proud it might cover declining power for a time eventually each new word carries less meaning coalitions of the unable decline denied weakness a strength i find we confuse international law with the rules we as citizens live under in the uk there is a clear line of authority one law applies one police one system of courts enforce it the omnipotent indivisible state hovers above for hobbes it’s what keeps us from a war of all against all on the international stage were nations stand we are closer to raw competition still we might never be as close as we are today to a unified system these are times of exceptional peace much of which is thanks to a system of multilateral treaties and organisation the tragic fruit of two world wars but like the laws we live under someone needs to enforce this system ‘covenants without the sword are but words’ under pax americana the us has been reluctant to remain the world’s policeman the treaties wear heavy the white house is not accountable to the rest of the world yet without it we would not have today the us remains under trump the largest contributor to the un the return of american isolationism has spelled a few things the enforcement of the postsoviet world order has definitely sagged american power appears at the same time supreme and selfconscious tariffs greenland venezuela and iran it feels the need to intervene but the sky still belongs to america allies were neither consulted or warned they were not needed the us has handled the iran war almost entirely alone the prime minister made it clear that british bases were not used for the first round of attacks as if that would have impeded the american shredding of iranian leadership on a fascinating wind of gaulliste militarism france sent most of its fleet into the zone‘grey hulls have to float somewhere ’ the first six days of us military action in iran cost the government usd bn that almost represents the total of france’s annual police budget that is europe’s premier military power it is the middling nations that cry for international law without the means or will to enforce it themselves international law is a fragile thing that should not be confused with the laws we as individuals live under on the big stage nations wrestle naked the little ones have only their voice to remind the greater powers to enforce the rules they have long abandoned unsubscribe caution this email originated from outside of iit delhi do not click links or open Subject: biology as clockwork
Body: view this post on the web at i’m trying to make models of biological systems that are scalable predictive and give a compelling interpretation about how such systems work in the past months i’ve tried different techniques that model oscillatory behaviour in biological processes i have two reasons out of many that i wanted to write about for why i’ve decided to focus on oscillatory phenomena one is historical motivation from essays i’ve read on the theory of biology the second is my layperson’s idea of what living systems do on the surface organisms do things in clockwork patterns humans sweat to perform homeostasis mammals have circadian rhythms and at the smaller level the cell hosts oscillatory chemical reactions like the krebs cycle or glycolysis crucially the idea linking biology and oscillators is not new in his book entitled ‘what is life’ schrödinger tries to build a link with organisms and clockwork a regular clock requires energy from the spring to maintain its order and so inevitably decays to heat and yet life seems to delay this process by consuming energy ever since clausius formalised entropy as the quantity that never diminishes physicists labelled chemical reactions as entropic and irreversible processes and yet schrödinger in the seventh chapter of his book ponders how living matter is able to produce ordered clockwork motion despite consisting of chemical reactions the unfolding of events in the life cycle of an organism exhibits admirable regularity with orderliness unrivalled by anything we meet with in inanimate matter the philosophy of living things as oscillators continued in the sixties in c h waddington’s transcripts from his ‘towards a theoretical biology’ seminar in waddington makes reference to the brian goodwin’s interpretation of the ‘cell as an oscillator’ goodwin was a developmental biologist who was also one of the first to propose a model of gene oscillator networks this link between biology and oscillating systems spilled over to the physical sciences in fact early examples of oscillatory chemical reactions like the belousov–zhabotinsky reaction were initially inspired by the the desire to mimic biological processes from the prehistory of the belousovzhabotinsky oscillator at winfree writes belousov had studied chemistry in zurich before the october revolution and was professor of chemistry in the ussr before world war his interests included biochemistry and found him endeavoring to model catalysis in the krebs cycle using the metal ion cerium instead of the proteinhound metal ions common in the enzymes of living cells the first thing that comes to mind when modelling oscillations is the fourier transform more modern treatments like dynamic mode decomposition are variations on this theme one takes a bunch of data shifts it and hopes for some lower dimensional space that explains what a biological system does there are mathematical reasons that suggest we should be more ambitious when modelling oscillatory systems in florin takens proved a theorem that the phase space of a dynamical system could be reconstructed from a set of observations provided that the variables of the system were bounded to this end i’ve tried timeseries methods like hankel dynamic mode decomposition which seems to work well on oscillatory processes like in wüstner’s work on glycolysis and synchronised lumination in yeast i’ve also tried it to model lotka volterra systems in ecology but one problem i’ve had with the time series methods i’ve tried is getting decent precision and capturing changing regimes i’ve been having is getting it to be general and scaleable enough in different regimes like when i’ve tested it on my friend david jordan’s bioreactor data i am still excited about oscillations but what is another promising way to understand what biological systems really are one strategy of mine has been to look at previous regime changes in other fields like physics and then think of what an analogue might be in biology to this end there is a very interesting parallel that occurred in the eighteenth century in physics the eighteenth century witnessed the birth of the first non classical science the study of heat in “order out of chaos man’s new dialogue with nature” ilya prigogine and isabelle stengers describe the study of heat as not only a scientific paradigm shift but a philosophical detour away from the rigid thinking of newton’s classical mechanics this change in thinking would serve as a transition into the study of thermodynamics and in my next essay i want to talk about this paradigm shift and how we could apply similar thinking to the field of biology by applying thermodynamic principles to life in closed systems acknowledgements my thanks to david jordan and david kim for their mentorship and support views here are my own and mistakes are all mine references wüstner d et al “dynamic mode decomposition for analysis and prediction of metabolic oscillations” schrödinger e what is life cambridge university press waddington c h towards a theoretical biology vol prolegomena edinburgh university press transcripts from the iubs symposium goodwin b c “oscillatory behavior in enzymatic control processes” advances in enzyme regulation – winfree a t “the prehistory of the belousovzhabotinsky oscillator” Subject: the vibe coding lie
Body: view image caption welcome to ai reflections weekly where i share my honest thoughts about the developments in ai every week for those of you who don’t know me i’m dr nandini seth a founding faculty member at masters’ union specializing in ai data analytics and statistics getting back to today’s edition a few weeks ago dario amodei told davos that ai would take over all coding within a year i’ve got a lot of dms since then including view image caption everyone wants to know whats the right move and i keep thinking that this beyond just code and has to do with how we learn anything at all when i was doing my phd at iim bangalore i spent three years on a problem that a language model could now summarise in two minutes that does not mean those three years were a waste of time i realised that they were about building the machinery in my head that could recognise an answer when i saw one and that machinery comes from getting lost in the rabbit holes often being wrong and sitting with confusion long enough to let the clarity hit this is what i think most people are getting wrong about ai and coding view image caption what i see in my classroom i have students who can get claude to build functional apps with a clean syntax in minutes and i also have students who struggle for hours to write something half as elegant view image caption they have the intuition and have built the right mental models through all that struggling on the other hand the students who prompt get stuck in the prompting loop when something breaks they dont have the machinery to understand what went wrong both groups feel productive but only one group is really learning view image caption this is a pattern researchers gave ai tools to scientists in a materials lab view image caption meanwhile junior researchers saw minimal gains they couldnt tell good outputs from poor ones and lacked the foundation to judge what the ai was giving them and it leads me to another question where do the experts come from view image caption they come from struggle and from years of doing things the hard way from debugging code line by line building systems that failed and figuring out why and reading documentation that didnt make sense until it suddenly does thats how you build the machinery but now were telling students they dont need to struggle by giving them tools that skip the hard parts and are celebrating how fast they can ship without asking what theyre learning in the process do you see the trap ai amplifies expertise but it also removes the process that creates expertise but there’s more to it view image caption the feedback loop that used to force learning and the frustration that made you dig deeper has been bypassed no one would want to struggle for hours when claude can get you to that answer in seconds thats rational but thats also how you never build the machinery view image caption more about the trap most people asking should i learn to code are asking the wrong question code is not a skill to acquire like learning excel or picking up spanish and that’s not the point anyway the point is building the machinery in your head that lets you solve problems systematically it is about developing intuition about how systems work and being able to look at something broken and understand why view image caption the devil’s advocate a lot of people dont really need that machinery if you have an audience a distribution channel or deep understanding of a customer problem you can vibe code a solution and print money the barrier to building software has collapsed y combinator says of their latest batch has codebases that are aigenerated now people are shipping products and making money with zero traditional coding skills if you already have the other pieces build ship make money i mean it but if everyone takes that path who builds the next generation of ai who debugs the systems when they break in ways the ai cant fix and who sees the problems that dont exist yet if disruption could be vibe coded it would already be disrupted view image caption view image caption the choice first understand what amodei is really saying anthropic engineers dont type code anymore but they still specify what to build make the design decisions review outputs and take responsibility when things break typing has become optional thinking is still mandatory second recognise that the scarce skill has now shifted into knowing when the output is wrong and why that requires understanding how systems work at the level of logic architecture and tradeoffs view image caption reply and tell me if you disagree i want to know if im missing something nandini view image caption ps there’s this one line that i keep thinking about thisto think through code you had to type itit was the tax you paid to access the thinkingnow i don’t know… ——— you are reading a plain text version of this post for the best experience copy and paste this link in Subject: phd synopsis presentation on covert communication
Body: dear all as part of her phd synopsis presentation ms soumita hazra will deliver a technical talk on covert communication against reactive adversaries the details are as follows date th march time am venue ee committee room title strategies and performance analyses for covert communication in the presence of reactive adversaries abstract reactive jamming adversaries inject jamming energy on the victim’s frequency band while monitoring different network frequencies to detect countermeasures based on the adversary’s detection capability we consider two complementary adversarial regimes in the first regime the adversary uses generalized energy detectors which consist of statistical detectors based on instantaneous and distributional energy metrics and datadriven detectors that use machine learning classifiers to learn discriminative patterns in the observed energy sequences in the second regime adhering to kerckhoffs’ principle the adversary exploits the publicly available details of the countermeasure for detection against these adversarial regimes we propose cooperative and networkcentric mitigation strategies respectively and analyze their reliability and covertness we solve interesting optimization problems over underlying parameters to enable reliable and covert communication to assess the practical feasibility of the firstregime strategies we implement before and afterdeployment setups on a softwaredefinedradiobased hardware testbed and to evaluate their detectability on real energy observations we collect the corresponding datasets to train and test the machine learning classifiers at the adversary both analytical and hardware evaluations show that the proposed strategies cannot be detected with a high probability for the secondregime strategies we use montecarlo simulations to show that the measured shannon’s entropy closely aligns with the ideal shannon’s entropy demonstrating their effectiveness you are welcome to attend regards harshan

Subject: me guest talk by dr sai tej paruchuri research scientist lehigh university usa
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the me guest talk by dr sai tej paruchuri research scientist lehigh university usa as per the schedule below date th april time pm venue me seminar room ii title kernelbased adaptive estimation and control from piezoelectric oscillators to fusion plasmas abstract adaptive techniques are a class of estimation and control methods that learn and adjust their behavior in real time based on incoming data they are designed to handle system uncertainties and maintain reliable performance under unknown or changing operating conditions classical adaptive methods typically rely on finitedimensional parameterizations of the uncertainties in the model however in complex dynamical systems a finite set of parameters may not be sufficient to capture the unknown dynamics this talk presents how embedding model uncertainties in reproducing kernel hilbert spaces rkhs provides a framework for nonparametric adaptive estimation and control of complex dynamical systems the first part of the talk focuses on kernelbased adaptive estimation of nonlinearities in piezoelectric oscillators and other representative dynamical systems it also illustrates how the kernelembedding framework leads to simple conditions for assessing whether the available data are sufficiently rich for accurate estimation offering practical guidelines for experimental implementation the second part extends the rkhs framework to adaptive control of magnetically confined nuclear fusion plasmas it also highlights experimental results that demonstrate classical adaptive control concepts in a simplified fusiondevice setting providing an important step towards the future implementation of nonlinear kernelbased controllers short bio sai tej paruchuri is a research scientist in the plasma control laboratory within the department of mechanical engineering and mechanics at lehigh university his current research focuses on modelbased and learningbased control of magnetically confined plasmas and nuclear fusion systems in collaboration with international fusion research facilities such as diiid kstar and tcv his broader research goal is to integrate approximation and learning theory into control theory to develop intelligent algorithms for controlling complex dynamical systems he received his phd in mechanical engineering and ms in mathematics from virginia tech where his work spanned adaptive estimation of nonlinearities in piezoelectric oscillators and control of systems governed by delay differential equations all interested are welcome to join the talk thanks and regards dr abhishek das assistant professor department of mechanical engineering iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: talk did indians invent calculus by prof k ramasubramanian iit bombay
Body: dear all did indians invent calculus this provocative question invites us to revisit the foundations of one of the most powerful intellectual tools in modern science while calculus is conventionally associated with newton and leibniz a growing body of scholarship points to sophisticated mathematical developments in the indian traditionparticularly in the works of the kerala school led by mādhava c th century this lecture explores what truly constitutes calculus the deeper ideas of change accumulation infinite processes and functionlike reasoning it will examine how such concepts appeared in indian mathematical texts long before their formalisation in europe central to the discussion is the yuktibhāṣā a remarkable text that presents systematic derivations and arguments arguably making it one of the earliest expositions of calculus reasoning anywhere in the world the lecture will also revisit historical debates including the views of bapu deva shastri the remarks of spottiswoode and subsequent critiques situating them within broader questions of knowledge transmission and historiography how do we define discovery in science and what does it mean to recognise multiple intellectual origins of foundational ideas we present to you a talk titled did indians invent calculus by prof k ramasubramanian of iit bombay date day march friday venue lh time pm please be seated before mins join the whatsapp group for such updates about the speaker prof k ramasubramanian is one among a small and unique cohort of indian scholars researchers and educators who have exalted expertise in sanskrit mathematics and astronomy his visionary and pioneering works have placed indias vast scientific brilliance and heritage on the world stage he holds a doctorate degree in theoretical physics a masters in sanskrit and a bachelors in engineering a combination which has enabled him to produce rigorous original work in his area in the fields of astronomy and mathematics there are gaps in our knowledge india about the major contributions from indian knowledge systems prof ramasubramanians life unbiased research and work has been dedicated in part to address this gap he has brought out several worldrenowned and thoroughly researched monographs for this purpose he serves as the professorincharge leading several research activities for the centre for traditional indian knowledge and skills ctiks at the indian institute of technology bombay india his core areas of expertise are researching preserving and disseminating ancient sanskrit literature in bharatiya gaṇitaśāstra mathematics and jyotiḥśāstra astronomy disciplines his pioneering research on indian scientific literature in sanskrit has led him to pathbreaking books editing several volumes and writing more than articles that have proved the might of indias scientific heritage and our sound legacy system of education for instance through his works the world has come to appreciate the presence of nontrivial mathematics and spherical trigonometry in gaṇitayuktibhāṣā the nuanced astronomical planetary models in tantrasaṅgraha the unique computational techniques in karaṇapaddhati and the mathematical ingenuity of lagnaprakaraṇa his research initiatives have been supported by mhrds science and heritage initiative sandhi since his latest contributions include an ambitious project to create a technological ecosystem for the collection preservation and digitization of sanskrit manuscripts and texts in searchable form what has made possible his expertise in both Subject: your ceo will use claude once and try to fire you
Body: hey friend the ceo of y combinator open sourced a folder of markdown files last week they tell claude to “act like a ceo” and “act like a staff engineer” he posted it on github like it was a major release his friend texted him calling it “god mode” the truth is that its just a folder of prompts and not that impressive at all every developer who has used claude code for more than a week has something like this on their machine a recent study ran three experiments with over people across gpt o gpt claude and gemini they found that chatbots designed to agree with you make people more extreme in their opinions they also make people more certain they’re right participants also became more convinced they’re smarter than average and they rated the agreeable bots as unbiased before you had to be naturally overconfident to overestimate yourself this badly now you can subscribe to it for a month rlhf the training process behind these models is designed to produce words that make you feel good if you get desensitized they retrain the model it adjusts to your tolerance automatically remember “ai will replace developers” that became “ai makes developers x productive” now it’s executives playing with a doll house and calling themselves architects your ceo builds a website over the weekend with claude and announces the company is “aifirst” on monday your manager might walk in tomorrow thinking half the team can go because they “shipped” something with claude if you understand what you’re building you catch when claude is wrong your manager who just discovered it last week cannot mo bitar made a great video about this that breaks down the whole dynamic if you want to make sure you’re not the one getting cut you need skills a prompt folder can’t replace i built a Subject: launch of surge program by sil
Body: dear students over the past month many of you approached me inquiring about the sil projects i was waiting to get more project ideas from faculty members this email provides details on all the exciting opportunities at sil for the past month weve been working tirelessly to expedite all processes and get the student innovation lab sil fully operational the wait is nearly over sil launches on april and were trying to make it accessible x this will be your lab a firstofitskind stateoftheart coworking space in room c equipped with highend d printers embedded systems kits advanced robotics setups powerful gpus and much more the physical space is ready were just awaiting interior work and equipment delivery check out the attached early computergenerated interior designs to see what your new lab will look like coming to the main agenda we are soon launching the summer research grant for excellence surge program through sil projects this is a firstofitskind initiative backed by alumni and department funding and it is highly inclusive enabling as many students as possible to boost their skills and execute innovative ideas this program will let you take up exciting research projects through sil for the summer and beyond all the projects will be funded through the sil research grant under the surge program so you dont have to worry about execution costs or any shortlisting criteria the research grant of up to rs lakh or even more can be provided upon appropriate approval to make it further exciting and rewarding similar to sura we will also select the top project groups for a weekly stipend of rs per student available to students the selection will be based on your profile and a short interview more details via separate email even though the stipend is for a limited number of students the research grant and access to sil are for all furthermore to boost your skills sil will regularly organize workshops on cuttingedge topics including physical ai edgeai embedded systems aiml more you can also extend your project along with sil access beyond summer holidays upon appropriate approval steps to apply for the surge program at sil phase by th march form a team of max members ug or pg choose one or more projects from the sil project list the updated project list will be shared by rd march phase th march th april email the faculty coordinator for your chosen sil project also keep in the cc phase th to th april after getting a nod from the potential faculty supervisor fill the surge registration form the form will be live on th march phase tentatively around midapril interviews will be conducted to select the top groups for the weekly stipend note all the groups under the surge program will get the research fund and access to sil infrastructure just the stipend component is limited to groups max students phase the program commences from the second week of the summer break —incentives under the surge program— access to sil coworking space x access might also be possible and cuttingedge infrastructure surge participation certificates research grant for all projects up to rs with clear justification for the funds but it can be increased subject to approval rs weekly stipend per student for months excellence certification top teams only access to regular workshops on physical ai edgeai embedded systems aiml etc sil open day demo participation top projects will win additional rs arduinoqualcomm goodies strong lors from faculty incubationstartup support for promising deeptech projects subject to reasonable project progress and completion additionally we are also partnering with arduinoqualcomm as our industry partner more may join soon you can get additional potential recognition in the form of certificates rewards internships and many other opportunities from them subject to utilizing their hardware or computing platforms for instance one of our student teams recently demoed their qualcomm uno qbased project at the qualcomm booth during ai impact summit and won the top innovative student project award from arduino ceo fabio violante x youre also welcome to share suggestions on improving surge sil operations after all youre sils primary stakeholders well soon host an information webinar before march to address any doubts about the surge program and sil stay tuned regards amartansh dubey assistant professor blk ee Subject: spp seminar series trilegal book discussion with akshay jaitly march pm lhc
Body: dear colleagues and students we are delighted to be hosting akshay jaitly founding partner trilegal for a book discussion at school of public policy around his recent book trilegal the making of a modern indian law firm details are given below title book discussion on trilegal the making of a modern indian law firm speaker akshay jaitly founding partner trilegal founder trustbridge discussants rohit chandra and meimathi mayavan spp time pm location lhc summary in this session we will be discussing akshay jaitlys new book trilegal the making of a modern indian law firm what does it take to start a new law firm how does one convince new clients to hire you how do legal questions intersect with public policy how is it different working with private clients vs government clients these are among the many questions that we will pose to akshay in what will be a wideranging discussion on the legal profession and some of its intersections with public policy as one of indias leading energy and infrastructure lawyers we will also be asking akshay for his insights on how the legal landscape in these sectors has evolved in the last few decades we will also be discussing how international corporations have changed their views on investing in india in the last few decades and how the energy transition has changed these calculations towards the end there will also be an open qa with the audience anyone interested in law public policy and its intersections with energy and infrastructure should consider attending hope to see many of you there rohit chandra assistant professor iit delhi school of public policy

Subject: invitation for webinar by dr miguel lopezbenitez on th march thursday at pm in bharti school
Body: dear faculty members and students a webinar is being organised by bharti school by dr miguel lopezbenitez senior lecturer associate professor school of computer science and informatics university of liverpool on the topic achieving extreme link reliability for xurllc services in g g networks the details are as follows date thursday time pm ist venue hybrid mode bharti school committee room room no iia bharti school of telecom link talk by dr miguel lopezbenitez meetingjoin microsoft teams abstract the th generation of cellular mobile communication systems introduced the concept of ultrareliable lowlatency communication urllc to support innovative applications such as industry intelligent transportation systems tactile internet remote healthcare and missioncritical services these scenarios as well as emerging applications such as largescale cyberphysical systems digital twins and immersive humanmachine interaction and their even more stringent requirements will remain highly relevant in future g networks under the extreme urllc xurllc paradigm the demanding reliability and latency targets of xurllc make the design of wireless access challenging at multiple protocol layers this talk will provide an overview of g g xurllc use cases their requirements and will present novel techniques to enhance link reliability and robustness by exploiting multiconnectivity through complementary mechanisms at the phy and mac layers speakers profile miguel lópezbenítez received the bsc and msc degrees with distinction in telecommunication engineering from miguel hernández university elche spain in and respectively and the phd degree summa cum laude in telecommunication engineering from the technical university of catalonia barcelona spain in from to he was a research fellow with the centre for communication systems research now the institute for communication systems university of surrey uk in he joined the university of liverpool uk as a lecturer assistant professor with the department of electrical engineering and electronics he is currently a senior lecturer associate professor with the school of computer science and informatics his research interests include wireless communications and networking cellular mobile communications and the application of artificial intelligence to communication systems we welcome you to attend the Subject: public policy club talk draft national electricity policy march noon
Body: dear all the public policy club at iit delhi is pleased to invite you to a session on designing indias energy transition role of electricity policy and institutions which will explore the evolution of indias electricity sector and the policy and institutional frameworks shaping the countrys ongoing energy transition the session will draw on insights from the draft national electricity policy nep and discuss how policymakers balance objectives such as reliability affordability sustainability and competitiveness while steering india towards a lowcarbon energy future speaker details mohit kumar gupta is chief manager at the national load despatch centre nldc gridindia with over years of experience in the indian power sector he has played an important role in indias renewable energy integration efforts and was part of the core team involved in the design and implementation of the renewable energy certificate rec mechanism his work spans areas such as ancillary services system reliability regulatory affairs and transmission pricing he is an electrical engineer from iit bhu varanasi holds an mba in finance from fmsbhu and is currently pursuing a phd in energy transition and electricity markets at the school of public policy iit delhi venue spp conference room b date monday march time pm please see the link below please do join us for what promises to be an engaging discussion on the policy dimensions of indias energy transition regards public policy club iit delhi

Subject: i almost gave up on this job interview
Body: two weeks ago i sat in front of a blank vs code window for three hours no ai agents no copilot no ai autocomplete just me and a blinking cursor i had to build several hard features on top of an existing codebase for a senior engineer role the company’s rule for the takehome no ai tools basic tab completion in your ide and nothing else one screen three hours ship working features i use ai coding agents every single day it writes my python scaffolds my react generates my data models and streaming logic most mornings i open a terminal and start prompting before i’ve finished my coffee when i read those rules i genuinely considered dropping out i couldn’t remember the last time i’d built something real without ai the features involved streaming data visualization and interactive state management each one was substantial on its own so i gave myself one week to prepare every morning i opened a blank file no ai no documentation i wrote api routes from memory i built data validation models until the imports came without thinking i drilled streaming patterns and async code until my fingers stopped reaching for autocomplete it felt like relearning to drive stick shift after years of automatic the first few days were humbling i blanked on syntax i’d used hundreds of times i had to rederive patterns that ai normally writes for me in seconds by day three the muscle memory started coming back by day five i was building small features in under an hour with nothing but my editor then came the real thing three hours on the clock i typed carefully for the first twenty minutes secondguessing every line by hour two i was in flow the preparation had done its job i shipped every feature streaming data visualization interactive ui it worked i got the offer the scariest part wasn’t the assessment it was day one of that practice week i opened a blank file and discovered how much i’d quietly lost over the past year aiassisted coding had made me faster than i’ve ever been it had also eroded skills i didn’t realize i was losing until someone took the tools away i still use ai coding agents every day i’m not going back to writing everything by hand but i’m glad someone forced me to prove i could still code without it talk soon zen ps we talk about this inside the ai native engineer community how to stay sharp underneath the ai tools because the tools neha karlupia senior research associate harvard university date th march time pm venue ksbs committee room title connectomics of the human cerebral cortex in health and disease abstract human cognition depends on synaptic connectivity and communication among diverse brain cell types disruptions in these circuits underlie many incurable neurological and psychiatric disorders despite Subject: fwd department lecture series talk by prof jithin ravi on friday at am in the ee committee room
Body: reminder to the talk today at am original message subject fwd department lecture series talk by prof jithin ravi on friday at am in the ee committee room date from arpan chattopadhyay to allgroup original message subject department lecture series talk by prof jithin ravi on friday at am in the ee committee room date from head ee to dfb cc head ee dear sirmadam this is to inform you that there will be a talk on friday at am by prof jithin ravi assistant professor in the department of electronics and electrical communication engineering at the indian institute of technology kharagpur the title of the talk abstract and his cv are given below title asymptotics of twosample tests abstract in twosampling testing one observes two independent sequences of independent and identically distributed random variables generated according to two unknown distributions p and p and the goal is to decide whether p p null hypothesis or p neq p alternative hypothesis a classical solution is the gutman test which compares the empirical distributions of the two sequences and accepts the null hypothesis if the jensen–shannon js divergence between them is below a given threshold in this talk we consider a generalization of the gutman test referred to as the divergence test which replaces the js divergence with an arbitrary divergence for this class of tests we consider the exponential decay rate of the typeii error probability under a fixed typei error constraint first we show that the divergence test achieves the optimal firstorder error exponent namely twice the bhattacharyya distance between p and p regardless of the specific divergence used second we demonstrate that when the divergence is invariant the divergence test attains the same secondorder asymptotics as the gutman test finally we establish a connection between twosample testing and the robust goodnessoffit testing problem bio jithin ravi is an assistant professor in the department of electronics and electrical communication engineering at the indian institute of technology kharagpur he received his mtech and phd degrees in electrical engineering from the indian institute of technology bombay mumbai in he completed his first postdoctoral fellowship at the tata institute of fundamental research mumbai in followed by a second postdoctoral position at the signal theory and communications department universidad carlos iii de madrid leganés spain from to his research interests include information theory wireless communications informationtheoretic security and statistical Subject: final submission portal details and other instructions
Body: dear finalist teams we are pleased to share the final submission form for this hackathon this form will be used to collect the final materials for your projects ahead of the demo day only one submission should be made per team please ensure that a single team member ideally the team leader completes the form and uploads all required files as we have finalist teams we expect a total of submissions final submission form link as discussed earlier each team is required to submit three components through the form project code and documentation presentation slides a demo video of your project submission guidelines are mentioned inside the form go through them carefully make sure that your repository should also include a readme file describing the project listing team members providing setup instructions and including links to your demo video and any deployed website or application if your project includes very large files such as model weights larger than mb please upload those to google drive set the permissions to public and include the link in your readme file please prepare your ppt slides using the starter template shared inside the form you are welcome to edit the visual design and presentation style of the slides however please do not change the order or sequence of the slides as the judging panels will be reviewing presentations using a common structure the same presentation deck that you submit through the form will be used during the final demo day as we will be compiling all team presentations into a single system in advance it will be helpful if you keep the rubric in mind while preparing your ppt slides please also note that during the judging process only the first three minutes of the video may be reviewed by the microsoft panel to understand the technical aspects and overall approach of your project the overall video cannot be longer than minutes please make sure that all required materials are uploaded before submitting the form apologies for the delay in sharing the form and thank you for your patience we appreciate all the effort you have put into your projects and look forward to reviewing your final submissions best Subject: the internet is dying heres what replaces it
Body: hey friend yesterday i told you how writing skills not coding got me promoted to senior engineer the engineers who get ahead are the ones who can communicate their impact to leadership today i want to share something that worries me about learning online i noticed it about a year ago across linkedin my feeds are full of ai experts whove never shipped a production system giving confident advice to thousands of people i keep seeing misleading posts about x ai coding and build any system in minutes racking up thousands of likes then i started seeing it everywhere reddit threads read like hidden ads half the helpful replies in technical subreddits are bots spamming chatgpt summaries tiktok is full of people giving confident answers about ai systems theyve clearly never built the problem isnt just that the content is fake its that it looks real and people are making career decisions based on it i grew to senior engineer working for github ive seen what actually matters in ai careers and right now the fake advice is pulling people like you away from what actually works the demand for ainative engineers in the industry is real but the places where youd normally learn from are flooded with ai slop instead i wrote these emails by hand from real career experiences building real ai systems and growing my own career my student vittor didnt get hired because he just read and watched my content he got hired because he was in the community getting feedback on his project from people who had shipped similar things i share ideas through my content but people actually change inside my community tomorrow ill share exactly how the ai native engineer community works and why it is the right fit for you talk soon zen ps free content that distracts you is everywhere real Subject: fwd department lecture series talk by prof jithin ravi on friday at am in the ee committee room
Body: original message subject department lecture series talk by prof jithin ravi on friday at am in the ee committee room date from head ee to dfb cc head ee dear sirmadam this is to inform you that there will be a talk on friday at am by prof jithin ravi assistant professor in the department of electronics and electrical communication engineering at the indian institute of technology kharagpur the title of the talk abstract and his cv are given below title asymptotics of twosample tests abstract in twosampling testing one observes two independent sequences of independent and identically distributed random variables generated according to two unknown distributions p and p and the goal is to decide whether p p null hypothesis or p neq p alternative hypothesis a classical solution is the gutman test which compares the empirical distributions of the two sequences and accepts the null hypothesis if the jensen–shannon js divergence between them is below a given threshold in this talk we consider a generalization of the gutman test referred to as the divergence test which replaces the js divergence with an arbitrary divergence for this class of tests we consider the exponential decay rate of the typeii error probability under a fixed typei error constraint first we show that the divergence test achieves the optimal firstorder error exponent namely twice the bhattacharyya distance between p and p regardless of the specific divergence used second we demonstrate that when the divergence is invariant the divergence test attains the same secondorder asymptotics as the gutman test finally we establish a connection between twosample testing and the robust goodnessoffit testing problem bio jithin ravi is an assistant professor in the department of electronics and electrical communication engineering at the indian institute of technology kharagpur he received his mtech and phd degrees in electrical engineering from the indian institute of technology bombay mumbai in he completed his first postdoctoral fellowship at the tata institute of fundamental research mumbai in followed by a second postdoctoral position at the signal theory and communications department universidad carlos iii de madrid leganés spain from to his research interests include information theory wireless communications informationtheoretic security and statistical inference you Subject: how i got promoted to senior at github
Body: hey friend yesterday i told you about vittor who built one complete ai project and got hired as an ai engineer in three months his project worked because it was finished easy to explain and showed real fullstack skills today i want to talk about something that surprised me in my own career during performance evaluation season i could have written the th test in our code thats what good engineers do right you ship more code you add more coverage and you keep your head down hoping the work speaks for itself keep your head down and let the work speak for itself instead i spent that time on a single document it described how the support ai id built helped github increase revenue without firing anyone my document told a story about how support teams could now handle way more volume it showed i understood the whole picture the code i pushed and what it meant for real people and real business outcomes that document got forwarded up the chain and helped my promotion to senior engineer at years old the promotion didnt come from writing more code than everyone else it came from being able to translate what i built into language that mattered to people outside my team most engineers never learn this they assume good work gets recognized automatically it doesnt impact that isnt communicated doesnt exist tomorrow ill share why community matters more than ever for learning how to accelerate your career the internet isnt what it used to be for helping you achieve more talk soon zen ps in the ai native engineer community we cover both technical skills and career strategy because both matter ​join the ainative engineer community unsubscribe ​ ​ caution this email originated from outside of iit delhi do not click links or open attachments unless you recognize the sender and know the content is safe

Subject: the simple project that got my student hired
Body: hi friend yesterday i showed you that building with ai doesnt require a phd or deep math i built a voice transcription app with whisper and an llm and i didnt need to understand any neural network theory to make it work i just needed to know how to connect the right toolstoday i want to show you what kind of project actually gets people hired a simple ai project got my student vittor hired as an ai engineer in just three months not a complex multiagent system not a flashy demo not some overengineered proof of concept he built a simple ai system that answers questions about a consulting site using a python backend and a database most importantly he was able to explain the technical decisions during his interviews thats it simple clear complete vittor joined my community with no idea of the fundamentals a few months later he had an ai engineering role heres why his project worked nontechnical people understood it no explaining overly complex graphbased databases or agent architectures just i built an agent that helps users find information and here is the data that proves this works done it demonstrated real skills frontend backend ai integration deployment one project showing he could handle the full stack it was actually finished not done complete and deployed this is the difference between ainative engineers and everyone else most people never get there because they fall into one of two traps the vibe coding trap ai tools generate of a project fast feels amazing until you hit the wall the last requires understanding that vibe coders dont have vibe coders generate impressivelooking code they cant debug cant extend cant explain the tutorial trap people watch tutorial after tutorial about rag systems and ai agents they follow along nod their heads feel like theyre learning but they never ship anything ainative engineers avoid both traps they use ai to accelerate their work not replace their understanding this is what i call real agentic coding youre in control ai amplifies you you can explain every decision vittor did exactly this and companies hired him for it ive seen this pattern over and over the engineers who actually land roles are the ones building and shipping complete projects not the ones stuck in tutorial loops or generating code they cant explain you dont need to build something complex you need to build something complete tomorrow ill share something that surprised me about career growth its not what most engineers focus on talk soon zen ps vittor built his project with help from the ai native engineer community the feedback and guidance made all the difference ​join the ainative engineer community unsubscribe ​ ​ caution this email originated from outside of iit delhi do not click links or open attachments students interested in biomedical and healthcare entrepreneurship are especially encouraged to join for an invigorating talk and discussion details mentioned below date time monday to venue lh title sciences entrepreneurship technology management innovation digital transformation and artificial intelligence ai in the mba program william currently teaches data science and artificial intelligence Subject: you dont need a phd to build with ai
Body: hey friend zen here yesterday i shared a career quiz that maps you to your ideal ai pathover engineers have taken it so far whatever result you got i want to lower the fear barrier today when most people think about learning ai engineering they picture this complex math linear algebra calculus neural network architectures their brain shuts down before they even start i get it i felt the same way but heres what nobody tells you becoming an ainative engineer doesnt require you to understand any of that deeply you integrate models you dont build them from scratch heres a real example i built an ai transcription app that records your voice transcribes it using a local ai model then cleans up the messy transcript using a large language model ​ you talk into it with all your ums and halffinished sentences it spits out a clean usable transcript did i need to understand the math behind the whisper model no did i need to train my own model no i needed to understand how to use these tools how to connect them and how to turn them into something useful that is ainative engineering in practice the project uses browser apis for recording a python fastapi backend local ai with whisper and llm integration it runs entirely on your machine and heres the best part you can explain it in an interview without a whiteboard i built a voice transcription tool that cleans up messy recordings using local ai done they get it immediately no phd required the fear youre feeling its based on a misunderstanding of what this work actually looks like backpropagation has never come up in my work you need to know how to ship things that actually function in production if software engineering is selfteachable thousands of people have proven it is then ainative engineering is too its the same foundation with ai integration on top tomorrow ill show you exactly what kind of project actually gets people hired talk soon zen ps inside the ai native engineer community we have projects just like Subject: fwd re student project opportunity deep learning for therapeutic peptide prediction
Body: the trail email might be of interest to some of you please contact prof garima rani to get the details dhanya ct phd sheher dean academics rama kanta chair professor in civil and environmental engineering indian institute of technology iit delhi new delhi india phone office academic section homepage faculty homepage original message subject student project opportunity deep learning for therapeutic peptide prediction date from garima rani to eoa of office of dean academics dear dean academics office i request you to please forward this email to the interested students dear students i am garima a faculty member in the department of biochemical engineering and biotechnology at iit delhi my research focuses on understanding biological systems using quantitative modeling biophysics and aiml approaches for antimicrobial design i am looking for motivated students senior undergraduate msc mtech or msr to work on a computational project involving deep learningbased prediction of therapeutic peptide activity and toxicity the project will involve developing ai models that learn directly from peptide sequences to predict biological function and safety if successful the work may lead to research publications students interested in computational biology machine learning or datadriven biomedical research are especially encouraged to apply the abstract of the project is shown below antimicrobial peptides amps are gaining renewed attention as promising therapeutic agents in response to the global rise in antimicrobial resistance and the declining effectiveness of conventional antibiotics their broadspectrum activity and diverse mechanisms of action make them attractive candidates for nextgeneration antibacterial therapies this project aims to develop a deep learning framework to predict and prioritize the therapeutic potential of amps directly from their amino acid sequences we will use pretrained protein language models such as esm or protbert to convert sequences into numerical embeddings which will then be analyzed using bigru or transformerbased neural networks to identify patterns related to biological function a multitask learning approach will be used to simultaneously predict antimicrobial activity pmic and toxicity phc the predicted outputs will be integrated into a unified therapeutic score to rank candidate peptides based on their efficacysafety balance for further validation the overall goal is to build a datadriven pipeline that can support more efficient discovery and optimization of peptide therapeutics keywords deep learning multitask learning therapeutic prediction protein language models antimicrobial peptides amps prerequisites good programming skills in python familiarity with deep learning concepts and interest in computational biology or ai for biomedical applications preferred not mandatory experience with pytorchtensorflow basic familiarity with sequence models project type computational duration months can be decided based on discussion number of publications expected depending on progress please email me separately if you are interested in working on this project along with your cv and a brief description of your background and interests thanks and regards garima dr garima rani assistant professor department of biochemical engg and biotechnology indian institute of technology delhi Subject: why youre confused about ai its not your fault
Body: hi friend yesterday i told you how i went from failing my dutch exam to senior engineer at github by i shared that story because selfteaching got me there not grades or credentials now if you yourself been trying to figure out how to get into ai and feel completely lost i have good news its not your fault the ai space is flooded with people who have never shipped a single product telling you exactly what to do theorists with no production experience ai booster whove never built a real production app some say coding is dead others say you need a phd many are pushing vibe coding as if prompting chatgpt makes you an engineer all of the above is noise and its wasting your time let me clear something up that changed everything for me there are two paths most people talk about ml engineering and ai engineering ml engineers train models from scratch deep math statistics data science they compete against people with phds its a brutal path without the academic background ai engineers integrate existing models into applications they build products that solve real problems they understand models functionally not mathematically but most of these conversations completely miss a third option ainative engineering this isnt a single job title youll find on linkedin its an approach that works across ai software data and other forms of engineering roles an ainative engineer uses ai tools to code faster without skipping the learning they can spin up a rag system figure out why the ai is hallucinating and actually fix it they read the api docs theyre comfortable in the terminal and they ship real products from start to finish wellfounds ceo shared that companies are specifically seeking ainative engineers and pairing senior engineers with ainative juniors who actually know how to ship with ai you dont have to compete against statisticians with doctorates on this path and it builds on software engineering skills you can selfteach i did this at github and now i teach it the market is hungry for people with these skills this is the accessible path the one that doesnt require competing against statisticians with doctorates the one that builds on software engineering skills you can selfteach its what i have successfully done at github its what i teach and its what the market is hungry for once i understood this distinction everything became clearer i stopped chasing credentials i didnt need i focused on becoming ainative i want you to have that same clarity it made all the difference for me tomorrow ill share why ai is much less scary than it seems and how you can become ainative talk soon zen ​unsubscribe ​ ​ caution this email originated from outside of iit delhi do not click links or open attachments unless you recognize the sender and Subject: invitation for spie student chapter invited talk
Body: dear all greetings from the spie student chapter of iit delhi we are pleased to invite you to an expert talk by dr anirban dhar the talk will be held inperson and the details are as follows title impact of waveguide design and material composition on specialty optical fiber performance event timing pm march tuesday event mode only inperson venue a blockiii opc committee room abstract the application of optical fiber beyond communication requires modified waveguide structures and doping of specific materials to enable diverse applications ranging from industrial material processing medical technologies strategic sectors and advanced scientific research to accomplish the full potential of specialty fibers demands sustained innovation in tailored waveguide architectures engineered glass compositions advanced fabrication methodologies and precise optical and material characterization by strategically integrating structural design with compositional engineering key fiber properties such as nonlinearity dispersion gain and power handling can be tuned precisely this talk will highlight how novel waveguide designs and customized glass chemistries can be leveraged to tune fiber performance further about the speaker dr anirban dhar is currently working as a principal scientist in the fiber optics and photonics division at csircentral glass and ceramic research institute kolkata he previously held postdoctoral research position at the institute of photonics and electronics czech republic and at the optoelectronics research center uk dr dhar’s research area include development of specialty optical fiber of various kinds for applications in amplifiers highpower lasers and sensors his significant contribution includes development of world’s first multimode amplifier active grin fiber novel dopants for improving fiber performance etc he has authored over scijournal publications holds uspatents and published book chapters he has delivered numerous invited talks in india and abroad he has guided several students for their phd and mtech thesis work and serving as associate professor at acsir he is recipient of young scientist award from mrsi to ensure matters” based on the life and contributions of padma shri prof rohini madhusudan godbole on th march at the seminar hall iit delhi from pm the film celebrates her pioneering work in particle physics for sustainable technologies at the indian institute of science bengaluru she is a fellow of the indian national academy of engineering born to a farming couple in a small village in andhra pradesh she broke several barriers and overcame several hardships to become the first engineer from her village a gold medallist from nit warangal and a doctorate from iit madras prof madhavi was the first female faculty member of the more than yearold department of civil engineering at indian institute of science iisc her research is focused on sustainable soil reinforcement earthquake geotechnical engineering and rock engineering she is known for her significant technical contributions as a geotechnical consultant to the worlds highest railway bridge across river chenab in jammu for years she received many awards including the ndtv science icon of the year distinguished alumna award of nit warangal best woman researcher in geotechnical engineering award from indian geotechnical society prof s k chatterjee outstanding researcher award of iisc ramoji excellence award in science and technology vishwakarma award teacher extraordinaire award and er avinash shirode yashokirti award she is Subject: i failed my exams then hit kyear at
Body: if you’d told yearold me that i would become a senior engineer working at github by earn € k a year i would not have believed you why because i failed my final highschool dutch exam my native language i still remember sitting that exam halfway through i quit just stood up and walked out i thought i could coast on what came naturally when the exam didn’t match that i completely crashed out so i scraped by high school with no idea what i wanted to do next i definitely wasn’t some coding prodigy who built apps at then i discovered something that changed everything i could teach myself software skills not in some expensive bootcamp just me a laptop and the internet i failed constantly got stuck googled error messages at am kept going anyway my first it job was software tester the most junior role you can possibly get i was just happy someone gave me a chance but this time i decided to change instead of relying on what came naturally i learned to automate tests with cypress and javascript after many late nights i finally figured it out that’s when i realized grades don’t matter companies care about what problems you can solve so i kept learning kept building kept solving problems i grew into cloud engineering at microsoft big tech impressive on paper right but i felt stuck i was solving other people’s problems in ways other people had already figured out so i quit microsoft and took a pay cut to join a smaller company where i’d be forced to figure things out myself it was uncomfortable every single day but i was learning faster than i ever had at microsoft uncomfortable but that was the point a year later i’d mastered my technical stack and landed a job at github a few months in the gpt api dropped while most engineers were debating whether ai was hype i started building with it i combined ai with the skills i’d already developed and shipped features that actually worked that’s what accelerated my path to senior the path from directionless new grad to senior engineer typically takes years i did it in not because i’m special because i discovered something most people never figure out degrees and grading systems don’t determine your success you do selfteaching still works so does solving real problems and combining ai with actual engineering skills this is exactly what i teach now to you and tens of thousands of viewers on youtube all so you dont waste thousands of hours going in the wrong directions like me over the next few emails i’ll share everything i’ve learned about becoming an ainative engineer everything i wish someone had told me when i was starting out tomorrow i’ll start by explaining why so many people are confused about ai in their careers and why it’s not your fault talk soon zen ​unsubscribe ​ ​ caution this email Subject: re ieee vts talk on copper sintering for power electronics packaging by dr sri krishna bhogaraju on nd march pm ee committee room
Body: dear all this is a gentle reminder about todays seminar the venue is the ee committee room time pm regards soumya shubhra nag associate professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi new delhi phone office home page on soumya shubhra nag wrote dear all we are pleased to invite you all to the ieee vehicular technology society talk by dr sri krishna bhogaraju on monday nd march the venue is the ee committee room time pm title copper sintering for power electronics packaging opportunities and challenges in the era of wide bandgap semiconductors abstract as the world pivots toward mass electrification the limitations of traditional soldering are becoming the thermal bottleneck of modern power electronics this keynote explores the transition from conventional joining techniques to copper cu sinteringa transformative power electronics packaging technology essential for the next generation of sic and gan power modules key discussion pillars the material advantage why copper we will compare the thermomechanical properties of cusintered joints against silver ag sintering and traditional solders focusing on superior thermal conductivity and reliability under hightemperature cycling the sintering mechanism an exploration of the physics behind solidstate diffusion looking at how material choice defines sintering mechanisms design and process rules engineering challenges we will candidly address the pain points hindering industrywide adoption including oxidation control sinteirng temeprature and the complexities of surface metallization and sintering atmosphere the road ahead identifying the research gaps that remain for mtech and phd scholars from lowpressure sintering formulations to longterm reliability modeling in harsh environments session goal to move beyond the theoretical and engage in an interactive dialogue on how cusintering will enable the ultrahigh power densities required for evs renewable energy grids and aerospace applications biography sri krishna bhogaraju holds a phd in the field of copper sintering from tu berlin and combines over a decade of research in copper sintering today leads product development at cunex as its cofounder and ceo his work addresses critical challenges in packaging reliability efficiency and cost supporting the adoption of widebandgap semiconductors and the electrification of energy and transportation systems regards soumya shubhra nag associate professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi new delhi phone office home page

Body: attention the round starts on monday march utc hello moonshine we are happy to announce the fourteenth kotlin heroes competition which will be held on codeforces kotlin heroes episode is open for everybody regardless of a division we will be glad to see you among the participants it starts on monday march utc the contest duration is hours you are allowed to use kotlin only to solve the problems register now → the round writers are bleddest awoo adedalic and neon dont miss the round top three winners will get prizes of and respectively top will win a kotlin heroes tshirt competitors solving at least one problem will enter into a draw for one of kotlin heroes tshirts please note that we are not able to ship prizes to any country state province or territory subject to comprehensive ofac sanctions including belarus cuba iran north korea russia syria or the crimea donetsk or luhansk regions for the complete list please visit this page the round is held in accordance with slightly modified icpc rules the round is unrated the contest will have problems of various levels of complexity you are allowed to only use kotlin to solve these problems participants are ranked according to the number of correctly solved problems ties are resolved based on the lowest total penalty time for all problems which is computed as follows for each solved problem a penalty is set to the submission time of that problem the time since the start of the contest an extra penalty of minutes is added for each failed submission on solved problems ie if you never solve the problem you will not be penalized for trying that problem if two participants solved the same number of problems and scored the same penalty then those of them who had previously made the last successful submission will be given an advantage in the distribution of prizes and gifts want to compete do not forget to register for the contest and check your handle on the registration page to help you get familiar with kotlin jetbrains has prepared a tutorial on competitive programming in kotlin and a practice round where you can try to solve a few simple problems in kotlin all solutions are open which means
