Subject: re ieee pels distinguished lecture by prof akshay kumar rathore on th friday pm at the ee committee room block ii
Body: dear all this is a gentle reminder for the talk at pm in the ee committee room block ii regards soumya shubhra nag associate professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi new delhi phone office home page on soumya shubhra nag wrote dear all we are pleased to invite you all to the ieee power electronics society distinguished lecture by prof akshay kumar rathore nus singapore on february th friday pm in the ee committee room block ii iit delhi the details of the talk are given below the flyer is available here flyerpelsprof akrpdf topic fundamental device switching frequency control of multilevel inverters for medium voltage drives abstract multilevel inverters are a preferred choice for medium voltage industry applications because they allow operation at multiple of dc link voltage and reduce the thd as compared to the conventional twolevel inverters this keynote will explain a method for obtaining very low switching frequency operation hz to hz of medium voltage multilevel inverters that permits a significant reduction of the device switching frequency and minimize the switching losses while not compromising on the thd of the machine currents the technique has been extended for the common mode elimination in the dualinverter fed openend winding motor drives system about prof akshay kumar rathore akshay kumar rathore fellow ieee is currently a professor and director of power and energy research area with the department of electrical and computer engineering with the national university of singapore singapore he has authored or coauthored more than papers on softswitching currentfed dcdc converters multilevel inverters and dcm rectifiers including about ieee transactions his research interests include power electronics and control of electric motor drives dr rathore is was the recipient of several prestigious awards such as the ieee ias andrew w smith outstanding young member achievement award the isao takahashi power electronics award the ieee david irwin early career award the ieee bimal bose award for industrial electronics applications in energy systems the nagamori award and the distinguished alumnus award young achiever from iit bhu varanasi india he edited a book on advanced concepts and technologies for electric transportation published by crc press in he has delivered above invited Subject: seminar by dan bilezikian on the th of march at pm in the cbme committee room
Body: the centre of biomedical engineering iit delhi cordially invites you to a healthcare colloquium series talk by dan bilezikian university of california los angeles details mentioned below refreshments will be served date time march pm venue cbme committee room title quantum biology of the eukaryotic cilium an ancient enigmatic organelle revealed as a multifaceted quantumenabled transducer abstract cilia and their nucleating bodies centrioles are enigmatic structures in cell biology the immotile primary cilium lacking motor proteins required to drive fluid flow was widely considered vestigial throughout the th century in sharp contrast is the modern view of primary cilia as central to sensation morphogenesis and within the brain novel object detection and the regulation of satiety key features of conscious awareness contemporaneously understanding the roles of quantum mechanics in biology has progressed from trivial applications in bioorganic chemistry to the conclusion that life tunnels entangles and establishes extended quantum coherences within diverse families of proteins in explorations of eukaryotic quantum biology many of the current proteins of interest are found within the ciliary microenvironment including vibrational coherence in visual rhodopsins electron entanglement in magnetosensory cryptochromes and tunneling within olfactory receptors and ion channels centrioles and their extensions as the central microtubulebased core of cilia have further been considered to exhibit longrange and longlasting optical coherences with unknown physiological roles consequently we argue that understanding the ciliumcentriole complex will require bridging classical biology with emerging quantum biophysics in this talk we introduce the essential elements of quantum biology alongside the emerging frontiers of ciliary biology aiming to facilitate interactions between these fields with an eye towards developing novel biophysical and biomedical hypotheses speaker bio daniel bilezikian researches the role of quantum mechanics in biology broadly focusing on recurring motifs applicable to diverse eukaryotes he holds a bsc from cornell univeristy in materials science engineering where he was awarded for work integrating traditional nanoscience techniques with biological substrates after being introduced to quantum biology as an undergraduate he pursued the field as a source of bioinspiration for molecular quantum technologies as a phd student in the lab of paul s weiss at ucla where he first assembled biologys quantum toolbox as a set of mechanisms utilized by living systems to enable quantum behavior at body temperatures realizing the majority of eukaryotic proteins of interest were found in the cilium his work has since focused on shining a new light on this enigmatic organelle eom

Body: dear all we are pleased to invite you to the national science day for an enlightening talk on women in science catalysing viksit bharat to be delivered by prof yama dixit associate professor centre for atmospheric sciences iit delhi the talk is organized by prof manabendra saharia associate professor dept of civil and environmental engineering iit delhi in collaboration with the indian society of remote sensing isrs event details topic understanding past and modern climate change to better predict future date th february saturday time pm pm venue hall no gb b block research and innovation park iit delhi mode of talk hybrid online and offline online ms teams link national science day women in science catalysing viksit bharat guest talk by prof yama dixit meetingjoin microsoft teams please see the link below for poster about the speaker dr yama dixit is an associate professor at the centre for atmospheric sciences at iit delhi she has a bsc hons in chemistry from delhi university and masters degrees in environmental sciences from jawaharlal nehru university new delhi she received a phd degree in earth sciences from the university of cambridge uk as a gates cambridge scholar she was a marie curie postdoctoral fellow at ifremer france and a postdoctoral research fellow at the earth observatory of singapore before joining iit delhi her broad area of research focusses on proxy reconstructions and palaeoclimate dynamics changes in hydrology abrupt climate change and impacts on ancient societies her research interests aim to understand the patterns and mechanisms of climate change by using the natural climate experiments of the past archived in lake and ocean sediments in particular much of her research has focused on understanding indian monsoon variability hydroclimate reconstructions of the mediterranean and the indopacific warm pool and more recently on monitoring the stable isotopes of water vapour and precipitation to understand modern Subject: ieee vts talk by dr sri krishna bhogaraju on nd march pm ee committee room
Body: dear all we are pleased to invite you all to the ieee vehicular technology society talk by dr sri krishna bhogaraju on monday nd march the venue is the ee committee room time pm title copper sintering for power electronics packaging opportunities and challenges in the era of wide bandgap semiconductors abstract as the world pivots toward mass electrification the limitations of traditional soldering are becoming the thermal bottleneck of modern power electronics this keynote explores the transition from conventional joining techniques to copper cu sinteringa transformative power electronics packaging technology essential for the next generation of sic and gan power modules key discussion pillars the material advantage why copper we will compare the thermomechanical properties of cusintered joints against silver ag sintering and traditional solders focusing on superior thermal conductivity and reliability under hightemperature cycling the sintering mechanism an exploration of the physics behind solidstate diffusion looking at how material choice defines sintering mechanisms design and process rules engineering challenges we will candidly address the pain points hindering industrywide adoption including oxidation control sinteirng temeprature and the complexities of surface metallization and sintering atmosphere the road ahead identifying the research gaps that remain for mtech and phd scholars from lowpressure sintering formulations to longterm reliability modeling in harsh environments session goal to move beyond the theoretical and engage in an interactive dialogue on how cusintering will enable the ultrahigh power densities required for evs renewable energy grids and aerospace applications biography sri krishna bhogaraju holds a phd in the field of copper sintering from tu berlin and combines over a decade of research in copper sintering today leads product development at cunex as its cofounder and ceo his work addresses critical challenges in packaging reliability efficiency and cost supporting the adoption of widebandgap semiconductors and the electrification of energy and transportation systems regards soumya shubhra nag associate professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi new delhi phone office home page

Subject: ieee pels distinguished lecture by prof akshay kumar rathore on th friday pm at the ee committee room block ii
Body: dear students we are pleased to invite you all to the ieee power electronics society distinguished lecture by prof akshay kumar rathore nus singapore on february th friday pm in the ee committee room block ii iit delhi the details of the talk are given below the flyer is available here flyerpelsprof akrpdf topic fundamental device switching frequency control of multilevel inverters for medium voltage drives abstract multilevel inverters are a preferred choice for medium voltage industry applications because they allow operation at multiple of dc link voltage and reduce the thd as compared to the conventional twolevel inverters this keynote will explain a method for obtaining very low switching frequency operation hz to hz of medium voltage multilevel inverters that permits a significant reduction of the device switching frequency and minimize the switching losses while not compromising on the thd of the machine currents the technique has been extended for the common mode elimination in the dualinverter fed openend winding motor drives system about prof akshay kumar rathore akshay kumar rathore fellow ieee is currently a professor and director of power and energy research area with the department of electrical and computer engineering with the national university of singapore singapore he has authored or coauthored more than papers on softswitching currentfed dcdc converters multilevel inverters and dcm rectifiers including about ieee transactions his research interests include power electronics and control of electric motor drives dr rathore is was the recipient of several prestigious awards such as the ieee ias andrew w smith outstanding young member achievement award the isao takahashi power electronics award the ieee david irwin early career award the ieee bimal bose award for industrial electronics applications in energy systems the nagamori award and the distinguished alumnus award young achiever from iit bhu varanasi india he edited a book on advanced concepts and technologies for electric transportation published by crc press in he has delivered above invited talks keynotes and tutorials in several events across the globe he is the coeditorinchief of ieee transactions on industrial electronics distinguished lecturer of the ieee power electronics society and is serving on the committees of the ieee medal in power engineering ieee nikola tesla award and ies fellow evaluation committee he is a member of the ieee ias society executive board and ies society adcom regards soumya shubhra nag assistant professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi new delhi phone office home page links

Subject: civil engineering seminar series prof ashutosh bagchi concordia university canada on structural health monitoring of dams scheduled on friday th february at noon
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend a talk under the civil engineering seminar series by professor ashutosh bagchi concordia university canada scheduled on friday th february at noon in room no blockiii indian institute of technology iit delhi title of the talk structural health monitoring of dams abstract of the talk modern infrastructure worldwide is under increasing stress due to aging assets climate change and rising demand many bridges dams and transport systems were built decades ago and are now reaching or exceeding their design lifespans structural health monitoring shm with smart sensors internet of things iot artificial intelligence ai machine learning ml and digital twins are increasingly being used to monitor and maintain infrastructure health dams are important assets serving critical functions such as water storage hydroelectric power generation and flood control despite their significance dams also pose substantial risks to downstream communities and infrastructure if not maintained and operated properly there are over large dams globally many of which have exceeded years of service and are showing signs of aging moreover more than dam failures worldwide have resulted in catastrophic damage to life the economy and the environment these failures are not merely historical events they remain a potential threat if existing structures are not adequately maintained this presentation focuses on the general overview of shm and its application to dams and discusses the benefits and challenges biography of the speaker dr ashutosh bagchi is a professor of structures and infrastructure engineering in the department of building civil and environmental engineering at concordia university montreal canada where he served as the chairhead of the department from to he is a professional licensed engineer and fellow of the canadian society for civil engineering csce he is internationally recognized for experimental and analytical research in the areas of structural health monitoring shm earthquake engineering and smart infrastructure he has authored more than articles in peer reviewed journals and conference proceedings dr bagchi is a recipient of the teaching excellence award at concordia and a member of several professional societies including international society for structural health monitoring and canadian dam association the Subject: talk on secure federated learning for low rank matrix models on th february am
Body: dear all you are invited to a technical talk titled secure federated learning for low rank matrix models by ankit pratap singh from iowa state university details of the talk are given below venue bharti date th feb time am abstract modern federated and distributed machine learning systems are vulnerable to different types of failures one natural and powerful class of attacks is the byzantine attack where some nodes may behave arbitrarily and even collude these nodes may know the data the algorithm and all its parameters including those used by the center and can use this information to design worst case attacks in this talk we analyze secure byzantine resilient algorithms for solving three federated low rank matrix learning problems that share common features low rank matrix completion multi task representation learning and robust principal component analysis rpca these problems appear in many modern machine learning and medical imaging applications such as recommender systems federated sketching accelerated dynamic mri and fourier ptychography a newer set of applications where the rpca model is becoming popular is large language model llm compression although powerful llms are expensive to run on edge or consumer devices which makes strong compression necessary this naturally leads to an rpca view of the problem the algorithms discussed in this talk are secure and communication efficient making them practical for large scale federated deployment speaker bio ankit pratap singh is a phd candidate in the department of electrical and computer engineering at iowa state university his research focuses on federated and secure machine learning and has led to publications at icml and among others he was awarded the research excellence award in by iowa state university he received a master’s degree in statistics and computing from banaras hindu university bhu india in where he was awarded the gold medal for securing first position in the msc statistics and computing program he has worked as a machine learning researcher at the international finance corporation world bank group where he developed agentic ai systems he has also worked as an ai researcher at thoughtworks focusing on llm driven systems and synthetic data generation pipelines regards harshan dr harshan jagadeesh associate professor dept of electrical engineering iit delhi Subject: optica student chapter seminar
Body: greetings from the optica student chapter of iit delhi we are delighted to invite you to a distinguished lecture by prof marco bellini istituto nazionale di ottica–cnr lens florence italy the talk will be conducted in online mode and the details are as follows title manipulating the character and shape of ultrashort quantum light states date february friday time pm to pm ist abstract gaining full control over the quantum state and the mode structure of nonclassical light may ultimately enable new investigations in quantum optics and represents a major challenge for future quantum technologies quantum state engineering has advanced rapidly with versatile nongaussian tools such as photon addition and subtraction enabling operations largely inaccessible in gaussian quantum optics photon subtraction can enhance nonclassicality and entanglement in an existing state while photon addition can generate nonclassicality and entanglement independently of the input however engineering a state in a single welldefined mode is often insufficient as experimentally prepared modes may differ from those used for processing detection or efficient coupling to matter systems access to and control over the rich spectrotemporal structure of quantum light can significantly expand the capacity to communicate manipulate and store quantum information in this talk prof bellini will present recent experimental results from his group in florence on photonbyphoton generation manipulation and characterization of ultrashort quantum light pulses with arbitrary spectrotemporal shapes kindly register for the event using the link below the meeting link for the talk will be shared with all registered participants in due course the event flyer is attached herewith for your reference and circulation we look forward to your participation in this enriching session

Subject: invitation for spie student chapter invited talk
Body: dear all greetings from the spie student chapter of iit delhi we are pleased to invite you to an guest lecture by prof josé luís fabris the talk will be held inperson and the details are as follows title spectroscopic wideband optical sensors date february thursday ​time pm to pm venue a opc committee room abstract optical sensors interrogated in the spectral domain are advantageous compared to counterparts that deliver a singleparameter signal the information coded in the entire spectral response band of the sensor allows access to a higher number of sensing features enhancing the prospects of smart sensors aided by artificial intelligence a wellknown example is the fbg fiber bragg grating whose optical response is the spectral reflectance of a distributed bragg reflector engraved in the core of an optical fiber although versatile this kind of sensor requires dedicated equipment for its production and its relatively narrow spectral band limits the information coded in the signal in recent years my group in brazil demonstrated the possibility of multiplexing several macrobend sensors in series in a single optical fiber bringing new applications for this underrated and simple production device this talk will highlight applications of this multiplexed macrobend optical fiber sensor in biomedics robotics and quasidistributed tactile platforms moving from guided optics to free propagation of light another class of spectral optical sensors will be discussed which makes use of uvvis ultravioletvisible spectroscopy and sers surface enhanced raman scattering applications in the fields of precision agriculture and environmental monitoring will be addressed about the speaker josé l fabris received the bsc in physics from the federal university of paraná paraná brazil in the msc degree from the fluminense federal university rio de janeiro brazil in and phd degree from the university of são paulo são paulo brazil in he is currently a full professor with the utfpr federal university of technology paraná — campus curitiba brazil is the leader of the research group of photonic devices and applications at utfpr and the head of the laser laboratory since its foundation in presided the brazilian society of microwaves and optoelectronics – sbmo from to and received the academic merit award prof attílio j giarola from that society in he coauthored more than scientifc papers in jounals and conferences his current main research area is photonics with special interest in optical fiber sensors optical spectroscopy and plasmonics to ensure your participation we kindly request you to register at please join and bring this announcement to the notice of all interested warm regards soorej thekkeyil president spie student chapter iit delhi

Subject: photonics lecture series on th feb time pm online
Body: dear all the optics and photonics centre opc invites everyone to join an online talk as part of the photonics lecture series pls the talk will also be broadcast in the opc committee room please find the details of the talk below title ai for photonic sensing applications in sustainability speaker dr subhasri chatterjee senior scientist tcs research mode online teams link date th february thursday time pm ist broadcast venue a blockiii opc committee room abstract ai is increasingly enhancing photonic sensing by enabling rapid highsensitivity detection and automated interpretation of complex optical signals for sustainability applications the integration of machine learning with photonic platforms such as spectroscopy and plasmonic sensing enables realtime monitoring of water quality with improved selectivity and lower detection limits in the context of nanoplastic pollution in aquatic environments aiassisted plasmonic sensors can detect ultralow concentrations of nanoplastics by analyzing subtle shifts in localized surface plasmon resonance signals caused by nanoplastic interaction with functionalized sensor surfaces these systems can identify polymer signatures and estimate nanoplastic concentrations in complex water matrices such as wastewater groundwater and surface water this combination of ai and plasmonic photonic sensing provides a scalable nondestructive approach for continuous monitoring of nanoplastics in water supporting sustainable water management and pollution mitigation efforts biography subhasri chatterjee received her bsc in physics and msc in applied optics from the university of calcutta she was subsequently awarded the national photonics fellowship of india through which she engaged with iiser kolkata as a research intern she completed her phd in from city university of london uk supported by the erasmus mundus scholarship and then pursued postdoctoral research – through an industrial collaboration involving samsung korea and rockley photonics usa since she has been associated with tcs research as a consultant and senior scientist her primary research domain is optics and photonics with extensive experience in optical spectroscopy biomedical optics plasmonics polarimetry and computational modelling she has authored more than publications in peerreviewed journals and international conferences and has served as a reviewer for multiple scientific journals at tcs research her current research focuses on photopolarimetric sensing and plasmonic sensing technologies regards head opc room no b Body: prof gregory scholes william s tod professor of chemistry at princeton university will deliver an exciting talk from ultrafast dynamics in photosynthetic light harvesting to quantum biology today at pm in the senate room at iit delhi please be seated by pm you are invited to experience this intellectually stimulating session best shilpi ps refreshments have been arranged post the talk shilpi sharma sheher associate dean academics outreach new initiatives batch of chair professor department of biochemical engineering and biotechnology indian institute of technology delhi new delhi satish chauhan dear students and colleagues we are delighted to invite you to an institute lecture by prof gregory scholes william s tod professor of chemistry at princeton university on th feb at pm in the senate room at iit delhi please be seated by pm refreshments have been arrange post the talk title of the talk from ultrafast dynamics in photosynthetic light harvesting to quantum biology about the speaker prof gregory scholes is the william s tod professor of chemistry at princeton university he has been serving as the editorinchief of the journal of physical chemistry letters published by the acs since previously he is a fellow of the royal society london since and served as the chair of the princeton department of chemistry from to and is prof greg scholess research group studies how complex molecular systems in chemistry and biology interact with light we are interested to learn the mechanisms for photoinitiated processes like solar energy conversion the scholes group uses ultrafast lasers to time processes and reveal unforeseen details using multidimensional electronic spectroscopy projects undertaken by the scholes group include photobiomodulation medicine photosynthesis solar energy conversion excitonic materials and mechanisms of photoactivated catalysis in synthetic chemistry we look forward to your enthusiastic participation regards shilpi shilpi sharma sheher associate dean academics outreach new initiatives batch of chair professor department of biochemical engineering and biotechnology indian institute of technology delhi new delhi india abstract of the talk the parallel and synergistic developments of atomic resolution structural information new spectroscopic methods their underpinning formalism and the application of sophisticated theoretical methods have led to a step function change in our understanding of photosynthetic light harvesting these new spectroscopic methods in particular multidimensional spectroscopies have enabled a transition from recording rates of processes to focusing on mechanism such studies indicated the possibility that advanced ultrafast techniques can give insights into the time evolution of the density matrix of the system i will explain the story of how our understanding of these experiments evolved and what these developments teach us about light harvesting in general quantum biology is the field at the intersection of quantumrelated physics and the biology of living systems the goal of the field is to determine if quantum phenomena underpin biological function at the macroscale such results supported by compelling experimental evidence will be important because they will show how quantum effects can have functional relevance even in very complex and nominally classical systems in order to define the scope of quantum biology with a forwardfacing view to help focus the research agenda i will propose open questions fundamental to consolidating the field of quantum biology graham r fleming and gregory d scholes quarterly reviews of biophysics e – the development and applications of multidimensional biomolecular spectroscopy illustrated by photosynthetic light harvesting gregory d scholes graham r fleming alexandra olayacastro and rienk van grondelle nature chem – lessons from nature about solar light harvesting gregory d scholes and graham r fleming proc natl acad sci usa under consideration what is quantum biology

Subject: reminder scai seminar ai for transformative impact pushmeet kohli google deepmind
Body: dear all for the next event in our scai seminar series we have the privilege of hosting a highly eminent researcher someone who played a key role in the work that led to the nobel prize in chemistry dr pushmeet kohli vice president of research at google deepmind please note the details of his talk below date th february thu time pm venue seminar hall title ai for transformative impact abstract scientific progress is entering a new era at google deepmind we are moving beyond traditional experimentation toward a paradigm where ai serves as a catalyst for solving onceunsolvable problems across the physical and biological sciences this session explores the frontier of aidriven discovery detailing how we are tackling grand challenges in genomics materials science and physics from the transformative impact of alphafold to recent leaps in material synthesis we will discuss how ai is fundamentally accelerating the scientific method crucially this acceleration demands that we innovate in safety just as fast as we innovate in science we will conclude with a look at synthid a prime example of how we are building the necessary tools to preserve trust and authenticity in an increasingly synthetic world bio pushmeet kohli is a distinguished scientist and vp of research at google deepmind he founded and leads the ai for science and strategic initiatives unit which uses ai for breakthroughs in biology materials fusion math software and cybersecurity his team developed alphaevolve for accelerating ai research and synthid for safe ai deployment his key achievements include the nobel prizewinning alphafold model for protein structure prediction one of the most cited ai biology papers citations kohlis team also pioneered large language modelbased ai agents like alphaevolve and ai coscientist leading to discoveries in math and biology before deepmind he spent a decade at microsoft research becoming director of research for the cognition group his doctoral thesis received the sullivan doctoral thesis award in time recognized him as one of the most influential people in ai thanks scai seminar organising committee if you are interested in knowing about Subject: talk interaction with prof kirill bolotin freie university berlin on feb friday ms
Body: dear colleagues and students we would like to invite you for a talk and interaction by prof kirill bolotin from physics department of freie university of berlin excellence cluster for chiral electronics date th feb friday time hrs venue seminar room ms physics department iitd title physics in germany navigating the path to research and industry from the foundations of quantum mechanics to modern breakthroughs in the quantum hall effect and spintronics germany remains a global powerhouse in physics yet for many international students the prospect of moving here is clouded by concerns about language barriers complex bureaucracy and immigration hurdles in this talk prof kirill bolotin offers an insider’s perspective on the reality of pursuing research and higher studies in germany furthermore he will talk about his research on nanomechanical probing manipulation and control of excitons in d materials in particular his group demonstrated an approach to induce controlled tensorial mechanical strain in twodimensional d materials and heterostructures at cryogenic temperatures a technique that can be used to investigate manybody behaviors of excitons about the speaker prof kirill bolotin is an expert in electron transport and optoelectronics of twodimensional materials with a phd from cornell university and a postdoc from columbia university he has been a professor at the freie university of berlin in germany since a recipient of the nsf career award the sloan foundation award and an erc starting grant prof bolotin’s work —including discoveries in the fractional quantum hall effect in graphene recordstrong electric fields in d materials strainrelated pseudomagnetic fields in d semiconductors— has been cited over times thanks regards joyee joyee ghosh associate professor department of physics indian institute of technology delhi iitd hauz khas new delhi india tel o

Subject: prof gregory scholes william s tod professor of chemistry princeton university institute lecture
Body: dear students and colleagues we are delighted to invite you to an institute lecture by prof gregory scholes william s tod professor of chemistry at princeton university on th feb at pm in the senate room at iit delhi please be seated by pm refreshments have been arrange post the talk title of the talk from ultrafast dynamics in photosynthetic light harvesting to quantum biology about the speaker prof gregory scholes is the william s tod professor of chemistry at princeton university he has been serving as the editorinchief of the journal of physical chemistry letters published by the acs since previously he is a fellow of the royal society london since and served as the chair of the princeton department of chemistry from to and is prof greg scholess research group studies how complex molecular systems in chemistry and biology interact with light we are interested to learn the mechanisms for photoinitiated processes like solar energy conversion the scholes group uses ultrafast lasers to time processes and reveal unforeseen details using multidimensional electronic spectroscopy projects undertaken by the scholes group include photobiomodulation medicine photosynthesis solar energy conversion excitonic materials and mechanisms of photoactivated catalysis in synthetic chemistry we look forward to your enthusiastic participation regards shilpi shilpi sharma sheher associate dean academics outreach new initiatives batch of chair professor department of biochemical engineering and biotechnology indian institute of technology delhi new delhi india abstract of the talk the parallel and synergistic developments of atomic resolution structural information new spectroscopic methods their underpinning formalism and the application of sophisticated theoretical methods have led to a step function change in our understanding of photosynthetic light harvesting these new spectroscopic methods in particular multidimensional spectroscopies have enabled a transition from recording rates of processes to focusing on mechanism such studies indicated the possibility that advanced ultrafast techniques can give insights into the time evolution of the density matrix of the system i will explain the story of how our understanding of these experiments evolved and what these developments teach us about light harvesting in general quantum biology is the field at the intersection of quantumrelated physics and the biology of living systems the goal of the field is to determine if quantum phenomena underpin biological function at the macroscale such results supported by compelling experimental evidence will be important because they will show how quantum effects can have functional relevance even in very complex and nominally classical systems in order to define the scope of quantum biology with a forwardfacing view to help focus the research agenda i will propose open questions fundamental to consolidating the field of quantum biology graham r fleming and gregory d scholes quarterly reviews of biophysics e – the development and applications of multidimensional biomolecular spectroscopy illustrated by photosynthetic light harvesting gregory d scholes graham r fleming alexandra olayacastro and rienk van grondelle nature chem – lessons from nature about solar light harvesting gregory d scholes and graham r fleming proc natl acad sci usa under consideration what is quantum biology

Subject: dmse seminar talk by prof taylor d sparks university of utah th february pm committee room department of materials science and engineering
Body: dear all we are pleased to invite you to the upcoming seminar in our departmental series prof taylor d sparks from the materials science and engineering department at the university of utah will visit our department to deliver an engaging talk on his research you are warmly encouraged to attend the session if you wish to meet prof sparks please contact prof suresh neelakantan details of the talk title the llm revolution in materials science from data extraction to crystal design date time time pm venue committee room department of materials science and engineering speaker dr taylor d sparks professor of materials science and engineering at the university of utah abstract large language models are igniting a quiet revolution in how we practice materials science what began as tools for language and code are rapidly becoming engines for scientific discovery capable not only of reading our literature but of designing our materials in this talk i trace a new endtoend paradigm that runs from unstructured text to engineered crystal structures i begin with knowmat our agentic llmdriven framework for transforming the materials literature into structured machinereadable data knowmat converts pdfs tables and narrative text into validated json schemas enabling automated database construction largescale literature mining and mlready datasets with builtin quality control this shifts data curation from a manual bottleneck into an automated scalable scientific instrument i then move from understanding to creation i introduce crystext a framework that uses llms to generate full crystallographic information files cifs directly from naturallanguage prompts rather than treating crystal generation as a purely numerical problem crystext treats it as a language problem allowing composition symmetry and even thermodynamic stability to be specified in text with reinforcement learning layered on top these models learn not just to speak crystallography but to obey its physics together knowmat and crystext define a new closed loop for materials discovery literature → structured data → generative design → candidate materials llms are no longer just assistants to materials scientists they are becoming codesigners brief biosketch dr taylor d sparks is a professor of materials science and engineering at the university of utah he holds a bs in mse from the university of utah an ms in materials from uc santa barbara and a phd in applied physics from harvard university he was a royal society wolfson visiting fellow at the university of liverpool and is a recipient of the nsf career award he currently serves as editorinchief of integrating materials and manufacturing innovation and as director of graduate affairs for the john and marcia price college of engineering he is active in tms mrs and acers and is the cohost of the materialism podcast regards rohit and suresh

Subject: scai seminar ai for transformative impact pushmeet kohli google deepmind
Body: dear all for the next event in our scai seminar series we have the privilege of hosting a highly eminent researcher someone who played a key role in the work that led to the nobel prize in chemistry dr pushmeet kohli vice president of research at google deepmind please note the details of his talk below date th february thu time pm venue seminar hall title ai for transformative impact abstract scientific progress is entering a new era at google deepmind we are moving beyond traditional experimentation toward a paradigm where ai serves as a catalyst for solving onceunsolvable problems across the physical and biological sciences this session explores the frontier of aidriven discovery detailing how we are tackling grand challenges in genomics materials science and physics from the transformative impact of alphafold to recent leaps in material synthesis we will discuss how ai is fundamentally accelerating the scientific method crucially this acceleration demands that we innovate in safety just as fast as we innovate in science we will conclude with a look at synthid a prime example of how we are building the necessary tools to preserve trust and authenticity in an increasingly synthetic world bio pushmeet kohli is a distinguished scientist and vp of research at google deepmind he founded and leads the ai for science and strategic initiatives unit which uses ai for breakthroughs in biology materials fusion math software and cybersecurity his team developed alphaevolve for accelerating ai research and synthid for safe ai deployment his key achievements include the nobel prizewinning alphafold model for protein structure prediction one of the most cited ai biology papers citations kohlis team also pioneered large language modelbased ai agents like alphaevolve and ai coscientist leading to discoveries in math and biology before deepmind he spent a decade at microsoft research becoming director of research for the cognition group his doctoral thesis received the sullivan doctoral thesis award in time recognized him as one of the most influential people in ai thanks scai seminar organising committee if you are interested in knowing about Subject: today departmental seminar dr karishma bhasne sr research fellow umass th feb pm ksbs committee room
Body: dear all this is just a kind reminder for todays seminar by dr karishma bhasne in ksbs committee room at pm details of the talk can be seen below hope to see you all best saurabh on saurabh raj wrote dear all we invite you to the ksbs departmental talk on th february at pm in the ksbs committee room the speaker is dr karishma bhasne a senior research fellow at the university of massachusetts amherst usa she works in the field of neurodegenerative diseases please circulate this information in your department all are cordially invited details may be found below speaker dr karishma bhasne senior research fellow university of massachusetts amherst date th february time pm venue ksbs committee room title characterization of diseasespecific tau highmolecularweight assemblies and their propagation abstract tau aggregation and intercellular spread are central features of multiple neurodegenerative tauopathies yet the molecular determinants that govern diseasespecific tau propagation remain poorly understood while recent cryoem studies have revealed structural diversity among tau aggregates derived from human brain tissue it remains unclear whether these structural differences translate into distinct cellular interactions and spreading mechanisms across diseases to address this we isolated highmolecularweight tau assemblies from postmortem human brain tissue spanning alzheimers disease corticobasal degeneration progressive supranuclear palsy and picks disease we then examined their biochemical composition interaction networks and cellular behavior our comparative analyses reveal that beyond structural variation tau assemblies exhibit pronounced diseasespecific differences in isoform composition biomarkers associated protein interactomes and functional properties relevant to cellular uptake notably tau assemblies derived from alzheimers disease selectively interact with lrp receptor promoting cellular internalization whereas assemblies from other tauopathies do not indicating distinct molecular pathways underlying tau spread across diseases our study sheds light on the molecular mechanisms driving tau uptake and elucidates a crucial step in developing and evaluating the taulrp complex as a therapeutic target for tauopathies speaker bio dr karishma bhasne is a senior research fellow at the university of massachusetts amherst where she investigates the molecular mechanisms underlying neurodegenerative diseases she completed her phd with professor samrat mukhopadhyay at iiser mohali focusing on α synuclein and its cellular interactions during her postdoctoral fellowship in lila gieraschs lab at the umass amherst she investigated the role of molecular chaperones in regulating synaptic vesicle formation she currently leads research examining diseasespecific tau propagation across multiple tauopathies thank you best regards saurabh saurabh raj phd assistant professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology hauz khas new delhi india saurabh raj phd assistant professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: reminder invitation for spie student chapter talk
Body: gentle reminder prof kedar khare head optics and photonics centre indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india original message subject invitation for spie student chapter talk date from hodopc to allfaculty allstudents dear all greetings from the spie student chapter of iit delhi we are pleased to invite you to an engaging lecture by prof k thyagarajan former professor of physics the talk will be held inperson and the details are as follows title integrated quantum photonics date february wednesday ​time pm to pm venue ii lt near scoops abstract photons are playing a significant role in quantum science and technology with applications in quantum computing quantum key distribution quantum teleportation and many other areas integrated quantum photonics iqp deals with integration of photonic components on a single chip providing us with all the advantages of integration in terms of compactness low power consumption novel configurations and components which are pre aligned during fabrication nonlinear optcal process of spontaneous parametric down conversion in waveguides forms an important technique for the generation of entangled photon pairs which form a very important resource in the field of quantum information science and technology squeezed states and in the realization of low noise parametric amplifiers the talk will cover how optical waveguide devices can lead to the generation and manipulation of photon pairs that are entangled in different degrees of freedom such as polarization spatial mode etc the generation of hybrid entangled states hyperentangled states and higher dimensional entangled states as well as in the generation of squeezed states and realization of low noise parametric amplifiers about the speaker krishna thyagarajan has more than four decades of experience as a professor of physics at the indian institute of technology delhi iitd and then at bennett university times media group he has played multiple roles across teaching research and administration as a professor head of the department and the officiating director itd he has contributed significantly to the fields of fiber optics and quantum photonics he has held numerous visiting scientist positions across the globe including in usa france canada japan hong kong and poland he was awarded the fiber optic person of the year by lucent technologies finolex and voice and data india in he was elected as fellow of the optical society of america and in as a fellow of the indian national academy of engineers in he was decorated with the title of officier dans lordre des palmes académiques by the french government in january he received the teaching excellence award from iit delhi and in the mahatma hans raj gaurav samman from hans raj college university of delhi he also served as a consultant to tejas networks india pvt ltd bangalore looking into advanced issues related to high capacity communication through optical fibers he has held key positions in national and international federal committees overseeing funding allocations and scientific work in the areas of quantum photonics optical telecommunication and integrated photonics he has more than research papers several patents authorship of more than internationally acclaimed textbooks and has nationally acclaimed physics education videos on electromagnetics for class xii and on quantum electronics his recent book titled integrated quantum photonics has just been published by springer new york to ensure your participation we kindly request you to register at please join and bring this announcement to the notice of all interested warm regards soorej thekkeyil president spie student chapter iit delhi

Subject: feb pm lh talk indian science technology and society in th century the seminal work of sri dharampal by dr md srinivas
Body: dear all have you ever heard of rhinoplasty nose reconstruction practiced by indians in th century and before or about efficient community practice of inoculation against smallpox or why and how was indian iron and steel of superior quality and known for its durability welcome to the works of sri dharampal a gandhian who studied india with an eye on detail through archival and other records including british ones and without overglorifying historicity or harboring biases let us hear dr md srinivas arguably among the foremost scholars on the works of sri dharampal on wednesday feb from to pm at lh indian science and technology in the eighteenth century some contemporary european accounts is the first of dharampaljis books based on the materials collected in the course of his extensive study in the british archives it compiles several articles by early british officers scholars and observers about the indian sciences of astronomy and mathematics and the indian technological practices in metallurgy agriculture architecture and medicine and more the book created a new appreciation of the sophistication and efficacy of indian sciences and technologies before the coming of the british the talk shall briefly describe the indian sciences and technologies discussed in the articles collated in this book the distinguishing features that made these technologies specifically indian according to dharampal and the purpose of the european observers who so painstakingly documented these further in much of his work dharampalji was concerned with discovering the detailed functioning of the indian society polity in different spheres before the coming of the british in the later phase of his life he had come across detailed accounts of a survey that the british had carried out in the s in about localities of chengalapattu to answer precisely that question based on this survey and other information we briefly describe the affluence the abundance the beauty and the functionality of these localities that emerges from this description negating the images of persistent poverty and dysfunctionality of prebritish india you are cordially invited to a talk titled indian science technology and society in th century the seminal work of sri dharampal by dr md srinivas date day feb wednesday time to pm venue lh add to calendar about the speaker dr md srinivas is a padmashree awardee science engineering and the chairman of the centre for policy studies he is a member of the national syllabus and teachinglearning material development committee nstc he has earlier served as vicechairman of the indian institute of advanced study shimla and as member of the indian council of historical research prof srinivas was elected a fellow of the indian national science academy in for his work in history and philosophy of science he did his phd under the supervision of prof emil wolf at the university of rochester ny usa and then worked in the department of theoretical physics university of madras his research work in theoretical physics has been in the areas of conceptual and mathematical foundations of quantum mechanics and quantum optics dr srinivas has published several studies on indian contributions in mathematics astronomy logic and linguistics and on the status of our traditional agriculture architecture and education with the objective of comprehending and cherishing the essential civilizational genius of india not only in the matter of science and technology but also in other fields of thought and organization and helping in formulating a polity society that would allow the indian people and their genius to flourish and assert themselves in the present day world this has led him to work on various aspects of indian civilizational ideas and institutions and how they got disrupted during the two centuries of british rule more about him can be found here professor m d srinivas centre for policy studies join the whatsapp group for such events and talks warm regards dr nomesh bolia chair professor of jaswinder tarvinder chadha chair of operations research professor department of mech engg iit delhi iitd Subject: hss seminar series wednesday february pm
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to the next hss seminar on wednesday february by j daniel luther oxford university please see the link below for poster we look forward to seeing many of you there hss seminar series team date february time pm venue hss committee room ms chair madhulika sonkar department of huss iit delhi title how to read tagore wrong and other ideas on queering normativity abstract what is the value of reading tagore wrong in contemporary public culture how does a wrong reading offer pathways to uncover deeply embedded power structures that determine the limits of the permissable queering normativity develops a queer methodology to analyse a queer archive for the impact of normativity on subjecthood and the ways in which it shapes and curtails gender and sexuality in contemporary south asian public culture queering normativity and south asian public culture engages with both the consolidation and the unsettling of normativity through artefacts of south asian public culture including canonical figures such as rabindranath tagore literary and cinematic texts bollywood films advertisements social media posts and ubiquitous ephemera in south asia and beyond through these texts the author unpacks the construct of canon the nation woman as a postcolonial subject the home and the child marriage samesex sexuality and identity speaker bio j daniel luther is the associate programme director at the rhodes scholarship university of oxford their research focuses on sexuality queer theory and gender in south asian public culture they are the author of queering normativity and south asian public culture wrong readings only and have recently coedited queer asia as method their previous work includes an edited volume queer asia decolonizing and reimagining sexuality and gender

Subject: invitation to “communitydriven ai a roadmap for india’s last mile” – february iit delhi presummit india ai impact summit
Body: dear all we invite your participation in the presummit workshop of the india ai impact summit titled communitydriven ai a roadmap for indias last mile scheduled for february at iit delhi organized jointly by the yardi school of artificial intelligence and the bhagwan birsa munda cell bbmc iit delhi with the support of the ministry of tribal affairs government of india this convening brings together leading ai researchers policymakers practitioners and civil society leaders to initiate a shared national dialogue and cocreate indias first communitydriven ai roadmap the workshop is envisioned as a platform to shape how ai systems are designed deployed and governed to ensure they are participatory responsive and accountable to the realities of indias lastmile contexts the programs structure is designed to bridge cuttingedge ai research with social institutional and governance realities of lastmile access the program will bring together three keynotes thirteen invited talks two panel discussions a voices from parallel communities session three thematic breakout sessions and a final synthesis to shape actionable policyrelevant outcomes the program is structured to progress from aicentric perspectives to social and governance realities before converging into a dialoguedriven synthesis the opening sessions will focus on advances assumptions and constraints in contemporary ai including models architectures evaluation paradigms and system design choices sessions grounded in field realities service delivery constraints institutional capacities community expectations and challenges in citizenfacing deployments will follow two themecentered panels have been designed to facilitate crossdomain dialogue across technology policy and implementation ecosystems the voices from the parallel communities session will further ground the discourse in lived experience the breakout sessions will translate discussions into priority use cases design tradeoffs minimum safeguards and realistic implementation pathways we expect that these will directly feed into a white paper and communitydriven ai roadmap for lastmile public systems for a detailed program agenda and registration link please visit the workshop website at we encourage members of the iit delhi community especially those interested in ai public systems governance policy and social impact to join us for the workshop and participate in various sessions including contributing to discussions that will happen through the days and sharing their perspective this is a unique opportunity to be part of a nationallevel conversation on how ai research and innovation can meaningfully shape inclusive and responsible deployment at scale we look forward to your participation and engagement please see the link below for poster with warm regards on behalf of the organizing committee sandeep raunak hari parag and vivek sandeep kumar associate professor head machine intelligence signals and network misn lab department of electrical engineering jointly with yardi school of ai and bharti school of ttm the indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india phone Subject: promoting indigenous alternative to overleaf
Body: dear colleagues and students i am sharing below as received an important and timely message from prof abhijnan chakraborty iit kharagpur which i believe is highly relevant for our academic community i strongly echo the sentiments expressed below as academic institutions we must actively explore costeffective and highquality indigenous solutions that reduce our dependence on expensive foreign platforms adopting such homegrown technologies aligns well with the vision of atmanirbhar bharat which emphasises selfreliance vocal for local” and make for world encouraging indiandeveloped tools not only helps in conserving valuable foreign exchange but also strengthens our national innovation ecosystem and safeguards data sovereignty i encourage faculty members researchers and students to explore latexio provide constructive feedback and consider its adoption wherever feasible note etsc is not discontinuing the overleaf subscription immediately your feedback will be important in helping us take an informed decision in the future message many of us use overleaf for our scientific paper writing and it is a monopoly indian universities and researchers alone contribute millions of us dollars towards overleaf subscriptions yearly and the amount is increasing every year this entire money goes out of the country to challenge this monopoly few of us at iit kharagpur have developed latexio an indian alternative to overleaf which has all necessary functionalities like secure cloudbased editing version history and templates tailored for academic documents apart from offering realtime collaboration aipowered writing assistance and fast and seamless compilation for research and technical teams most importantly latexio prioritises data sovereignty all user data is stored and processed on indian cloud infrastructure ensuring that indian authors’ manuscripts datasets and intellectual property remain in india the ai engine that powers latexio’s writing assistance runs on the same indian cloud stack so drafts reviews and comments are never sent to foreign proprietary models or external data centers due to heavily optimized code and efficient ai features we can be – more affordable than overleaf helping indian universities save significantly on costs and associated foreign exchange outflows please try latexio and share the link with others we would be eager to know your feedback and suggestions on how to improve it further regards sourabh prof sourabh bikas paul head educational technology services centre iit delhi iit delhi coordinator nptel

Subject: departmental seminar dr karishma bhasne sr research fellow umass th feb pm ksbs committee room
Body: dear all we invite you to the ksbs departmental talk on th february at pm in the ksbs committee room the speaker is dr karishma bhasne a senior research fellow at the university of massachusetts amherst usa she works in the field of neurodegenerative diseases please circulate this information in your department all are cordially invited details may be found below speaker dr karishma bhasne senior research fellow university of massachusetts amherst date th february time pm venue ksbs committee room title characterization of diseasespecific tau highmolecularweight assemblies and their propagation abstract tau aggregation and intercellular spread are central features of multiple neurodegenerative tauopathies yet the molecular determinants that govern diseasespecific tau propagation remain poorly understood while recent cryoem studies have revealed structural diversity among tau aggregates derived from human brain tissue it remains unclear whether these structural differences translate into distinct cellular interactions and spreading mechanisms across diseases to address this we isolated highmolecularweight tau assemblies from postmortem human brain tissue spanning alzheimers disease corticobasal degeneration progressive supranuclear palsy and picks disease we then examined their biochemical composition interaction networks and cellular behavior our comparative analyses reveal that beyond structural variation tau assemblies exhibit pronounced diseasespecific differences in isoform composition biomarkers associated protein interactomes and functional properties relevant to cellular uptake notably tau assemblies derived from alzheimers disease selectively interact with lrp receptor promoting cellular internalization whereas assemblies from other tauopathies do not indicating distinct molecular pathways underlying tau spread across diseases our study sheds light on the molecular mechanisms driving tau uptake and elucidates a crucial step in developing and evaluating the taulrp complex as a therapeutic target for tauopathies speaker bio dr karishma bhasne is a senior research fellow at the university of massachusetts amherst where she investigates the molecular mechanisms underlying neurodegenerative diseases she completed her phd with professor samrat mukhopadhyay at iiser mohali focusing on α synuclein and its cellular interactions during her postdoctoral fellowship in lila gieraschs lab at the umass amherst she investigated the role of molecular chaperones in regulating synaptic vesicle formation she currently leads research examining diseasespecific tau propagation across multiple tauopathies thank you best regards saurabh saurabh raj phd assistant professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: invitation for participation and nomination – presummit “communitydriven ai a roadmap for india’s last mile” – february iit delhi
Body: dear all we invite your participation in the presummit workshop of the india ai impact summit titled communitydriven ai a roadmap for indias last mile scheduled for february at iit delhi organized jointly by the yardi school of artificial intelligence and the bhagwan birsa munda cell bbmc iit delhi with the support of the ministry of tribal affairs government of india this convening envisioned as a platform to shape how ai systems are designed deployed and governed to ensure they are participatory responsive and accountable to the realities of indias lastmile contexts the programs structure is designed to bridge cuttingedge ai research with social institutional and governance realities of lastmile access the program will bring together three keynotes thirteen invited talks two panel discussions a voices from parallel communities session three thematic breakout sessions and a final synthesis to shape actionable policyrelevant outcomes the program is structured to contemporary ai including models architectures evaluation paradigms and system design choices sessions grounded in field realities service delivery constraints institutional capacities community expectations and challenges in citizenfacing deployments will follow two themecentered panels have been designed to facilitate crossdomain dialogue across technology policy and implementation Subject: today departmental seminar dr rachana tomarramanujan fellow thsti th feb pm ksbs committee room
Body: dear all this is just a kind reminder for todays talk by dr rachana tomar at pm in the ksbs committee room the details of the talk can be seen below hope to see you all best saurabh on saurabh raj wrote dear all we invite you to the ksbs departmental talk on th february at pm in the ksbs committee room the speaker is dr rachana tomar a ramanujan fellow working at translational health science and technology institute thsti faridabad haryana please circulate this information in your department all are cordially invited details may be found below speaker dr rachana tomar dst inspire faculty at university of delhi date th february time pm venue ksbs committee room title chemical biology of dna damaging agents abstract dna is susceptible to structural modifications following oxidative damage these arise both from exogenous and endogenous oxidants dietary exposure to fungal derived carcinogen aflatoxin b afb along with hepatitis virus infection are among the significant risk factors associated with liver cancer or hepatocellular carcinoma hcc the third leading cause of global cancerrelated fatalities aflatoxin exposure ultimately leads to hepatocarcinogenesis through genotoxic processes these include metabolic activation to an epoxide subsequently formation of the stable covalent dna adducts and mutagenesis the genotoxicity of afb is largely ascribed to the bulky stable afb fapy dg adducts which induces g to t transversions a prominent mutation at codon of the tp gene is commonly seen in hcc patients from subsaharan african and asian countries as well as the regions with endemic presence of hepatitis infection along with aflatoxin b exposure a major goal in cancer research is to identify mutagenic signatures corresponding with exposure to specific environmental carcinogen investigating mechanisms underlying afb specific mutational signatures are crucial to establish risk factors for disease before the tumor itself appears and provide biomarkers of exposure and windows for therapeutic intervention on the other hand urea lesions in dna arise from common oxidative dna lesions such as thymine glycol tg or oxodg produced endogenously if left unrepaired urea lesions have potential to stall dna replication both in vitro and in vivo and induce point mutations in a sequencespecific manner hence studies focusing urea adducts repair and replication are of significant interest and will have implications in mutagenesis speaker bio dr rachana tomar has obtained her doctoral degree from indian institute of technology delhi under supervision of prof bishwajit kundu at kusuma school of biological sciences in the area of protein biophysics she has worked as a postdoc and research assistant professor under mentorship of prof mike stone in the chemistry department at vanderbilt university nashville tennessee usa her research interest focuses on understanding chemical and biological consequences of molecules that damage dna at vanderbilt university she investigated upon environmental toxins derived as well as endogenously produced oxidative dna lesions or adducts very recently she has been awarded prestigious ramanujan fellowship sponsored by anusandhan national research foundation anrf govt of india for working upon an independent research proposal in dbt lab translational health science and technology institute faridabad haryana thank you best regards saurabh saurabh raj phd assistant professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology hauz khas new delhi india saurabh raj phd Subject: seminar invite
Body: dear all the centre of biomedical engineering iit delhi cordially invites you to a talk by dr kartik pondicherry anton paar austria details mentioned below refreshments will be served date time monday am to pm venue cbme committee room block iii title advanced rheological testing of polymers abstract rheology is the science of flow and deformation behaviour of materials and it is extensively used to study the viscoelastic properties of polymers from mapping the shearratedependent viscosity to studying the temperaturedependent properties such as its glasstransition temperature softening point etc rheology also helps in determining the processingrelated parameters of these materials the current talk offers an introduction to rheology with a special focus on testing of polymers used in medical field from hydrogels to implant materials this includes conventional rotational and oscillatory rheometric along with information about dynamic mechanical analysis dma this talk also brushes on tribological testing of such polymers wherein the friction and wear behaviour of these samples is studied examples of reallife applications include different forms of catheters mammary implants tissues contact lenses etc speaker bio dr kartik pondicherry holds a degree in engineering in metallurgy and materials science from india masters in nanotechnology from germany and a doctorate in tribology from austria dr pondicherry has been working extensively in the field of tribology for the past plus years and is associated with the rheometry department at anton paar for the past years he has been actively involved in the scientific community including stle in addition to authoring scientific publications he has also authored book chapters and numerous white papers showcasing innovative test and analysis methodologies eom prof sarvesh kumar srivastava phd group leader the medical microrobotics medicine lab advisor international students indian institute of technology delhi

Subject: students interested in working on superradiance in biological structures a quantum biophysicsbiochemistry project
Body: dear students i am aarat kalra a new faculty member at the centre for biomedical engineering at iit delhi previously i worked on the electronic properties of protein polymers called microtubules typically microtubules play well known structural roles in the cell but we showed that they also have interesting photophysical properties i am looking for three students in total at either at the senior undergraduate or at the masters msc mtech andor msr level to work on both computational simulating superradiance and performing experiments creating superradiant structures on the surface of protein polymers such as microtubules notably if successfull the project is expected to lead to publications interested students must already have some computational if interested in simulations or experimental if interested in wetlab work experience the abstract of the project is shown below superradiance is a quantum mechanical phenomenon in which several chromophores that are separated by short distances absorb and emit light collectively in contrast to classical fluorescence in which adjacent chromophores emit separately in superradiance chromophores emit radiation as a single giant collective dipole here we aim to first create and then characterize supramolecular superradiant states on the surface of protein polymers called microtubules microtubules have a long history of being used in biohybrid sensing as they are chemically stable at room temperature highly mechanically stiff and can be biochemically conjugated to a variety of species through exposed surface residues we will use wellcharacterized perylene diimide pdi derivative chromophores connected to a polyethylene glycol peg linker to create supramolecular superradiant states to overcome the difficulty of attaining the short enough separations and the narrow set of molecular orientations required for superradiance on the protein surface we will harness a combination of bioconjugation approaches simultaneously targeting surfaceexposed lysine glutamic acid and cysteine residues among others we will then polymerize microtubules using these pditubulin constructs and distinguish superradiance from fluorescence using timeresolved spectroscopy and computational simulations crucially we will measure radiative lifetime enhancement factors using timeresolved microscopy and observe longdistance energy migration along the microtubule surfacethe gold standard test for superradiance our work will illustrate the feasibility of using protein polymers as substrares for quantum effects which can subquently be harnessed for sensing misfoldeddiseased states of proteins keywords quantum biology superradiance energy transfer microtubules quantum biophysics ​ prerequisites project is experimental duration months number of publications expected please email me in a separate email if you are interested in working on this project you migt like to look up my lab website for details about the research group best regards aarat p kalra assistant professor centre for biomedical engineering indian institute of technology delhi best regards aarat p kalra assistant professor centre for biomedical engineering indian institute of technology delhi links

Subject: re talk announcement a holistic view on robust distributed cooperative control of networked systems
Body: a gentle reminder for the talk at pm today shubhendu bhasin professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india web email tel o r fax original message subject talk announcement a holistic view on robust distributed cooperative control of networked systems date from shubhendu bhasin to dear all dr maitreyee dutta is visiting the department and will deliver a talk at pm tomorrow in the ee committee room title a holistic view on robust distributed cooperative control of networked systems datetime jan pm venue ee committee room abstract over the century it has been observed that collaboration in a coordinated fashion among several dynamical systems facilitates the execution of complex tasks such as scientific reconnaissance homeland security search and rescue operations surveillance of ecosystems to name a few naturally information sharing is a key element of cooperative control in order to ensure that the systems reach an agreement over certain variables of interest several conventional algorithms rely on bidirectional communication and availability of centralised data reliance on global information that is shared in an undirected connected manner requires a large communication bandwidth and can lead to catastrophic breakdown of the interconnected network due to a single point of failure moreover several consensual algorithms assume by default that the data received by any system in the network is accurate it is well known that sensors embedded in any robotic system are susceptible to faults which can manifest themselves as persistent constant or timevarying offsets and noises in the measurements direct implementation of faulty measurements in the control loop of any physical system can not only reduce efficiency but also cause accidents in severe cases if we take fidelity to reality into account the consensus problem becomes particularly challenging when there is a restriction in the communication bandwidth and the transmitted measurements are faulty this presentation will cover some distributed control theoretic algorithms robust to sensor faults for different types of systems communicating through a unilateral network the presented work will showcase some of the contributions from my phd and postdoctoral research to the field of control of multiagents systems bio maitreyee dutta received her btech degree in electrical engineering and mtech degree in control industrial automation from national institute of technology silchar india in and respectively she received her doctoral degree from centre for systems and control iit bombay in her phd thesis focused on robust distributed control algorithms for networked systems she is currently working as a postdoctoral researcher in systems and control engineering department institute of science tokyo formerly tokyo institute of technology japan her current research interests include networked dynamical systems atomic clocks nonlinear systems adaptive control and chaos theory best shubhendu
