Subject: invitation for webinar by prof falko dressler on th february wednesday at pm in bharti school
Body: dear school faculty members and dear students a webinar is being organised by bharti school by prof falko dressler chair for telecommunication networks school of electrical engineering and computer science tu berlin on the topic virtualized edge computing in the vehicular micro cloud the details are as follows date wednesday time pm ist venue hybrid mode bharti school committee room room no iia bharti school of telecom link abstract prof falko dressler will discuss the challenges and opportunities of distributed data management solutions ranging from the mobile edge to the data centers modern g networks promise to provide all means for communication in this domain particularly when integrating mobile edge computing mec however it turns out that despite the many advantages it is unlikely that such services will be provided with sufficient coverage as a novel concept virtualized edge computing vedge have been proposed that bridges this gap we present a learningbased approach to make such an vedge resilient to dynamics failures and even malicious attacks in particular we contrast centralized and federated learning approaches and reinforcement based approaches speaker’s profile falko dressler is full professor and chair for telecommunication networks at the school of electrical engineering and computer science tu berlin he received his msc and phd degrees from the dept of computer science university of erlangen in and respectively dr dressler has been associate editorinchief for ieee trans on network science and engineering ieee trans on mobile computing and elsevier computer communications as well as an editor for journals such as ieeeacm trans on networking elsevier ad hoc networks and elsevier nano communication networks he has been chairing conferences such as ieee infocom acm mobisys acm mobihoc ieee vnc ieee globecom he authored the textbooks selforganization in sensor and actor networks published by wiley sons and vehicular networking published by cambridge university press he has been an ieee distinguished lecturer as well as an acm distinguished speaker dr dressler is an ieee fellow an acm fellow and an aaia fellow he is a member of the german national academy of science and engineering acatech he has been serving on the ieee comsoc conference council and the acm sigmobile executive committee his research objectives include next generation wireless communication systems in combination with distributed machine learning and edge computing for improved resiliency application domains include the internet Subject: inae delhi chapter and department of civil and environmental engineering at iit delhi seminar by prof dr rajesh dhakal on january friday pm ist in a hybrid mode
Body: dear madamsir delhi chapter of indian national academy of engineering inae and department of civil and environmental engineering at indian institute of technology iit delhi are jointly organizing a seminar event in a hybrid mode details of which are given below seminar titled investigations and innovations in seismic performance of nonstructural elements sponse a journey towards lowdamagelowloss buildings abstract current versions of seismic design codes worldwide aim to achieve lifesafety in severe and rare earthquakes as a result not many modern buildings have collapsed and people have rarely died in such buildings even in severe earthquakes however current seismic design principles allow structures to damage even in minormoderate shakings consequently modern building stocks have suffered damage in all recent earthquakes and the financial losses to the community arising from damage and downtime of these buildings have been unacceptably high in many earthquakes observations from recent earthquakes have highlighted that the majority of seismic losses in buildings are attributable to damage of secondary components known as nonstructural elements ie nses hence enhancing seismic performance of nonstructural elements is a must if we want to minimize financial implications of future earthquakes unsurprisingly awareness of the importance of sponse research has significantly increased lately and researchers are striving to better understand the inherent weaknesses in the current nses design and installation practices and to develop lowdamage solutions for key nses this presentation will provide an overview of the research conducted in new zealand to i better understand the inherent weaknesses in the way nses are designed and installed in buildings currently ii development of innovative solutions for some drift and acceleration sensitive nses to remain damage free during moderatesevere earthquakes and iii experimental validation of superior seismic performance of the proposed lowdamage nse designs through static and dynamic tests biography of the speaker professor rajesh dhakal is the head of civil engineering department at university of canterbury in new zealand where he is also a chartered professional engineer he completed bachelor of civil engineering degree from tribhuvan university nepal in with a gold medal and master of structural engineering from ait thailand with another gold medal he received phd from the university of tokyo in his current research interests are i seismic performance of nonstructural elements ii modelling analysis testing and design of rc structures and iii seismic loss minimization in buildings in his career so far prof dhakal has supervised more than postgraduate research students and authored more than peerreviewed technical papers in different facets of structural and earthquake engineering based on his research outputs and impact prof dhakal has been ranked among the top structural engineering researchers in the world by elsevier and researchgate prof dhakal has served in multiple national and international panels including his appointment as an expert advisor to the government of nepal for postearthquake reconstruction following the gorkha earthquake and the subsequent review of nepals building seismic design standard nbc prof dhakal was elected the president of the international association of sponse seismic performance of nonstructural elements in tenure completed in prof dhakal has received more than a dozen awards for research excellence in multiple countries most notable among these are the prestigious ivan skinner award for advancement of earthquake engineering research in new zealand and the nepal engineers association special contribution award conferred by the prime minister of nepal for outstanding service and leadership in the aftermath of the gorkha nepal earthquake prof dhakal has delivered dozens of invitedplenarykeynote lectures in top institutes and conferences worldwide and served as an editorial board member for several international journals since prof dhakal has been serving as the chief editor of the bulletin of the nz society for earthquake engineering in recognition of his contribution and leadership in earthquake engineering prof dhakal was made a fellow of engineering nz in and a fellow of the nz society for Subject: talk announcement a holistic view on robust distributed cooperative control of networked systems
Body: dear all dr maitreyee dutta is visiting the department and will deliver a talk at pm tomorrow in the ee committee room title a holistic view on robust distributed cooperative control of networked systems datetime jan pm venue ee committee room abstract over the century it has been observed that collaboration in a coordinated fashion among several dynamical systems facilitates the execution of complex tasks such as scientific reconnaissance homeland security search and rescue operations surveillance of ecosystems to name a few naturally information sharing is a key element of cooperative control in order to ensure that the systems reach an agreement over certain variables of interest several conventional algorithms rely on bidirectional communication and availability of centralised data reliance on global information that is shared in an undirected connected manner requires a large communication bandwidth and can lead to catastrophic breakdown of the interconnected network due to a single point of failure moreover several consensual algorithms assume by default that the data received by any system in the network is accurate it is well known that sensors embedded in any robotic system are susceptible to faults which can manifest themselves as persistent constant or timevarying offsets and noises in the measurements direct implementation of faulty measurements in the control loop of any physical system can not only reduce efficiency but also cause accidents in severe cases if we take fidelity to reality into account the consensus problem becomes particularly challenging when there is a restriction in the communication bandwidth and the transmitted measurements are faulty this presentation will cover some distributed control theoretic algorithms robust to sensor faults for different types of systems communicating through a unilateral network the presented work will showcase some of the contributions from my phd and postdoctoral research to the field of control of multiagents systems bio maitreyee dutta received her btech degree in electrical engineering and mtech degree in control industrial automation from national institute of technology silchar india in and respectively she received her doctoral degree from centre for systems and control iit bombay in her phd thesis focused on robust distributed control algorithms for networked systems she is currently working as a postdoctoral researcher in systems and control engineering department institute of science tokyo formerly tokyo institute of technology japan her current research interests include networked dynamical systems atomic clocks nonlinear systems adaptive control and chaos theory best shubhendu shubhendu bhasin professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india web email tel o r fax

Subject: department seminar by prof soumen sarkar on january at am
Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department seminar by prof soumen sarkar from iit madras on january wednesday at am the details are given below title lscategory and topological complexity of real torus manifolds and dold manifolds of real torus type venue room no academic complex west b date and time january wednesday at am speaker prof soumen sarkar abstract the real torus manifolds are a generalization of small covers which are a topological generalization of smooth projective real toric varieties and the dold manifolds of real torus type are a class of nontrivial fibre bundles over the projective product spaces with real torus manifolds as fibres in this talk ill compute the exact value of the lscategory of these two types of manifolds then well obtain sharp bounds on their topological complexities ill show that under certain hypotheses the topological complexities of real torus manifolds of dimension n are either n or n well discuss on the bounds for the topological complexity of generalized real bott manifolds and in many cases the difference between these upper and lower bounds is less than this is a part of a joint work with navnath and koushik all are cordially invited to attend best regards mathematics department colloquium team

Subject: seminar on rheology of polymers for biomedical applications at cbme
Body: dear all the centre of biomedical engineering iit delhi cordially invites you to a talk by dr kartik pondicherry anton paar austria details mentioned below refreshments will be served date time monday am to pm title advanced rheological testing of polymers abstract rheology is the science of flow and deformation behavior of materials and it is extensively used to study the viscoelastic properties of polymers from mapping the shearratedependent viscosity to studying the temperaturedependent properties such as its glasstransition temperature softening point etc rheology also helps in determining the processingrelated parameters of these materials the current talk offers an introduction to rheology with a special focus on testing of polymers used in medical field from hydrogels to implant materials this includes conventional rotational and oscillatory rheometry along with information about dynamic mechanical analysis dma this talk also brushes on tribological testing of such polymers wherein the friction and wear behavior of these samples is studied examples of reallife applications include different forms of catheters mammary implants tissues contact lenses etc speaker bio dr kartik pondicherry holds a degree in engineering in metallurgy and materials science from india masters in nanotechnology from germany and a doctorate in tribology from austria dr pondicherry has been working extensively in the field of tribology for the past plus years and is associated with the rheometry department at anton paar for the past years he has been actively involved in the scientific community including stle in addition to authoring scientific publications he has also authored book chapters and numerous white papers showcasing innovative test and analysis methodologies eom

Subject: departmental seminar dr sonal jain dst inspire faculty at university of delhi th jan pm ksbs committee room
Body: dear all we invite you to the ksbs departmental talk on th january at pm in the ksbs committee room the speaker is dr sonal jain a dst inspire faculty at university of delhi working in the fields of genetics epigenetics and genomics all are cordially invited details may be found below speaker dr sonal jain dst inspire faculty at university of delhi date th january time pm venue ksbs committee room title biological signatures across time from ancient dna and epigenetics to disease risk prediction abstract this talk presents an integrated research trajectory that spans ancient dna analysis forensic dna phenotyping and epigenetics and aiassisted predictive modelling for noncommunicable diseases ncds beginning with ancient dna studies the work addresses methodological challenges associated with highly degraded genetic material to reconstruct ancestry and phenotypic traits these foundations transition into forensic dna phenotyping focusing on externally visible characteristics inferred from dna and their relevance in investigative and populationspecific contexts the talk then advances to forensic epigenetics highlighting dna methylationbased age estimation and environmentally responsive markers particularly within underrepresented indian populations finally the seminar explores the integration of genetic and epigenetic features into aidriven predictive models for ncd risk moving molecular inference from retrospective reconstruction toward forwardlooking public health applications collectively the work demonstrates how molecular data across time scales can be unified through computational and systemslevel approaches thank you best regards saurabh saurabh raj phd assistant professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: fwd dmse seminar talk by prof mainsh tiwari ucl mechanical engineering th january pm lh
Body: dear all gentle reminder of today’s seminar by prof manish tiwariucl pm at lh details mentioned below thanks and best regards ankur goswami phd associate professor office room no department of materials science and engineering academic complex west b indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india phone mobile original message subject dmse seminar talk by prof mainsh tiwari ucl mechanical engineering th january pm lh date from seminar to allfaculty allstudents cc rmalik replyto rmalik dear all we are pleased to invite you to the next talk in our departmental seminar series prof mainsh tiwari ucl mechanical engineering uk will be visiting our department and delivering an engaging seminar on his research you are warmly encouraged to attend the session if you wish to interact with prof mainsh tiwari please get in touch with prof ankur goswami details of the talk title safe and sustainable slippery surfaces date time january pm pm venue lh speaker prof mainsh tiwari ucl mechanical engineering uk abstract there are numerous wellknown and extensively studied examples of slippery surfaces in plants such as lotus leaves rose petals and pitcher plants and in animals including polar bear fur shark skin and butterfly wings however these elegant natural systems have not evolved to meet the severe robustness requirements that practical engineered surfaces are often required to withstand in this presentation i will focus on two strategies to address some of these limitations first i will demonstrate how mechanical flexibility can be exploited to enhance robustness second i will show how pitcherplantinspired surfaces can be designed to withstand highspeed liquid impacts these strategies could be instrumental in eliminating the use of poly and perfluoroalkyl substances pfas in slippery surface treatments which pose major environmental and human health concerns emerging engineered surface examples based on reticular porous materials will be Body: dear all we are pleased to invite you to the next talk in our departmental seminar series prof mainsh tiwari ucl mechanical engineering uk will be visiting our department and delivering an engaging seminar on his research you are warmly encouraged to attend the session if you wish to interact with prof mainsh tiwari please get in touch with prof ankur goswami details of the talk title safe and sustainable slippery surfaces date time january pm pm venue lh speaker prof mainsh tiwari ucl mechanical engineering uk abstract there are numerous wellknown and extensively studied examples of slippery surfaces in plants such as lotus leaves rose petals and pitcher plants and in animals including polar bear fur shark skin and butterfly wings however these elegant natural systems have not evolved to meet the severe robustness requirements that practical engineered surfaces are often required to withstand in this presentation i will focus on two strategies to address some of these limitations first i will demonstrate how mechanical flexibility can be exploited to enhance robustness second i will show how pitcherplantinspired surfaces can be designed to withstand highspeed liquid impacts these strategies could be instrumental in eliminating the use of poly and perfluoroalkyl substances pfas in slippery surface treatments which pose major environmental and human health concerns emerging engineered surface examples based on reticular porous materials will be presented to demonstrate resilience to liquid impacts at speeds approaching those encountered in category five hurricanes bio professor tiwari is a royal society wolfson fellow and professor of nanoengineering in ucl mechanical engineering he directs the nanoengineered systems laboratory at ucl and serves on Subject: hss seminar series wednesday january pm
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to the next hss seminar on wednesday january by prof abhishek bhati bowling green state university details are below and in the below link poster we look forward to seeing many of you there hss seminar series team date january time pm venue hss committee room ms chair sarbeswar sahoo department of huss iit delhi title ai for the public good exploring the civil society sector’s use of artificial intelligence in india abstract artificial intelligence ai tools such as chatgpt have been used widely by civil society organizations csos however most knowledge about ais use by csos is emerging from practitioners experiences primarily in the global north this research focuses on understanding how csos use generative ai tools to advance their mission and what are the potential pitfalls or challenges of this emerging technology this study employs a mixedmethod research design combining quantitative and qualitative analysis of survey responses and interviews from ngosnonprofit across india and united states us the research examines how csos are adopting and using ai technologies highlighting systematic biases in ai use across the rural–urban divide between large and small organizations and causes supported in doing so this study illuminates both the transformative potential of ai for advancing cso work and the challenges that accompany its adoption and usage the findings from this project will benefit csos and policymakers by helping them understand the impact of disruptive technologies on the global civil society sector speaker bio abhishek bhati is an associate professor of political science at bowling green state university in ohio usa and a – fulbrightnehru scholar his research examines nonprofit studies international development civil society and global politics with particular interest in how nonprofit and civil society organizations navigate resource environments and respond to structural inequalities he also received the prestigious fulbrightnehru fellowship to study the impact of ai technology on the civil society sector in india

Subject: talk announcement prof manish tiwari mechanical engineering university college london on nanoengineered sensors for surgical and interventional sciences
Body: dear all prof manish tiwari from mechanical engineering university college london will give an invited talk on tn january monday at the department of electrical engineering the details are as follows date and time th january monday am onwards venue ee committee room block ii title nanoengineered sensors for surgical and interventional sciences abstract miniature sensors are poised to have a transformative impact on patient outcomes in surgery and interventional healthcare more broadly in this presentation i will begin with introducing nanoengineered pressure and force sensors focusing on their integration into surgical gloves to enhance operative procedures and instrumented childbirth next i will present a neurosurgical example in which these sensorised gloves provide a promising route to improving surgical training through realtime monitoring and deep learningbased assessment of surgical skills next i will discuss the development of flexible nanocomposites for oxygen sensing and respiratory pattern monitoring these technologies are particularly relevant to perioperative and critical care settings and may also find applications in regenerative medicine finally i will present an electrochemical sensing platform based on nanocomposites for the detection of biomarkers associated with sepsis and acute rejection in kidney transplantation i will conclude by outlining current limitations and reflecting on key opportunities for future research bio professor tiwari is a royal society wolfson fellow and professor of nanoengineering in ucl mechanical engineering he directs the nanoengineered systems laboratory at ucl and serves on the management board of ucl institute of healthcare engineering his healthcare research is hosted by the ucl hawkes institute and he is a member of the steering team of ucls manufacturing futures laboratory a new centre dedicated to advanced materials and manufacturing technologies his research has received four prestigious grants from the european research council erc he advises two startup companies is on the board of the royal national orthopaedic hospital nhs trust stanmore and is a member of the editorial teams of three international journals you are invited to attend the talk and interact with prof tiwari best regards dhiman dr dhiman mallick associate professor department of electrical engineering indian institute Subject: navadhi badadhoc hypothesis “fits the data fails the test”
Body: dear all team rsf is happy to announce badadhoc hypothesis “fits the data fails the test” a competition under navadhi of proving absurd yet thoughtfully unscientific hypotheses using science the session would explore how hypothesis evolves sometimes in unexpected ways ever wondered “butterflies could cause cyclones” or “statistical significance increases when deadlines approach” or “eating at rajdhani increases cgpa by ” how about proving something like this now this is not about right or wrong hypotheses and not about labelling ideas as “good” or “bad” instead it’s about understanding • how data shapes hypotheses • how explanations change as new results appear • how small interpretational choices can have large downstream effects the drill is simple a minute presentation on the hypothesis of your choice followed by questions where the participants have to defend their hypothesis who can participate any student registered in iitd how to participate single participation or in a group of maximum where and when lh am – pm dos present a hypothesis of your choice cite all the material used to prove that hypothesis and give credit to the sites used do n’ts no plagiarism allowed the hypothesistheory should not be true and don’t send theories about fictional characters or copyrighted material submit your abstract or description of your hypothesis in the following link by th jan selected participants would receive a link to submit their ppt the audience is the judge and all the participants will receive exciting goodies warm regards team rsf

re integrated photonics seminar pm th jan tue ms by dr anat siddharth iitd mtech applied optics alum
Body: dear all we will have an exciting seminar on tue th jan at pm in ms by one of our mtech applied optics graduates dr anat siddharth who is now cto of deeplight sa located in switzerland germany title lownoise frequencyagile photonic integrated lasers abstract lasers underpin modern science and technology enabling applications from eye surgery to gravitationalwave detection and quantum information processing despite their ubiquity most commercial lasers still rely on decadesold architectures that are bulky costly and limited in coherence and tunability while silicon photonics has enabled scalable and compact optical systems integrated lasers have so far fallen short in delivering the ultrahigh coherence and frequency agility required beyond classical communications in this talk i will present recent breakthroughs achieved during my phd at epfl in hybrid photonicintegrated lasers that bridge this longstanding gap between bulk and integrated systems using waferscale cmoscompatible fabrication we monolithically integrate piezoelectric mems thin films aln pzt on silicon nitride to realize ultralownoise lasers with fast energyefficient frequency tuning this approach enables up to × faster actuation than legacy bulk lasers while maintaining compactness and low power consumption i will also introduce a complementary platform based on pockels materials such as lithium niobate and lithium tantalate enabling photonic integrated extendeddbr edbr lasers with direct electrooptic tuning these devices exhibit low latency high linearity large frequency excursion and flat actuation bandwidths up to mhz together these platforms establish a new class of coherent frequencyagile integrated lasers combining bulklevel performance with waferscale manufacturability they open the door to scalable deployment in demanding applications such as distributed fiberoptic sensing nextgeneration atomic clocks neutralatom quantum computing and quantum key distribution bio anat siddharth is the chief technology officer at deeplight sa and coinventor of the core laser technologies on which the company is built deeplight is a spinoff from epfl and kit developing highperformance photonic integrated lasers and frequency combs for nextgeneration sensing and communication applications anat completed his phd in the laboratory of photonics and quantum measurements at epfl under prof tobias j kippenberg where his research focused on lownoise frequencyagile photonic integrated lasers he did his mtech in applied optics at iit delhi and btech in engineering physics from iit guwahati regards vivek venkataraman associate professor

Subject: ieor seminar series multisectoral decision analytics by dr chaitra gopalappa on dec friday at am
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to the next entry in the industrial engineering and operations research seminar series with a talk given by prof chaitra gopalappa please find appended below the details of the seminar venue ii me committee room time am jan thursday title multisectoral decision analytics addressing barriers through machine learning and operations research abstract health outcomes while directly linked to clinical factors are largely influenced by intersecting socioeconomic environmental behavioral and structural factors broadly referred to as social determinants of health health outcomes can thus serve as a metric and focal point for development of sustainable and equitable public policies and programs such programs include diseaseagnostic multisectoral health intervention strategies ie preventive and interceptive programs that span health and nonhealth sectors such as sustainable food housing and economic programs in addition to clinical care however designing suitable models for such multisectoral decision analyses face multiple barriers due to issues ranging from data sparsity and heterogeneity to computational scalability and policy relevance in this talk taking a public health lens i will discuss some of my labs research at the intersection of machine learning and operations research to address barriers related to largescale modeling multidisease modeling and multisectoral modeling speaker biography chaitra gopalappa phd is an associate professor in mechanical and industrial engineering at the university of massachusetts amherst massachusetts usa her research is in areas of simulation markov decision processes reinforcement learning and machine learning she leads the aiengineering graduate certificate program for the college of engineering she teaches graduate level courses in reinforcement learning and deep learning her research interests are broadly in sociotechnical systems with emphasis on systems thinking to develop sustainable policies and programs she is open to collaborative multidisciplinary work and can contribute to work in data and decision analytics her lab is funded by grants from the us national science foundation national institutes of health us centers for disease control and prevention the world health organization and the university of massachusetts amherst all interested may attend best regards varun varun ramamohan phd associate professor department of mechanical engineering indian institute of technology delhi web

talk announcement numerical discretization schemes that preserve flatness
Body: dear all dr ashutosh jindal is visiting the department and will deliver a talk at pm today in the ee committee room title numerical discretization schemes that preserve flatness datetime jan pm venue ee committee room abstract differential flatness serves as a powerful tool for controlling continuoustime nonlinear systems in problems such as motion planning and trajectory a similar concept known as difference flatness also exists for discretetime systems although many control systems evolve in continuous time control implementation is performed digitally requiring discretization it is well known in the literature that discretization does not necessarily preserve structural properties and it has been established that in general flatness is not preserved under discretization whether exact or approximate in this talk i will discuss a systematic approach to constructing numerical schemes that preserve flatness bio ashutosh jindal received his phd in systems and control from the indian institute of technology bombay where his research focused on feedback linearization of discretized nonlinear systems and the development of structurepreserving methods for digital nonlinear control he is currently a postdoctoral researcher working on higherorder networks and multiagent coordination for autonomous systems his research interests include nonlinear and digital control structurepreserving discretization and networked control of autonomous multiagent systems best shubhendu shubhendu bhasin professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india web email tel o r fax

Subject: talk by padma bhushan sri m on yoga on th jan at pm in dogra hall
Body: dear iitd family all are invited for the talk by padam bhushan sri m on th jan at pm in dogra hall as there are limited seats kindly register yourself using link a brief bio of sri m sri m born mumtaz ali khan in in kerala india is a contemporary spiritual teacher humanitarian and author who bridges traditional indian spirituality with universal human values trained in multiple streams of indian philosophy and yoga he undertook extensive pilgrimages across india studying under eminent saints and sages and integrating insights from vedanta tantra and sufi traditions he is the founder of the satsang foundation and the visionary behind the walk of hope a km national pilgrimage promoting peace harmony and social unity recognised for his contributions to spiritual and social welfare sri m was awarded the padma bhushan by the government of india in his writings including apprentice to a himalayan master and the journey continues blend autobiography spiritual instruction and practical guidance earning him recognition as a modern interpreter of indian spiritual heritage abstract of the talk this talk explores the perspectives of sri m on yoga and meditation as integrated practices for personal and societal transformation moving beyond the perception of yoga as a set of physical postures sri m emphasizes its role as a holistic discipline that cultivates awareness ethical conduct and inner equilibrium meditation in his view is a practical tool for attaining mental clarity emotional balance and selfknowledge enabling practitioners to transcend cultural and religious boundaries the talk highlights the concept of living yoga wherein meditative awareness informs daily actions and relationships bridging personal growth with social responsibility by examining sri ms insights the session seeks to illuminate the applicability of yoga and meditation as transformative tools in contemporary life head nrcvee iit delhi ph

integrated photonics seminar pm th jan tue ms by dr anat siddharth iitd mtech applied optics alum
Body: dear all we will have an exciting seminar on tue th jan at pm in ms by one of our mtech applied optics graduates dr anat siddharth who is now cto of deeplight sa located in switzerland germany title lownoise frequencyagile photonic integrated lasers abstract lasers underpin modern science and technology enabling applications from eye surgery to gravitationalwave detection and quantum information processing despite their ubiquity most commercial lasers still rely on decadesold architectures that are bulky costly and limited in coherence and tunability while silicon photonics has enabled scalable and compact optical systems integrated lasers have so far fallen short in delivering the ultrahigh coherence and frequency agility required beyond classical communications in this talk i will present recent breakthroughs achieved during my phd at epfl in hybrid photonicintegrated lasers that bridge this longstanding gap between bulk and integrated systems using waferscale cmoscompatible fabrication we monolithically integrate piezoelectric mems thin films aln pzt on silicon nitride to realize ultralownoise lasers with fast energyefficient frequency tuning this approach enables up to × faster actuation than legacy bulk lasers while maintaining compactness and low power consumption i will also introduce a complementary platform based on pockels materials such as lithium niobate and lithium tantalate enabling photonic integrated extendeddbr edbr lasers with direct electrooptic tuning these devices exhibit low latency high linearity large frequency excursion and flat actuation bandwidths up to mhz together these platforms establish a new class of coherent frequencyagile integrated lasers combining bulklevel performance with waferscale manufacturability they open the door to scalable deployment in demanding applications such as distributed fiberoptic sensing nextgeneration atomic clocks neutralatom quantum computing and quantum key distribution bio anat siddharth is the chief technology officer at deeplight sa and coinventor of the core laser technologies on which the company is built deeplight is a spinoff from epfl and kit developing highperformance photonic integrated lasers and frequency combs for nextgeneration sensing and communication applications anat completed his phd in the laboratory of photonics and quantum measurements at epfl under prof tobias j kippenberg where his research focused on lownoise frequencyagile photonic integrated lasers he did his mtech in applied optics at iit delhi and btech in engineering physics from iit guwahati regards vivek venkataraman associate professor

Subject: invitation for tejohm a threeday celebration of rural india traditional knowledge systems sustainability and communityled innovation to be held from th to th january at iit delhi
Body: dear all greetings from navchetna student society of crdt and savera student led initiative of iit delhi we are pleased to invite all students staff members and faculty members of iit delhi to tejohm a threeday celebration of rural india traditional knowledge systems sustainability and communityled innovation to be held from th to th january at iit delhi as part of crdt’s foundation week celebrations inspired by the ideals of swami vivekananda tejohm draws upon his vision of nationbuilding rooted in the upliftment of villages empowerment of communities selfreliance and harmony between knowledge ethics and service tejohm seeks to create a living interactive platform where academia grassroots practitioners artisans innovators and students come together to engage with rural realities beyond textbooks and classrooms the event celebrates rural livelihoods indigenous knowledge sustainability practices crafts and social innovation highlighting their relevance in today’s development discourse a key feature of tejohm is experiential learning where participants will have the opportunity to • interact directly with artisans grassroots innovators and rural entrepreneurs • explore live displays and exhibitions of artisanal crafts traditional technologies and rural products • engage in dialogues panel discussions cultural performances and interactive sessions that bridge theory with practice this event will also give us the opportunity to see the national award winning artisans and witness their craft in action and to have hands on experience we warmly invite you to be part of tejohm and contribute to this collective celebration of india’s rural heritage knowledge traditions and future possibilities we look forward to your enthusiastic participation with regards head crdt indian institute of technology iit delhi new delhi india o fax email

infrastructure finance at the hong kong university of science and technology carbon neutrality climate change thrust he obtained his phd in climate policy and finance from eth zurich in he researches technologies this feedback in cost reductions while learning places project developers in precarious situation invest now or wait until technology matures and costs reduce this workshop imparts modeling skills to attendees as they learn to recognize real option value embedded in innovative technologies and how that value can be influenced by policy choices candidates are requested to carry a laptop and functioning license of microsoft excel first half of the workshop will be spent on fundamentals of real option pricing followed by modeling of dairy industry decarbonization please note a second workshop on climate innovation financing geared toward phd candidates and participants interested in pursuing research will be organized at pm at the same venue interested participants are infrastructure assets while aspects of innovation finance and infrastructure finance along with their policydriven approach are well examined independently the concurrence of innovation finance and Subject: hss seminar series tuesday january pm
Body: dear all date january time pm venue seminar hall iit delhi chair arjun ghosh department of huss iit delhi title not only a trend why digital humanities matter in an era of intensifying technological change abstract in this lecture i argue that incorporating the digital humanities into education is not simply valuableit is more vital than ever it is far more than a question of keeping up with innovation it concerns the future viability of humanistic critique while computational systems are reshaping the ways we encounter texts images and soundand more generally access to information and the construction of human memorywe must proceed with significant caution in much of the global majority world where the telling of history has too often been orchestrated elsewhere it may be tempting to regard such advances as peripheral yet i contend that these emergent algorithmic regimes hold the potential to reaffirm rather than redress longstanding epistemic and narrative inequities speaker bio david wrisley is a comparative medievalist and digital humanist his research straddles the domains of late medieval court culture mediterranean studies multilingual corpora analysis and the spatial humanities he founded and organized the first digital humanities training institute in the middle east in beirut in please see the link below for poster

Body: the evolutionary boundaries and businesseconomic dynamics of the “new” space economy speaker prof anthony p d’costa honorary professorial fellow university of melbourne australia whenwhere at pm in academic complex west abstract the lunar landing by isro with chandrayaan in and the bringing back of a carbonrich sample also in from bennu an asteroid that is billion years old by nasa are recent examples of space projects undertaken by governments in search for scientific knowledge that also promises benefits for humanity less known are the subtle yet visible shifts taking place in the wider space sector with private business participation thus giving rise to a “new” space economy nse there is considerable research on the dynamics of different industries and sectors analyzing the technological economic business institutional and policy dimensions how relevant are these for nse in this exploratory work informed by the recently published the oxford handbook of the new space economy this presentation briefly addresses first what is nse second identifies and disaggregates some of the key forces behind nse and its growing importance to the economy and third offers a basic understanding of the anticipated social and economic development implications of the wider evolving space economy it concludes with some ethical dilemmas associated with extraterrestrial activities in outer space speaker bio anthony p d’costa is an honorary professorial fellow university of melbourne he has taught at the university of washington national university of singapore copenhagen business school university of melbourne and the university of alabama in huntsville he has fourteen books to his credit and is widely published in the areas of the political economy of development in india and east asian industrialization globalization and economic development he has been a recipient of numerous fellowships including fulbrighthays american institute of indian studies abe of the japan foundation unuwider helsinki korea foundation and posco at the east west center honolulu his most recent publication is the oxford handbook of the new space economy while his th book indian business economic development and the jobs dilemma in the twentyfirst century will be also published by oxford university press in

Body: dear all we are pleased to invite you to the gyan ganga distinguished lecture series on river sustainability organized by the nmcgiitddutch collaboratory for intelligent river systems and clean yamuna center of excellence on water indrivers we will be joined in person by prof pierre kirstetter professor school of meteorology school of civil engineering and environmental science university of oklahoma he will share the outlook on probabilistic radar quantitative precipitation estimates and quantification of extremes event details talk quantitative precipitation estimation with weather radar discussion and outlook date january time am pm venue committee room department of civil and environmental engineering iit delhi event poster online ms teams link th gyan ganga distinguished lecture on river sustainability prof pierre kirstetter meetingjoin microsoft teams about the lecture progress in precipitation estimation is critical to advancing weather and water budget studies and predicting natural hazards caused by extreme events from the local to the global scales weather radar uniquely captures key precipitation characteristics such as its spatial and temporal distribution because the measurement is indirect quantitatively interpreting the radar information content on precipitation can improve by complementing any deterministic best estimate with explicit estimation of uncertainty and extremes through probabilistic approaches we will address the impact of probabilistic radar quantitative precipitation estimates qpe on understanding hydrometeorological processes and hydrologic applications weather radar emerges as a cornerstone for the global understanding of water fluxes an outlook on radar qpe for hydrology and quantification of extremes will be presented that includes the expected impact of innovations such as the phasedarray technology about the speaker prof kirstetter holds a dipl ing msc eng in civil engineering and environmental science from the grenoble institute of technology earned in he also obtained an msc in geosciences and a phd in meteorology from grenoble alps university france in and respectively from to he contributed to the preparation of the meghatropiques satellite mission focused on the water cycle with the french space agency cnes in he joined the university of oklahoma ou to lead the development of the ounoaa ground validation multiradarmultisensor system gvmrms this initiative fostered collaboration between nasa and noaa enhancing science synergy and technology exchange with applications in numerical and weather prediction natural disaster prediction hydrology and the study of the global water cycle pierres expertise lies in integrating uncertainty and risk into precipitation estimation thereby enhancing the communication of severe weather and flood hazard predictability to directly benefit society pierre has supervised over masters and doctoral students postdoctoral and research scientists at the university of oklahoma as well as from various national and international universities and research institutes several of these students have received prestigious awards he is an associate editor ae for the journal of hydrology and a former ae for the ams journal of hydrometeorology pierre chaired the th international precipitation conference and has been awarded the international precipitation Body: dear all we are pleased to invite you to the gyan ganga distinguished lecture series on river sustainability organized by the nmcgiitddutch collaboratory for intelligent river systems and clean yamuna center of excellence on water indrivers we will be joined in person by prof rao s govindaraju vice president of institutes and centers at discovery park christopher b and susan s burke distinguished professor lyles school of civil and construction engineering purdue university west lafayette in us he will share the recent developments in assessing uncertainties in water quality estimates using river stream networks event details talk assessing watershed health and sustainability through stream networks date january time pm pm venue committee room department of civil and environmental engineering iit delhi event poster about the lecture stream networks serve as corridors for movement of water and associated constituents and are critical for maintaining ecosystem functions water and contaminant fluxes are used to assess watershed health and sustainability in terms of reliability resilience and vulnerability indices however limited and sporadic data availability make this a challenging task this presentation will explore the use of limited data and the use of statistical techniques to quantify uncertainty in water quality estimates and the subsequent propagation of uncertainty in the assessment of water bodies for sustainability in the upper midwest of usa implications for locations with limited and ungauged locations will be discussed watershed hydrology and climatic influences he is interested in developing algorithms for analyzing and learning from hydrologic data he specializes in problems dealing with uncertainty and spatial variability his scholarly accomplishments include numerous peerreviewed journal articles four books and twentyfive book chapters his research work has been funded by various agencies such as nsf epa dod and doe he has chaired several national level committees and has served on the editorial boards of two journals he served as the editorinchief of journal of hydrologic engineering of american Subject: event workshop on financing of lowcarbon innovative technologies
Body: dear students and faculty members we are pleased to invite you to a part workshop on ‘financing of lowcarbon innovative technologies’ to be delivered by dr anurag gumber assistant professor climate infrastructure finance hong kong university of science and technology details for both parts are given below we warmly encourage all students and faculty members to attend and participate in the discussion about speaker anurag gumber is an assistant professor in climate infrastructure finance at the hong kong university of science and technology carbon neutrality climate change thrust he obtained his phd in climate policy and finance from eth zurich in he researches at the intersection of technology innovation asset finance and infrastructure development his research investigates how lowcarbon energy technologies mature from a financing point of view how financial actors such as banks and institutional investors can increase investments to lowcarbon projects and how the development processes for building such lowcarbon projects can be derisked prior to obtaining his phd anurag worked in industry for over seven years advising several governments development banks and infrastructure investors he holds a master’s degree in public administration from harvard university a bachelor’s degree from birla institute of technology science pilani and the cfa designation workshop part details workshop title ‘financing of lowcarbon innovative technologies’ part basic rsvp link to attend who should attend workshop is intended for participants across all levels of experience event address lh lecture hall complex date and time january lunch will be served workshop part details workshop title ‘financing of lowcarbon innovative technologies’ part advanced rsvp link to attend who should attend phdlevel candidates and those interested in pursuing research event address lh lecture hall complex date and time january lunch will be available from pm abstract part decarbonization policy can be summarized as a journey up the technology abatement curve cheaper lowcarbon innovations are financed before more expensive ones with targets used to propel innovation and learning in hardtoabate sectors to bring down future abatement costs of costlier technologies this feedback in cost reductions while learning places project developers in precarious situation – invest now or wait until technology matures and costs reduce this workshop imparts modeling skills to attendees as they learn to recognize real option value embedded in innovative technologies and how that value can be influenced by policy choices candidates are requested to carry a laptop and functioning license of microsoft excel first half of the workshop will be spent on fundamentals of real option pricing followed by modeling of dairy industry decarbonization please note a second workshop on climate innovation financing geared toward phd candidates and participants interested in pursuing research will be organized at pm at the same venue interested participants are welcome to attend this workshop as well abstract part netzero pathways to mitigate the effects of climate change require substantial finance and mass development of low carbon technology infrastructure assets while aspects of innovation finance and infrastructure finance along with their policydriven approach are well examined independently the concurrence of innovation finance and mass development is unparalleled as a result policymakers must guide investments into innovative technologies beyond early stages until social goals of decarbonization are met this requires not to merely subsidize projects for feasibility sake but to create a substantive and diverse financial system surrounding lowcarbon technologies in this workshop we will dive into two main frameworks in transitions literature namely technology innovation systems tis and multilevel perspective mlp that provide analytical constructs for analyzing such financial development accordingly we will discuss the growth of key technologies globally and endeavor to apply these frameworks on india’s industrialclimate policy please note that this workshop is geared towards phd candidates or those interested in pursuing research majority of the workshop will be a discussion on the theoretical frameworks followed with some time for discussion on india’ industrialclimate policy and possible research directions attendees will be required to read key papers shared by the presenter prior to the workshop the paper will be shared by th jan candidates are requested to carry a laptop and a functioning license of microsoft excel for any queries please contact ashwini mudgal or ekta baranwal warm regards dr kaveri iychettira and prof ambuj sagar school of public policy

Subject: seminar on chinas decarbonization pathways and dis similarities with india by dr anurag gumber hong kong university of science and technology
Body: dear students and faculty members we are pleased to invite you to seminar on chinas decarbonization pathways and dis similarities with india to be delivered by dr anurag gumber assistant professor climate infrastructure finance hong kong university of science and technology we warmly encourage all students and faculty members to attend and participate in the discussion kindly use this link to rsvp and let us know if you will be able to attend the session workshop details venue lhc lecture hall complex iit delhi date and time th january tea and snacks will be served about the speaker anurag gumber is an assistant professor in climate infrastructure finance at the hong kong university of science and technology carbon neutrality climate change thrust he obtained his phd in climate policy and finance from eth zurich in he researches at the intersection of technology innovation asset finance and infrastructure development his research investigates how lowcarbonenergy technologies mature from a financing point of view how financial actors such as banks and institutional investors can increase investments to lowcarbon projects and how the development processes for building such lowcarbon projects can be derisked prior to obtaining his phd anurag worked in industry for over seven years advising several governments development banks and infrastructure investors he holds a masters degree in public administration from harvard university a bachelors degree from birla institute of technology science pilani and the cfa designation abstract despite leading renewable energy installations chinas energy sector investment is heavily skewed towards solar and wind in this seminar we will discuss a recent work from climate infrastructure and finance group at hkust guangzhou that analyzes investment requirements across models and scenarios to assess chinas energy technology investment needs and choices we will discuss the extraordinarily wide range of estimated capital needs among models and across scenarios with chinas lowcarbon transition requiring average annual capital investment of billion including usd billion in the energy technologies we will also discuss the primary drivers of such variation and two distinct choices that china faces namely a more capitalintensive renewablecentric pathway that continues public and private overinvestment in solar and wind but demands higher grid readiness investments or a lower capital nuclearcentric pathway that relies on dispatchable baseload generation with minimal integrationrelated costs but depends wholly on public investments and fiscal stability at the end we will make a comparison of indias choices with authors research for any queries please contact ashwini mudgal or ekta baranwal warm regards dr kaveri iychettira and prof ambuj sagar school of public policy

Subject: photonics seminar pm th jan wed ms by samyak gothi iitd btech engg phys alum
Body: dear all we will have an exciting seminar on wed th jan at pm in ms by one of our recent btech engg physics graduates samyak gothi who is now pursuing his phd in the floquet lab at the university of maryland title applications of kerrnonlinearity towards synthetic frequency dimensions and lidar abstract photonics has become a powerful and versatile field shaping both our understanding of fundamental physical phenomena and a wide range of modern technologies on the fundamental side the emerging area of topological photonics explores how light can exhibit robust protected behaviors analogous to those found in topological insulators at the same time photonics underpins many practical technologies including light detection and ranging lidar which has attracted growing attention in recent for its role in sensing and autonomous navigation our group recently proposed a protocol to realize quantized topological pumping using electrooptic modulation eom the conventional eom can be replaced fourwavemixing braggscattering fwmbs process thereby relaxing the bandwidth and materialplatform constraints associated with eoms however this comes with a tradeoff kerr nonlinearities such as crossphase modulation can significantly degrade topological pumping we identify the regimes of pumping and devise techniques to preserve its quantization in a complementary direction we use the recently pioneered kerrinduced synchronization kis to enhance the sensitivity and speed of the existing frequency comb based lidar systems both of these are steps towards advancement of alloptical technologies sridhar et al nat phys – moille et al nature – regards vivek venkataraman associate professor

Subject: advertisement for crl microwave filters for wireless system design
Body: dear students i am offering the course crl microwave filters for wireless system design” this semester the course will run on mondays care committee room and wednesdays care seminar room both rooms are located at ground floor of blockiii the course is broadly divided in two halves the first one looks at the filters from system perspective of wireless communications wireless communication architectures especially those of satellites communications mobile communications and ultrawideband uwb communications will be taught and various parameters of filters in these architectures will be studied the second half will deal with approximation of electromagnetics into circuit theory and designing of lowpass prototype filters for butterworth chebyeshev and elliptic responses finally the course will close on synthesizing characteristic polynomials for the above mentioned filters from here on a practitioner can simply follow textbook recipes for designing filters of their desired specifications the course is particularly interesting for students interested in microwave filters wireless communication system hardware and network circuit theory the course contents are communication systems radio spectrum and information noise in communication systems requirements of filter networks circuit theory approximations linear networks in time domain and in frequency domain lowpass prototype characteristics lowpass prototype filter functions computer aided synthesis of characteristic polynomials generation of novel filter functions i encourage you to register for this course the only prerequisite is undergraduate circuits concepts kd

Subject: me guest talk by prof gustaaf b jacobs on discontinuous galerkin spectral element dgsem code developments for computations of chemically reacting flow
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the seminar by prof gustaaf b jacobs professor department of aerospace engineering san diego state university scheduled on friday th january at pm details of the talk are given below date and time friday th january from pm to pm venue me seminar room block title discontinuous galerkin spectral element dgsem code developments for computations of chemically reacting flow presenter prof gustaaf b jacobs abstract the computational fluid dynamics of turbulent chemically reacting flow is central to design of modern energy systems such as hydrogenfueled gas turbines and rotating detonation combustors the complexity of the nonlinear exchange of momentum and energy has made it very challenging to find highfidelity solutions to this type of problem and has left essential physical phenomena poorly understood due to the large number of scales that coexist in this problem it is beneficial to develop highorder accurate algorithms first highorder schemes are better at propagating waves over long distances and capturing small scales secondly they do so with dramatically reduced resources eg a coarse grid and increased efficiency for a given accuracy highorder methods thus allow for faster prototyping in this talk i will discuss a semilagrangian method that solves the socalled filteredmass density function model a probability density function model for the transport of species the approximation is shown to be consistent with excellent numerical stability and accuracy characteristics bio professor gustaaf jacobs received a msc in aerospace engineering from delft university of technology in where after graduation he was appointed to research associate he received a phd in mechanical engineering from the university of illinois at chicago following graduation in august of he was appointed visiting assistant professor in the division of applied mathematics at brown university he later combined this position with a postdoctoral fellowship at the department of mechanical engineering at the massachusetts institute of technology as of august he was appointed assistant professor of aerospace engineering at san diego state university and was promoted to associate professor in august of in he was promoted to full professor he graduated with a honor propaedeuse from delft university of technology in he was awarded a university fellowship at the university of illinois he received an afosr young investigator award in and became an associate fellow of the american institute of aeronautics and astronautics in all interested are welcome to join the talk thank you pratik das and abhishek das department of mechanical engineering iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: photonics seminar pm th jan wed ms by samyak gothi iitd btech engg phys alum
Body: dear all we will have an exciting seminar on wed th jan at pm in ms by one of our recent btech engg physics graduates samyak gothi who is now pursuing his phd in the floquet lab at the university of maryland title applications of kerrnonlinearity towards synthetic frequency dimensions and lidar abstract photonics has become a powerful and versatile field shaping both our understanding of fundamental physical phenomena and a wide range of modern technologies on the fundamental side the emerging area of topological photonics explores how light can exhibit robust protected behaviors analogous to those found in topological insulators at the same time photonics underpins many practical technologies including light detection and ranging lidar which has attracted growing attention in recent for its role in sensing and autonomous navigation our group recently proposed a protocol to realize quantized topological pumping using electrooptic modulation eom the conventional eom can be replaced fourwavemixing braggscattering fwmbs process thereby relaxing the bandwidth and materialplatform constraints associated with eoms however this comes with a tradeoff kerr nonlinearities such as crossphase modulation can significantly degrade topological pumping we identify the regimes of pumping and devise techniques to preserve its quantization in a complementary direction we use the recently pioneered kerrinduced synchronization kis to enhance the sensitivity and speed of the existing frequency comb based lidar systems both of these are steps towards advancement of alloptical technologies sridhar et al nat phys – moille et al nature – regards vivek venkataraman associate professor

Subject: reminder departmental seminar on friday january by prof bismark singh
Body: dear all it is our great pleasure to announce a departmental seminar by prof bismark singh from the university of southampton uk on friday january at am the details of the talk are given below speaker prof bismark singh university of southampton uk title balancing user accessibility and facility load fairness in undesirable facility location problems abstract typically within facility location problems fairness is defined in terms of accessibility of users however for facilities perceived as undesirable by communities hosting them fairness between the usage of facilities becomes especially important limited research exists on this notion of fairness in a series of works we have attempted to close this gap by developing new classes of combinatorial optimization models for the allocation of populations of users to facilities such that access for users is balanced with a fair utilization of facilities the optimality conditions of the underlying nonconvex quadratic models state the precise balance between accessibility and fairness further we define new axioms of fairness and a metric to quantify the extent to which fairness is achieved in both optimal and suboptimal allocations we show that a continuous relaxation of our central model is sufficient to achieve a perfect extent of fairness while a special case reduces to the classical notion of proportional fairness we present computational results using actual data from the state of bavaria in germany the main part of this work is based on two articles published with my students both in the informs journal on computing in ongoing work we are studying supermodularity properties of this new class of objective functions time and venue friday january at am at room no academic complex west b all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team dr ekata saha assistant professor department of mathematics indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: national youth day interaction with prof h c verma on january
Body: dear students on the occasion of national youth day january commemorating the birth anniversary of swami vivekananda iit delhi will be hosting a special interactive session with prof h c verma national youth day celebrates the spirit of curiosity the courage to question and the pursuit of knowledge with purposevalues that resonate deeply with prof vermas life and work for generations of students his concepts of physics has not merely been a textbook but a gateway to clear thinking and a deeper understanding of science beyond his widely read books prof verma is a distinguished physicist and educator having served for many years as a professor of physics at iit kanpur with contributions to both experimental nuclear physics and science education reform in india the session will cover themes such as learning and teaching mistakes and growth science education in india what it means to remain young in thought while contributing meaningfully to society the format will include an interview with prof verma followed by interaction with students we invite all students to submit their questions in advance through the microsoft form link provided below common themes emerging from these submissions will be taken up during the session along with opportunities for live interaction link form deadline january we strongly encourage everyone to participate and make the most of this rare opportunity to interact with one of indias most respected educators and thinkers best regards parth gautam deputy general secretary ug curriculum research cocurricular and academic interaction council caic

Subject: ay semester ell semiconductor process technology
Body: dear students i am floating the following elective course for this semester title semiconductor process technology course code ell credits slot a m th am prerequisites ell ell mll pyl mcl mcl cll esl ddl apl objectives on successful completion of this course the student will acquire an understanding of unit processes and tools involved in front end of line feol and back end of line beol fabrication of sibased integrated circuits including semiconductor devices such as mosfets passives interconnectsrouting planarization integration and basics of packaging this course will prepare them for advanced courses in process optimization and packaging and to work in industry contents semiconductor materials semiconductor growthpurification crystal structure defects doping diffusion unit processes in device fabrication including oxidation ion implantation rapid thermal processing optical lithography cleanroom basics vacuum systems plasma processes etching chemical and physical gas chemistry physical vapor deposition chemical vapor deposition cvd mocvd mbeald planarization and process integration device yield introduction to device and system level packaging target cohort ell is suitable for ug students who are interested in seeking a career in high technology industry the growth of which in india is being catalyzed by the indian semiconductor mission ism in india global jobs in semiconductor industry or research in allied areas this course will run concurrently with ell ic technology ell semiconductor process technology additional topics which are optional for the ell cohort may include soifdsoi technology organic lowdimensional carbon based materials process simulation using industrystandard software ug students crediting ell will be welcome to participate in this phase if they wish it is being offered separately as not all ug students may satisfy the credit requirements formally for a level course such as ell ell while prior knowledge of how devices work would be nice it is not essential to following this course since device processing careers tend to attract students with backgrounds in heat transfer mass transfer and design unsurprisingly semiconductor manufacturers such as tsmc globalfoundries intel etc tend to be rather wellknown as employers of chemical engineering and mechanical engineering students besides electrical engineering and physics majors the erp system should allow you to register if you have credited any of the courses listed in the prerequisites however if you have difficulty in doing so please send me email cheers Subject: mathematics department seminar prof tumulesh solanky january
Body: dear colleagues and students we are pleased to announce a department seminar to be delivered by prof tumulesh solanky an esteemed alumnus of our department and currently a faculty member at the university of new orleans the details of the seminar are given below date january time pm – pm venue academic complex west b title on strategies for generalizing the partition problem formulation abstract partitioning treatments by comparing them to a control treatment is a fundamental problem in statistics for over eighty years this problem has been studied by numerous researchers using a variety of designs to establish partitioning criteria and optimize data collection strategies in this presentation we examine several key formulations from the literature through the lens of practical application particular emphasis is placed on the design proposed by tong which extended bechhofer’s indifferencezone concept to partition treatments relative to a control population tong’s formulation unified several earlier approaches and had since attracted considerable interest building on tong’s versatile formulation we propose a generalization that partitions treatments within the indifference zone as a distinct and identifiable group while preserving the foundational concept of the indifference zone we show that tong’s formulation arises as a limiting case of the proposed generalization for the generalized formulation we present both a purely sequential procedure and a twostage procedure together with their theoretical properties finally an illustrative example is provided to demonstrate the proposed generalization and to compare it with other procedures in the literature you can read more about the speaker at all faculty members research scholars and students are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team rahul singh assistant professor department of mathematics indian institute of technology delhi

Body: to all at indian institute of technology iit delhi dear madam sir merry christmas delhi chapter of indian national academy of engineering inae is organizing a national seminar event in a hybrid mode jointly with department of civil and environmental engineering at indian institute of technology iit delhi details of which are given below seminar on title national education policy nep envisioning implementation in engineering and technology curricula abstract the national education policy nep outlines the vision of new education system of india that is bharat nep represents a transformative vision for indias education system with significant implications for engineering and technology curricula it emphasizes holistic multidisciplinary and flexible learning to prepare graduates for a rapidly evolving technological landscape implementing nep in engineering education requires rethinking curriculum design pedagogy assessment and institutional culture a core feature of nep is the shift from rigid to multidisciplinary education engineering curricula are encouraged to integrate humanities social sciences management and ethics alongside technical subjects this approach aims to produce engineers who are not only technically competent but also socially responsible innovative and empathetic problemsolvers the policys provision for multiple entry and exit points offers flexibility to learners and promotes lifelong learning nep also stresses experiential and skillbased learning for engineering and technology programs this translates into greater emphasis on projectbased learning internships industry partnerships and realworld problem solving emerging areas such as artificial intelligence ai machine learning ml data science renewable energy robotics and cybersecurity are to be embedded into curricula to ensure relevance to industry and society faculty development and continuous upskilling become crucial to effectively deliver these modernized programs moving away from rote memorization nep advocates competencybased and influential assessment methods that evaluate conceptual understanding creativity and application technologyenabled learning platforms virtual laboratories and digital resources further support inclusive and scalable education implementing nep in engineering and technology education needs to be done by envisioning a learnercentric flexible and futureready ecosystem successful realization will depend on coordinated efforts by institutions faculty industry and policymakers to align such vision with practice speaker professor dr anil sahasrabudhe fnae biography of speaker professor dr anil sahasrabudhe fnae is currently the chairman of executive committee of the national assessment and accreditation council naac he held responsibilities such as head of mechanical engineering chairman library committee chairman jee dean academic affairs and deputy director at indian institute of technology iit guwahati from to he earned his be degree mechanical engineering in from karnataka university securing first rank and a gold medal masters degree in and phd degree in both from indian institute of science iisc bangalore in between he had brief stints of working as scientific officer in iisc and engineer trainee in tata consulting engineers before starting his teaching career in the newly started northeastern regional institute of science and technology itanagar arunachal pradesh and again in the newly started iit guwahati he is currently chairman of national educational technology Subject: departmental seminar on friday january by prof bismark singh
Body: dear all it is our great pleasure to announce a departmental seminar by prof bismark singh from the university of southampton uk on friday january at am the details of the talk are given below speaker prof bismark singh university of southampton uk title balancing user accessibility and facility load fairness in undesirable facility location problems abstract typically within facility location problems fairness is defined in terms of accessibility of users however for facilities perceived as undesirable by communities hosting them fairness between the usage of facilities becomes especially important limited research exists on this notion of fairness in a series of works we have attempted to close this gap by developing new classes of combinatorial optimization models for the allocation of populations of users to facilities such that access for users is balanced with a fair utilization of facilities the optimality conditions of the underlying nonconvex quadratic models state the precise balance between accessibility and fairness further we define new axioms of fairness and a metric to quantify the extent to which fairness is achieved in both optimal and suboptimal allocations we show that a continuous relaxation of our central model is sufficient to achieve a perfect extent of fairness while a special case reduces to the classical notion of proportional fairness we present computational results using actual data from the state of bavaria in germany the main part of this work is based on two articles published with my students both in the informs journal on computing in ongoing work we are studying supermodularity properties of this new class of objective functions time and venue friday january at am at room no academic complex west b all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team dr ekata saha assistant professor department of mathematics indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india
