Subject: opportunity research internships and projects at mind lab cbme
Body: dear students the mechanobiology of injury and degeneration mind lab at the center for biomedical engineering cbme is looking for motivated and curious students to join us for upcoming research internships and project positions our lab operates at the intersection of physics mechanics and neuroscience with an overarching goal investigate how traumatic brain injuries tbis trigger longterm neurodegeneration we use continuum and molecular simulations based on fundamental physical principles capture the multiscale link between mechanical injuries and protein aggregation project mesoscale emergence of tau condensates at a continuum scale tau is an intrinsically disordered protein crucial for stabilizing microtubules in neurons however under conditions of injury or disease tau undergoes liquidliquid phase separation llps forming condensates that can eventually lead to toxic aggregates this work aims at uncovering the biophysical principles that govern this emergence and determine its evolution into pathological aggregates positions at this time we have the following positions available research internships open to undergraduate btech students interested in gaining experience in computational modeling and mechanobiologymasters projects open to mtechmsr students looking for a rigorous thesis project involving multiscale simulations and datadriven modeling requirements we welcome students from diverse engineering and science backgrounds mechanical material sciences physics bioengineeringbiosciences etc who have a strong foundation in mechanics or physics proficiency in programming python or matlab interest or experience in computational modeling finite element analysis molecular dynamics etc a desire to solve complex biological problems using engineering principles how to apply interested candidates should visit our website to learn more about our work to apply please send an email to with the subject line internshipproject application your name including a Subject: invitation to the rd lecture in the gyan ganga distinguished lecture series on river sustainability by the centre of excellence on water indrivers
Body: dear all we are pleased to invite you to the gyan ganga distinguished lecture series on river sustainability organized by the nmcgiitddutch collaboratory for intelligent river systems and clean yamuna center of excellence on water indrivers we will be joined in person by prof sharad k jain visiting professor department of civil engineering indian institute of technology gandhinagar he will share the recent developments in the technologies for sustainable river rejuvenation event details talk emerging and green technologies for sustainable river rejuvenation date december time pm pm venue senate room iit delhi event poster about the lecture growing population and expanding economy in india is leading to everincreasing water demands as more river flows are stored and diverted to meet the rising demands many rivers are facing degradation higher withdrawals of water from aquifers are leading to falling ground water levels depleting lean season river flows and other consequences at the same time water quality of river flows is degrading due to influx of polluted return flows from agricultural areas and dumping of partially or untreated waste from municipal and industrial areas combined impacts of all these activities is widespread river health deterioration a range of catchmentcentric solutions need to be implemented to rejuvenate rivers inflow of pollutants to the rivers from farmlands can be checked by proper monitoring and management of chemical fertilizers and soil nutrients a range of grey and green options can be employed to control flood damages and recharge aquifers environmental flows are let in the river to sustain the aquatic ecosystem this talk will discuss an emerging technology for soil health management hyperspectral imaging is emerging as a powerful technique to monitor soil nutrients and crop health in addition to large and medium storage reservoirs ponds and tanks are an efficient option to conserve flood flows recharge aquifers and promote biodiversity environmental flows when scientifically determined and implemented by involving the society immensely help in rejuvenating rivers and keeping them healthy about the speaker dr sharad jain is currently working as a visiting professor civil engineering department iit gandhinagar india prior to this he served nih roorkee as a scientist from to and as director national institute of hydrology roorkee india during he served iit roorkee as visiting professor in civil engineering department from mar to mar dr jain has coauthored five books which have been published by to view the announcement latencyaware and resilient stream data processing in edge computing ieee vehicular technology society vts distinguished lecturer dl talk title latencyaware and resilient stream data processing in edge computing abstract recent years have witnessed a huge proliferation of lowcost devices connected on the internet of things given the large amounts of data generated by these devices near the edge of the network there is an increasing need to process them near the network edge to meet the strict latency requirements for the applications for instance connected autonomous vehicle applications such as collision warning autonomous driving and traffic efficiency applications have a strict latency requirement ranging from to millisecond to produce timely actions edge computing improves the quality of service for such applications by filling the latency gaps between the devices and the typical cloud infrastructures while micro data centers provide computing resources that are geographically distributed careful management of these resources near the edge of the network is vital for ensuring efficient costeffective and resilient operation of the system while providing lowlatency access for applications executing near the network edge this talk will first introduce the notion of micro data centers and the edge computing architecture we will then discuss the algorithms techniques and design methodologies focusing on efficient and resilient resource allocation for latencysensitive stream data processing in edge computing finally we will discuss some open research problems in this area and discuss potential directions for future work biography balaji palanisamy is an associate professor in the school of computing and information at the university of pittsburgh he received his phd degree in computer science from the georgia institute of technology in his research interests include blockchains data privacy data security privacypreserving system design and scalable and efficient resource management for cloud and edge computing systems his research publications have appeared in several top journals including ieee tdsc Body: dear all you are invited to attend a talk on latencyaware and resilient stream data processing in edge computing by prof balaji palanisamy university of pittsburgh at am on monday dec in room computing ieee vehicular technology society vts distinguished lecturer dl talk title latencyaware and resilient stream data processing in edge computing abstract recent years have witnessed a huge proliferation of lowcost devices connected on the internet of things given the large amounts of data generated by these devices near the edge of the network there is an increasing need to process them near the network edge to meet the strict latency requirements for the applications for instance connected autonomous vehicle applications such as collision warning autonomous driving and traffic efficiency applications have a strict latency requirement ranging from to millisecond to produce timely actions edge computing improves the quality of service for such applications by filling the latency gaps between the devices and the typical cloud infrastructures while micro data centers provide computing resources that are geographically distributed careful management of these resources near the edge of the network is vital for ensuring efficient costeffective and resilient operation of the system while providing lowlatency access for applications executing near the network edge this talk will first introduce the notion of micro data centers and the edge computing architecture we will then discuss the algorithms techniques and design methodologies focusing on efficient and resilient resource allocation for latencysensitive stream data processing in edge computing finally we will discuss some open research problems in this area and discuss potential directions for future ieor seminar series supply chain risk management by dr akhil singla on dec friday at pm
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to the next entry in the industrial engineering and operations research seminar series with a talk given by dr akhil singla on supply chain risk management please find appended below the details of the seminar venue ii me committee room time pm december friday title tactical and strategic risks from supply disruptions in competing supply chains abstract supply chain disruptions can lead to both tactical ie loss of shortterm sales during a disruption and strategic ie loss of longterm market share consequences we model the impact of a supply disruption on competing supply chains in which two firms compete for a limited backup supply we describe strategies for both firms in a twostage game comprising i preparation which involves investment prior to the disruption to secure backup supply and ii response which involves postdisruption purchasing from the secured backup supply for a component whose availability has been compromised firms maximize their longrun profit while simultaneously deciding their preparation and response strategies we find the equilibrium strategy for firms in the two stages of the game we describe the conditions under which a firm can use its preparation investment to not only minimize its disruption risks but also capture more market share we also introduce a leaderfollowerbased gametheoretic model that helps measure each firms risk exposure by estimating the benefit of preparation we identify the primary factors that influence the firms preparation investment and affect customer satisfaction and show that these depend on the size of the firm and the length of the disruption this enables us to characterize the appropriate balance between protecting market share and exploiting a disruption to gain market share speaker biography dr akhil singla is a postdoctoral scholar in the department of industrial engineering and management sciences at northwestern university working with prof sanjay mehrotra he received his phd in iems from northwestern university under prof seyed iravani his research focuses on design and control principles for supply chains and service operations his dissertation was recognized with the best dissertation award at the supply chain analytics institute annual conference he also serves as an adjunct lecturer at northwestern all interested may attend best regards varun varun ramamohan phd associate professor department of mechanical engineering indian institute of technology delhi web

Subject: reminder me guest talk by dr gaurav kumar from ntu singapore
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the me guest talk by dr gaurav kumar a postdoctoral research fellow ntu singapore as per the schedule below date thursday th december time pm venue me seminar room ii title tackling a grand challenge in steel industry hydrogen embrittlement abstract the steel industry which is a cornerstone of modern infrastructure and manufacturing confronts a formidable challenge which demands urgent attention hydrogen embrittlement the presence of hydrogen in metallic materials can cause catastrophic early fracture the biggest challenge lies in observing the hydrogen and its associated influences in microstructure to this end our research group have developed the cryogenic atom probe tomography cryoapt for hydrogen mapping and applied it in combination with a micromechanical approach to investigate hydrogen embrittlement in steels our efforts have led to new insights for deciphering hydrogen trapping and embrittling mechanisms in steels facilitating the development of the steel microstructure that has a good resistance to hydrogen embrittlement hydrogen interaction with a crack tip in the presence of a deformation induced phase transformation is also an important issue to understand and tackle for this we have made an attempt to understand how the structurally critical mechanical aspects like fracture toughness and crack propagation rates in steels consisting of metastable phase gets affected by the presence of hydrogen short bio dr gaurav kumar is a postdoctoral research fellow in the school of materials science and engineering at the nanyang technological university singapore ntu singapore he is working in the group of prof eason yisheng chen his research focuses on the understanding and mitigation of hydrogen embrittlement in pipeline stainless and bainitic steels via analytical modelling and advance characterisation techniques including fib tem and atom probe tomography dap prior to joining ntu singapore dr kumar completed his phd from the indian institute of technology bombay where he was a prime ministers research fellow pmrf all interested are welcome to join the talk thanks and regards dr abhishek das assistant professor department of mechanical engineering iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: physics department seminar on attosecond dynamics december pm in ms
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to a physics department seminar on attosecond dynamics by prof p c deshmukh from camost iit iiser tirupati please find appended below the details of the seminar title of the seminar attosecond dynamics in atomic photoionization venue and timing ms december friday at pm speaker prof p c deshmukh camost iit and iiser tirupati tirupati abstract of the seminar movement of an electron wavepacket in atoms and molecules takes place in a very short time of the order of an attosecond sec we will visit some exciting aspects of attosecond dynamics to celebrate the nobel prize in physics awarded to pierre agostini ferenc krausz and anne l’huillier who “demonstrated a way to create extremely short pulses of light that can be used to measure the rapid processes in which electrons move or change energy” the attosecond pulses enable measurement of the eisenbudwignersmith ews scattering time delay in atomic photoionization no such delay was considered by einstein in his interpretation of the photoelectric effect that this is measurable at all in photoionization seems puzzling since the photoelectron does not have independent existence prior to photoabsorption – just as an electron does not exist prior to nuclear decay we shall resolve this issue invoking fundamental symmetries in the standard model of physics a few exciting results from the works of the nobel laureates will be used to illustrate state of the art applications of attosecond physics furthermore we shall discuss how the ews theory of quantum scattering enables us to obtain natural limits on how quantum information can be processed finally we shall discuss how quantum entanglement enables us to obtain a detailed mechanism of molecular photofragmentation pathways by studying ews time delay please see the link below for abstract keywords photoionization time delay quantum information processing entanglement of photofragments references zhong s vinbladh j busto d et al attosecond electron–spin dynamics in xe d photoionization nat commun s baral raghavan k easwaran j jose aarthi ganesan pc deshmukh atoms makos i busto d benda j et al nature communications brief biosketch of the speaker dr p c deshmukh is a theoretical atomic physicist he is the ‘convener and mentor’ of the centre for atomic molecular and optical sciences and technologies camost which is a joint initiative of the iit tirupati and the iiser tirupati concurrently he is ‘rv chair professor’ at the school of computer science and engineering rv university bengaluru and also the ‘chief technology advisor’ to the vivekananda institute of professional studies new delhi he has taught advanced courses and guided graduate research primarily at the iitmadras for over three decades also he has taught at iit mandi georgia state university atlanta usa university of western ontario london canada and at the iit tirupati and the iiser tirupati his research group is one of the leading contributors to relativistic manybody studies of attosecond dynamics in atomic photoionization processes also he has made important contributions to the applications of lambert wand polylogarithm functions to problems in pure and applied physics dr deshmukh has authored two books foundations of classical mechanics and quantum mechanics – formulation methodologies and applications he is a visionary educator and has significantly influenced teaching classical and quantum physics especially advanced atomic physics contributing over two hundred and fifty videolectures available online on the internet please see the link below for biosketch dr brajesh kumar mani associate professor department of physics indian institute of technology delhi hauz Subject: me guest talk by dr gaurav kumar from ntu singapore
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the me guest talk by dr gaurav kumar a postdoctoral research fellow ntu singapore as per the schedule below date thursday th december time pm venue me seminar room ii title tackling a grand challenge in steel industry hydrogen embrittlement abstract the steel industry which is a cornerstone of modern infrastructure and manufacturing confronts a formidable challenge which demands urgent attention hydrogen embrittlement the presence of hydrogen in metallic materials can cause catastrophic early fracture the biggest challenge lies in observing the hydrogen and its associated influences in microstructure to this end our research group have developed the cryogenic atom probe tomography cryoapt for hydrogen mapping and applied it in combination with a micromechanical approach to investigate hydrogen embrittlement in steels our efforts have led to new insights for deciphering hydrogen trapping and embrittling mechanisms in steels facilitating the development of the steel microstructure that has a good resistance to hydrogen embrittlement hydrogen interaction with a crack tip in the presence of a deformation induced phase transformation is also an important issue to understand and tackle for this we have made an attempt to understand how the structurally critical mechanical aspects like fracture toughness and crack propagation rates in steels consisting of metastable phase gets affected by the presence of hydrogen short bio dr gaurav kumar is a postdoctoral research fellow in the school of materials science and engineering at the nanyang technological university singapore ntu singapore he is working in the group of prof eason yisheng chen his research focuses on the understanding and mitigation of hydrogen embrittlement in pipeline stainless and bainitic steels via analytical modelling and advance characterisation techniques including fib tem and atom probe tomography dap prior to joining ntu singapore dr kumar completed his phd from the indian institute of technology bombay where he was a prime ministers research fellow pmrf all interested are welcome to join the talk thanks and regards dr abhishek das assistant professor department of mechanical engineering iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: re photonics lecture series on th dec time am a opc committee room
Body: gentle reminder original message subject photonics lecture series on th dec time am a opc committee room date from hodopc to dear all the optics and photonics centre opc invites everyone to attend a talk as part of the photonics lecture series pls details of the talk are provided below title perspective on processing and properties of diamond for quantum applications speaker prof raj n singh oklahoma state university usa mode offline date th of december monday time am ist venue a opc committee room abstract diamond is a fascinating material due to its wide band gap optical transparency and high thermal conductivity rendering it an ideal wide band gap semiconductor for quantum electronics and optical devices useful under ambient and extreme conditions of high temperatures and intense radiation specifically diamond has nitrogenvacancy nv and siliconvacancy siv defect centers with unusual characteristics making it attractive for these unique applications one can control by microwave optical signal electric and magnetic fields the qubit states in nv centers for quantum network quantum memory and quantum sensing some of these applications require small nanometer or micrometer size diamond crystals containing preferably only one type of nv defects for greatest sensitivity individual addressability and applicability we are addressing these challenges by developing processing approaches to synthesize diamond single crystal arrays containing only one type of in situ doped nv and siv defect centers by microwave plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition mpecvd and characterized by scanning electron microscopy raman and photoluminescence spectroscopies and optically detected magnetic resonance odmr techniques these results along with a brief overview on the promise of diamond for quantum applications and our current research activities will be presented and discussed biography dr raj n singh is a regents professor and served as a founding head of school of materials science and engineering williams companies distinguished chair professor director energy technologies programs at the oklahoma state university osu he received his scd degree from massachusetts institute of technology and bs from iit kanpur in materials science and engineering he worked at argonne national laboratory gerd center and university of cincinnati uc before joining osu in dr singh has been recognized for his engineering leadership through his scholarly activities journal articles referred reports and presentations pioneering inventions of mi composite processing technology leading to commercialization granted patents for graduating students with ms and phd degrees and through numerous professional awards in recognition of his engineering leadership such as member of the national academy of engineering nae rishi raj medal for innovation and commercialization from american ceramic society american association for the advancement of science aaas fellow national academy of inventors nai fellow albert sauveur achievement award of asm international regents professor osu fellow of the asm international fellow of the american ceramic msr synopsis presentation on robust federated learning
Body: dear all as part of the msr synopsis presentation mr usayd shahul bsy will give a technical talk on robust federated learning the details are as follows date th december time pm venue bharti school title forta dft coded real domain aggregation for byzantine resilient federated learning abstract secure aggregation enables privacy preserving collaborative model training in federated learning fl a key challenge to this is maintaining robustness against byzantine attacks where malicious users can inject corrupted updates while simultaneously managing the numerical realities of the aggregation process traditional secure aggregation methods rely on finite field arithmetic this inherently introduces numerical precision errors and arithmetic overflows creating vulnerabilities that sophisticated adversaries can exploit to bypass outlier detection pointing at this dual challenge we introduce fourier based outlier resilient trust aggregation forta a novel byzantine resilient secure aggregation framework that operates entirely in the real domain forta leverages discrete fourier transform dft codes for security and privacy this eliminates the need for vulnerable quantization and modular arithmetic the core innovation is a dft guided modified krum aggregation rule we demonstrate that in a practical finite precision environment numerical noise perturbs krums outlier detection to mitigate this issue forta exploits the intrinsic error localization properties of the dft decoder to derive statistical confidence estimates effectively tracking the suspicion level of each user this tracker is used as feedback to dynamically adjust the standard krum score this effectively distinguishes persistent adversarial outliers from transient numerical noise we also provide theoretical guarantees for our dft based localization method and further demonstrate that this side information guided krum modification achieves improvement in the fl systems convergence rate and overall robustness this is the first work of its kind to formally address and mitigate the effect of numerical stability on byzantine resilience in secure aggregation for fl you are welcome to attend regards harshan

Subject: me guest talk by dr ujjawal arya postdoctoral research associate purdue university
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the me guest talk by dr ujjawal arya postdoctoral research associate purdue university as per the schedule below date friday th december time pm venue me seminar room ii title tribology under extreme conditions lubricant levitation film instability and droplet deformation in highspeed bearing lubrication abstract tribological performance under extreme operating conditions is governed by complex fluidstructure interactions that often extend beyond the limits of conventional lubrication theory at high surface speeds as encountered in electric vehicle drivetrains aerospace turbomachinery and precision manufacturing systems the interplay between fluid inertia air entrainment and surface tension can lead to unstable lubricant films and loss of adhesion on moving surfaces such phenomena directly influence friction wear and energy efficiency in critical machine elements such as rollingelement bearings one of the most striking manifestations of this regime is the aerodynamic leidenfrost effect ale where a rapidly moving surface generates a thin air film that levitates lubricant droplets preventing wetting once a critical velocity threshold is exceeded to investigate this phenomenon experiments were conducted on a customdesigned rotating test rig comprising various bearing components with highspeed imaging used to visualize lubricantfilm levitation and droplet deformation under different operating conditions complementary to these experiments a numerical model based on softelastohydrodynamic lubrication softehl theory was developed to simulate ale and quantify droplet deformation near highspeed surfaces providing a mechanistic understanding of the observed behavior the combined insights reveal that beyond specific speed thresholds lubricant adherence is severely inhibited leading to starvation and altered flow distribution near the bearing raceway these findings offer fundamental insight into the mechanisms governing lubrication failure at high speeds and establish a framework for the design of more reliable and efficient tribological systems operating under extreme conditions bio dr ujjawal arya is a postdoctoral researcher at purdue universitys heterogeneous integration design and characterization hidac lab where he leads the development of experimental platforms and a new reliability characterization facility for microelectronic components he earned his ms and phd in mechanical engineering from purdue universitys mechanical engineering tribology laboratory metl in where he developed innovative visualization techniques and validated computational models to investigate lubrication phenomena in highspeed rollingelement bearings prior to that he received his btech hons in mechanical engineering from iit kharagpur in drawing on deep expertise in experimental design data acquisition and multiphysics modeling dr aryas research seeks to bridge the disciplines of tribology and reliability engineering he integrates highfidelity experimental visualization with numerical and analytical modeling to reveal the coupled mechanisms governing lubrication wear and longterm system durability his research and teaching have been recognized through multiple awards and accolades for excellence impact and contribution to advancing engineering education and research looking ahead his research will continue to focus on advancing the field of tribology while drawing inspiration from his ongoing work in reliability testing to inform the design of more durable and efficient mechanical systems all interested are welcome to join the talk thanks and regards dr abhishek das assistant professor department of mechancial engineering iit delhi

Subject: departmental seminar dr christopher thomas institut de biologie du développement de marseille th dec am ksbs committee room
Body: dear all we invite you to the ksbs departmental talk on th dec at am in the ksbs committee room the speaker is dr christopher thomas a group leader at the institut de biologie du développement de marseille cnrs aixmarseille université studying the mechanisms that control ovarian follicle growth selection and ovulation they develop ex vivo imaging models of the mammalian ovary to uncover how communication between follicle cells and between neighbouring follicles ensures the release of a fertilisable egg please circulate this information in your department all are cordially invited details may be found below speaker dr christopher thomas group leader institut de biologie du développement de marseille ibdm aixmarseille université date th december time am venue ksbs committee room title revealing the secrets of ovulation abstract ovulation is essential for reproduction during ovulation an egg is released from an ovarian follicle into the oviduct once released the egg can be fertilised by the sperm and give rise to a new embryo ovulation takes place inside the body impeding studies of its progression the exact mechanisms that control ovulation have therefore remained unclear in this work we devised methods to study the entire process of ovulation live in isolated ovarian follicles from mice using a longterm culture and imaging system a combined approach of confocal and twophoton microscopy allowed for the study of ovarian processes at both the cellular and whole follicle scale we show that ovulation proceeds through three distinct phases follicle expansion i contraction ii and rupture iii culminating in the release of the egg follicle expansion is driven by the secretion of hyaluronic acid and an osmotic gradientdirected influx of fluid into the follicle subsequently smooth muscle cells in the outer follicle drive follicle contraction follicle rupture is initiated by the formation of a stigma in the thinnest region of the follicle wall followed by the exit of follicular fluid and cumulus cells and finally the rapid release of the egg taken together these results establish a mechanistic framework for ovulation a process of fundamental importance to reproduction short bio dr christopher thomas is a reproductive biologist and research group leader at the developmental biology institute of marseille ibdm france he completed his phd in the group of dr suzanne madgwick at the institute for cell and molecular biosciences university of newcastle uk his research focused on oocytes the precursors to egg cells in the ovary his findings redefined our understanding of cell cycle regulation during oocyte meiosis and revealed how oocytes repurpose key pathways to adapt to this highly specialised cell division in dr thomas joined the laboratory of dr melina schuh at the max planck institute for multidisciplinary sciences in göttingen germany as a postdoctoral researcher shifting from studying single cells to a tissuescale perspective he set out with the challenge of liveimaging mammalian ovulation with colleagues he developed a groundbreaking model system that for the first time enabled us to visualise the entire process of ovulation in mouse ovarian follicles at cellular resolution and to describe its underlying mechanismsa landmark achievement in reproductive biology in dr thomas established his independent research group at ibdm marseille his team uses livecell imaging and follicle culture techniques to investigate how ovarian follicles compete for the capacity to ovulate and how oocytefollicle cell communication ensures the proper coordination of ovulation and meiosis his pioneering approach brings ovarian biology into the modern era tackling fundamental biological questions with significant clinical implications that until now we lacked the technology to address please see the link below thank you best regards saurabh saurabh raj phd assistant professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: celebrating international day of persons with disabilities – december rd
Body: dear iit delhi community greetings from the office of accessible education oae and the office of diversity inclusion odi today we join the world in celebrating the international day of persons with disabilities a day dedicated to promoting inclusion accessibility and equal opportunity for all at iit delhi this day holds special significance because of the strong vibrant and inspiring presence of our students with disabilities who enrich our campus with their resilience talent and leadership their contributions continually reinforce our commitment to building an equitable and inclusive community as we celebrate this important day here are a few meaningful and engaging ways you can participate things you can do today i read about disabilities recognised in the rpwd act take a moment to read about the disabilities recognised under the rights of persons with disabilities rpwd act understanding these categories is a simple yet powerful step toward building awareness and becoming a more empathetic and informed community member ii experience a different perspective try a simple activity to experience the world differently for a few minutes navigate a short familiar path with reduced audio noisecancelling or earplugs read a paragraph using a screen reader try writing with the hand that is not your dominant one these small exercises can spark powerful reflections on everyday accessibility iii discover a story you didnt know take out minutes to read a reallife story of a changemaker with a disabilityathletes scientists artists or innovators even better take a moment to speak with our students with disabilities on campus their journeys experiences and everyday perspectives offer powerful insights into resilience creativity and what true inclusion looks like share one inspiring line or reflection with a friend or colleague today iv watch films on disability inclusion indian films margarita with a straw taare zameen par black srikanth international films the theory of everything the story of stephen hawkings life and journey a beautiful mind inspiring biography exploring mental health wonder a heartwarming story on disability and acceptance the peanut butter falcon adventure film celebrating ability and friendship rain man iconic story on neurodiversity and family the upside uplifting film on caregiving dignity and unlikely friendships coda a heartfelt comingofage story about a hearing teenager while being the only hearing member of her deaf family crip camp journey of the historic disability rights movement in america let this day serve as a reminder that inclusion is a shared responsibilityand that even small steps can create a more empathetic accessible and welcoming iit delhi for everyone if you would like to contribute more actively you are encouraged to visit the oae office in lh you can volunteer collaborate or simply share your ideas on how we can make our campus more inclusive for all warm regards office of Body: reminder for talk at today on preeti ranjan panda wrote title scaleout chiplet based systems design architecture and pathfinding speaker puneet gupta electrical and computer engineering department ucla venue seminar hall room khosla school of it building datetime wed dec am abstract as conventional technology scaling becomes harder d integration provides a viable pathway to building larger systems at lower cost waferscale chipletbased systems as much as x larger than largest modern socs pose new opportunities and challenges in their architecture and design we describe a waferscale gpu concept and discuss our experience designing a chiplet waferscale processor system pointing out key challenges and solutions next we describe our ongoing work on developing a crossstack pathfinding framework for large distributed d d systems identifying areas where technology development would help design metrics substantially especially for the important class of distributed machine learning training applications speaker bio puneet gupta received the btech degree in electrical engineering from the indian institute of technology delhi new delhi india in and the phd degree from the university of california at san diego san diego ca usa in he is currently a faculty member with the electrical and computer engineering department university of california at los angeles he cofounded blaze dfm inc sunnyvale ca usa in and served as its product architect until he has authored over papers us patents a book and two book chapters in the areas of systemtechnology cooptimization as well as variabilityreliability aware architectures dr gupta is an ieee fellow and was a recipient of the nsf career award the acmsigda outstanding new faculty award src inventor recognition award and the ibm faculty award he currently leads the system benchmarking thrust within src jump chime packaging center

Subject: today departmental seminar dr tanmay mitra kennedy institute of rheumatology university of oxford st dec pm ksbs committee room
Body: dear all we invite you to the ksbs departmental talk on st dec at pm in ksbs committee room the speaker is dr tanmay mitra a senior postdoctoral research fellow at the kennedy institute of rheumatology university of oxford working on immunological synapses and immunecell signalling in noncommunicable diseases such as cancers and autoimmune disorders please circulate this information in your department all are cordially invited details may be found below speaker dr tanmay mitra date st december time pm venue ksbs committee room title rewiring the immune synapse with tcell engagers how flexibility membrane mechanics and synaptic architecture shape tcell engager potency abstract conventional t cell engager tce design focuses on affinity and epitope targeting yet often neglects how conformational flexibility and membrane mechanics influence t cell signaling we sought to investigate how structural flexibility and target membrane properties shape the performance of bispecific t cell engagers by integrating saxsinformed structural analysis quantitative imaging of cd tcell immune synapse on tunable supported lipid bilayers slbs we examined how conformational flexibility and paratope spacing of the engagers and diffusivity of integrin ligands icam affect t cell activation synapse patterning and cytotoxic output we have shown that proximal signaling in t cell synapse and bispecific potency are collectively influenced by intermembrane contact distance and molecular flexibility rigid formats outperform flexible ones even when epitope spacing is matched excessive flexibility introduces spatial uncertainty compromising synapse fidelity and cytotoxic efficacy shannon entropy of the targetbound engagers and pplcgamma emerged as the best predictors of cytotoxic potency furthermore anchored icam enhanced perforin release in comparison with mobile icam demonstrating that mechanics of the target biomolecules also modulated effector function our ongoing work integrates structureguided modeling to test the hypothesis that early cd ingress is flexibility and sheardependent we are now extending our investigations to trispecific engagers combining cd tumor antigens and costimulatory targets to enhance function at low cd affinity in conclusion our ongoing efforts demonstrate that tcell engager potency is not just encoded in molecular affinity but in how an immune engager sculpts the synapse thank you best regards saurabh saurabh raj phd assistant professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology hauz khas new delhi india saurabh raj phd assistant professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology hauz khas new delhi india

Body: dear all we are pleased to invite you to attend the upcoming talk on nvidia’s latest advances in large language models and generative ai platforms the session will cover cuttingedge developments scaling of llms attendees will see how the same ai platform is powering breakthroughs in domains such as healthcare manufacturing climate science financial services and robotics with real‑world industry use cases finally the talk will showcase nvidias deep collaborations with leading research institutions and scientific supercomputing centers and what this emerging ai infrastructure means for universities research labs and the future of higher education brief introduction to the speaker pradeep gupta is currently vice president of generative ai and accelerated computing solutions architecture at nvidia he leads worldwide team of solutions architects across industry verticals at nvidia with over years at nvidia pradeep has been instrumental in advancing generative ai accelerated computing and enterprise ai solutions his leadership has driven innovation in ai model optimization highperformance computing and largescale ai infrastructure shaping the future of ai adoption across industries as a key architect of cuttingedge ai solutions pradeep has played a pivotal role in enabling enterprises to leverage ai at scale transforming industries through hardware Subject: photonics lecture series on th dec time am a opc committee room
Body: dear all the optics and photonics centre opc invites everyone to attend a talk as part of the photonics lecture series pls details of the talk are provided below title perspective on processing and properties of diamond for quantum applications speaker prof raj n singh oklahoma state university usa mode offline date th of december monday time am ist venue a opc committee room abstract diamond is a fascinating material due to its wide band gap optical transparency and high thermal conductivity rendering it an ideal wide band gap semiconductor for quantum electronics and optical devices useful under ambient and extreme conditions of high temperatures and intense radiation specifically diamond has nitrogenvacancy nv and siliconvacancy siv defect centers with unusual characteristics making it attractive for these unique applications one can control by microwave optical signal electric and magnetic fields the qubit states in nv centers for quantum network quantum memory and quantum sensing some of these applications require small nanometer or micrometer size diamond crystals containing preferably only one type of nv defects for greatest sensitivity individual addressability and applicability we are addressing these challenges by developing processing approaches to synthesize diamond single crystal arrays containing only one type of in situ doped nv and siv defect centers by microwave plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition mpecvd and characterized by scanning electron microscopy raman and photoluminescence spectroscopies and optically detected magnetic resonance odmr techniques these results along with a brief overview on the promise of diamond for quantum applications and our current research activities will be presented and discussed biography dr raj n singh is a regents professor and served as a founding head of school of materials science and engineering williams companies distinguished chair professor director energy technologies programs at the oklahoma state university osu he received his scd degree from massachusetts institute of technology and bs from iit kanpur in materials science and engineering he worked at argonne national laboratory gerd center and university of cincinnati uc before joining osu in dr singh has been recognized for his engineering leadership through his scholarly activities journal articles referred reports and presentations pioneering inventions of mi composite processing technology leading to commercialization granted patents for graduating students with ms and phd degrees and through numerous professional awards in recognition of his engineering leadership such as member of the national academy of engineering nae rishi raj medal for innovation and commercialization from american ceramic society american association for the advancement of science aaas fellow national academy of inventors nai fellow albert sauveur achievement award of asm international regents professor osu fellow of the asm international fellow of the american ceramic society fellow of graduate school uc whitney gallery of technical achievers gecrd publication awards gecrd patent awards gecrd bronze silver and gold patent medallions he also serves as member of editorial boards of international journals regards head opc room no b blockiii optics and photonics centre indian institute Subject: talk on fabrication and longterm reliability of monocrystalline silicon solar cells with passivating contacts
Body: dear faculty and students talk by prof sumit agarwal colorado school of mines usa scheduled on th nov wednesday from pm in department of energy science and engineerings committee room block v nd floor room no on title fabrication and longterm reliability of monocrystalline silicon solar cells with passivating contacts abstract global energy demand will continue to increase and the ability of fossil fuels to meet these demands is limited due to the associated climate change concerns in response to these concerns new energy installations are increasingly based on renewable energy resources such as wind and solar to further develop solar energy as a renewable energy resource it is critical to improve the efficiency and reliability of siliconbased solar cells which represent more than of the current photovoltaics market in this presentation i will discuss strategies to improve the efficiency of silicon solar cells via passivating contacts which serve both as a contact layer and a passivation layer for the crystalline silicon csi surface these types of contacts are currently used in industriallymanufactured c si solar cells i will discuss the fabrication of these contacts the underlying principle for charge transport through these contacts and their performance on both planar and textured surfaces i will also discuss field degradation mechanism of csi solar cells and describe strategies that can be implemented to suppress these defects about speaker sumit agarwal is a professor of chemical and biological engineering at the colorado school of mines csm since and holds a jointappointment with the national renewable energy laboratory he joined csm after his postdoctoral research at the university of massachusetts – amherst prior to this he received his phd in chemical engineering from the university of california – santa barbara and his ms and b tech degrees from the university of new mexico and the indian institute of technology varanasi respectively his current research is focused on development of industriallyrelevant fabrication techniques for ultrahighefficiency crystalline silicon solar cells plasma processing of materials and surface processes during atomic layer processing of materials for semiconductor applications best wishes ‪prof vamsi krishna komarala head nanoscale research facility department of energy science and engineering indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india ph email

Subject: gentle reminder quantifying wellbeing in sustainability research – seminar on th nov – lh
Body: dear students and faculty members we are pleased to invite you to an engaging seminar on “quantifying wellbeing in sustainability research” to be delivered by dr narasimha d rao professor of energy systems yale universityseminar details date th november time – pm venue lh lecture hall complex iit delhi abstract several frameworks have been proposed to represent the environmental limits of human activity—such as planetary boundaries safe operating space sufficiency and consumption corridors—all aimed at safeguarding the wellbeing of current and future generations however these frameworks often lack the theoretical and analytical foundations necessary to effectively inform policy despite its wellknown limitations income continues to serve as the dominant metric of human progress in this talk the speaker will outline emerging analytical approaches to quantifying human wellbeing he will discuss the concept of decent living standards and its application within the climate research community to establish a minimum threshold for resource use and greenhouse gas emissions pathways the talk will also highlight new research on selfassessed wellbeing and its relationship with consumption offering insights into how these perspectives can help operationalize the notion of sufficiency finally the speaker will share thoughts on future research directions that link wellbeing frameworks to feedbacks between environmental impacts and human wellbeing about the speaker narasimha d rao is a professor of energy systems at the yale school of the environment his research examines the relationship between energy systems human wellbeing and climate change his project decent living energy quantifies the energy needs and climate impacts of eradicating poverty around the world by blending economics and engineering with ethical analysis his current focus is on investigating the barriers to household electrification and clean technology adoption in energy transitions he is a lead author on the ipcc’s seventh assessment report and on the un emissions gap report he has testified at a us congressional house subcommittee hearing and served on multistakeholder panels at the un social and economic council his work has been supported by the european research council national science foundation environmental protection agency and other organizations he is also a senior research scholar at the international institute for applied systems analysis iiasa he received his phd from stanford university eiper program in environment and resources and masters in technology policy and electrical engineering from the massachusetts institute of technology we warmly encourage all students and faculty members to attend and participate in the discussion for any queries please contact ashwini mudgal or ekta baranwal warm regards prof kaveri iychettira and prof ambuj sagar school of public policy iit delhi

Subject: departmental seminar dr tanmay mitra kennedy institute of rheumatology university of oxford st dec pm ksbs committee room
Body: dear all we invite you to the ksbs departmental talk on st dec at pm in ksbs committee room the speaker is dr tanmay mitra a senior postdoctoral research fellow at the kennedy institute of rheumatology university of oxford working on immunological synapses and immunecell signalling in noncommunicable diseases such as cancers and autoimmune disorders please circulate this information in your department all are cordially invited details may be found below speaker dr tanmay mitra date st december time pm venue ksbs committee room title rewiring the immune synapse with tcell engagers how flexibility membrane mechanics and synaptic architecture shape tcell engager potency abstract conventional t cell engager tce design focuses on affinity and epitope targeting yet often neglects how conformational flexibility and membrane mechanics influence t cell signaling we sought to investigate how structural flexibility and target membrane properties shape the performance of bispecific t cell engagers by integrating saxsinformed structural analysis quantitative imaging of cd tcell immune synapse on tunable supported lipid bilayers slbs we examined how conformational flexibility and paratope spacing of the engagers and diffusivity of integrin ligands icam affect t cell activation synapse patterning and cytotoxic output we have shown that proximal signaling in t cell synapse and bispecific potency are collectively influenced by intermembrane contact distance and molecular flexibility rigid formats outperform flexible ones even when epitope spacing is matched excessive flexibility introduces spatial uncertainty compromising synapse fidelity and cytotoxic efficacy shannon entropy of the targetbound engagers and pplcgamma emerged as the best predictors of cytotoxic potency furthermore anchored icam enhanced perforin release in comparison with mobile icam demonstrating that mechanics of the target biomolecules also modulated effector function our ongoing work integrates structureguided modeling to test the hypothesis that early cd ingress is flexibility and sheardependent we are now extending our investigations to trispecific engagers combining cd tumor antigens and costimulatory targets to enhance function at low cd affinity in conclusion our ongoing efforts demonstrate that tcell engager potency is not just encoded in molecular affinity but in how an immune engager sculpts the synapse thank you best regards saurabh saurabh raj phd assistant professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: workshop on introduction to energy modelling in macro rd dec
Body: dear students and faculty members we are pleased to invite you to a workshop on introduction to energy modelling in macro details are given below workshop details date rd december time venue sopp computer lab room academic block west building b iit delhi rsvp kindly use this link to rsvp and let us know if you will be able to attend the session description of training this training will introduce attendees to the iitd netzero inda nzi project and macro which is one of the core models in use as part of nzi it is a bottomup multisectoral infrastructure optimization model for macroenergy systems macro cooptimizes the design and operation of userdefined models of multisector energy systems and networks and enables users to explore the impact of energy policies technology costs and performance demand patterns and other factors on the energy system both as a whole and at the sector level the macro development team have built on their experience developing the genx and dolphyn models to design a new architecture which is easier and faster to expand to new energy technologies policies and sectors high level presentations in the morning will cover the model examples of national regional and sectoral models built using macro and examples of data sets prepared for entry into macro the morning will wrap up with a qa session the afternoon will involve an informal selected applications in wireless communication systems by dr nilesh jha date from sandeep kumar to dear all you are all invited to an interesting seminar on the intersection of ai and wireless communication by dr nilesh jha the details of the talk are below sit time am date st november online meeting linklink title data driven approaches for selected applications in wireless communication systems from classical to deep learning abstract enabled by enhanced hardware development novel technologies and algorithm development wireless communication has become ubiquitous to modern technologies meeting their everincreasing latency connectivity and data rate requirements however as traditional algorithms and model designs approach saturation in their modelling inference and robustness capabilities significant research focus is given to data driven methods the seminar presents datadriven bayesian signal processing methods for selected physical layer applications in the upcoming beyond fifth generation and sixth generation wireless communication systems where we first investigate traditional bayesian machine learning scaled through onlinestreaming machine learning using methods from approximate posterior inference for interference cancellation in overtheair aggregation systems we then examine potential pitfalls in applying the above traditional approaches and their mitigation through tools from deep learning focussing on the algorithm deficit scenario in decentralized resource management for cellfree mimo systems where algorithm design becomes complicated due to the system constraints and the model deficit scenario in channel estimation for unmanned aerial vehicles where accommodating various spatiotemporal statistics via traditional bayesian approaches is challenging bio nilesh kumar jha received his btech degree in electrical engineering from the indian institute of technology delhi india in and his phd from the department of electronic Subject: ‘energy transitions workshop’ at school of public policy th nov
Body: dear students and faculty members we are pleased to invite you to energy transitions workshop to be delivered by dr narasimha d rao professor of energy systems yale school of the environment workshop details date th november time venue sopp committee room room academic block west building b iit delhi registration link kindly use this link to rsvp and let us know if you will be able to attend the session abstract in this workshop the speaker will explore the components current status and key challenges of the global energy transition toward a decarbonized netzero economy the talk will examine technology options across major demand sectorsbuildings transport and industryhighlighting their relative advantages limitations and potential combinations that can achieve different climate mitigation pathways as described in integrated assessment scenarios the discussion will also cover the state of progress in energy transitions worldwide including the evolution of policy instruments national pledges and the current status of the paris agreement bringing in the global south perspective the speaker will address issues of climate equity the concept of a just transition and emerging ideas for evaluating fair effort in national climate commitments about the speaker narasimha d rao is a professor of energy systems at the yale school of the environment his research examines the relationship between energy systems human wellbeing and climate change his project decent living energy quantifies the energy needs and climate impacts of eradicating poverty around the world by blending economics and engineering with ethical analysis his current focus is on investigating the barriers to household electrification and clean technology adoption in energy transitions he is a lead author on the ipccs seventh assessment report and on the un emissions gap report he has testified at a us congressional house subcommittee hearing and served on multistakeholder panels at the un social and economic council his work has been supported by the european research council national science foundation environmental protection agency and other organizations he is also a senior research scholar at the international institute for applied systems analysis iiasa he received his phd from stanford university eiper program in environment and resources and masters in technology policy and electrical engineering from the massachusetts institute of technology for any queries please contact ashwini mudgal or ekta baranwal we warmly encourage all interested students and faculty members to attend and participate in the discussion warm regards dr kaveri iychettira and prof ambuj sagar school of public policy

Subject: quantifying wellbeing in sustainability research – seminar on th nov – lh
Body: dear students and faculty members we are pleased to invite you to an engaging seminar on “quantifying wellbeing in sustainability research” to be delivered by dr narasimha d rao professor of energy systems yale universityseminar details date th november time – pm venue lh lecture hall complex iit delhi abstract several frameworks have been proposed to represent the environmental limits of human activity—such as planetary boundaries safe operating space sufficiency and consumption corridors—all aimed at safeguarding the wellbeing of current and future generations however these frameworks often lack the theoretical and analytical foundations necessary to effectively inform policy despite its wellknown limitations income continues to serve as the dominant metric of human progress in this talk the speaker will outline emerging analytical approaches to quantifying human wellbeing he will discuss the concept of decent living standards and its application within the climate research community to establish a minimum threshold for resource use and greenhouse gas emissions pathways the talk will also highlight new research on selfassessed wellbeing and its relationship with consumption offering insights into how these perspectives can help operationalize the notion of sufficiency finally the speaker will share thoughts on future research directions that link wellbeing frameworks to feedbacks between environmental impacts and human wellbeing about the speaker narasimha d rao is a professor of energy systems at the yale school of the environment his research examines the relationship between energy systems human wellbeing and climate change his project decent living energy quantifies the energy needs and climate impacts of eradicating poverty around the world by blending economics and engineering with ethical analysis his current focus is on investigating the barriers to household electrification and clean technology adoption in energy transitions he is a lead author on the ipcc’s seventh assessment report and on the un emissions gap report he has testified at a us congressional house subcommittee hearing and served on multistakeholder panels at the un social and economic council his work has been supported by the european research council national science foundation environmental protection agency and other organizations he is also a senior research scholar at the international institute for applied systems analysis iiasa he received his phd from stanford university eiper program in environment and resources and masters in technology policy and electrical engineering from the massachusetts institute of technology we warmly encourage all students and faculty members to attend and participate in the discussion for any queries please contact ashwini mudgal or ekta baranwal warm regards prof kaveri iychettira and prof ambuj sagar school of public policy iit delhi

Subject: plenary talk as pert of janjatiya gaurav diwas celebrations on th november
Body: dear all as part of the celebrations marking the th birth anniversary of bhagwan birsa munda iit delhi is observing janjatiya gaurav diwas to honour the indomitable spirit leadership and cultural heritage of india’s tribal communities we are privileged to host a plenary talk by shri vibhu nayar senior ias former secretary ministry of tribal affairs government of india on the theme of leadership studiomicrophone “david vs goliath the leadership mystery” in this thoughtprovoking talk shri nayar will reflect on the essence of leadership — how vision conviction and moral strength enable individuals and communities to triumph against overwhelming odds drawing inspiration from the life and legacy of bhagwan birsa munda the session will explore enduring lessons of courage integrity and transformative leadership the talk will be followed by an interactive session with the speaker over high tea and snacks calendar day date friday november fiveo’clock time pm – pm roundpushpin venue auditorium ri park iit delhi this event organised by the bhagwan birsa munda cell bbmc iit delhi commemorates janjatiya gaurav varsh — celebrating years of bhagwan birsa munda’s enduring legacy of resistance and inspiration we warmly invite all faculty students and staff to join and engage in this special session on leadership learning and legacy thanks and regards vivek kumar coordinator bhagwan birsa munda cell head crdt indian institute of technology iit delhi new delhi india o fax email

Subject: regarding doubt of tutorial question
Body: dear students there was a doubt asked by someone regarding question of tutorial the doubt was that we are finding out torque by partially differentiating it wrt theta but i and i are also dependent on theta so why are we not considering it the answer for this is that we are considering partial derivative of torque wrt theta now when we take partial derivative we tend to keep other variables constant it is true that our field energy is a function of i i and theta but when we have to find torque we have to take the partial derivative wrt theta considering i i to be constant our torque is a mechanical quantity which is dependent on the value of theta mechanical quantity it is for this reason that in spite of i i being functions of theta we are treating them as constants while finding torque you could refer to the book electric machines by ij nagrath and dp kothari to get some more insight abhirup bose eez

Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department seminar by prof urban larsson iit bombay india hikaru university of tsukuba japan and takahiro hiroshima university japan on combinatorial games abstract this will be a playful deep dive into various topics in combinatorial game theory divided into three parts beginners are welcome when maximum restricted nim meets josephus problem hikaru we will talk about the relationship between maxrestricted nim and the josephus problem maxrestricted nim introduced by levin is a variant of nim where the number of stones one can take from a pile of size m is limited by a rule function fm the josephus problem is a wellknown mathematical puzzle dating back to antiquity in this problem people are arranged in a circle and proceeding in one direction every kth person is removed to determine the final survivor i will explain an interesting property of this games grundy number sequence and provide an intuition for how it elegantly relates to the josephus problem the dragonfly moth game and polygonal numbers takahiro dragonfly and moth are twoplayer two piles nim games a player takes at lest two stones from one pile and return at least one stone to the other pile so that the total number of stones decreases or they take i stones from one pile together with j tokens from the other pile so that ijc where c is a given game parameter surprisingly the ppositions correspond to polygonal numbers for example if c the set of ppositions describes … and the triangle number appears we will explain why this happens in addition the classical conway theory for partizan normal play games will be reviewed urban speaker biographies hikaru manabe is a firstyear undergraduate student at the university of tsukuba japan his research focuses on combinatorial game theory and he is currently a visiting researcher in the department of industrial engineering and operations research at the indian institute of technology bombay he has received several awards from organizations such as the ieee and the information processing society of japan ipsj additionally he has experience as a session chair at an international conference and he is organizing a conference in this field in the last three years he has published papers in scopusindexed journals and delivered presentations at domestic and international conferences takahiro yamashita is an rd grade phd student at the department of mathematics hiroshima university japan he is a student in combinatorial game theory his main topic revolves around impartial subtraction games he is the one of the organizer of the international conference on combinatorial game theory in japan that will be held on march urban larsson is an associate professor at the department of industrial engineering and operations research at the indian institute of technology bombay india he is a worldwide researcher and teacher in combinatorial game theory and organizes workshops and conferences on this subject he has won awards such as a killam fellowship and he is the editor of the volumes games of no chance and and ijgts special issues on combinatorial game theory and he publishes regularly Subject: departmental seminar by prof anirban dasgupta on november thursday at pm
Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department seminar by prof anirban dasgupta from iit gandhinagar on november thursday at pm the details are given below speaker prof anirban dasgupta venue room no academic complex west b date and time november thursday at pm title deterministic coreset for lp subspace embedding abstract joint work with supratim shit rachit chhaya and dan feldman in the face of the data deluge smart algorithms play a significant role over the last couple of decades coresets a small and efficiently calculable data summary have grown in popularity both in theoretical and practical settings they enable approximating large optimizations while needing only a fraction of the resources in this talk we will discuss a few recent results related to creating coresets for two related problems symmetric tensor factorization and lp subspace embedding our coresets for tensor factorization are online in nature ie for every incoming point an irrevocable decision is made on whether to include it in the coreset for lp subspace embedding we also present a deterministic coreset by generalizing the work of batson spielman and srivastava bss and extending it from l to lp short bio of the speaker anirban dasgupta is currently the n rama rao chair professor of computer science engineering at iit gandhinagar prior to joining iit gandhinagar he was a senior scientist at yahoo labs in sunnyvale anirban works on algorithmic problems involving massive datasets largescale machine learning analysis of large social networks and randomized algorithms in general he did his undergraduate studies at iit kharagpur and doctoral studies at cornell university he has received the google faculty research award the cisco university award the icdt best newcomer award the google india aiml award and the acm stoc year test of time award in all are cordially invited to attend best regards mathematics department colloquium team

Subject: talk by ishan jindal samsung rd
Body: dear all we are very happy to invite you to a seminar on modular and selective reasoning inferencetime optimization for large language models below are the details of the talk date th november venue lh time pm title modular and selective reasoning inferencetime optimization for large language models abstract large language models llms demonstrate remarkable reasoning capabilities but remain prohibitively expensive to deploy at scale most of the computational cost arises at inference time where models redundantly explore multiple reasoning paths or overuse large model capacity for tasks that smaller models could handle in this talk i will present two complementary approaches for inferencetime optimization of reasoning in llms first offloaded reasoning or introduces a modular paradigm in which a smaller model performs the reasoning while a larger model focuses on synthesis and refinementachieving up to × faster inference without retraining second path of least resistance polr exploits prefix consensus across reasoning traces polr preserves accuracy while cutting token usage and latency by together these methods redefine how we think about efficient reasoningshifting the optimization focus from model training to inferencetime computation the talk will discuss empirical results theoretical underpinnings and emerging directions toward scalable sustainable reasoning systems speaker bio ishan jindal phd is a staff engineer at samsung rd indiadelhi where he leads research on efficient and adaptive large language models for nextgeneration agentic ai systems his work focuses on llm inferencetime optimization prompting and finetuning and humanintheloop reasoning systems before joining samsung he was a staff research scientist at ibm research almaden usa where he contributed to the development of multilingual nlp systems for ibm watson and codeveloped the universal propbank dataset his research has appeared in premier venues including acl emnlp naacl eacl icassp and he holds multiple us patents in deep learning and semantic understanding all interested are cordially invited to attend the seminar

Subject: number theory seminar on thursday november by prof koji tasaka
Body: dear all it is our great pleasure to announce a number theory seminar by prof koji tasaka from kindai university japan on november at noon the details of the talk are given below title spherical designs and modular forms abstract a spherical design regarded as a spherical analogue of a cubature formula is defined for a finite subset of the sphere in ddimensional euclidean space and is characterized by a quantity called its strength determining the strength of a given finite subset on the sphere is a central problem in this area in this talk i will share some results on the relationship between this topic and the theory of modular forms involving euclidean lattices quaternion algebras weighted theta series and the nonvanishing of fourier coefficients of cusp forms this is a joint work with masatake hirao and hiroshi nozaki time and venue thursday november noon at room no academic complex west b all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team dr ekata saha assistant professor department of mathematics indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: today departmental seminar prof denis thieffry ens institute curie paris th nov pm lh at lhc
Body: dear all this is just a kind reminder for the seminar on th november at pm by prof denis thieffry the seminar will take place in lh lhc details are available in the trailing email please let me know if anyone is interested in interacting with the speaker that day so we can plan the schedule accordingly best saurabh on saurabh raj wrote dear all we invite you to the ksbs departmental talk on november at pm in lh at lhc the speaker is prof denis thieffry a professor at ecole normale supérieure institut curie psl university paris france please circulate this information in your department all are cordially invited details may be found below speaker prof denis thieffry date th november time pm venue lh lhc title reproducible computational modelling of acute promyelocytic leukaemia resistance to retinoic acid therapy abstract acute promyelocytic leukaemia apl arises from an aberrant chromosomal translocation involving the retinoic acid receptor alpha rara gene predominantly with the promyelocytic leukaemia pml or promyelocytic leukaemia zinc finger plzf genes the resulting oncoproteins block the haematopoietic differentiation program promoting aberrant proliferative promyelocytes retinoic acid ra therapy is successful in most of the pmlrara patients while plzfrara patients frequently become resistant and relapse recent studies pointed to various underlying molecular components but their precise contributions remain to be deciphered in this respect we have integrated the main underlying signalling transcriptional and epigenetic regulatory mechanisms into a mechanistic network model using a logical formalism we have demonstrated that this model captures key features of the apl cell responses to ra depending on the genetic background the explicit inclusion of the histone methyltransferase ezh allowed the assessment of its role in the resistance mechanism distinguishing between its canonical and noncanonical activities the model dynamics was thoroughly analysed using tools integrated in the public software suite maintained by the colomoto consortium the model serves as a solid basis to assess the roles of novel regulatory mechanisms as well as to explore novel therapeutical approaches in silicon speaker bio denis thieffry obtained his phd in at the free university of brussels under the direction of rené thomas and made postdocs in mexico unam germany mpi berlin and belgium univ ghent dt was appointed as full professor of bioinformatics at the university of aixmarseille in france in before moving to paris in to assume the position of professor of systems biology at the ecole normale supérieure ens he is currently associate editor of the journals plos computational biology and nar genomics bioinformatics he has published over articles and book chapters mostly in international journals proceedings and books his current research focuses on the dynamical modelling of the regulatory network controlling haematopoieticimmune cell fate specification and reprogramming in close collaboration with several experimental teams publication list the speaker has also shown interest in interacting with faculty members if anyone is interested please let me know by st november thank you best regards saurabh saurabh raj phd assistant professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology Subject: doubt raised in q of tutorial
Body: an interesting doubt was raised in class today regarding q of tutorial find the clarification doubt raised if current is a function of theta why partial derivative of field energy with theta will not be considered clarification it has to be understood that the relation between current with theta is mentioned as law of deflection meaning for a particular construction of moving iron meter the inductance varies in a manner that from certain deflection theta observed in the meter the current can be related to theta as given in the expression it doesnt mean current is varied with theta hence the question is how the inductance should vary such that the current reading follows given expression solution is provided accordingly the assertion in the doubt is valid for electromechanical system where current changes with position the moving iron meter is not such a system best wishes डॉ सुमित कुमार प्रामाणिक dr sumit kumar pramanick सह प्राध्यापक associate professor विद्युतीय अभियांत्रिकी विभाग department of electrical engineering भारतीय प्रौद्योगिकी संस्थान दिल्ली indian institute of technology delhi नई दिल्ली भारत new delhi india वेबसाइट website फ़ोन phone o
