Subject: fwd talk on homogeneity with respect to a part of variables and accelerated stabilization on at pm in ee committee room ii
Body: a gentle reminder for the talk tomorrow at pm ee committee room original message subject talk on homogeneity with respect to a part of variables and accelerated stabilization on at pm in ee committee room ii date from head ee to dear all there will be a talk by prof denis efimov on homogeneity with respect to a part of variables and accelerated stabilization as per following schedule date time september tuesday at pm venue ee committee room ii title homogeneity with respect to a part of variables and accelerated stabilization abstract the presentation addresses the problem of transforming a locally asymptotically stabilizing timevarying control law to a global one with accelerated finitefixedtime convergence rates the approach relies on an extension of the theory of homogeneous systems to homogeneity only with respect to a part of the state variables and on the associated partial stability properties the proposed control design builds upon the kind of approaches first studied in mcloskeymurray and uses the implicit lyapunov function framework a sampledtime implementation scheme of the control law is also presented and its properties are characterized the method is illustrated by finitetime and nearly fixedtime stabilization of a nonholonomic integrator about the speaker denis efimov received phd degree in automatic control from the saintpetersburg state electrical engineering university russia in and drsc degree in automatic control in from the institute for problems of mechanical engineering ras saintpetersburg russia from to he was working in the l s cnrs supelec france the montefiore institute university of liege belgium and ims cnrs lab university of bordeaux france in he joined inria lille nord europe center starting from he is the scientific head of valse team he is a member of several ifac tcs and a senior member of ieee he is also serving as an associate editor for ieee transactions on automatic control and automatica thanks Subject: talk on homogeneity with respect to a part of variables and accelerated stabilization on at pm in ee committee room ii
Body: dear all there will be a talk by prof denis efimov on homogeneity with respect to a part of variables and accelerated stabilization as per following schedule date time september tuesday at pm venue ee committee room ii title homogeneity with respect to a part of variables and accelerated stabilization abstract the presentation addresses the problem of transforming a locally asymptotically stabilizing timevarying control law to a global one with accelerated finitefixedtime convergence rates the approach relies on an extension of the theory of homogeneous systems to homogeneity only with respect to a part of the state variables and on the associated partial stability properties the proposed control design builds upon the kind of approaches first studied in mcloskeymurray and uses the implicit lyapunov function framework a sampledtime implementation scheme of the control law is also presented and its properties are characterized the method is illustrated by finitetime and nearly fixedtime stabilization of a nonholonomic integrator about the speaker denis efimov received phd degree in automatic control from the saintpetersburg state electrical engineering university russia in and drsc degree in automatic control in from the institute for problems of mechanical engineering ras saintpetersburg russia from to he was working in the l s cnrs supelec france the montefiore institute university of liege belgium and ims cnrs lab university of bordeaux france in he joined inria lille nord europe center starting from he is the scientific head of valse team he is a member of several ifac tcs and a senior member of ieee he is also serving as an associate editor for ieee transactions on automatic control and automatica thanks regards oo head ee

Subject: ieee apscon call for paper
Body: dear all ieee sensors council is happy to announce the fourth edition of the ieee applied sensing conference apscon at delhi from to february this follows the resounding success of the ieee apscon preceding conferences in bangalore in goa in and hyderabad in ieee apscon is a premier conference dedicated to applied sensing technologies bringing together researchers industry experts and students to explore innovations across diverse domains apscon invites original research papers not being considered for publication elsewhere of pages in standard ieee conference template on applications of sensors and sensing techniques in one of the following ten tracks but are not limited to tracks track agriculture and food technology track transportation systems track medical and digital healthcare track manufacturing and automation track environment and climate change monitoring track infrastructure and sustainability track robotics and digital twin track wearables and immersive technologies track analytical instrumentation track emerging quantum technologies special session special session ai for sensing other sessions session i live demo session ii student research forum session iii journal prepublished paper session iv sensors letters sl rerouted papers option a session v direct to sensors letters papers option b publication of papers in conference proceedings and ieee sensors letters authors get two options of submissions option a to the conference through online submission portal option b direct to the ieee sensors letters through scholarone website papers submitted to option a will be reviewed by the technical program committee of apscon for quality and scope if accepted the authors will be able to present their work during the conference such papers submitted and accepted via option a will be published in the conference proceedings papers submitted via option b will be reviewed by the editorial team of ieee sensors letters and will be published directly in this journal if accepted authors of such papers are expected to present their work during apscon provided the topic aligns with the scope of the conference papers that are not accepted under option b may be submitted via option a after appropriately addressing reviewers comments from ieee sensors letters important dates august paper submission opens september paper submission closes option b for direct to sensors letters september paper submission closes option a submission to the conference november notification of acceptance december author registration opens december final submission closes january author registration closes january early bird registration closes industry day full of industryled activities thematic roundtable meetings focused sessions keynote talks tutorialsworkshops sensors startup summit the emerging ecosystem of startups will be invited to network and get together to share their successstories opportunities marketplace and technological challenges live demos of their business model is also invited students research forum we invite advanced stage phd work and completed theses not older than months mtechms theses and undergrad high level research projects to present and get inputs from the experts this will give these aspiring students a platform to network improve their work besides exploring postdoctoral opportunities andor job offers sensors standards opportunities ieee sensors councils standards committee invites you to explore sensors domains standards development opportunities while sharing an overview of its activities for more information please visit ieeeapsconorg best regards dhiman dr dhiman mallick associate professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology Subject: discrepancies in cv window reopened for rectification
Body: dear students during the ongoing cv verification process it has been observed that several submissions contain discrepancies this is a serious matter if any such entries are flagged you will be asked to remove the same and the respective linessections will appear blank in your cv in view of the large number of such cases the cv submission window is being reopened one final time up to st august pm all students must remember to eliminate any false or unverifiable entries such as fake projects internships or achievements ensure that the pors and ecas mentioned on page are exactly the same as those listed on page any inconsistency will be flagged and you will be asked to remove it if you are mentioning any non iit delhi pors and ecas you must attach all legitimate supporting documents for verification not include any internships which are undertaken during the academic semester in your cv any overlapping internships should not be listed if you are mentioning any non ocs internship you must attach the offer letter completion letter with hr details clearly mentioned and an official email screenshot for verification the above points are only indicative and not exhaustive please note that once a cv has been flagged no editing will be permitted thereafter any misrepresentation of information will be treated as a serious matter and may lead to disciplinary action including debarment from the placement processimportant it has come to our notice that some secondyear hva students have created their cvs on the portal for placements you are hereby advised to kindly visit the ocs office and deregister yourselves at the earliest failure to do so will result in disqualification from participating in the placement process during your final yearthis is the final opportunity to rectify your cv failing which the flagged content will be permanently removed and your participation in the placement process may be adversely affected best regardsocs office

Subject: thank you for the support
Body: dear all i write this mail to express my gratitude and appreciation for all the support and encouragement shown to me during my term as dean diversity and inclusion this was the first term of the deanship and the first time for such an office we had to work without any precedents and make up a roadmap as we went along each and every other administrative unit in the institute helped with this and gave support advice and checks and balances as required these three years have personally helped me grow and learn tremendously and i hope have also been somewhat transformative for the institute we have received very positive feedback from students colleagues and parents encouraging us to believe we were on the right track there are some visible and obvious changes brought about especially with regard to accessible infrastructure and inclusive spaces both in the classrooms and outside as always the creation of a new entity created some discomfort and unease but also as always open conversations and dialogues helped as the initial phase of this office ends and a new dean takes over i am sure that you all will continue your support of the odi and all the verticals i would especially like to thank the director prof banerjee and the dds both prof sreekrishnan and prof nema and prof sagar for their unflinching support and open door policy as we navigated some tricky terrain to all my colleagues in the deans committee – past and present and of course all the administrative staff who are the backbone of the institute many thanks and to the students i would like to say i continue to be here and will be available but in another office  best angelie angelie multani dean diversity inclusion iit delhi

Subject: synopsis pres of akanksha dixit
Body: student akanksha dixit eez venue sit committee room time am thursday july th title design of a privacyaware temporal supersampling architecture abstract achieving a high qualityofexperience qoe in modern graphics applications demands low latency high frame rates realism and strong privacy safeguards this thesis addresses these challenges holistically within the limits of available hardware resources we begin with reducing the motiontophoton delay mpd in vr systems which is the time between a user’s head movement and the corresponding update a common mpd reduction technique is asynchronous time warping atw which reprojects the already rendered frame based on the most recent head position however the challenge lies in invoking atw at the right time instance within the refresh cycle hence we propose predatw a predictor that monitors the status of hardware resources and finds the right time to invoke the atw algorithm our predictor has an error of only ms across several popular vr applications we extend this approach further and make it work for highrefresh rate monitors they run at hz sadly the latest gpus also struggle to render frames at such high rates continuously extrapolationbased frame generation techniques are used to predict intermediate frames from already rendered frames thereby increasing the perceived frame rate in this thesis we target a guaranteed x frame rate increase from hz to hz using extrapolation no single existing extrapolation algorithm performs consistently well across all scene types each one is tailored to specific scenarios and exhibits strengths and weaknesses depending on the context hence we propose x rate a frame generation framework that combines multiple existing methods to deliver results superior to any individual algorithm x rate achieves x the rendering rate while delivering highquality frames outperforming the nearest competitor extranet with a improvement in the psnr next we propose a bespoke extrapolation method we propose a novel lightweight frame extrapolation algorithm patchex that exploits the perceptual sensitivity to generate the extrapolated frame additionally a wavelet transform wtbased filter pruning technique is applied to compress the extrapolation network significantly reducing the runtime our results demonstrate that patchex achieves a and improvement in psnr over the latest extrapolation methods extranet and extrass respectively while being x and x faster resp finally we address the data security and privacy challenges in highrefresh rate ar systems ar devices can inadvertently expose sensitive visual data ranging from bystanders’ identities to confidential physical documents existing privacypreserving methods are often too computationally heavy for realtime execution on resourceconstrained ar headsets hence we introduce arguard a lightweight realtime framework that integrates a saliencyaware object detection network with a novel irreversible obfuscation algorithm arguard operates at fps on microsoft hololens detecting and protecting sensitive regions with and higher accuracy as compared to the stateoftheart respectively we achieve a reduction in privacy leakage as compared to the best existing method bystandar to summarize this thesis presents a unified framework for addressing both performance and privacy issues in highrefreshrate graphics applications smruti ranjan sarangi hitech robotics and autonomous systems chair professor computer science and engineering iit delhi joint appt with electrical engineering iit delhi hauz khas new was inspired by gandhi kumarappa and vinoba he dedicated his life to using science and technology as a tool for nationbuilding particularly for holistic integrated rural development crdt has scheduled a session as part of this seminar on “holistic rural development contemporary possibilities” this session will have presentations of minutes only by research scholars masters students of iit delhi we invite you to submit a audioembedded ppt on the session theme latest by th august sunday pm via this google form a committee of professors of iit delhi will screen the submissions received and best certificate of participation submit your google slides presentation min voice embedded on this google form instructions to prepare your short thematic presentation the presenter should deeply understand the work of devendrabhai kumarappa gandhi and connect her his presentation to the philosophy of these selfless pioneers visit website and also study any critical works of m k gandhi and j c kumarappa the presentation should be directly related to holistic rural development should be inspired by the thoughts of devenrabhai kumarappa gandhi and importantly how your work relates to their thoughts and contemporary possibilities arising thereof the presentaiton should be of maximum mins only maximum of slides the presentation should be audio video embedded selected participants will be informed only selected participants will be contacted each selected participant will get mins live to present at the devendrabhai centenary seminar on august three best presenters will be honoured with best presenter award other presenters will be awarded a certificate of participation instructions for the short thematic presentation are also available on the google form looking forward to active participation from large number of phd scholars and msc students of the iit delhi on this important thematic area which is critical for nationbuilding warm regards head crdt iit delhi head crdt Subject: fwd membership applications for indradhanu for academic year
Body: dear all please see the mail below for membership to indradhanu best angelie angelie multani dean diversity inclusion iit delhi begin forwarded message from subject membership applications for indradhanu for academic year date august at pm ist to dean diversity and inclusion dear peers greetings from indradhanu the lgbtqia collective of iit delhi how often do we seriously think about the importance of gender and sexuality what they mean and what roles they play in our lives while all of us come to iit delhi to strive towards our academic goals there is a need to equip ourselves with information to respect human differences and diversity mutually this is where indradhanu comes into the picture for those interested indradhanu intends to create a safe space for conversation and dialogue on issues relating to varied human identities we hope to rethink conventional notions of masculinity and femininity and think over love family relationships community and alternative interpretations of the same help remove social taboos associated with gender and sexuality in addition we would like to address concerns surrounding the queer lives on campus and create awareness on navigating them with pride and dignity indradhanu is one of the four verticals under the office of diversity and inclusion and we strive to make iitd a more inclusive campus fill the form below if youd like to become a member of the collective link to membership form note current members include students belonging to the lgbtqia community as well as allies once you fill out the form an indradhanu coordinator will contact you and schedule a short interaction to get to know you better before you officially join the collective in case of doubts contact mahima ug himanshu pg regards vaivab das admin coordinator indradhanu fulbright nehru doctoral research scholar and phd student indian institute of technology delhi

Subject: re talk on probabilistically robust decision making under uncertainty
Body: a gentle reminder for the talk at pm today in the ee committee room shubhendu bhasin professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india web email tel o r fax original message subject talk on probabilistically robust decision making under uncertainty date from shubhendu bhasin to date time aug wed at pm venue ee committee room ii title probabilistically robust decision making for uncertain dynamical systems abstract typically how much do we know about an uncertain dynamical system uds matters a lot when we want to control them aiming to accurately capture the evolution of such uds is impossible as true system uncertainties cannot be captured exactly lack of exact system knowledge increases the difficulty in estimating the limits of the uncertain systems performance as a result we often seek to control such uds such that the resulting control decisions from robust decision making rdm paradigms render the uds insensitive to what we dont know about them however nature can violate the assumptions that the rdm module assumes for the system uncertainties with small probability controlling uds under such unforeseen events necessitates the addition of probabilistic rigour on top of the existing rdm approaches in this talk i shall propose a probabilistic rdm prdm approach using the uncertain gap between the dynamical system models with and without the uncertainty induced by an appropriate distance metric the proposed framework will allow us to analyse the potential performance degradation of a control action on a uds when such rare violation events occur the fertile nature of the probabilistic robust control research area will be highlighted using a list of interesting future research directions speaker bio venkatraman renganathan is currently working as a lecturer at cranfield university in the uk previously he was a postdoctoral research fellow at the department of automatic control in lund university sweden he completed his phd in mechanical engineering on from the university of texas at dallas usa he finished his ms in electrical engineering on from the arizona state university usa and his bachelors degree in electrical electronics engineering in from anna university in india his research interests include probabilistic robust control risk bounded motion planning and adaptive control of uncertain networked systems

Subject: departmental seminar dr ashima bhaskar icgeb rd sept pm ksbs committee room
Body: dear all we invite you to the ksbs departmental talk on rd september at pm in the ksbs committee room the speaker is dr ashima bhaskar currently working as a research scientist at the international centre for genetic engineering and biotechnology icgeb please circulate this information in your department all are cordially invited details may be found below speaker dr ashima bhaskar date rd september time pm venue committee room ksbs title defeating tuberculosis target the bug or the host abstract tuberculosis tb a deadly disease caused by the intracellular pathogen mycobacterium tuberculosis mtb has existed since time immemorial and continues to remain one of the leading causes of mortality by a single infectious agent classic antitb therapy which comprises the administration of multiple antimycobacterial drugs fails to provide complete sterilization in the host incessant rise in drugresistant tb cases further highlights the failure of current antitb therapy which only focuses on targeting microbial pathways host immune system plays a pivotal role in the containment of the infection while mtb has evolved brilliant strategies to avoid immune surveillance which facilitates its survival replication and persistence recent studies hint towards the pathogeninduced histone modifications as an emerging host subversion strategy employed by a number of bacteria wherein virulence factors are shown to alter host epigenome by modulating histone acetyltransferases and histone deacetylases we are deciphering the role of different hdacs in modulating adaptive immune responses during tb pathogenesis we attempt to put forth hdac inhibitors or their specific targets as potential candidates for hostdirected therapy in adjunct with the existing antitb regime which may lead to enhanced bacterial clearance shorter treatment times reduced tissue damage a decline in drugresistant strains and a lower risk of relapse thank you best regards saurabh saurabh raj phd assistant professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: reminder departmental seminar dr tanmoy saha harvard medical school th august am ksbs committee room
Body: dear all this is just a reminder for tomorrows seminar in the ksbs committee room at am by dr tanmoy saha the details of the talk are in the trailing mail we hope to see many of you there best saurabh on saurabh raj wrote dear all we invite you to the ksbs departmental talk on th august at am in the ksbs committee room the speaker is dr tanmoy saha currently working as an instructor at the department of medicine harvard medical school and associate bioengineer at the department of medicine brigham and womens hospital please circulate this information all are cordially invited details may be found below speaker dr tanmoy saha date th august time am venue committee room ksbs title harnessing nanoscale cellular communication for next generation anticancer therapeutics abstract aberrant intercellular communication underlies disease progression for example cancer cells communicate with neighboring cells using extracellular proteins and physical nanotube formation to gain survival advantages i investigate such cellular communication mechanistically and design novel therapeutic strategies immunotherapy has made a paradigm shift in cancer treatment but it only responds to less than of cancer patients i have shown how cancer cells use multiple checkpoints to block the immune cells i have introduced bifunctional immunoengineered nanotherapeutics that can block multiple cancer immune interactions and can deliver pharmacological drugs specifically to the cancer cells we have shown increased therapeutic efficacy in lung cancer where traditional immunotherapy fails furthermore we investigated a novel mechanism of immune evasion by cancer cells through nanoscale physical communication we have used highresolution electron and optical microscopy to identify the nanotubemediated mitochondrial hijack by cancer cells from t cells the transfer of mitochondria metabolically empowers the cancer cells and increases their proliferation metastasis and drug resistance in contrast the t cell population depletes because of metabolic deactivation blocking the nanotubemediated mitochondria transfer by pharmacological inhibitors has shown potential therapeutic implications in increasing the intrinsic t cell immune response and elevating therapeutic efficacy in combination with traditional immunotherapy short bio dr saha is an entrylevel faculty member at harvard medical school and an associate bioengineer at mass general brigham he has completed an msc from visva bharati university and a phd from the indian institute of science education and research pune he was a postdoctoral fellow at harvardmit health science and technology dr sahas major research direction is to develop tools to study cellular communication and introduce novel therapeutic strategies he has published his research in prestigious journals including nature nanotechnology science advances j am chem soc cell pnas etc he has received independent research grants from the department of defense and the melanoma research alliance and many awards including the best thesis award scholar in training award etc thank you best regards saurabh raj phd assistant Subject: re invited talk by prof dirk hovy aug at
Body: a gentle reminder the talk is starting in mins thanks tanmoy original message subject invited talk by prof dirk hovy aug at date from tanmoy chakraborty to dear all prof dirk hovy is visiting iit delhi and giving a talk on tuesday august th he is highly influential in nlp working a lot on ai ethics computational social science multilinguality etc please let me know if you or your students want to meet him in person venue for the talk sit time aug title speaking fluent gibberish why language models do not understand language and what to do about it abstract in a world where ai can generate everything from translations to poetry and code its tempting to believe that these models truly understand us despite its linguistic prowess todays generative ai still resembles a clever mimic rather than a genuine linguist in this talk we will look at thought experiments like the chinese room to look at the limitations of statistical models knowledge their inability to grasp context and nuance and the risks of overestimating their capabilities well find out what this has to do with getting lost in translation sounding like our own grandfathers and encountering an incomprehensible lion diving into philosophy linguistics and nlp we investigate what it truly means to understand a language emphasizing the theoretical and practical implications for future language technology i will illustrate the important with some recent work in my group on social context in models ie how socioeconomic status and gender and emotion impacts llms and what it means for safety and utility in llms bio dirk hovy is a professor in the computing sciences department of bocconi university the dean for digital transformation and ai and the scientific director of the data and marketing insights research unit previously he was faculty at the university of copenhagen got a phd from uscs information sciences institute and a linguistics masters from marburg university in germany he is interested in what computers can tell us about language and what language can tell us about society he is also interested in ethical questions of bias and algorithmic fairness in machine learning dirk has authored over articles on these topics and two textbooks on nlp in python dirk has cofounded and organized several workshops on computational social science and ethics in nlp was a local organizer for the emnlp conference and general chair of emnlp he was awarded an erc starting grant project for research on demographic bias in nlp in his spare time he enjoys cooking leather working and picking up heavy things to put them back down thanks tanmoy

Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the me guest talk by prof zonghong lin from national taiwan university ntu as per the schedule below date monday th august time pm venue me seminar room ii title selfpowered devices based on triboelectrification abstract designing devices with selfpowered sensing function has become a popular research field since its emergence in recent decades triboelectrification occurs when two materials come into contact with each other causing charge transfer that leads to oppositely charged surfaces the amount of charge transfer varies depending on material composition by combining triboelectrification with electrostatic induction relevant devices can be designed if used for energy collection purposes scientists generally refer to them as triboelectric nanogenerators tengs but if used for selfpowered sensing purposes scientists call them triboelectric nanosensors tenss in our previous research on tenss we demonstrated the concept of selective detection of some targets by specific materials or their surfacemodified probes when the targets are adsorbing or binding to the surface different electrical output signals will be generated compared to before and these changes can be used for qualitative and quantitative analysis of the targets in the past few years we have further developed solidliquid tenss for measuring targets such as metal ions small molecules proteins and microorganisms compared with our previously developed solidsolid tenss we have not only improved several shortcomings but also established sensing mechanism and working principle which are very important research achievements in this field we also look forward to expanding the applications of the solidliquid tenss in the near future bio zonghong lin professor national taiwan university ntu lab website research areas micro and nanomaterialsgenerators for bioelectrical stimulation applications selfpowered biochemical sensors biomedical diagnostic devices wearable healthcare electronics and remote intelligent monitoring platform dr zonghong lin received his phd from the national taiwan university ntu in and continued with his postdoctoral research at the ntu and the georgia tech during the years of subsequently dr lin joined the institute of biomedical engineering national tsing hua university nthu as assistant professor in and was Body: dear all we have a new wellbeing counsellor level os who joined iitd in august we welcome her into our iitd family and hope to benefit from her counselling experience and expertise and also wish her all the very best here at iitd a brief biosketch is given under biosketchsamriddhi samriddhi is a compassionate psychotherapist with an mphil in psychoanalytic psychotherapy from dr br ambedkar university delhi and a masters in psychology from the university of delhi her practice is rooted in empathy deep listening and the quiet radical act of making space for feelings that are tangled for truths not yet spoken trained across varied clinical landscapes she offers inclusive therapy and counselling for those navigating anxiety identity or the chaotic beauty of simply being human her approach is traumainformed queeraffirming and deeply attuned to the uniqueness of each persons story her work isnt just grounded its gently transformative a space where emotional clarity begins to breathe and selfunderstanding unfolds like morning light with experience as a senior behaviour therapist counselling programme director and psychodynamic practitioner across ngos private organizations and private practice she blends psychological insight with communityrooted care bringing thoughtful support to those seeking healing meaning and renewal to seek help she believes is to step into ones becoming through soulful conversation and thoughtful care she walks alongside her clients not to lead or follow but to move in rhythm with their needs for her therapy is a slow and vivid dance toward healing insight and meaning dr sreedevi upadhyayula associate dean student affairs student welfare professor class of chair department of chemical engineering indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india phone

Subject: invited talk by prof dirk hovy aug at
Body: dear all prof dirk hovy is visiting iit delhi and giving a talk on tuesday august th he is highly influential in nlp working a lot about ai ethics computational social science multilinguality etc please let me know if you or your students want to meet him in person venue for the talk sit time aug title speaking fluent gibberish why language models do not understand language and what to do about it abstract in a world where ai can generate everything from translations to poetry and code its tempting to believe that these models truly understand us despite its linguistic prowess todays generative ai still resembles a clever mimic rather than a genuine linguist in this talk we will look at thought experiments like the chinese room to look at the limitations of statistical models knowledge their inability to grasp context and nuance and the risks of overestimating their capabilities well find out what this has to do with getting lost in translation sounding like our own grandfathers and encountering an incomprehensible lion diving into philosophy linguistics and nlp we investigate what it truly means to understand a language emphasizing the theoretical and practical implications for future language technology i will illustrate the important with some recent work in my group on social context in models ie how socioeconomic status and gender and emotion impacts llms and what it means for safety and utility in llms bio dirk hovy is a professor in the computing sciences department of bocconi university the dean for digital transformation and ai and the scientific director of the data and marketing insights research unit previously he was faculty at the university of copenhagen got a phd from uscs information sciences institute and a linguistics masters from marburg university in germany he is interested in what computers can tell us about language and what language can tell us about society he is also interested in ethical questions of bias and algorithmic fairness in machine learning dirk has authored over articles on these topics and two textbooks on nlp in python dirk has cofounded and organized several workshops on computational social science and ethics in nlp was a local organizer for the emnlp conference and general chair of emnlp he was awarded an erc starting grant project for research on demographic bias in nlp in his spare time he enjoys cooking leather working and picking up heavy things to put them back down thanks tanmoy

Subject: talk on probabilistically robust decision making under uncertainty
Body: date time aug wed at pm venue ee committee room ii title probabilistically robust decision making for uncertain dynamical systems abstract typically how much do we know about an uncertain dynamical system uds matters a lot when we want to control them aiming to accurately capture the evolution of such uds is impossible as true system uncertainties cannot be captured exactly lack of exact system knowledge increases the difficulty in estimating the limits of the uncertain systems performance as a result we often seek to control such uds such that the resulting control decisions from robust decision making rdm paradigms render the uds insensitive to what we dont know about them however nature can violate the assumptions that the rdm module assumes for the system uncertainties with small probability controlling uds under such unforeseen events necessitates the addition of probabilistic rigour on top of the existing rdm approaches in this talk i shall propose a probabilistic rdm prdm approach using the uncertain gap between the dynamical system models with and without the uncertainty induced by an appropriate distance metric the proposed framework will allow us to analyse the potential performance degradation of a control action on a uds when such rare violation events occur the fertile nature of the probabilistic robust control research area will be highlighted using a list of interesting future research directions speaker bio venkatraman renganathan is currently working as a lecturer at cranfield university in the uk previously he was a postdoctoral research fellow at the department of automatic control in lund university sweden he completed his phd in mechanical engineering on from the university of texas at dallas usa he finished his ms in electrical engineering on from the arizona state university usa and his bachelors degree in electrical electronics engineering in from anna university in india his research interests include probabilistic robust control risk bounded motion planning and adaptive control of uncertain networked systems shubhendu bhasin professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas Subject: reminder sparc seminar by dr ville takala university college london thursday august am
Body: title towards an entrepreneurial welfare state a conceptual perspective speaker dr ville takala lecturer teaching in global prosperity at the ucl institute for global prosperity university college london venue lh lecture hall complex time thursday august am pm abstract the recent turn towards challengedriven missionoriented or transformative innovation policy has emphasised that governments must proactively shape and cocreate market and innovation processes to address grand societal challenges of the st century as a result the socalled entrepreneurial state has been promoted in traditional welfare states in europe over the past decade tasked with steering economic development towards socially and environmentally desirable outcomes by reviewing key literature and drawing on empirical data from finland and the uk this presentation contrasts the entrepreneurial state and the welfare state as two distinct governmental rationalities the presentation puts forward the empirically grounded conceptual perspective that whereas a traditional welfare state addresses societal concerns primarily through reactive functions regulation redistribution provision of social services funded through taxation an entrepreneurial welfare state proactively shapes steers and incentivises market and innovation activities to match societal needs the presentation analyses the conflicting demands that the entrepreneurial welfare state places on public bureaucracy about the speaker dr ville takala is lecturer teaching in global prosperity at the ucl institute for global prosperity he is a sociologist whose research explores the digital future of the state particularly as it relates to the affordances of new digital data sources in addition his research investigates novel policy instruments such as challenge prizes and their capacity to drive challengedriven innovation in the public sector villes phd which he completed at the department of sociology at goldsmiths university of london focusses on questions surrounding the ownership of data within the context of the nordic welfare state following his phd ville worked at the ucl institute for innovation and public purpose as a research fellow between ville was postdoctoral researcher and pi of the business finland funded research project towards an entrepreneurial welfare state the practices of challengedriven innovation policies at the hanken school of economics debananda misra assistant professor school of public policy

Subject: departmental seminar dr sudipta tung ashoka university th september am ksbs committee room
Body: dear all we invite you to the ksbs departmental talk on th september at am in the ksbs committee room the speaker is dr sudipta tung currently working as a faculty member at ashoka university please circulate this information in your department all are cordially invited details may be found below speaker dr sudipta tung date th september time am venue committee room ksbs title metabolic time machine dietdriven plasticity and adaptation across life stages abstract the evolutionary mismatch hypothesis suggests that modern diets have changed faster than the metabolic systems shaped by natural selection yet we lack direct multigenerational tests of this idea especially across life stages in mammals and humans such experiments are blocked by practical and ethical limits drosophila melanogaster offers a rare workaround a short generation time and the ability to control proteincarbohydrate ratios exactly keeping diets isocaloric in our work we use fullfactorial combinations of larval and adult diets track their effects on development reproduction and lifespan and follow these responses over many generations under experimental evolution we combine these assays with multiomics and models that connect individual physiology to population dynamics this approach begins to answer a key question how do mismatches between developmental and adult nutrition shape both shortterm performance and longterm evolutionary outcomesin contexts as different as human metabolic disease and wildlife facing climatedriven dietary change short bio sudipta tung is a dbtwellcome trust india alliance early career fellow at ashoka university and leads a lab that studies how diet shapes physiology and evolution in drosophila melanogaster the work combines experimental evolution physiological assays rnaseq and other omics with computational models that generate predictions tested through targeted experiments linking molecular changes to population outcomes best saurabh saurabh raj phd assistant professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: sparc seminar by dr ville takala university college london thursday august am
Body: title towards an entrepreneurial welfare state a conceptual perspective speaker dr ville takala lecturer teaching in global prosperity at the ucl institute for global prosperity university college london venue lh lecture hall complex time thursday august am pm abstract the recent turn towards challengedriven missionoriented or transformative innovation policy has emphasised that governments must proactively shape and cocreate market and innovation processes to address grand societal challenges of the st century as a result the socalled entrepreneurial state has been promoted in traditional welfare states in europe over the past decade tasked with steering economic development towards socially and environmentally desirable outcomes by reviewing key literature and drawing on empirical data from finland and the uk this presentation contrasts the entrepreneurial state and the welfare state as two distinct governmental rationalities the presentation puts forward the empirically grounded conceptual perspective that whereas a traditional welfare state addresses societal concerns primarily through reactive functions regulation redistribution provision of social services funded through taxation an entrepreneurial welfare state proactively shapes steers and incentivises market and innovation activities to match societal needs the presentation analyses the conflicting demands that the entrepreneurial welfare state places on public bureaucracy about the speaker dr ville takala is lecturer teaching in global prosperity at the ucl institute for global prosperity he is a sociologist whose research explores the digital future of the state particularly as it relates to the affordances of new digital data sources in addition his research investigates novel policy instruments such as challenge prizes and their capacity to drive challengedriven innovation in the public sector villes phd which he completed at the department of sociology at goldsmiths university of london focusses on questions surrounding the ownership of data within the context of the nordic welfare state following his phd ville worked at the ucl institute for innovation and public purpose as a research fellow between ville was postdoctoral researcher and pi of the business finland funded research project towards an entrepreneurial welfare state the practices of challengedriven innovation policies at the hanken school of economics debananda misra assistant professor school of public policy

Subject: departmental seminar dr tanmoy saha harvard medical school th august am ksbs committee room
Body: dear all we invite you to the ksbs departmental talk on th august at am in the ksbs committee room the speaker is dr tanmoy saha currently working as an instructor at the department of medicine harvard medical school and associate bioengineer at the department of medicine brigham and womens hospital please circulate this information all are cordially invited details may be found below speaker dr tanmoy saha date th august time am venue committee room ksbs title harnessing nanoscale cellular communication for next generation anticancer therapeutics abstract aberrant intercellular communication underlies disease progression for example cancer cells communicate with neighboring cells using extracellular proteins and physical nanotube formation to gain survival advantages i investigate such cellular communication mechanistically and design novel therapeutic strategies immunotherapy has made a paradigm shift in cancer treatment but it only responds to less than of cancer patients i have shown how cancer cells use multiple checkpoints to block the immune cells i have introduced bifunctional immunoengineered nanotherapeutics that can block multiple cancer immune interactions and can deliver pharmacological drugs specifically to the cancer cells we have shown increased therapeutic efficacy in lung cancer where traditional immunotherapy fails furthermore we investigated a novel mechanism of immune evasion by cancer cells through nanoscale physical communication we have used highresolution electron and optical microscopy to identify the nanotubemediated mitochondrial hijack by cancer cells from t cells the transfer of mitochondria metabolically empowers the cancer cells and increases their proliferation metastasis and drug resistance in contrast the t cell population depletes because of metabolic deactivation blocking the nanotubemediated mitochondria transfer by pharmacological inhibitors has shown potential therapeutic implications in increasing the intrinsic t cell immune response and elevating therapeutic efficacy in combination with traditional immunotherapy short bio dr saha is an entrylevel faculty member at harvard medical school and an associate bioengineer at mass general brigham he has completed an msc from visva bharati university and a phd from the indian institute of science education and research pune he was a postdoctoral fellow at harvardmit health science and technology dr sahas major research direction is to develop tools to study cellular communication and introduce novel therapeutic strategies he has published his research in prestigious journals including nature nanotechnology science advances j am chem soc cell pnas etc he has received independent research grants from the department of defense and the melanoma research alliance and many awards including the best thesis award scholar in training award etc thank you best regards saurabh raj phd assistant professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: departmental seminar dr bhargab kalita nyu grossman school of medicine th august am ksbs committee room
Body: dear all we invite you to the ksbs departmental talk on th august at am in the ksbs committee room the speaker is dr bhargab kalita currently working as a postdoctoral researcher at the nyu grossman school of medicine please circulate this information amongst all all are cordially invited details may be found below speaker dr bhargab kalita date th august time am venue committee room ksbs title exploring tumorinitiation events in highrisk rhabdomyosarcoma uncovers therapeutic vulnerabilities abstract alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma arms is a highrisk cancer and among the most aggressive pediatric soft tissue sarcomas with a poor survival outcome as the disease advances overall pediatric patients with arms harboring chromosomal translocation t or t that results in a pax fkhr or pax fkhr fusion transcription factors exhibit a greater incidence of tumor relapse metastasis and poor survival outcome thereby underscoring the urgent need to develop effective therapies to treat this subtype of childhood cancer using genomic engineering in human ipsc cells i have developed a novel and controlled experimental model system ie muscle progenitors that allowed me to understand epigenetic remodeling underlying the cancer initiation events and metastatic phenotype of highrisk pediatric sarcoma tumors using integratedomics approach ie rnaseq cutrunseq d chromatin mapping hic promoter capture hic pchic and systematic comparisons with patientderived xenografts and primary tumors approach i uncovered how these fusion transcription factors reorganizes the chromatin architecture during tumor initiation and premalignant events to establish superenhancers that drive the expression of key mitochondrial target genes altering mitochondrial metabolism to promote tumor growth and aggressiveness in highrisk rhabdomyosarcoma thank you best regards saurabh saurabh raj phd assistant professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: reminder lecture by dr dr dipankar choudhury of ansys inc friday august pm
Body: computational fluid dynamics as an enabler of digital engineering methods and opportunities dr dipankar choudhury ansys fellow ansys inc and adjunct faculty at the university of notre dame august pm senate hall abstract the use of commercial computational fluid dynamics tools is now in its fifth decade with widespread adoption in industry research laboratories and academia this presentation provides a perspective on the current state of the art as well as the challenges in the development of largescale sophisticated engineering analysis systems that underline the pervasive usage in research and development progress in these software systems is related to advancements in areas like mathematical modeling numerical analysis geometry modeling and mesh generation high performance computing visualization and results analysis multiphysics methods and most recently in the incorporation of ai and machine learning finally the presentation addresses the question of what is involved in the adoption of engineering simulation tools by every engineer in industry and every researcher and student in academia about the speaker dr dipankar choudhury ansys fellow leads advanced technology and exploratory rd in several areas at ansys inc in addition he leads ansyss academic program which includes coordinating collaborative research and education partnership programs with academia centered around engineering simulation prior to taking this role dipankar was responsible for ansys incs technical directions in the fluids business unit dipankar obtained his be in mechanical engineering at bits pilani and his phd in computational fluid dynamics and heat transfer from the university of minnesota after his graduation he held engineering and product management positions at creare inc and fluent inc where he was part of the founding group and the chief technology officer he is a member of the asme aiaa and the asee and has technical publications in journals conference proceedings and trade magazines dr choudhury is an adjunct faculty at the university of notre dame and an invited lecturer at leading institutions worldwide dr vivek v buwa dean planning Subject: reminder spp policy in practice seminar pm by dr abhishek jain ias
Body: dear students and colleagues i am delighted to invite you to a policy in practice seminar delivered by dr abhishek jain titled research and governance where are we missing out a brief description of the talk and bio of the speaker are at the bottom of this mail the talk is organized jointly by spp and the ird office and will take place in ird conference room th floor main building iit delhi all interested are welcome please note the revised time best wishes suma athreye school of public policy iit delhi title research and governance where are we missing out date time august friday pm ist venue ird conference room th floor main building iit delhi abstract why despite having best of research institutions and intelligent government functionaries both are not able to get the best out of each other is research leading to improved governance at the ground level and does governance functionaries rely on latest and cuttingedge research to improve public policy design and policy implementation why and how both research and governance can be improved for each other and what top institutions like iit can pioneer in this regard do we need hitherto unexplored and outofthebox newer ways to get the best out of each other this talk will delve into these issues with author having been a senior government functionary with years experience and also a researcher with focused field publications in the area of development economics brief bio of speaker dr abhishek jain is an indian administrative service ias officer of batch presently posted as secretary finance planning public works economics statistics government of himachal pradesh he has years experience in senior government positions he holds a phd development economics master in international dev policy duke usa fellow company secretary advanced management programme in public policy indian school of business masters in economics he has authored india’s first ‘handbook on census’ and around fifty papers on governance and development issues with field evidence as an ias officer

Subject: re talk announcement realtime linear model predictive control for quadrotors on se an analytical koopmanbased realization
Body: a gentle reminder for the talk today date time aug wed at pm venue ee committee room ii title realtime linear model predictive control for quadrotors on se an analytical koopmanbased realization abstract this talk presents an analytical linear parameter varying lpv representation of quadrotor dynamics utilizing koopman theory facilitating computationally efficient linear model predictive control lmpc for realtime trajectory tracking by leveraging carefully designed koopman observables the proposed approach enables a compact liftedspace evolution that mitigates the curse of dimensionality while preserving the nonlinear characteristics of the system we develop an lpvlmpc framework that explicitly incorporates system constraints ensures realtime feasibility and provides a tracking performance comparable to computationally intensive nonlinear mpc nmpc the proposed control schemes are validated through highfidelity px quadrotor simulations in ros gazebo and experimental evaluations demonstrating their effectiveness in agile flight scenarios to the best of our knowledge this is the first analytical koopman lmpc approach for quadrotor drones that does not depend on training data to achieve experimental validation marking a significant step toward efficient realtime predictive control of quadrotors bio debdipta goswami is an assistant professor in the department of mechanical and aerospace engineering at the ohio state university where he leads the systems optimization and autonomous robotics soar lab he completed his undergrad in electrical and telecommunication engineering at jadavpur university subsequently he earned his phd in electrical and computer engineering from the university of maryland in under the supervision of prof derek a paley following his doctorate he conducted postdoctoral research at princeton university from to collaborating with prof clarence w rowley goswamis research focuses on the intersection of control theory and machine learning particularly in datadriven modeling and control of dynamical systems his expertise includes operatortheoretic methods reservoir computing and model predictive control with applications in aerial robotics and autonomous systems his work has been published in leading conferences and journals contributing to advancements in nonlinear systems datadriven estimation and multiagent systems at the osu goswami continues to explore structured learning of control systems from data aiming for guaranteed performance in realworld applications he also explores the design of an agile autopilot for multirotor drones and mission planning of both fixedwing and multirotor uavs all are welcome to attend best shubhendu

Subject: reminder hss seminar series wednesday august pm
Body: dear all you are all cordially invited to the second hss seminar of the semester on wednesday august by prof amit prasad details are as below and please see the link below for poster we look forward to seeing many of you there hss seminar series team date august time pm venue committee room ms department of humanities and social sciences th floor main building indian institute of technology delhi speaker amit prasad georgia institute of technology chair naveen thayyil department of huss iit delhi title j p s uberoi science swaraj and a postcolonial agenda abstract in more than half a century ago uberoi had succinctly characterized the “matrix of science and swaraj in today’s world rich poor international national white black” for uberoi science like any other knowledge was intimately tied to the political and it was imperative for independent india to challenge “the ruling scientific theories of nature” because they were undergirded by vivisection and violence and replicated colonial hegemony he thus traced an alternative genealogy of modern science and proposed an alternative science that relied on a nondualist semiological method unlike many other sociologists of science of his time and at present as well the alternative science he presented was not bounded within the nonwest or the west instead he sought to transgress the dualist boundaries between the west and the nonwest as well as several others such as those between sciencetruth and value while emphasizing the discursive power of such a divide in this presentation i critically engage with uberoi’s writings on science to highlight their continued relevance for an equitable and nonviolent postcolonial agenda speaker bio amit prasad is a professor at the school of history and sociology in georgia institute of technology he specializes in global transnational and postcolonial sociology and history of science technology and medicine his research focuses on the history of the present – in particular how history of colonialism continues to impact present day norms values and practices his goal has been to excavate the complex and often contradictory entanglements of colonial tropes ideologies etc with emergent knowledges and practices of science technology and medicine his publications include imperial technoscience entangled histories of mri in the united states britain and india mit press and science studies meets colonialism polity drawing on an ethnographic study of a stem cell clinic he is writing his third book that is tentatively titled miracle or science scientific uncertainty contested ethics and global melange in a stem cell laboratory he is currently the editor of the journal science technology and society sage

Subject: spp policy in practice seminar pm by dr abhishek jain ias
Body: dear students and colleagues i am delighted to invite you to a policy in practice seminar delivered by dr abhishek jain titled research and governance where are we missing out a brief description of the talk and bio of the speaker are at the bottom of this mail the talk is organized jointly by spp and the ird office and will take place in ird conference room th floor main building iit delhi all interested are welcome best wishes suma athreye school of public policy iit delhi title research and governance where are we missing out date time august friday pm ist venue ird conference room th floor main building iit delhi abstract why despite having best of research institutions and intelligent government functionaries both are not able to get the best out of each other is research leading to improved governance at the ground level and does governance functionaries rely on latest and cuttingedge research to improve public policy design and policy implementation why and how both research and governance can be improved for each other and what top institutions like iit can pioneer in this regard do we need hitherto unexplored and outofthebox newer ways to get the best out of each other this talk will delve into these issues with author having been a senior government functionary with years experience and also a researcher with focused field publications in the area of development economics brief bio of speaker dr abhishek jain is an indian administrative service ias officer of batch presently posted as secretary finance planning public works economics statistics government of himachal pradesh he has years experience in senior government positions he holds a phd development economics master in international dev policy duke usa fellow company secretary advanced management programme in public policy indian school of business masters in economics he has authored india’s first ‘handbook on census’ and around fifty papers on governance and development issues with field evidence as an ias officer thanks suma suma athreye school of public policy iit delhi

Subject: talk announcement realtime linear model predictive control for quadrotors on se an analytical koopmanbased realization
Body: date time aug wed at pm venue ee committee room ii title realtime linear model predictive control for quadrotors on se an analytical koopmanbased realization abstract this talk presents an analytical linear parameter varying lpv representation of quadrotor dynamics utilizing koopman theory facilitating computationally efficient linear model predictive control lmpc for realtime trajectory tracking by leveraging carefully designed koopman observables the proposed approach enables a compact liftedspace evolution that mitigates the curse of dimensionality while preserving the nonlinear characteristics of the system we develop an lpvlmpc framework that explicitly incorporates system constraints ensures realtime feasibility and provides a tracking performance comparable to computationally intensive nonlinear mpc nmpc the proposed control schemes are validated through highfidelity px quadrotor simulations in ros gazebo and experimental evaluations demonstrating their effectiveness in agile flight scenarios to the best of our knowledge this is the first analytical koopman lmpc approach for quadrotor drones that does not depend on training data to achieve experimental validation marking a significant step toward efficient realtime predictive control of quadrotors bio debdipta goswami is an assistant professor in the department of mechanical and aerospace engineering at the ohio state university where he leads the systems optimization and autonomous robotics soar lab he completed his undergrad in electrical and telecommunication engineering at jadavpur university subsequently he earned his phd in electrical and computer engineering from the university of maryland in under the supervision of prof derek a paley following his doctorate he conducted postdoctoral research at princeton university from to collaborating with prof clarence w rowley goswamis research focuses on the intersection of control theory and machine learning particularly in datadriven modeling and control of dynamical systems his expertise includes operatortheoretic methods reservoir computing and model predictive control with applications in aerial robotics and autonomous systems his work has been published in leading conferences and journals contributing to advancements in nonlinear systems datadriven estimation and multiagent systems at the osu goswami continues to explore structured learning of control systems from data aiming for guaranteed performance in realworld applications he also explores the design of an agile autopilot for multirotor drones and mission planning of both fixedwing and multirotor uavs all are welcome to attend best shubhendu shubhendu bhasin professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india web email tel o r fax

Subject: hss seminar series wednesday august pm
Body: dear all you are all cordially invited to the second hss seminar of the semester on wednesday august by prof amit prasad details are as below and please see the link below for poster we look forward to seeing many of you there hss seminar series team date august time pm venue committee room ms department of humanities and social sciences th floor main building indian institute of technology delhi speaker amit prasad georgia institute of technology chair naveen thayyil department of huss iit delhi title j p s uberoi science swaraj and a postcolonial agenda abstract in more than half a century ago uberoi had succinctly characterized the “matrix of science and swaraj in today’s world rich poor international national white black” for uberoi science like any other knowledge was intimately tied to the political and it was imperative for independent india to challenge “the ruling scientific theories of nature” because they were undergirded by vivisection and violence and replicated colonial hegemony he thus traced an alternative genealogy of modern science and proposed an alternative science that relied on a nondualist semiological method unlike many other sociologists of science of his time and at present as well the alternative science he presented was not bounded within the nonwest or the west instead he sought to transgress the dualist boundaries between the west and the nonwest as well as several others such as those between sciencetruth and value while emphasizing the discursive power of such a divide in this presentation i critically engage with uberoi’s writings on science to highlight their continued relevance for an equitable and nonviolent postcolonial agenda speaker bio amit prasad is a professor at the school of history and sociology in georgia institute of technology he specializes in global transnational and postcolonial sociology and history of science technology and medicine his research focuses on the history of the present – in particular how history of colonialism continues to impact present day norms values and practices his goal has been to excavate the complex and often contradictory entanglements of colonial tropes ideologies etc with emergent knowledges and practices of science technology and medicine his publications include imperial technoscience entangled histories of mri in the united states britain and india mit press and science studies meets colonialism polity drawing on an ethnographic study of a stem cell clinic he is writing his third book that is tentatively titled miracle or science scientific uncertainty contested ethics and global melange in a stem cell laboratory he is currently the editor of the journal science technology and society sage

Subject: civil engineering seminar series by prof vaneet aggarwal professor at purdue university scheduled on thursday st july at am in the committee room block iv room no department of civil engineering indian institute of technology iit delhi
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend a talk under the civil engineering seminar series by prof vaneet aggarwal professor at purdue university scheduled on thursday st july at am in the committee room block iv room no department of civil engineering indian institute of technology iit delhi title distributed ridesharing using deep reinforcement learning abstract the rapid growth of ridesharing services offers a compelling opportunity to reshape urban mobility through personalized efficient and scalable transportation yet a core challenge remains how to plan routes dynamically for each driver in real time in a way that balances rider preferences vehicle constraints and citywide efficiency in this talk ill present a demandaware pricingdriven framework for vehiclepassenger matching and route planning that operates under live conditions and continuously adapts to changing ride requests unlike traditional approaches that rely on static routing or simplistic heuristics with limited ride grouping our method learns to generate optimized multiride routes on the fly it incorporates driver decisionmaking by allowing pricing proposals based on expected future rewards and destinations informed by a deep qnetwork trained on supplydemand patterns customers in turn are given flexibility to accept or reject rides based on personalized preferences including price delay tolerance carpooling willingness and vehicle type the system further improves efficiency by proactively dispatching idle vehicles to highdemand areas using deep reinforcement learning for demand forecasting we validate our approach on millions of realworld trips from the nyc taxi dataset extending the analysis to multiple vehicle types and diverse rider behaviors the results highlight the systems effectiveness in largescale realtime settings and demonstrate its potential to drive smarter more adaptive ridesharing systems in practice bio vaneet aggarwal received the btech degree in from indian institute of technology kanpur india and the ma and phd degrees in and respectively from princeton university princeton nj usa he is currently a university faculty scholar and professor at purdue university where he has been since jan prior to this he worked as a researcher at att labsresearch florham park nj for four and a half years he was adjunct assistant professor at columbia university vajra adjunct professor at iisc bangalore and visiting faculty at kaust saudi arabia his research interests are in reinforcement learning generative ai and quantum computing dr aggarwal was the recipient of princeton universitys porter ogden jacobus honorific fellowship in and iit kanpurs sridhar memorial award in he further received purdues most impactful faculty innovator award in he also received the jack neubauer memorial award recognizing the best systems paper published in the ieee transactions on vehicular technology the ieee infocom workshop best paper award the neurips workshop best paper award and the ieee william bennett prize award recognizing the best paper published in ieeeacm transactions on networking he was on the editorial board of the ieee transactions on green communications and networking the ieee transactions on communications and the ieee transactions on network science and engineering he is currently serving on the editorial board of the ieeeacm transactions on networking and is coeditorinchief of the acm journal on transportation systems he has been pc cochair for multiple workshops at infocom aaai ijcai and conferences including gamenets qnlp and organized other workshops eg nsf pqai pqai he is also ieee comsoc distinguished lecturer thanks and regards office of the head department of civil engineering room no blockiv indian institute humanities and social sciences cordially invites you to a book discussion by professor aniruddha dutta the book discussion will be followed by high tea event details are as below and in the attached poster event title globalising through the vernacular kothis hijras and the making of queer and trans identities in india abstract since the s lgbtq movements in india have gained visibility and some degree of state recognition and rights this talk explores how this process has resulted in constrained forms of representation and upward mobility for nonelite nonmetropolitan communities such as kothis and hijras a spectrum of trans feminine people typically assigned male at birth drawing on my book globalising through the vernacular kothis hijras and the making of queer and trans identities in india bloomsbury i will outline how these communities facilitate the transregional expansion of queer politics but remain irreducible to emerging identity categories and become subordinated through linguistic and scalar hierarchies that reinforce inequities of class and caste the book analyses this process through the framework of ‘vernacularisation’ retheorising it as not the local adaptation capitalism liberalism caste andor nationalism simultaneously it will explore how such communities rearticulate lgbtq discourses in potentially liberatory ways bio aniruddha dutta is an associate Subject: mathematics colloquium on july thursday at pm in room no academic complex west b
Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department colloquium by prof shuchita goyal bits pilani on july thursday the details are given below title graph complexes date july thursday at pm venue room no academic complex west b speaker prof shuchita goyal abstract in topological combinatorics graph complexes refer to simplicial complexes that are generated using a particular graphtheoretic property of a graph there are several graph complexes like neighbourhood complex multineighbourhood complex independence complex matching complex higher matching complex etc to name a few a matching in a graph g is a collection of disjoint edges the perfect matching complex of a graph g is a simplicial complex whose facets are perfect matchings in g in this talk we will discuss the perfect matching complex of hexagonal tiling all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team

Subject: integrated photonics with handson training on meep
Body: dear students the optics and photonics center opc iit delhi is offering one threecredit courses this semester course opl – integrated photonics with handson training on meep objective the objective of this course is to provide a comprehensive introduction to integrated photonics covering both theoretical foundations and practical aspects of photonic device design and simulation students will learn about waveguide theory photonic components such as modulators detectors and resonators and the principles of photonic integrated circuit pic design a significant focus will be placed on handson training using meep an opensource fdtd simulation tool to model and analyse passive as well as active photonic structure by the end of the course students will be equipped with both the conceptual understanding and computational skills needed to design simulate and interpret the behaviour of integrated photonic devices and systems class details daytime mtf to pm any changes will be communicated first lecture on st august location opc committee room a rd floor rd block instructor prof awanish pandey best profpsenthilkumaran head optics and photonics centre chair professor prof ajoy ghatak chair indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: odi x hss event book talk by professor aniruddha dutta
Body: dear all indradhanu the lgbtqia student collective in collaboration with the office of diversity inclusion and the ma cst program department of humanities and social sciences cordially invites you to a book discussion by professor aniruddha dutta the book discussion will be followed by high tea event details are as below and in the attached poster event title globalising through the vernacular kothis hijras and the making of queer and trans identities in india abstract since the s lgbtq movements in india have gained visibility and some degree of state recognition and rights this talk explores how this process has resulted in constrained forms of representation and upward mobility for nonelite nonmetropolitan communities such as kothis and hijras a spectrum of trans feminine people typically assigned male at birth drawing on my book globalising through the vernacular kothis hijras and the making of queer and trans identities in india bloomsbury i will outline how these communities facilitate the transregional expansion of queer politics but remain irreducible to emerging identity categories and become subordinated through linguistic and scalar hierarchies that reinforce inequities of class and caste the book analyses this process through the framework of vernacularisation retheorising it as not the local adaptation or translation of globaltransnational discourses but as the positioning of nonelite communities and discourses as local or vernacular the talk will touch upon how vernacularisation erases the role of nonelite communities in transnational lgbtq movements and delegitimises kothihijra discourses and practices that contravene dominant forms of lgbtq identity politics aligned with transnational capitalism liberalism caste andor nationalism simultaneously it will explore how such communities rearticulate lgbtq discourses in potentially liberatory ways bio aniruddha dutta is an associate professor of gender womens and sexuality studies at the university of iowa duttas research interests include transnational sexualities globalisation development political economy and the institutionalisation of gender and sexual politics in india date and time th july venue hss committee room ms humanities and social sciences dept fifth floor main building iit delhi rsvp here on behalf of indradhanu team shahzad gani hehim faculty advisor indradhanu office of diversity and inclusion assistant professor centre for atmospheric sciences indian institute of technology delhi links
