Subject: new course announcement bml mechanics of biological systems
Body: dear students we are pleased to announce a new graduatelevel elective being offered at the center for biomedical engineering in this semester course name bml mechanics of biological systems slot ad course instructor prof aayush kant course objective to introduce students to the fundamental principles of solid and fluid mechanics applied to living systems the course aims to build an understanding of key mechanical principles eg equilibrium beam theory navierstokes equations and amalgamating them toward developing intuition for solving mechanobiological problems across scales who is it for students with a background in mechanical engineering applied mechanics material science physics chemistry and mathematics are welcome particularly if you are interested in gaining an applied understanding of mechanics in biological systems students with a background in biology are also encouraged to join as the course assumes only a high school knowledge of physics and mathematics course contents scope of continuum mechanics in biological systems refresher statics and dynamics refresher mathematical preliminaries tensors odes pdes stress and strain in d physical meaning and relationships kinematics stresses in higher dimensions generalized constitutive laws linear elasticity lehi and nonlinear behavior equilibrium equations and their application to biological systems thinwalled cylinders and pressurized spheres in physiology eg blood vessels alveoli beam bending and torsion in biological contexts eg bones tendons distinction between solids and fluids hydrostatics and fluid kinematics newtonian and nonnewtonian biological fluids eg blood mucus conservation of mass and momentum in continuum fluids navier–stokes equations and simplified flow cases viscoelastic behavior in soft tissues and biological gels fluidstructure interactions and wallwetting phenomena in biological systems eg cardiovascular and pulmonary flows expected learning outcomes by the end of the course you will understand how mechanics applies to biological systems across scales build and analyze simple models for mechanical behaviour in living systems differentiate between physical regimes elastic vs viscoelastic newtonian vs nonnewtonian develop intuition and basic skills necessary for realworld applications and research for any queries feel free to reach out to the instructor best prof neetu singh professor head center for biomedical engineering indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi alternate email webpage

diffusion growth and mechanics in batteries date and time th july pm link abstract lithiumion batteries have come to be used as the preferred power source for many electronic devices their applications have also been scaled up to electric vehicles as well as grid storage however for the scaling up to be truly commercially viable the natural limitations of charge capacity in the traditionally used materials need to be overcome this necessitates the exploration of newer materials silicon has emerged as a promising candidate as such a new material on the anode side now silicon expands by more than in volume when it is fully charged by lithium this gigantic growth of silicon throws up a number of challenges in its immediate adoption as a anode material these challenges can be answered by properly understanding the solid mechanical issues associated with its growth in this talk i will first present a general framework based on finite deformation theory incorporating diffusion growth and mechanics i will then discuss a few studies that apply this framework to various solid mechanical issues fundamentally induced by the diffusioninduced stresses within the anode particles in particular i will discuss possibilities of buckling and other general forms of instability surface stresses which become increasingly important at the nanometric length scales of the particles and also mechanical degradations associated with something referred to as the solid electrolyte interphase that are formed on such particles about the speaker dr jeevanjyoti chakraborty is an associate professor in the mechanical engineering department of iit kharagpur he has worked on the mathematical modelling of various situations involving fluid mechanics and solid mechanics coupled occasionally with bits of electrochemistry earlier he has worked on modelling fluid flow through deformable confinements exploring various interfacial phenomena currently the prime focus of his work is investigating issues of diffusion growth and stress in silicon anode particles of lithiumion batteries this is the topic on which he is going to deliver his talk he did integrated btech and mtech through the dual degree programme at the mechanical engineering department of iit kharagpur with specialization in mechanical systems design subsequently he did his phd from iit kharagpur itself he did two postdocs first at the mathematical institute at the university of oxford and then at the school of mathematics university of birmingham thereafter he had a brief stint as a dst inspire faculty at iisc finally he joined iit kharagpur as a faculty in the mechanical engineering department in over the years he has taught courses on st year mechanics fluid mechanics mechanics of solids applied elasticity and advanced mechanics of solids everyone is welcome to attend the talk with best regards sabyasachi chatterjee assistant professor applied mechanics iit delhi office room b block iv

Subject: canceled mathematics colloquium on july thursday at am in room no academic complex west b
Body: dear all the talk has been canceled due to unforeseen circumstances with regards mathematics department colloquium team original message subject tomorrow at am mathematics colloquium on july thursday at am in room no academic complex west b date from biplab basak to allgroup seminar a gentle reminder original message subject mathematics colloquium on july thursday at am in room no academic complex west b date from biplab basak to allgroup seminar dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department colloquium by prof ashish k srivastava saint louis university usa on july thursday the details are given below title leavitt path algebras at the crossroads of algebra analysis and noncommutative geometry date july thursday at am venue room no academic complex west b speaker prof ashish k srivastava abstract leavitt path algebras are certain quotients of path algebras where the relations are inspired from cuntzkrieger relations for graph calgebras leavitt path algebras have deep connections with symbolic dynamics and they capture the homological properties of both path algebras and their koszul dual and hence they form an important class of noncommutative algebras we give a construction for graded automorphisms of leavitt path algebras and as an application we study zhang twist of leavitt path algebras and describe new classes of irreducible representations of leavitt path algebras all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team

Subject: me guest talk by mr apurva anand university of maryland on machine learning assisted aerodynamic inverse design and optimization of rotor blades challanges and future scope
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the me guest talk by mr apurva anand from the university of maryland as per the schedule below date wednesday th july time pm venue me seminar room ii title machine learning assisted aerodynamic inverse design and optimization of rotor blades challenges and future scope abstract rotor blade optimization presents a multifaceted challenge as traditional design methodologies rely on computationally exhaustive highfidelity computational fluid dynamics cfd conversely lowfidelity techniques such as potential flow based codes are inaccurate especially in the regions of flow separation my research proposes leveraging artificial neural networks anns to predict the performance polar of a given airfoil geometry and to facilitate the inverse design of airfoil a modified form of anns known as tandem neural networks tnns is implemented the airfoil inverse design is a multipoint optimization problem at multiple angles of attack and therefore the tnns are trained on the vectors of performance polar instead of individual angles of attack the requirement of large number of high fidelity data is a major challenge for training surrogate models and therefore a novel multifidelity architecture is developed to use both low and high fidelity data without compromising the accuracy of the model the inverse designed airfoil is then for rotor blade optimization bio apurva anand is a phd candidate at university of maryland college park hes working at alfred gessow rotorcraft center in aerospace engineering department he completed his ms in aerospace engineering from indian institute of science and worked at airbus as a flight physics engineer his current research focuses on development of surrogate models for design and optimization of rotor blades his areas of interest are machine learning design optimization aerodynamics and numerical simulations all interested are welcome to join the talk thank you dr abhishek das and dr rajan prasad department of mechanical engineering iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: applied mechanics invited talk by prof jeevanjyoti chakraborty iit kharagpur
Body: dear all we will have an online seminar by prof jeevanjyoti chakraborty associate professor department of mechanical engineering iit kharagpur details of the seminar are as follows title diffusion growth and mechanics in batteries date and time th july pm link abstract lithiumion batteries have come to be used as the preferred power source for many electronic devices their applications have also been scaled up to electric vehicles as well as grid storage however for the scaling up to be truly commercially viable the natural limitations of charge capacity in the traditionally used materials need to be overcome this necessitates the exploration of newer materials silicon has emerged as a promising candidate as such a new material on the anode side now silicon expands by more than in volume when it is fully charged by lithium this gigantic growth of silicon throws up a number of challenges in its immediate adoption as a anode material these challenges can be answered by properly understanding the solid mechanical issues associated with its growth in this talk i will first present a general framework based on finite deformation theory incorporating diffusion growth and mechanics i will then discuss a few studies that apply this framework to various solid mechanical issues fundamentally induced by the diffusioninduced stresses within the anode particles in particular i will discuss possibilities of buckling and other general forms of instability surface stresses which become increasingly important at the nanometric length scales of the particles and also mechanical degradations associated with something referred to as the solid electrolyte interphase that are formed on such particles about the speaker dr jeevanjyoti chakraborty is an associate professor in the mechanical engineering department of iit kharagpur he has worked on the mathematical modelling of various situations involving fluid mechanics and solid mechanics coupled occasionally with bits of electrochemistry earlier he has worked on modelling fluid flow through deformable confinements exploring various interfacial phenomena currently the prime focus of his work is investigating issues of diffusion growth and stress in silicon anode particles of lithiumion batteries this is the topic on which he is going to deliver his talk he did integrated btech and mtech through the dual degree programme at the mechanical engineering department of iit kharagpur with specialization in mechanical systems design subsequently he did his phd from iit kharagpur itself he did two postdocs first at the mathematical institute at the university of oxford and then at the school of mathematics university of birmingham thereafter he had a brief stint as a dst inspire faculty at iisc finally he joined iit kharagpur as a faculty in the mechanical engineering department in over the years he has taught courses on st year mechanics fluid mechanics mechanics of solids applied elasticity and advanced mechanics of solids everyone is welcome to attend the talk with best regards sabyasachi chatterjee assistant professor applied mechanics iit delhi office room b block iv

Subject: talk titiled copulsing fda radar by dr vijay kumar mishra from army research lab usa
Body: talk is on tuesday july hi talk has been rescheduled on july th at pm at the same venue title copulsing fda radar date and time monday july th at pm venue care committee room room blockiii speaker dr vijay kumar mishra arl usa thanks and regards monika original message subject talk titiled copulsing fda radar by dr vijay kumar mishra from army research lab usa date from monika aggarwal to dear all i would like to invite you to an exciting talk on copulsing fda radar date and time monday july th at pm venue care committee room room blockiii speaker dr vijay kumar mishra arl usa abstract target localization based on frequency diverse array fda radar has lately garnered significant research interest a linear frequency offset fo across fda antennas yields a rangeangle dependent beampattern that allows for joint estimation of range and directionofarrival doa prior works on fda largely focus on the onedimensional linear array to estimate only azimuth angle and range while ignoring the elevation and doppler velocity however in many applications the latter two parameters are also essential for target localization further there is also an interest in radar systems that employ fewer measurements in temporal doppler or spatial signal domains in this context this chapter provides an overview of fda in coarray domain to address the aforementioned multiple challenges in particular we focus on copulsing fda radar that employs coprime lshaped fda wherein coprime fos are applied across the elements of lshaped coprime array and each element transmits at a nonuniform coprime pulse repetition interval this copulsing fda yields significantly large degreesoffreedom dofs for target localization in the rangeazimuthelevationdoppler domain while also reducing the timeontarget and transmit spectral usage next we examine cluttersuppression for an airborne copulsing fda radar using novel spacetimeadaptive processing stap techniques namely costap finally we extend the copulsing concept to continuouswave radar with a hardware demonstration for automotive radar applications online link thanks and regards monika

Subject: re talk titiled copulsing fda radar by dr vijay kumar mishra from army research lab usa
Body: hi talk has been rescheduled on july th at pm at the same venue title copulsing fda radar date and time monday july th at pm venue care committee room room blockiii speaker dr vijay kumar mishra arl usa thanks and regards monika original message subject talk titiled copulsing fda radar by dr vijay kumar mishra from army research lab usa date from monika aggarwal to dear all i would like to invite you to an exciting talk on copulsing fda radar date and time monday july th at pm venue care committee room room blockiii speaker dr vijay kumar mishra arl usa abstract target localization based on frequency diverse array fda radar has lately garnered significant research interest a linear frequency offset fo across fda antennas yields a rangeangle dependent beampattern that allows for joint estimation of range and directionofarrival doa prior works on fda largely focus on the onedimensional linear array to estimate only azimuth angle and range while ignoring the elevation and doppler velocity however in many applications the latter two parameters are also essential for target localization further there is also an interest in radar systems that employ fewer measurements in temporal doppler or spatial signal domains in this context this chapter provides an overview of fda in coarray domain to address the aforementioned multiple challenges in particular we focus on copulsing fda radar that employs coprime lshaped fda wherein coprime fos are applied across the elements of lshaped coprime array and each element transmits at a nonuniform coprime pulse repetition interval this copulsing fda yields significantly large degreesoffreedom dofs for target localization in the rangeazimuthelevationdoppler domain while also reducing the timeontarget and transmit spectral usage next we examine cluttersuppression for an airborne copulsing fda radar using novel spacetimeadaptive processing stap techniques namely costap finally we extend the copulsing concept to continuouswave radar with a hardware demonstration for automotive radar applications online link thanks and regards monika

Subject: mathematics colloquium on july thursday at am in room no academic complex west b
Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department colloquium by prof ashish k srivastava saint louis university usa on july thursday the details are given below title leavitt path algebras at the crossroads of algebra analysis and noncommutative geometry date july thursday at am venue room no academic complex west b speaker prof ashish k srivastava abstract leavitt path algebras are certain quotients of path algebras where the relations are inspired from cuntzkrieger relations for graph calgebras leavitt path algebras have deep connections with symbolic dynamics and they capture the homological properties of both path algebras and their koszul dual and hence they form an important class of noncommutative algebras we give a construction for graded automorphisms of leavitt path algebras and as an application we study zhang twist of leavitt path algebras and describe new classes of irreducible representations of leavitt path algebras all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team

Subject: re invited talk by prof ravi prakash carleton university on noninvasive sensory platforms for health and environmental applications
Body: gentle reminder for the talk today at pm on dhiman mallick wrote dear all prof ravi prakash from carleton university canada will give an invited talk on th june monday at the department of electrical engineering the details are as follows date and time th june monday pm onwards venue ee committee room block ii title noninvasive sensory platforms using nonconventional materials and flexible substrates for health and environmental applications abstract organic biosensors rely on polymerbased semiconductors dielectrics and conductive materials often in conjunction with some inorganic materials such as metal nanoparticles metal oxides etc to create tunable device behavior for target applications such devices offer many benefits for implementation as sensory platform including solution processability costeffectiveness ease of manufacturing and superior compatibility to functional nanomaterials and biomolecules these benefits have led to intense research in suitable materials device geometries and detectiontransduction methods in sensory platform for chemical biological and environmental applications in my talk i will share some of our recent research highlights on implementing organic materials based noninvasive biosensor technologies for detection of metabolites and proteomic biomarkers target applications include monitoring body homeostasis and identifying early signs of pathogenesis for certain diseases including parkinsons disease and alzheimers disease more specifically the talk will cover electrolyte gated fet egfet platforms and carbon nanoparticles based otfts and eis devices amongst the sensors discussed we will take a closer look at integrating functional nanomaterials within device framework to achieve the desired sensory response various device design and modeling strategies will be briefly discussed biography dr ravi prakash is an associate professor in the department of electronics engineering with crossappointment in the systems and computer engineering department at carleton university he received his bachelors degree in mechanical and biomedical engineering from indian institute of technology madras india and his msc and phd in electrical and computer engineering from university of calgary canada prior to joining carleton in he was an assistant professor in the electrical and computer engineering department at queens university at carleton dr prakash oversees the interdisciplinary organic sensor and devices laboratory osdl where his team develops novel chemical and biological sensors pointofcare diagnostic platforms direct printed flexible and hybrid flexible electronics for wearables and sensors for environmental monitoring applications his research contributions have led to over peerreviewed publications including journal publications conference publications book chapters and patents dr prakash is a senior member of the institute of electrical and electronics engineers ieee and he is affiliated with several ieee technical societies including the ieee engineering in medicine and biology society embs and the ieee sensors council he is a licensed professional engineer in the province of ontario you are invited to attend the talk best regards dhiman dr dhiman mallick associate professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india tel o m email web interdisciplinary microsystems lab iml links

Subject: phd viva announcement nivedita shrivastava
Body: time and venue of the phd viva nd july pm sitgnd flr seminar room name of the student nivedita shrivastava eez title design of secure architectures for neural networks abstract neural network models are highvalue intellectual property—trained over large datasets with significant computational resources any compromise can lead to ip theft privacy violations and commercial losses this thesis proposes a comprehensive design for building a secure and highperformance computing platform for neural networks addressing key challenges from encryption to sidechannel resilience securing neural processing units npus requires enforcing key security properties such as confidentiality integrity authentication freshness and resistance to sidechannel attacks to preserve model confidentiality encryption of weights and biases is essential however performing encryption in shared components such as the cpu in a systemonchip soc can expose the system to cache sidechannel attacks csca particularly when widely trusted encryption routines like aes are implemented in software in our first contribution we review csca countermeasures and show that addressbased defenses while obfuscatory can still be broken in nologlogn time to make such attacks more practical we propose a theoretical classification framework along with a twophase attack strategy that reduces the required attempts to just underscoring the urgency for a fast hardwarebased secure encryption engine consequently we designed a lightweight highthroughput encryption engine that employs ephemeral keys and fewer rounds yet achieves aesequivalent security with up to x lower latency next we turn to the systemlevel vulnerabilities in npus particularly their reliance on offchip dram and system buses which remain unencrypted and vulnerable to tampering replay coldboot and bus snooping attacks we analyze and model memory access behavior across popular neural network dataflows and develop lightweight hardware that enables integrity and freshness verification at the layer level—achieving a speedup we also address memory and timingbased sidechannel attacks we categorize existing defenses and show their limitations through practical attacks to counter them we propose a novel compression and binningbased obfuscation technique which applies multiplicative noise to model parameters this expands the attack search space to over this work presents a unified design framework for secure npus—spanning encryption memory protection and sidechannel protection — all without sacrificing performance making it both practical and resilient against evolving attack vectors smruti ranjan sarangi hitech robotics and autonomous systems chair professor computer science and engineering iit delhi joint appt with electrical engineering iit delhi hauz khas new delhi ph website

Subject: scst student scholarships revision of pocket allowance and annual family income limit
Body: dear all many congratulations for the increase in the pocket allowance and income limit for the free messing facility this is an outcome of the collective effort we all have made together for those who are not familiar with the issue here is a brief outline the initiative for caste equity ice and the scst cell were receiving many queries regarding the scholarship and support for scst students at the institute most queries came from firstyear students enrolled in various programs at the institute therefore it was decided to organize a meeting for btech mtechmsc and phd students belonging to the scst category on wednesday september at pm in lh many students raised concerns regarding the eligibility exact provisions and procedure for availing the free mess facility scst students whose parental income falls below rs lakh used to receive free messing along with a monthly pocket allowance of rs however the amount and the income limit were set up in and were not revised as per the inflation prof pravin ingole chairperson scst cell and i met with the director and dean academics and raised the issue of inequity in the scholarship provisions for scst students we presented a report to the director and dean academic and requested an increase in the income limit and pocket allowance along with exemption from hostel seat rent and other support to address the financial distress of scst students from the past several months prof pravin and i have been following up on our requests and have had a couple of meetings with the director and dean academic regarding this finally the request received approval from the director and the bog last month and the notification came yesterday the income limit for the free mess is now lakhs which is at par with the ews income criteria the pocket allowance amount has been increased from rs to rs per month while this is a significant development that will ease the burden on scst students there is a need to continuously work on the concerns that still remain unresolved the director has confirmed to prof pravin and me that scst students will also receive hostel seat rent exemption in addition we are also working on instituting a merit scholarship for scst women students to the tune of rs per year we are also working on setting up a financial distress fund to help scst students navigate financial distress moving forward the ice and scst cell will work with the academic section to create a webpage about available scholarships and support for scst students on the instituteacademic section website we will ensure that this webpage also lists available scholarships for scst students from the central and state governments and has a scholarship calendar informing students of the deadlines for various scholarships please note that we will have an allscst students meeting next month to clarify the steps to avail the free messing facility and discuss the updates on other scholarshiprelated provisions last but not least i would like to mention the contribution of the student volunteers and pors working with ice in securing the increase in the pocket allowance and income limit i also wanted to make an appeal please come forward to work with ice it is only with the collective efforts of students like you that we will be able to deal with many challenges and achieve excellence ice pors are selected from the volunteers who have contributed to the work of ice here is the link to volunteer for ice best yashpal yashpal jogdand associate professor of psychology advisor initiative for caste equity ice office of diversity and inclusion indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india phone begin forwarded message from jr cdn subject Subject: inae delhi chapter and applied mechanics department seminar by professor dr arun r srinivasa on friday th june from am to pm ist in a hybrid mode at iit delhi
Body: dear madamsir delhi chapter of indian national academy of engineering inae and applied mechanics department at indian institute of technology iit delhi are jointly organizing a seminar event in a hybrid mode details of which are given below seminar titled breaking up is hard to do simulating fracture of quasibrittle materials viscoelastic solids and delamination of composites using grafea a novel graphbased nonlocal mechanics approach abstract we demonstrate a new graphbased finite element analysis grafea method to study damage and fracture in materials the central idea behind this approach is to leverage classical fea to study fracture by enhancing it with a nonlocal edgebased damage and fracture criterion we utilize the tools of discrete differential geometry and treat the mesh of a traditional fea as a cell complex then it becomes possible to treat fracture propagation on the dual cell complex as disconnection of edges of the original mesh this allows us to piggyback on already developed and tested fea for structural response with a nonlocal criterion for the breakage of the edges of the mesh we apply this method to a the fracture propagation in a quasibrittle material and b the dynamic fracture or tearing depending upon strain rate of a nonlinear viscoelastic solid such as an adhesive under conditions of different strain rates and c delamination in composite structures the code is implemented as an extension of commercial software abaqus to demonstrate that it is possible to use this as an add on to conventional fea we also show that by judiciously combining the facture response with beam and plate theories we can achieve remarkable improvement in computational speed minutes on a laptop compared to hours or days using abaqus d on a supercomputer biography of the speaker dr srinivasa is currently associate dean for student success at the college of engineering at texas am university tamu in the usa and holds the jn reddy chair in applied mechanics at the department of mechanical engineering at tamu he is dedicated to the undergraduate teaching mission of the department and college and has served as the associate department head for the department of mechanical engineering his research interests are in the simulation and optimization of fracture fatigue and materials processing impact and dynamics of continua nonlocal and cosserat theories biomechanics and the foundations of continuum thermodynamics he has authored and coauthored over journal publications in peerreviewed journals and has coauthored three books apart from several articles on engineering education his educational interests include the incorporation of technology into education in a way that is inclusive and accessible to students from different backgrounds and the development of quantitative design and decisionmaking activities as the foundation of engineering education he was copi and director for the nsf red revolutionizing engineering departments grant for the department of mechanical engineering to create a community of practice focused on continuous innovation in teaching he was awarded the ralph coates roe award from the american society of engineering education for his contributions to research and teaching in mechanical engineering the university professorship for undergraduate teaching excellence upute award the ben sparks medal from the american society of mechanical engineers asme for his contributions in fostering new innovative applications and approaches to the teaching of mechanical engineering the worcester reed warner medal by the american society of mechanical engineers for seminal contribution to the permanent literature of engineering and the archie higdon distinguished educator award by the american society of engineering education for his work in mechanics education at the university level he has won the association of former students distinguished achievement award for teaching both at the college level and the university level the bp award for teaching excellence at tamu the halliburon professorship for scholarly excellence and contributions to engineering the outstanding graduate teaching award the william keeler faculty fellowship as well as the benjamin dasher best engineering education paper award from the frontiers in engineering conference most recently he was awarded the asme best teacher award by the asme student chapter of tamu date and time friday th june from am to pm indian standard time ist venue for inperson attendees committee room blockiv applied mechanics department indian institute of technology iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india the microsoft ms teams meeting link for attending the seminar is for more details url is given below all interested are requested to attend the seminar and inform others who might also be interested thank you with best regards vasant matsagar honorary secretary inae delhi chapter

Subject: summer safety precautions
Body: dear all all residents students and employees are advised to be cautious while using electrical appliances during the ongoing summer spell as they are a major cause of fire incidents in laboratories offices ups rooms cold room of hostels etc use fans and air conditioners acs optimally — only as per requirement always monitor electrical appliances while they are in use and switch them off when not in use ups units should be switched off when not in use to avoid unnecessary electrical load and risk it is advised to installed proper rating ac as per area to maintain right temperature during peak summer in ups room having more than batteries and for rest of the season use exhaust system faulty sockets plugs and wires must be replaced immediately and should not be used until fixed never leave electrical appliances ‘on’ while leaving the room or premises for longer duration all heads of departments hods are advised to install an additional ac in critical labs and server rooms to allow alternate operation for uninterrupted cooling ensure to display mobile numbers visibly on doors of officer incharge and lab technicianoffice superintendent for swift communication in case of any emergency recently it has found that mcbs is not tripping in case of fire therefore the institute engineer is requested to ensure all electrical fittings are intact and auto cutoff system is working properly and it should be periodically examined ac service mechanics should be closely monitored to ensure that there are no loose wires and avoid to wrap outdoorindoor electrical leads with ac water outlet pipe avoid any joints in wiring of electrical appliances to prevent short circuits or overheating fire officials should be directed to verify that all fire safety arrangements are checked and functional all are requested to ensure clearance of exit arrangement in case of emergency and no hurdle should be in front or near exit gate best regards drmkjain safety officer

Subject: advisory on air conditioning units operation in the institute
Body: dear all in light of the prevailing summer and monsoon seasons guidelines were issued on may for compliance regarding the use of air conditioners in all laboratories and offices meanwhile there were some instances of “electronic card pcb failure” and fire incidents in some labs and offices in every case it was noticed that users set the temperature of acs at °c setting the desired room temperature at °c signals the master controller of the ac unit to run at full load all the time as °c is hard to reach under present weather conditions which is the major reason for breakdowns of inverter acs and fire hazards it is once again requested to comply with the following guidelines for general safety and optimum functioning of the concerned ac units for comfort cooling the temperature of the ac should not be set below °c unless required split or windowtype acs should not be kept running at a stretch for more than hours in case of prolonged low to no cooling abnormal noise and heating the machine should be switched off immediately and reported to the maintenance unit for checking the maintenance and upkeep of acs that have been procured and installed by an individual useracademic unit which are without approval from the ac committee shall be their responsibility the infra unit is not responsible for the proper functioning of these machines due to abnormally high ambient temperature intermittent resting of the ac units is necessary users are requested to use the ac judicially and keep it switched off when the laboffice is not occupied if required users may reach out to the ac maintenance unit for installation of timers to managecontrol usage as well your cooperation is solicited in reducing the wastage of energy and ensuring a safe working environment ac committee of iit delhi with warm regards er ashok kumar institute engineer indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi—

Subject: talk by prof dinshaw s balsara
Body: dear all the seminar will take place tomorrow th of june at pm the venue for the talk is room no the department of mathematics in the academic complex west the title and the abstract are appended below dear all prof dinshaw s balsara notredame usa is visiting the mathematics department he will give a talk with the following details title general purpose alternative finite difference weno afdweno for conservative systems and systems with nonconservative products and mimetic constraints time friday th june pm to pm venue dept of mathematics academic complex west abstract in their landmark sequence of papers shu and osher the authors presented two highly efficient finite difference weno schemes the latter finite difference weno scheme shu and osher has become wildly successful and garnered thousands of citations we call that the fdweno scheme however in shu and osher they also presented an alternative finite difference weno afdweno scheme which was slower to catch on we explain why that scheme was slower to catch on it is because all ingredients that are needed to make a production code out of afdweno were not available at that time besides the scheme was not easy to understand at the time of its initial presentation we demystify the afdweno algorithm in this talk in this talk we explain why the afdweno scheme nevertheless had several significant advantages if it could be developed into an automated algorithm for production codes this talk is devoted to developing afdweno into a simple algorithm that is easily explained to others and also easily implemented in production codes to reach that goal we had to make several algorithmic innovations which we explain here the original fdweno schemes were also only viable for conservation laws but the field has moved on and it is very normal for scientists and engineers to discover hyperbolic pde systems that have nonconservative products often with stiff source terms to accommodate such pde systems we present the first of its kind afdweno scheme that can retain strict conservation when the pde is conservative and yet accommodate nonconservative products due to their efficiency there is also an interest in developing afdweno schemes that have mimetic constraints like divergencefree mhd and rmhd the methods also have to be physical constraint preserving and pcp versions of divpreserving afdweno schemes will also be presented this vastly expands the class of pdes that can be treated with afdweno schemes several examples are demonstrated in this talk parts on youtube warm regards harish kumar department of mathematics iit delhi india

Subject: talk by prof dinshaw s balsara
Body: dear all the talk has been postponed due to some unforeseen circumstances we will announce the new timing next week warm regards harish kumar department of mathematics iit delhi india on jun at pm harish kumar wrote dear all prof dinshaw s balsara notredame usa is visiting the mathematics department he will give a talk with the following details title general purpose alternative finite difference weno afdweno for conservative systems and systems with nonconservative products and mimetic constraints time friday th june pm to pm venue dept of mathematics academic complex west abstract in their landmark sequence of papers shu and osher the authors presented two highly efficient finite difference weno schemes the latter finite difference weno scheme shu and osher has become wildly successful and garnered thousands of citations we call that the fdweno scheme however in shu and osher they also presented an alternative finite difference weno afdweno scheme which was slower to catch on we explain why that scheme was slower to catch on it is because all ingredients that are needed to make a production code out of afdweno were not available at that time besides the scheme was not easy to understand at the time of its initial presentation we demystify the afdweno algorithm in this talk in this talk we explain why the afdweno scheme nevertheless had several significant advantages if it could be developed into an automated algorithm for production codes this talk is devoted to developing afdweno into a simple algorithm that is easily explained to others and also easily implemented in production codes to reach that goal we had to make several algorithmic innovations which we explain here the original fdweno schemes were also only viable for conservation laws but the field has moved on and it is very normal for scientists and engineers to discover hyperbolic pde systems that have nonconservative products often with stiff source terms to accommodate such pde systems we present the first of its kind afdweno scheme that can retain strict conservation when the pde is conservative and yet accommodate nonconservative products due to their efficiency there is also an interest in developing afdweno schemes that have mimetic constraints like divergencefree mhd and rmhd the methods also have to be physical constraint preserving and pcp versions of divpreserving afdweno schemes will also be presented this vastly expands the class of pdes that can be treated with afdweno schemes several examples are demonstrated in this talk parts on youtube warm regards harish kumar department of mathematics iit delhi india

Subject: short course by prof dietmar oelz school of mathematics physics university of queensland aus
Body: dear all online link to join the course is as follows original message subject short course by prof dietmar oelz school of mathematics physics university of queensland aus date from mani mehra to dear all you are cordially invited to attend the short course on partial differential equation pde models in mathematical biology by prof dietmar oelz school of mathematics physics university of queensland brisbane aus under uq professor mobility program iit delhi and uqiitd research academy as per the below schedule title partial differential equation pde models in mathematical biology lecture thursday th june am pm lecture friday th june am pm lecture monday th june am pm lecture tuesday th june am pm venue academic complex west wing a room no speaker prof dietmar oelz the course will focus on mathematical models of biological phenomena from diverse areas unlike many phenomena in the physical sciences to which mathematics has been widely and successfully applied for a very long time biological phenomena tend to be characterized by a high degree of variability and complexity the challenge in modelling them typically lies in identifying a small enough set of variables or aspects for the mathematics to be tractable without failing completely to capture the essence of what is happening unlike in many mathematics courses where much time is spent on finding solutions to welldefined mathematical problems in this course a significant amount of time will be spent on the art of constructing models of biological systems and also on the interpretation of solutions of these new sorts of models while this will inevitably involve learning some specific biology the ability to turn complicated biological phenomena into tractable mathematical models is widely applicable also beyond biology more specific details are as follows basics of the diffusion equation which in the context of mathematical biology can be regarded as the fundamental model for random motion and building block of many pde models in biology fisherkpp equation as a model for tissue invasion through tumour cells and habitat invasion travellingwave analysis in d the chemotaxis equation for cell migration in development and immune response and the patlakkellersegel model for aggregation eg of dictyostelium discoideum including critical mass for blowup of solutions in d pattern formation the classical turing model for biological pattern formation such as the stripes of zebras and tigers and recent mechanochemical model for pattern formation in embryos of the fresh water animal hydra stability analysis of constant stead states another class of pde models i could touch upon are structured differentialintegral models eg for the dynamics of infectious diseases and the size distribution of bacteria yet i have the feeling that in might be better to use the remaining time for handson exercises simulating some of those equations through simple finite difference schemes all are welcome to attend the talk ps thanks to department of mathematics and uqiitd research academy for partial financial support thanks mani mani mehra fnasc professor department of mathematics indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi phone o office b b webpage

understand at the time of its initial presentation we demystify the afdweno algorithm in this talk in this talk we explain why the afdweno scheme nevertheless had several significant advantages if it could be developed into an automated algorithm for production codes this talk is devoted to developing afdweno into a simple algorithm that is easily explained to others and also easily implemented in production codes to reach that goal we had to make several algorithmic innovations which we explain here the original fdweno schemes were also only viable for conservation laws but the field has moved on and it is very normal for scientists and engineers to discover hyperbolic pde systems that have nonconservative products often with stiff source terms to accommodate such pde systems we present the first of its kind afdweno scheme that can retain strict conservation when the pde is conservative and yet accommodate nonconservative products due to their efficiency there is also an interest in developing afdweno schemes that have mimetic constraints like divergencefree mhd and rmhd the methods also have to be physical constraint preserving and pcp versions of divpreserving afdweno schemes will also be presented this vastly expands the class of pdes that can be treated with afdweno schemes several examples are demonstrated in this talk parts on youtube warm regards harish kumar department of mathematics iit delhi india

Subject: short course by prof dietmar oelz school of mathematics physics university of queensland aus
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the short course on partial differential equation pde models in mathematical biology by prof dietmar oelz school of mathematics physics university of queensland brisbane aus under uq professor mobility program iit delhi and uqiitd research academy as per the below schedule title partial differential equation pde models in mathematical biology lecture thursday th june am pm lecture friday th june am pm lecture monday th june am pm lecture tuesday th june am pm venue academic complex west wing a room no speaker prof dietmar oelz the course will focus on mathematical models of biological phenomena from diverse areas unlike many phenomena in the physical sciences to which mathematics has been widely and successfully applied for a very long time biological phenomena tend to be characterized by a high degree of variability and complexity the challenge in modelling them typically lies in identifying a small enough set of variables or aspects for the mathematics to be tractable without failing completely to capture the essence of what is happening unlike in many mathematics courses where much time is spent on finding solutions to welldefined mathematical problems in this course a significant amount of time will be spent on the art of constructing models of biological systems and also on the interpretation of solutions of these new sorts of models while this will inevitably involve learning some specific biology the ability to turn complicated biological phenomena into tractable mathematical models is widely applicable also beyond biology more specific details are as follows basics of the diffusion equation which in the context of mathematical biology can be regarded as the fundamental model for random motion and building block of many pde models in biology fisherkpp equation as a model for tissue invasion through tumour cells and habitat invasion travellingwave analysis in d the chemotaxis equation for cell migration in development and immune response and the patlakkellersegel model for aggregation eg of dictyostelium discoideum including critical mass for blowup of solutions in d pattern formation the classical turing model for biological pattern formation such as the stripes of zebras and tigers and recent mechanochemical model for pattern formation in embryos of the fresh water animal hydra stability analysis of constant stead states another class of pde models i could touch upon are structured differentialintegral models eg for the dynamics of infectious diseases and the size distribution of bacteria yet i have the feeling that in might be better to use the remaining time for handson exercises simulating some of those equations through simple finite difference schemes all are welcome to attend the talk ps thanks to department of mathematics and uqiitd research academy for partial financial support thanks mani mani mehra fnasc professor department of mathematics indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi phone o office b b webpage

Body: dear students are you ready to make an impact we invite you to join the schneider go green competition this global challenge is supported by schneider electric’s youth education entrepreneurship Subject: applied mechanics invited talk by prof sayan gupta iit madras
Body: venue applied mechanics committee room iv time may pm title energy harvesting to computing the dynamics of networked coupled systems abstract networks of coupled dynamical systems provide powerful frameworks for modelling complex phenomena—from energy harvesting to social dynamics this talk introduces the key features of such models and the challenges subsequently the talk discusses how inspired by the brains natural rhythms a novel approach is developed for storing and retrieving memories using networks of chaotic oscillators that qualitatively mimics neuronal dynamics unlike traditional computing where data storage and retrieval is based on binary vectors with indexed addresses the proposed model encodes data as phase synchronized states and their retrieval much like the brain is based on content similarity the chaos improves memory capacity and robustness and offer insights into how brains possibly handle cognitive tasks this study offers opportunities for developing more adaptive efficient and brain inspired computing systems with potential applications to neuromorphic computing speaker bio sayan gupta is a professor and the head of the department of applied mechanics biomedical engg iit madras his group the uncertainty lab focusses on problems involving nonlinear dynamics stochastic mechanics and networked dynamical systems in a variety of engineering applications he also leads the interdisciplinary center on complex systems dynamics iit madras and is the coordinator of the interdisciplinary dual degree program with the same name all are welcome to attend the talk with best regards sabyasachi chatterjee assistant professor applied mechanics iit delhi office room b block iv

Subject: me guest talk by dr mandeep saini university of twente on multiphase flow dynamics
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the me guest talk by dr mandeep saini university of twente as per the below schedule date tuesday rd june time pm venue me seminar room ii title multiphase flow dynamics abstract multiphase systems are prevalent in both natural environments and industrial applications to effectively understand and control these systems detailed investigations using numerical analytical and experimental approaches are required in this talk he will present his research on two distinct multiphase flow phenomena cavitation and inkjet printing the study of cavitation demonstratesthrough a combination of experiments simulations and theoretical analysisthat the collapse of a spherical cap shaped bubble attached to a wall can generate a jet directed away from the wall this jet formation is linked to a singularity predicted by potential flow theory for the inkjet printing case two specific problems will be addressed a the numerical modeling of surface tension effects focusing on marangoni flows commonly observed in evaporating droplets and b the influence of polymer additives on jet formation and breakup as the ink is ejected from the nozzle bio mandeep is a postdoctoral researcher in the physics of fluids group at the university of twente working under the supervision of detlef lohse his research lies broadly in the area of numerical multiphase flows currently he is focussing on challenges in inkjet printing in collaboration with canon production printing he earned his phd at sorbonne university conducting research on cavitation at the institut jean le rond dalembert prior to his doctoral studies he completed a masters in mechanical engineering at iit guwahati and a bachelors degree at nit hamirpur in india outside of academia he enjoys playing badminton and road cycling all interested are welcome to join the talk thank you dr abhishek das and dr pratik das department of mechanical engineering iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: reminder mathematics colloquium on may tuesday at pm in room no academic complex west b
Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department colloquium by prof pradip kumar shiv nadar university delhi ncr on may tuesday the details are given below title minimal surfaces in complex hyperbolic space with complete ends and parabolic higgs bundles date may tuesday at pm venue room no academic complex west b speaker prof pradip kumar abstract in this talk we will see the detailed correspondence between two geometric structures on a punctured riemann surface sigma of negative euler characteristic on one side we have minimal immersions into the complex hyperbolic space mathbbch with unipotent monodromy at the punctures and other side stable parabolic mathrmpu higgs bundles given a representation rho pi sigma to mathrmpu with parabolic monodromy we explicitly construct the associated parabolic higgs bundle e v oplus l phi arising from a rhoequivariant minimal immersion conversely starting from a stable parabolic higgs bundle with prescribed nilpotent residues we recover the corresponding equivariant minimal surface this is an ongoing work with indranil biswas and john loftin all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team

Subject: prof aarat kalra is looking for students interested in working on quantum biophysics for thesis projects
Body: dear students i am aarat kalra a relatively new faculty member at the centre for biomedical engineering at iit delhi previously i worked on the electronic properties of protein polymers called microtubules i am looking for student researchers who might be interested in working on a computational and multidisciiplinary project in my lab on the broad area of quantum biology the abstract of the project is shown below spinorbit coupling has been wellharnessed to tailor the distribution of electron spin states in inorganic materials for next generation computing and to fabricate semiconductors however could spinorbit coupling also play useful roles in biology could this quantum mechanical phenomenon help us design a magnetic fieldbased therapeutic modality in our group we are interested in setting up a computational protocol to quantify spinorbit coupling in biomolecules such as vitamin b and tannic acid and then investigate how magnetic fields of different intensities may influence the distribution of electrons present in the singlet or the triplet state which may further influence their reactivity keywords quantum biology magnetobiology spin orbit coupling magnetoreception ​ prerequisites project is computational number of publications expected should you be interested in working with me please email me with your cv and give information on your research interests feel free to circulate this message among other students and in other forums i look forward to hearing back best regards aarat p kalra assistant professor centre for biomedical engineering indian institute of technology delhi links

Subject: re seminar by prof dragan maksimovic on th may pm at iia
Body: a gentle reminder for today’s talk by prof maksimovic from pm at iia bharti school regards sreyam sreyam sinha phd assistant professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india original message subject seminar by prof dragan maksimovic on th may pm at iia date from sreyam sinha to dear all i am glad to invite you to a seminar by prof dragan maksimovic from university of colorado boulder on th may monday from pm at iia bharti school prof maksimovic is a distinguished professor a fellow of ieee and the director of the colorado power electronics center he has coauthored more than publications and the widely adopted textbook fundamentals of power electronics title of the talk highefficiency highdensity composite dcdc converter architectures time th may monday pm venue iia bharti school abstract in electric drivetrain architectures including xev and electrified aircraft applications a boost dcdc converter is often utilized to interface a battery system to variablespeed ac drives thus enabling the system operation at increased dc bus voltages wide bandgap sic devices lead to improvements in efficiency and reductions in the size of magnetic components in standard boost converter realizations we then show how further improvements can be achieved using composite architectures where stresses and losses on sic devices and passive components are substantially reduced optimization of composite converters involves complex design tradeoffs in terms of losses size and reliability to address these challenges a systematic design methodology is presented which involves selection of the converter architecture planar magnetics design control techniques and electrothermal codesign the approach is illustrated by modeling simulations and experimental results on a kw sic composite dcdc converter prototype featuring kwl power density and drivecycle weighted efficiency biography dragan maksimović received the bs and ms degrees in electrical engineering from the university of belgrade serbia in and respectively and the phd degree in electrical engineering from the california institute of technology pasadena ca usa in from to he was with the university of belgrade since he has been with the department of electrical computer and energy engineering university of colorado boulder co usa where he is currently a distinguished professor and director of the colorado power electronics center he has coauthored more than publications and the textbooks fundamentals of power electronics and digital control of highfrequency switchedmode power converters prof maksimovic received the ieee pels r david middlebrook achievement award and the ieee william e newell power electronics award his research interests include power electronics for renewable energy sources and energy efficiency highfrequency power conversion using wideband gap semiconductors and digital control of switchedmode power converters you can also find the details in the attached flyer regards sreyam sreyam sinha phd assistant professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi सहअध्यक्ष नेत्र रोग विभाग सर गंगा राम अस्पताल नई दिल्ली विषय मोतियाबिंद कारण लक्षण और आधुनिक उपचार विकल्प चर्चा के मुख्य बिंदु हैं मोतियाबिंद क्या है – यह कैसे विकसित होता है और दृष्टि को कैसे प्रभावित करता है। संकेतों को पहचानना – शुरुआती लक्षण और कब मदद लेनी चाहिए। जोखिम कारक और रोकथाम – अपनी आँखों की सुरक्षा के लिए जीवनशैली की आदतें। उन्नत उपचार विकल्प – पारंपरिक सर्जरी से लेकर अत्याधुनिक लेजर तकनीक और प्रीमियम इंट्राओकुलर लेंस iols तक। प्रश्नोत्तर सत्र – विशेषज्ञ से अपने प्रश्नों के उत्तर पाएँ। दिनांक मई मंगलवार समय अपराह्न स्थल सेमिनार हॉल यह सत्र विद्यार्थियों संकाय सदस्यों कर्मचारियों और देखभाल करने वालों केयरगिवर के लिए बनाया गया है जो नेत्र स्वास्थ्य चिकित्सा विज्ञान या प्रौद्योगिकी और स्वास्थ्य देखभाल के संबंध में रुचि रखते हैं। पंजीकरण विवरण अपनी भागीदारी सुनिश्चित करने हेतु कृपया दी गई लिंक पर क्लिक करके पहले पंजीकरण कराएं हम इस ज्ञानवर्धक चर्चा में आपकी भागीदारी की प्रतीक्षा कर रहे हैं सादर शिल्पी अनुवाद का श्रेय हिंदी विभाग आईआईटीदिल्ली shilpi Subject: mathematics colloquium on may tuesday at pm in room no academic complex west b
Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department colloquium by prof pradip kumar shiv nadar university delhi ncr on may tuesday the details are given below title minimal surfaces in complex hyperbolic space with complete ends and parabolic higgs bundles date may tuesday at pm venue room no academic complex west b speaker prof pradip kumar abstract in this talk we will see the detailed correspondence between two geometric structures on a punctured riemann surface sigma of negative euler characteristic on one side we have minimal immersions into the complex hyperbolic space mathbbch with unipotent monodromy at the punctures and other side stable parabolic mathrmpu higgs bundles given a representation rho pi sigma to mathrmpu with parabolic monodromy we explicitly construct the associated parabolic higgs bundle e v oplus l phi arising from a rhoequivariant minimal immersion conversely starting from a stable parabolic higgs bundle with prescribed nilpotent residues we recover the corresponding equivariant minimal surface this is an ongoing work with indranil biswas and john loftin all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team

the talk highefficiency highdensity composite dcdc converter architectures time th may monday pm venue iia bharti school abstract in electric drivetrain architectures including xev and electrified aircraft applications a boost dcdc converter is often utilized to interface a battery system to variablespeed ac drives thus enabling the system operation at increased dc bus voltages wide bandgap sic devices lead to improvements in efficiency and reductions in the size of magnetic components in standard boost converter realizations we then show how further improvements can be achieved using composite architectures where stresses and losses on sic devices and passive components are substantially reduced optimization of composite converters involves complex design tradeoffs in terms of losses size and reliability to address these challenges a systematic design methodology is presented which involves selection of the converter architecture planar magnetics design control techniques and electrothermal codesign the approach is illustrated by modeling simulations and experimental results on a kw sic composite dcdc converter prototype featuring kwl power density and drivecycle weighted efficiency biography dragan maksimović received the bs and ms degrees in electrical engineering from the university of belgrade serbia in and respectively and the phd degree in electrical engineering from the california institute of technology pasadena ca usa in from to he was with the university of belgrade since he has been with the department of electrical computer and energy engineering university of colorado boulder co usa where he is currently a distinguished professor and director of the colorado power electronics center he has coauthored more than publications and the textbooks fundamentals of power electronics and digital control of highfrequency switchedmode power converters prof maksimovic received the ieee pels r david middlebrook achievement award and the ieee william e newell power electronics award his research interests include power electronics for renewable energy sources and energy efficiency highfrequency power conversion using wideband gap semiconductors and digital control of switchedmode power converters you can also find the details in the attached flyer regards sreyam sreyam sinha phd assistant professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: reminder colloquium on thursday may by prof v kumar murty
Body: dear all it is our great pleasure to announce a special colloquium by prof v kumar murty from university of toronto canada on may at pm prof v kumar murty is a very distinguished mathematician he was doctoral student of prof john tate and received his doctorate from harvard university in in he was appointed as an associate professor at the university of toronto and in he was promoted to full professor he was the chair of the department of mathematics at the university of toronto during and again from he served as the director of the fields institute between the details of the talk are given below title lfunctions and modular forms abstract in modern number theory these two themes l functions and modular forms have played and are playing a very significant role as the receptacles of reciprocity laws in this talk we will discuss how the two are related and in particular we will discuss two ways to define the lfunction of a modular form each of these methods gives rise to a different way to approximate the lfunction we will then discuss a conjectural definition of a new kind of lfunction which might help us understand the splitting of primes in infinite extensions time and venue thursday may pm at room no academic complex west b all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team dr ekata saha assistant professor department of mathematics indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: kind invitation to attend inauguration on th may monday and participate in ippd international conference
Body: dear all greetings it is our great pleasure to announce and inform you about the nd global forum and international conference on industrial plasma processes and diagnostics ippd may to be held at the lecture hall complex lhc iit delhi the main conference is on may we kindly extend you this invitation and request the honor of your presence for the events inauguration on th may monday at am and attend various sessions to explore the utility of plasmas in our daily life also the conference has a broader audience including ug master and phd students with material electrical energy biohealthcare and plasma science backgrounds apart from scientists and faculty from different parts of india and abroad the relevant information may be found on the following website goal of the conference the primary goal of this conference is to provide motivation and training to young students engineers and researchers also the aim is to update the stateoftheart recent scientific and technological findings of lowtemperature plasma processes used for some societal applications the broad outlook of this conference outlines some of the grand scientific challenges to which significant contributions from plasma nanosciencerelated research can be foreseen also this international forum is focused on advancing the frontiers of the science of plasma processes and their investigation via plasma diagnostics through the presentation of cuttingedge research and fostering informal interactions among scientists of all career stages the conference program includes diverse speakers and discussions of leaders from institutions and organizations worldwide concentrating on the latest developments in the field including emerging energy and environmental technologies abstract plasmas are wellknown tools for our daily lives we are now dreaming of generating green energy from fusion as soon as possible among the various areas of study considerable emphasis is being placed on lowtemperature plasmas and their societal applications using plasmabased devices operated at a very low pressure compared to atmospheric pressure over the past few decades the cold atmospheric pressure plasmas have emerged as a potential candidate for different kinds of applications eg energy electronics agriculture biomedical food preservation textile etc for any practical application we need to design a plasma process and utilize a recipe that is controlled by the plasma parameters and energy of the plasma species one needs to employ innovative and dedicated plasma diagnostics toolstechniques to study and optimize the process consequently extensive basic studies have been conducted on their applications of lowtemperature plasmas in different areas notably the synthesis and etching of thin films by plasma processes have been widely applied in a variety of industrial sectors the structure control of thin film is one of the prime factors in most of these applications it is well known that the structure of this film is closely associated with plasma parameters and species of plasma which are electrons ions radicals and neutrals in plasma processes however the precise control of structure by plasma process is still limited due to inherent complexity reproducibility and control problems in the practical implementation of plasma processing therefore the study of the fundamental physical properties that govern the plasmas becomes more crucial for molecular scale control of film structure and corresponding properties for new generation nanoscale film materials their development and applications in this sense integrated experimental studies including diagnostics and computer modeling of process plasmas to quantify the effect of the unique chemistry and structure of the growing film by radical and plasma control are realized apart from plasmabased procedures the conference will also include plasma in energy environment and plasmabased techniques used for biohealthcare agriculture and other applications main conference dates may th and may th venue lh iit delhi time am onward on may am onward on may kindly find sometime from your busy schedule and attend expert talks and presentations based on your time we gratefully acknowledge funding from anrf and various industries for this event for any queries please write to all are cordially invited to attend regards bibhuti convenor ippd bibhuti bhusan sahu phd associate professor department of energy science and engineering dese indian institute of technology delhi iit hauzkhas new delhi india ph Body: dear all it is our great pleasure to announce a special colloquium by prof v kumar murty from university of toronto canada on may at pm prof v kumar murty is a very distinguished mathematician he was doctoral student of prof john tate and received his doctorate from harvard university in in he was appointed as an associate professor at the university of toronto and in he was promoted to full professor he was the chair of the department of mathematics at the university of toronto during and again from he served as the director of the fields institute between the details of the talk are given below title lfunctions and modular forms abstract in modern number theory these two themes l functions and modular forms have played and are playing a very significant role as the receptacles of reciprocity laws in this talk we will discuss how the two are related and in particular we will discuss two ways to define the lfunction of a modular form each of these methods gives rise to a different way to approximate the lfunction we will then discuss a conjectural definition of a new kind of lfunction which might help us understand the splitting of primes in infinite extensions time and venue thursday may pm at room no academic complex west b all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team dr ekata saha assistant professor department of mathematics indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: reminder me guest talk by prof aashish priye u cincinnati
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the me guest talk by prof aashish priye chemical engineering at the university of cincinnati as per the below schedule date wednesday th may time pm venue me seminar room ii title accessible and inexpensive molecular testing via microfluidics systems engineering and toyinspired physics abstract every year infectious diseases claim millions of livesover million from respiratory infections aloneoften due to slow costly or inaccessible diagnostics imagine a smartphonesized device that could analyze a single drop of blood or saliva in minutes identifying pathogens like sarscov zika or dengue before they become viral motivated by the need to democratize healthcare access particularly in resourcelimited settings we integrate microfluidics biochemistry and systems engineering to create innovative affordable molecular diagnostic solutions in this talk i will describe how we study microscale transport phenomenasuch as fluid flow in tiny channels and chaotic mixingin conjunction with the biochemistry of dna and nucleic acid reactions by combining experimental insights with computational models we develop diagnostic tests that are faster more sensitive and more reliable i will showcase our transformation of fundamental insights into practical diagnostic tools including toyinspired physics for developing selfactuated systems smartphonebased dna detection systems crisprenhanced paper strips for rapid testing and steampowered biochemical reactions that operate without electricity these innovations improve upon the sensitivity and specificity of conventional dna tests while significantly reducing turnaround time and complexity enabling their deployment beyond traditional laboratories into resourceconstrained areas where they are most needed beyond research we actively promote accessible science through outreach and handson learning initiatives by engaging students in microfluidics and diagnostic innovation we are cultivating a new generation of scientists dedicated to advancing equitable healthcare worldwide bio aashish priye is an associate professor of chemical engineering at the university of cincinnati bringing years of expertise in the development of innovative bioanalytical devices for molecular diagnostics he earned his bs in chemical engineering from vit india in and his phd from texas am university in followed by a threeyear postdoctoral fellowship at sandia national laboratories at uc he teaches courses in fluid mechanics heat and mass transfer and a specialized elective on microfluidics and microscale transport phenomena his research has led to the creation of novel molecular diagnostic platforms including a convective pcr thermal cycler a smartphoneenabled dna analysis tool and a labonadrone system his contributions to science and technology have been recognized through several honors most notably the nsf career award the federal award for outstanding technology development and the phillips research award outside the lab he finds scientific inspiration in nature and everyday objects which informs his creative approach to science and fuels thoughtprovoking discussions with students all interested are welcome to join the talk thank you dr abhishek das and dr supreet singh bahga department of mechanical engineering iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india

cardholders copy of bpl card copy of aadhar card copy of pan card note income certificates signed by a notaryoath commissioner will not be accepted additionally students must also submit institute
