Subject: reminder भारत अंतरिक्ष प्रयोगशाला summer internship program space education and employment for all students viksit bharat
Body: we are delighted to invite you to the summer internship which includes a training program in rocketry remote sensing advanced drone sessions cansat cubesat space entrepreneurship astronomy astrophysics and disaster management the primary goal of this internship and workshop is to enhance space education and explore opportunities for technological advancement the government of india under the visionary leadership of honorable pm shri narendra modi has initiated groundbreaking reforms in the space sector these initiatives are designed to enhance and promote space education research and development nationwide a key highlight of these efforts is the celebration of india space week scheduled from august to august along with national space day on august the bharat antriksh saptahindia space lab including the department of science and technology organizes this event following the successful india space week event held from august to national space day and winter internship india space lab has launched a summer internship with a training programme about summer internship india space lab भारत अंतरिक्ष प्रयोगशाला summer internship programme undergraduate and postgraduate students and research scholars in recognized universities or institutions in india and abroad can apply for the india space lab summer internship participants will work closely with various verticals divisions and cells of space and receive training in drone technology air taxi cansat and cubesat student satellite rocketry remote sensing gis space entrepreneurship astronomy and in addition space webinar applicants must apply online by completing the registration form designation of intern space tech intern registration registration for the summer internship and training program will open on april st at pm the online application link is open from st april may th till pm public notice the india space lab भारत अंतरिक्ष प्रयोगशाला summer internship has a total of available seats selection shall be conducted on a merit basis determined by the candidates marks in the examination the training will start on june th and continue until july st with the possibility of an extension to august th registration link online summer internship technical training module days june th july th i days of advanced drone technology air taxi june th to june th ii days of cansat and cubesat student satellite june th to june nd iii days of rocketry training program june th to june th iv days of remote sensing gis sessions june th to july st v days of space astronomy sessions july th to july th vi days of space entrepreneurship sessions july th to july th vii project focused on technology and official works july th to july th viii days of disaster management sessions july th to july st space webinar space education employment th july registration for lateral entry does not involve an examination process for officials faculty research scholars and students the internship training program will offer lateral entry for officials faculty research scholars and students interested in technology or various projects participants can select the technology they wish to learn and join the ongoing sessions important individuals who join through lateral entry will not be classified as part of the internship instead they will receive a certificate upon completing the training program lateral entry india space lab is pleased to announce an opportunity for officials faculty research scholars and students to engage in lateral entry into their preferred technology areas this initiative does not involve an examination process participants will receive a training certificate upon completion rather than an internship certificate lateral entry registration we look Body: gentle reminder sent from my iphone begin forwarded message from abhishek dixit date may at pm ist to g bhuvaneswari subject re phd viva of ms anjali eez ﻿thank you so much ma’am sent from my iphone on may at am g bhuvaneswari wrote ﻿congratulations abhishek warm regards bhuvaneswari on abhishekdixit wrote title phd viva of ms anjali eez date may thursday am mode offline ee committee room thesis title fullduplex operations and reliability enhancement in indoor visible light communication networks short abstract visible light communication vlc is a wireless communication technology that utilizes optical waves in the visible light range nm nm for transferring data it usually consists of lightemitting diodes leds at the transmitters which serve the dual purpose of a light source and a data transmitter this work explores novel techniques to enhance indoor vlc networks by leveraging their inherent fullduplex capabilities allowing simultaneous twoway communication unlike traditional radio frequency rf systems which operate in halfduplex mode it addresses key challenges such as limited cell coverage and intercell interference by analyzing contentionbased and contentionfree mac protocols of ieee a fullduplex optical mac fdomac is proposed for contentionfree access offering improved throughput and compatibility in multiaccess point environments the study also refines the markov model analysis of csmaca for better accuracy and evaluates fullduplex techniques like busy tone to address the hidden node problem in addition it presents hardware design and reliability analysis of fullduplex vlc transceivers using mtbf and life cycle cost modeling facilitating more reliable and costeffective indoor vlc systems all src members faculty members research scholars and pg students are invited to attend the phd viva thanks and regards prof abhishek dixit research supervisor copy to prof arvind mishra sterlite technology external examiner dean academics associate dean Subject: remindermathematics colloquium on may tuesday at pm in room no academic complex west b
Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department colloquium by prof tshewang phuntsho gedu college of business studies royal university of bhutan on may tuesday the details are given below title hybridization frameworks for metaheuristics in combinatorial optimization applications in finance and operations research date may tuesday at pm venue room no academic complex west b speaker prof tshewang phuntsho abstract numerous metaheuristics such as evolutionary computation eg genetic algorithms swarm intelligence eg ant colony optimization particle swarm optimization and artificial immune systems have been developed to solve nphard problems and achieve quasioptimal solutions within a reasonable time however according to the no free lunch theorem nflt no single metaheuristic is universally superior for all problems many researchers suggest that rather than proposing new metaheuristics future research should focus on hybridizing existing methods to create synergistic effects — a challenging but promising direction hybrid metaheuristics are also expected to form a foundational framework for future ai development due to their depth and adaptability this talk introduces two hybridization frameworks tested on scheduling problems with financial implications the first framework proposes a collaborativeparallel hybridization approach that uses thompson sampling and multicriteria decision analysis to holistically evaluate and select the best hybrid architecture from multiple options it incorporates an onboard taguchi design of experiments doe to finetune algorithm parameters this framework was tested on hybrid combinations derived from six different metaheuristics to solve resourceconstrained project scheduling problems with discounted cashflows rcpspdc the second framework introduces a distributed adaptive metaheuristics selection dams approach which leverages distributed computing nodes to hybridize heterogeneous metaheuristics it uses chernoffhoeffding upper confidence bounds ucb to evaluate and adaptively select the best methods for solving rcpspdc with milestone payments rcpspdcmp dams customizes a tailored set of metaheuristics for each project instance from five different metaheuristics with parameters pretuned using classical particle swarm optimization pso experimental results demonstrate that the ucb based dams framework significantly outperforms existing approaches in the literature biography tshewang phuntsho is a postdoctoral fellow in business optimization at the university of south florida usa he currently serves as a lecturer at the royal university of bhutan gedu college of business studies and as head of the business research center at gcbs he also worked as a research assistant at sophia university tokyo specializing in aidriven financial optimization and computational intelligence he holds a phd in green science and engineering data science from sophia university japan where his research focused on hybrid computational intelligence frameworks for financial combinatorial optimization he earned an msc in mathematical engineering applied finance and optimizationdata analytics from the university of l’aquila italy and a ba in mathematics and philosophy from hiram college usa additionally he obtained a postgraduate certificate in higher education from the royal university of bhutan dr phuntsho has been awarded several prestigious scholarships including the jds scholarship japan the abruzzo regional grant italy and the royal government of bhutan scholarship usa he has also secured multiple research grants such as the annual university research grant rub and the ignas grant he has published numerous scopusindexed journal and conference papers in renowned platforms such as ieee access taylor francis connection science mdpi algorithms and springer his research interests include ai machine learning financial optimization project scheduling and computational intelligence all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team

Body: title phd viva of ms anjali eez date may thursday am mode offline ee committee room thesis title fullduplex operations and reliability enhancement in indoor visible light communication networks short abstract visible light communication vlc is a wireless communication technology that utilizes optical waves in the visible light range nm nm for transferring data it usually consists of lightemitting diodes leds at the transmitters which serve the dual purpose of a light source and a data transmitter this work explores novel techniques to enhance indoor vlc networks by leveraging their inherent fullduplex capabilities allowing simultaneous twoway communication unlike traditional radio frequency rf systems which operate in halfduplex mode it addresses key challenges such as limited cell coverage and intercell interference by analyzing contentionbased and contentionfree mac protocols of ieee a fullduplex optical mac fdomac is proposed for contentionfree access offering improved throughput and compatibility in multiaccess point environments the study also refines the markov model analysis of csmaca for better accuracy and evaluates fullduplex techniques like busy tone to address the hidden node problem in addition it presents hardware design and reliability analysis of fullduplex vlc transceivers using mtbf and life cycle cost modeling facilitating more reliable and costeffective indoor vlc systems all src members faculty members research scholars and pg students are invited to attend the phd viva thanks and regards prof abhishek dixit research Subject: reminder an overview of tribology at luleå university of technology april am venueii
Body: dear all speaker prof emeritus braham prakash division of machine elements luleå university of technology luleå sweden date april wednesday time am venue block ii room seminar room mechanical engineering abstract tribology research at luleå university of technology ltu has a rich history spanning more than years rooted in the division of machine elements the early research efforts were primarily centered on the lubrication of machine elements with a strong emphasis on elastohydrodynamic lubrication over time the research landscape has broadened significantly now encompassing nearly every facet of tribology current research at ltu covers a wide range of topics including multiphysics and multiscale modelling and simulation of contact phenomena lubrication across all regimes—from boundary to elastohydrodynamic and tribological applications in rolling element bearings clutches hydraulic motor components tires ski friction biotribology and hightemperature environments a growing area of focus is sustainable tribology including the development of lubricants and materials based on green chemistry these activities are carried out in close cooperation with industry partners this presentation will begin with a brief introduction to luleå university of technology and the division of machine elements it will then highlight the research infrastructure and outline key research themes special emphasis will be placed on the speaker’s areas of interest such as the tribology of sealing elastomers hydraulic motors waterbased lubrication leadfree engine bearings lubricant roles in gear pitting and hightemperature tribology the talk will conclude with an overview of tribology education at ltu including undergraduate and postgraduate courses biosketch prof braham prakash is a professor emeritus in the division of machine elements at luleå university of technology ltu sweden with a distinguished career in tribology and mechanical engineering he served at ltu from to as a professor with a focus on tribology and head of tribolab prior to this he held a prominent academic role at the indian institute of technology delhi iitd from to as lecturer and chief design engineer at itmmec his early industry experience includes engineering and management roles at gabriel india ltd larsen toubro ltd and bits pilani prof prakash has held prestigious visiting appointments at global institutions including tsinghua university china tokyo university of science japan chiba institute of technology japan tokyo institute of technology and indian institutes of technology his research spans a wide range of tribological topics such as hightemperature tribology friction and wear of advanced materials lubrication mechanisms tribotesting and failure analysis he has supervised over phd candidates and numerous postdoctoral researchers significantly contributing to advancements in tribology and surface engineering he holds a phd from iit delhi with a thesis on the tribological properties of metallic glasses an mtech in design of production machines from iit delhi and a bsc engineering in mechanical engineering from punjab engineering college chandigarh prof prakash has developed and taught a wide array of undergraduate and postgraduate courses in tribology and machine elements he is an awardwinning researcher recognized with honors such as the stle wilbur deutsch memorial award best review and editorial awards from the journal friction and jsps fellowship he has served as a guest editor and editorial board member for leading tribology journals and has actively contributed to eu project evaluations academic assessments and industrial contact research his scientific contributions include over peerreviewed journal articles sponsored research projects two patents and editorial roles in conference proceedings and technical books he is a life member of the tribology society of india and a member of several international professional societies including the association for iron steel technology usa and jsps alumni club thanks sujeet

Subject: mathematics colloquium on may tuesday at pm in room no academic complex west b
Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department colloquium by prof tshewang phuntsho gedu college of business studies royal university of bhutan on may tuesday the details are given below title hybridization frameworks for metaheuristics in combinatorial optimization applications in finance and operations research date may tuesday at pm venue room no academic complex west b speaker prof tshewang phuntsho abstract numerous metaheuristics such as evolutionary computation eg genetic algorithms swarm intelligence eg ant colony optimization particle swarm optimization and artificial immune systems have been developed to solve nphard problems and achieve quasioptimal solutions within a reasonable time however according to the no free lunch theorem nflt no single metaheuristic is universally superior for all problems many researchers suggest that rather than proposing new metaheuristics future research should focus on hybridizing existing methods to create synergistic effects — a challenging but promising direction hybrid metaheuristics are also expected to form a foundational framework for future ai development due to their depth and adaptability this talk introduces two hybridization frameworks tested on scheduling problems with financial implications the first framework proposes a collaborativeparallel hybridization approach that uses thompson sampling and multicriteria decision analysis to holistically evaluate and select the best hybrid architecture from multiple options it incorporates an onboard taguchi design of experiments doe to finetune algorithm parameters this framework was tested on hybrid combinations derived from six different metaheuristics to solve resourceconstrained project scheduling problems with discounted cashflows rcpspdc the second framework introduces a distributed adaptive metaheuristics selection dams approach which leverages distributed computing nodes to hybridize heterogeneous metaheuristics it uses chernoffhoeffding upper confidence bounds ucb to evaluate and adaptively select the best methods for solving rcpspdc with milestone payments rcpspdcmp dams customizes a tailored set of metaheuristics for each project instance from five different metaheuristics with parameters pretuned using classical particle swarm optimization pso experimental results demonstrate that the ucb based dams framework significantly outperforms existing approaches in the literature biography tshewang phuntsho is a postdoctoral fellow in business optimization at the university of south florida usa he currently serves as a lecturer at the royal university of bhutan gedu college of business studies and as head of the business research center at gcbs he also worked as a research assistant at sophia university tokyo specializing in aidriven financial optimization and computational intelligence he holds a phd in green science and engineering data science from sophia university japan where his research focused on hybrid computational intelligence frameworks for financial combinatorial optimization he earned an msc in mathematical engineering applied finance and optimizationdata analytics from the university of l’aquila italy and a ba in mathematics and philosophy from hiram college usa additionally he obtained a postgraduate certificate in higher education from the royal university of bhutan dr phuntsho has been awarded several prestigious scholarships including the jds scholarship japan the abruzzo regional grant italy and the royal government of bhutan scholarship usa he has also secured multiple research grants such as the annual university research grant rub and the ignas grant he has published numerous scopusindexed journal and conference papers in renowned platforms such as ieee access taylor francis connection science mdpi algorithms and springer his research interests include ai machine learning financial optimization project scheduling and computational intelligence all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team

subject seminar invite on engineering excitons in d lateral heterostructures and devices” on th april am date april at pm ist to resentfrom hi everyone we are pleased to invite you to a departmental seminar on engineering excitons in d lateral heterostructures and devices” by prof prasanna kumar sahoo quantum materials device research lab qmdrl materials science centre indian institute of technology kharagpur on th april at am at dmse committee room the seminar is being hosted by prof krishna balasubramanian the abstract of the talk is as follows atomically thin semiconductors such as transition metal dichalcogenides tmds have opened a new field with exotic physical properties and exciting potential applications there are enormous possibilities in combining diverse d materials for the unique design of efficient optoelectronic and quantum devices among these lateral heterostructures which can only be fabricated through direct growth present unique opportunities for engineering the formation confinement and transport of electrons holes excitons phonons and polaritons we have developed a novel approach for directly fabricating seamless tmd lateral heterostructures and superlattices with controlled d interfaces alloying and spatial modulation using chemical vapor deposition electrical transport measurements revealed diode behaviour across the d lateral junctions promising for electroluminescence at room temperaturetemperaturedependent photoluminescence from neutral exciton trion and quantum emitters provides a better understanding of the optical properties of these asgrown d lateral heterostructures we demonstrate unique electrooptical properties using an npn lateral heterostructure including tunable photoconductance achieved through controlled exciton and trion generation via resonant excitation our findings provide a significant step forward in understanding and harnessing excitonic properties of d lateral heterostructures paving the way for future innovations in d quantum materials and multimodal optoelectronic devices speaker bio dr sahoos research focuses on exploring and understanding exotic twodimensional d quantum materials and their heterostructures which have a fundamental and wide range of technological implications in future optoelectronics such as leds photovoltaics and quantum technologies his work has covered various nanomaterials including d materials and heterostructures graphene and beyond group iiiv based semiconductor nanowires and sensors he exploits a combination of materials synthesis heterostructuring and device fabrication for physicochemical properties assessment he is a pioneer in the invention of the onepot and insitu growth of multijunction d lateral heterostructures and superlattices via the waterassisted cvd technique for the last several years he has focused on lateral and vertical heterostructures and tuning physical properties via doping and alloying to access exotic properties of d materials regards harsha

materials science and engineering indian institute of technology delhi new delhi ph begin forwarded message from iitd work subject seminar invite on engineering excitons in d lateral heterostructures and devices” on th april am date april at pm ist to resentfrom hi everyone we are pleased to invite you to a departmental seminar on engineering excitons in d lateral heterostructures and devices” by prof prasanna kumar sahoo quantum materials device research lab qmdrl materials science centre indian institute of technology kharagpur on th april at am at dmse committee room the seminar is being hosted by prof krishna balasubramanian the abstract of the talk is as follows atomically thin semiconductors such as transition metal dichalcogenides tmds have opened a new field with exotic physical properties and exciting potential applications there are enormous possibilities in combining diverse d materials for the unique design of efficient optoelectronic and quantum devices among these lateral heterostructures which can only be fabricated through direct growth present unique opportunities for engineering the formation confinement and transport of electrons holes excitons phonons and polaritons we have developed a novel approach for directly fabricating seamless tmd lateral heterostructures and superlattices with controlled d interfaces alloying and spatial modulation using chemical vapor deposition electrical transport measurements revealed diode behaviour across the d lateral junctions promising for electroluminescence at room temperaturetemperaturedependent photoluminescence from neutral exciton trion and quantum emitters provides a better understanding of the optical properties of these asgrown d lateral heterostructures we demonstrate unique electrooptical properties using an npn lateral heterostructure including tunable photoconductance achieved through controlled exciton and trion generation via resonant excitation our findings provide a significant step forward in understanding and harnessing excitonic properties of d lateral heterostructures paving the way for future innovations in d quantum materials and multimodal optoelectronic devices speaker bio dr sahoos research focuses on exploring and understanding exotic twodimensional d quantum materials and their heterostructures which have a fundamental and wide range of technological implications in future optoelectronics such as leds photovoltaics and quantum technologies his work has covered various nanomaterials including d materials and heterostructures graphene and beyond group iiiv based semiconductor nanowires and sensors he exploits a combination of materials synthesis heterostructuring and device fabrication for physicochemical properties assessment he is a pioneer in the invention of the onepot and insitu growth of multijunction d lateral heterostructures and superlattices via the waterassisted cvd technique for the last several years he has focused on lateral and vertical heterostructures and tuning physical properties via doping and alloying to access exotic properties of d materials regards harsha

Subject: i wasnt always a nodes person
Body: hey ​ still waiting to take that dive into fusion ​ you’ve got all the tools you could ever need to create hollywoodlevel visuals within your reach ​ but there’s one thing holding you back… ​ nodes ​ you’re just not a “nodes person” or so you tell yourself ​ to you nodes just don’t make sense ​ what order do they go in ​ how do you connect them together ​ what purpose does each node have ​ it’s all a mystery ​ and thinking about it for too long makes you dizzy ​ to top it all off there’s over and counting nodes in fusion ​ how the heck do you choose which ones to use ​ all of this can be super overwhelming and it’s enough to make you flatout avoid going into fusion more on this tomorrow ​ but here’s the truth about working with nodes ​ nobody thinks they’re a “nodes person” when they first start out ​ nodes are scary to look at ​ but after you do a bit of digging and getting used to them they’re actually pretty intuitive ​ there’s a reason most professional vfx programs use node systems foundry nuke flame and blender — to name a few ​ i remember when i took that first leap into fusion ​ i’d just come from a layerbased compositing software so working with nodes was completely alien to me ​ and let me tell you — it was daunting ​ especially since i also thought i wasn’t a “nodes person” ​ i truly believed i’d never be able to wrap my head around how nodes work ​ but i did it ​ and now i wouldn’t choose to work any other way ​ i actually love working with nodes ​ so next time you’re thinking about diving into fusion – do it ​ if i can figure out how to work nodes so can you ​ once you’ve nailed down your understanding of nodes the skys the limit when it comes to what you’ll be creating ​ need an extra push of motivation to get you working in fusion keep an eye on your inbox tomorrow ​ talk soon ​ casey ​ ps still tempted to just avoid fusion tune into tomorrow’s email to find out why that’s a bad idea… youre receiving this email because youve signed Subject: mathematics colloquium on may tuesday at am in room no academic complex west b
Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department colloquium by dr raghavendra tripathi nyu abu dhabi on may tuesday the details are given below title counting erdos matrices and some related problems date may tuesday at am venue room no academic complex west b speaker dr raghavendra tripathi abstract a classical inequality for bistochastic matrices due to marcus and ree states that the square of the frobenius norm is at most the maximal trace of the matrix erdos asked to characterize the matrices that saturate the marcusree inequality the problem has received little attention until recently and even for x matrices the problem was solved only last year in this talk we will explain this problem and what is known about it so far the main goal is to advertise several related problems in random matrix theory combinatorics and optimal assignments that naturally appear during the investigation of this problem all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team

Subject: colloquium on wednesday april by dr lalit vaishya from isi delhi at am
Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department colloquium by dr lalit vaishya from indian statistical institute delhi isi delhi on april at am the details are given below title infinitude of zeros of twisted spinor zeta function associated to siegel modular form of degree abstract in the first part of this talk we present a brief overview of siegel modular forms of degree and the associated dirichlet series mainly we will talk about the character twist of the spinor zeta function zfs chi displaystylesumn ge fraclambdafnchinns associated to a siegel eigenform f in skgamma and its analytic property here lambdafn denotes the nth siegel eigenvalue of f in the second part we will survey about partial generalized riemann hypothesis for lfunctions associated to modular forms which says that there are infinitely many zeros on the critical line in particular we show that the twisted spinor zeta function zfs chi has infinitely many zeros on the critical line for a quadratic character we also try to look at some applications this is ongoing work with manish k pandey time and venue wednesday april am at room no academic complex west b speaker dr lalit vaishya all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team dr ekata saha assistant professor department of mathematics indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: alumni donor wall design competition
Body: dear students as you might be aware iit delhi has a strong global alumni base who have continued to engage with institute both intellectually and financially it is proposed to build an alumni donor wall to recognise the financial contributions of our alumni nature of contributions from alumni donors alumni donations are used for a wide variety of purposes apart from unrestricted donations to the general endowment alumni also support student scholarships travel grants welfare and wellness programmes csr infrastructurehostels clubs and experiential learning and various research and academic initiatives in different labscoedepartmentscentresschools etc about iit delhi endowment fund endowment funds are a global phenomenon established by educational institutions to ensure their longterm financial stability and program support they rely on donations from alumni corporations and philanthropists investing these contributions to generate income this income is then utilized to fund activities for the institutions benefit often in perpetuity alumni donor wall objectives the objective of the alumni donor wall is to a express gratitude to the donor alumna of iit delhi b record for posterity the contributions of the particular alumni c inspire others to contribute to their alma mater and d instil pride in the campus community about our institute the alumni donor wall will be implemented on a physical space of approximate dimensions ft x ft the actual implementation of the design will depend on the availability of space and nature of design we invite the participation of all iitd students in a designing competition for the alumni donor wall students may work individually or in groups not more than to propose alumni donor wall designs the design must be unique and feasible to implement three levels of donor contributions are to be recognised so the design must differentiate accordingly the design must include locations where donor names will be placed currently the number of donors to be recognised is about which will increase to at least donors at the same time the design should never look incomplete or complete during the next years design needs to be aesthetically pleasing and inspiring without appearing to be a “rich man’s wall” design may be inspired by living or nonliving things associated with iit delhi and the philosophy of giving back to the alma mater the highresolution size up to mb image and design document pptpdf file is to be submitted to the following link the last date for design submission is may the selected alumni donor wall design and portions thereof will be used freely by the institute on its website information brochures and newsletters posters and other outreach documents etc apart from implementing physically on the iit delhi campus the top shortlisted logos will get a cash prize of rs each looking forward to receiving your design entry best regards nilanjan senroy dean alumni relations

Subject: seminar an overview of tribology at luleå university of technology april am venueii
Body: dear all speaker prof emeritus braham prakash division of machine elements luleå university of technology luleå sweden date april wednesday time am venue block ii room seminar room mechanical engineering abstract tribology research at luleå university of technology ltu has a rich history spanning more than years rooted in the division of machine elements the early research efforts were primarily centered on the lubrication of machine elements with a strong emphasis on elastohydrodynamic lubrication over time the research landscape has broadened significantly now encompassing nearly every facet of tribology current research at ltu covers a wide range of topics including multiphysics and multiscale modelling and simulation of contact phenomena lubrication across all regimes—from boundary to elastohydrodynamic and tribological applications in rolling element bearings clutches hydraulic motor components tires ski friction biotribology and hightemperature environments a growing area of focus is sustainable tribology including the development of lubricants and materials based on green chemistry these activities are carried out in close cooperation with industry partners this presentation will begin with a brief introduction to luleå university of technology and the division of machine elements it will then highlight the research infrastructure and outline key research themes special emphasis will be placed on the speaker’s areas of interest such as the tribology of sealing elastomers hydraulic motors waterbased lubrication leadfree engine bearings lubricant roles in gear pitting and hightemperature tribology the talk will conclude with an overview of tribology education at ltu including undergraduate and postgraduate courses biosketch prof braham prakash is a professor emeritus in the division of machine elements at luleå university of technology ltu sweden with a distinguished career in tribology and mechanical engineering he served at ltu from to as a professor with a focus on tribology and head of tribolab prior to this he held a prominent academic role at the indian institute of technology delhi iitd from to as lecturer and chief design engineer at itmmec his early industry experience includes engineering and management roles at gabriel india ltd larsen toubro ltd and bits pilani prof prakash has held prestigious visiting appointments at global institutions including tsinghua university china tokyo university of science japan chiba institute of technology japan tokyo institute of technology and indian institutes of technology his research spans a wide range of tribological topics such as hightemperature tribology friction and wear of advanced materials lubrication mechanisms tribotesting and failure analysis he has supervised over phd candidates and numerous postdoctoral researchers significantly contributing to advancements in tribology and surface engineering he holds a phd from iit delhi with a thesis on the tribological properties of metallic glasses an mtech in design of production machines from iit delhi and a bsc engineering in mechanical engineering from punjab engineering college chandigarh prof prakash has developed and taught a wide array of undergraduate and postgraduate courses in tribology and machine elements he is an awardwinning researcher recognized with honors such as the stle wilbur deutsch memorial award best review and editorial awards from the journal friction and jsps fellowship he has served as a guest editor and editorial board member for leading tribology journals and has actively contributed to eu project evaluations academic assessments and industrial contact research his scientific contributions include over peerreviewed journal articles sponsored research projects two patents and editorial roles in conference proceedings and technical books he is a life member of the tribology society of india and a member of several international professional societies including the association for iron steel technology usa and jsps alumni club thanks sujeet

Body: we have started the online talk now best dr neel kanth kundu assistant professor care iit delhi web original message subject re online talk invitation for a talk on thz hardware development for future quantum communication network on wednesday april at pm date from neel kanth kundu to dear all the talk will be delivered online via ms teams since the speakers flight got postponed meeting link meeting id passcode qw ue cd thanks and regards dr neel kanth kundu assistant professor care iit delhi web original message subject re invitation for a talk on thz hardware development for future quantum communication network on wednesday april at pm date from neel kanth kundu to dear all a gentle reminder for the talk tomorrow at pm at the care committee room by dr kaveh delfanazari from the university of glasgow google calendar invite thanks and best regards dr neel kanth kundu assistant professor care iit delhi web original message subject invitation for a talk on thz hardware development for future quantum communication network on wednesday april at pm dear all i would like to invite you to an exciting talk on thz quantum communications organized by care date and time wednesday april at pm venue care committee room room blockiii title thz hardware development for future quantum communication network abstract with the exponential growth in demand for highbandwidth communication it is crucial to consider not only the optimal network platform but also the security and privacy of transmitted information millimetre mm waves and terahertz thz frequencies with their high carrier rates have been proposed as key enablers to surpass the shannon capacity limit of current communication systems by offering ultrawideband signal transmission these frequencies also support wireless links that can interface seamlessly with optical communication infrastructure however most solidstate components operating in the ghz to thz range particularly sources and detectors remain inefficient bulky and unsuitable for lowpower onchip operation in this talk i will outline the key challenges and present our thz hardware solutions aimed at enabling thz quantum communication for future quantum networks m zhang et al ieee transactions on quantum engineering k delfanazari nature photonics bio dr kaveh delfanazari holds a leverhulme trust research fellowship from the royal academy of engineering and is an associate professor university senior lecturer of electronic and nanoscale engineering at the james watt school of engineering and the centre for quantum technology university of glasgow uofg uk his recent awards include a personal research fellowship from the royal society of edinburgh dr delfanazari is a senior member of ieee a steering committee member of ieee quantum a committee member of the iop quantum electronics and photonic group iop superconductivity group and a fellow of the higher education academy uk he has held positions as a senior research associate in quantum devices and circuits at the university of cambridge uk a research fellow and project leader in superconducting and quantum metamaterials at the university of southampton uk dr delfanazari investigated integrated superconducting terahertz thz emitters and antennas based on the josephson effect during his phd work at the university of tsukuba japan his research work in japan led him to receive the deans award for excellence in phd thesis the japanese government scholarship several travel grants and international best paper and presentation awards thanks and best regards Subject: me guest talk by prof aashish priye u cincinnati
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the me guest talk by prof aashish priye chemical engineering at the university of cincinnati as per the below schedule date wednesday th may time pm venue me seminar room ii title accessible and inexpensive molecular testing via microfluidics systems engineering and toyinspired physics abstract every year infectious diseases claim millions of livesover million from respiratory infections aloneoften due to slow costly or inaccessible diagnostics imagine a smartphonesized device that could analyze a single drop of blood or saliva in minutes identifying pathogens like sarscov zika or dengue before they become viral motivated by the need to democratize healthcare access particularly in resourcelimited settings we integrate microfluidics biochemistry and systems engineering to create innovative affordable molecular diagnostic solutions in this talk i will describe how we study microscale transport phenomenasuch as fluid flow in tiny channels and chaotic mixingin conjunction with the biochemistry of dna and nucleic acid reactions by combining experimental insights with computational models we develop diagnostic tests that are faster more sensitive and more reliable i will showcase our transformation of fundamental insights into practical diagnostic tools including toyinspired physics for developing selfactuated systems smartphonebased dna detection systems crisprenhanced paper strips for rapid testing and steampowered biochemical reactions that operate without electricity these innovations improve upon the sensitivity and specificity of conventional dna tests while significantly reducing turnaround time and complexity enabling their deployment beyond traditional laboratories into resourceconstrained areas where they are most needed beyond research we actively promote accessible science through outreach and handson learning initiatives by engaging students in microfluidics and diagnostic innovation we are cultivating a new generation of scientists dedicated to advancing equitable healthcare worldwide bio aashish priye is an associate professor of chemical engineering at the university of cincinnati bringing years of expertise in the development of innovative bioanalytical devices for molecular diagnostics he earned his bs in chemical engineering from vit india in and his phd from texas am university in followed by a threeyear postdoctoral fellowship at sandia national laboratories at uc he teaches courses in fluid mechanics heat and mass transfer and a specialized elective on microfluidics and microscale transport phenomena his research has led to the creation of novel molecular diagnostic platforms including a convective pcr thermal cycler a smartphoneenabled dna analysis tool and a labonadrone system his contributions to science and technology have been recognized through several honors most notably the nsf career award the federal award for outstanding technology development and the phillips research award outside the lab he finds scientific inspiration in nature and everyday objects which informs his creative approach to science and fuels thoughtprovoking discussions with students all interested are welcome to join the talk thank you dr abhishek das and dr supreet singh bahga department of mechanical engineering iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: re seminar by dr eric freysz at the physics department monday april am
Body: gentle reminder on dr sunil kumar wrote dear all it is with immense pleasure that we invite you for a seminar by dr eric freysz of universite de bordeaux france please find more details as below title a short journey through terahertz physics from airplasma source to the generation of multiplevortex beams and hyperraman spectroscopy time and venue monday april am physics seminar room ms abstract terahertz thz sources available nowadays are able to cover a very broad spectral range spanning from ghz up to thz since the thz photons can excite and probe the farir modes of variety of different materials gas liquid solid their applications are exploding in many different fundamental and applied fields during this talk i will give a short overview over our most recent works in the thz field at first i will present our investigation about the farfield thz beam profile generated from an air plasma source indeed while plasmas generated in air by twocolor femtosecond laser pulses are a well established technique to generate ultrashort fs and intense thz field gvcm the generated thz field pattern is still under debate for complete details i will show that the combination of different thz imaging techniques makes it possible to address this debate in the second part i will present a simple way to generate multiple vortexbeams with multiple topological charges we will show that an array of up to x vortex beams with multiple topological charges can be generated the advantage and limitation of the method we implemented will be discussed towards the end i will present thz hyperraman spectroscopy of a silicon wafer where i will show that such a timeresolved spectroscopy makes it possible to follow easily the very rapid and strong population of the optical phonons induced by the hot carriers generated by subpicosecond ir pulses it gets initiated over a few hundreds of femtoseconds and lasts throughout the duration of the nearir pulse about the speaker dr eric freysz is directeur de recherche emerite au cnrs and senior member of optica former optical society of america he has authored more than publications in international journal holds patents and supervised more than phd students eric received his phd from univ bordeaux in june in laser physics under the supervision of prof bernard couillaud former ceo of coherent inc and prof andré ducasse former director of the école supérieure doptique paris and laboratoire charles fabry cnrs paris after his phd he got a oneyear grant from the dret to continue his research at the university of bordeaux and was also a consulting engineer at lectrasystem for building co laser for laser cutting machines in october he joined the cnrs as a research associate in october he got his state thesis on a subject dealing with linear and nonlinear optical spectroscopy of critical microemulsion from may to may he was a research fellow at the university of berkeley california in the group of pr y r shen there he ran the first spectroscopic study of water interfaces using near ir ir surface sumfrequency technique back in france he created his own group of research on nonlinear optical spectroscopy in Subject: invitation for a talk on thz hardware development for future quantum communication network on wednesday april at pm
Body: dear all i would like to invite you to an exciting talk on thz quantum communications organized by care date and time wednesday april at pm venue care committee room room blockiii title thz hardware development for future quantum communication network abstract with the exponential growth in demand for highbandwidth communication it is crucial to consider not only the optimal network platform but also the security and privacy of transmitted information millimetre mm waves and terahertz thz frequencies with their high carrier rates have been proposed as key enablers to surpass the shannon capacity limit of current communication systems by offering ultrawideband signal transmission these frequencies also support wireless links that can interface seamlessly with optical communication infrastructure however most solidstate components operating in the ghz to thz range particularly sources and detectors remain inefficient bulky and unsuitable for lowpower onchip operation in this talk i will outline the key challenges and present our thz hardware solutions aimed at enabling thz quantum communication for future quantum networks m zhang et al ieee transactions on quantum engineering k delfanazari nature photonics bio dr kaveh delfanazari holds a leverhulme trust research fellowship from the royal academy of engineering and is an associate professor university senior lecturer of electronic and nanoscale engineering at the james watt school of engineering and the centre for quantum technology university of glasgow uofg uk his recent awards include a personal research fellowship from the royal society of edinburgh dr delfanazari is a senior member of ieee a steering committee member of ieee quantum a committee member of the iop quantum electronics and photonic group iop superconductivity group and a fellow of the higher education academy uk he has held positions as a senior research associate in quantum devices and circuits at the university of cambridge uk a research fellow and project leader in superconducting and quantum metamaterials at the university of southampton uk dr delfanazari investigated integrated superconducting terahertz thz emitters and antennas based on the josephson effect during his phd work at the university of tsukuba japan his research work in japan led him to receive the deans award for excellence in phd thesis the japanese government scholarship several travel grants and international best paper and presentation awards thanks and best regards dr neel kanth kundu assistant professor care iit delhi Subject: seminar by dr eric freysz at the physics department monday april am
Body: dear all it is with immense pleasure that we invite you for a seminar by dr eric freysz of universite de bordeaux france please find more details as below title a short journey through terahertz physics from airplasma source to the generation of multiplevortex beams and hyperraman spectroscopy time and venue monday april am physics seminar room ms abstract terahertz thz sources available nowadays are able to cover a very broad spectral range spanning from ghz up to thz since the thz photons can excite and probe the farir modes of variety of different materials gas liquid solid their applications are exploding in many different fundamental and applied fields during this talk i will give a short overview over our most recent works in the thz field at first i will present our investigation about the farfield thz beam profile generated from an air plasma source indeed while plasmas generated in air by twocolor femtosecond laser pulses are a well established technique to generate ultrashort fs and intense thz field gvcm the generated thz field pattern is still under debate for complete details i will show that the combination of different thz imaging techniques makes it possible to address this debate in the second part i will present a simple way to generate multiple vortexbeams with multiple topological charges we will show that an array of up to x vortex beams with multiple topological charges can be generated the advantage and limitation of the method we implemented will be discussed towards the end i will present thz hyperraman spectroscopy of a silicon wafer where i will show that such a timeresolved spectroscopy makes it possible to follow easily the very rapid and strong population of the optical phonons induced by the hot carriers generated by subpicosecond ir pulses it gets initiated over a few hundreds of femtoseconds and lasts throughout the duration of the nearir pulse about the speaker dr eric freysz is directeur de recherche emerite au cnrs and senior member of optica former optical society of america he has authored more than publications in international journal holds patents and supervised more than phd students eric received his phd from univ bordeaux in june in laser physics under the supervision of prof bernard couillaud former ceo of coherent inc and prof andré ducasse former director of the école supérieure doptique paris and laboratoire charles fabry cnrs paris after his phd he got a oneyear grant from the dret to continue his research at the university of bordeaux and was also a consulting engineer at lectrasystem for building co laser for laser cutting machines in october he joined the cnrs as a research associate in october he got his state thesis on a subject dealing with linear and nonlinear optical spectroscopy of critical microemulsion from may to may he was a research fellow at the university of berkeley california in the group of pr y r shen there he ran the first spectroscopic study of water interfaces using near ir ir surface sumfrequency technique back in france he created his own group of research on nonlinear optical spectroscopy in he was promoted directeur de recherche in cnrs in for months he was invited professor at the university of pittsburgh in the physicalchemistry department from to he was scientific consultant for the ceacesta in the laser physics department for the megajoule project from january to january he was the director of a joint research institute gathering four laboratories in the physics department of university of bordeaux from january to december he was director of the laboratory centre de physique moléculaire et hertzienne umr cnrs from january to december he was member of the regional committee for research and technological development the administration and scientific board of the university of bordeaux from may to april he was deputy director and then administrator of the science and technology department at the university of bordeaux his current research interests are around laser physics femtosecond laser and amplifiers optical parametric oscillators and amplifiers build around nonlinear crystals and fibers nanosecond microlasers for ignition of aeronautics engines ir and thz spectroscopic techniques with kind regards sunil dr sunil kumar department of physics indian institute of technology delhi haus khas new delhi india tel web

Subject: departmental seminar dr kush coshic max planck institute of biophysics th april pm ksbs committee room
Body: dear all we invite you to the ksbs departmental talk on th april at pm in ksbs committee room the speaker is dr kush coshic post doctoral associate max planck institute of biophysics all are cordially invited details may be found below speaker dr kush coshic date th april time hrs venue committee room ksbs title molecular simulations of nucleic acid packaging physical virology and beyond abstract packaging of nucleic acids is essential for all life occurring across diverse scales and complexities virus particles with their dense packaging allow us to study fundamental packaging principles i will begin by introducing a multiresolution mr approach to determine the complete structure of bacteriophage hk including its base pair genome mimicking the action of a packaging motor we simulated genome loading and refined the packaged capsid structure at increasing resolutions generating a million atom model of the entire virion including internal water and ions surprisingly our simulations reveal a loop extrusion mechanism for dna packaging resulting in diverse genome configurations and unique viral particle attributes microsecondlong allatom simulations explored the packaged genomes impact on capsid structure internal pressure electrostatics and the diffusion of water ions and dna this adaptable methodology can be applied to other dsdna viruses like herpes i will then broaden the scope to discuss my ongoing work on modeling rna packaging — both in the context of viruses such as dengue and in understanding the role of ribonucleoproteins rnps and other packaging factors involved in rna packaging inside living cells time permitting i will very briefly talk about some of my relevant publications and ongoing projects coshic k et al nature – thank you best regards anita anita roy phd assistant professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology hauz khas new delhi india tel

Subject: alumni donor wall design competition
Body: dear students as you might be aware iit delhi has a strong global alumni base who have continued to engage with institute both intellectually and financially it is proposed to build an alumni donor wall to recognise the financial contributions of our alumni nature of contributions from alumni donors alumni donations are used for a wide variety of purposes apart from unrestricted donations to the general endowment alumni also support student scholarships travel grants welfare and wellness programmes csr infrastructurehostels clubs and experiential learning and various research and academic initiatives in different labscoedepartmentscentresschools etc about iit delhi endowment fund endowment funds are a global phenomenon established by educational institutions to ensure their longterm financial stability and program support they rely on donations from alumni corporations and philanthropists investing these contributions to generate income this income is then utilized to fund activities for the institutions benefit often in perpetuity alumni donor wall objectives the objective of the alumni donor wall is to a express gratitude to the donor alumna of iit delhi b record for posterity the contributions of the particular alumni c inspire others to contribute to their alma mater and d instil pride in the campus community about our institute the alumni donor wall will be implemented on a physical space of approximate dimensions ft x ft the actual implementation of the design will depend on the availability of space and nature of design we invite the participation of all iitd students in a designing competition for the alumni donor wall students may work individually or in groups not more than to propose alumni donor wall designs the design must be unique and feasible to implement three levels of donor contributions are to be recognised so the design must differentiate accordingly the design must include locations where donor names will be placed currently the number of donors to be recognised is about which will increase to at least donors at the same time the design should never look incomplete or complete during the next years design needs to be aesthetically pleasing and inspiring without appearing to be a “rich man’s wall” design may be inspired by living or nonliving things associated with iit delhi and the philosophy of giving back to the alma mater the highresolution size up to mb image and design document pptpdf file is to be submitted to the following link the last date for design submission is may the selected alumni donor wall design and portions thereof will be used freely by the institute on its website information brochures and newsletters posters and other outreach documents etc apart from implementing physically on the iit delhi campus the top shortlisted logos will get a cash prize of rs each looking forward to receiving your design entry best regards nilanjan senroy dean alumni relations

Subject: invitation to health and thalassemia checkup camp th april ex hall iit delhi
Body: greetings from nss iit delhi we are pleased to inform you that a health and thalassemia checkup camp is being organized on th april in collaboration with the rotary club from am to pm at ex hall iit delhi thalassemia is a serious inherited blood disorder that affects the bodys ability to produce hemoglobin individuals who are carriers often remain unaware due to a lack of symptoms but if two carriers marry there is a chance their child may inherit thalassemia major a condition that requires lifelong blood transfusions and treatment a simple screening can determine whether a person is a carrier and help in making informed choices in the future we strongly encourage everyone to participate in this crucial test alongside thalassemia screening the camp will also offer several free health services including bone densitometry to assess bone strength eye checkup dental checkup oral cancer detection blood pressure and blood sugar testing and consultations with both a general physician and a gynecologist this is a valuable opportunity to take charge of your health and get guidance from medical professionals without the hassle of scheduling multiple appointments we invite all students faculty and staff to actively participate and help foster a healthier and more informed campus environment to stay updated with the latest information regarding the camp kindly join whatsapp group through the following link looking forward to your enthusiastic participation for any queries contact vaishali warm regards ankesh jain associate professor department of electrical engineering coordinator national service scheme nss iit delhi

Subject: civil engineering seminar series dr arulalan t scientist c in imd today at noon
Body: dear all we are pleased to invite you to a civil engineering seminar series dr arulalan t scientist c in india meteorological department imd new delhi about the speaker dr arulalan t has bsc in physics mtech and phd in atmospheric oceanic sciences from cas iit delhi in february dr arulalan joined the numerical weather prediction division of the india meteorological department imd new delhi as a scientistc over the past four years he has been actively involved in cyclone track forecasting using nine globalregional weather models he successfully predicted cyclones from to achieving a landfall position error of less than km and contributing to zero mortality title heatwaves over india and its teleconnections under °c and °c warmer worlds time date april friday venue block iv lt topic of seminar developing a better scientific understanding of anthropogenic climate change and climate variability especially the predictionprojection of climate futures with useful temporal and geographical resolution and quantified uncertainties and using that knowledge to inform adaptation planning and action will become crucially important in the coming years generating such policyrelevant knowledge may be particularly important for developing countries such as india it is with this backdrop that in this paper we analyze future heat waves in india by using observations and a large number of model simulations of historical °c and °c warmer worlds in both the future scenarios there is an increased probability of heat waves during june and july when the indian monsoon is in full swing and humidity is high which makes the heat events even more of a health risk while the highest temperatures in heat waves may not increase much in future climates the duration and areal extent of the heat waves will most likely increase leading to the emergence of new heat waveprone zones in india the results indicate that the joint frequencies of the longest duration and large area events could be nearly threefold greater in the °c and fivefold greater in the °c future scenarios compared to historical simulations thus overall the study indicates a substantial increase in the risk of heat events that typically elicit warnings from forecasters the teleconnections due to atmospheric blocking over northwest atlantic at hpa and rossby waves cause heatwaves over northwest india and will make early heatwaves due to these teleconnections under °c and °c warmer worlds the likely widespread and persistent nature of heat wave events in the future as revealed by this study will require planning and adaptation measures beyond the shortterm disaster planning frameworks currently in place exploring what these measures might look like is beyond the scope of this study but it underlines the importance of developing climate knowledge with high temporal and geographical resolution capable of informing adaptation policy and planning thanks and regards office of the head department of civil engineering room no blockiv indian institute of technology iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india email telephone secretary telephone direct

Subject: seminar by dr matthew cherukara ucl united kindom
Body: to all facultystudents time date april friday venue cbme committee room iii speaker profile about the speaker dr matthew cherukara has a background in physics msci university of nottingham and completed a dphil at the university of oxford in biomedical engineering with his thesis on quantitative mri methods and their applications to stroke matthew now works as a postdoctoral research fellow at university college london in quantitative mri in a range of applications matthew has lectured in mathematics and medical imaging at the undergraduate level and has experience teaching in high schools outside of work his interests include reading history books hiking music and hospitality topic of seminar quantitative magnetic susceptibility mapping qsm is a developing mri technique that uses the phase of the complex mr signal to reconstruct distributions of magnetic susceptibility this susceptibility can be affected by deposited minerals such as calcium or iron and by levels of oxygenation in blood vessels as such qsm has been used to quantitatively assess these species in the brain and other parts of the body we have used qsm to assess changes in susceptibility in the brains of children with sickle cell anaemia an inherited disease of the haemoglobin and correlated changes in brain susceptibility with cognitive and motor skills compared to healthy familial controls Subject: civil engineering seminar series prof eric a davidson fullbrightnehru distinguished senior scholar ggsiu delhi and prof at univ of maryland center for environmental science
Body: dear all we are pleased to invite you to a distinguished lecture by prof eric a davidson fulbrightnehru distinguished senior scholar guru gobind singh indraprastha university delhi and professor at the university of maryland center for environmental science details of the talk title human alteration of the global nitrogen cycle speaker prof eric a davidson date april wednesday time pm venue committee room iit delhi abstract of the talk over the past century the production of reactive nitrogenprimarily through the haberbosch processhas significantly altered the natural nitrogen cycle this has enabled global food production to keep pace with population growth but at the cost of widespread environmental degradation one of the most pressing concerns is the steady rise in atmospheric n₂o concentrations which icecore and instrumental records show have increased sharply over the last two millennia primarily due to agricultural and industrial emissions this talk will examine the evolving nitrogen flows in agriculture highlighting the inefficiencies in nitrogen use where less than half of applied nitrogen reaches harvested products the excess is lost to the environment as pollution contributing to water eutrophication air quality issues and climate change emerging technologies and sustainability efforts are now focusing on green ammoniaproduced using renewable energyas a promising solution for decarbonizing nitrogen fertilizer production india is at the forefront of this shift with the worlds first green ammonia demonstration plant established by the acme group in bikaner rajasthan beyond agriculture green ammonia is also being explored as a lowcarbon fuel for the shipping industry presenting new opportunities and challenges biographical sketch dr eric a davidson is professor at the appalachian laboratory of the university of maryland center for environmental science where he also served as director for six years his research focuses on terrestrial nutrient cycling greenhouse gas emissions from soils global biogeochemical cycles and sustainable agriculture he is a past president and fellow of the american geophysical union agu a fellow of the american association for the advancement of science aaas and is recognized as a highly cited researcher by web of science dr davidson has served as north american center director for the international nitrogen initiative and as nasa project scientist for the largescale biosphereatmosphere experiment in amazonia he was also a jefferson science fellow and currently serves as senior editor of agu advances his previous editorial roles include global biogeochemical cycles global change biology and the soil science society of america journal dr davidson earned his phd from north carolina state university and completed postdoctoral research at the university of california berkeley and nasa ames research center he spent years at the woods hole research center where he also served as president and executive director he is the author of science for a green new deal connecting climate economics and social justice and you cant eat gnp as part of his fulbrightnehru project in india dr davidson is investigating the environmental and socioeconomic implications of green ammonia technologies for fertilizer production his work involves extensive engagement with stakeholders including policymakers industry leaders scientists and farmers to assess expectations and awareness of sustainable nitrogen management strategies in the indian context thanks and regards office of the head department of civil engineering room no blockiv indian institute of technology iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india email telephone secretary telephone direct

Subject: hss seminar series on democracy’s dhamma buddhism in the making of modern india wednesday april pm
Body: dear all you are all cordially invited to the seminar on wednesday april by drgitanjali surendran details are given below we look forward to seeing many of you there hss seminar series team rensa sahiinii norbu and naveen date april time pm venue committee room ms department of humanities and social sciences th floor main building indian institute of technology delhi speaker gitanjali surendran jindal global university chair bharati puri department of huss iit delhi title democracy’s dhamma buddhism in the making of modern india c abstract in b r ambedkar publicly converted to buddhism raising questions about his turn from constitutionalism to religion the answer lies in buddhism itself in the late colonial era the struggle to produce an appropriate buddhism for a nationinthemaking reveals a secret history foundational to modern india thinkers activists reformers pilgrims and monks from around south southeast and east asia discussed universalism nationalism modernity democracy and caste radicalism and advocated an indian return to buddhism and the buddha this book traces this genealogy through the buddhist itineraries and political projects of figures like anagarika dharmapala swami vivekananda rabindranath tagore jawaharlal nehru vinayak d savarkar rahul sankrityayan and ambedkar to reveal how buddhism emerged as democracy’s dhamma the religion of democracy speaker bio gitanjali surendran s professor of history and executive director of the centre for research in history at jindal global law school where she has been teaching since her work has been published in edited volumes and in the media her research interests include modern south asian cultural and intellectual history environmental and gender history she is also interested in public history and is exploring ways to bring academic history into public discourse her latest book democracy’s dhamma buddhism in the making of modern india c came out in july last year with cambridge university press dr naveen thayyil department of humanities and social sciences iit delhi hauz khas new delhi

Subject: open talk on friday april by dr venkat ramanan sri ramanasramam
Body: to all facultystaffstudents title of the talk forty verses on reality a primer to selfrealization date day april friday time pm venue lecture hall complex lh speaker dr venkat s ramanan is the president of sri ramanasramam and is the great grandnephew of sri ramana maharshi he took over as the th president of the ashram in and we at iit delhi are privileged to have him amongst us to contribute as a guest faculty for vev an open elective course offered by nrcvee dr venkat ramanan is a medical doctor who practised medicine in maryland for over years before choosing to return to india for good with his family and dedicate his life to serve the maharshis ashram and his devotees abstract for the talk this collection of verses were composed by sri ramana maharshi in response to the requests of his devotees including muruganar and kavyajanta ganapathi muni a few stray verses composed by him on vedanta were arranged by the devotees without success they requested him to compose a fresh set of verses the versus on reality is a composition on jnana pure and simple with no mention of god anywhere this crown jewel of advaita was finished in august by ramana maharshi these versus with its core teachings of selfinquiry are an in dispensable and rare text for aspirants who strive for reality concepts like discrimination inquiry and the nature of experience are lucidly explained this prepares the true spiritual seeker for a headlong plunge within to the innermost depths of spiritual heart to attain and be the self best regards head nrcvee iit delhi ph

committee room block iv room no department of civil engineering at indian institute of technology iit delhi title of the seminar bilateral research collaborations in aiml applications in environment sciences and engineering between india and australia date monday th april pm abstract of the seminar bilateral collaboration in artificial intelligence ai and machine learning ml research between india and australia holds significant promise for addressing critical environmental challenges each country contributes unique strengths indias proficiency in scalable ai solutions and datadriven policy frameworks complements australias advanced capabilities in environmental modelling and sustainable engineering innovations this partnership has the potential to enhance predictive analytics related to climate change water resource management biodiversity conservation and renewable energy optimization by promoting joint research initiatives establishing datasharing frameworks and technology iit delhi and the university of southern queensland discuss the potential impact of such collaboration and propose an outline for the steps to be taken to strengthen bilateral relations in aimldriven environmental sciences and engineering biographical sketch of the speaker dr ekta sharma is an early career research academic currently serving as an australiaindia women research fellow in Subject: re new flavor of ell online learning online algorithms
Body: dear all please note that this course will not be floated next semester regards gourab original message subject new flavor of ell online learning online algorithms date from gourab ghatak to dear students if you intrigued by the challenge of making optimal decisions without knowing the future i invite you to join the upcoming online learning course ell next semester where we will dive deep into online algorithms — a powerful framework for decisionmaking under uncertainty important note unlike previous offerings of this course that focused on bandit frameworks this years offering will mainly focus on online algorithms some problems that we will tackle are the skirental problem when should you buy versus rent to minimize longterm costs without knowing how long youll need the skis the secretary problem how do you hire the best candidate when you must make an irreversible decision on the spot the bin packing problem how can you efficiently pack objects of varying sizes into bins as they arrive in sequence the adwords problem how should an advertiser dynamically bid for ad slots to maximize visibility while staying within budget despite uncertainty in future bids these problems and more will be discussed in light of competitive analysis and realworld applications from ecommerce pricing strategies to online caching to wireless communications and beyond if youre interested in algorithmic decisionmaking theoretical foundations with practical impact or just enjoy tackling intellectually stimulating problems this course is for you looking forward to seeing many of you in the class regards gourab
