Subject: me guest talk by mr deepak prakash kumar dept of mechanical engineering texas am university
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the me guest talk by mr deepak prakash kumar dept of mechanical engineering texas am university as per the below schedule date tuesday th april time pm venue me seminar room ii title trajectory planning and task allocation for autonomous ground and aerial vehicles abstract autonomous vehicles are increasingly utilized in civilian and military contexts for tasks such as medicine delivery and surveillance these vehicles can also access hardtoreach areas making them ideal for such missions the talk focuses on trajectory planning and task allocation for autonomous ground and aerial vehicles which are critical problems to tackle when planning a given mission trajectory planning is crucial for vehicles such as fixedwing unmanned aerial vehicles and hypersonic vehicles which are constantly in motion and have curvature constraints on their path since they cannot change direction instantaneously the objective is to find the leastcost path to travel from one location and orientation to another either on a plane or at a constant altitude over the surface of the earth while satisfying curvature constraints in realworld scenarios multiple vehicles often collaborate to accomplish a mission making task allocation vital for efficient task distribution and path planning this talk will explore various problems within these domains tailored to their specific applications additionally the talk will cover experimental work i have been performing as the team captain of texas am universitys student team competing in the prestigious sae autodrive competition sponsored by general motors the goal of the competition is to develop a level autonomous car capable of autonomously navigating in complex environments with static and dynamic obstacles traffic lights and obstructed lanes and roads bio deepak prakash kumar is a phd candidate in the department of mechanical engineering at texas am university he holds a btech in engineering design and an mtech in automotive engineering from the indian institute of technology madras his research interests encompass path planning for autonomous ground and aerial vehicles algorithms for vehicle routing problems planning and control of autonomous vehicles and vehicle dynamics he has also been leading texas am universitys student team which is comprised of nearly students competing in the prestigious sae autodrive competition sponsored by general motors for nearly two years he successfully led the team to a secondplace finish in the nation in the competition all interested are welcome to join the talk thank you abhishek das and rajan prasad department of mechanical engineering iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: tomorrow design inquiry as cooperative learning institute seminar by dr liam fennessy visiting faculty from rmit melbourne
Body: you are invited to this session by prof liam fennessy from rmit melbourne australia dear students and colleagues on th april we bring to you an interesting institute seminar titled design inquiry as cooperative learning by prof liam fennessy associate dean learning teaching rmit melbourne australia attached is the flyer please block your calendar best shilpi here are further details date th april friday time pm venue seminar hall iit delhi abstract of the talk notions of health human nonhuman and environmental are coconstructed by sociotechnological practices and constitute rich territories for collaborative design inquiry where problems are opened out not to solve but to see taking the position that design projects done in the world and with people are inherently a practice of cooperative heutagogy this lecture reflects on past projects to discuss moments and perhaps offer some ways to reframe codesign about the speaker associate professor liam fennessy supervises doctoral candidates teaches undergraduate industrial design students conducts research and undertakes various academic leadership activities at rmit university in melbourne australia liams academic work is concerned with how design practice might better attend to the socioculturalenvironmental implications of new product and service development his research has two key foci on design pedagogy and practice and on design projects that deal with broad questions of care specifically the sociality sustainability and dematerialization of productservicesystems liams research activities are always structured around design collaboration and span topics including a design in the conservation science domain with a particular emphasis on design to support the management and improvement of endangered species design for animal welfare and enrichment for zoos and agricultural contexts and novel approaches to animal computer interactions b design for circularity and sustainability with a specific agenda in informing public policy and business systems transitions c design for health through a longterm collaborative design inquiry into diabetes and the complex human social institutional and technological constructs that script notions of care and selfcare and large cross university multidisciplinary project with australian red cross exploring blood and plasma donation process through new product and service development d design pedagogies where the educational space of design practice is actively crafted as a place to prototype and test new design methods and to challenge presumed Subject: fwd talk by prof namrata vaswani iowa state university on at am in the ee committee room
Body: there will be talk on april at am in the ee committee room by prof namrata vaswani professor from iowa state university interested students can attend the talk the title abstract and her cv are given below title byzantineresilient alternating gd and minimization altgdmin for partlydecoupled federated low rank matrix learning and applications in mri namrata vaswani iowa state university abstract modern distributed and federated learning systems are vulnerable to various kinds of adversarial attacks byzantine attacks are one of the most difficult attacks to deal with since the adversarial nodes are omniscient know everything about all nodes’ algorithms and node outputs at each algorithm iteration and can collude we introduce provably byzantineresilient algorithms for solving three different vertically federated learning lowrank lr matrix learning problems – lr matrix completion lr columnwise sensing and lr phase retrieval – all of which involve solving a partlydecoupled optimization problem and all involve dealing with data heterogeneity across nodes these problems find important applications in recommender system design multitask representation learning for fewshot learning federated sketching accelerated dynamic mri and fourier ptychography our proposed algorithms byzaltgdmin are provably byzantineresilient modifications of alternating gd and minimization altgdmin altgdmin introduced in our recent work is a novel faster and more communicationefficient alternative to alternating minimization altmin for partlydecoupled optimization problems these are problems in which the set of optimization variables can be split into two subsets such that the optimization with respect to at least one subset keeping the other fixed is decoupled if time permits we will also show realdata experimental results on the advantage speed and generality of altgdminbased methods over the existing stateoftheart within dynamic mri based on “byzantine resilient and fast federated fewshot learning” icml and “a simple proof for efficient federated low rank matrix recovery from columnwise linear projections” ieee trans information theory “fast low rank columnwise compressive sensing for accelerated dynamic mri” ieee trans computational imaging bio namrata vaswani received a phd from the university of maryland college park umd in and a btech from iitdelhi in india in since fall she has been with the iowa state university where she is currently the anderlik professor of electrical and computer engineering her research interests lie in data science with a particular focus on statistical machine learning and signal processing she also directs the cymath stem graduate student led k math tutoring program vaswani has served as an associate editor area editor or guest editor for the ieee transactions on information theory ieee transactions on signal processing the ieee signal processing magazine and proceedings of the ieee she is a recipient of the ieee signal processing society best paper award the umd ece distinguished alumni award and the iowa state midcareer achievement in research award vaswani is an aaas fellow class of and an ieee fellow class of best wishes prof shankar prakriya

Subject: gentle reminder for me guest talk artificial intelligence for fluid simulations some exciting new avenues by prof hs udaykumar
Body: dear all this is a gentle reminder for the me guest talk on thursday th march by dr h s udaykumar roy j carver professor of mechanical engineering associate dean for research and faculty university of iowa usa in the department of mechanical engineering date and time thursday march from pm to pm venue me seminar room block details for attending online link to ms teams meeting meeting id passcode kj jr pz title artificial intelligence for fluid simulations some exciting new avenues abstract with the exponential growth more appropriately resurgence of artificial intelligence ai there are myriad ways in which ai has been making inroads into physics simulation and analysis while ai particularly in its most recent incarnation via deep neural networks has penetrated into various fields of application in two primary forms large language models and convolutional neural networks which form the bases for narrow ai by suitably combining these two forms of ai models there is now a rapidly growing field of application of machine learning and ai to understand simulate and analyze physics problems including the evolution of vector fields application of ai to physical problems demands specialization and adaptation to ensure that physical constraints conservation laws constitutive laws boundary conditions are respected this has led to several types of padl physicsaware deep learning approaches such as pinns neural operators etc in this talk i will show ways in which ai techniques have been incorporated into learning and predicting an archetypal complex physics problem namely compressible multimaterial reactive flow i will highlight areas of success and point to shortcomings and areas for improvement and extensions brief introduction of the speaker udaykumar is roy j carver professor of mechanical engineering and associate dean for graduate programs research and faculty at the university of iowa his research focus is on modeling and simulation of moving boundary problems in thermomechanical systems ranging from phase change thermal storage biomedical applications involving cardiovascular and gastrointestinal mechanics energetic material dynamics in propulsion and munitions and multiphase flows he has published over journal papers in varied topic areas of biomedical and mechanical engineering he has been supported by grants from nsf whitaker foundation biomedical engineering grant nih doe va research grants and various dod agencies udaykumar serves on various universitylevel committees and is also an invited participant in dod visioning workshops such as the arl disruptive energetics farterm tech forecasting workshop multiple years a member of the organizing committee for the aps shock compression conference and a member of the advisory board Subject: expert talk on perovskite solar cells a journey from to bifacial perovskite photovoltaic device
Body: dear colleaguesstudents you are all cordially invited for the expert talk titled metal oxide on halide perovskites a journey from to bifacial perovskite photovoltaic device by prof shaibal k sarkar department of energy science and engineering indian institute of technology bombay date th march friday from pm venue dept of energy science and engineering committee room blockv nd floor room no abstract hole transport layer htl in halide perovskite solar cells has three significant criteria to fulfil a carrier selectivity through adequate bandmatching while minimizing the overpotential loss b better carrier mobility to avoid interfacial recombination and minorly c optical transparency in the visible spectral regime a thin metal oxide film can address these challenges by providing a stable and efficient hole transport pathway however processinduced interfacial damage remains a significant concern such damage can deteriorate the contact quality reduce charge extraction efficiency and compromise the longterm operational stability of the device overcoming these issues requires advanced fabrication techniques that preserve interface integrity while leveraging the benefits of metal oxidebased htls in this presentation i aim to explore the materialmethod relationship that has driven a remarkable leap in device efficiency—from a modest to an impressive bifacial— while final evaluation has been completed course coordinators approval is not required for course audit or withdrawal kindly complete the auditwithdrawal of courses within the timeline provisions related to auditing courses are applicable only as per the coursesofstudy for ug students audit is possible upto a limited number of credits for electives only pg students do not get credit for audited courses credits can i audit my current extra hu course ans yes please raise a studentgeneralrequest i audited many courses during the covidaffected semesters are they counted in the credit limit ans no they are not counted courses audited during the five semesters between jan and may are not counted in the credit audit limit i have already credited sufficient de courses can i audit an extra one ans yes Subject: me guest talk by dr h s udaykumar roy j carver professor of mechanical engineering associate dean for research and faculty university of iowa usa
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the seminar by dr h s udaykumar roy j carver professor of mechanical engineering associate dean for research and faculty university of iowa usa scheduled on thursday th march in the department of mechanical engineering at indian institute of technology iit delhi date and time thursday march from pm to pm venue me seminar room block title artificial intelligence for fluid simulations some exciting new avenues abstract with the exponential growth more appropriately resurgence of artificial intelligence ai there are myriad ways in which ai has been making inroads into physics simulation and analysis while ai particularly in its most recent incarnation via deep neural networks has penetrated into various fields of application in two primary forms large language models and convolutional neural networks which form the bases for narrow ai by suitably combining these two forms of ai models there is now a rapidly growing field of application of machine learning and ai to understand simulate and analyze physics problems including the evolution of vector fields application of ai to physical problems demands specialization and adaptation to ensure that physical constraints conservation laws constitutive laws boundary conditions are respected this has led to several types of padl physicsaware deep learning approaches such as pinns neural operators etc in this talk i will show ways in which ai techniques have been incorporated into learning and predicting an archetypal complex physics problem namely compressible multimaterial reactive flow i will highlight areas of success and point to shortcomings and areas for improvement and extensions brief introduction of the speaker udaykumar is roy j carver professor of mechanical engineering and associate dean for graduate programs research and faculty at the university of iowa his research focus is on modeling and simulation of moving boundary problems in thermomechanical systems ranging from phase change thermal storage biomedical applications involving cardiovascular and gastrointestinal mechanics energetic material dynamics in propulsion and munitions and multiphase flows he has published over journal papers in varied topic areas of biomedical and mechanical engineering he has been supported by grants from nsf whitaker foundation biomedical engineering grant nih doe va research grants and various dod agencies udaykumar serves on various universitylevel committees and is also an invited participant in dod visioning workshops such as the arl disruptive energetics farterm tech forecasting workshop multiple years a member of the organizing committee for the aps shock compression conference and a member of the advisory board Subject: me guest talk by dr h s udaykumar roy j carver professor of mechanical engineering associate dean for research and faculty university of iowa usa
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the seminar by dr h s udaykumar roy j carver professor of mechanical engineering associate dean for research and faculty university of iowa usa scheduled on thursday th march in the department of mechanical engineering at indian institute of technology iit delhi date and time monday march from pm to pm venue me seminar room block title artificial intelligence for fluid simulations some exciting new avenues abstract with the exponential growth more appropriately resurgence of artificial intelligence ai there are myriad ways in which ai has been making inroads into physics simulation and analysis while ai particularly in its most recent incarnation via deep neural networks has penetrated into various fields of application in two primary forms large language models and convolutional neural networks which form the bases for narrow ai by suitably combining these two forms of ai models there is now a rapidly growing field of application of machine learning and ai to understand simulate and analyze physics problems including the evolution of vector fields application of ai to physical problems demands specialization and adaptation to ensure that physical constraints conservation laws constitutive laws boundary conditions are respected this has led to several types of padl physicsaware deep learning approaches such as pinns neural operators etc in this talk i will show ways in which ai techniques have been incorporated into learning and predicting an archetypal complex physics problem namely compressible multimaterial reactive flow i will highlight areas of success and point to shortcomings and areas for improvement and extensions brief introduction of the speaker udaykumar is roy j carver professor of mechanical engineering and associate dean for graduate programs research and faculty at the university of iowa his research focus is on modeling and simulation of moving boundary problems in thermomechanical systems ranging from phase change thermal storage biomedical applications involving cardiovascular and gastrointestinal mechanics energetic material dynamics in propulsion and munitions and multiphase flows he has published over journal papers in varied topic areas of biomedical and mechanical engineering he has been supported by grants from nsf whitaker foundation biomedical engineering grant nih doe va research grants and various dod agencies udaykumar serves on various universitylevel committees and is also an invited participant in dod visioning workshops such as the arl disruptive energetics farterm tech forecasting workshop multiple years a member of the organizing committee for the aps shock compression conference and a member of the advisory board for the propellants explosives and pyrotechnics journal all interested are welcome to join the talk thank you abhishek das and pratik das department of mechanical engineering iit delhi hauz khas new bangalore on th march his research interests include activation of small molecules using organometallic compounds homogeneous catalysis and molecular precursors for certain materials materials for hydrogen storage and hydrogen generation and catalysis the details of the seminar are as follows date th march monday venue lh time pm high tea pm talk title digestive ripening facilitated nanoengineering of diverse bimetallic nanostructured materials abstract solvated metal atom dispersion smad together with digestive ripening transform colloids comprised of metal nanoparticles of broad size distribution nearly monodisperse our group exploited the strengths of this combination of synthetic methodologies to realize nearly monodisperse nanoparticles of a wide variety of metals mg ca mn fe co pd cu ag au al in and eu in the past bimetallic nanostructures of metals are especially interesting as they exhibit synergistic properties arising from their monometallic counterparts and hence offer the possibility to integrate and modulate them as required codigestive ripening has emerged as an excellent synthetic strategy to realize shape and sizecontrolled colloidal bimetallic nanostructures in this regard our group prepared a wide array of bimetallic heterostructures such as coreshell composites alloy and intermetallic nanoparticles using this strategy detailed mechanistic insights into the formation of such novel structures have also been established some of the bimetallic nanosystems prepared by codigestive ripening method displayed exquisite catalytic activities bringing out the synergism of the constituents of such systems our group has also been working on developing tandem catalysts for dehydrogenation and hydrogenation of certain organic compounds in an effort to use liquid organic hydrogen carriers lohc as storehouses of hydrogen in this talk our contributions toward the exploits of smad and digestive ripening for realizing various nanostructured Subject: talk on international day of happiness at pm th march in lh
Body: dear team this is a request to communicate a talk on international day of happiness at pm th march in lh the united nations proclaimed march th as the international day of happiness in the date was chosen to coincide with the march equinox symbolising balance and harmony key themes for achieving happiness on this occasion of the international day of happiness we invite you for a talk by dr satinder singh rekhi who works to promote happiness in academic setups across the universities globally his foundation has also funded a mind lab for research on the science of happiness at iit delhi which will be formally inaugurated on this day below are the details of the talk title of talk taming the monkey mind venue lh time pm date th march about the speaker dr satinder singh rekhi is the founder of the rekhi happiness foundation which has set up more than academic centres for studying happiness in universities across the globe he is an electrical engineer graduate from the indian institute of technology kharagpur and has a masters degree in business from california state university he is the founder of r systems he was awarded the distinguished alumni award from iit kharagpur he was also awarded the presidents gold medal from california state university he is an honorary chairman of the rekhi centre of excellence for the science of happiness indian institute of technology kharagpur he is also the international advisor to the gross national happiness center bhutan he works with academic institutes across the globe to set up centres of happiness and mind labs for the scientific pursuit and understanding of happiness he is actively engaged in teaching and conducting workshops on happiness abstract of the talk the human mind often behaves like a monkey mind jumping from one thought to another this mind plays a key role in experiencing happiness can better awareness of the way the mind functions lead to a happier life can one learn to manage the brain for better contentment and happiness how does the brain create unnecessary stress can happiness be made a priority for our brains these are some topics which this talk will explore regards jyoti

Subject: talk and campus treewalk on citizen science and biodiversity
Body: hi all with so many campus trees in spring bloom undergoing a makeover and birds feasting on the many fruits on offer its time to reacquaint ourselves with the nature around us dr geetha ramaswami an ecologist at the nature conservation foundation will give a talk on citizen science and biodiversity on saturday march nd at am the talk will happen online at details below this will be followed with a treewalk on campus the next morning march rd sunday at am led by our very own professor ashwini vaidya the assembly point for the walk is the neelkanth hall in the old campus east side please fill this form to register talk people technology scale great science citizen science is a revolutionary way of democratising the process of knowledge creation in citizen science nonprofessionals can ask scientific questions design scientific studies collect curate and analyse data and devise solutions to these questions in this talk i will give an overview of citizen science in india and some reallife problems that odd years of communitycontributed data have helped address bio geetha leads seasonwatch a citizen science project looking at the effects of seasons on tree phenology since march in the past i have been a postdoctoral research associate with the nature conservation foundation with an interest in invasive plants i worked on an invasive plant lantana camara for my phd trying to understand how the environment affects where and how this species spreads and also how indigenous species respond to the presence of this invasive plant i later worked on a short project assessing the reasons by which the management of lantana has largely failed in indian forests i currently work on understanding the impacts of lantana on native plantdisperser interactions a side note we have a mailing list on campus for bird watching tree walks and such nature based activities weve not been very active lately but with more interest and excitement from everyone well Subject: new flavor of ell online learning online algorithms
Body: dear students if you intrigued by the challenge of making optimal decisions without knowing the future i invite you to join the upcoming online learning course ell next semester where we will dive deep into online algorithms — a powerful framework for decisionmaking under uncertainty important note unlike previous offerings of this course that focused on bandit frameworks this years offering will mainly focus on online algorithms some problems that we will tackle are the skirental problem when should you buy versus rent to minimize longterm costs without knowing how long youll need the skis the secretary problem how do you hire the best candidate when you must make an irreversible decision on the spot the bin packing problem how can you efficiently pack objects of varying sizes into bins as they arrive in sequence the adwords problem how should an advertiser dynamically bid for ad slots to maximize visibility while staying within budget despite uncertainty in future bids these problems and more will be discussed in light of competitive analysis and realworld applications from ecommerce pricing strategies to online caching to wireless communications and beyond if youre interested in algorithmic decisionmaking theoretical foundations with practical impact or just enjoy tackling intellectually stimulating problems this course is for you looking forward to seeing many of you in the class regards gourab

Subject: bioinspired fluidstructure interactions institute seminar on th march pm lh
Body: dear students and colleagues we are delighted to invite you to this interesting institute seminar title bioinspired fluidstructure interactions from waveassisted propulsion to agile flight with membrane wings speaker prof rajat mittal johns hopkins university md usa venue lhc time pm to pm march abstract the continuous advancement of computational power coupled with new software tools and numerical algorithms is opening novel avenues for research exploration and applications at the intersection of computational fluid and structural mechanics waveassisted propulsion wap systems utilizing elastically mounted hydrofoils provide a simple way of converting wave energy into thrust nature excels at utilizing soft materials and structures that bend deform and stretch as they interact with the environment and much can be learnt from analyzing the performance of natures devices for instance fish leverage their remarkably flexible bodies and fins to harness energy from flow and vortices propelling themselves with an elegance and efficiency that confounds engineers bats fly with unparalleled agility and speed by using their flexible membrane wings each of these problems involves a complex and elegant interplay between fluid dynamics and structural mechanics historically investigations into such phenomena were constrained by available tools but computational advancements now facilitate exploration of these multiphysics problems with an unprecedented level of fidelity precision and realism in my presentation i will discuss several projects that harness the capabilities of highfidelity sharpinterface immersed boundary methods to address problems in engineering and biology involving fluidstructure interaction bio of the speaker rajat mittal is a professor of mechanical engineering at johns hopkins university with a secondary appointment in the school of medicine he earned his btech from the indian institute of technology kanpur in an ms in aerospace engineering from the university of florida and a phd in applied mechanics from the university of illinois at urbanachampaign in mittal conducted postdoctoral research at the center for turbulence research at stanford university focusing on largeeddy simulation he began his teaching career at the university of florida in and was a faculty member at george washington university from to since he has been a professor at johns hopkins university his research spans computational fluid dynamics vortexdominated flows biomedical engineering biological fluid dynamics fluidstructure interaction and flow control he has received several prestigious awards including the francois frenkiel and stanley corrsin awards from the aps division of fluid dynamics as well as the lewis moody and freeman scholar awards from asme he is a fellow of asme aps and aimbe and an associate fellow of aiaa mittal is an associate editor of the journal of computational physics and frontiers of computational physiology and medicine and serves on the editorial boards of the international journal for numerical methods in biomedical engineering and physics of fluids we look forward to your enthusiastic Subject: dont have time to figure out fusion
Body: hey ​ most resolve editors i talk to have one big burning question on their mind… ​ “how will i ever find the time to learn fusion”​ ​ i bet you’ve asked yourself this at least once before right ​ look i get it ​ fusion feels so intimidating most editors just pretend it doesn’t even exist… ​ it’s just like the weird guy at the bus stop they avoid making eye contact with ​ here’s the top things about fusion that overwhelm most people… ​ redcircle nodes seriously nodes what the heck are those things ​ redcircle there are two screens in fusion… why ​ redcircle no layers how the heck am i supposed to make anything cool without layers like in adobe after effects or photoshop ​ redcircle keyframes and animation there’s no timeline how do i animate stuff​ ​ ​ of course you could poke around and figure it all out on your own… if only you had the time ​ but with all the cutting up footage colour grading adding captions most editors are racing against the clock as it is ​ heres the thing – all of those things are actually pretty simple to learn and understand when you have the right guide seriously ​ that’s what we do here at ground control ​ our goal is to get all that junk out of the way as soon as possible and replace all those worries and fears with confidence ​ checkmarkbutton nodes these little buggers seem so scary right now but before long you’ll actually love them and start to prefer them as a way of working with images seriously it happens all the time ​ checkmarkbutton screens the two viewers in fusion are like hands you can pick up any node and take a closer look by just loading it into the viewer ​ checkmarkbutton no layers even though there isn’t a “layers panel” on the interface we’re still working with layers we’re still putting images over other images it’s just a little different interface when this clicks so much stuff gets easier in fusion ​ checkmarkbutton animation fusion is actually really great with animations but the interface doesn’t Subject: defeat the haunted house of fusion
Body: “i never thought i’d be able to do this” ​ this is the kind of thing i hear a lot from our students ​ see most resolve editors look at the fusion page like a haunted house from the movies ​ it’s big it’s scary and you would much rather go home and keep leading your normal life than to set foot inside ​ and i get it the fusion page feels so different than the other pages of resolve there’s screens for some reason there’s no timeline and what the heck are these node thingys ​ ​ muahahahahaha abandon all hope ye who enter the fusion page ​ but fusion doesn’t have to be so intimidating ​ here’s what tony had to say after taking one of our courses… ​ fusion was a nightmare before discovering caseys channel using his videos i was able to follow along and just copypaste fusion comps and learn some stuff for myself too i knew i had to buy this course and i do not regret it i am now excited to dive into the fusion page not only for the course but for my own projects as well this course took a fear in resolve and turned it into a very enjoyable creative outlet for me tony g ground control student ​ but how do we take someone who’s deathly afraid of fusion and make it enjoyable to them ​ easy we teach you fusion by not teaching you fusion ​ no i didn’t forget to take my meds again… lemme explain ​ when you learn a piece of software you can learn what all the buttons do how to open and organize a project even how to make some cool stuff by following along with tutorials… ​ but you don’t truly learn to make your own creations with it until you learn the concepts behind what you’re doing ​ the concepts are the key ​ the concepts are the little reasons and thinking that tell you why to click the buttons and which buttons to click ​ take cooking for example… i love food metaphors ​ an accomplished chef doesn’t just know how to crack an egg set the stove to medium heat use a whisk etc he knows why it’s best to use medium heat why it’s important to add grease to the pan and what changes he could make to the whole process to get a different kind of egg dish ​ and all that knowledge is easily transferable to just about any other kind of food as well ​ this is the kind of mindset we’re building in our students who want to learn fusion ​ we don’t teach fusion if we did it’d be “click this slider add this node” booorinnggg ​ instead we show you the concept of masking why would you mask something what’s the point how are masks used in a variety of workflows ​ and it’s crazy because the technical steps click this button add this node are easy once you learn why you need to use a certain technique ​ in fact and this is crazy but we start to see students just guess how to do something technical after we help them understand the concepts and they’re usually right ​ that means they’re actually learning more than we’re teaching isn’t that nuts ​ i love this so much ​ want to learn more about the concepts of visual effects ​ ​ heres a full minute presentation i gave at resolvecon ​ ​ ​ its not a short video but its packed with wisdom and its been an inspiration for so many people ​ so go grab your favourite mug make yourself some coffee and sit back relax and let the knowledge sink in ​ talk soon ​ casey ​ ps any concepts about fusion you’re especially confused about ​ hit reply and let me know tomorrow i’ll be diving into all the confusing things that make video editors stay away from fusion youre receiving this email because youve signed up for updates and marketing emails from groundcontrolfilm we make awesome davinci resolve fusion courses but we dont want our emails to be a bummer ​ only want occasional emails about sales and announcements let us know here and well take you off our regular emails list ​ ​ Subject: rd acl decision on book borrowing facility from any unit library
Body: the acl in its rd meeting held on has decided the following with reference to the above cited subject book borrowing facility from any unit library acl members were of the opinion that many unit libraries are nonfunctional and do not have much usage the facultystudent and staff of the institute should have the facility to borrow the books from any unit library the librarian shared the following procedureguidelines for borrowing books from any unit libraries central library will coordinate with unit libraries for borrowing books the users request to borrow books from unit libraries will be processed within days users can request any books from the unit libraries for borrowing through the central library at the circulation counter upon receiving the request from the users central library will request the hodincharge of the unit library to transfer the requested books to central library for a limited period of time once the books are received from the unit library central library will inform the concerned user and the book will be issued to the user through central librarys koha software as per the existing circulation policy users will only return such books to the central library at the circulation counter central library will maintain the records and ensure that books are transferred back to the respective unit libraries once they are returned the acl appreciated this initiative and approved the proposal the members also suggested that the library should make efforts to implement koha software including the books borrowing facility module in all the unit libraries in view of the above all the unit libraries are requested to support and cooperate in this endeavour and facilitate the book borrowing facility amongst the unit libraries dr nabi hasan librarian head central library membersecretary acl circulation acl all faculty students and staff through circular mail

Subject: civil engineering seminar series prof matt wilson from university of canterbury new zealand scheduled on monday th march at noon
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the civil engineering seminar by professor matt wilson director of the geospatial research institute toi hangarau and professor in the school of earth and environment university of canterbury new zealand scheduled on monday th march at noon in committee room block iv room no department of civil engineering at indian institute of technology iit delhi title of the seminar mapping waters future advances in geospatial technology for smarter surface water management abstract of the seminar water is a critical resource for humanity yet its management faces major challenges with droughts floods and declining water quality all becoming increasingly prevalent in this talk he will present examples of recent advances in geospatial technology which present opportunities to rise to these challenges drawing from four areas of research within the geospatial research institute at the university of canterbury new zealand digital twins close the gap between data and decisionmakers enabling integration from multiple data sources including realtime data and rapid analysis on demand he will present their flood resilience digital twin which automates the flood assessment process to empower decision makers for improved flood risk management such developments can form part of a digital twin ecosystem whereby multiple systems can share data and analysis to solve critical environmental and social issues advanced visualization can help public engagement with analysis of environmental issues for example to illustrate scenarios of future urban development or environmental restoration he will demonstrate their use of virtual reality technology to visualize scenarios of flooding to help communities better understand their risks geospatial artificial intelligence is enabling us to make more effective use of the everincreasing amounts of spatial data particularly from remote sensing targeting issues for positive environmental and social impacts we need to develop robust algorithms towards effective solutions for local to global impacts he will provide examples of how they are doing this for applications in support of our digital twin development advances in remote sensing is rapidly increasing the amount of data available for water resource assessments providing excellent synoptic coverage the forthcoming nisar mission shows considerable promise for high spatial resolution soil moisture retrievals with observations available on day revisit interval global navigation satellite system reflectometry gnssr based on the sensing of reflected signals of opportunity can help to fill temporal gaps in these data he will introduce new zealands rongowai airborne remote sensing mission which comprises of a nextgeneration gnssr receiver mounted on a domestic air new zealand q commercial aircraft and the processing of these data into estimates of surface inundation and soil moisture he will conclude with a vision for how each of these areas can be combined towards addressing the critical global challenges of climate change and biodiversity loss and their implications for environmental and human wellbeing biographical sketch of the speaker matthew wilson is the director of the geospatial research institute and a professor in the school of earth and environment his research is in the broad areas of hydrology and geographical information science with a primary focus in the assessment of flood risk using computational modelling and geospatial analysis techniques and the assessment of uncertainty he is particularly interested in the use of remote sensing and machine learning methods within environmental analyses matt is part of the rongowai team developing algorithms for assessing surface water from remote sensing signals obtained from an air new zealand q aircraft he is leading the development of environmental digital twins which automate complex analytical processes using disparate data particularly those from remote sensing building on a successful prototype current research is embedding naturebased scenarios for flood mitigation within automated modelling of flooding enabling communitycentered risk assessments in related work he is using virtual reality to communicate the implications of flooding for communities all interested are cordially invited to attend the seminar thank you head department of civil engineering room no blockiv indian institute of technology iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india email telephone secretary telephone direct

Subject: ieor seminar series talk by dr rajan batta on march
Body: dear all we welcome you to another interesting session as a part of the industrial engineering and operations research ieor seminar series our next speaker is dr rajan batta suny distinguished professor department of industrial and systems engineering university at buffalo buffalo new york usa please find details about the talk and the speaker below date and time monday march from am to am venue me seminar room block title uav search and routing planning in a disaster area abstract this talk starts by discussing the search and routing planning srp problem for an unmanned aerial vehicle uav to maximize the total number of casualties detected in a disasteraffected area within a limited mission duration first a mixedinteger nonlinear programming minlp model is formulated to linearize the model continuous search time variables are discretized such that each can only take a finite number of possible values therefore the resulting mixed integer linear programming milp problem approximates the original problem this approximation is shown to be highly accurate however it cannot solve problems with more than search regions in less than three hours second an exact solution approach is introduced which can solve problems of size or smaller during the given computational time limit next an efficient clustering heuristic is suggested to solve larger instances of the original problem with more than search regions finally a case study based on the turkeysyria earthquakes is presented the results reveal despite thousands of casualties remaining missing for weeks in the reallife scenario the proposed solution methods can help detect of casualties within a few hours in provinces under study following the analysis of the single vehicle problem several steps are currently being undertaken to enhance the model these include modeling uncertainty in the number of casualties in each region using multiple uavs to achieve the search mission and incorporation cooperation between the uavs to enhance the search process details of these steps will also be shared in the talk biography dr rajan batta is a suny distinguished professor in the department of industrial and systems engineering at the university at buffalo usa he works on search and reconnaissance problems he also works on supply chain design problems both in the contexts of humanitarian logistics and manufacturing systems he is a fellow of the institute of industrial and systems engineers iise and the institute for operations research and the management sciences informs he has been the recipient of several research awards he has received iises highest award the frank and lillian gilbreth industrial engineering award he has also twice received the koopman prize from informs military and security society another recent award from informs is the lifetime achievement award in location analysis thanks and best regards prashant palkar assistant professor ieor department of mechanical engineering iit delhi

Subject: invitation panel discussion on social identities in a changing world
Body: dear all initiative for caste equity ice office of diversity and inclusion iitdelhi is pleased to invite you to a panel discussion by the prof stephen reicher university of st andrews and prof nick hopkins university of dundee on the topic of social identities in a changing world date th march saturday time pm to pm venue senate room iit delhi invitee speakers stephen reicher stephen reicher is professor at the school of psychology and neuroscience university of st andrews prof reicher is a social psychologist focused on social identity processes and collective behavior he has published widely on crowd action leadership nationalism intergroup hatred conformity and the psychology of tyranny he has been a consultant to a wide range of bodies including police agencies the equalities and human rights commission and the scottish and uk governments on a range of topics from social inclusion to behavior in emergencies to public order policing nick hopkins nick hopkins is a senior lecturer in psychology at dundee university and joint editor of the british journal of social psychology nick hopkins focuses on the construction of group identity and its role in organizing group behavior his research includes the identity experiences of british muslims and the social psychology of collective participation especially in mass gatherings such as the magh mela in allahabad india his work is also relevant to the health and wellbeing of participants in such events for registration please fill out the form here regards initiative for caste equity ext forwarded by oo dean diversity inclusion prof angelie multani dean diversity inclusion indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi telephone links

Subject: mathematics colloquium on march thursday at pm in room no academic complex west b
Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department colloquium by prof krishna maddaly ashoka university on march thursday at pm the details are given below title delocalisation in some random operator models speaker prof krishna maddaly ashoka university date march thursday time pm venue room no academic complex west b abstract we consider certain random selfadjoint operators in quantum theory that exhibit dynamical delocalisation specifically we show the existence of states for which the expected values of their positions tend to infinity over time under the evolution generated by these operators this behavior is not possible for eigenstates of any selfadjoint operator on a hilbert space in this sense the spectrum appears to contain more than just the usual eigenvalues this is joint work with peter hislop and werner kirsch best mathematics seminar coordinator

Subject: ieor seminar series talk on march by dr ankur garg air india express
Body: dear all we welcome you to the next industrial engineering and operations research ieor seminar series talk we are happy to invite dr ankur garg from air india express for an ieor talk he will discuss largescale integer programming models solution methodologies and heuristics for scheduling and disruption recovery in the airline industry please find details about the talk and the speaker below date and time thursday march from venue senate room title scheduling models and heuristics in the airline industry abstract like all transportation businesses airlines offer a fertile ground for the application of network models from the field of operations research what makes the application of these optimization models more imperative for the airline industry is the critical need to optimally utilize expensive resources such as aircraft challenges in concurrent availability of different resources including aircraft crew airport slots etc to deliver the service regulations governing each of these resources and the perishable nature of the airline seat inventory therefore the objective of various scheduling models in airlines is to maximize the output of these resources under the constraints that these resources work in sync while being governed by the safety technical or any other operational requirements this session proposed to outline various models applied for commercial and operations planning in the airline industry for the purpose of flight schedule design fleet assignment aircraft scheduling crew scheduling and ground staff scheduling in addition to the above planning models this session also proposes to cover disruption recovery models in airlines on the analytical models and solution approaches this session proposes to cover various types of network formulations such as timespace network and activityonnode networks mathematical formulations involved such as assignment problem setpartitioning problem maximum flow problem and solution methodologies such as column generation lagrangian relaxation benders decomposition and heuristics like grasp to solve these largescale mixed integer programming models biography dr ankur garg is presently serving as chief commercial officer at air india express where he is responsible for network planning revenue management sales distribution marketing and customer experience prior to this dr garg worked with indigo as the vice president of revenue management and ancillary revenue from to before his stint in aviation dr garg spent almost a decade in various roles in management consulting and corporate strategy he holds a btech in production and industrial engineering from iit delhi and a pgdm from iim ahmedabad his deep interest in the area of operations research motivated him to pursue his phd in operations management from iim lucknow while continuing to pursue his professional career ankur continues to balance his professional work and his passion for research in the area of operations management he also takes guest faculty sessions at various business schools on subjects like revenue management scheduling and operations management please see the link below for flyer thanks and best regards prashant palkar assistant professor ieor department of mechanical engineering iit delhi

Subject: reminder seminar adhesion science recent developments and prospects dr kash mittal th march am ii
Body: dear all title adhesion science recent developments and prospects speaker dr kash mittal former editorinchief journal of adhesion science and technology former editorinchief reviews of adhesion and adhesives date march wednesday time am venue me seminar room block ii room abstract the subject of adhesion is veritably inter multi and transdisciplinary and for a holistic approach to adhesion a synergistic interaction is required among the various disciplines involved viz surface chemistry rheology and fracture mechanics even a cursory look at the literature will evince that there has been a quantum jump in our knowledge of why and how things stick together and all signals indicate that this trend will continue unabated there have been recent exciting developments in many facets of adhesion science and a complete discussion of all these will be prohibitively long so in this talk the recent advances in the following areas will be discussed acidbase interactions and their relevance to adhesion investigation of interfacial interactions polymer surface modification coupling agents or adhesion promoters and super hydrophobicity as an epilogue some of the unsolved problems which need intensified rd efforts will be highlighted as for the future of adhesion science the prospects look very bright and the fraternity of adhesionists stickologists will keep on growing at a high pace biographical sketch of dr kashmiri lal mittal dr kashmiri lal mittal was associated with the ibm corporation from through currently he is teaching and consulting worldwide in the broad areas of adhesion as well as surface cleaning he has initiated organized and chaired a large number of international symposia and is the editor of published books dealing inter alia with adhesion measurement adhesion of polymeric coatings polymer surfaces adhesive joints adhesion promoters thin films polyimides surface modification contact angle and wettability surface cleaning and surfactants he has received many awards and honors is a robert l patrick fellow of the adhesion society and is listed in many biographical reference works he was the editorinchief of the international journal of adhesion science and technology until april and ishas been a member of the editorial boards of a number of scientific and technical journals dr mittal was recognized for his contributions and accomplishments by the worldwide adhesion community by organizing in his honor on his th birthday the st international congress on adhesion science technology in amsterdam in papers from countries were presented in he was honored by the global surfactant community by inaugurating the kash mittal award in the surfactant field in his honor for his large efforts and significant contribution to the field of colloid and interface chemistry in he was honored by the maria curieskłodowska university lublin poland by awarding him the title of doctor honoris causa in he was recognized by dedicating volumes of the advances in colloid and interface science in his honor on his th birthday in he was recognized for publication of his edited books by two symposia held in his honor symposium on recent advances in adhesion science and technology held at the american chemical society meeting in boston and symposium on surfactant science and technology retrospects and prospects held in melbourne australia a special issue of colloids and surfaces a vol issues nov was dedicated to him to honor the publication of his th edited book in he was elected an honorary fellow of the indian chemical society also in two books were published in his honor he founded the journal entitled reviews of adhesion and adhesives raa as well as the new book series entitled adhesion and adhesives fundamental and applied aspects he was editorinchief of raa until june best regards sujeet

Subject: uqiitd seminar series talk by dr satish singh iit delhi alumnus
Body: dear all please join us for an insightful session with dr satish singh phd an iitd alumnus and head of drug product development at astria boston the title of the talk is my personal journey from iitd through the pandemic years and the covid vaccine date tuesday th march time pm pm ist pm pm aest venue lh first floor lecture hall complex iit delhi link to join online please see the link below were looking forward to you taking part in this enlightening session best regards abstract life takes us on a journey much as we would like to say that we are in control it is happenstance that often Subject: todays lecture do we fully understand the fundamental electromagnetic interactions institute lecture on rd march pm
Body: reminder for this interesting talk today from pm in lh dear students and colleagues we are delighted to invite you to the th institute lecture of by prof elena besley from the university of nottingham uk on rd march at pm in lh at iit delhi title of the talk do we fully understand the fundamental electromagnetic interactions abstract of the talk when charged interfaces are near touching electrostatic interactions exhibit a counterintuitive behaviour leading to both attractive and repulsive forces regardless of the sign of charge on the interfaces in this talk we will demonstrate and discuss these complex electrostatic phenomena in a variety of physical and chemical scenarios we will further extend these studies to include the casimir effects between near touching neutral interfaces which are quantum mechanical in nature as they stem from the permanent existence of fluctuating fields on either side of the quantum cavity created between the interfaces due to the lack of sophisticated instrumentation capable of measuring these subtle changes in electrostatic and casimir force these effects remained experimentally elusive for many years drawing little interest outside the theoretical community however with the recent rise of research in highresolution force measurements plasmonics and metamaterials the explosive potential of the electrostatic and casimir effects has become apparent showing that these forces can be manipulated and investigated at the unprecedented level of accuracy and versatility about the speaker elena besley frsc is professor of theoretical and computational chemistry and head of materials chemistry at the university of nottingham united kingdom she holds a royal society wolfson fellowship awarded to internationally leading outstanding senior scientists to support their research in the uk besleyâ€ trademark s theoretical and computational work has made a broad general impact across multiple and diverse disciplines in chemical sciences she has developed theoretical methods which have transformed our fundamental understanding of electrostatic phenomena in the gas phase plasmas and solvents her pioneering modelling studies of electron and ionbeam induced irradiation of nanostructures significantly aided the advancement of stateoftheart imaging techniques further notable research achievements include effective computational solutions to gas storage and the control of chemical hierarchy reactivity and interactions within designer porous materials and advances in fundamental understanding of the complex patterns emerging in packing of elastically deformable nanomaterials and their adsorption on surfaces prof e besley received numerous recognitions including outstanding female scientist and scholar â€œacademianet profiles of leading women scientistsâ€ epsrc career acceleration fellowship and epsrc research leaders awards erc consolidator grant royal society leverhulme trust senior research fellowship her profile was included in the new feature â€œphysical chemistry people and perspectivesâ€ of the th edition of atkinsâ€ trademark physical chemistry textbook elena besley is associate editor of nano letters for the body of work which will be presented at the iit delhi institute lecture prof besley received a lifetime achievement award from the electrostatics society of america the award reads â€œpresented to elena besley for her outstanding contributions to the field of electrostatics especially in development of theories in charged interactions and their applications the friendly society offers you this token of our admiration and gratitudeâ€ we look forward to your enthusiastic participation and an overall enriching experience regards shilpi sharma associate dean academics outreach Subject: reminder inae talk at department of civil engg
Body: dear all delhi chapter of indian national academy of engineering inae and department of civil engineering at indian institute of technology iit delhi are jointly organizing a talk in a hybrid mode on monday rd march from to ist title sensors sensing and society engineering a sustainable and resilient future abstract engineering plays a fundamental role in tackling global challenges from climate change to digital transformation at the heart of these solutions lies the advancement of sensors and sensing technologies which serve as the foundation for intelligent systems that shape modern society as highlighted in the ukris tomorrows engineering research challenges terc report the future of engineering will be defined by how effectively we harness these technologies to drive sustainability resilience and societal wellbeing this talk will explore how sensing technologies are transforming engineering research and its impact across sectors by focusing on three critical areas environmental sensing and net zero goal humancentric sensing for health and wellbeing and sensing for digital and physical infrastructure however the increasing reliance on sensing technologies also raises questions around data ethics accessibility and security how do we ensure that sensordriven decisionmaking remains transparent inclusive and aligned with societal values by positioning sensors and sensing as a cornerstone of engineering innovation this presentation calls for a multidisciplinary collaborative approach to research and development engineering solutions must integrate insights from computing materials science and social sciences to create systems that are not only technologically advanced but also socially responsible through realworld case studies and forwardlooking discussions this session will emphasize the need for a new engineering paradigmone that leverages sensing technologies to drive sustainability inclusivity and societal impact biography of the speaker elena is a professor of pervasive computing and associate provicechancellor for research at coventry university uk her work concerns the inception of sensorbased systems to resolve applications where i wireless transmission of datainformationknowledge is essential and ii the application needs are as such that intelligent processing of data at source sensing point is critical in order to enable robust and ethical decision making prof elenas research draws from computer science engineering and social sciences in particular she worked for several years on devising machine learning techniques to support knowledge extraction from data in real time on resource constrained devices she takes whole system and whole society approaches to her research she is a fellow of the uks womens engineering society is the national director for the uks doctoral training alliance and an honorary professor at several universities prof elena serves in the humanitarian engineering energy sectors bodies and leads projects that engage communities with renewable technologies in the global south as pathways to empowerment and employment her goal is to reflect on the value of sensors in the most constrained sociotechnical systems and leverage their potential towards a better society prof elena believes in the power of data and our unlimited ability to extract actionable knowledge from it please see the Subject: seminar adhesion science recent developments and prospects dr kash mittal th march am ii
Body: dear all title adhesion science recent developments and prospects speaker dr kash mittal former editorinchief journal of adhesion science and technology former editorinchief reviews of adhesion and adhesives date march wednesday time am venue me seminar room block ii room abstract the subject of adhesion is veritably inter multi and transdisciplinary and for a holistic approach to adhesion a synergistic interaction is required among the various disciplines involved viz surface chemistry rheology and fracture mechanics even a cursory look at the literature will evince that there has been a quantum jump in our knowledge of why and how things stick together and all signals indicate that this trend will continue unabated there have been recent exciting developments in many facets of adhesion science and a complete discussion of all these will be prohibitively long so in this talk the recent advances in the following areas will be discussed acidbase interactions and their relevance to adhesion investigation of interfacial interactions polymer surface modification coupling agents or adhesion promoters and super hydrophobicity as an epilogue some of the unsolved problems which need intensified rd efforts will be highlighted as for the future of adhesion science the prospects look very bright and the fraternity of adhesionists stickologists will keep on growing at a high pace biographical sketch of dr kashmiri lal mittal dr kashmiri lal mittal was associated with the ibm corporation from through currently he is teaching and consulting worldwide in the broad areas of adhesion as well as surface cleaning he has initiated organized and chaired a large number of international symposia and is the editor of published books dealing inter alia with adhesion measurement adhesion of polymeric coatings polymer surfaces adhesive joints adhesion promoters thin films polyimides surface modification contact angle and wettability surface cleaning and surfactants he has received many awards and honors is a robert l patrick fellow of the adhesion society and is listed in many biographical reference works he was the editorinchief of the international journal of adhesion science and technology until april and ishas been a member of the editorial boards of a number of scientific and technical journals dr mittal was recognized for his contributions and accomplishments by the worldwide adhesion community by organizing in his honor on his th birthday the st international congress on adhesion science technology in amsterdam in papers from countries were presented in he was honored by the global surfactant community by inaugurating the kash mittal award in the surfactant field in his honor for his large efforts and significant contribution to the field of colloid and interface chemistry in he was honored by the maria curieskłodowska university lublin poland by awarding him the title of doctor honoris causa in he was recognized by dedicating volumes of the advances in colloid and interface science in his honor on his th birthday in he was recognized for publication of his edited books by two symposia held in his honor symposium on recent advances in adhesion science and technology held at the american chemical society meeting in boston and symposium on surfactant science and technology retrospects and prospects held in melbourne australia a special issue of colloids and surfaces a vol issues nov was dedicated to him to honor the publication of his th edited book in he was elected an honorary fellow of the indian chemical society also in two books were published in his honor he founded the journal entitled reviews of adhesion and adhesives raa as well as the new book series entitled adhesion and adhesives fundamental and applied aspects he was editorinchief of raa until june best regards sujeet

Subject: do we fully understand the fundamental electromagnetic interactions institute lecture on rd march pm
Body: dear students and colleagues we are delighted to invite you to the th institute lecture of by prof elena besley from the university of nottingham uk on rd march at pm in lh at iit delhi title of the talk do we fully understand the fundamental electromagnetic interactions abstract of the talk when charged interfaces are near touching electrostatic interactions exhibit a counterintuitive behaviour leading to both attractive and repulsive forces regardless of the sign of charge on the interfaces in this talk we will demonstrate and discuss these complex electrostatic phenomena in a variety of physical and chemical scenarios we will further extend these studies to include the casimir effects between near touching neutral interfaces which are quantum mechanical in nature as they stem from the permanent existence of fluctuating fields on either side of the quantum cavity created between the interfaces due to the lack of sophisticated instrumentation capable of measuring these subtle changes in electrostatic and casimir force these effects remained experimentally elusive for many years drawing little interest outside the theoretical community however with the recent rise of research in highresolution force measurements plasmonics and metamaterials the explosive potential of the electrostatic and casimir effects has become apparent showing that these forces can be manipulated and investigated at the unprecedented level of accuracy and versatility about the speaker elena besley frsc is professor of theoretical and computational chemistry and head of materials chemistry at the university of nottingham united kingdom she holds a royal society wolfson fellowship awarded to internationally leading outstanding senior scientists to support their research in the uk besley’s theoretical and computational work has made a broad general impact across multiple and diverse disciplines in chemical sciences she has developed theoretical methods which have transformed our fundamental understanding of electrostatic phenomena in the gas phase plasmas and solvents her pioneering modelling studies of electron and ionbeam induced irradiation of nanostructures significantly aided the advancement of stateoftheart imaging techniques further notable research achievements include effective computational solutions to gas storage and the control of chemical hierarchy reactivity and interactions within designer porous materials and advances in fundamental understanding of the complex patterns emerging in packing of elastically deformable nanomaterials and their adsorption on surfaces prof e besley received numerous recognitions including outstanding female scientist and scholar “academianet profiles of leading women scientists” epsrc career acceleration fellowship and epsrc research leaders awards erc consolidator grant royal society leverhulme trust senior research fellowship her profile was included in the new feature “physical chemistry people and perspectives” of the th edition of atkins’ physical chemistry textbook elena besley is associate editor of nano letters for the body of work which will be presented at the iit delhi institute lecture prof besley received a lifetime achievement award from the electrostatics society of america the award reads “presented to elena besley for her outstanding contributions to the field of electrostatics especially in development of theories in charged interactions and their applications the friendly society offers you this token of our admiration and gratitude” we look forward to your enthusiastic participation and an overall enriching experience regards shilpi sharma associate dean academics outreach new initiatives batch of chair professor department of biochemical engineering and biotechnology indian institute of technology delhi new delhi india

Subject: dmse seminar talk by prof bhaskaran muralidharan iit bombay on th february pm
Body: hi everyone prof bhaskaran muralidharan from iit bombay is scheduled to present his work on monday february th at pm in the dmse committee room we hope you can join us for this exciting talk here are the details of the talk title nanoscale device modeling from atom to circuits date and time monday february th pm venue room no dmse committee room academic complex west speaker prof bhaskaran muralidharan from iit bombay abstract quantum transport which stems from an esoteric quantumphysics theory has evolved into a very advanced device modeling platform and has also morphed itself into atomistic tcad frameworks our group has over the past decade developed a composite quantum transport modeling framework spanning several applications including advanced logic and memory devices emerging devices optoelectronics and quantum technologies our efforts have included proposals on advanced magnetoresistive memory devices and novel transistors that employ spinvalley physics in the dmaterial platform in this presentation while conveying the salient points of our developments we wish to share a futuristic outlook with the ultimate ambition of multiscaling from the atom to the circuit specifically we will cover the stateoftheart atomistic modeling of magnetic randomaccess memory cells for both spintransfer torque stt and spinorbit torque sot random access memories sttrams and sotrams we then demonstrate our latest advancements in terms of coupling the atomistic device modeling platform with hspice simulations to realize energy efficient neurmomorphic circuit functionalities we finally close the loop by extending our platform to the field of quantum technologies with our latest developments on machine learning based simulation platforms for qubits in the bilayer graphene platform g klimeck and t boykin springer handbook of semiconductor devices k camsari s chowdhury and s datta springer handbook of semiconductor devices a sharma a tulapurkar and b muralidharan j appl phys s banerjee k jana a basak m s fuhrer d culcer and b muralidharan phys rev applied v vadde b muralidharan and a sharma ieee trans elec dev v vadde b muralidharan and a sharma j phys d appl phys a mukherjee and b muralidharan d materials bio prof bhaskaran muralidharan obtained his btech in engineering physics from the indian institute of technology iit bombay in his m s and ph d in electrical engineering from purdue university west lafayette usa in and respectively between he was a postdoctoral associate at the massachusetts institute of technology mit and at the institute for theoretical physics at the university of regensburg germany since he has been a faculty in the department of electrical engineering at iit bombay where he is currently a professor his core research area is computational quantum transport and its applications to modeling and simulation of beyond moore devices his research output spans diverse areas of emerging nanoscale devices ultimately built on top of a broad and fundamental foundation of utilizing quantum transport for novel functionalities he was also the recipient of the apsiusstf professorship award in the shastri indocanada fellowship and the serbstar award in he is a recipient of the excellence in teaching award in iit bombay he is an associate editor in the ieee transactions on nanotechnology on the editorial board of scientific reports and materials for quantum technology iop he has also been a visiting professor at the institute for quantum computing iqc in the university of waterloo canada and the instituteq in aalto university finland regards harsha n s harsha gunda assistant professor department of materials science and engineering indian institute of technology delhi
