Subject: inae talk at department of civil engg
Body: dear all delhi chapter of indian national academy of engineering inae and department of civil engineering at indian institute of technology iit delhi are jointly organizing a talk in a hybrid mode on monday rd march from to ist title sensors sensing and society engineering a sustainable and resilient future abstract engineering plays a fundamental role in tackling global challenges from climate change to digital transformation at the heart of these solutions lies the advancement of sensors and sensing technologies which serve as the foundation for intelligent systems that shape modern society as highlighted in the ukris tomorrows engineering research challenges terc report the future of engineering will be defined by how effectively we harness these technologies to drive sustainability resilience and societal wellbeing this talk will explore how sensing technologies are transforming engineering research and its impact across sectors by focusing on three critical areas environmental sensing and net zero goal humancentric sensing for health and wellbeing and sensing for digital and physical infrastructure however the increasing reliance on sensing technologies also raises questions around data ethics accessibility and security how do we ensure that sensordriven decisionmaking remains transparent inclusive and aligned with societal values by positioning sensors and sensing as a cornerstone of engineering innovation this presentation calls for a multidisciplinary collaborative approach to research and development engineering solutions must integrate insights from computing materials science and social sciences to create systems that are not only technologically advanced but also socially responsible through realworld case studies and forwardlooking discussions this session will emphasize the need for a new engineering paradigmone that leverages sensing technologies to drive sustainability inclusivity and societal impact biography of the speaker elena is a professor of pervasive computing and associate provicechancellor for research at coventry university uk her work concerns the inception of sensorbased systems to resolve applications where i wireless transmission of datainformationknowledge is essential and ii the application needs are as such that intelligent processing of data at source sensing point is critical in order to enable robust and ethical decision making prof elenas research draws from computer science engineering and social sciences in particular she worked for several years on devising machine learning techniques to support knowledge extraction from data in real time on resource constrained devices she takes whole system and whole society approaches to her research she is a fellow of the uks womens engineering society is the national director for the uks doctoral training alliance and an honorary professor at several universities prof elena serves in the humanitarian engineering energy sectors bodies and leads projects that engage communities with renewable technologies in the global south as pathways to empowerment and employment her goal is to reflect on the value of sensors in the most constrained sociotechnical systems and leverage their potential towards a better society prof elena believes in the power of data and our unlimited ability to extract actionable knowledge from it please see the link below for flyer venue for inperson attendees civil engineering committee room room no blockiv department of civil engineering indian institute of technology iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india the microsoft teams link for attending the seminar is meeting id passcode cd d y thanks and regards ann francis phd assistant professor department of civil engineering indian institute of technology Subject: dmse seminar talk by prof nariman enikeev ufa university of science and technology uust russia on th february pm
Body: hi everyone prof nariman enikeev from ufa university of science and technology uust russia is scheduled to present his work on friday february stat pm in the dmse committee room we hope you can join us for this exciting talk here are the details of the talk title nanostructural design of ultrastrong austenitic steels by severe plastic deformation date and time friday st february pm venue room no dmse committee room academic complex west speaker prof nariman enikeev from ufa university of science and technology uust russia abstract new materials with superior performance are highly demanded for advanced applications steels are among the most important materials for various industries and there is a global need to further improve their multifunctional properties for example austenitic stainless steels are known for their outstanding corrosion resistance good formability high durability and so on however the yield strength of these steels is relatively low which limits their use in many potential applications nanostructuring through extremely large straining under high pressures to significantly refine the microstructure of metallic materials in order to obtain ultrafinegrained states attracts much attention of researchers since it can significantly improve the mechanical and functional properties of existing materials this presentation features a review of the broad research activity performed on the microstructure and mechanical behavior of nanostructured austenitic steels such as corrosionresistant steels and steels with the effect of twinning induced plasticity twipsteels along with the effects of grain structure refinement a recently discovered phenomenon of redistribution of alloying elements due to severe plastic deformation is discussed the influence of structural features on the mechanical characteristics of steels and their resistance to external influences as well as the effect of hardening by annealing and an increase in plasticity in the highstrength state of nanostructured steel due to the plasticity mechanism which takes into account the interaction of grainboundary solute segregations and dislocations is analyzed the report also reviews studies of the effects of irradiation on the structure of nanocrystalline materials which demonstrated their much higher resistance to radiation damage compared to their coarsegrained counterparts data presented in numerous publications have confirmed that grain size reduction can be an effective strategy for developing new radiationresistant materials in the last decades materials scientists have emphasized the method of refinement of the microstructure of metallic materials using severe plastic deformation spd spd materials are characterized by submicron grain sizes in some cases the grains can be milled to nanometer sizes the combination of ultrafinegrained ufg microstructure and nanostructural features in spd materials provides a significant improvement in their mechanical and functional properties targeted control of nanostructural parameters can provide additional opportunities to design improved multifunctional properties of ufg materials including radiation resistance the presentation presents an overview of studies on the changes in the structure and properties of ufg materials obtained by spd as a result of irradiation it is shown that grain refinement can be a powerful tool for creating advanced radiationresistant materials in general bulk ufg metals and alloys produced by spd show superior mechanical performance and improved resistance to model and neutron irradiation bio dr habil nariman enikeev holds positions of principal researcher in research lab metals and alloys under extreme impacts and professor of physics of metals and materials science department of ufa university of science and technology uust he received his phd degree in condensed matter physics in institute for physics of molecules and crystals in ufa russia and got then habilitation drsci in mechanics of deformed solids and condensed matter physics on the topic of grain boundaries and superstrength of nanostructured materials in institute for problems in mechanical engineering of the russian academy of sciences in saint petersburg russia he pursued research positions at the uust and saint petersburg university and attended as a visiting researcher university of vienna austria chungnam national university korea university of rouen france karlsruhe institute of technology germany etc prof enikeev scholarly endeavors are reflected in his extensive publication record which boasts over papers monographs as well as granted intellectual properties his scientific interests cover investigation of nanostructured materials produced by severe plastic deformation theoretical and experimental foundations for understanding the influence of nanoscale features of the mechanical and functional properties of metallic materials it includes but is not limited to grain boundary effects solute segregation deformation mechanisms mechanical performance etc his research portfolio also extends to areas such as multiscale simulation xray analysis and currently additive manufacturing for developing advanced bioactive scaffolds for medical applications further demonstrating his multifaceted contributions to science and engineering as a result of scientific activity nariman enikeev has published more than a hundred papers many of which are in highranked international journals he is a coauthor of monographs patents and a certificate of registration of the software package he is also ranked as belonging to the percentile of the top cited russian scientists by russian science index in the physical sciences and astronomy area thanks harsha n s harsha gunda assistant professor department of materials science and engineering indian institute of technology delhi

dmse seminar talk by prof sanghamitra neogi university of colorado boulder on th february pm
Body: dear all prof sanghamitra neogi from the university of colorado boulder usa is scheduled to give a seminar on monday february th at pm in the dmse committee room we hope you can join us for this exciting talk here are the details of the talk title atom to device developing atomistic thermal model of microelectronic devices using physicsaware ai date and time monday february th at pm venue room no dmse committee room academic complex west speaker prof sanghamitra neogi university of colorado boulder usa abstract the stateoftheart nanometer nmscale microelectronic transistors are heterogeneous structures that include semiconductors dielectric materials and metals within confining nanoscale dimensions the confined geometry results in selfheating that accelerates defect generation and lead to the decline of the transistors our previous studies showed that heat conduction in nmscale systems can be drastically different from their bulk counterparts moreover heat transport in nanoscale systems that include multiple confining surfaces interfaces and materials with different degrees of crystallinity or disorder is far from understood atomistic modeling techniques have shown remarkable accuracy while predicting thermal conductivities of isolated nanoscale systems however the computational costs of firstprinciples approaches prohibit us to analyze such complex systems in this talk i will discuss how atomistic modeling approaches combined with machine learning methods allow us to overcome this challenge and predict thermal properties of sub nm confined geometry field effect transistors we compute the thermal properties of multiinterface transistor heterostructure using graphics processing units molecular dynamics gpumd a highly efficient generalpurpose molecular dynamic package fully implemented on gpus we used gpumd framework to train machinelearned potentials called neuroevolution potentials neps using the neps and molecular dynamics approaches we calculate the effective thermal properties of the heterostructure under steadystate and transient heating conditions respectively we obtain inplane and crossplace thermal conductivities interfacial thermal conductance and resistance of each layer of the heterostructures and discuss their differences from bulk properties our model provides nanoscale physics insight for designing nanoscale transistors with desired thermal budget and power consumption we gratefully acknowledge funding from the defense advanced research projects agency microsystems technology office agreement no hr for the work bio sanghamitra neogi is an associate professor at the ann and hj smead department of aerospace engineering sciences at the university of colorado boulder additionally she is a program faculty at the materials science and engineering program at the university of colorado boulder prior to joining cu she received her bsc and msc in physics from jadavpur university kolkata and indian institute of technology kanpur india respectively she received her phd in theoretical condensed matter physics from the pennsylvania state university and was a postdoctoral research associate at the max planck institute for polymer research mainz germany her research was featured in the ieee spectrum feature physicists teach ai to simulate atomic clusters physicsinformed machine learning might help verify microchips jul and received mention in the journal of physics d applied physics article the applied physics by pioneering women a roadmap she was an associate editor for the european physical journal b condensed matter and complex systems thanks harsha n s harsha gunda assistant professor department of materials science and engineering indian institute of technology delhi

Subject: institute seminar today can we make machine learning safe for safetycritical systems institute seminar by prof thomas g dietterich
Body: reminder for todays seminar dear students and colleagues we are delighted to invite you to an institute seminar by prof thomas g dietterich oregon state university usa on th february at pm in the seminar hall at iit delhi prof dietterich will talk on can we make machine learning safe for safetycritical systems abstract of the talk the impressive new capabilities of systems created using deep learning are encouraging engineers to apply these techniques in safetycritical applications such as medicine aeronautics and selfdriving cars this talk will discuss the ways that machine learning methodologies are changing to operate in safetycritical systems these changes include a building highfidelity simulators for the domain b adversarial collection of training data to ensure coverage of the socalled operational design domain odd and specifically the hazardous regions within the odd c methods for verifying that the fitted models generalize well and d methods for estimating the probability of harms in normal operation there are many research challenges to achieving these but we must do more because traditional safety engineering only addresses the known hazards we must design our systems to detect novel hazards as well we adopt levesons view of safety as an ongoing hierarchical control problem in which controls are put in place to stabilize the system against disturbances disturbances include novel hazards but also management changes such as budget cuts staff turnover novel regulations and so on traditionally it has been the human operators and managers who have provided these stabilizing controls are there ways that ai methods such as novelty detection nearmiss detection diagnosis and repair can be applied to help the human organization manage these disturbances and maintain system safety speakers bio dr dietterich is university distinguished professor emeritus in the school of electrical engineering and computer science at oregon state university dietterich is one of the pioneers of the field of machine learning and has authored more than refereed publications and two books his current research topics include robust artificial intelligence robust humanai systems and applications in sustainability dietterich is the recipient of the feigenbaum prize for applied ai and the recipient of the ijcai award for research excellence dietterich is also the recipient of the aaai distinguished service award and the acml distinguished contribution award both recognizing his many years of service to the research community he is a former president of the association for the advancement of artificial intelligence and the founding president of the international machine learning society other major roles include executive editor of the journal machine learning cofounder of the journal for machine learning research and program chair of aaai and nips he currently chairs the computer science section of arxivorg we look forward to your enthusiastic participation regards shilpi sharma associate dean academics outreach new initiatives batch of chair professor department of biochemical engineering and biotechnology indian Subject: what is so responsible about responsible ai invitation for an institute lecture on th february
Body: dear students and colleagues we are delighted to invite you to the rd institute lecture of by prof geoffrey rockwell from the university of alberta on th february at pm in lh at iit delhi title of the talk what is so responsible about responsible ai abstract of the talk on march th elaine hertzberg was hit by an uber selfdriving car who was responsible in this talk geoffrey rockwell will talk about the opportunities and limitations of the responsible artificial intelligence approach to ai ethics he will look at philosophical discussions around moral responsibility and how they apply to ai he will argue for a dialogical approach to ai that is responseable about the speaker dr geoffrey martin rockwell is a professor of philosophy and digital humanities at the university of alberta he presently holds a canada cifar ai chair at the alberta machine intelligence institute he has a phd in philosophy from the university of toronto and has published on subjects such as artificial intelligence and ethics philosophical dialogue textual visualization and analysis digital humanities instructional technology computer games and multimedia his books include defining dialogue from socrates to the internet humanity books and hermeneutica coauthored with stéfan sinclair mit press hermeneutica is part of a hybrid text and tool project with voyant tools voyanttoolsorg an awardwinning suite ofanalytical tools he recently coedited right research modelling sustainable research practices in the anthropocene open book publishers and on making in the digital humanities ucl press we look forward to your enthusiastic participation and an overall enriching experience regards shilpi sharma associate dean academics outreach new initiatives batch of chair professor department of biochemical engineering and biotechnology indian institute of technology delhi new delhi india

Subject: can we make machine learning safe for safetycritical systems institute seminar by prof thomas g dietterich
Body: dear students and colleagues we are delighted to invite you to an institute seminar by prof thomas g dietterich oregon state university usa on th february at pm in the seminar hall at iit delhi prof dietterich will talk on can we make machine learning safe for safetycritical systems abstract of the talk the impressive new capabilities of systems created using deep learning are encouraging engineers to apply these techniques in safetycritical applications such as medicine aeronautics and selfdriving cars this talk will discuss the ways that machine learning methodologies are changing to operate in safetycritical systems these changes include a building highfidelity simulators for the domain b adversarial collection of training data to ensure coverage of the socalled operational design domain odd and specifically the hazardous regions within the odd c methods for verifying that the fitted models generalize well and d methods for estimating the probability of harms in normal operation there are many research challenges to achieving these but we must do more because traditional safety engineering only addresses the known hazards we must design our systems to detect novel hazards as well we adopt levesons view of safety as an ongoing hierarchical control problem in which controls are put in place to stabilize the system against disturbances disturbances include novel hazards but also management changes such as budget cuts staff turnover novel regulations and so on traditionally it has been the human operators and managers who have provided these stabilizing controls are there ways that ai methods such as novelty detection nearmiss detection diagnosis and repair can be applied to help the human organization manage these disturbances and maintain system safety speakers bio dr dietterich is university distinguished professor emeritus in the school of electrical engineering and computer science at oregon state university dietterich is one of the pioneers of the field of machine learning and has authored more than refereed publications and two books his current research topics include robust artificial intelligence robust humanai systems and applications in sustainability dietterich is the recipient of the feigenbaum prize for applied ai and the recipient of the ijcai award for research excellence dietterich is also the recipient of the aaai distinguished service award and the acml distinguished contribution award both recognizing his many years of service to the research community he is a former president of the association for the advancement of artificial intelligence and the founding president of the international machine learning society other major roles include executive editor of the journal machine learning cofounder of the journal for machine learning research and program chair of aaai and nips he currently chairs the computer science section of arxivorg we look forward to your enthusiastic participation regards shilpi sharma associate dean academics outreach new initiatives batch of chair professor department of biochemical engineering and biotechnology indian institute of technology delhi new delhi india Subject: inae delhi chapter department of civil engineering and uqiitd research academy seminar by prof dr david lange on february friday pm ist in a hybrid mode at iit delhi
Body: dear madamsir delhi chapter of indian national academy of engineering inae department of civil engineering at indian institute of technology iit delhi and the university of queensland uq iit delhi research academy uqidra at iit delhi are jointly organizing a seminar event in a hybrid mode details of which are given below seminar titled holistic fire safety in built infrastructure abstract fire safety is a subject of significant impact and importance in the built environment since the first codes and regulations that deal with fire safety were introduced hundreds of years ago the discipline has evolved to a proper recognized engineering discipline in many countries nevertheless the context in which fire safety is delivered is constantly changing and with increasing complexity of our built environment codebased approached to fire safety may not provide the level of safety that is expected by society recent incidents highlight the negative fire safety outcomes of fires involving timber buildings as well as combustible cladding and batteries this seminar will discuss the role that fire safety has played in the built environment and the importance of a holistic approach to fire safety in todays buildings drawing on the results of ongoing research uqidra projects as well as research at the university of queensland we will discuss recent developments in structural fire engineering timber and facade fire safety and how these can all be integrated into the fire safety strategy of a building biography of the speaker dr david lange is an associate professor in structural and fire safety engineering in the school of civil engineering at the university of queensland uq he is a chartered fellow of engineers australia a member of the national engineering register in australia a registered international professional engineer an apec engineer and a registered professional engineer in queensland he joined uq in after years in the research industry sector in sweden his research interests include fire safety engineering and resilience of infrastructure and communities and he has been active in both fields of research for several years participating in and leading a range of funded projects and other research activities of various scales his work has had significant impact on fire safety and fire safety engineering in australia date and time friday th february at pm indian standard time ist venue for inperson attendees civil engineering committee room room no blockiv department of civil engineering indian institute of technology Subject: institute lecture today advances in understanding atmospheric aerosol formation from molecular scale reactions to global impacts
Body: starting soon see you all tomorrow dear students and colleagues we are delighted to invite you to the nd institute lecture of by prof katrianne lehtipalo from the university of helsinki finland on th february at pm in the seminar hall at iit delhi title of the talk advances in understanding atmospheric aerosol formation from molecular scale reactions to global impacts abstract of the talk atmospheric aerosol particles affect both air quality and climate it is estimated that more than half of them form in the atmosphere from gaseous precursor vapors in a complex chain of physical and chemical reactions the recent developments in instrumentation have enabled direct measurements of the first steps of the aerosol formation and growth processes happening in the size range on â€“ nanometers in this seminar i will review some of the technical developments and scientific results from both simulation chamber experiments as well as field observations related to atmospheric new particle formation processes finally i will discuss open questions in the field of atmospheric aerosols and new particle formation about the speaker katrianne lehtipalo is professor in atmospheric science and physics at the university of helsinki and finnish meterological institute she obtained phd in at university of helsinki and has worked as visiting scientist at paul scherrer institute switzerland she leads the atmospheric aerosols research group at the institute for atmospheric and earth system research her research concentrates on developing methods to detect the smallest recently formed nanoclusters and aerosol particles and understanding their formation and growth processes she is author of numerous highimpact publications and has won several grants and awards for her work we look forward to your enthusiastic participation and an overall enriching experience regards shilpi sharma associate dean academics outreach new initiatives batch of chair professor department of Subject: institute lecture tomorrow advances in understanding atmospheric aerosol formation from molecular scale reactions to global impacts
Body: see you all tomorrow dear students and colleagues we are delighted to invite you to the nd institute lecture of by prof katrianne lehtipalo from the university of helsinki finland on th february at pm in the seminar hall at iit delhi title of the talk advances in understanding atmospheric aerosol formation from molecular scale reactions to global impacts abstract of the talk atmospheric aerosol particles affect both air quality and climate it is estimated that more than half of them form in the atmosphere from gaseous precursor vapors in a complex chain of physical and chemical reactions the recent developments in instrumentation have enabled direct measurements of the first steps of the aerosol formation and growth processes happening in the size range on â€“ nanometers in this seminar i will review some of the technical developments and scientific results from both simulation chamber experiments as well as field observations related to atmospheric new particle formation processes finally i will discuss open questions in the field of atmospheric aerosols and new particle formation about the speaker katrianne lehtipalo is professor in atmospheric science and physics at the university of helsinki and finnish meterological institute she obtained phd in at university of helsinki and has worked as visiting scientist at paul scherrer institute switzerland she leads the atmospheric aerosols research group at the institute for atmospheric and earth system research her research concentrates on developing methods to detect the smallest recently formed nanoclusters and aerosol particles and understanding their formation and growth processes she is author of numerous highimpact publications and has won several grants and awards for her work we look forward to your enthusiastic participation and an overall enriching experience regards shilpi sharma associate dean academics outreach new initiatives batch of chair professor department of Subject: ieor talk th feb by dr boli chen university college london
Body: dear all hope you are doing good i am writing to welcome you to the industrial engineering and operations research ieor seminar series we are glad to have dr boli chen from university college london joining us inperson this week dr chen will be talking about his work at the intersection of mobility ai and computation technologies please find details about the speaker and the talk below date and time th feb from am to noon venue senate room title intelligent control for smart and sustainable mobility abstract recent advancements in ai computation and communication technologies have driven significant progress in robotics and autonomous systems among these connected and automated vehicles cavs are ready to become the first highly safetycritical autonomous systems available to the public with broader adoption cavs have the potential to make road transport greener safer and more efficient however realizing these benefits depends on our ability to ensure system reliability safety and efficiencychallenges that lie at the heart of control engineering in particular providing safety guarantees remains a central concern for selfdriving vehicles and other autonomous systems increasingly integrated into society this talk will explore some key control and decisionmaking challenges in cavs such as realtime control and planning with enhanced situational awareness coordinated platooning with traffic signal information and smart charging technology that benefits both the grid and the vehicle biography boli chen ieee sm obtained his phd degree in control systems from imperial college london uk in he was a postdoc at imperial college london with the control and power group from to since september he is a lecturer in the department of electronic and electrical engineering at university college london where he is associated with the sensors systems and circuits research group and the ucl robotics institute his research focuses on the control optimization and estimation of complex dynamical systems with rich applications in smart cities eg transportation electric energy systems and sensor networks dr boli chen is a member of the ieee control systems society technical committee on smart cities he serves as an associate editor for the ieee transactions on intelligent transportation systems and the european journal of control additionally he is a member of the euca conference editorial board and the ieee itsc editorial board please see the link below for flyer thanks and regards amber srivastava assistant professor ieor mechanical engineering hauz khas iit delhi

Subject: civil engineering seminar series dr sayantan majumdar from desert research institute usa scheduled on monday th february at pm
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the civil engineering seminar by dr sayantan majumdar monty assistant research professor of hydrologic sciences and remote sensing at the desert research institute reno nevada usa scheduled on monday th february at pm in committee room block iv room no department of civil engineering at indian institute of technology iit delhi title of the seminar integrating satellite remote sensing climate data and machine learning to quantify irrigation water use abstract of the seminar groundwater is a key component of global water resources and is the largest source of earths liquid freshwater it is extensively used for drinking water and to support global food production consequently groundwater consumption has significantly increased owing to the pressing demands for water food and energy primarily driven by the increasing global population despite its critical role in the waterfoodenergy nexus very few regions in the united states us or elsewhere actively monitor their groundwater withdrawals extraction or pumping for implementing sustainable water management solutions the existing methods for estimating groundwater withdrawals and irrigation water use consumptive use are either costly and timeconsuming or they cannot generate dependable predictions at the scales required for effective local management here we develop a novel approach combining water balance components evapotranspiration precipitation runoff and others and land use obtained using openly available remote sensing and hydroclimate data sets with statistical and machine learning models to estimate irrigation water use across various regions of the us eg kansas arizona nevada oregon and the mississippi alluvial plain our models can explain variance in groundwater pumping depths and variance in groundwater pumping volumes when compared to insitu meter data this holistic approach provides a valuable tool for water resource management as it enables us to monitor and assess the impact of irrigation practices on groundwater resources by implementing sustainable water management solutions based on these estimates we can work towards ensuring longterm water security and mitigating the risks associated with increasing groundwater consumption as part of this talk dr majumdar will delve into stateoftheart datasets and methods for estimating irrigation water use although our initial focus has been on the united states there is potential to adapt and apply this approach to other regions such as the indian subcontinent and southeast asia where water security challenges are widely prevalent biographical sketch of the speaker dr sayantan majumdar is an assistant research professor of hydrologic sciences and remote sensing at the desert research institute reno nevada usa he is also serving as an adjunct faculty as part of the university of nevada reno unr and dri graduate program of hydrologic sciences earlier he was a postdoctoral fellow at the department of civil and environmental engineering colorado state university usa he has also interned at meta formerly facebook and planet labs dr majumdar is a computational hydrologist with expertise in geospatial data science machine learning remote sensing and scientific computing he has a strong track record of producing highimpact crossdisciplinary research at the intersection of remote sensing machine learning geoinformatics and hydrology dr majumdar has a phd degree in geological engineering from missouri university of science and technology usa his doctoral research was focused on groundwater withdrawal estimation using integrated remote sensing datasets and machine learning he is currently working on multiple projects funded by nasa us geological survey usgs us bureau of reclamation usbr national park service nps state of nevadaus department of the treasury and national institutes of health nih during this talk dr majumdar will also share his journey from being a masters student at the indian institute of remote sensing iirs isro to a faculty at dri and how gisremote sensinggeospatial data science are leveraged across academia industry and research institutions to solve some of the greatest challenges of this century all interested are cordially invited to attend the seminar thank you head department of civil engineering room no blockiv indian institute of technology iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india email telephone secretary telephone direct

Body: join us for an insightful session with dr anjana rustagi phd associate professor in the department of botany gargi college university of delhi the session will focus on biotechnological interventions for improvement of indian musa varieties dont miss the chance to learn from one of the leading experts in this field date monday th february time am ist pm aest onwards venue lh first floor lecture hall complex iit delhi link to join online abstract of the talk this talk will focus on the utilization of biotechnological interventions to improve indian musa banana varieties which are vital for food security and livelihoods but face challenges due to biotic and abiotic stresses conventional breeding is hindered by the crops sterility polyploidy and long life cycle making advanced techniques like somatic embryogenesis genetic transformation and crisprcas based genome editing essential successful regeneration of indian varieties like somrani monthan via embryogenic cell suspension and development of transgenic matti and grand naine varieties with enhanced disease and stress tolerance highlight significant progress these efforts emphasize the need for further exploration of indigenous banana genotypes to achieve mass propagation genetic improvement and germplasm conservation ensuring a resilient and sustainable banana crop for the future about the speaker dr anjana rustagi associate professor at gargi college university of delhi holds a phd in botany with over years of teaching and research experience her work focuses on plant regeneration genetic transformation and stress tolerance in crops like musa and brassica juncea she has contributed significantly to understanding abas role in embryogenesis and has numerous publications and edited books legacy youtube dil se iit delhi podcasts iit delhi hosts us national security advisor jake sullivan iit delhi in collaboration with the ihub foundation for cobotics ihfc the institutes technology innovation hub proudly hosted mr jake sullivan national security advisor nsa of the united states on january mr sullivan delivered a compelling talk titled the united states and india building a shared future addressing a distinguished gathering at the institute his insightful speech emphasized the progress of the indiaus strategic partnership and explored avenues for future alliances to strengthen bilateral relations particularly in technology and innovation the director of iit delhi prof rangan banerjee emphasized the strong and growing linkages between american institutions and iit delhi highlighting ongoing bilateral collaborations un envoy mr amandeep singh gill welcomed at iit delhi for discussion on ai governance iit delhi recently welcomed mr amandeep singh gill un undersecretarygeneral for digital and emerging technologies and secretarygenerals envoy on technology for an engaging discussion on the critical topic of ai governance mr gill emphasized the need for active youth involvement in shaping the global digital compact he highlighted the vital role of young innovators and students in ensuring that technology development remains fair and equitable for all during his visit mr gill explored the vibrant startups ecosystem nurtured at the foundation for innovation and technology transfer fitt iit delhi he interacted with teams from cyran ai mobisec tensor dynamics and synergy quantum these startups presented their innovative solutions aimed at addressing pressing societal challenges and showcased how emerging technologies can contribute to global wellbeing cdot and iit delhi collaborate on building blocks for thz communication front ends the centre for development of telematics cdot the premier telecom rd centre of the department of telecommunications dot government of india has signed an agreement with iit delhi to work on building blocks for thz communication front ends for g technology this collaboration is part of the telecom technology development fund ttdf g call for proposal by the department of telecommunications the initiative aims to accelerate research and development for the g ecosystem aligning with the bharat g vision to design develop and deploy advanced g network technologies these technologies aim to provide ubiquitous intelligent and secure connectivity for a superior quality of life the primary objective of this project is to develop fundamental devices and components essential for thz systems envisioned for g communications additionally these thz systems will support applications in areas such as military communications and material characterization iit delhi alumni relations signs mou with prof vijay vazirani to establish the prof v n vazirani institute lecture series prof vijay vazirani has signed a memorandum of understanding mou with iit delhi alumni relations and endowment office to launch the prestigious prof v n vazirani institute lecture series this initiative honors the pioneering contributions of prof v n vazirani to the field of structural engineering the lecture series aims to bring together distinguished scholars and researchers to share their expertise and insights with iit delhis vibrant academic community by participating in this platform speakers have the unique opportunity to inspire and shape the next generation of engineers we warmly invite scholars and researchers to be part of this esteemed lecture series if you are interested in collaborating and contributing please reach out to us to explore this opportunity at strengthening international collaborations iit delhi hosts newcastle university delegation on january nd the department of civil engineering at the indian institute of technology iit delhi had the privilege of hosting a distinguished delegation from newcastle university uk led by professor chris day vice chancellor and president this visit marked a significant step towards fostering stronger academic and research collaborations between the two renowned institutions the newcastle university delegation included prof christopher day vice chancellor president newcastle university laura mitford head of international recruitment development prof claire walsh director of civil and geospatial engineering prof jaime m amezaga deputy director water security hub a productive meeting was held between the delegation and the faculty members of the department of civil engineering at iit delhi discussions focused on exploring future collaborations in areas such as civil engineering geospatial technologies and water security ihfc of iit delhi launches coinnovation centres across india to foster innovation and entrepreneurship the technology innovation hub tih of iit delhi ihfc has embarked on a transformative initiative to establish coinnovation centres cic in collaboration with ten prestigious institutes across india this ambitious project aims to nurture a culture of innovation technology development and entrepreneurship among indias youth on january the first cic was inaugurated in bengaluru at pes university this marks the beginning of a nationwide network of coinnovation centres other premier institutes ready for the immediate launch of their cics include indian institute of engineering science and technology iiest shibpur kolkata thapar institute patiala srm university of science and technology chennai indian institute of technology gandhinagar these institutes represent a diverse geographical and academic spectrum underscoring the widereaching impact of this initiative iit delhi and university of exeter strengthen collaborative partnership on january iit delhi and the university of exeter signed a landmark agreement to strengthen their collaborative partnership by committing resources to three key areas of shared priority and expertise sports science elite performance and rehabilitation climate science environmental data and clean energy operations research ai and automation this partnership is closely aligned with the ukindia roadmap combining expertise from both institutions to drive impactful research and innovation in sports science the collaboration aims to support indias rapidly growing sports sector by addressing the needs of sports startups elite athlete performance rehabilitation and the role of physical activity in promoting a healthier society in climate science and clean energy the partnership will leverage complementary expertise in science and policy to meet industry needs and support the transition to a sustainable netzero future additionally the iit delhi exeter joint symposium was held on january th on sports healthcare science and engineering organized by the office of the dean of international programmes iit delhi successfully brought together experts from iit delhi and the university of exeter to explore collaborative opportunities in research industry partnerships and education the symposium highlighted the synergy between the two institutions showcasing their unique and complementary expertise in addressing the evolving needs of indias rapidly expanding sports sector discussions focused on cuttingedge advancements in sports science healthcare innovations and engineering solutions to enhance athletic performance and wellbeing project abhay transforming truck driver health safety project abhay an initiative by the centre for rural development technology crdt iit delhi in collaboration with foresight foundation and supported by the ministry of road transport highways morth has made remarkable strides in improving the health vision and safety of indias truck drivers the projects impact was highlighted during the culmination ceremony at iit delhi where prof vivek kumar crdt iit delhi presented the findings in the esteemed presence of shri nitin gadkari honble union minister for road transport highways and prof rangan banerjee director iit delhi since its launch in march project abhay has successfully screened over truck drivers across uttar pradesh rajasthan madhya pradesh maharashtra karnataka and tamil nadu addressing critical health and vision challenges faced by this essential yet underserved workforce last call distinguished alumni awards nominations as we near the final weeks of the nomination period for iit delhis prestigious distinguished alumni awards daa we invite you to help us recognize the extraordinary achievements of our alumni community the distinguished alumni awards celebrate excellence across diverse domains from groundbreaking technological innovations to impactful social initiatives past recipients have included industry leaders pioneering researchers successful entrepreneurs and changemakers who have shaped their respective fields we welcome nominations for iit delhi alumni who have demonstrated outstanding professional achievements significant contributions to academia or research notable entrepreneurial success remarkable public service or social impact excellence in leadership and innovation access the nomination form here dont let exceptional achievements go unrecognized your nomination could help showcase another inspiring story from our distinguished alumni community deadline february th for queries contact events and reunions ruby reunion class of date february th we register here your hostel your legacy iit delhi is embarking on a significant initiative to address the critical accommodation shortage on campus by rebuilding five of its old boys hostels aravali jwalamukhi karakoram kumaon and nilgiri with construction slated to begin in this project aims to expand and enhance the residential infrastructure currently accommodating around of the enrolled students the institute with the help of alumni corporates and philanthropists plans to raise approximately rs crores usd mn for this ambitious and muchneeded hostel complex over the next four years this project marks a paradigm shift in terms of how the institute will evolve in the years to come fostering closer interaction between alumni current students and institute authorities together we Subject: request for feedback on iit delhi’s draft diversity equity inclusion policy

Subject: reminder invitation for the ieee lecture on th february at pm
Body: dear all the ieee chapter iit delhi invites you to an engaging technical talk by prof anamitra pal from arizona state university usa on largebluediamond title voltage monitoring and control of active distribution systems spiralcalendar date th february alarmclock time pm roundpushpin venue ee committee room iit delhi talk details are provided below title voltage monitoring and control of active distribution systems abstract residential solar photovoltaic pv systems are integral for achieving the carbon neutral goals for at the same time power utilities who are responsible for the reliability and stability of the electric distribution grid are often unaware of the extent of behindthemeter solar pv penetration in the absence of realtime visibility and adequate control the increasing proliferation of residential pv systems can play havoc with the distribution feeder voltage consequently there is a genuine need to closely monitor and control the voltage over the entire length of the feeder this talk will describe how systemwide information obtained from a select few realtime sensors using machine learning can be used to optimize reactive power regulation for achieving coordinated robust and fast voltage control of active distribution systems to ensure trust in the machine learningbased approach formal guarantees of performance will also be established the talk will conclude by demonstrating additional systemwide benefits that an integrated approach towards monitoring and control provides to power utilities responsible for operating large complex distribution grids biography anamitra pal is an associate professor in the school of electrical computer and energy engineering at arizona state university asu his research interests include data analytics with a special emphasis on timesynchronized measurements artificial intelligenceapplications in power systems renewable generation integration studies and critical infrastructure resilience dr pal has received numerous accolades including the young critis award for his contributions to the field of critical infrastructure protection the outstanding young professional award from the ieee phoenix section the national science foundation career award in and the centennial professorship award from asu in this talk will provide invaluable insights into modern techniques for voltage monitoring and control in active distribution networks it is an excellent opportunity to interact with an expert in the field and expand your knowledge on advanced power system control dr yashasvi bansal assistant professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi

Subject: re photonic lecture series on th february pm ist
Body: optics and photonics centre opc invites all interested to a series of lectures by wellknown scientists in areas of optics and photonics details of lecture in this series is given below title time resolved imaging with two photon interferometry speaker dr ashley lyons affiliation university of glasgow uk date th february thursday time pm ist mode online link abstract measuring the time of arrival of photons gives access to a whole library of information otherwise inaccessible with other imaging schemes perhaps the simplest example is in light detection and ranging lidar where the arrival time can be used to infer the distance to an object in most convention time of flight systems the arrival time is measured electronically either by using time correlated single photon counting tcspc or by gating the detectorcamera this common limits the temporal resolution to picoseconds which has direct consequences for eg the depth resolution of lidar i will discuss recent work utilising interferometric techniques inspired by hongoumandel interferometry which allow this barrier to be broken and can reach femtosecond scale temporal resolution using only linear optics we demonstrate this approach can be applied to achieve micron resolution lidar and can be used to build d microscopes that can be made scanless and reach nanometre scale depth resolution we also show how the approach can be applied to fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy flim where it allows new fluorescent markers to be accessed and can act as a high sensitivity probe for parameters such as viscosity bio dr lyons is lecturer in the school of physics and astronomy at the university of glasgow and a research fellow with the royal academy of engineering he coleads the extreme light group at glasgow with prof daniele faccio which is formed of more than phdpostdoctoral researchers he completed his phd in at heriotwatt university in edinburgh under the guidance of prof faccio before moving to glasgow in the following year dr lyons also leads the alliance for research challenges in quantum technology a year initiative funded by the scottish funding council to connect quantum researchers to a broader range of fields and industries within scotland thanks regard profpsenthilkumaran head optics and photonics centre chair professor prof ajoy ghatak chair indian institute of technology delhi Subject: invitation for the ieee lecture on th february at pm
Body: dear all the ieee chapter iit delhi invites you to an engaging technical talk by prof anamitra pal from arizona state university usa on largebluediamond title voltage monitoring and control of active distribution systems spiralcalendar date th february alarmclock time pm roundpushpin venue ee committee room iit delhi talk details are provided below title voltage monitoring and control of active distribution systems abstract residential solar photovoltaic pv systems are integral for achieving the carbon neutral goals for at the same time power utilities who are responsible for the reliability and stability of the electric distribution grid are often unaware of the extent of behindthemeter solar pv penetration in the absence of realtime visibility and adequate control the increasing proliferation of residential pv systems can play havoc with the distribution feeder voltage consequently there is a genuine need to closely monitor and control the voltage over the entire length of the feeder this talk will describe how systemwide information obtained from a select few realtime sensors using machine learning can be used to optimize reactive power regulation for achieving coordinated robust and fast voltage control of active distribution systems to ensure trust in the machine learningbased approach formal guarantees of performance will also be established the talk will conclude by demonstrating additional systemwide benefits that an integrated approach towards monitoring and control provides to power utilities responsible for operating large complex distribution grids biography anamitra pal is an associate professor in the school of electrical computer and energy engineering at arizona state university asu his research interests include data analytics with a special emphasis on timesynchronized measurements artificial intelligenceapplications in power systems renewable generation integration studies and critical infrastructure resilience dr pal has received numerous accolades including the young critis award for his contributions to the field of critical infrastructure protection the outstanding young professional award from the ieee phoenix section the national science foundation career award in and the centennial professorship award from asu in this talk will provide invaluable insights into modern techniques for voltage monitoring and control in active distribution networks it is an excellent opportunity to interact with an expert in the field and expand your knowledge on advanced power system control dr yashasvi bansal assistant professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi

Subject: re departmental talk by prof sankar pal mon rd feb pm ee committee room
Body: a gentle reminder for the talk today at pm thanks tanmoy original message subject departmental talk by prof sankar pal mon rd feb pm ee committee room date from tanmoy chakraborty to dear colleagues and students prof sankar pal is visiting iit delhi on rd feb tomorrow he will give a talk in our department at pm kindly attend the talk plese find below the details of the talk title granular video mining and deep learning why and how venue ee committee room speaker prof sankar k pal national science chair govt of india president indian statistical institute kolkata abstract the talk first describes the components of granular computing grc and information granulessignificance of rough sets in granular computing and the relevance of generalized rough sets and entropy as a stronger paradigm for uncertainty modelingthen the problem of unsupervised video tracking in ambiguous situations based on prediction is considered as an example application of granular mining the concept of neighborhood rough filter that provides an estimate of the location and color model of objects for handling overlapping and occlusion is explained roles of different spatiocolor and spatiotemporal granules as well as the lower and upper approximations are statedthe third part deals with the significance of deep learning dl in object recognition and tracking in video after explaining the relevance of granulation in cnn convolutional neural nets forreducing the computation time the talk presents a deep architecture named grcnn granulated region proposal neural nets this is an improved version of the fast rcnn and faster rcnn for extracting rois regions of interest by incorporating spatiotemporal granulation in a deep alexnet architecture grcnn accepts videos directly as input spatiotemporal granules enable extraction of less number but more representative roipixels of object regions and thereby make the grcnn superior in realtime detection speed and accuracythe merits of grcnn are demonstrated as a case study on realtime traffic scenarios in a tata steel plant for anomaly detection towards safety analytics the talk concludes by mentioning the challenging issues and future directions of research including the evolution of the discipline since s and some concerns for beginners thanks tanmoy

Subject: re seminar on digital twin modelling of optical communication systems mon rd feb am in ii
Body: dear all you are invited to a seminar by our alumnus dr rishu raj on monday rd february at am in the ee committee room ii details are as follows title digital twin modelling of optical fibrebased communication systems abstract fulfilling the anticipated demands of future network technologies entails a plethora of challenges traditional approaches to tackle these challenges struggle with scalability in disaggregated systems leading to a shift towards datadriven methods especially machine learning digital twins offer a costeffective way to optimize network management and support decisionmaking however accurately predicting physical phenomena like stimulated raman scattering srs remains a challenge as conventional physicsbased models may fail due to variations in transmission spans we develop a deep neural network dnn model to predict the srsinduced raman tilt in optical fibers the dnn is trained with data obtained from experiments on the cosmos testbed located in the us and its performance is benchmarked against established analytical models speaker bio rishu raj is presently a postdoctoral research fellow at the connect research center in trinity college dublin ireland he has been awarded the marie skłodowskacurie actions postdoctoral fellowship mscapf funded by horizon europe the european unions flagship funding program he completed his phd in the department of electrical engineering at the indian institute of technology delhi india in for his phd thesis he received the innovative student project award given by the indian national academy of engineering inae he obtained the btech degree in electrical engineering from the national institute of technology agartala tripura india in where he was awarded the institute gold medal for academic excellence he is a member of the inae ieee and optica formerly osa his research interests include visible light communication optical communication networks and systems and nonlinear optics all are welcome to attend

Subject: departmental talk by prof sankar pal mon rd feb pm ee committee room
Body: dear colleagues and students prof sankar pal is visiting iit delhi on rd feb tomorrow he will give a talk in our department at pm kindly attend the talk plese find below the details of the talk title granular video mining and deep learning why and how venue ee committee room speaker prof sankar k pal national science chair govt of india president indian statistical institute kolkata abstract the talk first describes the components of granular computing grc and information granulessignificance of rough sets in granular computing and the relevance of generalized rough sets and entropy as a stronger paradigm for uncertainty modelingthen the problem of unsupervised video tracking in ambiguous situations based on prediction is considered as an example application of granular mining the concept of neighborhood rough filter that provides an estimate of the location and color model of objects for handling overlapping and occlusion is explained roles of different spatiocolor and spatiotemporal granules as well as the lower and upper approximations are statedthe third part deals with the significance of deep learning dl in object recognition and tracking in video after explaining the relevance of granulation in cnn convolutional neural nets forreducing the computation time the talk presents a deep architecture named grcnn granulated region proposal neural nets this is an improved version of the fast rcnn and faster rcnn for extracting rois regions of interest by incorporating spatiotemporal granulation in a deep alexnet architecture grcnn accepts videos directly as input spatiotemporal granules enable extraction of less number but more representative roipixels of object regions and thereby make the grcnn superior in realtime detection speed and accuracythe merits of grcnn are demonstrated as a case study on realtime traffic scenarios in a tata steel plant for anomaly detection towards safety analytics the talk concludes by mentioning the challenging issues and future directions of research including the evolution of the discipline since s and some concerns for beginners thanks tanmoy

Subject: advances in understanding atmospheric aerosol formation from molecular scale reactions to global impacts invitation for an institute lecture on th february
Body: dear students and colleagues we are delighted to invite you to the nd institute lecture of by prof katrianne lehtipalo from the university of helsinki finland on th february at pm in the seminar hall at iit delhi title of the talk advances in understanding atmospheric aerosol formation from molecular scale reactions to global impacts abstract of the talk atmospheric aerosol particles affect both air quality and climate it is estimated that more than half of them form in the atmosphere from gaseous precursor vapors in a complex chain of physical and chemical reactions the recent developments in instrumentation have enabled direct measurements of the first steps of the aerosol formation and growth processes happening in the size range on – nanometers in this seminar i will review some of the technical developments and scientific results from both simulation chamber experiments as well as field observations related to atmospheric new particle formation processes finally i will discuss open questions in the field of atmospheric aerosols and new particle formation about the speaker katrianne lehtipalo is professor in atmospheric science and physics at the university of helsinki and finnish meterological institute she obtained phd in at university of helsinki and has worked as visiting scientist at paul scherrer institute switzerland she leads the atmospheric aerosols research group at the institute for atmospheric and earth system research her research concentrates on developing methods to detect the smallest recently formed nanoclusters and aerosol particles and understanding their formation and growth processes she is author of numerous highimpact publications and has won several grants and awards for her work we look forward to your enthusiastic participation and an overall enriching experience regards shilpi sharma associate dean academics outreach new initiatives batch of chair professor department of biochemical engineering and biotechnology indian institute of technology delhi new delhi india

Body: dear all you are invited to a seminar by our alumnus dr rishu raj on monday rd february at am in the ee committee room ii details are as follows title digital twin modelling of optical fibrebased communication systems abstract fulfilling the anticipated demands of future network technologies entails a plethora of challenges traditional approaches to tackle these challenges struggle with scalability in disaggregated systems leading to a shift towards datadriven methods especially machine learning digital twins offer a costeffective way to optimize network management and support decisionmaking however accurately predicting physical phenomena like stimulated raman scattering srs remains a challenge as conventional physicsbased models may fail due to variations in transmission spans we develop a deep neural network dnn model to predict the srsinduced raman tilt in optical fibers the dnn is trained with data obtained from experiments on the cosmos testbed located in the us and its performance is benchmarked against established analytical models speaker bio rishu raj is presently a postdoctoral research fellow at the connect research center in trinity college dublin ireland he has been awarded the marie skłodowskacurie actions postdoctoral fellowship mscapf funded by horizon europe the european unions flagship funding program he completed his phd in the department of electrical engineering at the indian institute of technology delhi india in for his phd thesis he received the innovative student project award given by the indian national academy of engineering inae he obtained the btech degree in electrical engineering from the national institute of technology agartala tripura india in where he was awarded the institute gold medal for academic excellence he is a member of the inae ieee and optica formerly osa his research interests include visible light communication optical communication networks and systems and nonlinear optics all are welcome to attend

Subject: photonic lecture series on th february pm ist
Body: optics and photonics centre opc invites all interested to a series of lectures by wellknown scientists in areas of optics and photonics details of lecture in this series is given below title time resolved imaging with two photon interferometry speaker dr ashley lyons affiliation university of glasgow uk date th february thursday time pm ist mode online link abstract measuring the time of arrival of photons gives access to a whole library of information otherwise inaccessible with other imaging schemes perhaps the simplest example is in light detection and ranging lidar where the arrival time can be used to infer the distance to an object in most convention time of flight systems the arrival time is measured electronically either by using time correlated single photon counting tcspc or by gating the detectorcamera this common limits the temporal resolution to picoseconds which has direct consequences for eg the depth resolution of lidar i will discuss recent work utilising interferometric techniques inspired by hongoumandel interferometry which allow this barrier to be broken and can reach femtosecond scale temporal resolution using only linear optics we demonstrate this approach can be applied to achieve micron resolution lidar and can be used to build d microscopes that can be made scanless and reach nanometre scale depth resolution we also show how the approach can be applied to fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy flim where it allows new fluorescent markers to be accessed and can act as a high sensitivity probe for parameters such as viscosity bio dr lyons is lecturer in the school of physics and astronomy at the university of glasgow and a research fellow with the royal academy of engineering he coleads the extreme light group at glasgow with prof daniele faccio which is formed of more than phdpostdoctoral researchers he completed his phd in at heriotwatt university in edinburgh under the guidance of prof faccio before moving to glasgow in the following year dr lyons also leads the alliance for research challenges in quantum technology a year initiative funded by the scottish funding council to connect quantum researchers to a broader range of fields and industries within scotland regard profpsenthilkumaran head optics and photonics centre chair professor prof ajoy ghatak chair indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: dmse seminar talk by prof tom j savenije delft university of technology on st january pm
Body: dear all prof tom j savenije from delft university of technology in the netherlands is scheduled to present his work on friday january st at pm in the dmse committee room here are the details of the talk title metal halide perovskites for pv applications date and time friday st january pm venue room no dmse committee room academic complex west speaker prof tom j savenije delft university of technology abstract metal halide perovskites mhps have demonstrated great potential for various electronic applications including solar cells leds and xray detectors key aspects are the cheap and low temperature processing leading to relatively defect free semiconducting materials in addition the band gap tunability makes these layers of particular interest to fabricate multijunction solar cells including pvkpvk and pvksi tandem cells although we started fundamental studies on charge carrier dynamics in pvks already in in delft in we extended our research to full pvk devices in the first example i show how we use sequential thermal evaporation to deposit the pvk precursors in a layer by layer fashion after multiple cycles and thermal annealing highly crystalline preferentially orientated pvks are formed consisting of large grains in important aspect of this deposition method is its potential for upscaling moreover pvks deposited using codeposition will be shown in which we varied the deposition speed in addition we demonstrate that it is also possible to deposit mixedmetal pvks to obtain low bandgap materials which can function as bottom cells in tandem configuration finally we show how local micro strain is connected to the charge dynamics of excess charge carriers in triple cation pvks knowledge of the charge carrier dynamics is important since they determine the ultimate performance of a corresponding cell bio tom savenije did his phd under supervision of prof tj schaafsma at the section molecular physics of wageningen agricultural university wageningen the netherlands working on artificial photosynthesis after his defense in january he took up a postdoc position at the inorganic chemistry department tu delft afterwards he joined the group of dr jm warman at the radiation chemistry department iri tu delft there he developed a unique facility to measure the timeresolved photoinduced microwave conductance trmc in thin organic or hybrid films numerous groups all around the world now have copied this setup in he spent half year in the group of prof dr v dyakonov in wurzburg germany as a visiting professor since he is associate professor tu delft his major interest focuses on the relationship between composition and structure of in particular perovskites and their physical properties these materials have possible application in eg photovoltaic devices leds and radiation detectors he authored or coauthored international peerreviewed papers over the last decade he gave numerous presentations at international conferences including mrs icsm psco and hopv he has previously successfully collaborated on scientific projects with several semiindustrial partners including tata steel ijmuiden solliance eindhoven oxford pv uk saint gobain france imra europe france and hyet solar arnhem as pi he has successfully obtained grants funded by nwo echo enw klein nwo sustainable materials shellnwofom htm program of fom the dutch polymer institute htsm program of stw and ngf presently he collaborates intensively with the pvmd group headed by prof olindo isabella from the eemcs faculty of tu delft thanks harsha n s harsha gunda assistant professor department of materials science and engineering indian institute of technology delhi

Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department colloquium by dr soumi nandi indian institute of science iisc on february thursday at am the details are given below title piercing axisparallel boxes with axisparallel kflats speaker dr soumi nandi csa iisc bangalore date th february time noon venue room no academic complex west b abstract a kflat h is said to hit or pierce a set f subseteq mathbbrd if fcap hneqemptyset a set mathcalt of kflats kdimensional affine space is called a ktransversal of a family mathcalf of subsets of mathbbrd if for every f in mathcalf there exists a kflat in mathcalt that pierces f we say a family mathcalf has a ktransversal of size m or at most m if there exists a ktransversal mathcalt of mathcalf and mathcalt m or mathcalt leq m in this talk i will present the necessary and sufficient condition for an infinite collection of axisparallel boxes in mathbbrd to be pierceable by finitely many axisparallel kflats where leq k d this is a joint work with sutanoya chakraborty and arijit ghosh speaker bio dr soumi nandi is a walmart postdoctoral fellow at the computer science and automation csa in indian institute of science iisc bengaluru she completed her phd as a student at advanced computing and microelectronics unit acmu in indian statistical institute isi kolkata under joint supervision of sourav chakraborty and arijit ghosh her research interests broadly include combinatorics discrete geometry polynomial methods she is currently working on the following two types of problems geometric transversal theory and covering subsets of hypercube with nice geometric objects

Subject: dmse seminar talk by prof shahriar hossain the university of queensland uq on th january pm
Body: dear all prof shahriar hossain from the university of queensland uq is scheduled for a seminar on thursday january th at pm we hope you can join us for this exciting talk here are the details title materials spacetectonics a new paradigm for designing nextgeneration nanoporous materials for energy and biomedical applications date and time thursday th january pm venue room no dmse committee room academic complex west speaker prof shahriar hossain from the university of queensland uq abstract in this talk i will introduce the mission and vision behind materials nanotectonicsa pioneering conceptual framework for designing advanced functional inorganic nanospace materials this new paradigm focuses on engineering highsurfacearea nanoporous materials that offer abundant functional sites enhancing performance across a range of critical applications including energy storage catalysis targeted drug delivery and biosensing recent advancements in soft templating using amphiphilic surfactants and block copolymers have enabled the creation of mesoporous structures in diverse materials like metals metal oxides and carbonbased compounds notably mesoporous metals are particularly promising for electrocatalysis as their complex porous networks reveal a multitude of unsaturated atoms on highindex facets offering exceptional catalytic activity during this talk i will discuss the design strategies synthesis and characterization of these nanoengineered porous materialsspecifically those with magnetic electronic and plasmonic propertiesand explore their potential applications in supercapacitors precision drug delivery and biosensing technologies bio dr shahriar hossain is an associate professor in the school of mechanical and mining engineering with a joint appointment at the australian institute for bioengineering and nanotechnology aibn at the university of queensland uq as codirector of the australian centre of materials nanotectonics he leads multiple interdisciplinary research teams making significant advances in the fields of materials science magnetism and applied superconductivity recognized as a global leader in his field dr hossains pioneering work has significantly advanced the development of nanoengineered electronic magnetic and superconducting materials driving innovations in applications such as mri power cables fusion magnets and biosensors dr hossains research excellence is backed by prestigious awardsfellowshipsfunding including the australian research councils discovery early career researcher award decra the strategic research fellowship from the australian academy of sciences and the priming and bridging grant from the australian academy of technology and engineering his contributions have also been acknowledged with the vicechancellors emerging researcher excellence award and the vicechancellors excellent industry partnership award from the university of wollongong uow in addition to his role at uq dr hossain has held visiting scholar and professor positions at renowned institutions worldwide including the university of geneva switzerland ohio state university usa national institute for materials science japan nagoya university japan karlsruhe institute of technology germany institute of high pressure physics poland universitas indonesia and the institute of technology bandung indonesia to date he has published over highimpact sciindexed journal articles with his work attracting over citations and an impressive hindex of according to the google scholar setting him as a highly influential researcher in the scientific community more details in uq profile thanks harsha n s harsha gunda assistant professor department of materials science and engineering indian institute of technology delhi
