Subject: re photonic lecture series on th january pm
Body: a gentle reminder for the talk today at pm thank regard profpsenthilkumaran head optics and photonics centre chair professor prof ajoy ghatak chair indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india original message subject photonic lecture series on th january pm date from hodopc to optics and photonics centre opc invites all interested to a series of lectures by wellknown scientists in areas of optics and photonics details of lecture in this series is given below title midinfrared laser absorption spectroscopy on a chip speaker prof jana jagerska affiliation uit the arctic university of norway mode online link date th january wednesday time pm ist abstract optical sensing through spectroscopy is recognized as a promising application of mid infrared photonics aiming to exploit the intense and wellresolved absorption fingerprints of most molecules in the midinfrared spectral range in my presentation i will discuss the primary challenges that midinfrared photonics faces in sensing applications and present solutions derived from over five years of our active research in this area in the second part of my talk i will focus on two innovative waveguide designs that have been applied to sensitive gas detection these designs include slot waveguides and thinfilm membrane waveguides both optimized to i enhance the evanescent field interaction between the guided light and the gas sample while ii minimizing losses and iii suppressing spurious etalons a major sources of noise in dielectric waveguides with these waveguide sensors we have achieved detection of methane and carbon dioxide in the partsper billion ppb range additionally i will showcase the first onchip δ¹³c isotope ratio measurement achieving a precision on the order of ‰ comparable to highend commercial instruments biography jana jágerská is a full professor of photonics at uit the arctic university of norway and a team leader in the field of nanophotonics and laser spectroscopy focusing on midinfrared onchip sensors for trace gas detection regard profpsenthilkumaran head optics and photonics centre indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: reminder seminar on information extraction beyond diffraction limit at high intensity through supergrowth on th jan am
Body: gentle reminder for the seminar today at am in physics seminar room ms on jan at pm bhaskar kanseri wrote dear all we are organising a talkseminar by dr sethuraj k r from university of rochester in the area of optical imaging and super resolution you are invited to attend this talk details of which are given below best regards bhaskar speaker dr sethuraj k r university of rochester venue physics seminar room ms time am jan title of the talk “information extraction beyond diffraction limit at high intensity through supergrowth” abstract enhancing resolution in imaging science beyond the diffraction limit known as superresolution is critical for applications ranging from medical diagnostics to astronomy in farfield imaging existing superresolution techniques often suffer from substantial photon loss supergrowth a recently demonstrated phenomenon provides a breakthrough by enabling superresolution imaging at high intensity —addressing this limitation this talk delves into the first experimental realization of supergrowing fields and their applications in optical physics i will discuss the interplay between supergrowth and superoscillations advancements in twopoint resolution enhancement and potential applications in ranging technologies like lidar furthermore findings from supergrowth in speckle patterns reveal that fully developed speckles can exhibit nearly supergrowing regions these results pave the way for innovative approaches to extract information beyond the diffraction limit references jordan andrew n et al superphenomena for arbitrary quantum observables physical review a jordan andrew n superresolution using supergrowth and intensity contrast imaging quantum studies mathematics and foundations karmakar tathagata et al supergrowth and subwavelength object imaging optics express kr sethuraj et al experimental realization of supergrowing fields physical review research l viteripflucker valeria et al supergrowth in speckle patterns optics letters brief bio of speaker dr sethuraj k r is a postdoctoral associate at the institute of optics university of rochester working with prof nick vamivakas his research focuses on superresolution imaging statistical and quantum optics and novel frameworks for polarization analysis during his postdoctoral work dr sethuraj successfully demonstrated the experimental realization of supergrowing fields a phenomenon enabling highintensity superresolution imaging he completed his phd at physics department of iit delhi where he made significant contributions to understanding Body: optics and photonics centre opc invites all interested to a series of lectures by wellknown scientists in areas of optics and photonics details of lecture in this series is given below title midinfrared laser absorption spectroscopy on a chip speaker prof jana jagerska affiliation uit the arctic university of norway mode online link date th january wednesday time pm ist abstract optical sensing through spectroscopy is recognized as a promising application of mid infrared photonics aiming to exploit the intense and wellresolved absorption fingerprints of most molecules in the midinfrared spectral range in my presentation i will discuss the primary challenges that midinfrared photonics faces in sensing applications and present solutions derived from over five years of our active research in this area in the second part of my talk i will focus on two innovative waveguide designs that have been applied to sensitive gas detection these designs include slot waveguides and thinfilm membrane waveguides both optimized to i enhance the evanescent field interaction between the guided light and the gas sample while ii minimizing losses and iii suppressing spurious etalons a major sources of noise in dielectric waveguides with these waveguide sensors we have achieved detection of methane and carbon dioxide in the partsper billion ppb range additionally i will showcase the first onchip δ¹³c isotope ratio measurement achieving a precision on the order of ‰ comparable to highend commercial instruments biography jana jágerská is a full professor of photonics at uit the arctic university of norway and a team leader in the field of nanophotonics and laser spectroscopy focusing on midinfrared onchip sensors for trace gas detection regard profpsenthilkumaran head optics and photonics centre indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: reminder photonic lecture series on th january pm
Body: a gentle reminder for the talk today at pm optics and photonics centre opc invites all interested to a series of lectures by wellknown scientists in areas of optics and photonics details of lecture in this series is given below title exploring the exciton complexes in layered materials speaker dr sarthak das affiliation quantum innovation centre institute of materials research and engineering astar in singapore mode opc committee room block iii inperson date th january monday time pm ist abstract layered transition metal dichalcogenides tmdcs exhibit a nexus of strongly bound excitonic complexes that govern their unique optical and electronic properties this talk explores groundbreaking studies on excitonic phenomena in tmdcs focusing on the roles of spin valley and layer degrees of freedom in monolayer tmdcs broken inversion symmetry enables robust excitonic states like trions and biexcitons where we demonstrate that charged biexcitons dominate population densities and enable photocurrent generation at cryogenic temperatures a key study reveals the interplay between bright intralayer and dark interlayer excitons in fewlayer tmdc films uncovering strong layerdependent alternating wavefunction distribution and maintaining high exciton binding energy even in bulk form additionally bilayer ws demonstrates a linear quantumconfined stark effect contrasting with monolayer symmetry enabling tunable excitonic oscillator strength and positioning bilayer ws as an ideal candidate for ultrathin electroabsorption modulators we also report coherent trionmediated interlayer charge transport in ws graphene heterojunctions achieving stable trion states up to k and sub fs device switching times with resonant photocurrent tunable via gate voltage finally pulsed laser excitation creates charged biexcitons in monolayer ws with strong light absorption enabling a highly nonlinear ultrafast photocurrent in a selfpowered mode using these five particle quinton states we have further demonstrated the electrical tuning of the valley polarization with a sixfold increase in the degree of circular polarization the coherent formation between the neutral and charged excitons further overcomes the limitations of the neutral excitons for the practical realization of the valleytronics devices these results demonstrate transformative potential for valleytronics quantum photonics and nonlinear optoelectronics paving the way for compact energyefficient and reconfigurable device applications this work bridges fundamental science and practical engineering highlighting tmdcs as a platform for nextgeneration optoelectronic and quantum technologies biography sarthak das is currently serving as a research scientist and engineer rse at quantum innovation centre qinc part of the institute of materials research and engineering imre astar in singapore since january his area of expertise lies in quantum devices and engineering with layered semiconductors he received his phd from quantum electronics lab at the department of electrical and communications ece indian institute of science iisc bangalore his research primarily focuses on the utilization of lowtemperature spectroscopy techniques such as raman spectroscopy photoluminescence pl and microreflectance measurements to explore the interaction between light and matter in d materials at cryogenic temperatures additionally he possesses practical experience in fabricating heterostructure devices conducting theoretical studiesand employing nonlinear spectroscopy and electrooptical modulation techniques in layered materials currently his research at imre aims to advance the understanding of the fundamental properties of d materials for the development of qubitbased devices particularly in the development and characterization of spin valley qubits in line with singapore’s quantum engineering program s das g gupta and k majumdar physical review b s das prestigious ai early career fellowship an initiative by schmidt sciences this fellowship is designed to support earlycareer researchers working on bold interdisciplinary ai research that addresses the most critical challenges and opportunities for ensuring ai benefits society by fellowship details award size up to over three years purpose to fund specific research projects aligned with the ai hard problems in ai including areas like ai alignment robustness safety interpretability and ai for science goal to empower exceptional researchers to tackle the most pressing problems in ai and make groundbreaking contributions to the field who is eligible for the early career fellowship candidates must hold a phd or equivalent degree candidates must almost always have received their terminal degree after august we are willing to make exceptions however we have a strong preference for the most junior of candidates candidates must be affiliated with a university national laboratory or other nonprofit research institute however ai fellowships do not fund commercial work or those who are or choose to remain in the private sector during their fellowship if faculty candidates must be tenuretrack though untenured or equivalent as of october how to apply if you meet the eligibility criteria and wish to be considered for nomination please fill out the form linked below with your details deadline pm st january nomination process iit delhi will evaluate interested candidates and nominate up to individuals for this fellowship additional information you can learn more about the fellowship and past fellows here ai fellowship website fellowship cohort and projects ai hard problems in ai this fellowship is a unique opportunity to advance your research gain global recognition and join a network of worldclass scholars tackling the future of ai if you have any questions or need further clarification feel free to reach out regards sumit singh general secretary cocurricular and academic interaction council caic iit delhi links

Subject: photonic lecture series on th january pm
Body: optics and photonics centre opc invites all interested to a series of lectures by wellknown scientists in areas of optics and photonics details of lecture in this series is given below title exploring the exciton complexes in layered materials speaker dr sarthak das affiliation quantum innovation centre institute of materials research and engineering astar in singapore mode opc committee room block iii inperson date th january monday time pm ist abstract layered transition metal dichalcogenides tmdcs exhibit a nexus of strongly bound excitonic complexes that govern their unique optical and electronic properties this talk explores groundbreaking studies on excitonic phenomena in tmdcs focusing on the roles of spin valley and layer degrees of freedom in monolayer tmdcs broken inversion symmetry enables robust excitonic states like trions and biexcitons where we demonstrate that charged biexcitons dominate population densities and enable photocurrent generation at cryogenic temperatures a key study reveals the interplay between bright intralayer and dark interlayer excitons in fewlayer tmdc films uncovering strong layerdependent alternating wavefunction distribution and maintaining high exciton binding energy even in bulk form additionally bilayer ws demonstrates a linear quantumconfined stark effect contrasting with monolayer symmetry enabling tunable excitonic oscillator strength and positioning bilayer ws as an ideal candidate for ultrathin electroabsorption modulators we also report coherent trionmediated interlayer charge transport in ws graphene heterojunctions achieving stable trion states up to k and sub fs device switching times with resonant photocurrent tunable via gate voltage finally pulsed laser excitation creates charged biexcitons in monolayer ws with strong light absorption enabling a highly nonlinear ultrafast photocurrent in a selfpowered mode using these five particle quinton states we have further demonstrated the electrical tuning of the valley polarization with a sixfold increase in the degree of circular polarization the coherent formation between the neutral and charged excitons further overcomes the limitations of the neutral excitons for the practical realization of the valleytronics devices these results demonstrate transformative potential for valleytronics quantum photonics and nonlinear optoelectronics paving the way for compact energyefficient and reconfigurable device applications this work bridges fundamental science and practical engineering highlighting tmdcs as a platform for nextgeneration optoelectronic and quantum technologies biography sarthak das is currently serving as a research scientist and engineer rse at quantum innovation centre qinc part of the institute of materials research and engineering imre astar in singapore since january his area of expertise lies in quantum devices and engineering with layered semiconductors he received his phd from quantum electronics lab at the department of electrical and communications ece indian institute of science iisc bangalore his research primarily focuses on the utilization of lowtemperature spectroscopy techniques such as raman spectroscopy photoluminescence pl and microreflectance measurements to explore the interaction between light and matter in d materials at cryogenic temperatures additionally he possesses practical experience in fabricating heterostructure devices conducting theoretical studiesand employing nonlinear spectroscopy and electrooptical modulation techniques in layered materials currently his research at imre aims to advance the understanding of the fundamental properties of d materials for the development of qubitbased devices particularly in the development and characterization of spin valley qubits in line with singapore’s quantum engineering program s das g gupta and k majumdar physical review b s das m dandu g gupta et al acs photonics s kallatt s das s chatterjee et al npj d materials and applications s das s kallatt n abraham et al physical review b s das g gupta s chatterjee et al acs nano s das d huang i verzhbitskiy et al acs nano – regard profpsenthilkumaran head optics and photonics centre indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: seminar on information extraction beyond diffraction limit at high intensity through supergrowth on th jan am
Body: dear all we are organising a talkseminar by dr sethuraj k r from university of rochester in the area of optical imaging and super resolution you are invited to attend this talk details of which are given below best regards bhaskar speaker dr sethuraj k r university of rochester venue physics seminar room ms time am jan title of the talk “information extraction beyond diffraction limit at high intensity through supergrowth” abstract enhancing resolution in imaging science beyond the diffraction limit known as superresolution is critical for applications ranging from medical diagnostics to astronomy in farfield imaging existing superresolution techniques often suffer from substantial photon loss supergrowth a recently demonstrated phenomenon provides a breakthrough by enabling superresolution imaging at high intensity —addressing this limitation this talk delves into the first experimental realization of supergrowing fields and their applications in optical physics i will discuss the interplay between supergrowth and superoscillations advancements in twopoint resolution enhancement and potential applications in ranging technologies like lidar furthermore findings from supergrowth in speckle patterns reveal that fully developed speckles can exhibit nearly supergrowing regions these results pave the way for innovative approaches to extract information beyond the diffraction limit references jordan andrew n et al superphenomena for arbitrary quantum observables physical review a jordan andrew n superresolution using supergrowth and intensity contrast imaging quantum studies mathematics and foundations karmakar tathagata et al supergrowth and subwavelength object imaging optics express kr sethuraj et al experimental realization of supergrowing fields physical review research l viteripflucker valeria et al supergrowth in speckle patterns optics letters brief bio of speaker dr sethuraj k r is a postdoctoral associate at the institute of optics university of rochester working with prof nick vamivakas his research focuses on superresolution imaging statistical and quantum optics and novel frameworks for polarization analysis during his postdoctoral work dr sethuraj successfully demonstrated the experimental realization of supergrowing fields a phenomenon enabling highintensity superresolution imaging he completed his phd at physics department of iit delhi where he made significant contributions to understanding vectorial coherence and polarization properties bhaskar kanseri phd mnasc भास्कर कनसेरी ihfc chair professor department Body: dear all we are pleased to announce that dr parul pandey postdoctoral associate at the jacobs school of medicine and biomedical sciences university of buffalo will be presenting a talk on drbd acts as a transcriptspecific rna editing auxiliary factor in trypanosoma brucei details of the talk date thursday january rd time to am indian standard time am to am january rd new york time pm to pm australian eastern standard time venue ms teams link about the talk this talk will explore the mechanisms of uridine insertiondeletion rna editing in trypanosoma brucei focusing on how rnabinding proteins like drbd influence mrna stability and editing through interactions with editing complexes the study highlights the transcriptspecific role of drbd and its regulation by arginine methylation offering insights into posttranscriptional gene regulation in pathogens about the speaker dr parul pandey is a postdoctoral associate at the jacobs school of medicine and biomedical sciences university of buffalo her research targets rna processing and regulation in trypanosoma brucei through rnabinding proteins during her phd at banaras hindu university she explored sigma factor regulation in azospirillum brasilense contributing to insights on bacterial stress responses and nitrogen fixation dr pandeys work integrates molecular biology and bioinformatics to unravel rna regulatory networks in pathogens we look forward to your active participation in the seminar best regards p vigneswara ilavarasan phd professorincharge of the academy pica university of queensland indian institute of technology delhi research academy room no tx building department of textile and fibre engineering indian institute of technology delhi new delhi india phone email website links

Subject: invited talk by prof sharmistha bhadra mcgill university on biomedical sensing with flexible and solution processedprinted electronics
Body: dear all prof sharmistha bhadra from mcgill university will give an invited talk on tn january friday at the department of electrical engineering the details are as follows date and time th january friday pm onwards venue ee committee room block ii title biomedical sensing with flexible and solution processedprinted electronics abstract flexible electronics has the advantages of light weight portability and ability to fit onto arbitrary curved surfaces without significant changes in their characteristics on the other hand solution processedprinted electronics offers several advantages such as low cost simple as well as low temperature process high throughput and excellent compositional control due to these unique advantages flexible electronics along with solution processingprinting enable innovative lowcost technology for biomedical sensors and wearables in this talk i will present how my research team is utilizing flexible and solution processedprinted electronics for two biomedical sensing applications intraoral biopotential monitoring and photoplethysmography ppg sensing for intraoral biopotential monitoring we are developing lowcost smart intraoral wearables to monitor eeg electroencephalogram or eog electrooculography signal with potential application for sleep study for ppg sensing we are working towards development of a lowcost lowpower ppg sensing system i will identify some of the challenges of utilizing flexible and solution processed electronics for these two applications finally i will discuss about some emerging research areas related to biopotential monitoring or ppg sensing where flexible and solution processed electronics can have enormous potentials biography sharmistha bhadra is currently an associate professor at the in the department of electrical and computer engineering at mcgill university before joining mcgill university she was a natural sciences and engineering research council of canada postdoctoral fellow at the university of british columbia for months her current research interests are in the area of printed and flexible hybrid electronics microelectromechanical systems sensors and wearables and microelectronics her research program at mcgill university leverages conventional design and development tools as well as flexible printed electronics technology to find cost effective and high performance innovative electronic technology she has published over papers and one book chapter and holds patents in sensors and wearables area you are invited to attend the talk and interact with prof bhadra best regards dhiman dr dhiman mallick associate professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india tel o m email web interdisciplinary microsystems lab iml links

Subject: synopsis presentation of nivedita shrivastava monday am
Body: name of the student nivedita shrivastava title of the phd thesis design of secure hardware architectures for neural networks time and venue monday am sit building a ground floor abstract securing deep neural networks dnns is a problem of significant interest since machine learning ml models encapsulate highvalue intellectual property ip for instance collecting raw data for a midsized ai project through platforms like amazon mechanical turk can exceed k usd while the design and refinement of the model architecture and training methodology often represent investments of millions of dollars to ensure the confidentiality of model parameters it is essential to encrypt the model weights and associated parameters given the large size of modern neural network models and increasing demand for fast computation achieving highthroughput and lowlatency encryption becomes critical while aes one of the most popular and secure ciphers is widely adopted its fast ttable based sw implementations are vulnerable to cache sidechannel attacks csca in our first work we systematically analyzed over research papers focusing on the ongoing race between cscas countermeasures cms and counterattacks ctas we prove that while addressbased cms introduce obfuscation they can still be broken in onloglogn time for popular ciphers like aes sadly this bound translates to billions of encryptions to address this issue and reduce the required number of iterations we first propose a theoretical framework to systematically classify the stateoftheart cms based on their impact on the ttable address mapping then we propose a twophase attack framework to efficiently retrieve the secret key even in the presence of advanced cms our proposed attack can retrieve the key in just iterations in spite of stateoftheart cms hence it is necessary to implement encryption in hardware we observed that if the plaintext distribution has sufficient entropy fewer encryption rounds are required to generate ciphertexts and still maintain the same level of security as aes based on some recent results we propose a novel encryption engine that dynamically generates ephemeral keys for each data block we show that our design achieves at least the same security as aes with a x increase in encryption throughput subsequently we considered endtoend secure ml inferencing while trusted execution environments tees such as intel sgx and trustzone can provide a secure onchip execution environment they have very high overheads and are not suitable for memory intensive npus neural processing units the main issue lies in securing offchip data to solve this we extensively analyzed and characterized the offchip memory traffic pattern of different npus and designed a fast hw circuit to leverage these patterns we implemented mechanisms to ensure integrity and freshness of offchip data at the layer level this helped us to design an ultrafast and secure npu which is faster than the stateoftheart in addition to securing model weights we observed that the model architecture parameters themselves are attractive targets for adversariesthese parameters are susceptible to leaks through memory and timingbased side channels to address this we classified existing cms into four categories and observed that these cms primarily introduce additive noise to obfuscate the leaked patterns we show that this is not sufficient by proposing three attacks hence to further enhance security we introduced an additional layer of defense by incorporating multiplicative noise to achieve this we used spacefilling curves to tile compress and bin the data in a secure and efficient manner our proposed design successfully tackles scas and leads to a large search space of to summarize in this thesis we have proposed a comprehensive endtoend security architecture for ml inferencing that protects ml models against all known attacks that are based on direct and sidechannel based approaches smruti ranjan sarangi hitech robotics and autonomous systems chair professor computer science and electrical engineering head educational technology and services center iit delhi hauz khas new delhi ph website

nothing but deceit—these contrasting truths form the foundation of humanity’s most profound art and literature over three exhilarating days literati will transform the campus into a haven of creativity and thought abhinandan sekhri founder of newslaundry will deliver the inaugural keynote on th jan and mita vashisht a prominent indian actress will deliver the closing keynote on th jan we have also lined up three panel discussions discussing various facets of identity in the modern world to whet your creative appetite we have an assortment of quizzes and writing challenges as well as debates and designing competitions the competitions will test your wit creativity and intellect while offering a chance to bond and grow with the process not only this if you want to rekindle your love for books we have a book fair set up right outside lhc with stalls from wellknown bookstores like the oxford bookstore harper collins and preloved books from sisters of the people while visiting the bookfair do be on the lookout for the various word games and trivia related stalls inside lhc that also give you the chance to win a free book or two literati has always been a platform to showcase various forms of creative expression from all facets of life continuing our tradition we have a mushairah event on the th and a stage play drama on the th jan please find attached the updated full schedule for the coming three days join us as we dive into the timeless stories of knights and knaves where every moment is an opportunity to be inspired and every word carries the power to transform we look forward to seeing your participation in the fest note all events are free for iit delhi students you need to bring your id cards with you with love team literati — with warm regards Subject: invitation for vibhinn the lgbtqia pride festival of iit delhi
Body: dear students staff members and faculty greetings from indradhanu the official lgbtqia collective of iit delhi and the office of diversity inclusion we are excited to extend a warm invitation to the third edition of iit delhis lgbtqia pride fest vibhinn our worldview on the diversity of people and cultures is often shaped by our everyday social interaction however as social beings we often remain at odds with information that we believe is uncommon and at times unsettling indradhanu since its inception has worked towards forging dialogues where we turn our attention not merely to human difference but to understand the strength that human diversity provides to us as a community engaging in education vibhinn aims to provide that space for the campus community building on the success and positive reception of our last two editions vibhinn brings five enriching events for everyone this year were excited to collaborate with literati for an illuminating panel on survival expression and liberation in lgbtqia art and literature date event venue time description friday inaugural ceremony seminar hall pm pm the inauguration will consist of a spotlight conversation with justice dr s muralidhar former chief justice of odisha high court and a member judge of the delhi high court bench that decriminalised homosexuality reading down ipc in india for the first time in registration link vibhinn inaugural saturday all india queer collectives conference lh am pm every year iit delhi hosts lgbtq collectives from across the country including other iits and other universities colleges across india the daylong conference brings together students and their stories of making educational campuses more inclusive diverse and accessible this years theme repairing recognition would focus on how constitutional recognition and rights can be envisioned as shared and collective practices for a better future for all registration link vibhinn aiqcc queers got talent lh pm pm following the aiqcc we shall have the queer talent show a joyous celebration of diversity and resilience providing lgbtqia persons and allies a stage for artistic expression registration link vibhinn qgt sunday survival expression and liberation in lgbtqia art and literature literati x vibhinn seminar hall pm pm we aim to explore the interplay of truth and concealment in lgbtqia narratives across literature art and media further we wish to examine how queer stories navigate societal constraints while celebrating truth as a tool for selfexpression and liberation revealing insights into societal biases norms and aspirations pride march walk of remembrance nalanda grounds to central library pm pm we shall conclude vibhinn with a pride march where members of the lgbtqia community allies from the campus and other participants come together to promote greater acceptance visibility and solidarity registration link vibhinn march were thrilled to announce strides for pride a queerthemed exhibit in the canopy walkway connecting the main building and lhc this exhibit will showcase key elements of queer history marriage equality the evolution of pride flags and iconic figures of the lgbtqia movement dont miss this celebration of pride and progress if you have any inquiries regarding certain accessibility needs or require further information please do not hesitate to contact the following core committee members raavya himanshu indradhanu awaits your active participation in vibhinn best regards rahul bhardwaj ph sac representative indradhanu core committee member vibhinn Subject: civil engineering seminar series professor omar wani from the new york university usa scheduled on monday th january at pm
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the civil engineering seminar by professor omar wani from the new york university usa scheduled on monday th january at pm in committee room block iv room no department of civil engineering at indian institute of technology iit delhi title of the seminar understanding the dynamics of hydrologic risk using explainable parsimonious models abstract of the seminar human settlements and infrastructure in the vicinity of streams and rivers face both flood and erosional risks fluvial floods happen when discharge exceeds the carrying capacity of rivers and the lateral migration of rivers is a consequence of sustained bank erosion there is a large body of scientific literature on modeling the dominant mechanisms that drive these hydrologic and geomorphic responses however it is still challenging to make accurate predictions of both the river discharge and the resulting riverbank migration in this talk the speaker will discuss how using relatively parsimonious but explainable models equipped with the ease of performing monte carlo simulations can produce very insightful and more reliable assessments of hydrologic risk and its spatiotemporal dynamics the first part of the talk presents a probabilistic framework for generating rivermigration risk maps using smooth random functions the second part explores conditional risk in distributed stormwater infrastructure systems discussing it within the context of large culverts in the northeastern united states biographical sketch of the speaker dr omar wani is an assistant professor of environmental engineering at the new york university nyu in the usa where he leads the hydrologic systems group his research work entails advanced statistical and computational modeling of various water and waterinfrastructure systems in both built and natural environments before joining nyu dr wani conducted his postdoctoral work at the california institute of technology caltechs division of geological and planetary sciences and the university of california berkeley ucbs environmental systems dynamics laboratory dr wani has a phd degree in environmental engineering from eth zurich switzerland a joint masters degree from the delft institute for water education the netherlands and the technical university of dresden germany and a bachelors degree in civil engineering from the indian institute of technology iit roorkee india all interested are cordially invited to attend the seminar thank you head department of civil engineering indian institute of technology iit delhi Subject: spp invitation to talk on navigating climate finance insights from evaluations of the green climate fund
Body: dear all you are warmly invited to an insightful talk by dr archi rastogi chief evaluation advisor at the independent evaluation unit ieu of the green climate fund gcf this session promises to delve into the evolving landscape of climate finance and the critical role of evaluations in driving impact and innovation details of the talk topic navigating climate finance insights from evaluations of the green climate fund date friday january time pm pm venue lhc room brief bio of the speaker dr archi rastogi serves as the chief evaluation advisor at the independent evaluation unit ieu of the green climate fund gcf the worlds largest multilateral climate fund dr rastogi has worked at the interface of science and decisionmaking and most recently through policy evaluations he began his career at a grassroots nonprofit and has since worked in the media the un management consulting and multilateral organizations besides the academia he has undertaken nearly evaluations to advise the world bank un bodies bilateral agencies philanthropies governments development agencies and research agencies these evaluations are directed to provide evidence to decisionmakers at the gcf he was a task lead for the development of the evaluation policy for the institution providing a clear space for the use of evidence in policy making his research has variably looked into the social factors affecting effectiveness of policies and programmes for sustainable development his current research interests include the development of multilateral institutions effectiveness of climate finance and the role of value systems in decisionmaking he is a member of the editorial board for the journal society and natural resources and has served on the intergovernmental panel on biodiversity and ecosystem services he holds an adjunct appointment at the national university of singapore abstract in the dynamic and growing landscape of climate finance how do policy evaluations drive impact and innovation this presentation examines the intersection of global climate finance evaluation practices and institutional learning through the lens of the green climate fund gcf it begins with an overview of global climate finance flows and emerging trends in multilateral funding mechanisms followed by an exploration of the gcfs unique mandate governance and evaluation framework the role of the independent evaluation unit ieu in delivering objective highimpact assessments is highlighted along with key lessons on country ownership direct access challenges and institutional capacity to demonstrate the practical value of evaluations the presentation features a realworld example an evaluation of waterorgs initiatives showcasing how evidencebased insights inform funding decisions the discussion concludes with systemic challenges such as delays in project accreditation and implementation offering actionable recommendations to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of multilateral climate finance we look forward to your participation best regards anshu anshu ogra phd assistant professor school of public policy indian institute of technology delhi iitd associate editor at regional environmental change links

Subject: invitation for a talk on what is quantum machine learning and is it useful in industry
Body: dear all you are invited to attend an exciting talk on what is quantum machine learning and is it useful in industry by dr rajiv krishnakumar quantum algorithms researcher at quantumbasel switzerland with details as follows date friday jan time pm venue bharti abstract in this talk the speaker will introduce quantum machine learning and discuss some ideas for which the community is trying to understand if it will be useful the speaker will also take the excuse to present the company – quantumbasel – and discuss a bit about how they are trying to answer this question from an industry point of view and how that differs from academia speaker bio rajiv krishnakumar is a quantum algorithms researcher working at quantumbasel he has been in the quantum algorithms space for the past years his current interests are in understanding how quantum computing can help enhance current ai algorithms in particular investigating quantum enhancements to reservoir computing to solve time series and classification problems previously rajiv was at goldman sachs where he first worked as a data scientist on the trading floor before transitioning to the rd team where he worked as a quantum algorithms researcher on applications of quantum computing for finance usecases prior to his career in the private sector rajiv obtained his phd in applied physics from stanford university where he worked on quantum sensors after which he pursued a brief postdoctoral fellowship on quantum technologies joint with caltech and att google calendar link thanks and regards dr neel kanth kundu assistant professor care iit delhi web

Subject: re talk by dr zilong liu on waveform design for isac january am
Body: we are starting original message subject re talk by dr zilong liu on waveform design for isac january am date from gourab ghatak to dear all a gentle reminder for this talk scheduled at am today venue iia bharti school regards gourab original message subject re talk by dr zilong liu on waveform design for isac january am date from gourab ghatak to dear all please note that the venue of the following talk is being shifted to the room iia in the bharti school regards gourab original message subject talk by dr zilong liu on waveform design for isac january am date from gourab ghatak to dear all we are happy to host dr zilong liu from the university of essex for a seminar the details are as follows and attached please mark your calendars title waveform design for integrated sensing and communications isac date th january time am pm venue iia bharti school speaker zilong liu school of csee university of essex abstract a fundamental research problem in isac is how to design optimalgood waveforms for efficient enabling of both sensing and communications in the first part of this talk i will introduce a novel multicarrier isac waveform having low peaktoaverage power ratio property we consider a flexible and generic isac structure in which a number of noncontiguous subbands for data transmission are located in a large contiguous spectrum band optimization is carried out for those noncommunication subcarriers with the aid of the majorizationminimization method in the second part i will introduce several families of sensing sequences for lowcomplexity delaydoppler estimation in isac systems fundamental limits and systematic constructions of these sequences will be presented regards gourab

Subject: invitation for vibhinn the lgbtqia pride festival of iit delhi
Body: dear students staff members and faculty greetings from indradhanu the official lgbtqia collective of iit delhi and the office of diversity inclusion we are excited to extend a warm invitation to the third edition of iit delhis lgbtqia pride fest vibhinn our worldview on the diversity of people and cultures is often shaped by our everyday social interaction however as social beings we often remain at odds with information that we believe is uncommon and at times unsettling indradhanu since its inception has worked towards forging dialogues where we turn our attention not merely to human difference but to understand the strength that human diversity provides to us as a community engaging in education vibhinn aims to provide that space for the campus community building on our last two editions success and positive reception vibhinn has four enriching events in store for everyone friday inaugural ceremony the inauguration will consist of a spotlight conversation with justice dr s murlidhar former chief justice of odisha high court and a member judge of the delhi high court bench that decriminalised homosexuality reading down ipc in india for the first time in registration link vibhinn inaugural saturday all india queer collectives conference every year iit delhi hosts lgbtq collectives from across the country including other iits and other universities colleges across india the daylong conference brings together students and their stories of making educational campuses more inclusive diverse and accessible this years theme repairing recognition would focus on how constitutional recognition and rights can be envisioned as shared and collective practices for a better future for all registration link vibhinn aiqcc queers got talent following the aiqcc we shall have the queer talent show a joyous celebration of diversity and resilience providing lgbtqia persons and allies a stage for artistic expression registration link vibhinn qgt sunday pride march walk of remembrance we shall conclude vibhinn with a pride march where members of the lgbtqia community allies from the campus and other participants come together to promote greater acceptance visibility and solidarity registration link vibhinn march if you have any inquiries regarding certain accessibility needs or require further information please do not hesitate to contact the following core committee members raavya himanshu indradhanu awaits your active participation in vibhinn regards rahul bhardwaj ph sac representative indradhanu core committee member vibhinn indian institute of technology delhi links

Subject: dmse departmental seminar by prof anirudh natarajan epfl on th jan at pm
Body: dear all i hope you had an exciting start to the new semester department of material science and engineering is having a seminar by prof anirudh natarajan from epfl switzerland the seminar is on friday th january from pm we hope you can join us for this exciting talk here are the details of the talk title computational tools for the ab initio design of multicomponent alloys date and time friday th january pm venue room no dmse committee room academic complex west b speaker prof anirudh natarajan epfl abstract materials used in highperformance engineering applications are carefully designed to achieve optimal mechanical properties and chemical durability however relationships between alloy chemistry processing strategies and material properties remain unclear in this talk i will highlight recent advances in computational materials science that enable the rigorous and rational design of highperformance engineering alloys firstprinciples calculations will be used together with machinelearning and statistical mechanics techniques to rigorously describe the thermodynamic and kinetic properties of multicomponent alloys we will highlight the use of these computational techniques in designing refractory alloys for hightemperature applications as well as aluminum and magnesium alloys for lightweight structural applications the techniques and results presented in this talk provide important insights for the design of advanced structural alloys bio anirudh received a btech in metallurgical and materials engineering from the indian institute of technology madras a ms in materials science and engineering from the university of michigan ann arbor and a phd in materials from the university of california santa barbara he set up the laboratory of materials design and simulation mades at epfl in his research interests are in the computational design and discovery of advanced engineering materials thanks harsha n s harsha gunda assistant professor department of materials science and engineering indian institute of technology delhi

Subject: re talk by dr zilong liu on waveform design for isac january am
Body: dear all please note that the venue of the following talk is being shifted to the room iia in the bharti school regards gourab original message subject talk by dr zilong liu on waveform design for isac january am date from gourab ghatak to dear all we are happy to host dr zilong liu from the university of essex for a seminar the details are as follows and attached please mark your calendars title waveform design for integrated sensing and communications isac date th january time am pm venue iia bharti school speaker zilong liu school of csee university of essex abstract a fundamental research problem in isac is how to design optimalgood waveforms for efficient enabling of both sensing and communications in the first part of this talk i will introduce a novel multicarrier isac waveform having low peaktoaverage power ratio property we consider a flexible and generic isac structure in which a number of noncontiguous subbands for data transmission are located in a large contiguous spectrum band optimization is carried out for those noncommunication subcarriers with the aid of the majorizationminimization method in the second part i will introduce several families of sensing sequences for lowcomplexity delaydoppler estimation in isac systems fundamental limits and systematic constructions of these sequences will be presented regards gourab

Subject: re invitation to lecture by the united nations secretarygenerals envoy on technology on th jan
Body: dear all this is a gentle reminder entry has opened please join dear students and colleagues we are delighted to invite you to a lecture by the united nations secretarygenerals envoy on technology mr amandeep gill on th january pm in seminar hall at iit delhi please register title of the lecture new direction for technology governance abstract the united nations secretarygenerals envoy on technology will explore the current landscape of technology and ai governance highlighting the diverse approaches and regulatory frameworks being adopted worldwide with special attention to the unique challenges faced by the global south he will describe the importance of the decision on ai governance taken in the global digital compact gdc in september including the establishment of an international scientific panel a policy dialogue and initiatives to build capacity to address the ai divide he will emphasize the importance of youth engagement in the implementation of the gdc and highlight their crucial role in shaping the development of technology and managing its significant impact on societies so that all humanity benefits about the speaker mr amandeep singh gill was appointed undersecretary general and the united nations secretarygenerals envoy on technology in june in this role he spearheads the secretarygenerals strategic initiatives in technology facilitates coordination across the un system and engages with a diverse array of stakeholders and partners globally he is also a member of the secretarygenerals high level advisory body on ai and of his scientific advisory board his extensive experience in technology and diplomacy includes serving as executive director and colead of the un secretarygenerals highlevel panel on digital cooperation and as indias ambassador and permanent representative to the conference on disarmament in geneva mr gills academic credentials include a phd from kings college london a b tech from panjab university chandigarh and an advanced diploma in french history and language from geneva university he has authored two books nuclear security summits a history springer and you are never too far poems on the path wisdom tree in recognition of his influential work in the field of artificial intelligence time magazine named mr gill one of the most influential people in ai in fluent in english french hindi and punjabi mr gill brings a multicultural perspective to his work instructions for the event entry starts at pm and closes at full occupancy but not later than pm please make sure to bring your iitd i card you are requested not to carry any belongings except wallet and mobile phones looking forward to welcoming you best regards shilpi sharma associate dean academics outreach new initiatives batch of chair professor department of biochemical engineering and biotechnology indian institute of technology delhi new delhi shilpi sharma sheher associate dean academics outreach new initiatives batch Subject: mathematics colloquium on january wednesday at m in room no academic complex west b
Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department colloquium by prof viswanathan arunachalam national university of colombia bogotá colombia on january wednesday the details are given below speaker prof viswanathan arunachalam national university of colombia bogotá colombia date time th jan between and pm venue room no academic complex west b title of the talk an updated estimation method for epidemic models with stochastic perturbations abstract in this talk we present the updated estimation method to improve the forecasts for the population dynamics under seir epidemic models with stochastic perturbations the models for the population dynamics under seir epidemic models with stochastic perturbations are analyzed for the dynamics of the covid pandemic in bogotá and acute respiratory infectionari driven by the particulate matter pm and pm on the air quality due to climate change in bogotá colombia computational experiments for the stochastic model with random perturbations were performed and the model parameters were updated in their estimates all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team

Subject: mathematics colloquium on january friday at am in room no academic complex west b
Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department colloquium by prof manil t mohan iit roorkee on january friday the details are given below title title large deviations for the twotimescale stochastic convective brinkmanforchheimer equations date january friday time am venue room no academic complex west b speaker prof manil t mohan iit roorkee abstract the convective brinkmanforchheimer cbf equations are employed to characterise the motion of incompressible fluid in a saturated porous medium this talk investigates the small noise asymptotic of twotimescale stochastic cbf equations in two and three dimensional bounded domains more precisely we establish a wentzellfreidlin type large deviation principle for stochastic partial differential equations that have slow and fast timescales the slow component is the stochastic cbf equations in two or three dimensions perturbed by a small multiplicative gaussian noise while the fast component is a stochastic reactiondiffusion equation with damping the results are obtained by using a variational method based on weak convergence approach developed by budhiraja and dupuis khasminkiis time discretization approach and stopping time arguments in particular the findings from this study are also applicable to twodimensional stochastic navierstokes equations all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team

Subject: mathematics colloquium on january wednesdays at m in room no academic complex west b
Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department colloquium by dr neha nanda université caen normandie on january wednesdays the details are given below title rightangled artin groups are symmetric diagram groups date january wednesdays time pm venue room no academic complex west b speaker dr neha nanda université caen normandie abstract guba and sapir introduced a family of groups associated with semigroup presentations which are called symmetric and planar diagram groups in this talk we introduce diagram groups and discuss how rightangled artin groups can be seen as symmetric diagram groups in contrast to the fact that not all rightangled artin groups are planar diagram groups this was motivated by the example of pure virtual planar braid groups being symmetric diagram groups this is a joint work with paolo bellingeri and anthony genevois all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team

Subject: talk by dr zilong liu on waveform design for isac january am
Body: dear all we are happy to host dr zilong liu from the university of essex for a seminar the details are as follows and attached please mark your calendars title waveform design for integrated sensing and communications isac date th january time am pm venue ee committee room speaker zilong liu school of csee university of essex abstract a fundamental research problem in isac is how to design optimalgood waveforms for efficient enabling of both sensing and communications in the first part of this talk i will introduce a novel multicarrier isac waveform having low peaktoaverage power ratio property we consider a flexible and generic isac structure in which a number of noncontiguous subbands for data transmission are located in a large contiguous spectrum band optimization is carried out for those noncommunication subcarriers with the aid of the majorizationminimization method in the second part i will introduce several families of sensing sequences for lowcomplexity delaydoppler estimation in isac systems fundamental limits and systematic constructions of these sequences will be presented regards gourab

Subject: invitation to lecture by the united nations secretarygenerals envoy on technology on th jan
Body: dear students and colleagues we are delighted to invite you to a lecture by the united nations secretarygenerals envoy on technology mr amandeep gill on th january pm in seminar hall at iit delhi please register title of the lecture new direction for technology governance abstract the united nations secretarygenerals envoy on technology will explore the current landscape of technology and ai governance highlighting the diverse approaches and regulatory frameworks being adopted worldwide with special attention to the unique challenges faced by the global south he will describe the importance of the decision on ai governance taken in the global digital compact gdc in september including the establishment of an international scientific panel a policy dialogue and initiatives to build capacity to address the ai divide he will emphasize the importance of youth engagement in the implementation of the gdc and highlight their crucial role in shaping the development of technology and managing its significant impact on societies so that all humanity benefits about the speaker mr amandeep singh gill was appointed undersecretary general and the united nations secretarygenerals envoy on technology in june in this role he spearheads the secretarygenerals strategic initiatives in technology facilitates coordination across the un system and engages with a diverse array of stakeholders and partners globally he is also a member of the secretarygenerals high level advisory body on ai and of his scientific advisory board his extensive experience in technology and diplomacy includes serving as executive director and colead of the un secretarygenerals highlevel panel on digital cooperation and as indias ambassador and permanent representative to the conference on disarmament in geneva mr gills academic credentials include a phd from kings college london a b tech from panjab university chandigarh and an advanced diploma in french history and language from geneva university he has authored two books nuclear security summits a history springer and you are never too far poems on the path wisdom tree in recognition of his influential work in the field of artificial intelligence time magazine named mr gill one of the most influential people in ai in fluent in english french hindi and punjabi mr gill brings a multicultural perspective to his work instructions for the event entry starts at pm and closes at full occupancy but not later than pm please make sure to bring your iitd i card you are requested not to carry any belongings except wallet and mobile phones looking forward to welcoming you best regards shilpi sharma associate dean academics outreach new initiatives batch of chair professor department of biochemical engineering and biotechnology indian institute of technology delhi new delhi

Subject: reminder invited talk by dr mansi sood january pm to pm bharti school room
Body: a gentle reminder for the invited talk tomorrow january pm to pm bharti school room swades de phd professor of department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india ph work url webiitdacinswadesd cnrgiitdacin on swades de wrote dear all dr mansi sood a schmidt science fellow at mit will give an invited talk on january in bharti school the details are as follows datetime january pm to pm venue bharti school room title balancing sparsity and connectivity in distributed network design with random kout graphs abstract in several applications in distributed systems an important design criterion is ensuring that the network is sparse ie does not contain too many edges while achieving reliable connectivity eg to facilitate reliable communication convergence and privacy guarantees for distributed algorithms a class of network models known as ‘random kout graphs’ widely appear as a heuristic to balance connectivity and sparsity especially in settings with limited trust eg privacypreserving distributed aggregation however the implications of operational constraints such as node heterogeneity and failures on the connectivity of random kout graphs remain underexplored to address this gap we present deployable theorems to inform the choice of network parameters that guarantee reliable connectivity in regimes where nodes can be finite heterogeneous or unreliable our results underscore the usefulness of random kout graphs as a tool for balancing sparsity and connectivity in distributed network design bio mansi sood is a schmidt science fellow at the mit laboratory for information and decision systems working with devavrat shah since fall before this she received her phd in electrical and computer engineering at carnegie mellon university and completed her b tech and mtech in electrical engineering at the indian institute of technology iit bombay india her research interests span stochastic modeling network science and inference particularly in the context of complex sociotechnical systems that have an increasing grip on society and our everyday lives her work won a best paper award at the ieee international conference on communications icc ‘ a graduation day award in information theory and applications and she has been twice recognized as an eecs rising star mit ‘ and georgia tech ‘ for her contributions to outreach and mentorship she has been recognized with an unsung hero award at cmu the advanced graduate ambassadorship of the institute for advanced study ias princeton and excellence in research and mentorship at iit bombay you are invited to attend the talk and interact with the researcher regards swades de

Subject: city design vulnerability new course announcement for spring
From: head transportation research and injury prevention centre
Body: dear all it is with great pleasure we announce that dunu roy dr anubrotto k roy adjunct faculty with the trip centre is offering a threecredit course this spring semester called city design and vulnerability the vulnerable road user in the city registration for the course is through the erp with details as below course no trl c course title on erp special topics in mobility and traffic safety course coordinator prof girish agrawal credits prerequisite none days times m th am venue ms a take the elevator to the th floor and walk up the ramp until you run out of ramp course description most of humanitys cultural economic political and social accomplishments are said to have been led by the cities the urban population of the world has grown rapidly from about million in to billion in this trend is expected to continue with the urban population more than doubling its current size by at which point nearly of people will live in cities this course aims to empower students to examine the city as a node of power within a global system using its movement to unfold multiple perspectives we will do a series of readings ranging from history sociology engineering architecture arts geography economics and anthropology among others as well as explore the lived experience around us as individuals as well as citizens urban areas are centres of power but can power exist without nonpower so we shall examine the vulnerabilities of cities as well and the linkage between the two we will explore the dynamics of cities between powerful and powerless to understand what are the possible laws of motion of urbanization in india in a range of contexts the most visible motion in a city is the movement of people so we will talk about different modes of transportation and the vulnerabilities implicit within them we will then debate whether the powerful and the vulnerable see the city in multiple ways within the context of social economic and cultural access girish agrawal jd phd professor trip centre indian institute of technology delhi regards office of the head transportation research and injury prevention centre tripc room no ms th floor main building indian Subject: invited talk by dr mansi sood january pm to pm bharti school room
Body: dear all dr mansi sood a schmidt science fellow at mit will give an invited talk on january in bharti school the details are as follows datetime january pm to pm venue bharti school room title balancing sparsity and connectivity in distributed network design with random kout graphs abstract in several applications in distributed systems an important design criterion is ensuring that the network is sparse ie does not contain too many edges while achieving reliable connectivity eg to facilitate reliable communication convergence and privacy guarantees for distributed algorithms a class of network models known as ‘random kout graphs’ widely appear as a heuristic to balance connectivity and sparsity especially in settings with limited trust eg privacypreserving distributed aggregation however the implications of operational constraints such as node heterogeneity and failures on the connectivity of random kout graphs remain underexplored to address this gap we present deployable theorems to inform the choice of network parameters that guarantee reliable connectivity in regimes where nodes can be finite heterogeneous or unreliable our results underscore the usefulness of random kout graphs as a tool for balancing sparsity and connectivity in distributed network design bio mansi sood is a schmidt science fellow at the mit laboratory for information and decision systems working with devavrat shah since fall before this she received her phd in electrical and computer engineering at carnegie mellon university and completed her b tech and mtech in electrical engineering at the indian institute of technology iit bombay india her research interests span stochastic modeling network science and inference particularly in the context of complex sociotechnical systems that have an increasing grip on society and our everyday lives her work won a best paper award at the ieee international conference on communications icc ‘ a graduation day award in information theory and applications and she has been twice recognized as an eecs rising star mit ‘ and georgia tech ‘ for her contributions to outreach and mentorship she has been recognized with an unsung hero award at cmu the advanced graduate ambassadorship of the institute for advanced study ias princeton and excellence in research and mentorship at iit bombay you are invited to attend the talk and interact with the researcher regards swades de swades de phd professor of department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india ph work url webiitdacinswadesd Subject: seminar on th december at pm in lh by srinivasan g srivilliputhur on additive manufacturing
Body: dear all you are invited to a seminar with the following details title additive manufacturing of ceramicmetal composite coatings the example of b c on steel speaker srinivasan g srivilliputhur department of materials science and engineering university of north texas denton usa date thursday th december time pm venue lh abstract composites of engineering ceramic materials such as boron carbide b c silicon nitride si n with steels and other alloys are widely applicable in technologies that require high strengths and performance at elevated temperatures however the poor sinterability of b c and si n makes their manufacturing challenging rapidly emerging additive manufacturing am techniques offer significant potential for fabricating ceramicmetal composites by exploiting nonequilibrium processing pathways yet adopting am methods is complicated by the inherent brittleness of ceramics and the substantial differences in thermal expansion coefficients melting points and other properties of ceramics and metals this talk will focus on using laser surface engineering to create a nanocarbide composite coating on a low carbon steel substrate two powder precursors b c and b c wt fe were used with different laser powers and processing speeds a smooth crackfree coating was achieved with b c wt fe powder precursors the phase evolution and microstructure of the coating were studied using xray diffraction scanning electron microscopy and transmission electron microscopy these studies revealed a fine dendritic microstructure with afe phase dendrites and nanosized b c precipitates while interdendritic regions largely contained fe b and fe c phases the retention of b c in the coating was only observed at high laser power and scanning speed due to the lower thermodynamic stability of b c compared to fe b and fe c as confirmed with density functional theory calculations the coatings hardness increased nearly sevenfold compared to the steel substrate due to formation of highhardness ceramic phases and the refinement of the microstructure this nanocomposite coating shows high potential for advance engineering applications requiring thick hard coatings

Subject: seminar on safe hypotheses testing with prof ori davidov
Body: polite reminder title safe hypotheses testing with application to order restricted inference and beyond speaker prof ori davidov date dec time noon pm venue iia bharti school building online link original message subject seminar on safe hypotheses testing with prof ori davidov date from seminar to allfaculty allstudents dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department seminar by prof ori davidov from the department of statistics university of haifa israel on dec the details are given below title safe hypotheses testing with application to order restricted inference and beyond abstract hypothesis testing problems are fundamental to the theory and practice of statistics it is well known that when the union of the null and the alternative does not encompass the full parameter space the possibility of a type iii error arises ie the null hypothesis may be rejected when neither the null nor the alternative are true in such situations common in the context of order restricted inference the validity of our inferences may be severely compromised the study of the geometry of the distancetest a test widely used in constrained inference illuminates circumstances in which type iii errors arise and motivates the introduction of safe tests heuristically a safe test is a test which at least asymptotically is free of type iii errors a novel safe test is proposed and studied the new testing procedure is associated with a certificate of validity a pretest indicating whether the original hypotheses are consistent with the data consequently type iii errors can be addressed in a principled way and constrained tests can be carried out without fear of systematically incorrect inferences although we focus on testing problems arising in order restricted inference the underlying ideas are more broadly applicable the benefits associated with the proposed methodology are demonstrated by simulations and the analysis of several illustrative examples date dec time noon pm venue iia bharti school building speaker prof ori davidov you can read more about the speaker at all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team links

Subject: civil engineering seminar series professor prashant kumar from the university of surrey guildford surrey united kingdom scheduled on monday rd december at am
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the civil engineering seminar by professor prashant kumar from the university of surrey guildford surrey united kingdom scheduled on monday rd december at am in committee room block iv room no department of civil engineering title of the seminar unlocking the potential of naturebased solutions for air pollution and climate mitigation abstract of the seminar following the cuban missile crisis president john f kennedy famously remarked in his a strategy for peace speech we all breathe the same air we all cherish our childrens future and we are all mortal but is this true my lifes work questions this very premise and i fear the answer is no many vulnerable individuals breathe air that is far more hazardous than others this disparity is often underestimated this talk will delve into this issue presenting key findings from several gcare projects over the past two decades such as reclaim network plus gp streets greencities inhale healthy sailing iscape cotrace and samhe focused on indooroutdoor environments and both active and passive solutions using naturebased solutions for air pollution and climate adaptation this talk will also showcase the extensive work of the gcare team including the guildford living lab which has developed guidance tools policy briefs and codesigned naturebased solutions for mitigating air pollution and climate change it will further explore how various communities particularly vulnerable groups like the elderly and children are exposed to air pollution in different environments additionally professor prashant kumar will discuss how passive solutions can serve as effective exposure control strategies alongside policy changes aimed at promoting behavioral shifts brief biography of the speaker professor prashant kumar is chair in air quality and health the founding director of the global centre for clean air research gcare the founding codirector of the institute for sustainability and the founder of guilford living lab and the trustee of zero carbon guildford he obtained his phd engineering from the university of cambridge uk after winning a cambridgenehru scholarship and overseas research scholarship award he earned his masters degree in environmental engineering and management from the indian institute of technology iit delhi where he secured cgpa and won the outstanding postgraduate student award for his exemplary performance winner of the haagensmit clean air award regarded as the nobel prize in clean air achievements he was recognised as a top highly cited researcher by clarivate in and he received the university of surreys vicechancellor award for researcher of the year in and his paper on green infrastructure won the haagen smit prize for best paper from elsevier with over journal articles published in prestigious journals like science nature cities and chemical society reviews he has garnered citations hindex i index he has successfully secured over £ m in individual research funding from ukri including roles as principal investigator on the £ m reclaim network plus and £ m gp streets projects as well as support from industry and international organizations his research frequently appears in prominent media outlets including the bbc and the times kindly visit for more information all interested are cordially Subject: talk by dr gourab majumdar mitsubishi electric corp japan
Body: dear all a technical talk is titled silicon and wbg power semiconductors for power electronics trends impacts and challenges” by dr gourab majumdar senior fellow power device works mitsubishi electric corporation japan is scheduled on rd december the details of the talk is given below date december time am location ee committee room block ii title silicon and wbg power semiconductors for power electronics trends impacts and challenges abstract in the field of power electronics the design and implementation of power converters are undergoing significant changes due to the increasing global demand for electrification across various transportation methods and the collective push for energy conservation to address climate change issues silicon si insulated gate bipolar transistors igbts are the most commonly used power semiconductors for medium to high power conversion applications however this trend is shifting with the emergence of widebandgap wbg devices particularly those based on silicon carbide sic and gallium nitride gan the notable enhancement in electrical performance has resulted from the optimized use of silicon including both vertical and horizontal structural improvements these optimizations involve smaller feature sizes which lead to higher cell densities and new trench gate structures as well as vertical adjustments to minimize the drift layer and significantly reduce the bulk substrate material as a result devices developed with these technologies have significantly reduced overall operating losses while increasing switching frequencies and the efficiencies of power conversion systems used across various industries and services the ongoing development of these mainstream technologies aims to enhance the performancetocost ratio of key power devices such as igbts fastrecovery and schottky diodes mosfets and superjunction devices whether based on si sic or gan moreover sic and gan power devices including power modules are being extensively researched for future highefficiency power switching systems with the growing demand for electrification in the automotive industry the potential applications of these new devices are being thoroughly explored prototypes of functional transistors utilizing these widebandgap materials have demonstrated superior performance and significant potential therefore it is crucial to review the main features and advantages of si sic and ganbased power devices and modules as well as to identify the most commonly used alternatives in medium to high power conversion systems this presentation aims to provide an overview of the trends in si sic and gan power semiconductor technologies that are evolving to meet the needs of various key industries and to address the challenges ahead you are requested to attend this talk a short biography of the speaker is attached with this email best wishes dr sumit pramanick associate professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi new delhi india website phone o ￼
