Subject: final reminder uberstar and she invitation
Body: final reminder at uber we believe thatgreat minds don’t think alikea principle that fuels our commitment to diversity and inclusivity in the tech industry every march we host she a professional development summit to empower women and people from underserved communities to find and achieve their career ambitions fostering a community for the next generation in tech network with our leaders meet peers near you attend professional development sessions and explore life at uber she and uberstar uberstar is an initiative to provide earlycareer engineering internship opportunities to individuals from traditionally underrepresented populations in the technology industry the ultimate goal is to transition uberstar interns into our broader tech internship program and eventually into fulltime engineering roles at uber participants in she go through a selection process starting with a coding assessment and progressing to interview rounds to identify candidates for the uberstar program after completing their uberstar internship they undergo the same evaluation process as regular interns based on their manager’s recommendation they may be invited to return the following year for a summer internship paving the way for a potential fulltime career at uber what’s new this year to foster greater inclusivity and broaden our approach to diversity beyond gender we are welcoming students from a wide range of backgrounds this includes individuals who identify with disabilities members of the lgbt community and students from economically weaker sections by extending this opportunity to colleges across india we aim to provide these students with valuable insights into the world of technology and the possibilities of a career with uber what to expect watch this video to hear from our previous she participants watch now❯ she event details event date march registration deadline dec th pm all registered students will be required to appear for an online screening test on register now

Subject: me guest talk by dr anup barai from wmg the university of warwick uk
Body: dear all dr anup barai associate professor reader from wmg the university of warwick uk will be visiting iit delhi and a mechanical engineering guest talk is scheduled as below date wednesday th december time pm venue me committee room ii title of the talk novel battery thermal runaway prognostics methodology for electric and hybrid aircraft abstract zeroemission air travel is a reality thanks to the recent development and investment in electric vertical takeoff and landing evtol and electric conventional takeoff and landing ectol aircraft currently being developed certified and currently operating current lithiumion battery technologies have made this a reality battery safety diagnostics and prognosis recently received a major research focus for this new application the key challenges to realise this are hardware limitations lack of data for aibased software solution development and scalability of low trl research at cell level to pack in addition little low trl fundamental research has been done to perform battery safety prognosis in this presentation dr barai will focus on these challenges building on that methodologies already developed which could be implemented to perform battery thermal runaway prognosis will be discussed a spillover benefit of such methods will be their application for repurposing endoflife ev batteries for repurposing often grading and sorting of battery cells and modules for remanufacturing a nd life battery pack are essential the diagnosis techniques can be applied for rapid costeffective grading of eol ev battery modules this presentation will also discuss this aspect bio sketch since joining wmg in august dr anup barai has established a successful research theme in the area of developing methodologies for next generation characterisation of energy storage system for transport and stationary applications dr barai delivers research which has a tangible impact on industrial and academic researchers success making fundamental changes in the way energy storage systems are characterised in the past he delivered multiple commercial research packages authored high impact journal articles and led funded research projects in the area of lithiumion battery characterisation prior to joining wmg anup graduated with a firstclass msc degree in embedded systems design and a bsc honours degree in electrical and electronic engineering while working full time for wmg anup studied parttime for a phd degree which he completed in february he has developed novel characterisation techniques and enhanced existing tools for use within the automotive rail marine and aerospace sectors he is currently leading battery performance and safety testing and characterisationrelated research at wmg all interested are welcome to join the talk thanks and regards dr abhishek das assistant professor department of mechanical engineering iit delhi hauz khas new delhi india

society by dr brian oshea date from to allfaculty allstudents allstaff dear all the initiative for caste equity ice office of diversity and inclusion and the scst cell cordially invites to a seminar on understanding unconsciousimplicitautomatic biases in society by dr brian oshea school of psychology university of nottingham and scientific advisor project implicit harvard university date and time pm wednesday december venue lh link to join online title understanding unconsciousimplicitautomatic biases in society abstract understanding social and healthrelated biases in society are important for developing interventions the online project implicit platform has been gathering data from millions of people each year that can offer important insight into regional variation and changes in biases over time this talk will introduce you to this valuable resource and the insights we have gained to date bio dr brian oshea phd warwick is an assistant professor in the school of psychology at university of nottingham and scientific advisor for project implicit and project implicit health at harvard university his work explores how group memberships and identities shape attitudes and behavior with particular attention to prejudice discrimination and social justice a key area of his research is his involvement in project implicit an international network of researchers studying implicit cognitionautomatic thoughts and feelings that often operate outside of conscious awareness dr osheas work in this area contributes to understanding how unconscious attitudes and stereotypes influence behavior particularly in the context of intergroup relations and social inequality dr osheas research has been published in several highimpact peerreviewed journals including the proceedings of the national academy of sciences pnas political psychology social psychological and personality science journal of experimental psychology social cognition psychological assessment best yashpal Subject: holistic fitness workshop from jan to for all students of iit delhi reminder

student issues and empower each individual student of iit delhi board of student welfare bsw in collaboration with isha foundation will be organizing a day holistic fitness workshop with evening sessions of hour duration from pm to pm on each day starting from th january to st januray for this it is essential to empower our students in a way that they are able to handle their body mind and emotions more consciously and efficiently we would like to offer such techniques to all students program which would empower them to manage stress enhance focus and foster holistic wellbeing daily minutes practice of these can be truly transformational and can have immense positive impact the techniques will not only foster physical and mental wellness among students but would also bring focus and clarity thus enabling them to explore their fullest potential the innumerable benefits of these techniques have been scientifically established by various national and international agencies to mention a few reduction in the stress levels by harvard medical school brain derived neurotropic factors bdnf that determines the nature of our experience mental and emotional condition as per research regular practice of these techniques for just minutes a day can increase the bdnf level three folds in a positive way leading to a state of inner peace and joy the program would comprise of Subject: ice seminar on understanding unconsciousimplicitautomatic biases in society by dr brian oshea
Body: dear all the initiative for caste equity ice office of diversity and inclusion and the scst cell cordially invites to a seminar on understanding unconsciousimplicitautomatic biases in society by dr brian oshea school of psychology university of nottingham and scientific advisor project implicit harvard university date and time pm wednesday december venue lh link to join online title understanding unconsciousimplicitautomatic biases in society abstract understanding social and healthrelated biases in society are important for developing interventions the online project implicit platform has been gathering data from millions of people each year that can offer important insight into regional variation and changes in biases over time this talk will introduce you to this valuable resource and the insights we have gained to date bio dr brian oshea phd warwick is an assistant professor in the school of psychology at university of nottingham and scientific advisor for project implicit and project implicit health at harvard university his work explores how group memberships and identities shape attitudes and behavior with particular attention to prejudice discrimination and social justice a key area of his research is his involvement in project implicit an international network of researchers studying implicit cognitionautomatic thoughts and feelings that often operate outside of conscious awareness dr osheas work in this area contributes to understanding how unconscious attitudes and stereotypes influence behavior particularly in the context of intergroup relations and social inequality dr osheas research has been published in several highimpact peerreviewed journals including the proceedings of the national academy of sciences pnas political psychology social psychological and personality science journal of experimental psychology social cognition psychological assessment best yashpal yashpal jogdand associate professor of psychology advisor initiative for caste equity ice office of diversity and inclusion indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india phone links

Subject: connect learn and reflect swadesh jhabua rural immersion trip

Subject: me guest talk by dr dilip banerjee from nist usa
Body: dear all dr dilip banerjee from nist usa will be visiting iit delhi and a mechanical engineering guest talk is scheduled as below date wednesday th december time pm venue ii lt title of the talk an overview of recent efforts in developing optimized biaxial cruciform specimens of mild steels ss l and aluminum alloys abstract a methodology is described for obtaining optimum biaxial cruciform specimen designs by combining equibiaxial tension test data with finite element analysis fea in conjunction with the application of an appropriate optimization strategy this approach is applied for developing optimum specimen designs for an astm a steel a ss l and an aa xxxt alloy this methodology requires in sequence the a selection of an appropriate initial biaxial specimen design and development of an equivalent verified fea model b optimization of the verified fea models c fabrication of cruciform specimens according to the optimized dimensions and testing under appropriate loading conditions and d simulating the validation test with an equivalent fea model with boundary conditions obtained from the tests this study shows that such a combined testfeaoptimization approach can be successfully applied to develop optimum cruciform specimen designs for advanced lightweighting materials bio sketch dilip k banerjee is a research engineer in the mechanical performance group of the materials measurement laboratory mml at the national institute of standards and technology nist he received his ms and phd in materials engineering from the university of alabama he received his mba from the robert h smith school of business at the university of maryland college park and his btech honors in metallurgical engineering from iit kharagpur dr banerjee worked as a senior scientist in ues inc where he was a developer of the commercial finite element casting simulation software procast he later joined the general electric company as a leader of the software quality group in its information systems division dr banerjee joined nist as a program manager in the advanced technology program atp he served as a cochair of the atps proposal selection board in and later served as a senior program manager in the standards services division at nist subsequently he worked in the engineering laboratory at nist where his research work involved studying the effects of fire in structures dr banerjee has an extensive background in numerical modeling he worked in the nist technical team to investigate the failure of the world trade center building his current research effort is focused on developing accurate computational models in support of efforts of nist center of automotive lightweighting ncal to develop the measurement methodology and analysis necessary for the us auto industry to transition to advanced lightweighting materials his other major responsibility is to develop a digital twin framework for additive manufacturing of metals involving the laser powder bed fusion lpbf and directed energy deposition ded processes dr banerjee received various awards such as the korea advanced institute of science technology kaist overseas scholar award the fulbright us scholar award the outstanding achievement award from the general electric company and the john deere outstanding graduate student award from the university of alabama dr banerjee is a us department of commerce science and technology fellow and is an american society for quality certified software quality engineer he serves on the tms shaping and forming committee he is also a general electric company certified six sigma green belt all interested are welcome to join the talk thanks and regards dr abhishek das and prof d ravi kumar me seminar committee department of mechanical engineering iit delhi

Subject: mathematics colloquium on december thursday at am in committee room mz
Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department colloquium by prof soumen sarkar iit madras on december thursday the details are given below title title dynamics of polynomial vector fields on a sphere date december thursday time am venue mz committee room department of mathematics speaker prof soumen sarkar iit madras abstract david hilbert proposed a problem at the beginning of the s it is known as hilberts th problem which asks for the bound for the number of invariant algebraic curves in terms of the degree of polynomial vector fields in the plane this problem is solved in a few particular cases one can ask a similar question for the polynomial vector fields on the sphere in this talk ill characterize and study the dynamical properties of cubic vector fields on the sphere then ill show that there exist completely integrable cubic vector fields on the sphere and also study the maximum number of various types of invariant circles for homogeneous cubic vector fields on the sphere finally ill discuss phase portraits of certain cubic kolmogorov vector fields on the sphere all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team

Body: dear all dr dinesh kumar from danfoss drives denmark will be giving a research talk on impact of multiple gridconnected asd interactions on power quality dclink capacitor lifespan on monday th dec at am in the ee committee room please join the talk and circulate among interested students below are the details title impact of multiple gridconnected asd interactions on power quality dclink capacitor lifespan abstract gridconnected adjustable speed drives asds provide an effective energysaving solution for motors in various industrial applications however interactions among different asd topologies at the point of common coupling can result in power quality and reliability challenges this talk highlights these issues with a focus on the role of dclink capacitors in various asd topologies bio dr dinesh kumar is a senior member of ieee and the lead power electronics specialist at the global rd center of danfoss drives denmark he received his m tech from iit roorkee and phd in electrical engineering from the university of nottingham uk he has over years of experience in academia industry and international standardization committees with extensive technical competence in power electronics and power quality he is an active member of various iec technical committees nominated by danish national standardization with this he is an adjunct associate professor with school of electrical engineering and robotics queensland university of technology australia his research interests include motor drive harmonic analysis and mitigation techniques power quality and electromagnetic interference dr kumar is the editorinchief of the international journal of power electronics and the associate editor of ieee transactions on industry applications secsc and idc and ieee transactions on transportation electrification regards soumya shubhra nag associate professor department of electrical engineering indian institute of technology delhi new delhi phone office home page

Subject: reminder photonic lecture series on th december pm
Body: a gentle reminder for the talk today at pm optics and photonics centre opc invites all interested to a series of lectures by wellknown scientists in areas of optics and photonics details of lecture in this series is given below title advancing multimodal image registration with selfsupervised representation learning speaker elisabeth wetzer affiliation uit the arctic university of norway in tromsø mode online date th december time pm ist abstract multimodal images ie image captured by multiple sensors or microscopes carry complimentary information about the imaged sample generally it is necessary to align the captured images prior to fusing their information this multimodal image registration task can be very challenging in particular when the modalities differ strongly in their appearance and are characterized by nonlinear relationships between pixel values in this presentation representation learning techniques will be presented which originate from selfsupervised learning and can generate intermediate abstract representations of images of different modalities which are similar in intensity and capture shared structures of the images these shared representations turn the multimodal registration task into a monomodal one which is generally easier and enable intensitybased and featurebased registration methods biography elisabeth wetzer has received her phd in image processing at uppsala university and is currently associate professor in machine learning at uit the arctic university of norway in tromsø her research focuses on method development in deep learning particularly for biomedical image processing addressing problems associated with this application field such as learning from limited labels and imbalanced datasets link regard profpsenthilkumaran head optics and photonics centre indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: reminder uqiitd research academy knowledge nexus seminar series
Body: dear all join us for an engaging seminar on digital transaction platforms in asia where we will explore digital transaction platforms as functional interchanges for the complex transaction chains engendered by network economies serving as clearing houses for a cascading range of digital tokens this seminar will provide valuable insights expansion of digital platforms via mobile internet speaker dr adrian athique associate professor in digital cultures at the university of queensland day and date thursday th december time am to am ist pm aest venue room no tx ground floor department of textile fibre engineering building iit delhi join via ms team link join the meeting now meeting id passcode rsfpwk abstract of the talk whilst digital transactions have existed within financial systems and markets for decades it is the expansion of digital platforms via mobile internets that has made mundane digital transactions a ubiquitous feature of everyday life in this talk i posit digital transaction platforms as functional interchanges for the complex transaction chains engendered by network economies serving as clearing houses for a cascading range of digital tokens at a systemic level six classes of transaction platforms provide exchange functions necessary to the platform economy and consequently constitute the vital organs of digital capitalism in synchronising online marketplaces for goods services labour information and credit transaction platforms ensure the interoperability of profuse digital currencies the functioning of complex transaction chains and above all the velocity of money in digital societies asia is the region demonstrating the strongest and swiftest transition to digital transactions reflecting its moremobile tendencies digital majority competitive and cooperative investments in digital futures from this i infer that digital transactions are not only the nerves and veins of algorithmic capitalism but also symptomatic indicators of emergent transactional cultures each with their own material histories and aspirations social and semantic ontologies about the speaker adrian athique is associate professor in digital cultures at the university of queensland having previously held positions at the university of waikato and the university of essex adrians career research has focused upon the sociology and political economy of media in asia his major works include the multiplex in india with douglas hill indian media digital media and society transnational audiences the indian media economy vols with vibodh parthasarathi and sv srinivas digital transactions in asia with emma baulch and platform capitalism in india with vibodh parthasarathi he is currently leading the australian research council discovery project digital transaction platforms in asia and is contributing to the sshrc project global media and internet concentration best regards oo p vigneswara ilavarasan phd professorincharge pica Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department seminar by prof ori davidov from the department of statistics university of haifa israel on dec the details are given below title safe hypotheses testing with application to order restricted inference and beyond abstract hypothesis testing problems are fundamental to the theory and practice of statistics it is well known that when the union of the null and the alternative does not encompass the full parameter space the possibility of a type iii error arises ie the null hypothesis may be rejected when neither the null nor the alternative are true in such situations common in the context of order restricted inference the validity of our inferences may be severely compromised the study of the geometry of the distancetest a test widely used in constrained inference illuminates circumstances in which type iii errors arise and motivates the introduction of safe tests heuristically a safe test is a test which at least asymptotically is free of type iii errors a novel safe test is proposed and studied the new testing procedure is associated with a certificate of validity a pretest indicating whether the original hypotheses are consistent with the data consequently type iii errors can be addressed in a principled way and constrained tests can be carried out without fear of systematically incorrect inferences although we focus on testing problems arising in order restricted inference the underlying ideas are more broadly applicable the benefits associated with the proposed methodology are demonstrated by simulations and the analysis of several illustrative examples date dec time noon pm venue iia bharti school building speaker prof ori davidov you can read more about the speaker at all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team links

Subject: photonic lecture series on th december pm
Body: optics and photonics centre opc invites all interested to a series of lectures by wellknown scientists in areas of optics and photonics details of lecture in this series is given below title advancing multimodal image registration with selfsupervised representation learning speaker elisabeth wetzer affiliation uit the arctic university of norway in tromsø mode online date th december time pm ist abstract multimodal images ie image captured by multiple sensors or microscopes carry complimentary information about the imaged sample generally it is necessary to align the captured images prior to fusing their information this multimodal image registration task can be very challenging in particular when the modalities differ strongly in their appearance and are characterized by nonlinear relationships between pixel values in this presentation representation learning techniques will be presented which originate from selfsupervised learning and can generate intermediate abstract representations of images of different modalities which are similar in intensity and capture shared structures of the images these shared representations turn the multimodal registration task into a monomodal one which is generally easier and enable intensitybased and featurebased registration methods biography elisabeth wetzer has received her phd in image processing at uppsala university and is currently associate professor in machine learning at uit the arctic university of norway in tromsø her research focuses on method development in deep learning particularly for biomedical image processing addressing problems associated with this application field such as learning from limited labels and imbalanced datasets link regard profpsenthilkumaran head optics and photonics centre indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india

Subject: sad news
From: dean of student affairs iit delhi
Body: dear all with a very heavy heart it is our unfortunate duty to inform you of the tragic and untimely demise of our student surabhi verma surabhi was a firstyear phd student at the centre for atmospheric sciences and a resident of nalanda at iit delhi our faculty colleague prof yama dixit and the ph d student surabhi verma from the centre for atmospheric sciences iit delhi had gone to gandhinagar gujarat for a field trip to collect paleoclimate data while conducting an excavation they met with an accident due to which sadly our student surabhi was fatally injured and passed away while prof dixit who was also injured during the mishap is undergoing medical treatment in the hospital head cas is travelling to ahmedabad tonight to meet prof dixit and surabhis family our deepest condolences to her family friends and loved ones while we try to deal with the terrible pain and sorrow the loss to her family and friends is unimaginable we will update the iitd community as and when we will receive other information you are also requested to reach out to the multiple counselling avenues in our system if you need help in coping with this tragedy of course all faculty and administration are also there for any support a condolence meeting will be fixed by the registrar in due course with sincerest regrets for being the bearer of such news and regards dr b k panigrahi fieee fnae fnasc dean of student affairs professor hag department of electrical engineering founder head centre for automotive research and tribology cart indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india tel dos email

Subject: uqiitd research academy knowledge nexus seminar series
Body: dear all join us for an engaging seminar on digital transaction platforms in asia where we will explore digital transaction platforms as functional interchanges for the complex transaction chains engendered by network economies serving as clearing houses for a cascading range of digital tokens this seminar will provide valuable insights expansion of digital platforms via mobile internet speaker dr adrian athique associate professor in digital cultures at the university of queensland day and date thursday th december time am to am ist pm aest venue room no tx ground floor department of textile fibre engineering building iit delhi join via ms team link join the meeting now meeting id passcode rsfpwk abstract of the talk whilst digital transactions have existed within financial systems and markets for decades it is the expansion of digital platforms via mobile internets that has made mundane digital transactions a ubiquitous feature of everyday life in this talk i posit digital transaction platforms as functional interchanges for the complex transaction chains engendered by network economies serving as clearing houses for a cascading range of digital tokens at a systemic level six classes of transaction platforms provide exchange functions necessary to the platform economy and consequently constitute the vital organs of digital capitalism in synchronising online marketplaces for goods services labour information and credit transaction platforms ensure the interoperability of profuse digital currencies the functioning of complex transaction chains and above all the velocity of money in digital societies asia is the region demonstrating the strongest and swiftest transition to digital transactions reflecting its moremobile tendencies digital majority competitive and cooperative investments in digital futures from this i infer that digital transactions are not only the nerves and veins of algorithmic capitalism but also symptomatic indicators of emergent transactional cultures each with their own material histories and aspirations social and semantic ontologies about the speaker adrian athique is associate professor in digital cultures at the university of queensland having previously held positions at the university of waikato and the university of essex adrians career research has focused upon the sociology and political economy of media in asia his major works include the multiplex in india with douglas hill indian media digital media and society transnational audiences the indian media economy vols with vibodh parthasarathi and sv srinivas digital transactions in asia with emma baulch and platform capitalism in india with vibodh parthasarathi he is currently leading the australian research council discovery project digital transaction platforms in asia and is contributing to the sshrc project global media and internet concentration best regards oo p vigneswara ilavarasan phd professorincharge pica university of queensland indian institute of technology delhi research academy room no tx building department of textile and fibre engineering indian institute of technology delhi new delhi india Subject: re technical presentation by dr sara otero cofounder of radiantis at pm of th nov in ms
Body: title advancing ultrafast science with the new broadly tunable femtosecond laser system speaker dr sara otero cofounder of radiantis dr sunil kumar department of physics indian institute of technology delhi haus khas new delhi india tel web on dr sunil kumar wrote dear all please note that the venue for the presentation at pm of th nov by dr sara otero is ms dr sunil kumar department of physics indian institute of technology delhi haus khas new delhi india tel web on dr sunil kumar wrote dear students this is an early notice for a technical talk by dr sara otero cofounder of radiantis at pm of th nov all interested are welcome i would urge to the mtech pha and jop students in particular to make it convenient to attend the details are as follows it will take place either in ms or ms to be informed later about the speaker dr sara otero is a cofounder of radiantis and has served as the companys ceo since she is also the vicepresident for industry of the international commission of optics ico and the secretary of the board of directors of secpho the photonics cluster in spain with over years of experience in the photonics sector she has worked extensively in both industry and academia the proposed talk will cover the following title advancing ultrafast science with the new broadly tunable femtosecond laser system the radiantis oria series offers a versatile flexible and powerful illumination source for ultrafast scientific applications combined with a tisapphire oscillator this femtosecond family of optical parametric oscillators opos and second harmonic generators shg provides automated wavelength tuning across nm with high average power and repetition rates of mhz the radiantis oria series has been significantly upgraded with the integration of new features including an optional singleoutput beam combiner and a power attenuator which together complete its suite of tools for advanced scientific applications these enhancements along with improvements in overall performance robustness stability and userfriendliness offer scientists greater functionality and flexibility in their experiments the oria laser system is perfectly suited for a wide range of nonlinear optics applications supporting advanced research in multiphoton microscopy nonlinear spectroscopy frequency conversion and phase modulation it excels in providing precise characterization of material responses through both transmission and reflection measurements additionally the oria laser extend their capabilities to fluorescence spectroscopy for biomaterials and other visiblerange materials making it a versatile tool for exploring the complex nonlinear properties of various materials this flexibility makes the system invaluable for researchers looking to push the boundaries of scientific discovery dr sunil kumar department of physics indian institute of technology delhi haus khas new delhi india website

Subject: membership application for indradhanu the lgbtqia collective of iit delhi
Body: dear peers at iit delhi greetings from indradhanu the lgbtqia collective of iit delhi how often do we seriously think about the importance of gender and sexuality what they mean and what roles they play in our lives while all of us come to iit delhi to strive towards our academic goals there is a need to equip ourselves with information to mutually respect human differences and diversity this is where indradhanu comes into the picture for those interested we intend to create a safe space for conversation and dialogue on issues relating to gender and sexuality we hope to rethink conventional notions of masculinity and femininity and think over love family relationships and alternative interpretations of the same help remove social taboos associated with gender and sexuality in addition we would like to address concerns surrounding the queer lives on campus and create awareness on navigating them with pride and dignity indradhanu is one of the four verticals under the office of diversity and inclusion we strive to make iitd a more inclusive campus fill the form below if youd like to become a member of the collective link to membership form current members include folks belonging to the lgbtqia community as well as allies once you fill out the form an indradhanu coordinator will contact you and schedule a short interaction to get to know you better before you officially join the collective in case of doubts contact vaivab himanshu rahul regards rahul bhardwaj sac representative indradhanu forwarded by oo dean diversity inclusion prof angelie multani dean diversity inclusion indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi telephone links

Body: this is a gentle reminder for the event best regards svs on nov at am associatedeanoutreachnewinitiative wrote dear students and faculty members fyi begin forwarded message from mohammad ali haider subject iitdad and ku seminar by prof naoufel werghi on tue th nov date november at pm ist to subodh vishnu sharma associatedeanoutreachnewinitiative cc shantanu roy dear prof subodh could you please forward the message about this seminar to all students and faculty of iit delhi best haider mohammad ali haider vice provost for research and external engagement indian institute of technology iit delhi abu dhabi professor department of chemical engineering iit delhi associate faculty yardi school of artificial intelligence scai iit delhi member editorial advisory board acs sustainable chemistry engineering reclabin dear all please join the talk by dr naoufel werghi to discover how data representation in computer vision is transforming ai from traditional methods to groundbreaking deep learning innovations driving advancements across industries date tuesday th november time pm uae time pm india time venue lecture hall m building khalifa city iit delhiabu dhabi or online through the link title data representation as the cornerstone of innovation in computer vision bridging classical and deep learning approaches abstract computer vision once a subset of artificial intelligence before emerging as an independent field continues to be the catalyst for groundbreaking advancements in ai particularly in the realm of deep learning at the heart of this revolutionary progress lies the concept of data representation a notion that has evolved from its roots in traditional computer vision to become the cornerstone of modern deep learning architectures this seminar will explore the critical role of data representation in computer vision illuminating its significance across both classical and contemporary approaches we will begin by introducing the fundamental principles of data representation emphasizing its pivotal importance in the field the discussion will then traverse a diverse landscape of problems and applications demonstrating how data representation serves as the linchpin for innovation in computer vision bio dr naoufel werghi received a research habilitation and phd in computer vision from the university of strasbourg currently he is a full professor in the department of computer sciences and is leading the artificial intelligence and big data theme at the center of secure cyberphysical systems at khalifa university he also founded the computer vision and machine intelligence lab in khalifa university his main research area is d d imagevideo analysis and understanding where he has been leading several funded projects related to biometrics medical imaging robotics surveillance inspection and intelligent systems he is associate editor of the ieee transactions on circuits and systems for video technology the ieee journal of biomedical and health informatics and the eurasip journal for image and video processing best haider ￼

Subject: reminder uqiitd research academy knowledge nexus seminar series
Body: dear all we are pleased to invite you to an online talk by dr amit jaiswal assistant professor school of biosciences and bioengineering iit mandi himachal pradesh india day and date tuesday th november time am to am ist venue online using ms teams link tile of the talk localized surface plasmon resonance lspr in noble metal nanostructures from fundamentals to biomedical applications abstract noble metal nanostructures particularly gold and silver have significantly advanced sensing and biomedical fields through their unique size and shapedependent optical properties these plasmonic nanostructures leverage the phenomenon of localized surface plasmon resonance lspr enabling precise manipulation of lightmatter interactions at the nanoscale herein we will discuss about the applications of plasmonic nanostructures specifically nanorattles in the biomedical field the first part of the talk will provide a comprehensive overview of the fundamental principles underlying the shape and size dependent lspr phenomenon of plasmonic nanoparticles in the second part we will delve into the diverse applications of noble metalbased plasmonic nanostructures with a specific focus on biomedical applications these include a photothermal therapy by utilizing the strong light absorption properties of plasmonic nanostructures photothermal therapy can be achieved where targeted heating of tumor cells occurs upon exposure to nearinfrared light this noninvasive technique shows great potential for cancer treatment b surfaceenhanced raman scattering sers plasmonic nanostructures can provide highly sensitive sers substrates for the detection of trace analytes and for bioimaging by enhancing the raman signals of reporter molecules plasmonic sers bioimaging enables imaging and sensing short bio of the speaker dr amit jaiswal earned his btech degree in biotechnology from heritage institute of technology kolkata in followed by an mtech in biotechnology from iit guwahati in he pursued his doctoral studies at the centre for nanotechnology iit guwahati and successfully obtained his phd degree in after completing his phd he conducted postdoctoral research at washington university in st louis usa and technion israel institute of technology haifa in dr jaiswal joined iit mandi as an assistant professor and currently holds the position of associate professor in the school of biosciences and bioengineering iit mandi dr jaiswal is also currently serving as the associate dean research of iit mandi his research focuses on the field of nanobiotechnology in recognition of his research contributions he was honored with the department of atomic energy dae young scientist research award in and the mahe young scientist award in he is also an associate of the indian academy of sciences since dr jaiswals research achievements were further acknowledged with the indian national science academy insa medal for young scientists and his team received the gyti appreciation award he has authored more than peerreviewed journal articles and contributed to book chapters all are welcome to attend best regards oo p vigneswara ilavarasan phd professorincharge pica university of queensland indian institute of technology delhi research academy room no tx building department of textile and fibre engineering indian institute of technology delhi new delhi india Subject: invitation for institute seminar by prof c joshi pioneered the field of experimental plasma based particle accelerator
Body: dear all you are invited for the institute seminar by prof c joshi distinguished professor ucla date th december time pm to venue seminar hall iit delhi seating will begin from pm talk title perspective on beamdriven plasma wave acceleration abstract particle accelerators have been engines of discovery in our understanding of the universe and have applications in many areas of modern life from medicine to security the most powerful ones are ’s of kilometers in length determined by the strength of the accelerating electric field it has been four decades since the concept of using a relativistic plasma wake for charged particle acceleration was first proposed in relativistic plasma wakes the accelerating electric field can be orders of magnitude greater than in a conventional accelerator with the potential to reduce the size of the accelerating structure the driver for producing such wakes can be in intense laser pulse or a high current chargedparticle beam during this time ingenious solutions for generating the ultrahigh electric field over meterscale distances and generating and accelerating high quality electron and positron beams using such wakes have been realized in this talk i will give a personal perspective on the progress of the field of plasmabased acceleration driven by ultrashort electron bunches and where it is headed about the speaker professor chandrashekhar chan joshi is recognized as the father of the experimental field of plasmabased particle accelerators he started the first research group on plasma acceleration at ucla in and made landmark contributions to all four avatars of plasmabased wakefield accelerators such wakes are now being considered as accelerating structures for the next generation of particle colliders and compact light sources to make these critical instruments of scientific discovery compact and affordable over the past four decades joshi and his colleagues have demonstrated nearly every energy gain and accelerating gradient milestone and high such as ionization trapping betatron radiation and refraction of a relativistic particle beam at plasmavacuum boundary professor joshi has been honored with apsdpp’s excellence in plasma physics award maxwell prize ieee’s particle accelerator science and technology award and marie sklodowska curie award and medal lise meitner award and recently the alfven prize of the eps he is a fellow of the aps ieee and iop and an elected member of the us national academy of engineering all are invited please scan the qr code in the poster for registration in link below this will provide us an estimate of the expected strength of the audience with regards amita das

Subject: gyti awards
Body: dear students gandhian young technology innovation gyti awards have been established to celebrate and acknowledge the creativity and ingenuity of young student innovators across a wide spectrum of fields including engineering agriculture design life sciences pharmacy and other disciplines of science and technology the awards are aimed to recognize student innovators whose projects fall into one or more of the following categories mlm more from less for many frugal innovation award this category seeks ideas that excel in resource efficiency affordability and sustainability we are on the lookout for innovations that do more with less showcasing novel ways of economizing on materials while remaining extremely costeffective socially relevant technological innovation award in this category we celebrate ideas that address unmet social needs or enhance the functionality of existing solutions the focus is on increasing affordability and promoting circularity while ensuring compatibility with ecological principles technologicaledge award this award honors breakthrough ideas that boldly push the boundaries in various technological domains we encourage submissions that advance the frontiers of innovation across different disciplines we invite aspiring student innovators to participate in these awards by submitting their projects through our platform at gytitechpediain by december we welcome projects that tackle significant social environmental or technological challenges faced by various segments of society including disadvantaged individuals sectors spaces micro and small enterprises this call for submissions is open to both current and immediate past students of technical institutions and universities additionally faculty members who have supervised relevant theses or projects can nominate students who have graduated and left their institution in the last year if selected the award will be conferred upon the nominated student only for a comprehensive evaluation shortlisted projects will require a detailed report the final date for submission is december an esteemed panel of three to five reviewers will carefully assess all shortlisted entries these entries will also be included in the techpediain database with proper credit given to team members supervisors institutions and contact information furthermore the selected projects will be showcased at an exhibition attended by influential policymakers and practitioners from across the country distinguished awardees may also receive an invitation to the people festival of innovations held annually at the india international centre iic during november to nominate the student project please visit techpedias award page please note that only abstracts along with innovator details will be published on the website or shared in other ways students seeking incubation support should indicate their preference in the nomination form we are pleased to announce that projects with a focus on social and grassroots applications are also eligible for the hbn criiaindia awards an initiative by our sister institution gian for more information visit gianorghbncriiaindia this endeavor is supported by sristi if you have any questions or require further information please feel free to contact team techpediagyti at or call us at your enthusiastic cooperation will help make india a hub of creativity and inclusive innovation

Body: dear all speaker dr amit jaiswal assistant professor school of biosciences and bioengineering iit mandi himachal pradesh india day and date tuesday th november time am to am ist venue online using ms teams link tile of the talk localized surface plasmon resonance lspr in noble metal nanostructures from fundamentals to biomedical applications abstract noble metal nanostructures particularly gold and silver have significantly advanced sensing and biomedical fields through their unique size and shapedependent optical properties these plasmonic nanostructures leverage the phenomenon of localized surface plasmon resonance lspr enabling precise manipulation of lightmatter interactions at the nanoscale herein we will discuss about the applications of plasmonic nanostructures specifically nanorattles in the biomedical field the first part of the talk will provide a comprehensive overview of the fundamental principles underlying the shape and size dependent lspr phenomenon of plasmonic nanoparticles in the second part we will delve into the diverse applications of noble metalbased plasmonic nanostructures with a specific focus on biomedical applications these include a photothermal therapy by utilizing the strong light absorption properties of plasmonic nanostructures photothermal therapy can be achieved where targeted heating of tumor cells occurs upon exposure to nearinfrared light this noninvasive technique shows great potential for cancer treatment b surfaceenhanced raman scattering sers plasmonic nanostructures can provide highly sensitive sers substrates for the detection of trace analytes and for bioimaging by enhancing the raman signals of reporter molecules plasmonic sers bioimaging enables imaging and sensing short bio of the speaker dr amit jaiswal earned his btech degree in biotechnology from heritage institute of technology kolkata in followed by an mtech in biotechnology from iit guwahati in he pursued his doctoral studies at the centre for nanotechnology iit guwahati and successfully obtained his phd degree in after completing his phd he conducted postdoctoral research at washington university in st louis usa and technion israel institute of technology haifa in dr jaiswal joined iit mandi as an assistant professor and currently holds the position of associate professor in the school of biosciences and bioengineering iit mandi dr jaiswal is also currently serving as the associate dean research of iit mandi his research focuses on the field of nanobiotechnology in recognition of his research contributions he was honored with the department of atomic energy dae young scientist research award in and the mahe young scientist award in he is also an associate of the indian academy of sciences since dr jaiswals research achievements were further acknowledged with the indian national science academy insa medal for young scientists and his team received the gyti appreciation award he has authored more than peerreviewed journal articles and contributed to book chapters best regards sumita oo p vigneswara ilavarasan phd professorincharge pica university of queensland indian institute of Subject: reminder academic research on global challenges seminar on th november
Body: title academic research on global challenges speaker prof t venkatesan affiliation departments of physics and ece university of oklahoma ou usa scientific affiliate national institute of standards and technology nist gaithersburg md usa date th november time pm venue seminar hall iit delhi abstract in this talk i will address several interconnected global challenges my research team is addressing at the university of oklahoma ou in collaboration with the national institute of standards and technology nist and several other research institutions i will allude to exciting research opportunities in addressing these challenges so that we could potentially develop collaborations with the academic institutions in india extreme weather is wreaking havoc globally weather modelling and accurate prediction of extreme weather events torrential rains tornado hailstorms etc on a timely manner could save lives and avoid significant property loss ou is the epicenter of this area of research as the national weather center multi radar multi sensor group and the national severe storm laboratory of noaa the advanced radar research center aarc are all colocated on the ou campus with the meteorology department i will discuss the ramifications of a national level project involving ou and iit m pune that has begun with support from the ministry of earth sciences which we hope will involve multiple academic institutions in india over time our extreme weather is caused by our reliance on fossil fuel and one of the most exciting developments in clean energy has been the observation of parity in an inertial fusion experiment at lawrence livermore national labs experiment which has literally ignited a global race towards fusion with over startup companies in fusion energy we see opportunities for the development of a variety of detectors for several radiations neutron gamma alpha and ir photons and i will discuss some of these ideas a key next generation area in silicon is in advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration these enable increases in the circuit density per unit volume but also enhance the functionalities on silicon pulsed laser deposition is the latest tool to be added to the semiconductor industry by lam research and we see tremendous opportunities for academic researchers here development of pld related processes metrology and epitaxial functional materials on silicon i will discuss a few examples of such materials but advanced packaging also has created problems in defect location as the package thickness becomes prohibitive for most conventional techniques relying on photons electrons and heat i will discuss the role of magnetic field imaging of circuits as they can penetrate large depths and the critical role of aiml with extreme weather there will be further global episodes of pandemic and health is at an important juncture in the developing countries with incidence of cancer even among young people showing an alarming rise in cancer cases early detection of cancer and pathogens is the primary defense one has and we are developing breathomics breath based molecular biopsy as a rapid noninvasive technique to screen for cancer and pathogens i will discuss our nascent program with several clinicians at the ouhealth sciences center singapore cancer center and breathonix a singapore startup in developing screening strategies for several diseases using a single breath and the role of ai ml aiml is placing a significant demand on the technology of memristors for brainlike computing and i will mention the example of an organic platform that seems to meet the challenge last but not the least i will address the next generation computing in quantum can we replicate in a solid what can be done in an atomic array in an optical lattice i will mention the example of rydberg excitons in cu o and our current thin film challenges making these materials there is opportunity in developing novel solidstate qubits in material systems with nonexistent nuclear interference ceo and cao brief biography prof t venkatesan is currently with the center for quantum research and technology professor of physics and ece at university of oklahoma ou and scientific affiliate at nist gaithersburg he is a senior advisor to the office of vice president for research as the inventor of the pulsed laser Subject: applied mechanics seminar prof namrata gundiah
Body: dear all we are pleased to invite you to an inperson seminar by prof namrata gundiah dept of mechanical engineering iisc bangalore on the topic mechanics of soft materials venue iii lt time am november friday abstract soft materials including gels polymers and biological tissues often exhibit complex behaviors such as large nonlinear deformations anisotropic properties and timedependent viscoelastic responses hydrogels have tuneable nonlinear mechanical properties and offer unique advantages but low toughness and brittle fracture behaviors limit their use in loadbearing scenarios in this talk i will present recent work from our laboratory on the fracture characterization of model biomimetic hydrogels with varying crosslinking properties we highlight novel fabrication methods for hydrogels with similar elastic but distinct viscoelastic characteristics cavitation rheology experiments reveal shapebreaking transitions from spheroidal to ellipsoidal cavities in these gels which we model using a continuum growth framework we also explore the mechanobiological properties of cells cultured on elastic and viscoelastic hydrogels noting significant differences in cell deadhesion strength traction forces and migration behaviors finally i will discuss the impact of fiber reinforcement in corneal hydrogel tissues with a special focus on ocular disease of keratoconus the interplay between experiments and theory allows for deeper insights into the behavior of soft materials with implications for diverse fields such as biomaterials soft robotics and tissue engineering about the speaker namrata gundiah is a professor of mechanical engineering at the indian institute of science bangalore her research interests are broadly in nonlinear tissue mechanics and cell mechanobiology prior to joining the institute she worked as a postdoctoral fellow at the university of california san francisco she earned an ms and phd in mechanical engineering from the university of california berkeley in namrata has been awarded the ramanujan fellowship and the constance tipper silver medal from the international congress on fracture she is on the editorial board of biomechanics and modeling in mechanobiology and cell adhesion and migration journals she is also an associate editor at international journal for numerical methods in biomedical engineering all are welcome to attend regards

Subject: re seminar announcement sanyam agarwal saarland university on wednesday th november pm bharti cse seminar room
Body: we start in ten minutes on nov at nikhil balaji wrote ﻿gentle reminder this is happening today on nov at pm nikhil balaji wrote dear all we have sanyam agarwal from saarland university visiting us till december he will give a talk from pm at bharti the details of which are given below best nikhil date november wednesday time pm venue bharti title probabilistic generating circuits demystified abstract zhang et al icml plmr pp – introduced probabilistic generating circuits pgcs as a probabilistic model to unify probabilistic circuits pcs and determinantal point processes dpps at a first glance pgcs store a distribution in a very different way they compute the probability generating polynomial instead of the probability mass function and it seems that this is the main reason why pgcs are more powerful than pcs or dpps however pgcs also allow for negative weights whereas classical pcs assume that all weights are nonnegative one of the main insights of our paper is that the negative weights are responsible for the power of pgcs and not the different representation pgcs are pcs in disguise in particular we show how to transform any pgc into a pc with negative weights with only polynomial blowup pgcs were defined by zhang et al only for binary random variables as our second main result we show that there is a good reason for this we prove that pgcs for categorial variables with larger image size do not support tractable marginalization unless np p on the other hand we show that we can model categorial variables with larger image size as pc with negative weights computing setmultilinear polynomials these allow for tractable marginalization in this sense pcs with negative weights strictly subsume pgcs

Subject: bbmc brain storming discussion on tribal philosophy of the sustainable development on th november
Body: in continuation of the “janjatiya gaurav divas” celebration bhagwan birsa munda cell bbmc is holding a brain storming discussion in ri auditorium on th november at am event details title “tribal philosophy of the sustainable development” date and time th november am – pm speakers sh harsh chauhan ex chairperson national commission of schedules tribes ncst prof vm chariar crdt iit delhi sh laxman singh markam additional secretary office of chief minister govt of madhya pradesh sh dm kiran ceo sewa bridge consulting pvt ltd all are cordially invited preamble as global awareness of environmental and social challenges intensifies sustainable development models seek to incorporate diverse forms of knowledge especially those derived from tribal philosophy and indigenous knowledge systems because the tribal communities have long practiced sustainable methods in fact it is deeply rooted in their customs and traditions their social and economic practices offer valuable insights to address modern crises like climate change and overshooting the planetary boundaries this local and decentralized knowledge is priceless for developing climate adaptation strategies for centuries janjatiya communities in india have earmarked certain areas as “sacred groves” to protect trees its only in the last few decades the modern world had recognized the role of the groves in preserving the biodiversity hotspots thus tribal knowledge systems are not relics of the past but vibrant adaptable frameworks that can support modern sustainable development goals sdgs integration of tribal philosophy and indigenous knowledge into contemporary sustainable development resonates profoundly with the concepts of astitva existence and asmita identity within tribal communities for centuries tribal knowledge systems have been more than just practices they form the very essence of astitva by preserving a way of life interwoven with natural ecosystems this deep connection with nature is intrinsic to their identity asmita embodying values of respect and communal responsibility that have sustained their existence over generations experts will deliberate on how these ageold knowledge systems which emphasize respect and reverence to nature can complement modern development approach bhagwan birsa munda cell bbmc look forward to welcome you head crdt and coordinator bbmc indian to prof singh by the hon’ble president of india smt droupadi murmu on august the details of the lecture are provided below speaker prof bhim singh emeritus professor at iit delhi title renewable energya sustainable solution for humanity datetimevenue th november pm seminar hall abstract the global shift towards renewable energy has become imperative in addressing the challenges posed by climate change environmental degradation and the depletion of finite fossil fuels this talk will explore how solar photovoltaic energy offers a sustainable solution for humanity by analysing current technological advancements policy frameworks and economic impacts the talk highlights the potential of renewable energy to provide a reliable costeffective and environmentally friendly alternative to conventional energy sources additionally the talk will cover the socioeconomic benefits of renewable energy adoption such as job creation energy security and reduced greenhouse gas emissions as the world moves towards a lowcarbon future renewable energy emerges not only as a necessity but as a cornerstone for sustainable development and a cleaner more resilient future for allthe largescale development and deployment of renewable energy technologies are essential to the global pursuit of decarbonizing the energy sector to effectively harness variable and intermittent renewable energy sources like solar and wind and to integrate the electricity generated by these plants power electronics play a crucial role developing testing and commercializing appropriate power electronic devices such as voltage source converters and dcdc converters are key to maximizing the benefits of renewable energy the challenges involved are complex and require a comprehensive understanding of renewable energy resource characteristics electric machines electricity generation transmission distribution utilization systems circuit analysis and power electronics about the speaker professor bhim singh has received his be electrical from the university of roorkee now iit roorkee india in and his mtech power apparatus systems and phd from the indian institute of technology delhi india in and respectively in he joined the department of electrical engineering university of roorkee as a lecturer he became a reader there in in december he joined the department of electrical engineering iit delhi india as Body: dear everyone join us date nov venue dogra hall time pm pm for the amazing end of the semester public talk by prof jean surdej from the department of astrophysics university of liege belgium being organised by pac caic and the newly initiated project the iucaa centre for astronomy research and development icardiitd at the department of physics iit delhi he will give insights about the oneofakind m international liquid mirror telescope ilmt and a lot more prof jean surdej is honorary full professor and research director frs fnrs in astrophysics department of astrophysics geophysics and oceanography at university of liège belgium and vajra adjunct faculty at aries nainital india he is the principal investigator of the m international liquid mirror telescope ilmt a joint project of india canada and belgium commissioned at the devasthal campus of aries india the title and abstracts short and long versions for his talk are appended below title viewing the wonders of nature from camera obscura to the m international liquid mirror telescope ilmt abstract once again mother nature is at the forefront of astrophysical inventions the camera obscura inspiring physicists with the principle of how a telescope works we shall take a look at how such a camera works and how by slightly modifying it we can focus the light rays from a distant source onto a single point we will also show how using an old record player a pie plate a magnifying glass and a little olive oil you can make a liquidmirror telescope at your institute at least cm in diameter astronomers and engineers from liège belgium in association with canadian and indian colleagues have built a much larger one the m international liquid mirror telecope ilmt this innovative instrument uses a rotating mirror metres in diameter coated with a thin film of liquid mercury to collect and focus the light a liquid mirror telescope takes advantage of the fact that the surface of a rotating liquid naturally takes on a parabolic shape which is ideal for focusing light the reflected light passes through a sophisticated multilens optical corrector that produces sharp images over a wide field of view a largeformat electronic camera at focus records the images the metre international liquid mirror telescope ilmt has been installed at the aries aryabhatta research institute for observational sciences site in indias central himalayas at an altitude of m devasthal uttarakhand first light was obtained on april and the telescope is currently recording superb images longer version once again mother nature is telescope takes advantage of the fact that the surface of a rotating liquid naturally takes on a parabolic shape which is ideal for focusing light the reflected light passes through a sophisticated multilens optical corrector that produces sharp images over a wide field of view a largeformat electronic camera at focus records the images the metre international liquid mirror telescope ilmt has been installed at the aries aryabhatta research institute for observational sciences site in indias central himalayas at an altitude of m devasthal uttarakhand first light was obtained on april and the telescope is currently recording superb images this seminar will describe and illustrate the various components of the ilmt the ilmt is used in tdi mode time delayed integration to carry out deep surveys and photometric and astrometric observations with a high signaltonoise ratio these observations concern solar system galactic and extragalactic objects in a narrow band of sky centred around the equatorial declination of ° in principle the ilmt should regularly detect and monitor several tens of gravitational mirages it will also detect numerous supernovae transient phenomena asteroids and space debris the telescope was officially inaugurated at the devasthal site on march the start of the indian spring the first observations obtained with the ilmt are publicly accessible and free Subject: reminder photonic lecture series on th november pm
Body: dear all a kind reminder of the photonic lecture series pls talk today at pm optics and photonics centre opc invites all interested to a series of lectures by wellknown scientists in areas of optics and photonics details of lecture in this series is given below title singlecavity dualcomb lasers revolutionizing spectroscopy and ultrafast measurements speaker ursula keller affiliation eth zurich department of information technology and electrical engineering zürich switzerland mode online date th november time pm ist weblink to join abstract the optical frequency comb ofc revolution began in the late marked by three pivotal publications since then the field has been a major focus of research continuously evolving with new innovations an key advancement in ofc technology are dualcomb lasers which employs a pair of combs distinguished by a small yet precise difference in their spacing this allows for rapid pumpprobe and spectroscopy measurements without any mechanical delay lines we have invented new sharedcavity methods to generate two optical combs with slightly different adjustable pulse repetition rates by generating both combs within the same cavity the system is simplified and the combs exhibit highly correlated noise properties these singlecavity dualcomb lasers achieve low noise levels making them suitable for practical dualcomb measurements we pioneered two techniques based on polarization and spatial multiplexing in the polarization multiplexing approach enabled dualcomb spectroscopy from a single freerunning passively modelocked laser cavity a key milestone since then we have demonstrated lownoise performance using diodepumped ybdoped solidstate and verticalemitting semiconductor lasers to verify these lownoise properties we developed a highly sensitive pulse timing jitter characterization tool we have demonstrated coherent averaging of dualcomb signals enabling dualcomb spectroscopy applications with excellent signaltonoise ratios from freerunning dualcomb oscillators without additional stabilization many application demonstrations have been done with these lasers such as picosecond ultrasonics lidar timedomain thz spectroscopy equivalent sampling of sesam response spectroscopy with adjustable delay intervals d microscopy opo and midir spectroscopy and biomedical applications this talk will provide an introduction to dualcomb lasers and highlight several specific application demonstrations biography ursula keller a tenured physics professor at eth zurich since directed the nccr must ultrafast science program from to she earned her diplom from eth zurich in and a phd from stanford university in as a member of technical staff mts at bell labs from to she launched her independent research career keller cofounded timebandwidth products was acquired by jdsu in and k photonics in since she has served on the supervisory board of jenoptik her research is dedicated to advancing ultrafast science and technology with advancements in ultrafast solidstate and semiconductor lasers utilizing semiconductor saturable absorber mirrors sesams and achieving ultrashort pulse generation in the one to two opticalcycle regime with frequency comb generation and stabilization she applied these lasers to conduct attosecond experiments testing fundamental processes in quantum mechanics and pioneered the attoclock technique her awards include the swiss science prize marcel benoist international member of the national academy of sciences usa osa frederic ives medal spie gold medal ieee edison medal osa charles h townes award eps senior prize and two erc advanced grants and keller has supervised phd students authored journal articles and holds an hindex of with over citations according to google scholar in she authored a new graduate textbook on ultrafast lasers published by springer verlag h telle et al appl phys b – a apolonski et al phys rev lett – d j jones et al science – s m link et al optics express j pupeikis et al optica s m link et al science s l camenzind et al opt express c r phillips et al opt express j pupeikis et al photoacoustics s l camenzind et al optics express b willenberg et al applied optics a nussbaumlapping et al applied physics b f flöry et al ultrafast science w lu et al optics letters c p bauer et al nature communications b zhang et al acs photonics regard prof p senthilkumaran Subject: seminar announcement sanyam agarwal saarland university on wednesday th november pm bharti cse seminar room
Body: dear all we have sanyam agarwal from saarland university visiting us till december he will give a talk from pm at bharti the details of which are given below best nikhil date november wednesday time pm venue bharti title probabilistic generating circuits demystified abstract zhang et al icml plmr pp – introduced probabilistic generating circuits pgcs as a probabilistic model to unify probabilistic circuits pcs and determinantal point processes dpps at a first glance pgcs store a distribution in a very different way they compute the probability generating polynomial instead of the probability mass function and it seems that this is the main reason why pgcs are more powerful than pcs or dpps however pgcs also allow for negative weights whereas classical pcs assume that all weights are nonnegative one of the main insights of our paper is that the negative weights are responsible for the power of pgcs and not the different representation pgcs are pcs in disguise in particular we show how to transform any pgc into a pc with negative weights with only polynomial blowup pgcs were defined by zhang et al only for binary random variables as our second main result we show that there is a good reason for this we prove that pgcs for categorial variables with larger image size do not support tractable marginalization unless np p on the other hand we show that we can model categorial variables with larger image size as pc with negative weights computing setmultilinear polynomials these allow for tractable marginalization in this sense pcs with negative weights strictly subsume pgcs

Subject: course feedback for sem

Subject: iit delhi janjatiya gaurav divas celebrations inaugural event on th november reclaiming histories tribal leaders and movements in indias freedom struggle
Body: dear all in the year government of india declared th november as janjatiya gaurav divas a day dedicated to honor the courageous contributions of tribal freedom fighters in india’s struggle for independence this date holds special significance as it marks the birth anniversary of bhagwan birsa munda a revered tribal leader who championed the rights of his people against british colonial oppression known for his visionary leadership birsa munda inspired his community with the rallying cry abua raj setar jana maharani raj tundu jana let the kingdom of the queen be ended and our kingdom be established november is not only a day to remember bhagwan birsa munda but also to pay homage to the tribal heroes and freedom fighters from various regions across india who resisted colonial oppression movements such as tilka manjhi’s damin sangram in santhal the larka movement led by budhu bhagat sidhukanhu kranti the tana bhagat movement govind gurus resistance in mangarh and the rampa movement led by alluri sitarama raju exemplify the sacrifices made by the tribal communities in the fight for independence as stated by the honble prime minister on janjatiya gaurav diwas in there is valor in tribal society and there is cohabitation and inclusion with nature also india has to shape its future by learning from this grand heritage janjatiya gaurav diwas will become a momentous medium for us in this direction janjatiya gaurav divas is a solemn yet celebratory occasion that honors the spirit of india’s tribal communities the event aims to generate awareness in our present and future generations by highlighting the devout contribution independence struggle and cultural richness of the diverse tribal communities of the nation it also serves as a platform to educate and raise awareness about india’s tribal heritage and the crucial role the communities played in the country’s indigenous knowledge system this day highlights the valor resilience and wisdom embedded within tribal societies who not only defended their homeland but also embody a harmonious relationship with nature and a deep respect for community values the objectives of the janjatiya gaurav divas celebrations at iit delhi are multifaceted it encompasses educational awareness cultural recognition inspiration and celebration additionally it aspires to celebrate the unique cultural identity and knowledge systems of india’s tribal communities which binds the foundation of the nation’s heritage the event will also showcase the tribal way of life to get insights of sustainable practices and environmental conservation bhagwan birsa munda cell bbmc iit delhi has decided to organise “janjati month” and host a series of activities to celebrate the janjatiya gaurav divas to begin with the month long celebration we have scheduled a talk show reclaiming histories tribal leaders and movements in indias freedom struggle tomorrow th november in ri auditorium at pmthe event aims to inform one and all about the colonial struggles and achievements of tribal freedom fighters through discussions fostering a deep appreciation for the contributions in india’s independence we look forward to welcome you all in the event the poster of the event is attached for your reference bbm cell iit delhi head crdt and coordinator bbm cell indian institute of technology iit delhi new delhi india o fax email
