Body: dear all optics and photonics centre opc invites all interested to a series of lectures by wellknown scientists in areas of optics and photonics details of lecture in this series is given below title singlecavity dualcomb lasers revolutionizing spectroscopy and ultrafast measurements speaker ursula keller affiliation eth zurich department of information technology and electrical engineering zürich switzerland mode online date th november time pm ist weblink to join abstract the optical frequency comb ofc revolution began in the late marked by three pivotal publications since then the field has been a major focus of research continuously evolving with new innovations an key advancement in ofc technology are dualcomb lasers which employs a pair of combs distinguished by a small yet precise difference in their spacing this allows for rapid pumpprobe and spectroscopy measurements without any mechanical delay lines we have invented new sharedcavity methods to generate two optical combs with slightly different adjustable pulse repetition rates by generating both combs within the same cavity the system is simplified and the combs exhibit highly correlated noise properties these singlecavity dualcomb lasers achieve low noise levels making them suitable for practical dualcomb measurements we pioneered two techniques based on polarization and spatial multiplexing in the polarization multiplexing approach enabled dualcomb spectroscopy from a single freerunning passively modelocked laser cavity a key milestone since then we have demonstrated lownoise performance using diodepumped ybdoped solidstate and verticalemitting semiconductor lasers to verify these lownoise properties we developed a highly sensitive pulse timing jitter characterization tool we have demonstrated coherent averaging of dualcomb signals enabling dualcomb spectroscopy applications with excellent signaltonoise ratios from freerunning dualcomb oscillators without additional stabilization many application demonstrations have been done with these lasers such as picosecond ultrasonics lidar timedomain thz spectroscopy equivalent sampling of sesam response spectroscopy with adjustable delay intervals d microscopy opo and midir spectroscopy and biomedical applications this talk will provide an introduction to dualcomb lasers and highlight several specific application demonstrations biography ursula keller a tenured physics professor at eth zurich since directed the nccr must ultrafast science program from to she earned her diplom from eth zurich in and a phd from stanford university in as a member of technical staff mts at bell labs from to she launched her independent research career keller cofounded timebandwidth products was acquired by jdsu in and k photonics in since she has served on the supervisory board of jenoptik her research is dedicated to advancing ultrafast science and technology with advancements in ultrafast solidstate and semiconductor lasers utilizing semiconductor saturable absorber mirrors sesams and achieving ultrashort pulse generation in the one to two opticalcycle regime with frequency comb generation and stabilization she applied these lasers to conduct attosecond experiments testing fundamental processes in quantum mechanics and pioneered the attoclock technique her awards include the swiss science prize marcel benoist international member of the national academy of sciences usa osa frederic ives medal spie gold medal ieee edison medal osa charles h townes award eps senior prize and two erc advanced grants and keller has supervised phd students authored journal articles and holds an hindex of with over citations according to google scholar in she authored a new graduate textbook on ultrafast lasers published by springer verlag h telle et al appl phys b – a apolonski et al phys rev lett – d j jones et al science – s m link et al optics express j pupeikis et al optica s m link et Subject: invitation to an institute lecture by prof bhim singh on th november
Body: dear students and colleagues we are delighted to invite you to an institute lecture by prof bhim singh emeritus professor at iit delhi recipient of the prestigious vigyan shri award in engineering sciences for his immense contribution towards the development of power electronics for renewable energy sources including emobility the award was presented to prof singh by the hon’ble president of india smt droupadi murmu on august the details of the lecture are provided below speaker prof bhim singh emeritus professor at iit delhi title renewable energya sustainable solution for humanity datetimevenue th november pm seminar hall abstract the global shift towards renewable energy has become imperative in addressing the challenges posed by climate change environmental degradation and the depletion of finite fossil fuels this talk will explore how solar photovoltaic energy offers a sustainable solution for humanity by analysing current technological advancements policy frameworks and economic impacts the talk highlights the potential of renewable energy to provide a reliable costeffective and environmentally friendly alternative to conventional energy sources additionally the talk will cover the socioeconomic benefits of renewable energy adoption such as job creation energy security and reduced greenhouse gas emissions as the world moves towards a lowcarbon future renewable energy emerges not only as a necessity but as a cornerstone for sustainable development and a cleaner more resilient future for allthe largescale development and deployment of renewable energy technologies are essential to the global pursuit of decarbonizing the energy sector to effectively harness variable and intermittent renewable energy sources like solar and wind and to integrate the electricity generated by these plants power electronics play a crucial role developing testing and commercializing appropriate power electronic devices such as voltage source converters and dcdc converters are key to maximizing the benefits of renewable energy the challenges involved are complex and require a comprehensive understanding of renewable energy resource characteristics electric machines electricity generation transmission distribution utilization systems circuit analysis and power electronics about the speaker professor bhim singh has received his be electrical from the university of roorkee now iit roorkee india in and his mtech power apparatus systems and phd from the indian institute of technology delhi india in and respectively in he joined the department of electrical engineering university of roorkee as a lecturer he became a reader there in in december he joined the department of electrical engineering iit delhi india as an assistant professor where he became an associate professor in and a professor in professor singh is currently serving as an emeritus professor and serb national science chair at iit delhi since july professor singh is the chairman of bog sardar vallabhbhai national institute of technology surat since th august july for years he has published research papers in journals and more than papers in conferencesprof singh has guided phd dissertations and memtechmsr theses he has granted patents and filed patents he has executed more than ninety sponsored and consultancy projects he has coauthored a textbook on power quality power quality problems and mitigation techniques published by john wiley sons ltd best regards subodh sharma associate dean academics outreach new initiatives pankaj gupta chair professor of privacy and decentralisation associate professor department of computer science and engineering iit delhi

Subject: research seminar on materials and structural chemistry friday th november at pm
Body: dear all we are glad to invite you to the research seminar talks by two distinguished scientists this friday th november afternoon in the department of chemistry venue committee room department of chemistry time date pm th november friday here is the schedule of the talks pm pm ‘in situ and in operando xray scattering studies in materials chemistry’ by prof bo b iversen department of chemistry and interdisciplinary nanoscience center aarhus university denmark pm pm ‘superelectrophilic anions that bind noble gases’ – by prof simon grabowsky university of bern department of chemistry biochemistry and pharmaceutical sciences switzerland research interests of prof bo b iversen prof iversen is a leader in materials science and crystallography with expertise spanning the broad areas of thermoelectrics battery materials and supercritical fluids iversens work focuses on exploiting the tremendous power of structural studies to obtain a proper understanding of material properties this involves materials synthesis advanced property characterization as well as first principles computations the research interests of the iversen group revolve around topics in materials chemistry and materials crystallography with emphasis on application of synchrotron and neutron scattering methods they include synthesis characterization and application of energy materials chemical bonding electron density analysis nanoparticles supercritical fluids and hydrothermal liquefaction biooil research interests of prof simon grabowsky prof grabowsky is a leading scientist in the field of xray quantum crystallography and structural chemistry focusing on computational and experimental studies on chemical bonding especially those of inorganic molecular compounds please see the link below for poster you are all invited to attend the talks and the following scientific discussion best regards seminar organizing committee

are going to start from october please read the instructions below carefully morning afternoon oct thu g g oct sat g g oct mon g g oct tue g g oct wed g g nov mon g g nov tue g g nov wed g g nov thu g g nov fri g g three experiments will be conducted for the practical exam chemical kinetics potentiometric titration conductometric titration in the practical exam you will perform a new experiment using the methods of regular cmp experiments the procedure for the unknown experiment will be given to you before the test instructions when you enter the lab you randomly pick up one slip from the box that contains the code for your experiment you need to show that slip to the ta then heshe will enter the code of your experiment in the register you show the slip to the lab staff and they will show your working place after receiving your question paper you must follow the instructions some of the instructions will be given on your working bench stock solutions are labeled as a to r it will you should not talk with your colleagues during the test if your instructorta staff notices that you are talking with your colleagues they can reduce marks in the exam all the students get different concentrations as variables it is not possible to copy the results from others your results are unique that will not match with any other students results you bring all the necessary stationary items for the test penpencilerasercalculator etc do not disturb your colleagueslab staff for these items you should keep mobile phones on silent mode in the designated baggage area recheck whether you wrote your name entry number and group number on the answer sheet before giving it to the ta please sign a sheet for attendance after checking all your previous marks in quizzes and handouts please check Body: highlights amazon delhi session with yann lecun iit delhi wins this years interiit aquatics meet iit delhi and aiims jointly awarded major centre of excellence ai in healthcare paniit and iit delhi alumni events in amsterdam and paris new initiative of indian knowledge systems upcoming alumni events diamond jubilee reunion class of and crystal reunion class of alumniinstitute networking meet new yorknew jersey amazon delhi iit delhi hosted dr werner vogels chief technology officer of amazon for an insightful session on ai for good dr vogels shared his vision of how artificial intelligence can tackle some of the worlds most pressing challenges drawing from his work with startups focused on education and social impact the event which saw an overwhelming response from students and faculty emphasized ais potential to drive positive societal change and reshape industries dr vogels talk ignited discussions on the role of academia in contributing to aipowered solutions for global issues session with yann lecun dr yann lecun metas chief ai scientist and a pioneer in artificial intelligence and turing award winner visited and participated in a panel discussion at iitdelhi on october laying out his vision for the future of ai and its intersection with human capabilities during the panel discussion titled from neural mimics to smart assistants a journey into ais next frontiers dr yann emphasized the need for a rethink of ai architectures the advantages of opensource and indias unique potential in the ai landscape india has an important part to play in this because of the size of the population the diversity of cultures and value systems yann said the panel discussion was moderated by vishal gondal founder and ceo of goqii and iit delhi alumna jo agarwal cofounder and ceo of wysa iit delhi wins this years interiit aquatics meet honda cars india limited hcil has partnered with iit delhi to push the boundaries of cooperative intelligence ci an innovative ai technology aimed at improving humanmachine interaction this collaboration will focus on advancing automated driving systems and enhancing traffic safety through joint research and technology demonstrations under a recently signed memorandum of understanding mou iit delhi researchers will work closely with engineers from hcil and honda rd co ltd the goal is to develop aidriven solutions that enable smoother communication and collaboration between humans and machines ultimately paving the way for safer more efficient mobility systems iit delhi and aiims jointly awarded major centre of excellence ai in healthcare ministry of education announced establishment of three ai centres of excellence coe focused on healthcare agriculture and sustainable cities the goal is to foster interdisciplinary research develop innovative ai applications and create scalable solutions to address key challenges in these areas the coe on ai in healthcare with a budget of about rs crores over a period of five years will be jointly led iit delhi and aiims all india institute of medical sciences new delhi paniit and iit delhi alumni events in amsterdam and paris the pan iit global conference in amsterdam held on october th and th saw many iit directors and deans in attendance iit alumni from europe india usa and other parts of the world participated in this twoday event organized by paniit europe with a strong support from indian embassy in netherlands technology incubation heads from iits too attended this conference menu new initiatives towards advancement of iits were discussed during the event on the side lines of pan iit global conference a get together of iit delhi alumni was organized which was also attended by many iit delhi alumni based in netherlands the event saw fantastic participation as alumni from across decades came together to share experiences reminisce and reconnect alumni gave many new suggestions towards the advancement of institute and health programme funded by the french government where iit delhi is one of the partnering institutes this programme fosters a collaborative ecosystem linking universities research institutions hospitals startups and corporates its mission is to advance education and research in life sciences for health in order to address global health challenges new initiative of indian knowledge systems iit delhi launched a programme on indian knowledge systems iks with support from alumnus shri ram gupta the new programme aims to advance the integration of indian knowledge traditions with contemporary academic and research frameworks fostering dialogue between civilizational wisdom and scientific inquiry indian knowledge systems is an important area highlighted by the national Subject: new credit course announcement transformation of the transport system and cities for a sustainable future trv

Body: dear all transportation research and injury prevention centre is offering a onecredit course trv by prof herman knoflacher tu vienna for registration please send an email to the course coordinator prof rahul goel with a subject line indicating the course number we will send you an email confirming your registration trv the practice of the paradigm shift in transport and urban planning problems and successes of implementation one credit course evaluation attendance and quiz dates and november pm pm with breaks please do not register for this course if you have registered for trv in the ongoing semester as the class schedule will clash venue we will let you know prerequisite none note that the same eligibility criteria will be applied for students to register for the course as the usual erp registration eg maximum credits allowed in a semester course instructor the course will be offered by prof herman knoflacher who is the university professor of the institute for transport planning and traffic engineering university of technology vienna tu wien his research focus includes the design of transport elements transport system user behavior traffic infrastructure and mobility sustainable development of cities and mobility traffic safety energy consumption environment and basic interdisciplinary research about the course paradigm shift has become a buzzword and is applied in many areas although it is not fit for that this is the case in the transport sector as well as in urban and regional planning research is still done primarily at the symptom levels data is collected and measures are implemented and assumptions are made about peoples behavior the foundations for the paradigm shift in transport were laid in the years and practical implementation also began in some areas during this period however it has been enormously delayed due to the lack of both specialists and farsighted politicians nevertheless in the last years experiences with the effectiveness of the measures have been collected and analyzed from pedestrian traffic bicycle traffic and public transport and above all the elasticities in the modal split the course will cover these aspects of paradigm shift warm regards ramachandra rao kalaga ramachandra rao professor and head transportation research and injury prevention centre ms main building iit delhi Subject: mathsoc student lecture series talk
Body: dear students here is another interesting lecture series from mathsoc for you please find the details of the event below continuing our exploration of intriguing concepts in mathematics were excited to invite you to the next talk in our series partypopper this session takes us into the intersection of mathematics and quantum mechanics offering insight into the fascinating world of mutually unbiased bases mubs and their applications whether youre drawn to quantum theory or just curious about the structure of quantum tests this talk promises to be an enlightening experience barchart topic an introductory look into mutually unbiased bases speaker uditanshu sadual abstract in quantum mechanics two tests are considered complementary if the outcome of one reveals no information about the other this idea is formalised through mutually unbiased bases mubs for a complex space of dimension constructing a complete set of mubs is possible only when is a prime power for composite dimensions that do not fit this form full sets of mubs remain elusive to address this gap researchers develop approximate versions amubs in this talk well explore the properties and applications of mubs including their roles in optimal state determination entropic uncertainty measures and entanglement properties well also discuss how projective and unitary design features of mubs help us gauge how closely amubs approximate true mubs about the speaker uditanshu is a ndyear msc mathematics student with a keen interest in number theory algebra and topologybut hes easily tempted by an array of other topics too his talk is inspired by his summer internship at isi kolkata where he worked under prof subhamoy maitra in quantum cryptography outside academia youll often find him dancing or playing the flute and hes quite active on instagram as well spiralcalendar date roundpushpin venue mz mathematics department committee room alarmclock time pm join us for an engaging session that bridges abstract mathematics with quantum applications this is a unique opportunity to learn how mubs play a crucial role in the evolving field of quantum information dont miss out glowingstar for queries contact maalav best regards mathsoc iit delhi regards sumit singh general secretary cocurricular and academic interaction council caic iit delhi

Subject: civil engineering seminar series professor eng davide forcellini from the universita degli studi della repubblica di san marino scheduled on wednesday th october at noon
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend the civil engineering seminar by professor eng davide forcellini from the universita degli studi della repubblica di san marino scheduled on wednesday th october at noon in committee room block iv room no department of civil engineering title of the seminar dadvanced numerical simulations of soilstructure interaction ssi abstract of the seminar soil structure interaction ssi plays a significant role during seismic excitations for structures therefore many researchers have assessed its importance in emphasizing earthquake response both in buildings and bridge arena in this seminar a d numerical simulation of a soilstructure system that applies nonlinear hysteretic materials with advanced plasticity models shall be presented this approach enables to reproduce soil hysteretic elastoplastic shear response including permanent deformations and thus damping foundation impedances in particular applying the opensource computational interface openseespl implemented within the fe code opensees will be discussed this framework is capable of performing nonlinear dynamic analysis and apply userdefined materials to model the soil it is also powerful in modeling the interface and boundary conditions that are of extreme importance in ssi problems the aim is to reproduce the seismic response by a parametric study based on mutual behavior of soil and structural deformability in order to assess safety and cost reduction when ssi is considered in design procedures this talk will highlight assessment of seismic performances aiming at contributing to new easytouse design procedures for engineers all over the world brief biography of the speaker professor eng davide forcellini received his masters degree from the university of bologna in civil and environmental engineering in his masters thesis entitled study of soil structure interaction was developed in collaboration at the university of california san diego in collaboration with prof ahmed elgamal and dr jinchi lu since then he has continued to collaborate with prof ahmed elgamal and prof james m kelly at university of california uc berkeley usa he worked as a bridge engineer between and since he has been teaching at the universita degli studi della repubblica di san marino the university of san marino he completed his phd a structural optimized performance based earthquake engineering methodology and riskmanagement decision making at the university of san marino all interested are cordially invited to attend the seminar thank you head Subject: spp academic nov in lh
Body: dear colleagues and students our next academic seminar will be held on november th and will be delivered by prof shyama v ramani an economist by training who now runs her own ngo in kameswaram tn further details of the seminar appear below best wishes suma title on steering a behavioural transition from open defecation to toilet usage for sustainability speaker shyama ramani friend in need india trust and site sustainability abstract when toilets are introduced as a niche innovation in communities where the dominant social norm is open defacation od under what circumstances are there tipping points directed towards od free odf state to answer this question a twostep methodology is applied first a simple evolutionary game theoretic model of social norms is developed this game setting is inspired by the seminal works of fishbein and fishbein and ajzen in socialpsychology their theory of reasoned action and planned behavior tra offers a conceptual framework of the links between preexisting attitudes and behavioral intentions to predict behavior second simulations are conducted to identify factors influencing the tipping point towards universal toilet usage the findings contribute to understanding tipping points for social norm transitions the study shows how village characteristics existing social norms sanitation programs features and the evolving confidence of community members in using toilets drive the dynamics some villages transition to odf while others stagnate or even revert to od this highlights the importance of targeted interventions to influence tipping dynamics and achieve sustainable odf communities suma athreye school of public policy iit delhi

Subject: talk by dr chinmoy bhattacharya on array processing on oct at pm
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to a talk on array processing by dr chinmoy bhattacharya on monday oct at pm in room iia bharti school this talk is being jointly organised by the ieee vts delhi section chapter and bharti school further details about the talk and the speaker are given below talk title different facets of array processing an overview abstract array processing has existed for many years in radar sonar and radio astronomy signal processing and also for biomedical imaging such as computerized tomography ct recent advances in wireless standards from g to g g are generating not only explosive amounts of data but are bringing the concepts of digital beamforming adaptive smart antenna that heavily draws strength from the knowledge of existing radar phased array processing for the last two decades mimo is another general class of array processing that encompasses both radar and wireless communication paradigms in this talk we will attempt to provide a broad overview of array processing starting with uniform linear array ula to phased array digital beamforming to virtual array formation in autonomous vehicles to augment resolution in the azimuthal plane of the vehicle certain simulation results will be provided to illustrate the concepts raised in the talk speaker biography chinmoy bhattacharya received his be and me degrees in electronics and telecommunication from jadavpur university kolkata wb india he received his phd degree in from jadavpur university for his work on analysis of sar signal correlation in scalespace framework he was the head of electronics engineering department at the defence institute of advanced technology diat pune mh india from may to february he superannuated as a senior research scientist from armament research development establishment arde drdo pune india in january currently he is an adjunct professor of electronic instrumentation science sppu pune in this capacity he was the program chair for a national workshop on g wireless communication in pune university on february his research areas include signal processing for various radar and sensor configurations stochastic processes bioinformatics and mimo antennas in automobile applications he is a senior member of the ieee signal processing society usa regards seshan dr seshan srirangarajan associate professor department of Subject: reminder lecture on october the role of quantum information and microelectronics technologies in future information processing by prof supratik guha u chicago anl
Body: ieee electron devices society and the mrs university chapter at iit delhi welcome you to the following talk title the role of quantum information and microelectronics technologies in future information processing speaker prof supratik guha pritzker school of molecular engineering university of chicago scientific advisor argonne national laboratory venue lh lecture hall complex iit delhi date october time pm organized by iit delhi abstract it can be favorably argued that computing is beginning to have an impact upon our lives that the advent of the printing press in the th century has had the demands of energy ubiquity predictive accuracy and security that we expect from computing has pushed technology rd towards a couple of exciting directions in classical computing our conventional approaches have reached the limits of miniaturization as dictated by the laws of physics this calls for a fresh look at microelectronics the interaction of thermal electronic and possibly optical excitations in devices and their fabrication using nontraditional methods that exercise atomic level control in three dimensions at the same time the advent of quantum information science offers a theoretically sound way of computing sensing and communications with significant and specific advantages over classical methods but is limited by our ability to build the quantum coherent materials devices and systems capable of providing the superposition and entanglement control necessary these challenges have stimulated worldwide excitement in new rd fueled by governments academia established industry and startups it promises a vision of low power hybrid classical and quantum information processing in the future that will include computing communications and sensing in distributed and localized forms i will describe some of the breakthroughs and trends in ongoing materials and devices research in these areas worldwide and include as examples some of our ongoing research at the university of chicago and argonne national laboratory the talk will be at a general level accessible to a multidisciplinary audience bio supratik guha is a professor at the pritzker school of molecular engineering at the university of chicago and scientist at argonne national laboratorys physical sciences and engineering directorate where he leads the labs microelectronics and quantum information science strategic efforts he is the chief technology officer at the argonne led qnext one of the five department of energy national quantum information centers he is also the faculty director of the university of chicago delhi centre before joining argonne and the university of chicago in he spent twenty years at ibm research where he last served as the director of physical sciences responsible for ibms worldwide research in the physical sciences at ibm guha pioneered the materials research that led to ibms high dielectric constant metal gate transistor one of the most significant developments in silicon microelectronics technology the materials introduced by him can be found in the processors of the majority of smart phone products today as well as in ibm servers prior to leaving ibm in he was responsible for initiating as a manager ibms quantum computer on the cloud model and project and was the first professional manager to put together a multidisciplinary team for an integrated design of a quantum processor at argonne he has served as the director of the center for nanoscale materials and as the science advisor to the director responsible for argonnes overall science strategy his current research is on the discovery science of new materials and devices for future information technologies

Subject: reminder me guest talk by prof anupam sharma aerospace engineering at iowa state university usa
Body: dear all prof anupam sharma from the department of aerospace engineering at iowa state university usa will visit iit delhi a mechanical engineering guest talk is scheduled as below date friday th october time pm venue me seminar room block ii mechanical engineering department title dynamic stall onset and its prediction abstract dynamic stall is frequently observed in the rotor blades of helicopters wind turbines and the wings of rapidly maneuvering aircraft it results in significant unsteady forces and moments due to leadingedge vortex shedding while insects and small birds such as hummingbirds utilize this unsteady lift to enhance their flight this advantage is limited primarily to very low reynolds numbers re at moderate to high re the unsteady loads from dynamic stall can cause fatigue or catastrophic failure effective stall control measures are best applied at the onset of dynamic stall marked by the emergence of the dynamic stall vortex dsv consequently accurately identifying the onset of stall is crucial for practical applications and reducedorder modeling however predicting this phenomenon is challenging due to the need to resolve very smallscale events in the boundary layer this talk will explore various aspects of dynamic stall onset and is organized into three parts first he will present phenomena occurring during stall onset supported by wallresolved largeeddy simulations les results at moderate re the role of the laminar separation bubble lsb in stall onset will be emphasized along with the impact of airfoil geometry particularly thickness on the stall mechanism the second part will focus on characterizing the onset of dynamic stall introducing a novel parameter based on vorticity to estimate stall incipience across different types of dynamic stall in low and highre conditions finally he will discuss ongoing efforts to predict dynamic stall using costeffective hybrid ransles methods where we enhance rans models with les and experimental data through machine learning prof sharma is also available to meet with interested faculties and students before the talk please let us know all interested are welcome to join the talk please see the link below regards dr abhishek das and dr pratik das me seminar committee department of mechanical engineering iit delhi

Subject: reminderseminar by prof thamar solorio ee committee room oct am
Body: title the case of low resource nlp abstract low resource nlp is nowadays an umbrella keyword that covers a wide set of research directions often times the languages we use for developing and evaluating nlp approaches are not low in resources and we simply simulate a low resource scenario by limiting the amount of training data we give to our models in our recent work we argue that it is important to distinguish when the languages are truly lacking resources and propose to follow a more systematic way to represent work in this space i will present this position in my talk and will also discuss recent work in my group that contributes to improve language representation by exploring efficient approaches to diverse languages about the speaker thamar solorio is a professor in the nlp department at mbzuai she is also a tenured professor of computer science at the university of houston currently on leave she is the director and founder of the ritual lab her research interests include nlp for lowresource settings and multilingual data including codeswitching and information extraction more recently her interests have moved towards language and vision problems focusing on developing inclusive nlp she received a national science foundation nsf career award for her work on authorship attribution and was awarded the emerging leader abie award in honor of denice denton she served two terms as an elected board member of the north american chapter of the association of computational linguistics naacl and was pc cochair for naacl she is an editor in chief for the acl rolling review arr initiative and was a member of the advisory board for arr she serves as general chair for the conference on empirical methods in natural language processing dr jayadeva gsv chair professor ee department iit delhi

Subject: lecture on october the role of quantum information and microelectronics technologies in future information processing by prof supratik guha u chicago anl
Body: ieee electron devices society and the mrs university chapter at iit delhi welcome you to the following talk title the role of quantum information and microelectronics technologies in future information processing speaker prof supratik guha pritzker school of molecular engineering university of chicago scientific advisor argonne national laboratory venue lh lecture hall complex iit delhi date october time pm organized by iit delhi abstract it can be favorably argued that computing is beginning to have an impact upon our lives that the advent of the printing press in the th century has had the demands of energy ubiquity predictive accuracy and security that we expect from computing has pushed technology rd towards a couple of exciting directions in classical computing our conventional approaches have reached the limits of miniaturization as dictated by the laws of physics this calls for a fresh look at microelectronics the interaction of thermal electronic and possibly optical excitations in devices and their fabrication using nontraditional methods that exercise atomic level control in three dimensions at the same time the advent of quantum information science offers a theoretically sound way of computing sensing and communications with significant and specific advantages over classical methods but is limited by our ability to build the quantum coherent materials devices and systems capable of providing the superposition and entanglement control necessary these challenges have stimulated worldwide excitement in new rd fueled by governments academia established industry and startups it promises a vision of low power hybrid classical and quantum information processing in the future that will include computing communications and sensing in distributed and localized forms i will describe some of the breakthroughs and trends in ongoing materials and devices research in these areas worldwide and include as examples some of our ongoing research at the university of chicago and argonne national laboratory the talk will be at a general level accessible to a multidisciplinary audience bio supratik guha is a professor at the pritzker school of molecular engineering at the university of chicago and scientist at argonne national laboratorys physical sciences and engineering directorate where he leads the labs microelectronics and quantum information science strategic efforts he is the chief technology officer at the argonne led qnext one of the five department of energy national quantum information centers he is also the faculty director of the university of chicago delhi centre before joining argonne and the university of chicago in he spent twenty years at ibm research where he last served as the director of physical sciences responsible for ibms worldwide research in the physical sciences at ibm guha pioneered the materials research that led to ibms high dielectric constant metal gate transistor one of the most significant developments in silicon microelectronics technology the materials introduced by him can be found in the processors of the majority of smart phone products today as well as in ibm servers prior to leaving ibm in he was responsible for initiating as a manager ibms quantum computer on the cloud model and project and was the first professional manager to put together a multidisciplinary team for an integrated design of a quantum processor at argonne he has served as the director of the center for nanoscale materials and as the science advisor to the director responsible for argonnes overall science strategy his current research is on the discovery science of new materials and devices for future information technologies

Subject: me guest talk by prof anupam sharma aerospace engineering at iowa state university usa
Body: dear all prof anupam sharma from the department of aerospace engineering at iowa state university usa will visit iit delhi a mechanical engineering guest talk is scheduled as below date friday th october time pm venue me seminar room block ii mechanical engineering department title dynamic stall onset and its prediction abstract dynamic stall is frequently observed in the rotor blades of helicopters wind turbines and the wings of rapidly maneuvering aircraft it results in significant unsteady forces and moments due to leadingedge vortex shedding while insects and small birds such as hummingbirds utilize this unsteady lift to enhance their flight this advantage is limited primarily to very low reynolds numbers re at moderate to high re the unsteady loads from dynamic stall can cause fatigue or catastrophic failure effective stall control measures are best applied at the onset of dynamic stall marked by the emergence of the dynamic stall vortex dsv consequently accurately identifying the onset of stall is crucial for practical applications and reducedorder modeling however predicting this phenomenon is challenging due to the need to resolve very smallscale events in the boundary layer this talk will explore various aspects of dynamic stall onset and is organized into three parts first he will present phenomena occurring during stall onset supported by wallresolved largeeddy simulations les results at moderate re the role of the laminar separation bubble lsb in stall onset will be emphasized along with the impact of airfoil geometry particularly thickness on the stall mechanism the second part will focus on characterizing the onset of dynamic stall introducing a novel parameter based on vorticity to estimate stall incipience across different types of dynamic stall in low and highre conditions finally he will discuss ongoing efforts to predict dynamic stall using costeffective hybrid ransles methods where we enhance rans models with les and experimental data through machine learning prof sharma is also available to meet with interested faculties and students before the talk please let us know all interested are welcome to join the talk please see the link below regards dr abhishek das and dr pratik das me seminar committee department of mechanical engineering iit delhi

Subject: re annual public lecture of the new ma culture society thought oct at pm
Body: dear all this is a gentle reminder for the talk today please be seated in the seminar hall minutes before the start of the event best regards subodh subodh sharma associate dean academics outreach new initiatives pankaj gupta chair professor of privacy and decentralisation associate professor department of computer science and engineering iit delhi on oct at pm seminar wrote dear all on the occasion of the rolling out of the new ma culture society thought programme with its very first batch admitted in july we are launching the macst annual public lecture series the first annual lecture will be delivered by prof upinder singh eminent historian of ancient india and professor at ashoka university the series will be launched on this occasion by our director prof rangan banerjee dean of academics prof narayan kurur and head hss dept prof farhana ibrahim it is our great pleasure to welcome all the faculty students and staff of our institute to attend this event and we hope to see many of you there please save the date title himsaahimsa ancient debates on a perennial problem date nd october time pm venue seminar hall about the speaker prof upinder singh taught in st stephens college and the history department of the university of delhi before moving to ashoka university her expertise ranges over various aspects of ancient indian history and archaeology the history of ideas and indias interactions with the wider world she is the author of kings brāhmaṇas and temples in orissa an epigraphic study ad – ancient delhi the discovery of ancient india early archaeologists and the beginnings of archaeology a history of ancient and early medieval india from the stone age to the twelfth century the idea of ancient india essays on religion politics and archaeology political violence in ancient india and ancient india culture of contradictions she has edited delhi ancient history rethinking early medieval india and has coedited ancient india new research asian encounters exploring connected histories buddhism in asia revival and reinvention the world of indias first archaeologist letters from alexander cunningham to jdm beglar her most recent publications are new revised editions of her collection of essays the idea of ancient india and of her panoramic a history of ancient and early medieval india singh has been a recipient of the netherlands government reciprocal fellowship ancient india and iran trustwallace india visiting fellowship daniel ingalls fellowship at the harvardyenching institute and erasmus mundus fellowship at the university of leuven she was awarded the infosys award for social sciences—history in abstract of lecture the idea of a nonviolent ancient indian past is a myth but behind this myth lies the fact that ancient indian thinkers engaged seriously and intensely with the tension between violence and nonviolence perhaps more so than those in other parts of the world all traditions including the religions of nonviolence such as jainism and buddhism acknowledged that a certain amount of violence was necessary for rulers however a distinction was made between force that was necessary proportionate and legitimate on the one hand and that which was unnecessary excessive and illegitimate on the other through a discussion of the ideas of two wellknown figures the maurya emperor ashoka and the political theorist kautilya the lecture will show how two very different perspectives—one rooted in dharma the other in artha—could in fact converge engaging with the nuances of these ancient debates helps us think more meaningfully about our distant past and the problem of political violence in our own time please see the link below best wishes madhulika sonkar tsering nurboo and divya dwivedi macst coordinators with academic outreach and new initiatives iit delhi divya dwivedi associate professor philosophy and literature dept of humanities social sciences indian institute of technology delhi

the seminar combining environmental and phenotypic data unlocks vital cropenvironment relationships tech like remote sensing and iot offer realtime insights on crop health soil climate diseases and Subject: third annual dinesh mohan memorial lecture october
Body: the third dinesh mohan annual memorial lecture will be organised by the transportation research and injury prevention centre tripc indian institute of technology delhi you are cordially invited to the lecture event details day and date friday th october time hours venue seminar hall speaker dr nimmi l candappa project lead victorian network safety plan australia title reduce refine separate and mobilise applying safety principles to designs and across countries abstract since the first recorded fatality in the late s millions upon millions of lives have been lost on our roads worldwide in highincome or lowincome countries despite much investment research and investigation stringent enforcement design development and redevelopment death and severe injury persist on our roads at the end of last year the world health organization reiterated that road safety remains an urgent global issue this presentation explores reasons why driving a car presents a persistent safety challenge despite the years of work in this area and identifies some of the overall safety principles adopted within victorian road safety countermeasures to create a foundation for road safety concrete examples are used to highlight the ongoing creativity needed to embed the principles into practical designs and the importance of looking beyond the principles being a road safety detective in unearthing additional ways of improving safety with a particular focus on possible challenges in existing wire rope safety barrier design the presentation concludes with some broad comments on some difficulties in research transfer across countries the need to mobilise the road user for ultimate safety and the even greater need for a global collaboration to address road safety where it is most urgent in the low and middleincome countries about the speaker dr nimmi candappa is a traffic and road safety engineer with a phd in wire rope safety barriers she has over years of experience having worked at the victorian road authority monash university accident research centre muarc as well as being seconded to the dutch research institute swov with expertise in intersection safety wire rope safety barriers and safe system design her current role is to help implement safe system design across the victorian road network to eliminate deaths deepty jain phd assistant professor head who collaborating centre transportation research and injury prevention centre tripc indian institute of technology delhi iitd ms main building hauz khas new delhi pincode ph

Subject: seminar by prof thamar solorio ee committee room oct am
Body: title the case of low resource nlp abstract low resource nlp is nowadays an umbrella keyword that covers a wide set of research directions often times the languages we use for developing and evaluating nlp approaches are not low in resources and we simply simulate a low resource scenario by limiting the amount of training data we give to our models in our recent work we argue that it is important to distinguish when the languages are truly lacking resources and propose to follow a more systematic way to represent work in this space i will present this position in my talk and will also discuss recent work in my group that contributes to improve language representation by exploring efficient approaches to diverse languages about the speaker thamar solorio is a professor in the nlp department at mbzuai she is also a tenured professor of computer science at the university of houston currently on leave she is the director and founder of the ritual lab her research interests include nlp for lowresource settings and multilingual data including codeswitching and information extraction more recently her interests have moved towards language and vision problems focusing on developing inclusive nlp she received a national science foundation nsf career award for her work on authorship attribution and was awarded the emerging leader abie award in honor of denice denton she served two terms as an elected board member of the north american chapter of the association of computational linguistics naacl and was pc cochair for naacl she is an editor in chief for the acl rolling review arr initiative and was a member of the advisory board for arr she serves as general chair for the conference on empirical methods in natural language processing dr jayadeva gsv chair professor ee department iit delhi

Subject: phd viva cum talk announcement an optimization based framework for graph coarsening
Body: dear all we invite you to an insightful talkcum thesis defense of manoj kumar scheduled for tomorrow name mr manoj kumar eez research scholar dept of ee topic an optimization based framework for graph coarsening date monday time am onwards venue ee commiittee room block ii teams link link for the meeting title an optimizationbased framework for graph coarsening this thesis presents a comprehensive development of graph coarsening a critical dimensionality reduction technique that aims to create a smaller more manageable graph version while preserving its key properties many realworld graphs consist of structural data and contain features or contexts associated with each node traditional graph coarsening methods typically overlook these node features relying solely on a graph matrix eg adjacency or laplacian some recent deep learningbased approaches address this by incorporating both the graph matrix and node features but they are often designed for specific tasks this thesis introduces a novel optimizationbased framework for graph coarsening that takes both the graph matrix and node features as input learning a coarsened graph matrix and feature matrix simultaneously while ensuring that the coarsened graph remains ϵ ∈ similar to the original graph the featured graph coarsening fgc framework and its variants developed in the thesis represent a significant breakthrough in addressing computational challenges in largescale graph analysis extensive experiments using real and synthetic datasets validate the effectiveness of this framework in various applications such as graph clustering node classification stochastic block model identification and graph summarization moreover in various domains eg healthcare finance etc where graph structures are often unavailable this work also introduces methods to learn coarsened graphs directly from raw data eliminating the need for an initial graph structure and significantly enhancing scalability additionally a convex optimization framework is introduced which reduces computational complexity without sacrificing accuracy this research advances graph theory and contributes to a wide range of fields such as machine learning social networks and biological systems the thesis concludes with exciting future research directions including semisupervised coarsened graph learning and interdisciplinary applications underscoring its broad impact on graphbased machine learning the outcome of the work is featured in prestigious venues including icml jmlr uai miccai etc published kumar Subject: spp academic october in lh
Body: speaker dr pooja prasad venue lh title water security in semiarid regions are public investments in irrigation leading to climate resilience in agriculture abstract in this talk i first motivate why its important to study the semiarid rainfed regions and how changing monsoon patterns and increasing dry spells impact farmer vulnerability i then analyze public investments made for climate resilient agriculture the majority of which include investments in horticulture microirrigation and farm ponds using a sociohydrological approach i argue that the current investments which are made at farmscale may appear to address vulnerability of the beneficiary farmer but at the systems scale they worsen the impact of dry spells and droughts for the majority of smallholder farmers i call for the need to reimagine ways in which climate resilience in agriculture may be operationalized with principles of equity and justice at its core i will end with some recent work on this and share my research vision for the next years bio pooja prasad is an assistant professor in the school of public policy at iit delhi her research aims to influence public investments in land and water management to support livelihood security and sustainability in highly uncertain waterstressed regions of south asia and africa pooja uses a systems lens and a sociohydrological approach to capture interactions within and between social and natural systems prior to joining iit delhi pooja was a postdoctoral researcher at ihe delft institute for water education in the netherlands pooja has a phd in technology and development from ctara iit bombay she has a masters’ degree from stanford university and a btech from iit bombay links suma athreye school of public policy iit delhi

Subject: annual public lecture of the new ma culture society thought oct at pm
Body: dear all on the occasion of the rolling out of the new ma culture society thought programme with its very first batch admitted in july we are launching the macst annual public lecture series the first annual lecture will be delivered by prof upinder singh eminent historian of ancient india and professor at ashoka university the series will be launched on this occasion by our director prof rangan banerjee dean of academics prof narayan kurur and head hss dept prof farhana ibrahim it is our great pleasure to welcome all the faculty students and staff of our institute to attend this event and we hope to see many of you there please save the date title himsaahimsa ancient debates on a perennial problem date nd october time pm venue to be announced about the speaker prof upinder singh taught in st stephens college and the history department of the university of delhi before moving to ashoka university her expertise ranges over various aspects of ancient indian history and archaeology the history of ideas and indias interactions with the wider world she is the author of kings brāhmaṇas and temples in orissa an epigraphic study ad ancient delhi the discovery of ancient india early archaeologists and the beginnings of archaeology a history of ancient and early medieval india from the stone age to the twelfth century the idea of ancient india essays on religion politics and archaeology political violence in ancient india and ancient india culture of contradictions she has edited delhi ancient history rethinking early medieval india and has coedited ancient india new research asian encounters exploring connected histories buddhism in asia revival and reinvention the world of indias first archaeologist letters from alexander cunningham to jdm beglar her most recent publications are new revised editions of her collection of essays the idea of ancient india and of her panoramic a history of ancient and early medieval india singh has been a recipient of the netherlands government reciprocal fellowship ancient india and iran trustwallace india visiting fellowship daniel ingalls fellowship at the harvardyenching institute and erasmus mundus fellowship at the university of leuven she was awarded the infosys award for social scienceshistory in abstract of lecture the idea of a nonviolent ancient indian past is a myth but behind this myth lies the fact that ancient indian thinkers engaged seriously and intensely with the tension between violence and nonviolence perhaps more so than those in other parts of the world all traditions including the religions of nonviolence such as jainism and buddhism acknowledged that a certain amount of violence was necessary for rulers however a distinction was made between force that was necessary proportionate and legitimate on the one hand and that which was unnecessary excessive and illegitimate on the other through a discussion of the ideas of two wellknown figures the maurya emperor ashoka and the political theorist kautilya the lecture will show how two very different perspectivesone rooted in dharma the other in arthacould in fact converge engaging with the nuances of these ancient debates helps us think more meaningfully about our distant past and the problem of political violence in our own time please see the link below best wishes madhulika sonkar tsering nurboo and divya dwivedi macst coordinators with academic outreach and new initiatives iit delhi divya dwivedi associate professor philosophy and literature dept of humanities social sciences indian institute of technology delhi

Subject: phd viva cum talk announcement an optimization based framework for graph coarsening
Body: dear all we invite you to an insightful talkcum thesis defense of manoj kumar on graph coarsening name mr manoj kumar eez research scholar topic an optimization based framework for graph coarsening date monday time hours onwards venue ee commiittee room block ii teams link link title an optimizationbased framework for graph coarsening this thesis presents a comprehensive development of graph coarsening a critical dimensionality reduction technique that aims to create a smaller more manageable graph version while preserving its key properties many realworld graphs consist of structural data and contain features or contexts associated with each node traditional graph coarsening methods typically overlook these node features relying solely on a graph matrix eg adjacency or laplacian some recent deep learningbased approaches address this by incorporating both the graph matrix and node features but they are often designed for specific tasks this thesis introduces a novel optimizationbased framework for graph coarsening that takes both the graph matrix and node features as input learning a coarsened graph matrix and feature matrix simultaneously while ensuring that the coarsened graph remains ϵ ∈ similar to the original graph the featured graph coarsening fgc framework and its variants developed in the thesis represent a significant breakthrough in addressing computational challenges in largescale graph analysis extensive experiments using real and synthetic datasets validate the effectiveness of this framework in various applications such as graph clustering node classification stochastic block model identification and graph summarization moreover in various domains eg healthcare finance etc where graph structures are often unavailable this work also introduces methods to learn coarsened graphs directly from raw data eliminating the need for an initial graph structure and significantly enhancing scalability additionally a convex optimization framework is introduced which reduces computational complexity without sacrificing accuracy this research advances graph theory and contributes to a wide range of fields such as machine learning social networks and biological systems the thesis concludes with exciting future research directions including semisupervised coarsened graph learning and interdisciplinary applications underscoring its broad impact on graphbased machine learning the outcome of the work is featured in prestigious venues including icml jmlr uai miccai etc published kumar manoj sharma a kumar s a Subject: nrcvee talk on october pm pm
Body: nrcvee invites you to a talk simplicity in the age of complexity ramana maharshi on navigating life in the st century october pm venue lecture hall complex lh in a world overwhelmed by complexity we invite you to join us for a talk about exploring how we can pair sri ramana maharshis teachings meant for selfdiscovery with contemporary science to reduce stress and foster resilience in this session we will make use of the teachings of sri ramana maharshi as well as current trends in neuropsychology to uncover practical ways of simplifying our lives and navigating the frenetic highspeed modern world if we find ourselves unable to avoid stress worry and anxiety then taking a moment to investigate the internal mechanisms that nudge us toward such restless states and explore ways of cultivating internal resilience could be time wellspent it is our earnest intent to make available actionable strategies for participants to free up clutter in their minds and discover purity in their hearts your family is welcome to join in for the talk the session will be for minutes followed by minutes for questions and answers speaker michael highburger born in the united states in michael highburger spent six years studying continental philosophy at ut austin the university of copenhagen and baylor university he undertook graduate work in philosophy and linguistic anthropology at ut austin with a later stint at brite divinity school in the year he moved to sri ramanasramam tamil nadu south india the community where he now serves and edits the official ramana monthly english language emagazine saranagati having authored and edited numerous books on the advaita vedanta of ramana maharshi his years in india has also involved the study of interfaith dialogue within hinduism buddhism and christianity where he assists in hosting groups from the west and participating in interfaith conferences in recent years he has been hosted by various governmental and nongovernmental organisations in europe to lecture and lead meditation retreats

Subject: annual public lecture of the new ma culture society thought oct at pm
Body: dear all on the occasion of the rolling out of the new ma culture society thought programme with its very first batch admitted in july we are launching the macst annual public lecture series the first annual lecture will be delivered by prof upinder singh eminent historian of ancient india and professor at ashoka university the series will be launched on this occasion by our director prof rangan banerjee dean of academics prof narayan kurur and head hss dept prof farhana ibrahim it is our great pleasure to welcome all the faculty students and staff of our institute to attend this event and we hope to see many of you there please save the date title himsaahimsa ancient debates on a perennial problem date nd october time pm venue to be announced about the speaker prof upinder singh taught in st stephens college and the history department of the university of delhi before moving to ashoka university her expertise ranges over various aspects of ancient indian history and archaeology the history of ideas and indias interactions with the wider world she is the author of kings brāhmaṇas and temples in orissa an epigraphic study ad ancient delhi the discovery of ancient india early archaeologists and the beginnings of archaeology a history of ancient and early medieval india from the stone age to the twelfth century the idea of ancient india essays on religion politics and archaeology political violence in ancient india and ancient india culture of contradictions she has edited delhi ancient history rethinking early medieval india and has coedited ancient india new research asian encounters exploring connected histories buddhism in asia revival and reinvention the world of indias first archaeologist letters from alexander cunningham to jdm beglar her most recent publications are new revised editions of her collection of essays the idea of ancient india and of her panoramic a history of ancient and early medieval india singh has been a recipient of the netherlands government reciprocal fellowship ancient india and iran trustwallace india visiting fellowship daniel ingalls fellowship at the harvardyenching institute and erasmus mundus fellowship at the university of leuven she was awarded the infosys award for social scienceshistory in abstract of lecture the idea of a nonviolent ancient indian past is a myth but behind this myth lies the fact that ancient indian thinkers engaged seriously and intensely with the tension between violence and nonviolence perhaps more so than those in other parts of the world all traditions including the religions of nonviolence such as jainism and buddhism acknowledged that a certain amount of violence was necessary for rulers however a distinction was made between force that was necessary proportionate and legitimate on the one hand and that which was unnecessary excessive and illegitimate on the other through a discussion of the ideas of two wellknown figures the maurya emperor ashoka and the political theorist kautilya the lecture will show how two very different perspectivesone rooted in dharma the other in arthacould in fact converge engaging with the nuances of these ancient debates helps us think more meaningfully about our distant past and the problem of political violence in our own time please see the link below best wishes madhulika sonkar tsering nurboo and divya dwivedi macst coordinators with academic outreach and new initiatives iit delhi divya dwivedi associate professor philosophy and literature dept of humanities social sciences indian institute of technology delhi

Subject: invitation to talk by prof havazelet biancopeled on new approaches toward materials for mucoadhesion and nanohydrogels for injectable biomedical applications on october th at am
Body: dear all we are pleased to invite you to the upcoming seminar by prof havazelet biancopeled from technion israel institute of technology israel the seminar is on friday th october from am we are looking forward to you taking the time to participate the details of the talk are as follows title new approaches toward materials for mucoadhesion and nanohydrogels for injectable biomedical applications date and time friday th october am venue room lhc speaker prof havazelet biancopeled department of chemical engineering technion israel institute of technology haifa israel abstract in my talk i will share with you highlights from the two main research areas in my lab bioadhesion and polymernanogel hydrogels the mucosa gel layer is a secretion lining organs which are exposed to the outer surface of the body yet are not covered with skin transmucosal drug delivery involves transport of therapeutic agents through this layer this method of delivery offers several potential benefits over oral drug administration including relatively rapid uptake of a drug into the systemic circulation and enhanced bioavailability mucoadhesion namely adhesion of the drug carrier to the mucosa enhances the performance of transmucosal delivery systems by providing extended residence time of the drug at the site of application in my talk i will describe new approaches in mucoadhesion based on modification of polymers as a way to enhance mucoadhesion specifically we developed a novel class of polymers carrying unsaturated end groups michael type addition reactions are used to covalently attach these polymers to the mucus our studies involved synthesizing these biomaterials and extensive characterization of their properties we explored various dosage forms including tablets liquids nanoparticles and paste we demonstrate a significant improve in adhesion and lack of toxicity in the second part of my talk i will describe a new class of hydrogels based on a pair of polysaccharides where one polysaccharide is soluble and the other is in the form of nanogels ngs upon contact specific interactions such as hydrogen bonding lead to adsorption of the soluble polysaccharide chains on the surface of the ngs resulting in the formation of a physical hydrogel without the need to employ additional crosslinkers we developed a simple technique for creating polysaccharide nanogels of controllable size and demonstrated their stability at various conditions we then show for several pairs that polysaccharideng hydrogels are thermosresponsive and exhibit shearthinning and selfhealing properties these properties arise from the ability of the nanogels to act as crosslinking agents between chains due to the dynamic interactions between the chains and the nanogels the formed network dissociates under applied shear allowing the hydrogel to flow moreover elimination of the applied shear results in exceptionally fast and comprehensive recovery of the storage modulus reverting the mixture into a solid form these novel hydrogels display network recovery suitable for injectable biomedical applications while benefiting from the advantages of nanogels as carriers bio prof havazelet biancopeled is an expert in biomedical polymers hydrogels and bioadhesion she has received several awards for her professional accomplishments she has written about research publications edited a book and has more than ten patent applications either granted or pending biancopeled is the founder and former cso of sealantis ltd a company that develops manufactures and commercialize novel biomimetic tissue adhesives based on a technology invented in her lab her current research interests include polysaccharidebased hydrogels d bioprinting mucoadhesion drug delivery physical characterization of biological biomedical and biomimetic nanosystems thanks harsha n s harsha gunda assistant professor department of materials science and engineering indian institute of technology delhi

Subject: iks inaugural ceremony october am institute seminar hall
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to the inaugural ceremony of the indian knowledge systems programme a sponsored research project at iit delhi date th oct valmiki jayanti time am venue seminar hall about indian knowledge systems iks is an emerging area around the application of indias civilizational wisdom for better life and systems domestically and globally it refers to the dynamic and inclusive corpus of knowledge practices and living systems continuing for millenia in india accordingly the national education policy emphasizes the iks theme in its articulation in this trajectory the iks project at iit delhi is a pioneering initiative the aspiration is to not just take inspiration from the past but focus on how the knowledge ideas and insights are relevant and beneficial for the present and the future it aims to establish platforms for thought development through research and strategic dialogue in the following sectors public systems technology education pedagogy health wellbeing the inaugural ceremony will expound on this vision with a panel of esteemed speakers representing the sectors above laying out the foundations and interacting with the audience it is an Subject: iit delhi alumni newsletter september
Body: highlights crown prince sheikh khaled bin mohamed visited the iit delhis abu dhabi campus ms aisha bowe former nasa scientist inspires girl students at iit delhis stem mentorship program iit delhi and honda join forces to pioneer cooperative intelligence for future mobility honble president of india honors iit delhi professors with prestigious national awards iit delhi students excel at national crossword expedition bangalore city meet gurugram city meet a grand success upcoming events paniit alumni meet in amsterdam your hostel your legacy crown prince sheikh khaled bin mohamed visited the iit delhis abu dhabi campus on september iit delhis abu dhabi campus celebrated the beginning of undergraduate education as his highness sheikh khaled bin mohamed bin zayed al nahyan crown prince of abu dhabi visited and inaugurated this visit marks a significant chapter in the global expansion of iit delhi positioning the abu dhabi campus as a key player in international engineering education ms aisha bowe former nasa scientist inspires girl students at iit delhis stem mentorship program on september ms aisha bowe a former nasa rocket scientist entrepreneur stem advocate and future astronaut engaged with girl students from various delhincr schools at iit delhi the event was organized by iit delhis office of academic outreach and new initiatives as part of the ongoing stem mentorship program for girls the session saw an overwhelming response with ms bowe sharing insights from her journey and encouraging young girls to pursue careers in stem fields the stem mentorship program launched by iit delhi in is now in its third edition empowering girls to explore and excel in stem through inspiring mentorship and support iit delhi and honda join forces to pioneer cooperative intelligence for future mobility honda cars india limited hcil has partnered with iit delhi to push the boundaries of cooperative intelligence ci an innovative ai technology aimed at improving humanmachine interaction this collaboration will focus on advancing automated driving systems and enhancing traffic safety through joint research and technology demonstrations under a recently signed memorandum of understanding mou iit delhi researchers will work closely with engineers from hcil and honda rd co ltd the goal is to develop aidriven solutions that enable smoother communication and collaboration between humans and machines ultimately paving the way for safer more efficient mobility systems honble president of india honors iit delhi professors with prestigious national awards in a moment of pride for the iit delhi community two distinguished faculty members were honored by the honble president of india smt droupadi murmu for their outstanding contributions to education and science prof nidhi jain from the department of chemistry was awarded the national award to teachers nat recognizing her excellence in teaching and dedication to shaping the next generation of scientists and innovators prof bhim singh was presented with the prestigious vigyan shri award in engineering sciences prof singh was honored for his pioneering research and contributions to the field of power electronics particularly in renewable energy and emobility the vigyan shri award celebrates scientists who have made exceptional contributions to science and technology iit delhi students excel at national crossword expedition students from the indian institute of technology iit delhi have bagged a hattrick at the national intercollege crossword expedition nice organized by aicte all india council of technical education in collaboration with iit madras defending champions iit delhi won this expedition three times in a row establishing their excellence bangalore city meet bangalore city meet was held on september st which was organized by the office of alumni relations at iit delhi and the iit delhi alumni association with over alumni and their spouses in attendance spanning from the class of to the class of it was one of the largest and most vibrant city meets for the iit delhi alumni community gurugram city meet on september th the iit delhi alumni community gathered for a memorable gurugram city meet organized by the office of alumni relations and iit delhi alumni association the event saw an incredible turnout and the evening was filled with vibrant discussions and shared memories attendees enjoyed reconnecting with fellow graduates strengthening ties and celebrating their collective achievements upcoming events paniit alumni optics and photonics centre opc invites all interested to a series of lectures by wellknown scientists in areas of optics and photonics delivered through the website of optics learning centre at details of lecture in this series are title complex frequency excitations in classical and quantum photonics speaker dr aleksandr krasnok affiliation florida international university usa mode inperson at opc committee room and online date st oct time pm ist weblink to join please visit optics learning centre website abstract complex frequency cf signals introduce a new paradigm in wave physics offering a powerful approach to uncovering hidden poles and resonances in both classical and quantum photonic systems these signals reveal phenomena invisible to conventional methods paving the way for breakthroughs in light scattering quantum circuits and optical communication in this talk i will explore the theoretical foundations of cf excitations and demonstrate their transformative impact on photonics and quantum circuits this presentation offers insights into the future of photonics through the lens of complex frequency effects about the speaker dr aleksandr alex krasnok is an assistant professor in the department of electrical and computer engineering at florida international university he earned his phd in photonics from itmo university and completed postdoctoral research at the university of texas at austin prior to joining fiu he served as a research assistant professor and the founding director of the photonics core facility at the advanced science research center asrc at cuny dr krasnoks work in quantum technology photonics and complex frequency excitations has earned him awards such as the earlycareer award in nanophotonics and the leopold b felsen award for excellence in electrodynamics he leads innovative research in quantum engineering at fiu supported by funding from the department of energy and the national science foundation regards prof p
