Subject: audit and withdrawal sem has started ends on
Body: dear students the process of auditwithdrawal for semester is open in the erp system and will remain open till pm on kindly note that audit and withdrawal is not possible for those courses especially for dms for which the final evaluation has been completed course coordinators approval is not required for course audit or withdrawal kindly complete the auditwithdrawal of courses within the timeline provisions related to auditing courses are applicable only as per the coursesofstudy for ug students audit is possible upto a limited number of credits for electives only pg students do not get credit for audited courses withdrawal is possible for any course however kindly note that withdrawing from core courses may cause serious complications in your course schedule and might entail a delay in graduation withdrawing from courses which are prerequisites to other core courses can significantly delay your graduation after pm on your audit and withdrawal status for any course cannot be changed once a course is withdrawn you will not get any grade other than w once audited only npnf grades will be possible the nf grade is not eligible for remajors further a course that has not been withdrawn or audited will necessarily be awarded a valid credit grade frequently asked questions i am a pg student can i audit a course ans no if it is a core course yes if it is elective however audited courses do not count towards graduation requirements i am a ug student can i audit a course ans no if it is a core course yes if it is elective ug students may audit upto a total of credits if you have earned credits ngus are not counted credits waived in lieu of an exchange semester are not counted i am a dual degree student can i audit a course ans see ans and for the ug part a qualified yes for the pg part no what is the pass criterion for an audit course ans this depends on the course policy please check the course policy before you decide on auditing the course also there is no remajor facility for audited courses if in doubt ask your teacher should i withdraw from xxxnnn course ans please check if this is a core course if it is core and you are in btech nd year or earlier avoid withdrawal try to clear the course this semester itself if the course is a prereq for other courses do not withdraw if this is otherwise your last semester withdrawal will delay your graduation by a semester i am already eligible to graduate can i audit beyond the credit limit ans yes please raise a studentgeneralrequest i have already earned hu credits can i audit my current extra hu course ans yes please raise a studentgeneralrequest i audited many courses during the covidaffected semesters are they counted in the credit limit ans no they are not counted courses audited during the five semesters between jan and may are not counted in the credit audit limit i have already credited sufficient de courses can i audit an extra one ans yes please raise a studentgeneralrequest i am in th year should i withdraw from my btp course ans btp is a core course you need to clear it now i am in ug st year can i withdraw from any course ans withdrawing from any course will make you ineligible for branchchange based on cgpa please note that all st year courses are mandatory and you will have to do them sooner or later postponing st year courses later will disrupt your schedule significantly st year courses have their own timetable that does not gel with other courses also courses like pyp cml and mcp will be very difficult to do later on the process for course auditwithdrawal in erp is given below in case of any difficulty with the process of auditingwithdrawing a course in the erp system write to best wishes shouri ccd to all faculty for information process for auditwithdraw request access the student portal from the link login with your institute user id and password go to the auditwithdraw page by clicking on the registration link on the left sidebar select the course you wish to audit or withdraw then click on the corresponding button on the page provide the reason for your request and click on the submit button in case you want to take back your request for course withdraw click undo withdraw this can be done only during the period when the auditwithdraw timeline is open in case you want to take back your request for course audit click undo audit this can be done only during the period when the auditwithdraw timeline is open

Subject: seminar by professor dr steffen marburg on monday th september at pm in a hybrid mode at iit delhi
Body: dear madamsir greetings seminar on concepts for frequency sweep and efficient repeated analysis in the context of vibroacoustic optimization and uncertainty quantification abstract this presentation aims at passive noise control for vibroacoustic problems which are analyzed by finite and boundary element techniques the author distinguishes interior and exterior problems mainly because of the quantities used as the objective function to assess the acoustic quality for interior problems it is common to use local quantities such as the sound pressure at a field point or in rare cases energy density at a field point the situation is different for exterior problems where the radiated sound power accounts for a suitable and global quantity to assess the emission from a vibrating structure for most engineering purposes the assessment requires frequency sweeps in which the problem needs to be solved at many discrete frequencies in vibroacoustic optimization and in samplingbased uncertainty quantification it is very common that structural parameters are varied while the acoustic field remains the same throughout the entire process in this talk we will review concepts and recent developments of efficient frequency sweeps and repeated analysis with unmodified fluid domain for many practical cases the situation for interior problems is rather simple to survey either authors have applied a modal analysis and use a modal superposition for frequency sweep and repeated analysis or the concept of unmodified acoustic transfer vectors is applied both concepts are quite successful as long as certain conditions are fulfilled for exterior problems a modal superposition is possible but so far only for a limited number of cases practically applicable as will be discussed herein the concept of using acoustic transfer vectors becomes inefficient since the evaluation of the radiated sound power as an integral over a closed enveloping surface would require an excessively high amount of storage capacity therefore other concepts are being followed for frequency sweeps a number of methods is using a frequency interpolation based on a few discrete sample frequencies often these techniques are used together with krylovsubspace model order reduction techniques in recent years a number of socalled low rank approximations have been developed and applied to frequency sweeps the field of efficient repeated analysis shows some interesting developments which can be easily applied to samplingbased uncertainty quantification but do not seem to be easily and generally applied for optimization speaker professor dr steffen marburg professor steffen marburg obtained his phd degree from the technische universität tu dresden in germany from until he held the chair for engineering dynamics at the universität der bundeswehr university of the federal armed forces in munich germany in july he took over the chair of vibroacoustics of vehicles and machines of the technical university of munich his research interests include simulation and simulation methods of vibroacoustics uncertainty quantification experimental identification of parameters and parameter distributionsdamage detection and other problems of vibroacoustics in recent years even databased approaches using machinedeep learning techniques and sound due to nonlinear vibration phenomena have accounted for interesting new fields of his research steffen marburg is one of the coeditorsinchief of the journal of theoretical and computational acoustics associate editor of the journal of the acoustical society of america mechanical systems and signal processing and acoustics australia he is author of approximately peerreviewed journal papers and book chapters furthermore he is editor of a book on finite and boundary element methods and has worked as a guest editor for nine special issues of the journal of theoretical and computational acoustics he has been a director of the international institute of acoustics and vibrations since professor marburg is a wellknown expert in computational acoustics date and time monday th september at pm indian standard time ist venue for inperson attendees committee room blockii department of mechanical engineering indian institute of technology iit delhi the zoom platform link for attending the seminar is please see the link below for announcement flyer of the seminar all interested are cordially invited to attend the seminar and please spread the word about the seminar among others who might be interested thank you with best regards vasant matsagar

Body: there was an error in the subject of the previous email heres the revised version dear all optics and photonics centre opc invites all interested to a series of lectures by wellknown scientists in areas of optics and photonics delivered through the website of optics learning centre at details of lecture in this series are title complex frequency excitations in classical and quantum photonics speaker dr aleksandr krasnok affiliation florida international university usa mode inperson at opc committee room and online date st oct time pm ist weblink to join please visit optics learning centre awards such as the earlycareer award in nanophotonics and the leopold b felsen award for excellence in electrodynamics he leads innovative research in quantum engineering at fiu supported by funding from the department of energy and the national science foundation regards prof p senthilkumaran hocopc

Subject: me guest talk by prof chunti chang department of mechanical engineering national taiwan university
Body: dear all profchunti chang from the department of mechanical engineering national taiwan university will visit iit delhi a mechanical engineering guest talk is scheduled as below date th september time pm venue lh title resonance of subhemispherical water balloons shape analysis and frequency prediction abstract water balloons and water drops are different objects yet the work by chang on the similarities between the resonance behaviors of water balloons and water drops phys fluids reveals the similarities between their resonance behaviors changs work focuses on the balloons with pinning angles beyond ° superhemispherical balloons and the results are based on a limited number of modes in this study the resonance of balloons with pinning angles below ° subhemispherical balloons is examined the setup is similar to that for changs work except each balloon is enlarged to possess a larger inertia and a correlationbased method is adopted to visualize the balloons oscillation with these improvements this study successfully discovers more than modes many of them have not been reported in the literature for these modes a catalogue is constructed to demonstrate their onetoone correspondence to the modes of drops additionally a scaling scheme is proposed to assimilate the resonance frequencies of subhemispherical balloons and drops with these this study provides a simple framework for predicting a subhemispherical water balloons resonance with a theory for the resonance of sessile drops on a flat plate all interested are welcome to join the talk regards dr abhishek das and dr bahni ray me seminar committee department of mechanical engineering iit delhi

Subject: cas seminar today pm on hybrid mode
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to the following inperson with a hybrid mode online link below cas centre for atmospheric sciences indian institute of technology delhi seminar today from pm to pm speaker prof denise mauzarell with drs yuanyu xie and mi zhou professor of environmental engineering and international affairs princeton university usa date and time september tuesday pm to pm venue cas seminar room vi iit delhi online ms teams link title current and future pm trends in india influence of emissions meteorology and climate change abstract in this talk we will describe our recent work analyzing cpcb pm data from across india for we found progress towards meeting national clean air program goals to reduce pm concentrations however we found of annual pm air quality improvements and approximately half during winter when pollution is high can be attributed to favorable meteorological conditions which are unlikely to persist as the climate warms we also developed a new india specific stagnation index that links stagnation with pm concentrations we apply this index to an ensemble of climate models and find that future stagnation changes stem from the compounded effects of co warming driven circulation changes and aerosol driven local meteorological responses specifically co warming will reduce annual stagnation occurrences across most of india while increasing winter stagnation across the igp in addition atmospheric aerosols will increase stagnation in all seasons across india given these projections stringent air quality regulations in the igp during winters will be particularly important to reduce surface pm concentrations as climate warms such regulations will not only directly improve air quality but will also reduce future stagnation occurrences thereby indirectly increasing the effectiveness of the regulations we will also discuss ongoing work to couple a regional air quality model wrfchem with a power system capacity expansion model to evaluate the air quality and health implications of individual power plant emissions the goal is to build a tool that will facilitate the analysis of the synergies and tradeoffs between air quality health carbon emissions and system costs under various decarbonization pathways for indias power sector finally time permitting we will describe earlier research we conducted for china analyzing the large impact of small residential coal stoves used for heating in the region around beijing and the air quality improvements that result from halting their use there may be insights from chinas experience of relevance to india bio prof denise mauzerall is professor of environmental engineering and international affairs at princeton university holding a joint appointment between the princeton school of public and international affairs and the department of civil and environmental engineering she conducts scientific research that informs the development of farsighted energy and environmental policy her research examines opportunities to simultaneously reduce air pollutant and greenhouse gas emissions and evaluates the resulting benefits for climate public health and food security current research is examining the potential air quality and climate benefits of increased penetration of alternative energy vehicles and a decarbonizing global power sector optimized strategies for battery storage deployment the climate effects of hydrogen leakage when used for energy storage methane leakage from the oil and gas sector air pollution trends and mitigation strategies in india and china overseas financing of the power sector and evaluation of the effects of changes in agricultural production and human diets for climate and public health mauzerall has published over papers on environmentalenergy topics in top research journals she served on the us environmental protection agencys chartered science advisory board from is on the executive advisory board for the institute of advanced sustainability studies in potsdam germany spoke at the world economic forum in davos switzerland on opportunities to simultaneously address air pollution and greenhouse gas mitigation and has been a contributing author to the intergovernmental panel on climate change she is a coeditor in chief of the new journal sustainable horizons she sits on the executive editorial boards of the atmospheric environment and advances in applied energy journals at princeton she is on the executive committees of the andlinger center for energy and environment and the chadha center for global india mauzerall is jointly appointed in the school of public and international affairs and the department of civil and environmental engineering she is associated faculty in the atmospheric and oceanic sciences program the geosciences department the high meadows environmental institute the princeton institute for international and regional studies and the center on contemporary china at princeton dr mauzerall received a scb in chemistry from brown university a ms in environmental engineering from stanford university and a phd in atmospheric chemistry from the earth and planetary science department at harvard university for many years mauzerall has directed the phd program in spia where she is a core professor in the center for policy research on energy and environment she has taught courses at the undergraduate masters and doctoral levels including the undergraduate course global environmental issues and graduate course climate change science policy and mitigation as well as a collection of undergraduate taskforces and graduate workshops on a variety of environmental and sustainability topics

Subject: the night before the big bang unraveling the mystery
Body: dear all ever wondered what happened before the big bang dr wolfgang a wellknown theoretical astrophysicist will be giving a talk titled the night before the big bang the talk will cover all the aspects from how we reached our current level of understanding of the world and what actually came before the big bang this will include all the scientific and the mathematic proof required and will be far from just abstract title the night before the big bang date th september venue lh time pm about the speaker prof dr wolfgang dusch is the chair of astrophysics at the university of kiel and was for four years up to midjuly this year also the chair of the academic senate of his university his main fields of research are the mass growth of supermassive black holes and the atmospheres of exoplanets abstract according to our current understanding in astrophysics the universe originated billion years ago in a hot big bang and expands ever since an immediate question is what was there before the big bang in the talk he will first give an overview of how we reached our current understanding of the origin and evolution of the universe he will then show that due to quantum mechanical effects the question of what came before the big bang is meaningless everyone is welcome to attend this fascinating seminar best regards divyanshu bansal overall coordinator physics and astronomy club indian institute of technology delhi

Subject: jane streets see iit apply now
Body: dear students jane street will host our inhouse see iit program this december the program is open to iit delhi bombay and madras students who will graduate in and with undergraduate degrees in science and electrical engineering students attending iit bombay iit delhi or iit madras who are graduating in or when dec to dec where jane streets hong kong office f chater house connaught rd Subject: cas seminar september tuesday pm on hybrid mode
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to the following inperson with a hybrid mode online link below cas centre for atmospheric sciences indian institute of technology delhi seminar on september tuesday from pm to pm speaker prof denise mauzarell with drs yuanyu xie and mi zhou professor of environmental engineering and international affairs princeton university usa date and time september tuesday pm to pm venue cas seminar room vi iit delhi online ms teams link title current and future pm trends in india influence of emissions meteorology and climate change abstract in this talk we will describe our recent work analyzing cpcb pm data from across india for we found progress towards meeting national clean air program goals to reduce pm concentrations however we found of annual pm air quality improvements and approximately half during winter when pollution is high can be attributed to favorable meteorological conditions which are unlikely to persist as the climate warms we also developed a new india specific stagnation index that links stagnation with pm concentrations we apply this index to an ensemble of climate models and find that future stagnation changes stem from the compounded effects of co warming driven circulation changes and aerosol driven local meteorological responses specifically co warming will reduce annual stagnation occurrences across most of india while increasing winter stagnation across the igp in addition atmospheric aerosols will increase stagnation in all seasons across india given these projections stringent air quality regulations in the igp during winters will be particularly important to reduce surface pm concentrations as climate warms such regulations will not only directly improve air quality but will also reduce future stagnation occurrences thereby indirectly increasing the effectiveness of the regulations we will also discuss ongoing work to couple a regional air quality model wrfchem with a power system capacity expansion model to evaluate the air quality and health implications of individual power plant emissions the goal is to build a tool that will facilitate the analysis of the synergies and tradeoffs between air quality health carbon emissions and system costs under various decarbonization pathways for indias power sector finally time permitting we will describe earlier research we conducted for china analyzing the large impact of small residential coal stoves used for heating in the region around beijing and the air quality improvements that result from halting their use there may be insights from chinas experience of relevance to india bio prof denise mauzerall is professor of environmental engineering and international affairs at princeton university holding a joint appointment between the princeton school of public and international affairs and the department of civil and environmental engineering she conducts scientific research that informs the development of farsighted energy and environmental policy her research examines opportunities to simultaneously reduce air pollutant and greenhouse gas emissions and evaluates the resulting benefits for climate public health and food security current research is examining the potential air quality and climate benefits of increased penetration of alternative energy vehicles and a decarbonizing global power sector optimized strategies for battery storage deployment the climate effects of hydrogen leakage when used for energy storage methane leakage from the oil and gas sector air pollution trends and mitigation strategies in india and china overseas financing of the power sector and evaluation of the effects of changes in agricultural production and human diets for climate and public health mauzerall has published over papers on environmentalenergy topics in top research journals she served on the us environmental protection agencys chartered science advisory board from is on the executive advisory board for the institute of advanced sustainability studies in potsdam germany spoke at the world economic forum in davos switzerland on opportunities to simultaneously address air pollution and greenhouse gas mitigation and has been a contributing author to the intergovernmental panel on climate change she is a coeditor in chief of the new journal sustainable horizons she sits on the executive editorial boards of the atmospheric environment and advances in applied energy journals at princeton she is on the executive committees of the andlinger center for energy and environment and the chadha center for global india mauzerall is jointly appointed in the school of public and international affairs and the department of civil and environmental engineering she is associated faculty in the atmospheric and oceanic sciences program the geosciences department the high meadows environmental institute the princeton institute for international and regional studies and the center on contemporary china at princeton dr mauzerall received a scb in chemistry from brown university a ms in environmental engineering from stanford university and a phd in atmospheric chemistry from the earth and planetary science department at harvard university for many years mauzerall has directed the phd program in spia where she is a core professor in the center for policy research on energy and environment she has taught courses at the undergraduate masters and doctoral levels including the undergraduate course global environmental issues and graduate course climate change science policy and mitigation as well as a collection of undergraduate taskforces and graduate workshops on a variety of environmental and sustainability topics dr somnath baidya roy professor head centre for atmospheric sciences the rockefeller foundation climate science and technology chair professorincharge iit delhi sonipat campus indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi for cas matters Subject: remindermathematics department seminar on sep
Body: a gentle reminder for the seminar tomorrow at pm in the math department committee room mz by prof sudeep bapat dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department seminar by prof sudeep bapat from shailesh j mehta school of management iit bombay on sep the details are given below title neural networks for time series prediction abstract time series prediction is a crucial task in many domains including finance healthcare weather forecasting and energy consumption traditional methods like autoregressive models have limitations when dealing with complex nonlinear patterns in data neural networks particularly deep learning models have emerged as powerful tools for capturing these intricate relationships in this talk we start by covering the basics of neural networks including its architecture methodologies extensions and applications we will explore different kinds of neural networks such as recurrent neural networks rnns long shortterm memory lstm networks etc we will then highlight a particular neural network time series model called as the neural network autoregressive model nnar with its application to time series prediction tasks the applicability of the nnar model will be showcased through a practical use case in r date september time pm venue mz committee room department of mathematics speaker prof sudeep bapat all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team

Subject: seminar by rajeev gupta on th september am dmse committee room
Body: dear all we invite you all to the inperson talk by prof rajeev gupta scheduled on th september at am in the dmse committee room title lightweight high strength and corrosion resistant metallic materials for sustainable future speaker prof rajeev gupta department of materials science and engineering north carolina state university raleigh nc usa email abstract the strength and corrosion resistance of engineering alloys is limited by the conventional compositions production and processing technologies to realize the full potential of the metallic materials and increase their properties beyond the existing limits a number of challenges related to controlling the microstructure and therefore properties must first be resolved ongoing work in the speakers research group has demonstrated possibilities of developing new alloys with extremely high properties by combining suitable alloying elements and processing conditions and harnessing unique characteristics of the alloys with farfromequilibrium structure these alloys could be created by nonequilibrium processing techniques such as ball milling examples of alloys produced by ball milling and additive manufacturing will be presented where superior properties have been introduced by controlling microstructure and compositions the focus of the presentation will be on microstructureprocessingpropertyperformance relationships with a discussion on corrosion initiation and propagation mechanisms at multiple length scales varying from atomic level to tens of microns short biography rajeev gupta is an associate professor of materials science and engineering at north carolina state university rajeev received his btech in materials and metallurgical engineering from iit kanpur and phd in materials engineering from monash university australia before joining the faculty at nc state university he served as an assistant professor at the university of akron ohio he is also an associate editor of the journal of the electrochemical society rajeevs primary research interests lie in the broad areas of corrosion and material engineering his research group focuses on understanding the structureprocessingpropertyperformance relationships corrosion initiation and propagation mechanisms alloy design hightemperature corrosion and electrochemical manufacturing the fundamental research is intended to be applied in developing new materials corrosion characterization techniques material processing technologies and life prediction models rajeev has authored over publications holds two patents and is the recipient of the nsf career award ecs midcareer excellence rusty award ampp educator award and brian cherry award

Subject: institute lecture by prof john gero september pm seminar hall
Body: dear students and colleagues we are delighted to invite you to an institute lecture by prof john gero please note the time of the lecture and be seated in the hall minutes before the start of the lecture the duration of the lecture will be around minutes followed by discussion for about mins the details of the lecture are datetimevenue th sep pm seminar hall title inside the minds and brains of designers the cognition and neurocognition of design abstract recent advances in cognitive science and neurocognition through noninvasive brain measurements coupled with a dramatic reduction in their cost has made it possible to look inside minds and brains this talk will present what happens in the minds and brains of designers as they design it draws from cognitive and neurocognitive studies of architects engineers and industrial designers while they design it presents answers we have learned to questions such as · do design tools change the mind and brain activities of the designer using them · are there differences in the mind and brain activities of architects and engineers · are there differences in the brain activities for different learning styles · can your brain response be used to improve your ideation · what does chatgpt do to your brain responses · do brain activities correlate with design theory about the speaker john gero is the research professor in computer science and architecture at the university of north carolina he is the former professor of design science and director of the key centre of design computing and cognition at the university of sydney he has been a visiting professor of design and computation architecture mechanical engineering civil engineering artificial intelligence cognitive psychology computer science and computational social science at mit columbia university ucberkeley ucla cmu insalyon university of strathclyde epfl university of provence and gmu he is the authoreditor of books and has published some research papers with over citations web johngerocom best regards subodh subodh sharma associate dean academics outreach new initiatives pankaj gupta chair professor of privacy and decentralisation associate Subject: signing off as the nss coordinator at iit delhi
Body: dear iitd family please bear with me for what might be my final email to the iitd community in my capacity as nss coordinator its a bit longer than usual but i trust youll take the time along with me to reflect on the journey of nss iit delhi over the last six years at the onset let me extend my heartfelt thanks to all the students staff and faculty for being such an incredible support throughout this journey im especially grateful to prof rajesh prof nema and prof mittalthe three deans i had the privilege of working withfor their unwavering backing a special word of thanks to prof bala and prof sreekrishnan for their constant encouragement and to prof rao and prof banerjee for their invaluable help in advancing the social cause im deeply appreciative of the dedicated faculty mentors who have been a strong pillar of support throughout most importantly my sincerest gratitude goes to all the student members of the nss family who have always believed in the cause and made this journey meaningful i am also thankful to chandan office of dean and manoj office of ddo for their unwavering support i am deeply indebted to prof sangeeta kohli who always believed that i should take up this responsibility some key changes where i had the privilege to serve as a facilitator can be broadly divided into three main sections id rather not talk about numbers instead id like to talk about how nss iit delhi has been trying to improve its functioning which has led to meaningful and positive impacts a working and execution of projects the lifeline of nss iit delhi constitution of nss upon assuming the position i felt the necessity of formulating a constitution for nss in consultation with former faculty in charges prof rajesh and prof ravi and active inputs from the nss student leadership we created the constitution which has functioned not as a constraining instrument but as a comprehensive guiding framework for the operations of this organisation project involvement we have actively engaged students in meaningful projects across diverse domains and discontinued inactive ones following indepth reviews the evaluation sessions frequently extended over several days ensuring the inclusion of only the most socially significant projects several projects including aarohan bachpan teaching for the visually impaired and underdeveloped areas around iit delhi have made significant impacts in the education sector additionally know your rights blood donation camps cleanup drives ewaste and clothing collection drives staff teaching initiatives and mental health awareness sessionsparticularly during the covid pandemicdeserve a special mention active collaboration and a thrust on ground hours we have successfully engaged more ngos and collaborated with various student bodies in delhi leading to fruitful csr partnerships in kaizen and involving alumni in our initiatives had tried to stress and increase the importance of ground hours and serious internships for those interestedits now a stronger component to complete the hours requirement project documentation we have established a robust mechanism to document and sustain the key takeaways from successful projects strong filtering before a new project initiation we receive numerous proposals from external agencies seeking collaboration with nss often with only an intention to gain access to iitds infrastructure to address this weve developed a questionnaire to assess their real intentions which has helped us effectively filter out many such unwarranted requests project monitoring and team building activities project leaders were asked to meet the faculty mentors reporting findings of the ongoing projects and getting suggestions for upcoming activities more frequent meetings were initiated with team building initiatives these initiatives suffered to a certain extent during and after covid again picking up creating a yearly project timeline over the past two years weve focused on planning and streamlining activities ensuring they are wellorganized and do not clash with other events of the institute using digital project management tools an inhouse developed nss app is assisting volunteer engagement by providing realtime access to volunteering opportunities tracking hours and offering skillbased projects the app also includes a vital feature that keeps blood group data updated ensuring urgent calls for blood transfusions are instantly directed to the right individuals enabling lifesaving responses b mentorship and leadership getting interested active faculty mentors on boardnow we have twelve active faculty members assisting us in different domains many faculty members have been actively involved in shaping nss activities and we will need increased engagement from more faculty in the coming years expanding the student leadership team new student leaders have been appointed forming a dedicated team of technical and outreach executives with logistics tailored to meet the evolving needs of nss iit delhi c a working space stronger outreach activities and recognitions i was particularly keen to create a physical space for nss in iit delhi the majority of the meetings and brainstorming used to happen in the textile committee room however with the help of the administration special thanks to pramit and aditya we have been given a space in sac which is under the final stages of renovation and getting equipped to hold meetingsinteractions we aspire to create a dedicated space for meaningful discussions on social outreach planning new projects and documenting successful social initiatives at iit delhi the website has been regularly updated with comprehensive details and after personally reviewing the websites of around twenty institutes including several iits i can confidently say that our website stands out as one of the most userfriendly and informative offering a wealth of valuable resources blogs and success Subject: mtl certain points to bring to your notice again
Body: dear all the following are some minor points that i had already reiterated in lectures but recaling them again in series suman if the limit an is zero then no conclusion can be drawn for the series if limit an is not zero then the series is divergent limit an is a necessary condition for the series to be convergent if the series an has some negative terms mixed positive negative terms and the limit of the an is not zero then limitan is not zero and hence given seriesan will not converge in limit comparison test in series if a limit anbn is l finite not zero then both series an and series bn have identical nature convergent together or divergent together but if l or l is infinity then the series does not have the same nature if l and series bn converge only say series an is convergent nothing on divergence if l infinity and series bn is divergent only claim that series an is divergent nothing on convergence the leibnitz test is only for the alternating series and one way means if conditions limit an and an an hold then alternative series n an or n an converges means alternate plus minus signs in terms of the series but if the series do not have alternative sign terms then this test will not help also if any of the two conditions of the test are not true then this test will not give anything you may think of the dirichlet test pay attention to the words sequence series and sequence of partial sums of the series some results like the sandwich theorem for computing limits or the bolzanoweirtrass theorem work in sequences hence they work for sequences of partial sums of the series but these are not for series you can apply comparison tests to determine the nature of the series but no result proves series convergence by the sandwich theorem be careful with inequalities in comparison tests if you are confused please do check in rough for some values of n say n to convince yourself that the inequality you are writing is correct be careful of powers and factorials in the question a small mistake can lead to the wrong direction and wrong conclusion if the formula of the nth term an in the series or sequence is not explicitly given rather only the first few terms of the series or sequence are mentioned then you might have to figure out the pattern to see what is an carefully check how you can find an for odd or even n values or grouping two to three terms to see if you can get some pattern you have to try and see the pattern the question may need different limiting for odd even or grouping and it may then involve possibly idea of limit supremum and limit infimum that is why it is important to identify and see the nthterm formula in seriessequence allow infinity and infinity in supremum and infimum of a set or of a codomain of a function infinity if unbounded from above and infinity if unbounded from below also by conceptual logic and convention if s is an empty set then sups −infinity and infs infinity allow plusminus infinities in limsup and liminf concepts in functions discontinuity could be established via sequences or leftright limits ideas but you must be very convincing and correct in arguments for continuity you can use epsilondelta or leftright limits value of the function at that point be careful while writing domains of functions open bounded interval closed bounded interval r and semiopen intervals also whenever you claim the existence of a point say in any result like imv property or root of fx or something similar please be careful in writing the interval where this point belongs endpoints are vital to keep in mind where to use open interval and where to use closed intervals if you are using the epsilondelta definition please note the delta depends on the epsilon and the point x but whatever delta you suggest by your workedout formula it must always be positive no matter whatever epsilon we have and whatever x be best wishes aparna

Subject: seminar by professor dr achintya haldar on friday th september at am in a hybrid mode at iit delhi
Body: dear madamsir greetings seminar on reliability analyses of nonlinear dynamic systems excited in time domain using redset an alternative to random vibration and simulation abstract critical engineering dynamic systems must be designed for the sixnine reliability estimated with of the confidence level in the context of satisfying the performance based design pbd requirements at least in the united states us this requirement is in addition to the currently used codified design guidelines the most sophisticated deterministic analysis also requires that the dynamic loadings must be applied in the time domain necessitating the development of an alternative to the classical random vibration concept to consider uncertainty in the design time histories multiple time histories need to be considered requiring an alternative to simulation reliability evaluation of dynamic systems excited in the time domain redset is a multidisciplinary risk evaluation concept in the metaverse era to fill the knowledge gap that currently exists using redset the underlying risk can be extracted with a few additional deterministic time domain analyses using any suitable computer program instead of one that changes the current engineering design paradigm several advanced mathematical concepts are integrated producing compounding beneficial effects to obtain the desired results different types and forms of dynamic loadings are used to validate the redset concept including seismic very irregular windinduced wave moderately irregular and thermomechanical loading geometric shapes in the form of heating and cooling of solder balls used in computer chips time domain representations and the uncertainty quantification procedures including the use of multiple time histories are proposed for all these dynamic loadings both onshore and offshore structures are used for validation for wider multidisciplinary applications structures are represented by finite elements to capture different types of nonlinearities more appropriately the potential of redset is demonstrated for implementing pbd for the seismic loading now under development in the us redset which is an exciting development significantly improving the current stateoftheart and altering the widely used engineering design practices for critical structuressystems the work was supported by the national science foundation nsf under a prestigious research grant from the computational dataenable science and engineering cdse program cmmi the redset concept is discussed in more detail in the following book haldar a azizsoltani h gaxiolacamacho jr vazirizade sm huh j reliability evaluation of dynamic systems excited in time domain – redset alternative to random vibration and simulation john wiley sons new york usa speaker situations and circumstances are not in your favour but that never means that one must circumvent their ethics and morals as a way out you may be a good person your entire life but one mistake about remembering everything in a moment of panic i wrote some formulas on the palm of my hand i realized my mistake afterwards regardless of how much you know or want to achieve your results should Subject: mathematics department seminar on sep
Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department seminar by prof sudeep bapat from shailesh j mehta school of management iit bombay on sep the details are given below title neural networks for time series prediction abstract time series prediction is a crucial task in many domains including finance healthcare weather forecasting and energy consumption traditional methods like autoregressive models have limitations when dealing with complex nonlinear patterns in data neural networks particularly deep learning models have emerged as powerful tools for capturing these intricate relationships in this talk we start by covering the basics of neural networks including its architecture methodologies extensions and applications we will explore different kinds of neural networks such as recurrent neural networks rnns long shortterm memory lstm networks etc we will then highlight a particular neural network time series model called as the neural network autoregressive model nnar with its application to time series prediction tasks the applicability of the nnar model will be showcased through a practical use case in r date september time pm venue mz committee room department of mathematics speaker prof sudeep bapat all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team

Subject: re scai visitor talk on dense subgraph discovery using triadic decompositions
Body: starting in minutes original message subject re scai visitor talk on dense subgraph discovery using triadic decompositions date from sumeet agarwal to reminder for tomorrows talk and to sign up for meeting the speaker if interested original message subject scai visitor talk on dense subgraph discovery using triadic decompositions date from sumeet agarwal to dear all the yardi school of ai is hosting the following visitor talk by sabyasachi basu from the university of california santa cruz all are welcome to join and also to sign up for oneonone meetings with sabyasachi next monday at title dense subgraph discovery using triadic decompositions date and time monday th september pm venue sit abstract we look at a problem of decomposing a graph into several disjoint subgraphs with strict guarantees of internal density this relates to the rich community structure observed in realworld networks particularly social networks we present a spectral condition for the existence of a decomposition of a graph into such pieces the results require a structural assumption on the graph related to triadic closuretransitivity commonly observed in such networks we present an algorithm that produces such a decomposition and a counterpart that is able to recover such good subgraphs from networks we show that it is possible to cover large parts of socialnetworklike graphs with dense subgraphs of this sort in the course of this talk we will look at the algorithm and its relevance in real world networks to find communities moreover we will discuss the possibilities of using such decompositions in downstream tasks that benefit from internal density based on recent work spectral triadic decompositions of real world networks sabyasachi basu suman kalyan bera c seshadhri siam journal on mathematics of data science covering a graph with dense subgraphs via trianglerich sets sabyasachi basu daniel paulpena kun qian c seshadhri edward w huang karthik subbian to appear cikm bio sabyasachi basu is a phd student at uc santa cruz advised by c seshadhri he works on different problems on graphs graph decompositions sublinear algorithms and graph embeddings his primary interest is in designing efficient algorithms with good theoretical foundations that work well in practice he is also interested in combining perspectives from computer science physics and applied math in the study of complex networks thanks sumeet on behalf of scai seminar committee

Subject: re scai visitor talk on dense subgraph discovery using triadic decompositions
Body: reminder for tomorrows talk and to sign up for meeting the speaker if interested original message subject scai visitor talk on dense subgraph discovery using triadic decompositions date from sumeet agarwal to dear all the yardi school of ai is hosting the following visitor talk by sabyasachi basu from the university of california santa cruz all are welcome to join and also to sign up for oneonone meetings with sabyasachi next monday at title dense subgraph discovery using triadic decompositions date and time monday th september pm venue sit abstract we look at a problem of decomposing a graph into several disjoint subgraphs with strict guarantees of internal density this relates to the rich community structure observed in realworld networks particularly social networks we present a spectral condition for the existence of a decomposition of a graph into such pieces the results require a structural assumption on the graph related to triadic closuretransitivity commonly observed in such networks we present an algorithm that produces such a decomposition and a counterpart that is able to recover such good subgraphs from networks we show that it is possible to cover large parts of socialnetworklike graphs with dense subgraphs of this sort in the course of this talk we will look at the algorithm and its relevance in real world networks to find communities moreover we will discuss the possibilities of using such decompositions in downstream tasks that benefit from internal density based on recent work spectral triadic decompositions of real world networks sabyasachi basu suman kalyan bera c seshadhri siam journal on mathematics of data science covering a graph with dense subgraphs via trianglerich sets sabyasachi basu daniel paulpena kun qian c seshadhri edward w huang karthik subbian to appear cikm bio sabyasachi basu is a phd student at uc santa cruz advised by c seshadhri he works on different problems on graphs graph decompositions sublinear algorithms and graph embeddings his primary interest is in designing efficient algorithms with good theoretical foundations that work well in practice he is also interested in combining perspectives from computer science physics and applied math in the study of complex networks thanks sumeet on behalf of scai seminar committee

Subject: scai visitor talk on dense subgraph discovery using triadic decompositions
Body: dear all the yardi school of ai is hosting the following visitor talk by sabyasachi basu from the university of california santa cruz all are welcome to join and also to sign up for oneonone meetings with sabyasachi next monday at title dense subgraph discovery using triadic decompositions date and time monday th september pm venue sit abstract we look at a problem of decomposing a graph into several disjoint subgraphs with strict guarantees of internal density this relates to the rich community structure observed in realworld networks particularly social networks we present a spectral condition for the existence of a decomposition of a graph into such pieces the results require a structural assumption on the graph related to triadic closuretransitivity commonly observed in such networks we present an algorithm that produces such a decomposition and a counterpart that is able to recover such good subgraphs from networks we show that it is possible to cover large parts of socialnetworklike graphs with dense subgraphs of this sort in the course of this talk we will look at the algorithm and its relevance in real world networks to find communities moreover we will discuss the possibilities of using such decompositions in downstream tasks that benefit from internal density based on recent work spectral triadic decompositions of real world networks sabyasachi basu suman kalyan bera c seshadhri siam journal on mathematics of data science covering a graph with dense subgraphs via trianglerich sets sabyasachi basu daniel paulpena kun qian c seshadhri edward w huang karthik subbian to appear cikm bio sabyasachi basu is a phd student at uc santa cruz advised by c seshadhri he works on different problems on graphs graph decompositions sublinear algorithms and graph embeddings his primary interest is in designing efficient algorithms with good theoretical foundations that work well in practice he is also interested in combining perspectives from computer science physics and applied math in the study of complex networks thanks sumeet on behalf of scai seminar committee

Subject: welfare activities to be conducted by counselling services for the month of september
Body: dear students counselling services will be conducting various welfare activities for the months of september and october for which the details are provided below the welfare activities are divided into hostel outreach sessions and group therapy sessions hostel outreach sessions outreach sessions help us to reach out to the entire hostel community it promotes mental health across campus through programmes that educates raises awareness and reduces stigma with a particular focus on improving and maintaining student wellbeing in the month of september hostel outreach sessions would be majorly designed to provide an orientation to the first year students of ug and pg these hostel orientations will aim at providing sensitizing students with an overview of the mental health services available at iit delhi various ways to reach out for psychological support a general awareness about mental health and addressing the taboo associated with it you can find the dates of the sessions in the various hostels attached to this email group therapy sessions we are excited to announce the launch of our new group therapy sessions designed to provide support and foster personal growth in a supportive environment whether you are looking to manage stress improve your mental wellbeing or connect with others who share similar experiences these sessions offer a valuable opportunity for you what is group therapy group therapy is a form of psychotherapy where a small group of people meets regularly in presence of a therapist to discuss and work through their concerns together the sessions usually involve sharing personal experiences offering support to each other and learning new coping skills group therapy provides you with a safe space where you come together with others to share your experiences have a better understanding of your own situations and to learn fromwith each other how would group therapy be beneficial being a part of a group allows members to connect with others and have a sense of shared experiences group therapy provides a sense of support validation and belongingness it might also reduce the feelings of loneliness it offers you with different perspectives and viewpoints provides you with a space to practice and improve certain social skills if you have been thinking of going for therapy but feel hesitant about the same then group therapy might provide you with a space to experience therapy at a milder level who will be conducting these sessions these group sessions will be facilitated by the iitd student counselors details of the group therapy sessions for the month of september group i drawing a line how to set boundaries like a pro facilitator ms anjana sunil the group therapy sessions will aim at developing practical skills to help you communicate more effectively respect your own needs and maintain healthy relationships the sessions would be tailor made to include topics such as understanding and exploring boundaries differentiating between assertiveness passivity and aggression common obstacles and fears related to boundary setting and assertiveness and gaining handson experience in setting and maintaining boundaries while remaining respectful and clear tentative dates september september october october group ii the anxiety avengers strategies support and sharing facilitator ms anannya sharma these will be supportive and engaging group therapy sessions dedicated to understanding and managing anxiety in this safe and confidential space well explore practical strategies share personal experiences and build resilience together whether youre dealing with anxiety resulting from academic pressure social challenges or everyday stressors this session is designed to offer insights and coping tools tailored to your life come and connect with peers who understand what youre going through and take steps toward feeling more grounded and empowered tentative dates september september september october group iii riding the emotional rollercoaster healthy ways to manage emotional distress facilitator ms nishtha sharma the group sessions will include awareness understanding and managing of emotions and flexible use of emotion regulation strategies the sessions would also include the inculcating skills of changing emotional responses reducing vulnerability of emotions and managing emotions tentative dates september september september october how to register to secure your spot fill out the registration form by th september you can access the form here spaces are limited so we encourage you to register as soon as possible please note joining more than one group is not recommended what to expect confidentiality all sessions are conducted with the utmost respect for your privacy supportive environment share your experiences and gain insights in a nonjudgmental space interactive activities engage in exercises and discussions that promote personal development if you have any questions or need more information please feel free to reach out to counselling services at we look forward to welcoming you to these sessions and supporting you on your journey regards Body: dear all this is a gentle reminder for the colloquium today we are pleased to resume the colloquium series that highlights the research achievements of the members of the department in this edition prof sunil kumar will talk about his work that was published recently in nature communications the details are as follows title an ultrafast view of the lightmatter interaction at an interface in condensed matter speaker prof sunil kumar femtosecond spectroscopy and nonlinear photonics group department of physics indian institute of technology delhi india email when and where wednesday september hrs ms abstract femtosecond laser pulses can be used to induce and simultaneously study nonequilibrium dynamics of different types of coherent excitations in solids the coherent dynamics of the excitations of charge entities can construct real physical currents that they mimic sources of a new electromagnetic radiation whose frequency is determined by the time scale involved in the coherent dynamics of the excitations these are system specific and one can imagine all sorts of possibilities here i would like to motivate a discussion on this in my talk by giving an example of the charge and spin currents induced by femtosecond light excitation in metallic thin film heterostructures and at the interfaces therein the dynamic photoinduced currents are such that they generate thz radiation thus the study of the generated thz radiation allows us to learn about the nature of the coherent excitations in them which further can help to design the systems for enhanced properties please see the link below for details about work regards abhishek ps all students are highly encouraged to attend

Subject: thanks and jaagte raho
Body: dear students and colleagues faculty staff this will hopefully not take more than secs of your life to read however you may also choose to ignore the contents below since there are no grades or permissions or poltu or forward movement of any fileapplication or any other benefits at stake based on the below as you may be aware i completed my tenure as the dean student affairs of our revered institution on aug it was a privilege and at the same time an unparalleled personal challenge to serve as a part of a team working towards a forwardmoving postpandemic reset in our campus in my personal opinion i complete my term with the satisfaction of having contributed to creating a more humane and caring environment on campus one that empowers students without diluting the role of individual responsibilities each of us have towards our institute operationally maintaining uncompromisable integrity of the iitd system while ensuring full accountability of its parts in the student affairs section with completely transparent mechanisms was and remains a priority it is also imperative for me to state that i am very grateful for surviving my full term in spite of some serious challenges we faced as a community this was possible only because of your support and our collective efforts with every loss we faced in campus i lost a part of myself though that which has been lost shall not come back i have no choice but to be hopeful that mechanistic redundancies and tenacity noted in evolution of living systems will allow reestablishment of my personal life and your lives on campus despite the losses with every joy we faced in campus i gained new strength hope towards ensuring the quality of humanity dignity and integrity we imbibe especially as the leading academic institution of our country i am very grateful to prof arvind nema and prof t r sreekrishnan along with the director who had faith in me towards taking up this really challenging task of postpandemic reset of student life in campus of course they have also tolerated several of my jibes for this emotional atyaachaar im eternally thankful for that also at the same time it needs to be stated that whatever was there in my tank to give has been given with utmost sincerity i leave the office of student affairs with the hope that it is the most studentfriendly space in the campus of course a lot more needs to be done and im hopeful to have played some role in chalking out a path for the same i cannot express enough thanks to the student community the director and the staff of office of dean student affairs for tolerating my eccentricities personal operational and functional without doubting the commitment towards betterment of the campus from lifting the downed spirits while grappling with tragedies to sharing the joy and smiles from little steps that might serve as giant leaps in future mr chandan ms sapna singh mr ghanshyam mr devender mr subhash and of course prof rangan banerjee formed an unparalleled support system for me a special thanks to prof panigrahi who was a pillar of support along with profs pramit chowdhury tanushree chakraborty sreedevi upadhyayula and vivekanandan perumal i must also thank the counselling unit especially shachi maam and aakriti maam who laid the foundations of x availability for students and each other in the same vein our security officer mr sandeep sharma always stood by our side as a solid rock while providing soft cushion for us to fall on and we did fall quite a few times i seek forgiveness from those students for whom i could not serve up to their expectations i also seek forgiveness from the members of deans committee and the ecs who generously tolerated my shortcomings and came out in full support whenever i needed it in the last two years it is imperative for me to publicly thank my mother wife and son for allowing me to ignore my personal life completely for the last two years i sincerely hope they will welcome me back into their lives now the same applies to my colleagues in the kusuma school of biological sciences my family in the academic area of the campus finally the last couple of years in the dean student affairs office is summed up well by the following two songs kissi ki muskuraahaton pe ho nisaar kissi ka dard mil sake tau le udhaar kissi ke vaaste ho tere dil mein pyaar jeena issi ka naam hai written by shailendra sung by mukesh my way written by paul anka sung by frank sinatra for what is a man what has he got if not himself then he has naught to say the things he truly feels and not the words of one who kneels the record shows i took the blows and did it my way yes it was my way jaagte raho if you still have stamina left after having gone through the above and for context please see the below shared with all of you on september th addy over and out as dean and back to academia as a teacher and researcher regards aditya aditya mittal b tech ph d former dean student affairs and professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india tel dos email web sent on september at hrs subject jaagte raho dear students faculty and staff for information only this is a superlong email but i earnestly request you to kindly read through it fully many of us have had rather humble beginnings and upbringing while our humble settings may not have allowed us to be able to afford major luxuries in our childhood we did enjoy one unparalleled possession community support as an example in villages and small towns there would be a community responsibility for ensuring safety especially at night this safety was from wild animals thievesrobbersbandits and even entities that some of us classified as superstitions these entities included fear of the dark unknown and negative thoughts to ensure safety while allowing for comfortable sleeping of the whole community every family would take the responsibility of having one person assigned for onenight duty with a big stick a torchlantern this person would hit the stick on the roadstreets and walk through the whole villagetown throughout the night shouting jaagte raho the aim was to allow everyone to sleep but with a sound of safety from outside that confirmed that nothing is going to happen on my watch im there if the fearelement was large enough this duty would be done by couple of families together per night a rotation mechanism for all families would be created thus ensuring safety of each and every household in the community throughout the year in modern times the above is replaced by outsourced hiring of watchmenguards etc who are paid by pooling of resources another example of community responsibilities comes from experiences of hostel life from many of us residents of wings in hostels were not necessarily friends all the time however staying together in hostels and especially in same wings every day did build an unspoken bond even if we did not interact much these unspoken bonds were builtin via intimate details about each other how much time would a particular person spend in the restroomtoilet how much time would a particular person spend in the bathroomshower this helped us in planning when to use the common facilities without getting late for meals and classes while this may sound funny but such intimate details also allowed us to involuntarily gauge the health of each other in addition to the above and in absence of washing machines we even had indicators on when someone in our wings was feeling unwell or extralazy to wash clothes we would keep them soaked in buckets with soap water eg in the morning when water supply was good then we would come back from classes and wash them in the evening by hand again when water supply was good sometimes if the buckets with soaked clothes remained unattended for more than a day they would start stinking that stink alerted us to ask our wingmate on what was happening the obvious avoidance of washing clothes and taking showers a hallmark of busy and yet lazy hostel life would also act as an indicator if someone suddenly changed their habits for regular cleaning cycles we knew that there was something interesting happening in the life of our wingmate on the other hand abstaining from cleaning cycles beyond the regular stinks also alerted us that something negative may be happening no forced conversations were required for any of the above observations however there was a sense of community even today after years when my hostel mates and especially wingmates end up meeting me by chance the informality of unspoken words during our hostel tenures allows us to embracegreet each other as if time has not passed at all this has happened with me literally with some of you whose parents were my hostel mates or wingmates in one or more years of my hostel life there is now an urgent need for us to revive such community factors in their avatars that can be applicable to todays generation i cannot and will not enforce any ideas on you however led by your general secretaries class reps house secys i request you to discuss and evolve ideas that can be executed at a system level ideas that do not depend solely on individual qualities or efforts but are integrated automatically into the system one set of such ideas could be as follows this needs to be discussed within the student community to develop executable avatars for every course regardless of class size each student identify at least one student and exchange mobile numbers if any student is missing in consecutive classes of that course try to repeatedly eg times in hrs call them to ask if everything is ok if they still cant be contacted immediately alert the class representative and course coordinator for courses with lab components this can be easy lab partners can do this job for hostel residents a model similar to the above can be implemented within each wing or independent of wings within each floor or independent of floor within each hostel if any student is missing consecutive meals just call repeatedly until you can get in touch if you cant get in touch inform the house secy caretaker and warden while implementing any of the above ideas we need to be mindful of individual sensitivities also along with appreciating privacy issues and we must remember that we do not have to friends to execute responsibilities we just need to be jagrook aware and sensitive the biggest strength of our system is the collective thought processes of our students ie you thus instead of imposing policies im convinced that you ie our student community is responsible enough to debate evolve and execute common practices that can allow building of virtual human chains in both classrooms and beyond classrooms eg hostels outsideaccommodations etc but please also be aware that no matter how strong a metalalloy one uses to build a chain any chain is as strong as its weakest link finally instead of responding to this email i request and encourage you to have discussions with some of your student leaders g secy sac g secy caic g secy bhm g secy bsw g secy bsp from your discussions with above some models may evolve that we can agree towards for rapid implementation jaagte raho best wishes aditya ps if anyone is offended by any of the above contents please accept my apologies in advance the intention is not to offend anyone even slightly and the possible errors may simply be a result of me being a mere mortal with limited knowledgecommunicationskills aditya mittal b tech ph d dean student affairs and professor kusuma school of biological sciences indian institute of technology delhi hauz khas new delhi india tel dos Subject: spp academic seminar pm
Body: dear students and colleagues the next academic seminar on will be on the topic of climate science to inform adaptation and policy and will be delivered by krishna achuta rao of cas iitd please find details below and hope many of you will attend best wishes suma suma athreye school of public policy iit delhi title climate science to inform adaptation and policy venuelh time and date pm september speaker prof krishna achyuta rao centre for atmospheric sciences iitd abstract climate science has been focused on understanding the behavior of the climate system climate models have been a very useful tool in non only understanding how the climate system works but also to project how it can change in the future models and observations together can also tell us how natural variations occur through attribution techniques we can now quantify the natural and human contributions to changes in the longterm climate as well as specific extreme weather events much work exists on the projections of future climate and the resulting impacts on various sectors such as agriculture health water etc most of this has in the past focused on longterm multiple decades to a century changes and their impacts that depend on future emissions that are highly uncertain lately models are being used to predict the climate and its variations on actionable timescales forecasts a season ahead or for the next decade can be very useful in making various decisions however our capabilities in this are still primitive and much work needs to be done my work in climate science has been in these areas through examples of my past and ongoing research i will touch upon the possibilities for using science to inform adaptation and policy studies in general brief bio of speaker krishna achutarao joined the centre for atmospheric sciences in and worked extensively on the modelling of regional climate change weather and climate extremes climate change detection and attribution climate modeling climate variability climate model validation and diagnosis ocean heat content sealevel rise uv cdat currently he serves as the dean faculty please read more about his publications and projects by visiting the link below

Subject: physics department colloquium september wednesday hrs ms
Body: dear all we are pleased to resume the colloquium series that highlights the research achievements of the members of the department in this edition prof sunil kumar will talk about his work that was published recently in nature communications the details are as follows title an ultrafast view of the lightmatter interaction at an interface in condensed matter speaker prof sunil kumar femtosecond spectroscopy and nonlinear photonics group department of physics indian institute of technology delhi india email when and where wednesday september hrs ms abstract femtosecond laser pulses can be used to induce and simultaneously study nonequilibrium dynamics of different types of coherent excitations in solids the coherent dynamics of the excitations of charge entities can construct real physical currents that they mimic sources of a new electromagnetic radiation whose frequency is determined by the time scale involved in the coherent dynamics of the excitations these are system specific and one can imagine all sorts of possibilities here i would like to motivate a discussion on this in my talk by giving an example of the charge and spin currents induced by femtosecond light excitation in metallic thin film heterostructures and at the interfaces therein the dynamic photoinduced currents are such that they generate thz radiation thus the study of the generated thz radiation allows us to learn about the nature of the coherent excitations in them which further can help to design the systems for enhanced properties please see the link below for details about work regards abhishek ps all students are highly encouraged to attend

Subject: seminar by dr menghrajani on th august pm in dmse committee room
Body: dear all we invite you all to the inperson talk by dr kishan s menghrajani scheduled on th august at pm in the dmse committee room title controlling molecular systems with polaritonic metasurfaces speaker dr kishan s menghrajani school of physics and astronomy monash university wellington road clayton victoria australia abstract molecular strong coupling presents exciting opportunities in physics chemistry and materials science while significant attention has been given to modeling the molecular systems involved the crucial role of the photonic mode structure of optical cavities has been relatively underexplored our research demonstrates that the effectiveness of molecular strong coupling is critically dependent on the cavitys finessespecifically emission associated with a dispersive lower polariton is observed only in cavities with sufficiently high finesse by developing an analytical model of cavity photoluminescence in a multimode structure we elucidate the impact of finite finesse on polariton formation showing that a lower finesse diminishes the mixing of light and matter in polariton states we propose that understanding the detailed characteristics of the photonic modes supported by a cavity is as important for developing a coherent framework for molecular strong coupling as incorporating realistic molecular models keywords strongcoupling photoluminescence optical microcavity polaritons brief biography dr kishan menghrajani earned his phd in physics from the epsrc’s center for doctoral training in metamaterials at the university of exeter uk his doctoral research focused on the strong coupling between the vibrational modes of molecules and infrared surface plasmons within the broader field of lightmatter interactions prior to his phd he worked as a project associate at the indian institute of science iisc where he studied the optical properties of chiral plasmonics and metamaterial nanostructures his masters thesis conducted at the indian institute of technology madras iit madras involved an experimental study of localized surface plasmon resonances recently dr menghrajani joined monash university as a research fellow working with professor stefan maier on single particle dark field microscopy his expertise includes energymomentum spectroscopy nanofabrication techniques single particle dark field microscopy ftir raman spectroscopy and numerical electrodynamic modeling dr menghrajani is a selfmotivated researcher with demonstrated proficiency in interdisciplinary research areas thanks dmse seminar organizing committee
