scientists in areas of optics and photonics delivered through the website of optics learning centre at details of lecture in this series is given below title electronicphotonic mmwave systemonchips and passive devices in silicon cmos photonics speaker dr manuj singh boston university mode online date st of august time am ist weblink to join please visit optics learning centre website abstract silicon photonics has rapidly transitioned from academic research to a critical optical integrated circuit technology with major semiconductor companies like global foundries tsmc intel and ibm leading its commercialization as a morethanmoore extension to advanced cmos silicon photonics is particularly poised to address challenges in large mmwave mimo antenna arrays for g g communications and radar sensing we discuss a scalable electronicphotonic solution that integrates a lownoise amplifier lna with photonic coupledcavity modulators in a monolithic cmos process additionally we discuss overcoming polarization fluctuation challenges in soi platforms through a compact rapidadiabatic polarization splitterrotator rapsr design and designing energyefficient wdm communication links using coupled cavity resonators based on tridiagonal kac matrices biography manuj singh recently completed his phd in electrical engineering at boston university advised by prof milos a popovic his research interests lie in the field of integrated photonics and its applications for mmwave photonics and data communications his work focuses on developing rf photonic links based on ultrasensitive electrooptical modulatorssystems which connect baseband stations and mimo antenna arrays these rftooptical links serve as a low size weight power and cost swapc alternative to traditional metal wire Subject: पतंगबाजी में चाइनीज मांझे का प्रयोग न करें not to use chinese string manzha in kite flying
Body: प्रिय साथियो हाल ही में दिल्ली पुलिस ने शहर भर में कई अभियानों में चीनी मांझा की से अधिक रीलें जब्त कीं और तीन लोगों को गिरफ्तार भी किया गया। दिल्ली पुलिस ने तीन लोगों को गिरफ्तार किया और उनके कब्जे से चीनी मांझा या ग्लासलेपित सिंथेटिक पतंग स्ट्रिंग की कुल रील जब्त की गईं। में दिल्ली में चीनी मांझा पर प्रतिबंध लगा दिया गया था और नेशनल ग्रीन ट्रिब्यूनल ने पतंग उड़ाने के लिए इस्तेमाल किए जाने वाले नायलॉन या सिंथेटिक धागे पर भी इसी तरह का प्रतिबंध लगाया है। ये प्रतिबंध मनुष्यों पक्षियों अन्य जानवरों और पर्यावरण को होने वाले नुकसान को रोकने के लिए लगाए गए है। सभी से अनुरोध है कि पतंग उड़ाते समय चाइनीज मांझे का प्रयोग न करें। आपके संदर्भ के लिए एक समाचार का लिंक नीचे दिया गया है पर्यावरण विभाग भारत सरकार की अधिसूचना का लिंक। कृपया आपकी जानकारी के लिए राष्ट्रीय राजधानी क्षेत्र दिल्ली का विवरण भी नीचे दिया गया है। सभी से अनुरोध है कि पतंग उड़ाते समय सावधानी बरतें। पतंग उड़ाने के लिए सभी सड़कों से बचना चाहिए। सड़कों के पास पतंग उड़ाने से दोपहिया और साइकिल चालकों के साथ दुर्घटनाएं हो सकती हैं। बिजली की लाइन के पास भी पतंग नहीं उड़ानी चाहिए क्योंकि इससे मांझे में करंट आने का खतरा रहता है। सभी से सहयोग का अनुरोध है। यह सक्षम प्राधिकारी की अनुमति से जारी किया जाता है। सम्मान सुरक्षा अधिकारी dear all recently over reels of chinese string manjha were seized by the delhi police from multiple operations across the city and three people were also arrested delhi police arrested three people and total reels of chinese manjha or glasscoated synthetic kite string were seized from their possession the chinese manjha was banned in delhi in and the national green tribunal also imposed a similar ban on nylon or synthetic threads used for kite flying these bans were put in place to prevent harm to humans birds other animals and the environment all are requested not to use chinese string manjha while flying kites link of a news item is given below for your reference link of the notification of department of environment govt of nct of delhi is also given below for your information please all are further requested to be careful while flying kites all roads should be avoided for flying kites flying kites near the roads can lead to the accidents involving two wheeler and bicycles kite flying should not also be done near the electricity line as it may lead to electrocution through strings all are requested to cooperate this is issued with the permission of the competent authority regards security officer

Subject: nd cobotalks on future of modern robotics at addverb merging planning perception and control into one
Body: dear all you’ve been invited to nd cobotalks on future of modern robotics at addverb merging planning perception and control into one we will delve into a thoughtprovoking question are perceptioncontrol and planning fundamentally one and the same in the context of robotics and autonomous systems these three elements—perception control and planning—are often discussed as separate facets of robotic functionality but their integration is crucial for creating truly intelligent systems in this talk we will examine the interconnectedness of these components perception involves gathering and interpreting data from the environment control refers to executing actions based on that data and planning is about strategizing future actions but how distinct are these processes in practice we’ll explore how advancements in sensor technology and data processing are blurring the lines between perception and planning well also discuss how modern control algorithms increasingly rely on realtime sensory input and predictive modeling to enhance decisionmaking and adaptive behavior through realworld examples and case studies involving cobots legged robots human allied robots that we are building at addverb we’ll highlight how these elements are intertwined shaping the functionality of autonomous systems we’ll also consider the implications for system design and the challenges that arise when trying to unify these processes join us as we explore whether perception control and planning are truly separate entities or if they are in fact parts of a cohesive whole driving the future of intelligent and autonomous systems about the speaker rajesh kumar is a leading the r d facets in modern robotics at addverb technologies addverbcom which is a robotics manufacturing and embodied ai company he has been working on writing software and intelligence modules for legged robots collaborative arms exoskeletons and haptic devices earlier he has also worked on dedicated vision systems teleoperation modules grasping and inhand manipulation modules mobile robots slam architectures and other robots like cable driven robots etc he has published around papers in journals and conferences and has filed more than patents he holds a btech from indian institute of technology delhi and a phd from indian institute of technology delhi wed aug pm pm utc chennai kolkata mumbai new delhi we look forward to having you attend the event microsoft teams need help join the meeting now meeting id passcode bycisu

Subject: today mathematics department colloquium by prof l sunil chandran
Body: original message subject mathematics department colloquium date from seminar to allfaculty allstudents cc aparajita dasgupta replyto aparajita dasgupta dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department colloquium by prof l sunil chandran from department of computer science and automation iisc bangalore on th august the details are given below title representation of graphs using homothets of cubes an intermediate representation between contact representations and intersection graphs abstract there is a vast literature on representing graphs as the intersection graphs of cubes rectangles circles spheres and their higher dimensional versions here the requirement is that the set of vertices of the given graph is represented by a family of geometric objects of the specified type and the corresponding geometric objects of two vertices intersects if and only if there is an edge between these two vertices contact representations are a special case of intersection representations where two geometric objects when they intersect are only allowed to touch each other in other words the volume of the intersection is since the intersection has to be the subset of the boundary of the geometric objects involved there is a diversity of representations that can arise from applications intermediate between intersection representations without any restrictions and contact representations the simplest example is when we have a constraint on the volume of the intersection of two geometric objects say if s and s intersect vols cap s alpha min vols vols where alpha another variant is when a set of special points say p are defined within each cube and intersection of a pair of cubes is considered valid only if some of these points or none of these points are contained in the intersection a natural case is when p is just the central point or a small nucleus around the center in this paper we study a problem in this genre when the geometric objects are homothets of dcubes ie cubes in ddimensional space possibly of different sizes each vertex of the graph is to be mapped to a point in rd and is associated with a cube centered at this point so that the given graph is the intersection graph of these cubes here the extra constraints are no cube should contain the center of another cube for each vertex the boundary of its cube contains the point mapped to at least one of its neighbors in the graph in other words the side length of the cube of a vertex is times the distance to its nearest neighbour with respect to ellinfty norm this problem was formulated because of applications in pattern recognition and computer vision and was studied by several researchers in the late nineties we settle within additive terms a major open problem in this area formulated by boyer lister and shader in sphereofinfluence graphs using supnorm mathematical and computer modelling by showing that any graph without isolated vertices has a representation of the above form in left lceil frac n right rceil dimensional space where n is the number of vertices this is almost tight there exists an infinite family of graphs such that graphs in this family require a space of at least left lceil frac n right rceil dimension to achieve the required type of representation date august time pm venue mz committee room department of mathematics speaker prof l sunil chandran all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team

Subject: re talk announcement pricing for routing and flowcontrol in payment channel networks
Body: dear all you are invited to attend an exciting talk on pricing for routing and flowcontrol in payment channel networks by dr suryanarayana sankagiri epfl postdoc th august date th august time pm pm venue bharti title pricing for routing and flowcontrol in payment channel networks abstract a payment channel network is a blockchainbased overlay mechanism that allows parties to transact more efficiently than directly using the blockchain in this talk i shall introduce these networks from first principles starting from the basic building block of payment channels next i will introduce a mathematical model of this network which will highlight several interesting properties including the constraints the network imposes on payments i will then talk about the main contribution of this work which is the design of a decentralised network protocol to route and block payments in such a network i shall provide a proof that this protocol guides a payment channel network towards an optimal operating state for anysteadystate demand finally i shall illustrate the protocols behaviour through simulations bio suryanarayana sankagiri is a postdoc in epfl switzerland his research interests are in mathematical modeling and analysis of largescale systems using tools of probability networks and optimisation he is currently working on mathematical models for human comparison data as well as algorithms to learn from such data he obtained his phd in from the university of illinois urbanachampaign where his work focused on the security and performance analysis of blockchains he Subject: mathematics department colloquium
Body: dear all we are pleased to announce the mathematics department colloquium by prof l sunil chandran from department of computer science and automation iisc bangalore on th august the details are given below title representation of graphs using homothets of cubes an intermediate representation between contact representations and intersection graphs abstract there is a vast literature on representing graphs as the intersection graphs of cubes rectangles circles spheres and their higher dimensional versions here the requirement is that the set of vertices of the given graph is represented by a family of geometric objects of the specified type and the corresponding geometric objects of two vertices intersects if and only if there is an edge between these two vertices contact representations are a special case of intersection representations where two geometric objects when they intersect are only allowed to touch each other in other words the volume of the intersection is since the intersection has to be the subset of the boundary of the geometric objects involved there is a diversity of representations that can arise from applications intermediate between intersection representations without any restrictions and contact representations the simplest example is when we have a constraint on the volume of the intersection of two geometric objects say if s and s intersect vols cap s alpha min vols vols where alpha another variant is when a set of special points say p are defined within each cube and intersection of a pair of cubes is considered valid only if some of these points or none of these points are contained in the intersection a natural case is when p is just the central point or a small nucleus around the center in this paper we study a problem in this genre when the geometric objects are homothets of dcubes ie cubes in ddimensional space possibly of different sizes each vertex of the graph is to be mapped to a point in rd and is associated with a cube centered at this point so that the given graph is the intersection graph of these cubes here the extra constraints are no cube should contain the center of another cube for each vertex the boundary of its cube contains the point mapped to at least one of its neighbors in the graph in other words the side length of the cube of a vertex is times the distance to its nearest neighbour with respect to ellinfty norm this problem was formulated because of applications in pattern recognition and computer vision and was studied by several researchers in the late nineties we settle within additive terms a major open problem in this area formulated by boyer lister and shader in sphereofinfluence graphs using supnorm mathematical and computer modelling by showing that any graph without isolated vertices has a representation of the above form in left lceil frac n right rceil dimensional space where n is the number of vertices this is almost tight there exists an infinite family of graphs such that graphs in this family require a space of at least left lceil frac n right rceil dimension to achieve the required type of representation date august time pm venue mz committee room department of mathematics speaker prof l sunil chandran all are cordially invited to attend with best regards mathematics department colloquium team dr aparajita dasgupta associate professor department of mathematics indian institute of technology delhi

Subject: re talk on design thinking of quantum communication in quantum networks
Body: dear all this is a gentle reminder for the talk on design thinking of quantum communication in quantum networks today at pm in bharti best dr neel kanth kundu assistant professor care iit delhi web original message subject talk on design thinking of quantum communication in quantum networks date from neel kanth kundu to dear all you are invited to attend an exciting talk on design thinking of quantum communication in quantum networks by mr pankaj kumar research scholar nation taiwan university of science and technology with details as follows date monday aug time pm venue bharti abstract design thinking is an innovative approach that has been applied across various fields to solve complex problems through a usercentered perspective in quantum networks leveraging design thinking can provide novel insights and methodologies for addressing the unique challenges presented by quantum technologies this talk explores the application of design thinking principles to the design development and deployment of quantum communication systems we discuss efficient entanglement generation in quantum networks with relatively limited resources such as quantum memories additionally we focus on the entanglement routing problem to build longdistance entanglement for concurrent source destination pairs through multiple hops finally we examine important metrics for designing communication in quantum networks including fidelity channel capacity communication medium quantum memory success probability and quantum repeater limitations google calendar link thanks and regards dr neel kanth kundu assistant professor care iit delhi web

Subject: seminar modeling biological tissues across scales by dr karan taneja august cbme committee room
Body: dear all the centre of biomedical engineering iit delhi cordially invites you to a departmental seminar by dr karan taneja university of notre dame usa details mentioned below refreshments will be served date time august at venue b cbme committee room located at the rightmost end of st floor block iii title modeling biological tissues across scales abstract biomechanical phenomena in our bodies happen across multiple length scales with each scale having their own geometry material properties and physics for example the brain during gestation experiences drastic changes in volume and develops wrinkling patterns cortical folding these result from the proliferation and migration of cells leading to growth of the tissue on the other hand the force production and deformation characteristics of the skeletal muscle are determined by the orientation of fibers and stiffness of their surrounding connective tissue capturing these multiscale characteristics invivoinvitro are nontrivial but essential and insilico modeling frameworks play a vital role as robust alternatives in this talk computational frameworks for capturing the growth of the brain tissue and understanding the mechanisms by which muscles transmit force will be discussed using theories of finite growth and multiscale material homogenization this talk aims to address hypotheses such as the role of astrocytes in cortical folding and how shearing is necessary for force transmission in skeletal muscles bio dr karan taneja is a postdoctoral researcher at the university of notre dame notre dame in usa he earned his bachelor’s degree in civil engineering from delhi technological university new delhi india msc in structural engineering from tu delft delft the netherlands and phd in structural engineering from university of california san diego san diego ca usa his research is in computational biomechanics using solid mechanics and computational tools to develop multiscale models for biological materials collaborating with clinicians and experimentalists he aims to understand how lower level phenomena affect higher level behaviors in soft tissues in the human body providing insights that can help comprehend their role in related pathologies best regards dr naveen kumar singh assistant professor centre for biomedical engineering indian institute of technology delhi india Subject: talk on design thinking of quantum communication in quantum networks
Body: dear all you are invited to attend an exciting talk on design thinking of quantum communication in quantum networks by mr pankaj kumar research scholar nation taiwan university of science and technology with details as follows date monday aug time pm venue bharti abstract design thinking is an innovative approach that has been applied across various fields to solve complex problems through a usercentered perspective in quantum networks leveraging design thinking can provide novel insights and methodologies for addressing the unique challenges presented by quantum technologies this talk explores the application of design thinking principles to the design development and deployment of quantum communication systems we discuss efficient entanglement generation in quantum networks with relatively limited resources such as quantum memories additionally we focus on the entanglement routing problem to build longdistance entanglement for concurrent source destination pairs through multiple hops finally we examine important metrics for designing communication in quantum networks including fidelity channel capacity communication medium quantum memory success probability and quantum repeater limitations google calendar link thanks and regards dr neel kanth kundu assistant professor care iit delhi web

Subject: talk announcement pricing for routing and flowcontrol in payment channel networks
Body: dear all you are invited to attend an exciting talk on pricing for routing and flowcontrol in payment channel networks by dr suryanarayana sankagiri epfl postdoc th august date th august time pm pm venue bharti title pricing for routing and flowcontrol in payment channel networks abstract a payment channel network is a blockchainbased overlay mechanism that allows parties to transact more efficiently than directly using the blockchain in this talk i shall introduce these networks from first principles starting from the basic building block of payment channels next i will introduce a mathematical model of this network which will highlight several interesting properties including the constraints the network imposes on payments i will then talk about the main contribution of this work which is the design of a decentralised network protocol to route and block payments in such a network i shall provide a proof that this protocol guides a payment channel network towards an optimal operating state for anysteadystate demand finally i shall illustrate the protocols behaviour through simulations bio suryanarayana sankagiri is a postdoc in epfl switzerland his research interests are in mathematical modeling and analysis of largescale systems using tools of probability networks and optimisation he is currently working on mathematical models for human comparison data as well as algorithms to learn from such data he obtained his phd in from the university of illinois urbanachampaign where his work focused on the security and performance analysis of blockchains he obtained his btech in ee from iit bombay in please let me know if you need anything else from my side i look forward to an acknowledgement from you finalising the date of the talk as well as a word on Subject: seminar on nanoscale ferroelectric memoryprof siddheswar maikap nd august
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to attend a seminar by prof siddheswar maikap from the department of electronic engineering at chang gung university taiwan the details are as follows title ferroelectric memory for nanoscale nonvolatile memory and neuromorphic applications date nd august venue care committee room blockiii room time am abstract recently ferroelectric highk material such as doped hfo film has emerged as a promising candidate offering compatibility with cmos processes scalability and low power consumption as compared to the conventional perovskite ferroelectrics like pbzr tio srbi ta o and batio however doping concentration and dopant type plays a critical role in stabilizing the ferroelectric orthorhombic phase in hfo based thin films although differing dopant percentages is required to induce high ferroelectric polarization for example the ferroelectric fe property of various dopants have been reported but the zr doped hf zr o hzo is commonly investigated for future cmos compatible nonvolatile memory applications owing to the nonsymmetric polar metastable ophase pca formation the polarization value can be modulated in addition both metal electrode and interfacial layer also play a crucial role in stabilizing the ferroelectric ophase within doped hfo thin films the formation of the ferroelectric ophase in these films is largely influenced by the mechanical stress and strain resulting from the lattice mismatch and thermal expansion coefficient this talk will cover the review on doped ferroelectric materials with electrode interface engineering and neuromorphic characteristics it is expected that this ferroelectric memory will be mass production in the year therefore this topic has huge scope on research during this period or later too the promising characteristic of the d memory enables the device to be used as bioinspired electronic synapseneuromorphic in hardware based artificial intelligence ai application in future prof siddheswar maikap received his phd degree from the department of physics indian institute of technology iit kharagpur india in he is teaching at department of electronic engineering chang gung university taiwan from to till date and he has been associate professor in and professor since he has published more than sci journal papers and more than international conference papers as an author and coauthor seven patents including us and taiwan are holding flashrrammram and biosensors he has received “excellent research and innovation award” from itri industrial technology research institute taiwan on development of “sige buffer free compressively strained ge pfet on si with si epi passivation” his group received best oralposter paper awards from an international conference he is a reviewer of many high impact factors and reputed journals he has delivered more than keynoteinvited talks he was a part of a family to develop ferroelectric memory through national taiwan university and taiwan semiconductor manufacturing company ntutsmc projects in several years now his research focuses on ferroelectric memory and biosensing best regards samaresh das professor centre for applied research in Body: dear all this is a gentle reminder for the talk today please find your seating in the hall minutes before the talk begins best regards subodh on jul at pm subodh sharma wrote dear students and colleagues we are delighted to invite you to an institute lecture by dr ruchi choudhary on data science for energy transitions please note the time of the talk and be seated in the hall minutes before the start of the talk the details of the lecture are provided below datetimevenue july pm seminar hall title slipping through the net can data science help target energy transitions policy interventions abstract cities bring together people ideas and information to act as engines of creativity and innovation but across a city there can be a great deal of variation across households in their socioeconomic circumstances and in turn their energy use this heterogeneity can also be observed spatially and energy use can be impacted by underlying spatial inequality characterising this heterogeneity at play in cities and how it impacts energy demand is key to better understanding and modelling urban residential energy demand the lecture will present two cases a residential energy of the built environment at cambridge she leads the multidisciplinary energy efficient cities initiative initially funded by a science innovation award at cambridge she has led the research group on digital twins of built environment at the alan turing institute she is leading projects on modelling underground heat and cityscale geothermal systems district energy networks urbanintegrated farming Subject: reminder talk by dr steffen neumeir and dr jakob bandorf friedrichalexanderuniversität erlangennürnberg fau july pm
Body: dear all i am delighted to invite you to a jointresearch talk by dring steffen neumeier group leader associate professor and dr jakob bandorf research associate department of materials science and engineering friedrichalexanderuniversität erlangennürnberg fau university of erlangennürnberg germany scheduled on th july hrs ist venue dmse committee room the title of the talk is advancements in hightemperature materials influence of local chemical and structural heterogeneities on mechanical properties below is the abstract of the talk and a brief bios of the speakers looking forward to seeing you then if you want to meet the speakers in person afterwards for discussion please contact me ayan bhowmik abstract metallic and intermetallic hightemperature materials are pivotal for applications requiring exceptional thermal stability such as in aerospace and power generation these materials retain their strength creep resistance and oxidation resistance at elevated temperatures ensuring the reliability and efficiency of engines and reactors operating under extreme conditions their usage extends to critical components like turbine blades injection heads and combustion chambers where failure is not an option to enhance engine efficiency and durability there is a continuous need for new hightemperature materials with improved properties and temperature capabilities this presentation provides an overview of the research activities of the high temperature materials group at fau erlangennürnberg focusing on the development and characterization of advanced hightemperature materials these include ni co and febased superalloys intermetallic titanium aluminides insitu eutectic nialcrmo composites complex concentrated alloys and oxidationresistant coatings selected examples will illustrate how local accumulations and depletions of specific alloying elements influence the mechanical properties of these materials additionally results will demonstrate how highresolution and highenergy xray diffraction techniques facilitate the indepth characterization of superalloys revealing the behavior of ordered precipitate phases coherently embedded in a crystallographically similar matrix phase these microstructural investigations at the nanometer and atomic scale deepen our fundamental understanding of hightemperature materials enabling the design of new alloys with enhanced properties for superior performance and reliability speakers biography dr s neumeier dring steffen neumeier is a senior scientist and group leader at the department of materials science and engineering of the friedrichalexanderuniversity erlangennürnberg fau germany he studied materials science and engineering at the fau where he received his diploma dipling in afterwards he did his phd from to on th generation nibase superalloys in the group of prof m göken at the fau from where he obtained his doctorate degree with distinction in during his postdoc period from to in the group of prof c rae and prof h stone at the rollsroyceuniversity technology center of the university of cambrigde uk he worked on the identification and development of novel alloys for high temperature structural applications since he leads the “high temperature materials group” at the institute i general materials properties and is a lecturer at the fau dr neumeier’s primary research focus is on the correlation between composition processing microstructure and mechanical properties of high temperature materials such as ni co and febased superalloys titanium aluminides intermetallics complex concentrated alloys and coatings his further scientific interests are the characterization of structural materials by xray and neutron scattering and diffraction techniques dr steffen neumeier received the young scientist award in and the masing memorial award in of the german society for materials science dgm he authored more than peerreviewed journal and proceeding articles in the field of materials science he has a hindex of and was among the top two percent of the most cited scientists worldwide in dr j bandorf jakob bandorf is a research associate in the hightemperature materials group under the supervision of dr steffen neumeier at the institute for general materials properties msei of the university erlangennuremberg he has an over years’ experience in the field of the characterization of singlecrystalline co and nibase superalloys using hrxray diffraction his particular research focus in that field is the investigation of the influencing factors on the lattice parameters lattice misfit of singlecrystalline superalloys during his master studies he already gained insights into scientific work as a student assistant at the institute msei headed by prof dr mathias göken he passed his masters degree in materials science and engineering in with distinction and was honored with the department prize master of the department of materials science Subject: cas seminar on july tuesday pm
Body: dear all you are cordially invited to the following inperson cas seminar on july tuesday at pm speaker dr neil tandon associate professor york university canada date and time july tuesday pm venue cas seminar room vi title building confidence in regional projections of extreme precipitation abstract with rising temperatures models and observations have shown increasing extreme precipitation intensity over most of the globe this correspondence follows from basic thermodynamic principles as atmospheric temperature increases the equilibrium vapor pressure of water also increases in accordance with the clausiusclapeyron equation which means that there is more atmospheric moisture available to form precipitation regionally however changes in dynamicsspecifically vertical velocity of aircan act to greatly amplify or completely oppose the extreme precipitation increase expected from thermodynamic principles thus building confidence in regional projections of extreme precipitation intensity requires understanding the reasons for changes in vertical velocity during extreme precipitation events referred to as extreme ascent in this talk i will go over recent and current efforts to understand longterm changes in extreme ascent and challenges with accurately modelling extreme ascent i will include analysis of global climate models gcms as well as results from highresolution regional simulations and discuss the tradeoffs with each approach past studies based on analysis of gcm output have suggested a variety of reasons for changes in extreme ascent and my group has been performing controlled experiments with regional models to try to clarify matters these experiments suggest that a horizontal transport process called differential vorticity advection plays a key role in driving extreme ascent changes but important questions remain about the influence of convective parameterization model approximations of smallscale convection thus future efforts to build confidence in projections of extreme precipitation will likely require improvements to convective parameterization alongside these efforts increases in computational capability will allow greater usage of global convectionresolving models that do not require convective parameterization bio dr neil tandon is an associate professor of atmospheric science at york university in toronto in neil obtained his phd in applied physics and applied mathematics from columbia university under the supervision of prof lorenzo polvani afterwards he was a postdoctoral fellow in the group of prof paul kushner at the university of toronto funded partially by the canadian sea ice and snow evolution cansise network from until joining york in neil was a postdoctoral fellow in the climate research division of environment and climate change canada neils research focuses on climate dynamics he uses a combination of models observations and mathematical analysis to investigate how motions in earths atmosphere and ocean influence climate his work has helped to clarify the physical processes driving longterm changes in the atmospheric circulation with implications for desertification cloud abundance extreme precipitation and arctic sea ice motion he also investigates variability in the ocean circulation and its relationship to other aspects of climate variability sajeev philip

special topics in formal methods col where i will be focusing on sat solvers and their applications in trustworthy computing please find the belowappended course description the sat problem or boolean satisfiability problem is about determining whether a boolean formula can be satisfied by an assignment of truth values to its variables this problem is npcomplete and doesnt have an efficient algorithm that works for all cases however modern sat solvers demonstrate remarkable efficiency often resolving problems with tens of thousands of variables and millions of constraints this course aims to demystify sat solvers in the first half we will delve into the algorithms and heuristics underpinning modern sat solvers in the latter part we will explore recent applications in explainable or certified ai verification and synthesis of automated systems and graph optimization problems more details about the course can be found at feel free to reach out if you need more information regards priyanka chandruka new faculty fellow assistant prof cse iitd

Subject: school of public policy announcement of course for all students ug pg
Body: the school of public policy is offering the following special credit modules credit special topics courses and some new courses during the upcoming diwali semester julydecember these courses will help students gain a publicpolicy perspective on many technological and social issues these courses are open to all students ug pg who have earned the minimum required credits for enrolling in those courses for and level se rules in courses of stdy the main commitment expected from students is active class participation and engaging with the readings and discussions the details of these courses are mentioned below we hope interested students will take the opportunity to enrol in these courses regards sanjiva prasad course code spl course title advanced topics in policy studies climate change adaptation from theory to practice credit structure credits instructor prof anshu ogra lecture slot time slot h mon wed thu course description this course aims to equip students with the concepts tools and techniques required for effectively engaging with and contributing to adaptation policy and planning processes at national and regional levels students will learn the interrelationship between adaptation vulnerability and resilience theory overlaps between climate change adaptation and development and limits and barriers to adaptation course content introduction to key terms adaptation vulnerability and resilience adaptation governance from the local to the global level climate change adaptation and social policy knowledge systems and adaptation climate resilient development crd limits and barriers to adaptation maladaptation loss and damage adaptation finance adaptation planning and decision making in india current state and future visioning course code spl course title geographical information systems gis for public policy credit structure credits instructor prof rajarshi dasgupta lecture slot time slot ab mon thu course description students will achieve a fundamental understanding of gis and geospatial technology and their application in public policy and social science research students will learn several gisbased analytical tools understand and interpret spatial data and develop problemsolving skills through thematic maps students will get handson training to solve complex public policy problems through spatial analysis course content introduction to gis spatial data structure maps projection and overview of geospatial technology etc use of gis in public policy research theories and training on basic gis analysis and their application in public policy research eg rastervector processing digitization geodatabase creation and management overlay analysis creation of thematic maps etc advanced gis analysis and their application in public policy research eg spatial interpolation techniques hotspot analysis network analysis etc geographically weighted regression zonal statistics public participatory gis ppgis in public policy research use of nighttime satellite data for social science research practical on basic and advanced gis analysis case studies on gis applications in public health and natural resource management course code spl course title technology and globalisation credit structure credits instructor prof suma athreye lecture slot time slot a mon thu course description students will learn how technological changes and changes in industrial leadership have shaped the global economy the course will equip students to think about contemporary technological changes move to green technologies digitization and ai and how they may influence and are influenced by the international environment course content causes of growing international economic integration international economic integration versus globalization role of technology economics and politics in historical episodes of international economic integration international monetary system gatt wto and the growth of world trade contemporary production systems and industrial leadership environmental and political limits to international economic integration forces behind the retreat of international economic integration course code spl course title electricity sector reforms in the renewables era credit structure credits instructor prof sanjay mitra prof kaveri k iychettira lecture slot time slot f tue thu fri course description on completion of this course the students will be able to analyze the structure and governance of electricity systems with particular focus on the context of increasing renewable penetration and in developing country contexts the students will demonstrate an ability to apply concepts of power system economics including wholesale electricity market design regulation of generation and network segments retail competition and electricity tariff design they will also examine the limitations of economic theory particularly in the context of insufficient costrecovery in developing country settings they will be able to analyse contemporary policies and outcomes in the indian electricity sector evaluate proposed reforms such as the electricity amendment bill issues related to the transition to renewables in the power sector market design challenges and opportunities concerns of intermittency and related policies with particular emphasis on the challenges specific to the indian power sector such as access affordability and regional equity the students will develop handson expertise on the electricity sector with detailed case studies corresponding to each theory segment also using actual utility data they will be able to locate electricity sector issues within the wider public policy framework course content evolution of the vertically integrated electricity utility initial experiences in developed countries and early reformers independent electricity producers ipps regulation and deregulation independent system operators power system cost structures power system economics power purchase agreements – longterm risk distribution electricity market design – dayahead intraday balancing markets ancillary services tariff design for end consumers retail competition capacity remuneration mechanisms critique of the reforms experienced worldwide salience of the distribution sector access and affordability reforms rollback renewables country experiences china germany usa california texas mexico uk indian experience – electricity act cases of enron dabhol odisha delhi renewables penetration – impact on access electricity for agriculture tariffs regional equity national programmes kusum saubhagya deen dayal upadhyaya grameen vidyutikaran yojana excelbased exercises on the financial viability of discoms using actual utility data explore and develop renewables and reforms trajectories for different states electricity sector reforms and the larger public policy rubriccentrestate issues effects of the dominant global discourse on the renewables programme in india course code spl course title information communication technologies ict and society credit structure credits instructor prof rathin biswas lecture slot time slot ac tue fri course description the students will be able to understand the socially critical policyrelevant complex realworld developmental challenges and how technology can help in addressing those across various domains – water and sanitation health transportation education waste management urban environment etc they will learn the benefits limitations and challenges of information communication technologies ict including internet of things iot while addressing such challenges across various domains along with the associated policy nexus students will be able to Subject: me guest talk by prof dr zhixiong james guo on rd july at pm
Body: dear all dr zhixiong guo is a professor of mechanical and aerospace engineering at rutgers universitynew brunswick nj usa he will be giving the me department seminar on rd july as per below schedule date tuesday rd july time pm venue me committee room mechanical engineering department title of the talk interfacial heat transport in heterostructures abstract heat dissipation through heterostructures is of technological importance and fundamental research interest diamond is a desirable heat spreader for integrating with semiconductors to dissipate quickly large amount of heat generated in electronics the rapid development of ganondiamond devices holds much promise for thermal management of highpower electronics and devices hitherto the interfacial effect of an inherent epilayer between gan and diamond to thermal dissipation is less investigated one aim of this study is to understand and analyze the interfacial thermal boundary resistance tbr across a diamondgan heterostructure with an epilayer of different substrates the thickness effect of epilayer is also revealed besides cbn is drawing increasing attention because it not only owns diamondlike thermal properties but also is a promising material for fabricating optoelectronic devices it was found that the interfacial tbr reduced when the diamond cap or the gan substrate was replaced by the cbn further cbn can be directly grown on diamond without use of epilayer resulting in an unprecedented low tbr in the diamondcbn interface another aim is to analyze spectral heat transport at the interface with solid diamond and liquid water please see the link below for the details of the talk all interested are welcome to join the talk thanks and regards dr abhishek das and dr supreet singh bahga me seminar committee department of mechanical engineering iit delhi

Subject: talk by dr steffen neumeir and dr jakob bandorf friedrichalexanderuniversität erlangennürnberg fau july pm
Body: dear all i am delighted to invite you to a jointresearch talk by dring steffen neumeier group leader associate professor and dr jakob bandorf research associate department of materials science and engineering friedrichalexanderuniversität erlangennürnberg fau university of erlangennürnberg germany scheduled on th july hrs ist venue dmse committee room the title of the talk is advancements in hightemperature materials influence of local chemical and structural heterogeneities on mechanical properties below is the abstract of the talk and a brief bios of the speakers looking forward to seeing you then if you want to meet the speakers in person afterwards for discussion please contact me ayan bhowmik abstract metallic and intermetallic hightemperature materials are pivotal for applications requiring exceptional thermal stability such as in aerospace and power generation these materials retain their strength creep resistance and oxidation resistance at elevated temperatures ensuring the reliability and efficiency of engines and reactors operating under extreme conditions their usage extends to critical components like turbine blades injection heads and combustion chambers where failure is not an option to enhance engine efficiency and durability there is a continuous need for new hightemperature materials with improved properties and temperature capabilities this presentation provides an overview of the research activities of the high temperature materials group at fau erlangennürnberg focusing on the development and characterization of advanced hightemperature materials these include ni co and febased superalloys intermetallic titanium aluminides insitu eutectic nialcrmo composites complex concentrated alloys and oxidationresistant coatings selected examples will illustrate how local accumulations and depletions of specific alloying elements influence the mechanical properties of these materials additionally results will demonstrate how highresolution and highenergy xray diffraction techniques facilitate the indepth characterization of superalloys revealing the behavior of ordered precipitate phases coherently embedded in a crystallographically similar matrix phase these microstructural investigations at the nanometer and atomic scale deepen our fundamental understanding of hightemperature materials enabling the design of new alloys with enhanced properties for superior performance and reliability speakers biography dr s neumeier dring steffen neumeier is a senior scientist and group leader at the department of materials science and engineering of the friedrichalexanderuniversity erlangennürnberg fau germany he studied materials science and engineering at the fau where he received his diploma dipling in afterwards he did his phd from to on th generation nibase superalloys in the group of prof m göken at the fau from where he obtained his doctorate degree with distinction in during his postdoc period from to in the group of prof c rae and prof h stone at the rollsroyceuniversity technology center of the university of cambrigde uk he worked on the identification and development of novel alloys for high temperature structural applications since he leads the “high temperature materials group” at the institute i general materials properties and is a lecturer at the fau dr neumeier’s primary research focus is on the correlation between composition processing microstructure and mechanical properties of high temperature materials such as ni co and febased superalloys titanium aluminides intermetallics complex concentrated alloys and coatings his further scientific interests are the characterization of structural materials by xray and neutron scattering and diffraction techniques dr steffen neumeier received the young scientist award in and the masing memorial award in of the german society for materials science dgm he authored more than peerreviewed journal and proceeding articles in the field of materials science he has a hindex of and was among the top two percent of the most cited scientists worldwide in dr j bandorf jakob bandorf is a research associate in the hightemperature materials group under the supervision of dr steffen neumeier at the institute for general materials properties msei of the university erlangennuremberg he has an over years’ experience in the field of the characterization of singlecrystalline co and nibase superalloys using hrxray diffraction his particular research focus in that field is the investigation of the influencing factors on the lattice parameters lattice misfit of singlecrystalline superalloys during his master studies he already gained insights into scientific work as a student assistant at the institute msei headed by prof dr mathias göken he passed his masters degree in materials science and engineering in with distinction and was honored with the department prize master of the department of materials science at the fau erlangennuremberg he already came into contact with the field of superalloys in during his bachelor thesis dr ayan bhowmik assistant professor department of materials science and metallurgy
